reviews.comment: Dr. Fenning is genuine and caring professor He cares about the wellbeing of all his students and makes an effort to get to know all the students in his class. He will work with you for your grade and is overall one of the most caring professors at SMU

Brian is the most genuine and caring professor at SMU. He is humble and cares about the community. He is a good man, funny, and a good professor. Anyone complaining about him didn't go to class or do their work. You could take this class with closed eyes and still get an A. SMU is lucky to have him.

I don't know why there are three recent bad reviews because this professor is great. I took the personal responsibility and community class and learned a lot about myself and the world. My confidence and self love and happiness went up through this course and professor. He is kind, respectful, a great teacher, funny, and open minded.

He shows useless videos while trying to be cool in his awareness of college students, and permanently misses the mark. Easy homework but his useless class content doesn't help and is a waste of your time. The amount we pay for classes should compel more compelling professors, not wastes of spaces like this one, though.

Dr. Fennig is an amazing professor and person. He is an open-book, very accepting, fun to talk to, and smart. He cares about all of his students and makes sure we know this. There are 3 essays and services longs we have to do, but as long as you don't do the minimum, he will give >= B+. Prof. is great, HSP's course design is inefficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Fennig is a great person and fantastic professor. There are readings every class but participation is the most important thing in his class. If you have to take PRW I would definitely recommend Dr. Fennig. There are a few papers and a presentation but nothing too stressful.

Easiest class you will ever take. There are readings, but you don't have to actually read them to do well as long as you show up to class. A couple essays and assignments, all of which are graded really generously. Fennig is really nice and super easy to talk to, but the structure of the class makes it a bit of a waste of time.

Dr. Fennig is the best! Most homework is reading for PRW 3303. He is kind and really cares about his students. I absolutely would take him again and recommend him! He gives specific workable feedback on essays and helps his students improve. Great person and easy class if you do the readings! Take him if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Fennig and this class are super chill overall. Essentially, you'll read a text before class and discuss it during class. Definitely a class you can skate through by just showing up. Was not my favorite subject, but wasn't horrible. Dr. Fennig made it pretty easy and somewhat engaging.

Nicest and most chill professor at SMU. It's impossible to fail his class, you literally need to never show up and not do the assignments. Very fair grader and super cool to talk to about any topic you want

Honestly, Dr. Fennig is an amazing professor. His classes are mostly discussions about the readings before class. Any material he assigns, he provides on canvas. Very caring and engaging. Definitely recommend taking his class if you can.

Fennig is a great prof. He encourages discussion during class time about the topics (though your mileage may vary) and for everyone to be respectful. As for the class, you can see PRW as a second WRTR. The course is reading and essay heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fennig is easily one of the best professors at SMU. He fosters a friendly classroom environment and is genuinely a super nice guy. Additionally, he made the material very interesting and gives great feedback on essays/writings. He's a great professor and definitely worth taking! Ask him about his travels if you do take his class.

Professor Fennig is awesome and really cares about his students. Its an easy course and there is a good chunk of reading material, but you can get away with skimming the text during class. His lecture are where you really learn the meaning and discuss the good and bad of the text. He has an open mind and wants what's best for his students.
One of the best teachers at SMU. Not a hard class, very clear about what he wants for papers.

Dr. Fennig is a super easy and awesome professor. This class in particular doesnt require much work and he makes it clear what you need to get a good grade. The class itself is an easy A if you do the assignments with effort. Classes are boring and lecture heavy but he makes it as interesting as he can given the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but his teaching is called in every day, there's really no point to his class. If you need an easy A, here's your guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: You seriously cannot fail this class. He's a nice guy, doesn't assign practically any work so there's no time sink, and its material that you already know.

He's a great guy even though I had it as an 8am, he was really awake and got me interested in the topics we discussed. You have to go to class, but it's not bad. Good guy, easy class with little outside work, you don't learn a lot but that's the class not prof's fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is actually caring about his students and his lectures inspires me a lot. He is very transparent and shares his personal stories to encourage students sometimes. I think I am extremely lucky to meet a great person like him during my four years here.
Truly cares about students. Very inspiring and approachable. Would definitely recommend taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fennig is a kind, upbeat, and engaging professor. He makes relatively boring material exciting and is easy-going. I would highly recommend taking his PRW course.
Professor Fennig is the BEST professor to have for PRW! He keeps class interesting and is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet.
Loved his class. Best PRW professor. Is super nice and his lectures are actually really interesting.
Overall a great professor. Take him. His class is interesting, he's nice and the workload is light.
Pass/fail class. Just do not be absent. There are 4 papers overall - only 1-page double-spaced each. Forget about grammar, just write something interesting, and he will give you the point.
Dr. Fennig is a very kind and caring professor. He is very good about connecting with his students on a personal level and loves to learn from them.
Dr. Fennig is one of the best, most sincere professors at SMU. He makes PRW worth much more than just the requirement. You can learn a lot about life from this guy!
great guy, he clearly cares about his students and is teaching an important class, the class is pass/fail so its almost impossible not to pass as long as you show up.
Awesome PRW teacher! He cares about each of his students and makes class very interesting! The few assignments given are extremely easy, and the whole semester is fun and relaxed.
Dr. Fennig is super cool and makes PRW fun. You're basically guaranteed to pass this class as long as you don't skip too much and write the short and easy papers.

Dr. Fennig is by far one of my favorite professors. He is extremely engaging and really cares about each of the students in his class. I was not excited to take PRW and I am still not a huge fan of the class considering you get 1 credit hour for 3 hours worth of class, but he made it as best as it could be.
He is very passionate about what he does and can be pretty inspiring. Very optimistic! Although the class can be common sense, he makes it interesting.

Dr. Fennig is the best!!! He is super chill, funny, and cares about his job. We had a couple guided meditations, only 3 one page papers, and he always brings real people in the field into the lectures. I wish I could take PRW every year, its such a nice class to go to. TAKE HIM!!!
Great professor!
Best professor ever!

Dr. Fennig is a very funny, super engaging, and a great guy all around. In his PRW class, expect two or three one-page reflection papers on an out-of-class experience that brought you out of your comfort zone and one presentation about yourself. Cheap financial planning textbook required, but I didn't buy it. This is a pass/fail class.

If you have the chance to take him you should. All you need to do is show up and he makes the class enjoyable and really cares about he does. It is only 3 one page papers that get graded and you either pass or fail them no letter grade. Great class would highly recommend for a PRW teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy

Dr. Fennig is passionate about the topic and creates a fun environment that promotes interactive discussion. Not a class to sit back passively, you need to participate and do the reading. But the reading is not difficult. He provides clear and personal feedback on the weekly journal entries.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very genuinely nice guy who always show up energetic and passionate about what we are learning. Tells personal stories and creates a great environment to give opinions and open up. Really loves teaching and makes PRW more than bearable.
He tells great stories that inspire the class to discuss and act out on our beliefs in the real world. You can tell he truley loves what he does.

Dr. Fennig really deserves the 5.0 rating. He makes it a point to know all of his students by name and responds thoughtfully and genuinely to your OCEs. The in class discussions are fun - everyone has their piece to say. He is a professor who has a life-long impact on his students without realizing. Thank you, Dr. Fennig!

PRW is just one of those classes everyone has to go through. Fennig made the class actually enjoyable. I love participating in the class. He makes everything more fun and relaxed. He even showed me how to sell things on Craigslist.

Harris is such a good teacher and really wants to help you learn. Its a shame most PRW students don't take the class seriously enough for him to help them. He is entertaining and funny and makes every class interesting, you can't go wrong with him! Highly recommend.
Its a boring class to be sure but its easy and he really enjoys what he does as far as PRW classes go its pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great teacher! I don't dread going to PRW because of him. He actually cares about all of his students and wants them to succeed in life! He tries to make the class enjoyable and I admire that. If you can get him for your professor I recommend highly!

Brian is a great professor. I wish a life requirement for every human being would be to take this man's class. Cares about each and every student. Takes the time to individually thank and offer encouragement to every student. Very inspirational class.
most amazing human ever i love him

Very inspirational teacher with a lot of wisdom. I would definitely take another class with him if I could. Easy to pass as long as you participate and turn in the short 1 page, out of class experience papers.
Professor Fennig is one of the best PRW teachers that SMU has to offer. It's a short PassFail class and he utilizes his time fantastically. 1010 recommend
Great professor, would definitely take again

Bottom line: Show up and pass. You have 3-4 one page assignments a semester as well as one: Personal Identity project which takes a total of 10 minutes to do. He is very relaxed and friendly. Probably the most relaxed and chill of all the PRW 1101 professors. Definitely recommend.
Professor Fennig is seriously the best. That's basically the entire story. TAKE HIM. (But don't buy the book, that's my only regret. Seriously, don't.)
He was awesome!!!!!!!! So cool and nice and knows he's wasting your time so he kind of makes fun of himself. Would definitely take a class from him again.

In the classroom, he's the best. As the year progresses, you will learn that he is a total enigma outside of his work. PRW is kind of a pointless class, and I think he knows it. He always has this grin on his face like he knows he's just wasting your time...
Excellent coach and really good motivator, couldn't recommend him more. Super easy.

Awesome guy. Really cares about what he does and his students. Makes a class that everyone is forced to take and would normally be a blow off class and actually makes it interesting. Probably the nicest professor at SMU.
Great professor. Loves what he does. Take him.

Really chill guy. Didn't assign anything extra other than what the PRW course requires. I walked in late pretty often but he never made a big deal about it. He is passionate in what he is trying to teach students and makes the class interesting.
Entertaining teacher. No extra assignments. Is actually interested in what he is teaching. I felt like I learned something. Take him!

He's an awesome guy. Even though I had it as an 8am, he was really engaging and got me interested in the topics we discussed. You have to go to class, but it's worth. Great guy, easy class with little outside work
Relaxed and genuine guy.  Slight lisp but didn't bother me.  All wellness classes are easy regardless of teacher
He's chill. Everybody passes. Other teachers are easier. I thought it was going to be the most stupid class ever. I actually learned some stuff though.

He really takes an interest in his class. He has a passion for what he does, and it really comes out during class. He will keep you interested and engaged while giving you some great tips that are life-lasting! Fenning is a really friendly guy, and you'll enjoy his class.

Great guy to be around! always positive! i learned a lot about life from him, even if i don't agree with some of what is taught. We would see each other in la Madeline, and i was always greeted with a smile and a conversation. Good man, good teacher. take him if you really want to get something out of your wellness class
Loved this class. He's a fun guy; definitely recommend to take him for wellness.
Awesome guy. Amazing to be around. Highly Recommend.

Brian is such an amazing professor! Seriously one of the nicest guys I've ever met and makes you feel like you really mater. I actually enjoyed going to this class because of him. He's such a sweetheart and makes class really fun and interesting. Also super flexible and understanding about late work. TAKE HIM!
Looks like howie mandel from deal or no deal. He's so easy and doesn't care if you mess around. Take this class
This class was super fun - he made an 8 am class actually enjoyable! Great guy and a great wellness teacher.
Great guy, take him and you will have the easiest time in wellness

He's really great and funny. I couldnt imagine taking wellness with anyone else. if you miss a certain number of days, you automatically fail, but he's really flexible for illness and family emergencies. you have to write 4 1 pg papers... but he doesnt even care if you turn them in on time. he'd rather you do them well than fake it. excellent prof!
Loved him! Take him for Wellness!
super funny
Fennig is the best wellness teacher! His class is so chill, you only have to go and he will entertain you!! He makes it as fun as it's going to be (which is surprisingly pretty good!)

For having to teach at 8:00 he is extremely enthusiastic and fun.  He has pretty funny powerpoints and A LOT of what he says -really- has relevance in life.  If you listen carefully, you might pick up on some very useful ways to look at life.  He has some wisdom and life lessons to offer.

He is the best wellness professor there is, highly recommend his class, he is full of energy and life and draws you into his lessons of wellness which are amazing and life-changing, if you get the chance to take him, take him!
This was actually a fun class that I looked forward to going to every morning. He's a nice guy, too.
TAKE THIS WELLNESS. I'm serious. Easy, interesting, and he's really nice although maybe a little too interested in turning everyone into "well people". Oh well...it's easy.
So cute and sweet!
very nice, funny, generally a cool guy. one of the few teachers i actually miss seeing
nice guy. i actually enjoy wellness. doesn't care if you come in late. if you miss too many classes, you can go to his office and let him explain the lesson to you for credit.
Great guy! High energy and makes this class fun. Easy to talk to and understanding. Knows what he's talking about and helpful with workout. Laid back. I would take him again!
Really cool guy who keeps the class relatively interesting for what it covers.  Highly recommended.

Even though she grades pretty harshly, I can still tell that she tries her best and is very passionate about the class. In general, I really like Dr. Alford as a professor, and she gives an appropriate amount of work for the undergrad section of this class. My advice is to write more than you think you need to and follow the notebooks!

I love Dr. Alford. I took Computer Graphics with her, and I loved it so much. She really cares that you understand what's happening in lectures, and if you say you don't understand, she thanks you for telling her and goes through it differently. She doesn't require lectures, but you should definitely go or you will be lost.

They are the only one that teaches this class, so here are some tips: Attendance is a big part of the grade, quizzes are more important than the exams, make sure that you know how to do a proof sooner than later, and take advantage of ANY extra credit. They changed assignments from previous years, so the averages have been a little low.

Dr. Alford is an excellent professor that encourages class discussion, answers questions well, and cares about her students. Concepts for quizzes and tests are well telegraphed, and graded with partial credit. Content is very easy.
Too much homework, like 3 times more than my other cs class. No attendance but she has in class activities.

She is AWESOME!! I wish I could take all of my courses with her! she is caring, she is organize, she will tell you exactly what she really expects you for assignments. She will provide all the materials you need and answer to any question even silly ones very respectfully and in an interesting way!! I LOVE Her! she is amazing! highly recommended!!!

If you are comfortable with coding this class will be a breeze. There is no homework besides a few simple programs and finishing the lab assignments. There were lots of typos in her powerpoints but people would often correct her. The C++ part of the class was confusing because it was only covered in the lab but everything was pretty basic.

Absolutely love Prof. Alford. Class is very straight forward. Lecture and the occasional quizzes but she gives you practice quizzes beforehand that are very similar to the real thing so you're more than prepared for them. Midterm and final are 10-15 min oral tests where you explain/fix snippets of code that are same or similar to the ones in class

Prof Alford is an extremely caring person. She is so passionate about her field, and she genuinely wants you to succeed. Cares about her students and their well-being. Her class is tough but she will help you work through it. Very kind, very considerate. Overall a greatly inspiring experience.

Took CS 2240 with her for Spring 2020. Very kind and caring professor, and a solid lecturer. Probably one of the easiest profs to ask questions to, which helps a lot. If there's something you don't understand, tell her and she'll break everything down for you. However, the class (and particularly the lab) was a bit disorganized.

Very bad professor, barely reply to student email. Lecture was inconsistent so does her quizzes and exams. The mess she created cause the class to be harder. Sometime, I can tell she just want to rush the material and doesn't want to teach. Office hour session was useless. When you point out her mistake, she won't take it well personally.
Class is a mess, quiz answer key often incorrect. Professor and TA are never on the same page. Overall I wouldn't take again.

Dr. Ginger Alford is a really great prof. that cares a lot about students and how they perform in her class. Lectures are really straightforward and she does a FANTASTIC job at deconstructing difficult concepts, to the point where they seem remedial, to the point that some students think her classes are *too* easy. Very great educator.

Get ready to learn everything outside of class. Class was just practicing problems and they only way you could get a good grade was if you read the textbook and articles, watched his videos of the content, and spent hours studying for his exams. You also have no way of knowing what will actually be on the exams; the practice tests do not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although he really cares about preparing students for modern accounting. This is the worst class I have taken. Very little is taught in class, most is reading and self teaching. To stay up you need 4 hours a day 6 days a week. Tests take 50+ hours to study for and assignments are tedious and take 20+ hours. I do not recommend this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Had him for acct 2301 this past fall. He's amazing, and people who say otherwise are people who are not willing to put the work in for the class.

Accounting is hard, but if you put in the work, you will get what you want. He cares about your success and explains content well. Make sure you complete the homework and do pre-readings to be able to fully engage with the material in class.
Great, Prof. Class can be hard, but if you read beforehand, pay attention in class, and work the problems, you will do great. He is super helpful in class and office hours and has clear exepcations.

Sommers cares about his students and gives A LOT of resources to help you succeed. His lectures are fast paced tho so missing class isn't an option. I could've done better grade wise but I had extenuating circumstances. Overall, I say take his class, he knows what he's talking about and is clear about his expectations.

He is a great professor overall. He just goes through lecture slides kinda fast and overprepares us. Very available outside of class even though he is the dept chair and he genuinely cares about us and wants us to do well. He is very generous about giving half credit for exams if you got the idea right but the numbers wrong. Exams are also curved.

Genuinely the best professor i've had. He cares about his students success and is all around a great guy. Definitely a difficult class but he's by far the best teacher for this subject and theres honestly no one else I would take. Knows exactly what he's talking about and really tries to integrate it into everyones head, also is available for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ACCT 3415 was the worst class I've taken at SMU/Cox. It's advertised as streamlined for finance majors but, 95% Intermediate I/II material is included. The course is almost entirely self-taught. Class time is spent working problems with only answers & no explanation. Sommers is condescending even in office hours, and classmates regret taking this.

Is a good professor and genuinely nice, but is extremely strict and sets VERY high expectations like u should be able to get it on the first try or ur incompetent. Bad communicator, like he expects u to be a mind reader. Does offers curves which help a lot, tests and final are worth 80% and he locks grades so u cant see them until he updates it.

Mr. Sommers is an amazing professor, I really do not understand who is giving him bad reviews. Yes, the material is challenging but that's just the way it is. Professors exist to guide learning and understanding, not inject it into your head. He is caring, intelligent, and clearly hard-working. That's all you can really ask for in a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever graced at SMU. Arrogant, thinking he is some ivy league all achieving accounting teacher, when he really is a just a weird guy who likes to give a test every week. Not helpful when asking questions and makes your semester revolve ALL around his course !

Even if you're a hard worker, this class will still be extremely tough. All the exams take days to prep for, and there is one almost every 2 weeks. Barely anyone finishes the exams on time, and no one gets a 100 on the exam. The prep for this class is insane. Most of the time, you will be teaching yourself with little help from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Self important and disrespectful toward students. Hasn't adjusted his rigid teaching practices in years but is insulated because he is somehow the acc. chair. Made the class absolutely unbearable and overloaded students with so much material that no one actually retains any information from the class. Shouldn't be at SMU, but they won't do anything
male karen but worse
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a ton of reading but that's how you're supposed to learn the material (not in class). Do the textbook exercises before coming to class and everything makes sense in lecture. This class will enhance your understanding of accounting as it relates to finance. The exams are a combination of the textbook exercises and the review packets on Canvas.

This class is going to be hard regardless of professor so you have to go into this class knowing what your getting into. Sommers is very smart but also tough. However he is tough in the best interest of his students. Go to office hours and read the textbook!!

Sommers unnecessarily complicates this class. There are 5 tests, including an optional final, but his explanations make the material harder to understand. Review sessions before tests are unhelpful and often add to the confusion, making the class more challenging than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Greg seems to forget that not everyone is NICE and willing to let you join their study group. Greg always use to say, "who are you studying with"... the cliques stick together. Hard when you have him and the wannabe Finance bros.

If you are an Accounting major or a Finance major, he will make sure you know what you need to know. Yes the tests are hard, but if you want to be successful later in life, he will put you on the right track.

He is obvious very knowledgably of accounting, however he makes his class so much more difficult then it needs to be. His exams are worth 75% of your grade and very few people finish the exam on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid. It is impossible to keep up with the work, he is not helpful at all and you won't get proper feedback so you don't get to correct your mistakes, just take the B and go away is her attitude. Outright ugly to students when we ask for topic clarification, refuses to help.

Super hard class, every test takes days of preparation even if you understand the concepts as there are so many small details to pay attention to. He teaches quickly and sometimes with a confusing structure, but the material so much Im not sure if it could be taught differently. He gives advice to stay on track with the readings, id recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sommers is a nice person, but be prepared to teach yourself everything. He moved quickly in class and doesn't take the time to really explain (and when you ask him to he makes you feel like it's a burden). It's a ton of reading with not enough application practice.

Dr. Sommers is by no means an easy professor, partly because this course is inherently difficult. If you actually want to learn, you will. This class requires effort and hard work to succeed. He goes a little fast in his lectures but if you take good notes, you will understand by the time you self-study.

Sommers knows how the subject like the back of his hand and is great at explaining the concepts to beginners. His exams are tough IF YOU DON'T PRACTICE. If you study for 10-20 hours on avg. for each test, you will easily get an A. There is also 4% of extra credit and partial credit, and he is easily accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class lightweight, he taking some time off. But when he gets back rip it. So lighweight.
Horrible class. Exams are ridiculously difficult. Ridiculous amount of reading. He doesn't have lecture slides. Avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expect 2-3 hours of reading/prep before every class. Exams are extremely unfair, and he is inconsiderate and disrespectful to his students. Also, expect to learn everything independently; we were expected to learn several chapters despite not doing them in class. Take the other teacher for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was not as bad as I expected honestly, but be prepared to put in a lot of work. This class was definitely the hardest class I have taken in college so far. There is a lot of textbook reading and some of the material you have to learn yourself.

Intermediate 1 is extremely hard, and Prof. Sommers demands a lot of you - in order to understand the lectures (which are mostly just practice problems) you have to read 2-3 hours before every class. Prof. Sommers is a great teacher though, and answers questions very well. Just get ready to work.
I have WEEKLY meetings with my therapist due to the depression he has added to my life. AVOID. RUN FORREST RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor in SMU forever. Tests are extremely hard, even if you put in the effort, you cannot get a good grade.

Toughest class I have ever taken in college. However, if you put in the time and effort, it is possible to pass the class with a good grade. Almost every business major will have to take this at some point, so my advice is to start the class trying your hardest as the tests and assignments only get harder as you get deeper into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a tough teacher but passionate about accounting. Read the textbook for homework and attend class, each class is solely doing practice examples. While his tests are hard they are not unfair and there's no surprises. Along with tests there's also homework assignments to boost grades. He is one of the only professors in Cox I think you must have

Dr. Sommers is very knowledgeable and makes the material easy to understand. But you must do a lot of preparation, reading, and studying to pass his class. This is not an easy class. Be prepared for all the studying. On the exams, there are many problems that are hard to complete during the allotted time frame. use your free time to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Take the other professor for this course.

Dr. Sommers teaches a hard class; however, it's not that he is making the material difficult, it's that the material is that difficult on its own. He might not give you an easy A, but a teacher that truly cares about your retention of knowledge and future success will make you think in ways you have not. Show up, do the readings, and ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Sommers - he's truly a great guy and really cares about his students, but I highly recommend getting to know him and seeking out help if needed. The class is definitely difficult and took a lot of studying. Reading and attendance are absolutely crucial (he works problems in class). Actually loved the class but took a lot of work!

worst teacher ive ever witnessed in my life. does not give 2 sh**s about his students and his nipples are always sticking out through his shirt. id rather suck a dude off than take this guy again. I have no idea how he is not fired from the school yet
Ridiculous amount of reading. You basically have to teach yourself everything in this class.

Sommers is one of the best teachers on campus and his negative reviews are only from students who couldn't handle the difficulty. He has clear expectations and excellent lectures. I have learned more from this class than any of my other classes. If you are serious about your education, you won't regret taking him.

Dr. Sommers is a nice guy and tries his best to teach students the material but he makes the class really hard. His test are ridiculous hard and long around 15-16 written questions in 50 minutes. He's also a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sommers is a great professor and explains the concepts well. However, the class is so interesting and fun that it is worth it, and there is a lot of material to make your essays with. If you have time to commit, take him
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Every page read, every essay written, every discussion had is completely, entirely WORTH IT. Take this course!!!

Professor Halperin is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He has an encyclopedic knowledge of the subject, and has many personal experiences which are related. If you're interested in the subject matter, definitely take the course. That said, if you're taking the class just for Gen ed reqs or for an easy A, look elsewhere. Too much homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's always available to talk. He's one of those eccentric and brilliant professors that has a lot to say. There are books and papers piled from floor to ceiling in his office- he is very knowledgeable and reads a lot. His course material was a lot of reading and the subject is grim, but it was a worthwhile class to take. He is now my advisor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Awesome

This man is the reason I'm a HRTS major. He gives unprepared lectures because he knows so much. He is internationally known for his HRTS work and was chair of Amnesty Int'l. He has a wealth of knowledge and is tremendously down to earth. Hes putting SMU on the map. Prepare for lots of reading and writing. He is very accessible so go to office hours

No clear guidelines on grading, had no rubric for the class, simply put grades down on the papers, with no feedback (at most I ever saw was a one sentence feedback). There were NO connections to the readings in class. He simply assigned books, with no discussion or connection to class work. Never let us out on time,  disrespectful of students.

He is for sure the best professor I have taken yet.  I would not take his class if writing papers are hard for you b/c 7 page paper/week.   I never read or watched any of the films required but in order to get good grades you need to add a lot of quotes from them in your papers.  Focus on the terms written on the board and you will be fine.

If you actually do all of the work that you are supposed to do in this class, such as reading about a book a week and watching 4 movies a week, you would have no time for other classes. Somewhat of a hard grader on papers and the quizzes are impossible. Provides very little clarity into what he expects on assignments which makes the class difficult

Only take this class if you're passionate about human rights. There is a lot of work and he is a very tough grader, but if you love the subject then the class is amazing. He is the most inspirational person I have ever met and really cares about his students.
Best professor I have ever taken at SMU. Inspired me to declare a Human Rights major.

Professor Halperin's Human Rights course was the best class I ever took at SMU. He is so engaging and his passion for what he is teaching really shines through. I would HIGHLY recommend this class to any student who loves learning. It will transform the way you  look at the world, and transform it for the better!

Dr. Halperin is the best. He knows his stuff. This is not a class you take if you are not a serious student. This was a life changer. I have never worked as hard for another class. Loved him. Going with him to Poland in Dec.

EVERYONE should take this class. He's incredibly difficult, but incredibly intelligent. Respectful of everyone's opinions, willing to engage in discussion, and endlessly knowledgeable. Went to Poland with him over Winter Break and that, combined with this class, changed the entire way I looked at life. Don't be afraid of a challenge.

If you get stuck in this class don't buy the books, you never use them. He knows plenty about human rights & could make this a great class; however, he doesn't. He never gives you concrete assignments, grades strictly, & is just completely unorganized. The whole class is him talking about how horrible humans are (no powerpoints) Too many readings.

I took his Human Rights course and I loved it!  He is great speaker and the class is never boring!  Lots of reading and time outside of class is required.  This is a class that requires a lot from you.  Do not take if you have many challenging classes. He requires 20 hours of community service and their are 17 books,videos, many papers and project
This course opened my eyes to things I never even imagined.  I highly support this course and think you should check it out for a CF or History requirement.

Awesome teacher I love him! But it's a tough class, lots of reading, be prepared. Better to take this class during the summer. It's a big course load but it's well worth the effort that you put into it. He changes lives.
Tons of reading, but a life changing class.  Instructor is hot which is an added bonus.
He does a good job of respecting other peoples' opinions.  Assigns too much work (here's a tip, take it in the summer) but is definitely an enlightening class to take.
Halperin is one of the rare jewels among the SMU professors.  We are lucky to have him and this class will impact your life in one way or another.  But there is A TON OF READING - BE READY!!
Way too human rights oriented.  Very much a liberal and very much a amnesty international kind of guy.  Knows his stuff if you dig this type of rhetoric.
I had Rick as a professor and counselor over 8 years ago. He is the BEST! So glad to see everyone still loves him. Such an asset to SMU. Anyone who takes his classes is blessed by the experience.
Take this class.  It might change your life.  He makes you think about the world and care.  You will work hard but it will be worth your time. He has a passion for what he teaches.
Very dedicated too human rights..and knows his ****..take him for sure.

assigns ALOT of books (13+) but you dont really have to read them if you pay attention in lecture. you can learn alot from him if you try. make sure that you have a news article for EVERY SINGLE DAY for the journal.
A TON of reading but I learned a lot.
Extremely demanding but well worth it--Everyone at SMU should take this class
Loved Professor Hollifield! He's super knowledgeable, and although there's a quiz pretty much every day, they're doable. As long as you study and actually put in effort, you'll be fine.
Very interesting class. If you have the time and you put in the effort, you will get an A.
Nooooooooooooooooooooooooooo.

I really enjoyed Prof. Hollifield. He is super knowledgable, gives great feedback, and gives good grades when their deserved and isn't mean about it. Although there is a lot of readings and quizzes, as long as you just read and look at his lecture notes, you'll be fine. Getting an A is manageable, you just have to put in some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Old school politically incorrect professor with a good heart and humorous personality. Well respected and connected in the field of academia which allows him to ground a lot of what he is teaching in his own experiences. Can see how some people would not like his style of teaching though.

He's really not that bad. Extremely knowledgeable and an expert in his field. Can be pretentious at times, but he was always accessible when I emailed and went to office hours. Nowhere near the hardest polisci professor and an interesting guy. Go to class and put effort in and you can totally get an A.

Not enough words in the dictionary to express how you couldn't pay me to take him again. Course content would be far more interesting if he wasn't a prick abt teaching it. Reading quizzes at least once, sometimes 2x a week. Missing class isn't an option. You can end this class with either a good grade or your sanity & will to live, NOT both. GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: UGH just NOOOOOOOO

He knows a lot of words but "humility" is not one of them, never met a more arrogant human being, sinfully talks about his "accomplishments" which amount to a standard 30 year career, none of which lends toward being a good professor, which is what he should now be focusing on. Terrible grading, horrible class time use, do not take.
As a 4.0 student, I know a good professor when I see one no matter how tough they are, and he is nowhere near a decent one.

Professor Hollifield is very knowledgeable and loves to lecture. He is fairly demanding of students (a lot of information to know from like 4+ textbooks) but tbh I think he's alright. There are short quizzes towards the end of most classes, 2 exams, and a paper. He also offers a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Hollifield is obviously super smart, but his teaching style is not conducive to a great learning environment. The lectures are long, the homework is never-ending, and quizzes are TBD every class. Start your research paper early, start studying early, and pray. This class is hard, and he expects students to know everything. You must self-study!

He's incredibly smart, no question there. Just not very clear about how he grades, you don't get a tentative view of your overall grade until the end of November. Unclear on how much quizzes and extra credit count, and even if you get positive feedback in office on essays, you probably won't get an A.Quizzes are 20 questions, hard,w/ 10 min limit.

Clearly, Professor Hollifield has a prolific career in foreign affairs, but this does not translate into being a great teacher. He's a nice guy, but he can come across as condescending with his lofty stories about France and England. Participation is 30% and the exams are hit-or-miss, even if you read. Make sure to ask him what he's looking for.

decent lecturer, a little scattered brain at times. good thing about this class is you get a lot of extra credit opportunities. but grading scheme can be really confusing especially not knowing what he expects on papers. exam arent hard so long you come to class and read. can be witty at times
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Hollifield's lectures are very entertaining and informative. He always has really cool personal stories from his own travels he incorporates into class. He always goes over the materials in the quiz (daily quiz) during the lecture; I stopped reading after the first month and made an A. Go to class, pay attention, and you'll be fine.

Hollifield is fine as a professor, but will be grating on your nerves by the end. He loves talking about himself and his accomplishments, the trips he's going on and the big wigs he's friends with. It gets old. I would not have taken him if I didn't need the class to graduate - I've heard his section is still MUCH better than the other teacher's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He really knows his stuff and he's very accomplished in his career. However, his class is just him lecturing and it's often rather unorganized. He goes over all the materials on the quiz before we take it.

He knows a ton about European politics, and the only people who actually do poorly in his class are the ones who don't do any of the reading. How shocking that a professor would expect you to at least read for an upper level political science course.

Really loves to speak French to his confused class, brag about his Harvard 'colleagues,' and raises his voices randomly during lectures. Get past all this (and the fact he only teaches at 8 am) and what are you left with? The rare professor who can speak about modern and historical world economics and politics with passion, insight, and clarity.

I did learn a lot from the course, but his arrogance would deter me from wanting to take him again. If your German or French tell him, especially if you can speak/read it. He gloats over his awesomeness nonstop which is annoying, but overall I enjoyed learning as much as I did in his class.
Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at SMU.  His lectures are all over the place and make no sense.  It's also nearly impossible to get an A in this class.  Would NOT recommend him.

Dr. Hollifield is one of the most brilliant professors at SMU.  If you attend his class, participate, and apply a bit of effort, it is the most enlightening and informative class you will take at SMU.  And NOT as hard/bad as some of this other reviews purport. He puts world events into a proper context, and it is extremely fascinating.

Can't keep to the syllabus at all, quite arrogant. The quizzes are really easy but the mid-term/final/paper definitely aren't. You'll also have to listen to him gush about his German colleagues all through the class.
the class was completely unorganized and hard to follow. the course would have been interesting, however I do not recommend taking him for any class.
Hollifield is awesome. I had him for a few classes, always learned a lot and he is easy to get along with.
One of the best professors I have ever had.  Knowledgable, friendly, and passionate.  Don't graduate without taking at least one of his classes!

Hollifield is an alright guy, but he comes off as being very arrogant in class (which eventually becomes irritating).  He didn't follow the lecture outlines well and kept speaking to the class in French.  Also, be prepared to learn about how great his "colleages" at Harvard are.
No Comments

She is better than the other BLI teachers. Very reasonable with but she does have to grade picky for the class. Good amount of busy work to boost up grade if done correctly. If you are not good at presenting prepare yourself.
Great professor. She will work with you outside of class time. She has a very strict grading system, but once you learn it, you'll do great. I hated the reading quizzes.
Decent professor, but nothing extraordinary. Very picky when it comes to grading your presentations or other large assignments, so be prepared for those.

She cares about your success and is super understanding. She has great lectures, which create a great classroom environment. Everything that is listed in the syllabus is exactly what you'll receive, and her organization makes this one of the easiest classes I've taken.

Really nice professor and grades presentations pretty easily as long as you follow the rubric. Also gives very detailed feedback on presentations. Not too much outside of class work, for reading quizzes, there were a lot of chapters. Some of the work felt like busy-work, but overall easy class.

She is knit picky during presentations and comes across as a tough grader but she curves a lot at the end of the semester. She is a really nice and genuine professor who wants the best for all of her students.
This person is allergic to clarity. Vibes-based grading, passive-aggressive announcements, and lectures that felt like spoken word performances about their personal trauma. Iconically terrible.
This course was a psychological experiment to see how much nonsense one person can endure for 3 credit hours. The answer: not enough.

This class is very easy if you just do what is asked of you. Not a hard grader for presentations and there is a very clear rubric. Assignments throughout the semester are not hard. Extra credit for perfect attendance.

Most of your grade is based on 3 presentations, along with two quizzes on required readings (which I would recommend not procrastinating on). She gives helpful feedback and is clear about expectations. My only complaints are her lectures can drown on a bit and she's a bit of a harsh grader for presentations but its a laid back class most days.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring teacher, I did bad on my first presentation and she was able to work with me outside of class and give me a ton of helpful advise that helped me bounce back and do well on all other assignments. Would def recommend.
Absolutely hated this woman and what a colossal waste of time this course is.

The class is presentation-based based with you having a 2 min presentation, a 4 min one, and then a 10 min group presentation at the end. Just two quizzes based on the books for the class, and they're about presentation and communication skills. There's typically an in-class assignment but it is simple. Gives you an overview of the business school.

Quite a few lectures at the beginning of the semester but after that it is mainly presentation based. Just follow her instructions as closely as possible and you will get a good grade. Almost no homework and what little you have usually takes less than an hour.

You need to pay attention to the quizzes because there are so few assignments. She has great points and is a great presenter and is nitpicky about how you present, but it will make you better. Anything she says to you, take it because she is very smart and wants to be there for you as a teacher. Overall, great class somewhat difficult but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mcllvain is a great teacher. Her class is fairly easy and she teaches students useful stuff they should know for the future. The only thing I would say that is a bit difficult is the solo presentations. Even though the presentations were scary, I think they've helped me become a better speaker.I highly would recommend taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My favorite teacher in my first semester at SMU. Very clear about expectations and fair grading system. Reading the material matters for quizzes and actually learning to present well, so make sure you do the work and you'll leave with an A

It is a communications class so you will be presenting. Prof McIlvain always had feedback to give and we also got peer feedback. She records the presentations which allows you to look back at how you present

Great teacher for the course. Easy grader if it is clear you put time and effort in. If you struggle with public speaking I reccommed talking to her after the first class and she will grade you easier. The more improvement you show, the better she will grade you. DO the extra credit!! It will save your final grade and it is really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gotta go to class because obv its BLI, she's pretty nice overall and the work isnt too bad. Just make sure to follow the speech outlines to a T, as she grades heavy on if you follow the outline regardless of how good your speech was.

Show up to class and definitely practice for your presentations. She offers some extra credit, and it's very possible to do well in the class. She is super chill during lectures. Also takes the time to give good feedback, so even if you don't like public speaking, she likes to see progression.
Great professor, class is pretty boring but straightforward. Be ready to present 3 times during the semester, she will grade you strictly. Show up to class, present, and you'll make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet professor! Honestly do the work, stick to the rubric, and you'll 100% be fine. Should not be hard to get an A in this class if you simply just do the work. Two solo presentations and then a final group presentation. I think there are 2 quizzes for the full course, which aren't hard. Just make sure you get the book and you'll be fine.

super nice and very chill teacher. class is pretty much lectures with very little homework (2 50 question quizzes, both open note and a few big presentations). attendance is mandatory but you can just chill and still do great in the class. would def recommend

She will always stick to the rubric, so if you follow it you'll do well. If not, you won't. Attendance is -5/25 every time you miss class unexcused. The 2 quizzes will make or break your grade. Download the HBT books online for the quizzes.

McIlvain doesn't make BLI less boring, but at least the grading is lenient. The quizzes come from the textbook verbatim, and as long as your written assignments align with the rubric, you'll be fine. For presentations, she'll give you an A if you smile, appear confident, and talk about something goofy. Participate somewhat regularly too.

As long as you follow the rubric and presentation guidelines, you should be fine. Following the rubric shows the effort you put into the presentations and that you are engaged in class. I would consider her a fair/easy grader with straightforward expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. McIlvain is a good professor. She teaches clearly and if you put in effort, you'll get an A in the class. Don't completely write this class off though. There are two take home quizzes, three presentations and assigned reading. She is a somewhat harsh grader when it comes to presentations but she cares about her students' success. Take her!

This class was super boring, but it wasn't hard. If you're a good public speaker, you will probably do great. I didn't really learn anything from her lectures on public speaking, but the presentations themselves actually did push me to be a better speaker, especially since she gives good feedback.

She is a good presenter and gives good feedback, if your a not good at presenting then prepare to practice extra hard because she will not grade nicely you just for trying. Fun class and a good way to practice professional skills.

Very nice professor that gives you all the resources needed to do well in the class. Impossible to get below a B if you just put in a little bit of effort. She'll go over assignments if you show them to her. Stick to the rubric as she follows that religiously. Only reason I did't get an A is because I didn't read the grading rubric on an assignment

She sticks to the rubrics for grading, so always look at those. For just a BLI class, she makes you put in a lot of effort, and the reading/lectures get a little repetitive, but she is very supportive regarding presentations. You'll pass with an A if you put in the effort, attend class, and have her check over some assignments before submission.

Professor McIlvain is very nice but too tough on grades. This class should be an easy A but small things easily bring you down such. I would try to take a different professor but no hard feelings towards Hilary.

She's a good professor. Quizzes are open note- You can't go back, so you're stuck with what you choose. Class is primarily made up of three presentations (short intro, persuasive, and group). My main issue is she can be a tough grader. Sometimes you put in a lot of effort and get a lower grade than you hoped. Feedback is constructive and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the nicest and most caring professors at SMU. Gives you all the resources needed to get an A in her class. The class is impossible to get below a B let alone fail. She makes the class worthwhile and is always open to help in any way she can

McIlvain as a professor is alright. Unfortunately, the class she teaches (which is required by Cox) is really boring. Most classes you'll be sitting and listening with the occasional presentation you have to give to the class. It is pretty easy, and mostly just a show up and do it class, so professor doesn't weigh too much. Follow the rubrics.

Professor McIlvain is knowledgeable in her field and has amazing lectures. The class can feel tedious at times since some things seem like common sense but the information is important to make yourself better for the business setting.

I love Professor McIlvain. She is so caring and you can tell she really wants to prepare her students has best she can for the business school. She grades fairly and gives great feedback on what you should do to improve on your presenting. Only 2 reading quizzes but you don't read you won't do well on them but a lot of room to make up grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Grade is mostly based on presentations and she gives tons of feedback. Really kind lady and there is barely any homework. A few open book reading quizzes but they're not that hard. She is pretty good at making her lectures engaging even though it's not the most interesting subject ever. Just prepare for presentations ahead of time, she's amazing

Most of the semester was presentations. Professor tried making the class fun and relevant to our future. She can be a tough grader so expect to get a couple of Bs even if you were a straight-A student. She even gave us a class period to work on our group project.

Class is not bad at all. Just follow directions and the rubric and you will do well. Presentations take up the last half of the semester so if you are not presenting, it is pretty relaxed. She likes participation. Tough grader on written assignments but very nice and tries to make class fun when she can. She even brought us tacos one time!

Dr. Johnston does care about her students! Because CHEM 1303 is a beginner chemistry class, she gives up to 10 points extra credit. Expect tests to be much harder than homework and practice problems assigned. Redo practice a million times! Really grasp onto all the material learned throughout the semester, as the final exam is a kicker!
Awesome teacher! Super accessible outside of class and always willing to help. If you put the work in you can definitely achieve whatever grade you are aiming for.

Dr. Johnston was a great professor. She was always accessible outside of class, whether it be by email or office hours. Lectures are all powerpoints, but she explains everything very well. Exams are most of your grade, but she replaces your lowest exam grade if your final exam grade is higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good professor. The class is tough, so be prepared to study a lot outside of class. It's chemistry though, so you should be prepared to work hard.
Who gave this lady a teaching credential and better yet who let her at SMU? Stop this disaster.
Lectures were recycled from a decade ago and still managed to make less sense than TikTok conspiracy theories. Grading was rude, feedback was useless, and deadlines moved like mirages. Avoid.
Dr. J is a really great professor. Chem is just hard. She provides ample resources and genuinely wants you to succeed. I hated Chem but I'd take her again if I needed to.
A terrible edition to the department.

People saying Johnston talks about herself and whatever is just untrue she genuinely never spent class time doing that. Regardless, she is a great teacher and walks thru problems step by step. she has practice tests and so many practice problems available, just need to take advantage of them. gen chem 2 is HARD regardless but she makes it doable
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A bad experience overall. spends more energy on being liked than actually teaching, shutting down opposing viewpoints in the process. You leave the class feeling like you've gained nothing

She explained all the concepts super clearly and showed every step. Attendance wasn't graded, but if you go and listen to every lecture you'll do fine. She also gives practice exams before the real tests which are super helpful.

The class feels like an ego trip for her, spends lectures talking about self, desperate for approval from students it's unprofessional and detracts from the subject. With no real research background, her teaching lacks depth and is exhausting to sit through.

Dr. Johnston is great, explains concepts thoroughly and genuinely wants students to learn. She provides lots of resources for test prep which resemble a lot of the questions tests and the tests are always reasonable. Highly recommend!!

The class is great. The subject matter is hard, but she gives good explanations if you pay attention. She is very willing to help during office hours and wants you to do well. The tests are hard, but she gave a mock test before that was almost identical. If you put in the work and go to class, it is very practical to get an a.

I feel bad for people who don't have a professor like her honestly. She teaches chemistry in a way that makes it so easy to understand and has many resources to study for exams. She gives more homework than some of my other professors but they are taken for completion and honestly don't much of an impact on your grade if you miss one.

Chemistry itself is awful, but Dr. Johnston does a wonderful job at teaching it. There are four exams, a cumulative final, and about 2 pieces of homework from the textbook each week that are participation grades. There's a reason why her classes fill up so fast, so if you can, definitely take her.

Just a hard class/subject but Johnston is definitely the best prof. Answers questions in & out of class and has previous exams and practice materials on Canvas before all the tests except the final. Attendance isn't mandatory but unless u know chemistry you should def go. Lectures from a powerpoint that's on Canvas you can download to follow along.

If you're taking chem at SMU Johnston is the BEST. Homework is light and graded on completion. Tests are difficult (chem in general) but she walks through tons of examples and is a very good lecturer. Highly recommend. Also she provides tons of practice tests before the real thing.

She is a very sweet lady, she does her best to teach chem but chem takes dedicated time outside of class. She is always available for office hours, and she truly does try to help her students succeed. Homework is weekly but is completion and 4 tests. She has 2 diff. grading schemes to get u the best grade. Get the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Dr. Johnston for lecture and lab, and she's honestly so sweet and great at teaching. Such a lovely professor, I just hate lab. That's not her fault though, I took it with another professor a previous semester and I can say that she makes it a little less miserable. Do the practice problems and you'll get an A, I just didn't care enough to try.

Dr. Johnston is great! This is my third time taking a class with her (two labs and lecture). She is very helpful in office hours and genuinely wants students to succeed. I highly recommend taking her classes.

Professor Johnston is by far my favorite chemistry professor. She provided great feedback on the homework and exams, and she genuinely cared for her students. She seemed very passionate about her job and chemistry in general, she was very knowledgeable and answered questions inside and outside the classroom. Definitely recommend her!
Her lecture slides are awesome. Got "A-" without ever attending her class. lol. She does not prepare you for the exams. Her office hours are always packed. Overall, she tries for her students.

Dr. Johnston was the best!! I had her for lecture and lab and she was always available to meet whenever I needed help. Gen chem is hard but you definitely want her as your teacher. Her slides are well organized and she provides way more helpful material than the other chem teachers here. Take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnston is such a great professor! I had her for both lecture and lab, and she was super helpful in both. She is clearly very knowledgeable about chemistry, and I hope that I can take another class with her in the future.

The class is very lecture heavy and can get boring at times. She moves a bit too swiftly on some topics during lecture and the class isn't very engaging. However, as a professor, she's very kind and caring, and will re-explain topics if you ask. Had her for the lab CHEM-1113 and she was great there too.
Love her. She's extremely helpful during the lab. Material can be a bit hard but she's available to help during office hours. I had a lot of fun in her lab. Grading is straightforward and fair.

I was in a horrible accident during her class and she was not understanding at all about my situation. I expressed my concern about not being able to pass her class and she basically shrugged her shoulders over email. I will say she is quick to respond to emails and the tests that I was prepared for were close enough to material she lectured on.

She is AWESOME! My favorite chem professor that I've had so far. She is a bit of a tough grader, but if you are ever confused or struggling with anything in lab she is more than happy to help. I've been sick a couple times, but labs are undroppable and she had me come in to take the quiz and do the actual lab online at home. She's so nice!

Gen Chem is a hard class, but Dr. Johnston has really nice, organized slides that make her lectures easy to follow. She is really kind and accessible outside of class for questions and help. The material is hard, but I think she is a good professor to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My big take away from the class is you want Hannah Johnston as your professor. Chem is a hard class no matter which professor you get, you are going to have to study and put in a decent about of time. However, Hannah has great lectures and covers the content really well. She is also super accessible outside of the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class. Great teaching styles. Great overall person.

Best math professor you can take for this course. I would consider him the GOAT. Caring and makes lectures funny with his jokes. If you follow the class examples and do the homework you'll do fine in this class.
Great professor. Would definitely take him again!

Best Business Calc Professor at SMU. Quiz ever Friday over the singular hw from the week. Gives very representative study guides for the exams. He is nice, funny, cares about his students, so If you have to take business calc I would highly recommend him.

Best Business Calc Professor at SMU. Quiz ever Friday over the singular hw from the week. Gives very representative study guides for the exams. He is nice, funny, cares about his students, so If you have to take business calc would highly recommend him.

Best business calculous professor at SMU. Quizzes every Friday, but its over what the single hw of the week is on, and those quizzes help you actually learn the material. Gives a very representative study guide for exams. He is super nice, funny, so if you have to take a business calculous class I would highly recommend him.

Dr. Soroko is the GOAT, and he knows it. Before he even walks in the room you feel is aura. Seriously he will probably be one of the best Calc teachers you can take. Thick Russian accent, but still easy to understand overall. He wants to make sure that everyone is paying attention so if you want to slack off take someone else... otherwise take him.
Not as nice as he tries to be if he doesnt' like you.

I actually have never dreaded going to this class. It is extremely easy as long as you show up and watch the movies. He wants you to do well but you HAVE to talk in class for participation. There are also two presentations but they are easy.
The professor does not create a supportive learning environment. Questions are not addresses, students are left wihtout resources or explanation needed to grasp the material.

I really enjoyed this class and how dedicated Dr. Icleanu is to his students. He was very open-minded and only challenged us to think beyond ourselves. As long as you watch the movies and participate in class, you should have no problem getting an A. Attendance is mandatory, so if you do not like attending class, this course may not be for you.

I am not quite sure how there are any bad reviews on here for Professor Icleanu. He is about as helpful and forgiving as professors come and he wants nothing more than to see you learn and succeed. In class, movie quizzes are 3 questions and very easy. One test on the movies, but it's more of a check-in. Amazing professor, would take again for sure

Talks a lot about personal life rather than the material, makes being in class uncomfortable, seems to want attention rather than to be teaching, rushes through material like even he doesn't want to be in class.

super sweet! willing to chat after class. I sent in multiple EC opportunities and they were all approved. happy to discuss your grade. I missed a BUNCH of assignments for personal reasons and was still able to turn them all in for almost full credit. lectures are not super relevant, just do the reading and you'll be fine! 9 excused absences!

I took him for SPAN 3373, but that wasn't an option. He's easy to reach outside of class. He gives a clear study guide the day before the exam. The only thing is that he talks over the other professor, Dupont, occasionally. Other than that, he's a great professor who wants you to pass.

reviews.comment: This class was by far the most interesting and engaging. It's a chilled class. The homework is straightforward and to the point. You watch a film and answer a few questions about it. The midterm is also based on the films (easy A), with no final exam. This class was interesting as an international student because it's about immigration.
One of the best professors, I've had. Always available for his students outside of class and wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought this was posted earlier, sorry about a late post. Professor Icleanu was an amazing professor whom I truly enjoyed for 1401 and 1402. I hope that everyone has as an amazing of a professor as Icleanu is at least once during their time at SMU!
Avoid this professor. Spends more time on personal anecdotes than teaching. Doesn't respect student time, cancels classes last minute. Total waste of resources.

I took this professor for SPAN 1401 & 1402. He was a fantastic professor. He cares about his students and gives good feedback on all assignments. All grading criteria are very clear. reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs, professor is condescending, lacks empathy. Makes learning a chore, don't subject yourself to this educational torture.

I have taken Professor Icleanu for both 1401 and 1402 now and I would highly recommend doing the same. In lecture, Icleanu is very informative and spends time breaking down the chapter content driven by class participation. He is caring, understanding, humorous, and truly wants you to be your best. I would highly recommend Professor Icleanu.

Hardest part of his class was sitting through her pointless lectures which seemed to take forever, all going on pointless tangents . I felt I could of grown a beard in the time it took to for him to finish his confusing lectures. and he takes peoples leaving to go to the bathroom personal and has even stopped class and waited for their return.
THE GOAT!!!!!!! Lots of homework, but class is very easy if you just do the work.

The professor was great, and I appreciated his efforts to encourage open-mindedness towards various perspectives. Despite it being a summer course, and having daily assignments, he made it very engaging. Outside of class, you can expect to dedicate a significant amount of time to reading and watching films.

Professor Icleanu was my FAVORITE professor. He goes out of his way to keep everyone engaged, he explains everything really well, he is funny, and he plays a lot of games with us. He genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching. You will not regret taking his class. He was incredible.

Professor Constantin Icleanu is one of the best professors I have ever had!  He is very nice and wants you to succeed in the class. There is homework every day, but they are not hard. I would highly recommend taking him.

reviews.comment: Best professor at SMU. If you are taking Spanish, take his class. He is really funny, and we play games in class every single day. He loves teaching and cares about his students. If you put in a little work your gonna do well. Very understanding.

Professor Icleanu is a pretty cool, no, REALLY cool. He does an excellent job teaching and it's very clear that he is passionate about his job. You learn a lot in his class yet the class still remains to be fun and incredibly interactive. You will have online homework every night but it's not bad. Overall great professor if not one of the best @SMU
This professor is the best Spanish teacher for 1402. Clear Grading and wants you to get an A. Great guy! Take him!

One of my favorite professors! Take it!
There's usually a lot of reading or material you have to watch before class. The professor is great and gives timely feedback on your essays. If you put in the work, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is such a nice professor!! The class is really easy, and he does his best to engage with the students by playing games. There is a lot of homework on Vistas, but it is quick and easy. He is really forgiving when it comes to writing assignments. The tests are really easy and straightforward if you study.
Super nice guy and genuinely cares about his students. Makes it clear what's going to be on tests & what to write for papers. Easy grader and plenty of extra credit.

Great professor! This is my 3rd semester with him. Participation plays a large role in this class. If you show up and contribute, you should have no problem getting an A. He cares about his students and listens to feedback from students. Overall, he gives interesting lectures and is an easy grader.

I can feel his passion from the lecture and he really wants us to participate and discuss in the class. A lot of materials to read and films to watch, time consuming but inspirational. When you receive a very low grade, go talk to him and see what's the problem, he might give you a redo chance. He's also pretty open to different ideas.
