reviews.comment: Some people love him, others hate him. This should be a pretty straightforward class when it comes to sports business. He posts all the lectures and the tests aren't that bad. Just make sure you do your Twitter and LinkedIn engagement to get easy credit. Group projects will be difficult because no one cares so be aware of that. Overall super chill
A waste of a class and my time and money. We should stop paying on professor's salaries like these.
Has a strong no friends kind of vibe

Awesome guy. He is very passionate about what he does and he makes the class fun. A lot of the time you will just sit there and do other class homework, but super easy class. He is a good grader, fun projects, very light. i would recommend this class to anybody.

This class is a great introduction to the principles of sports management. Do the work and come to class prepared and you will succeed. Possible exam questions are posted ahead of time. Pretty easy grading for case studies and group projects. Definitely lecture heavy but material is easy to understand and apply.
great teacher highly recommend.

Loved this professor! He is very passionate about his career and classes he teaches! He also will do everything he can to help you network or get the internship or job you want! Very understanding to his students and knowledgeable in his field.

Can be exceptionally unkind to students. The lectures feel like hours and it's hard to pay attention because he speaks so boringly. Literally no help at all, hateful when you ask for help, so you need to study on your own.

Great professor overall. Easily the best professor in the sport management department at SMU. He cares about his students and is very flexible even just a few days before things are due. He always offers extra credit opportunities and helps give students volunteer opportunities that he is given outside of class.
My man. Easy, low key, no real work requirements - this is the guy for us all.
Very friendly and very easy going. Willing to work with students to help them succeed. Easy work load and incredible class to take if you are interested in this subject.

Professor Troupe is my favorite professor. He is very supportive and gives amazing advice. I would 100% take him again. He brings in the best of the best speakers. He has 4 quizzes and they are really easy and he has 2 exams which are not bad at all. Homework is on the lighter side.

Great guy who always makes himself available to students. Class is very interesting if you are into sports, if not might be boring. I would put this class on the lighter side in terms of homework load. 3 tests, but graded assignments like quizzes pretty often.

Professor Zimakova is one of my favorite professors at SMU, she is very caring and helpful and uses her time in class to teach you not just about the Russian language, but also culture. One of my favorite classes I have taken at SMU and I actually was able to read and speak in Russian.

Caring professor and is very passionate about sharing her culture and language. She encourages students to get acquainted and is inclusive in her classes. There are so many assignments but she's happy to help. I've had to reach out to her a few times throughout the semester and she is quick to respond. Very helpful, caring, and her classes are fun.

Taking Russian with Professor Zimakova has been a highlight of my time at SMU. She is so kind and caring and willing to help when the concepts are tough. Class is a good variety of reading, writing, presentations, and conversation. I've loved having her as a professor.

I LOVE Dr. Zimakova! I've taken her for a few semesters now and she's the best. She is very passionate about teaching Russian and the culture, and she only really wants you to exceed. There is a decent amount of homework, but she's also is pretty relaxed on the deadlines. Definitely recommend!

SHE IS AMAZING. I have taken her for 3 semester and she cares so much about her students. Yes you do assignments but they are simple and done in class and she offers many chances for corrections. Easy A if you participate

Dr.Zimakova is an excellent professor. I have been taking her class for the third semester in a row, she's nothing but the best. Do your homework and stay on top of what you are supposed to do, and you will receive a good grade. Most of the bad reviews are from students who expected an easy grade without doing any work. She's truly awesome.

Prof. Zimakova's class has an emphasis on learning. She allows you to correct mistakes and submit corrections.  There was a lot of homework and reading but that is what comes with a language class. Her class was an amazing learning experience, truly.
Can't say enough bad things about this class. However bad you think it could be trust me it's worse. She was the worst teacher Ive ever had. I beg you whatever you do at SMU don't take her class.
Highly recommend this class. It is a great class to take and to fulfill your language requirement.
Russian 1402 have been an amazing class with Professor Zimakova and I learned so many details of Russian culture and language. Thank you for teaching this class, can't wait to sign up for next.
Not worth your time of day. You'd be better off independently reading. And by all means, do not submit a story as the final paper. She doesn't even read them.
The midterm and finals are ridiculously hard and you have to be able to identify works between poetry and fiction, the author, and who is speaking.

Dr. Zimakova is a very caring person. She's very passionate about Russia and truly spreads this enthusiasm about her nation - make sure to ask her about her life! There is lots of homework and class can sometimes be boring (even she said so once), but she is INCREDIBLY relaxed on grading - she understands how difficult it is to learn a new language

I really enjoyed her Russian Culture class. I found the readings and films to be interesting and the assignments, papers, and presentations were very manageable. Really interesting class! I definitely recommend her!
Not the best teacher at smu. very disorganized in the second semester. would avoid taking again. Hard on tests without any feedback and no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Take this class! Super fun and nice teacher. As long as you show up and do the work, you will get a good grade. She makes the class enjoyable.

Super sweet lady. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about Russian culture. This class is super easy if you study once in a while. She goes over the same chapter for weeks until you really understand it. She also is very lenient on due dates. Take this class, you'll stand out from the rest of the undergrads just taking spanish!
If you need to fulfill your language requirement, then take this class. You will learn a lot and you will have a lot of fun. Shes one of my favorite teachers at SMU.

Literally the nicest lady in the world - I really wish SMU would expand the Russian department because she teaches literally every class and she tries so hard to keep it alive. Our class had regular outings and gatherings (with her!) and so we all bonded so well. If you're not interested in Russian at all before, you will be interested by the end.
Love her. If you don't like foreign languages and are looking for to meet the lang requirements then take Russian.
took 1401 and the CF -- studied abroad in Moscow w/her. LOVE HER!!! Coolest, nicest prof in the world...ever. She just wants you to learn...period.
Amazing.. simply amazing
easiest class at school to get an A in.. so relaxed, you learn it surprisingly quickly after the alphabet which really is not that hard
WOW
Great professor. I highly recommend her
Awsome professor

Very easy, understanding, helpful, ... If you do not do well on the exam or homework you will always have another chance to re-do it. Her grading is very easy but you still get a lot out of her class. Classes are usually interesting. I recommend her to everybody, she is fun!
Great teacher. Makes an intimidating language fun and easy to learn. I would highly recommend her class.

The concept of the class is great however his class is WAY harder than it needs to be grading wise. Take Gwinn instead bc there is no reason u should be doing worse that the other sections of ITOM. Just dont waster your time and energy in this class. Should be an easy A, but he prevents that. He does teach good skills, but is not easily accessible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty much no one gets an a, or an a- he doesn't curve, and the averages on the exams are around 75. dont take him if u want a decent gpa

Absolute legend. The criteria is challenging but he truly wants you to do well and will help anyway needed. Is graded based on 2 midterms, 1 final exam and 5 homework assignments. The lectures are not mandatory but if you want to understand what is going on you must go.

DO NOT SKIP A CLASS you will be so behind. It's hard but manageable if you put in the work. Call him with any questions you have and he will help you. Make sure to go to test review sessions I got 16 points back once. He's definitely mean so. don't take anything he says personally. Overall he's a good teacher and this class teaches life skills
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So smug and full of himself and there's no known reason why. Find another prof to take. His course and his attitude is nauseating.

Honestly, he's so rude and needs humbling... but if you have to take him, I would recommend taking him junior year (if you are already proficient in Excel). Exams weren't bad just make a quizlet for the slides. But try to take the other ITOM teacher if you can, your life will be way easier.
He blows fr. No extra credit, rude when you ask questions. Don't take if you care about learning the field or having connections as bro is past his prime

LOVE HIM! He is hilarious and cares about his students. Exams are exactly like his practice exams. Homework is not bad and he is so easy to reach outside of class if you need help. If you go to class and pay attention, you'll be fine
Terrible class if you just need the credit. I was expecting a fun class but he is hyper specific on what he wants you to learn and will not give you a break.

His classes are very lecture-heavy, but he does a great job of making them entertaining through humor. If you study the slides and ask for help with the homework, you will get an A. Purely an effort class, if you show up and care, I would be surprised if you get anything lower than an A-. My favorite professor I've taken thus far. Shout out Rogers.

I don't know why people hate him so much. He has clear expectations for the exams and gives a practice version almost identical to the midterms. He isn't rude, he has sarcastic humor, which I found very entertaining—even if he was picking on me. The homework takes some time, but there are only about three. Do the work, and you will do well.

Rodgers is an interesting professor. Very rough around the edges, generally rude to people in class, but very informative and helpful outside of class. 4 Homeworks, 2 tests,and a final make up nearly your entire grade for the class. Go to class he shows examples of how to do problems on the tests. Take if you want, I would take Guin instead.

I did fine in the class. He wasn't my favorite professor of all time but not horrible either. Just follow along (but he does go quickly) and just get a windows laptop. He truly hates Apple products and your life will be much better if you just get a windows. Go to review sessions for your exam cause he almost always gives points back.

Professor Rogers has a lot of knowledge that he shares with his students. Be prepared to work out of class. He teaches what is useful overall rather than for the tests. He has a sense of humor where he pokes fun at students so be aware of that since it's not for everyone. There aren't many assignments so go to him early if you're struggling.

I found Rogers to be difficult to approach when I needed help so resorted to ALEC or YouTube. He belittles and bullies students making you feel dumb. I basically sat there and struggled in silence, perhaps it was my fault for not wanting to confront him but I also don't think I deserve to be treated that way. Avoid him.

Sat in a 3 hour lecture with Rodgers every week. I didn't mind the length, but I didn't mind the weird political tangents that started with "not to get political". Also what's you're beef with cats? I pay you to teach me how to use excel and access not about how you own a house in HP. Grades heavy on conceptual questions...

Genuinely this is the hardest class I have ever taken. Rogers goes SO fast, is impossible to reach outside of class, and acts like a bully towards his students. If you ask a question, he makes you feel like an idiot. The midterms are nearly impossible to pass, and its hard to get your grade up because there are so little assignments.

Rodgers is the kind of guy who puts others down while masking his core. On the first day of class, he compared himself to the other ITOM professor, who was actually much nicer and more skilled, calling him a 'dork.' The whole semester with Rogers was miserable—he bullied me and left me questioning how someone like him got hired at this university!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Those who admire rogers tend to be those in greek life. Rogers is tough and does not like to be questioned. Take him if you enjoy bringing him a "coffee" for extra credit points and can stand his egocentric personality.

NEVER take him. He is rude to everyone and makes you feel like you are dumb. He hardly responds to emails and will have Zooms over the weekend with a two-hour notice. The zooms aren't reviews it's more like class and if you miss you have to watch the videos to still know what is going on in class or you will be behind.

He is condescending and belittles you if you ask questions in class, cold comments inappropriate things to students, and makes it a difficult environment to succeed. You teach yourself everything and only learn for the exams. Take any other prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the class itself, ITOM can be sometimes tricky especially if you don't go to class since his slides that he uses for the test are not the clearest. The homeworks themselves can be difficult too. However, Rogers is a very nice man and wants his students to win which is cool to see. He cares and wants to help.

I have genuinely enjoyed Professor Roger's class! I did not do so well on my first exam, but he valued my attendance, attention, and participation, allowing me to retake the exam. I have already found the class content to be relevant in a multitude of settings. If you have not worked with excel before, it could be difficult, but very manageable.

Rogers is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students. If you miss points on an assignment or test, he will re-grade and is very generous. If you don't get at LEAST a B in this class, it means you never talked to him. Also, I could see some of the content being difficult for those who have never used MS Excel/Access.

He was a really nice guy and had some very good tips on how to apply what we learned in class in our future internships or jobs. The reviews for the midterms were very straightforward and he pulls a lot of questions from the class slides. Sometimes, the class could get boring as I felt like he spends too much time on things.

Class is hard but he gives points back on tests and assignments if you can prove you know your stuff. Knew no excel or database before the class and he made it easy to learn and engaging. Took as a night class and it was long but bearable. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Okay, if you can memorize the slides and & good w/ excel, you can get an A. Gmetrix, LinkedIn Learning, and youtube are good for excel prep. Tough grader, but he will give points back if you talk w him during his hours. He is an interesting man. DO NOT USE A MAC! It was a dense course if you dont know what to study, but it is all on the the slides.

This class is very manageable if you attend class, do the HW and pay attention. Even though the material is hard, prof. Rogers is accessible outside of class and very willing to help his students. He is very knowledgable in this area and you will learn alot. Honestly the class isn't bad at all if you just put in the time and effort.

Despite attending every class and working hard, Rogers was always very rude to me. If you ask for help, he will talk down to you and belittle you. I learned a lot about Excel, but the fact that he makes you learn Access and SQL is ridiculous. I wouldn't take him unless you have to. I did well in the class, but he is a very difficult human being.

Professor Rogers is a super cool dude that has a ton of experience in the technology field. His teaching style is a little weird, but he cracks a bunch of jokes and tries to make a boring class somewhat fun. ITOM with him is tough though, you often have to do a bunch of research in your own time to figure out the concepts. Tough class, fun prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Rodgers is a dickhead and a horrible teacher
Take any other professor

Rogers is a really polarizing professor, you either love him or you hate him. He's demeaning to students and constantly rude when questions are asked. The tests barely include Excel, most of it is memorization. I went in to test review and was told I didn't know what I was talking about and then was given partial credit for fully correct answers.

The class itself is straightforward if you follow along with him on Excel. If you're confused at all, ask him for help outside of class ASAP as he is more than willing to do so. If you fall behind, it is very hard to catch up. Pay attention to his lectures the day before exams since he often discussed in detail what will be on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It is important to follow along with the Excel and Access steps in class and practice them repeatedly on your own. Also, re-watch the lectures presentations as he will take info directly from slides on the test as well. Don't get the textbooks even if recommended in the beginning (don't need them at all). Also, the homework has clear instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily one of my favorite professors I've had. He cares a lot about his students and explains the material in a way that is super easy to understand. Homeworks are easy and straightforward and tests aren't bad just remember to study the PowerPoints.

Great professor. Makes a class that would otherwise be difficult and boring seem much more understandable and interesting. Very fair and will give lots of points back on tests and homework if you know the material but just made mistakes. Always willing to help and really cares about his students. Attendance is not mandatory but you should go.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He can be abrasive but I think he means well. ALWAYS go to his office hours to review your test to try to get points back-- he is v generous with that if you can show what you know. His practice tests are exactly like the actual tests. He has a thing against apple computers so its best if you have windows. You don't need the books.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Rogers is an excellent professor. His lecture is very easy-understanding. He uses a lot funny/ interesting examples to illustrate some very abstract concepts. And the exam is fully covered by his lectures. All you have to do is attending the class, listening to the lectures, doing your homework, taking the exams and getting an A!

This is a very easy class, but Rogers is very abrasive. I both experienced and witnessed him being unkind toward students. If you take him, you'll be fine, it's not hard to get an A as long as you come to lecture and study the powerpoints, but don't expect a nice professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great professor! His classes were interesting, his grading criteria was clear, and he is a nice guy. He gave extensions for homework when I was having computer issues, and really cares about his students.

Please save yourself and do not take Rogers. He is incredibly condescending towards students and inaccessible outside of class. His grading criteria is needlessly harsh and opaque. On a more positive note, he does a decent job of applying the class concepts to real-life scenarios.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you want to find a summer intern job, take his class!!!!! I don't know why so many bad reviews about him, but one thing I can tell, he is a great professor and he is not only teaching you about the course but more about life, everything he said in the class is to help you find a job one day, that's what we here for, period!
WORST Professor I have had. Rude to students, inaccessible and stuck up. Take any other professor but him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Among the best Cox professors, I have had. Extremely passionate and has had a long, successful career in the field. Highly recommend him. Your grade is only based on a handful of things so if you bomb it could be hard to recover. 4 HW assignments, 2 Exams, and a Final. He doesn't like helplessness.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took ITOM over the summer with him, and really made the experience not as bad as it could've been. Incredible at teaching the topics, but can be very condescending and curt when answering questions on things he has already gone over. Go to all his office hours and study sessions and you should be okay. If you put in the effort, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Be sure to think about all his concepts in business terms and you'll do well. Ask him what his expectations are for the homework and he'll tell you. Many don't read the textbook but most everything you need to know, you'll know if you just do the reading he assigns. Good businessmen and -women pass this class with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Available outside of class, but only on his inconvenient terms and does not respond to messages. Lots of errors on tests. Rude to people who ask questions and rambles in class. However, he is great at teaching the material and wants students to succeed. Easy A if you put in minimal effort. I took in the summer, and I would recommend for short term

I am an A student and learned a lot because he is good at explaining concepts. However he is condescending and talks down to students. He becomes aggressive and annoyed when you ask questions he thinks you should know the answer to. He is hardly ever accessible outside class and often doesn't provide grading feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rogers made ITOM 2308 my favorite class this semester, and I NEVER considered myself capable of doing anything on the computer. He lets you correct homework for points back. Tests can be a bit tricky. This guy ends his class saying, "Nobody loves you more, not even your mothers." And it's true! Such a funny and caring professor! True gem!

Great teacher, in the sense of making you learn how to use excel. Makes sure every student knows what to do before moving on. Funny guy too. Class was not stressful. Not the most accessible professor, but that's fair given the amount of students he has in each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands back tests to look over. Tests are pretty hard because they have all the computer stuff (worth about 20%) and the management stuff he goes over. Problem is we spend 95% of time in class on computer stuff and doesn't really talk about management. Will call you out in class if you're not paying attention. Take Gwinn instead for the easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rogers cares about all his students. If you put in effort you will do well. He will help you as much as needed and make sure you never fall behind. Never had a more caring professor. People that don't do well are people that expect an A just for showing up. Good sense of humor which keeps the three-hour class interesting.

the worst. i still get upset whenever i think about him and this class. very condescending man. this class was pretty hard given that its supposed to be an intro/general class. i would suggest taking the other professor. very little learning and a lot of memorization and teaching yourself access databases.

His class is unnecessarily difficult. It is not an easy A, you have to study and memorize everything. Never thought I'd see the day I would be studying! for excel! He just makes me livid. Take someone else. He has an aggressive sense of humor and if you can handle that, fine. He has strange office hours and prefers we text him. It's just a mess.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors for what would otherwise be an unenjoyable class. Really nice guy and he really cares about students. Will offer a lot of help for homework. Class is composed of tests and a few homeworks. Definitely recommend!
Good explanation of database and business reports

He is the best teacher I have ever taken. I rarely got bored in his three hour class, which says a lot. He seems like he loves what he does and he makes sure that students are never lost. He can be intimidating at first, but that is just his personality. He is very helpful and understanding when going over test grades. Best teacher.

Rogers is great. His teaching style is laid back and sometimes can lack very precise explanations, but he will always make sure you understand before he moves on. He is a very reasonable grader and will help you outside of class if you ask. One of the most caring professors I've ever met - def take him for ITOM 2308.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He cares about his students deeply. He is very funny and keeps us entertained even in the 3 hour class. He grades very fairly and helps you during tests and with your homeworks. Highly recommend him.

He is so caring and truly loves all his students. The tests are very easy and theres not many. He even accommodates if you have another test on the same day to let you take his later. He is genuinely there for every single student.

2 tests worth 20% each, 4 homework assignments totaling 35%, and a final worth 25%. Homeworks are not that bad, just show up to class the day they are due and he will help you out. Tests are moderately hard. Just go to the review the night before and know the powerpoints well and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Tests are extremely straightforward. Just study the powerpoints and go to his review sessions (and go to class--material is hands on and it's hard to catch up on your own). I recommend his 3 hour class--goes by fast. Has 3 tests, not cummulative. 4 homeworks that are easy 100s. Overall great guy and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: I'm an A student, and I found his tests difficult. It's strictly on memorization from definitions and if it isn't exact he won't take it. The tests consist of short answer for definitions, matching, and excel. It's supposed to be teaching about excel, but he doesn't take that as the heaviest part of the test. Has hws but those are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Exams test you on strict memorization and not necessarily understanding. You will memorize, almost word by word, the definitions on his powerpoints. It's easy to drift in and out of focus during his teaching. don't take the three hour lecture. Insider tip: he gives you back lots of points simply by talking about the test and correcting mistakes.

He will test how good your memorization skill is. Tests are from the slides so make sure you have enough time to study and memorize everything. For homework assignments, make sure you always ask for his comments before submitting. Lastly, don't ever skip his review sessions.

Professor Rogers is the best professor I have had thus far at SMU. I did not do well on the first midterm and he took the time to go over it with me and you get points back if you understand and take the time to meet with him. He made itom simpler to understand and I wish he had another class I could take. Highly recommend even if you arent honors

He only gave us 5-10 minutes to do the pop quiz which was worth 10% of the grade.  Some class contents are ambiguous. The final exam was 16 pages, which tested almost EVERYTHING covered in class.  He didn't tell us the exam was going to be THAT long so i was not mentally prepared. I was exhausted 3/4th way through.

Tests are tough and the material is difficult to memorize as opposed to other classes. He moves very quickly through class and it is hard to retain any information that he says. With that being said, 35% of the grade is homework which makes a big difference if you do poorly on a test. It is also very hard to sit through a 3 hour class.
Straight forward, tests are based on what is in the powerpoint slides from class. Helpful and will help you when you need it. Pay attention and you will earn the A.
Great professor. He goes over the material until all students understand it. He is very clear with the material and what to expect on tests and assignments, I would defintely recommend.

This guy is a pro in the most literal sense. He does this stuff for a living, so he knows what he's talking about. He could treat this as just a side hustle and do the bare minimum. Rogers has probably been the most available, helpful professor I've had to date. Take his 3 hour ITOM by any means possible; don't bring a "rotten apple!"

Most helpful professor I've had. Will text and call, even in evenings. Class is easy if you pay attention (and actually go). Homework is very easy too. I took the 3-hour Wednesday course. Definitely go for it- it's a lot less work than other ITOM 2308s

Professor Ritz is very kind and approachable. He cares about his students and wants them to do well. With that being said, unless you have to take this course or are naturally very good at biology, avoid it. The lectures are so boring and the tests are so comprehensive it is impossible to do well

Very hard class. Extremely monotone lectures with super outdated notes. His grammar kind of sucks so get ready to have to interpret the notes constantly. No study guide but he will say which parts of the chapters won't be tested. Get ready to spend hours reading the textbook. I'd suggest reading it twice for each test because he goes in DEPTH.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a sweet man, but my god was that class boring. The tests questions were convoluted and confusing. I got in the 80s on all the tests and I was usually above average, but still not an amazing grade. Def not an easy class, but if you put in a TON of time and study really hard for the tests, you'll probably walk away with a grade in the Bs.

he is a nice. the class is unnecessarily hard, so unless you need it, avoid it. lectures are boring and not engaging. he just talks and talks and talks. he gives out some pre-lecture study guide, but its a waste of time really, as he covers so much material during lecture that its like reading the book.just save yourself the time and read the book
needs to retire, old school lectures that have no use, dated material that doesn't help with assignments nor aligns with reading
Very difficult professor and not worth the work but what can you do? Try to find other options even petitioning to count something else for the course. He's a nice guy but way past his prime.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am a bio major. This class was not that difficult for me. Memorization heavy. In bio classes usually you work on memorizing systems so everything somewhat connects. This is not how Behavioral Neuro was. Just random topics tbh. He mentioned after first test 30% got an A and said that was typical. For final, go back and look over tests with TA.

Behav Neuro was challenging but he made it clear what to expect. He helped students by setting up discussion in canvas so students could ask each other questions and exchange notes. He drops one chapter test. You have to take the final. He has strict boundaries(ex. fixed test dates);if you stay in those boundaries and work hard he would love you.

Professor Ritz is the sweetest man. He was accessible outside the course and enjoyed answering questions and meeting with students. The material is complex, and you will have to study a lot for the exams. The tests come straight from the textbook and slides. However, it is a ton of information for only 50-point multiple-choice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is more of a biology class than psychology. His lectures are straight from the textbook but, reading the textbook as well as attending class is extremely beneficial. The first test is the easiest and then they get harder from there. The exams themselves are pretty difficult as you have to memorize a bunch of functions regarding the brain

Overall very nice and caring of his students learning the material. He is also quite funny and has a nice personality. Lectures are important so attend them and use the textbook. He makes the subject enjoyable and relatively more understandable. It is challenging, but so interesting, take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class requires you to take strong notes and follow along in the textbook. He requires you to know the information in and out for the test. However, if you study hard, pay attention in class, and read the book you will at least get a B on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is hard to understand, and the exams can sometimes be surprising at times, but he does explain the material very well! He wants you to do well and will discuss the material with you if you want. If you pay attention and take notes, and read the book, plus LOTS of studying, you will do fine. an A is hard to get
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Ritz is a very nice man and would answer any questions you have! He is very understanding. This class is more like a neuroanatomy class but without having to actually know exact anatomy. Its more focused on physiology. Tests are straightforward from his slides and textbook so its a very manageable class.
Basically a biology/anatomy course. I never saw where the psychology played in. I personally didn't like it, but for science lovers, you will probably like this.

Great professor, very quirky and knows his stuff. The course is more like a human anatomy course than a psyc course, something I appreciated. Study the textbook as well as the notes, and you'll be fine.

Biological Psychology, fun topic, ok interesting lecture, nice teacher, MC test (if you read the textbook and study the lecture notes you will do fine), lecture ppt are not given on blackboard (must take note by self, necessary), there's only tests, quizzes, and attendance grade

She's very nice, makes the class really easy to deal with because she knows everyone is an engineering major and we have other really hard classes lol. So grateful she didnt make this class incredibly difficult. Shes also very understanding and accommodating, loved her!

Professor Thiele was my favorite teacher that semester and it was my easiest class by far. She is very caring and does a good job making sure that tests aren't too hard and that everyone understands the content. However, she can get super disorganized and be late with putting in grades. Overall she's a great teacher who truly cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For OREM3308, there is a rubric which states how many points you need to make what grade. You get 1 per comment, 15/paper, etc. You can just plan what classes to show up for and what papers to write to get an A and not do all the work. Super easy - BUT YOU NEED TO SHOW UP TO CLASS, no matter how easy since its participation focused

The grade is determined by one test and one group project, which isn't great. Just reach out to her to get help on the group project early and you will be fine. Content isn't communicated all that well, but she is helpful in office hours.

Professor Thiele is very unorganized. There is a TON of reading and super long papers you have to write. Her grading criteria is clear and it is not hard to get an A if you do the work. The class is very similar to a book club. She is always late to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Thiele is nice, and is really interested in the subject matter. She makes her assignments + grading scale clear. Only real problem I have with her is that her class is very much participation heavy. It's hard sometimes to get a word in when the entire 40 person class is also trying to fight for their participation points. Overall good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Thiele had a hard time getting used to the virtual/in-person setup as a result of COVID-19, but it was very clear that she was dedicated to teaching us as much as she could about this subject, in which she is very qualified. Tests somewhat deviate from what is taught in class, and labs are entirely composed of textbook problems.

While she is a bit messy, Professor Thiele really cares about her students and wants you to do well. She gave a lot of bonus points for my class this semester. I will say, however, her exams are often harder than what you expect and the labs aren't really labs - just textbook questions she wants you to solve. You will have to teach yourself.

She is a little messy but she is so nice that it makes up for it. I highly recommend going to her office hours before a test she gives you tips on what to focus on. Her labs are just textbook problems!

You'll pass PRW1101 if you just show up and do the bare minimum, but he was a pretty entertaining one. He's a really cool guy. He's young too, so he's relatable to students as well. 2 or 3 easy one-page writing assignments over the course of the semester.

I can see some people think he is intense, but I think he also really cares about his students. He tries to take a class that doesn't mean much, and make it a class that you would get something out of, which was awesome. He's chill and upbeat. I really liked him

Ueline is a great man with a lot of enthusiasm for his job. I agree with all the other postings, he can take it a little too seriously and can be a lot to handle. He is very strict about a no technology policy and forces students to participate to an annoying extent.

Kind of super serious about a not so serious class. Was very passionate about what he teaches, and he truly believes in it and does it. He was just a little to much. However, he is a really nice great guy.

I absolutely agree with the other review, Ueline basically spent the whole class yelling motivational platitudes at us, and it was just annoying. If you want to take PRW and have a relaxing time, take it with someone else.

Newmon is a crazy intense guy. It seems like most freshman develop really solid relationships with their Wellness teachers, but I didn't think that was the case for students with him. He's a nice guy and definitely cares about his students, but he was way too serious and intense about a mandatory pass/fail class.
The best course I took at Cox, take her!
She's not prepared to teach. Maybe with some more experience she will get better but at the moment she has no clue how to lecture or how to write exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The slides are super clear and if you study them and do all the practice problems on the slides your pretty much guaranteed an A thanks to the Cox curve. I didn't like the group projects. I didn't know anyone and she sorted me into a random group. My group members didn't do much so I ended up having to do everything myself.

She expects you to know how to do the problems that she shows in class before even teaching you. She also overcomplicates every single concept in class. I had to teach everything to myself. Average on the first midterm was a 60 and she proceeded to say we didn't try hard enough instead of blaming herself. Super passive aggressive too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She would assign problems without covering the material that it's over, then act puzzled when students struggled to solve them. She goes way to fast. Also assigns excel outside of class without going over it  at all.
doesnt care if u get it or not, locks in and starts talking abt material as if we get it

Prof Rutigliano is super knowledgeable and very passionate about finance. You can tell she actually knows what she is talking about and isnt just reading off slides. if you pay attention you will learn a lot. Overall not an easy class and I would not take it as an elective but definitely worth it if you want to actually learn finance from a pro.

Oh my god don't take her. Half the stuff is not explained well, you have to buy Pearson, the textbook is unhelpful and she writes things on the board that is not in the slides and thus unless you are in class she won't help you. Her ability to answer questions is summed up to "I said it, thus it might be on the exam"

Don't know why her rating is so high.. she's not a good lecturer, and will stand there in silence while no one knows what's going on. The math is simple, but the word problems are weirdly worded, and all the multiple choice is meant to trick you. She also gives excel hw, and no one knows how to use it.

Valentina was a great Professor. The material is not straightforward and requires attending lectures to be fully understood. The exam questions were similar to assignments, so no big surprises if you have done your homework. The class seemed overwhelming at first but it's doable if you put in some work. I expect an A
Get ready to work hard, but you will learn a lot
Enjoyed the class, a bit subjective, and best to tow the line and grab the easy A.
took him for mno6201. easy class. but I don't "buy" many of the narratives he is telling. the cases were interesting, engaging lecturer overall.

Don is a an amazing professor,his lectures will force you to think and reflect. I enjoyed his class thoroughly, and was able to apply my learning from the class, immediately in my work and personal life.

Professor Vandewalle is one of the best professors I've ever taken at SMU. His lectures are so clear and interesting, with good applications. He is smartly dressed and professional, while also kind and understanding. He likes to engage in conversation with students and likes to make small jokes. I would definitely take him again!

Take this class if in Taos:  Vandewalle only teaches this one undergrad course (Executive MBA professor otherwise)! Great professor, great communicator, great lecturer, good sense of humor -- engages students and is contagiously passionate knowledgeable about subject. Tests are open note case studies requiring application of theory readings.

He is a great professor. The lectures are engaging and the material is very interesting. Also, the tests are very straight forward, which is nice.  I definitely recommend this class. Finally Toas is really fun and this class allows you to enjoy Taos and get a good grade at the same time.

Is an expert research, and also with the ability communicate to connect OB theories to actual management and leadership situations . Great multi-dimensional teaching style with engaging lectures, vivid video clips, exercises, and case studies. A must take class at the SMU Taos campus
I took this class in Taos and I LOVED it. It was fun and interactive. I would recommend this course to any SMU student.

I really liked this class.  While it falls under the business school (which I am not a part of), it was not like most Cox courses.  It was super interactive- we had a ton of class discussions and watched short videos.  I liked the class a lot.

I LOVED this class!!!I highly recommend it, Professor Vandewalle is the best and very knowledgeable about the subject. The class is small so it is generally very laid back and easy to participate. There just simply isn't a way to fail this class.The book is very interesting and easy to read. Take this class while in Taos, you won't regret it!

Dr. Vandewalle is awesome. Really good and practical material. One of the best classes I've taken. NOTE: THIS IS THE ONLY UNDERGRAD COURSE HE TEACHES. He is the chair of the whole management department and normally only teaches grad courses, and so taking his course is a GREAT OPPORTUNITY. He is super helpful in other areas of life too.

Don is without a doubt one of the coolest teachers at SMU. He's laid back, has a great sense of humor, and is always fair. He's one of the few that's truly invested in the lives of his students. The class is structured more as a discussion and expects his students to come prepared, but  he always keeps it casual with a good joke or story.

I enrolled into MNO4371 b/c I wanted to go to Taos and this was the only option (I was a Senior). Class ended up being one of my favorites of all time! The classes/cases were fun, challenging and insightful.  I definitely recommend this class, especially if you are going to Taos. Dr. Vandewalle grades fairly but promotes recreation and free time.

Dr. Vandewalle is easily one of the top couple professors I've had at SMU, after 5 semesters. The Taos environment helps keep students focused in any class, but I found it especially beneficial for knocking out a CF/4300 course. He goes to great lengths to make himself clear and to simplify the material without disrespecting its difficulty. Great!

This is such a great CF to take. One of the few CF courses offered at Cox. If you still have to take a CF or want a management credit I would highly recommend this course. Professor Vanderwalle is easy to get along with and is very helpful with the material. Small class size and a good discussion group

Vandewalle is one of the BEST professors at SMU.  This course was without a doubt the best class I took during my time at SMU.  Taos is the perfect place to take this class as you will get to go on field trips and take education out of the classroom.  TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I highly recommend this class!! I took it in Taos during the June term... and I'm so happy I did. We met five days a week, it was early (and I'm not a morning person) but I never dreaded going to class - in fact, I enjoyed it! Classes are super interesting, laid-back, and totally manageable. And the books are good!! Don is a great professor!

Very interesting class. Don is very knowledgeable about the topics discussed.  It is important to do all the reading and understand the theories and models. Don will tell you which ones you need to know for exams. The class is thought provoking.  Don is fair.  If you do the work, you will do well.
If you value your GPA, run. Workload is huge, grading is brutal, and there's zero consistency. You never know what counts or what doesn't. Easily the most frustrating class I've taken.              w
Not a great teacher, bad grader. The feedback on my work was borderline ridiculous

This professor relies heavily on loosely structured, projects with unclear expectations. Grading feels inconsistent, feedback is minimal, and standards are hard to pin down. It often seems that kissing up matter more than effort or mastery, leaving us frustrated and unsure how to genuinely succeed in the course.
This guy is severely rated too high.
He is very full of himself and will not allow for constructive criticism.

Most overqualified professor at this school. Look him up on google he is the man. He is the nicest guy ever and literally will not let you get below an A. Taught me a lot about debate and public speaking as well. Best professor I have ever had in college.
Best professor I have had! Strongly recommend taking him if you get the chance. Super passionate about what he teaches.
Voth is the best professor I've had at SMU. By far and away the coolest most understanding teacher ever. If you need an A, take him. Only thing this guy likes more than teaching is his Dr. Pepper!!
This is the Goat professor at SMU. Nicest guy and is great with debate. He also wants students to do well. 15/10 recommend taking him.

Dr. Voth is one of the kindest professors I have met at SMU. You can very easily tell that he genuinely cares for each student that he teaches and he is a very understanding professor. Not only that but he is also so passionate about everything he teaches. It makes learning much easier and exciting when your professor is very eager to teach you.
Professor Voth is the best. He is so understanding and accommodating to all of his students. If you get a chance to take his class DO IT!! He gave me an A and was a total homie of a professor. 10/10.

This class was so bad. We'd have to fact-check Voth on the quizzes we had each class on news/topics because his answers were wrong. His lectures were extremely repetitive and often just a way for him to brag about his accomplishments. He was not responsive to feedback from students at all. He also required us to do irrelevant work outside of class.

It is so refreshing to take a class with a professor who is so passionate about the material he is teaching. Our entire class loves Dr. Voth, which makes sense. He listens to you, respects you, and understands you. He also PROMOTES you to disagree if you disagree, which is so rare nowadays in academia. You will thank me if you take a class w/him.

Perhaps the easiest class taken at SMU. Very caring professor who has very easy assignments and coursework. Pro-tip: For this course at least, if you attend two debate tournaments over the year, you get a straight 100%. The debate is easy and you can use your computer in class. This is a public speaking class though, be warned.

Ben Voth is a true gem. He is so nice and always willing to help students when they need it. There's not a mean bone in his body and he has truly become one of my favorite teachers I've taken at SMU. Highly recommend.
Great professor who really cares about what he teaches. If you go to class "most" of the time, and get to know the professor, you should have no problem getting an A.
Professor Voth is amazing. I will take any class offered by him. He's less focused on busy work and grades and more focused on overall understanding. I wish more teachers taught the way he does.

The class is extremely easy and he's really passionate about what he's teaching, but the lectures themselves felt pointless until we approach an actual speech or debate. He's overly obsessed with James Farmer Jr. and overall the class felt slightly pointless but an easy A. Requires out of class work, judging debates and attending debates too.
The best professor I have had at SMU, I will definitely be taking more classes from him regardless if they go towards my major or not.

Dr. Voth is an amazing teacher and really cares about his students. I am a political science major and really appreciated how he tied in politics and world news to his class. Only two tests, but about 5 speeches. He is a relatively easy-grader-- but all-in-all he just wants you to learn how to use your voice and express your opinions.

TAKE THIS CLASS! He is super inspirational, teaches you things you would never learn yourself. The class isn't difficult. He cares about each one of his students individually and will do anything to help you.
A great professor who really really cares. As long as you are willing to work a little he'll help you out
The man is the greatest teacher at this school, bar none. take this class, youll be a better person for it.
First professor & class that had actually "made sense" to me... really great experience.
Professor Voth is passionate and cares about his studies. His class is not hard and often dry.

Dr. Voth is the most amazing professor I've ever had. He is passionate about communications & it shows when he teaches. He is very fair with grading, his assignments arent overwhelming & the tests are extremely straightforward. There is no reason not to get an A in this class if you actually try. Plus, he has incredible insight & you learn a lot.
Just an incredible professor.

Dr. Voth is amazing. This man truly deserves an award or something. He is always there for his students and he makes the lecture material interesting. He truly cares about everyones well being and if you have the option to, PLEASE do take a class with him. He is the kind of professor we need at SMU.

My absolute favorite teacher on this campus! He is so passionate about what he does & tries to ignite the same passion within his students. He isn't too hung up on attendance because he wants you to come to class because you WANT to, not because you HAVE to. He makes the subject matter interesting & will go out of his way to ensure that you do well
Anal in her grading and just a bad teacher. Super emo and yet old hilarious.
She's awful. Strict and doesn't make sense. Likes to be the center of attention even though she's like 50yo or something. Really strange

Quite possibly the worst university professor I have had the displeasure of learning from. Incredibly abrasive and prone to throwing temper tantrums, You might think you are in 2nd grade again with her hissy fits.
She's a though grader but if you listen to her input in conferences you will get good grades.
its embarassing how little she knows and that she holds the title of professor

She would be extremally vague with her feedback. She answers all of the questions you have with a
 question like, "well, what do you think?" and "Do you think that's right?" instead of telling you what
 you need to do to improve.
horrendous and painful to sit through and tolerate, horrible grader and gives insulting feedback

She is very difficult to deal with and highly irritable. Doesn't like questions and forced her opinions on you which you are forced to regurgitate for a good grade. Narcissistic and self-obsessed, constantly talks about her looks which is weird af.

Rude, thoughtless, and insensitive insecure woman who cannot be bothered to do her job and teach, makes you write things out that are how she wants them rather than allows you to develop your own ideas. When you don't, watch out, she's vindictive on grades.

Professor Hopper was a godsend last semester. I took her for WRTR 1313 which isn't an option for some reason. I was scared by the reviews on here but she ended up being my favorite professor on campus. She truly cares about her students and doesn't want to see anyone fail. She expects the best from each of her students and makes class personal.

is so rude to students and makes fun 
 of them for being confused or getting questions wrong. She makes no effort to actually 
 teach anything in office hours without being condescending. Her lectures are riddled with
 mistakes teaching us wrong. I hope SMU does something about her soon.
DOesn't give good feedback, class is wasteful, bad professor.

Rude and condescending, openly rolled her eyes at us if we asked a question she didn't like, way too much work for the class level and her expectation don't match her own effort she puts into classes. Do what they say, write everything she wants to hear from her own opinions rather than an analysis for the best grade possible. Or avoid her!!

Grade consists of 4 papers all on bland subjects. Conferences don't help as much as you need and the class feels silly to go to since you don't do much besides do an off topic assignments that aren't graded. Feedback is poor and always feels rushed.

She is the absolute worst, berated me throughout the semester, rudest professor I have ever known, hateful in her comments about my work, instead of teaching me how to be better and improve my skills, belittled me with her words. I truly hope SMU administrators see this and does something about it because no one deserves to be treated like this.

She is a very kind and caring professor who goes above and beyond to provide feedback on your papers. She is very strict on attendance, but also is very patient if you are open to her and keep a good line of communication. One of my favourite professors at SMU!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Hopper. If you establish a relationship with her, it will benefit you - as she really cares about each student individually. If you got class and go to your conferences, she will give you helpful feedback. Do your work and out in the effort and it will be reciprocated. Highly recommend.
Most amazing professor I have ever had, truly life changing!!  10/10 would take her if you can.

One of the worst professors at SMU. In order to pass, you must regurgitate back her same views and ideology. If you dare to disagree on anything, your grade will suffer. Truly, the secret to the positive reviews:  be a broken individual or be a savvy one that mimics. If you are an independent thinker and want to stay that way, take another class.
Super interesting Professor liked her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have never wanted to honor a person more than to remember the limitless legacy of someone who sacrificed their time in the service of students who understood the meaning of dignity. Much more than dignity, courage, and much more than courage compassion to change the world of so many one moment at a time.

I just wanted to give Professor Hopper the biggest shoutout. Her lectures gave me something I could never give back, a sense of narcissism I never knew I needed. Thanks Professor, I never knew how important it was to be a planet and a solar system! The pleasure was mine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved Ms. Hopper. I'm quiet in discussions, but she always pulled a response out of me. She also wrote a kind, heartfelt letter explaining our grade for each essay. I looked forward to her class every day. The reading was heavy, but I found myself enjoying the books as we went. Great conferences. I'm disappointed not to have her in the spring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class definitely requires a time commitment, lots of reading. Make sure to annotate while you're reading the texts and take detailed notes during discussions and you'll do fine. She does conferences for essays and helps steer you in the right direction with your essays. Definitely not an easy A, but a really fulfilling and engaging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Classes are enjoyable and discussion heavy. Make sure you take very good notes on the common themes that come up during lectures because they show up in the essays. Pay attention to her feedback. Attendance is mandatory but was super understanding if you're unable to go provided you email her. Enjoyed her class and would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures, but very difficult paper grading and an absolutely draconian attendance policy made the class less enjoyable. If you were late (even by 1 minute) to more than 3 classes, you lost 5 points on your overall grade, and if you missed more than 3 you lost 10.
Do not take her. Your entire grade is based upon papers. Her grading is impossible and this class will kill your confidence as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was tough, but i feel like I actually became a better writer, and it kinda paid off in the end. If you can, take another professor, but she's not too bad if you pay attention and don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally, the reason I dropped out of the honors program. She is the absolute worst, she berated me throughout our semester together, and instead of teaching me how to be better and improve my skills, she belittled me with her words. I truly hope she sees this message someday, because someone finally needs to put this professor in her place.

Personally, did not like Hopper for WRTR. Graded pretty tough and feedback wasn't very insightful for moving your grade upwards. Felt prescriptive despite her insisting to write what you can support from the texts. Small thing, but you can't see the class average on canvas to know if everyone is getting hit or not.

Don't fall victim to the pretense. The caring side is nothing more than narcissism in disguise. Listen to others. The secret to doing well is as stated: mimic back to the Professor what she believes. Your writing skills are secondary to anything else. Mirror the mantra, play to the false caring pretense, and you get an A.
Grades super dumb. Once gave me a bad essay grade for not quoting correctly when she wouldn't let us use the book during the timed essay. socratic seminars are her interrogating a few students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hopper is an amazing teacher, hands down. But sadly, most of her assignments are graded on her own opinions and what she believes is true. If you write something opposing her opinions, you get marked down. If you're okay with getting a B+ or even a B- and all for learning, go for it. If you need the high grade or GPA, don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, but worth it. Hopper is engaging and will cold call on you, but overall a caring professor. Always makes sure to note the grade doesn't define one's success, and is super understanding. Definitely recommend her for your first honors class - my whole class is taking her in the spring again, if that makes a difference.

Tons of drama with limited instruction. HINT: to succeed you must mirror exactly what Prof believes. If you do so, you will do great. If you express your own opinions (no matter how well written), you will not succeed. No real instruction, just indoctrination into the ideologies. If you seek to improve your writing skills, take another course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was traumatic. If you enjoy writing as a passion DO NOT take this class. If Im going to write a paper on a topic, DO NOT let me be blind the entire time. Blind lead the blind. Thanks for the grade.

Composed of four papers and a final exam paper. Cannot skip class and she wants to see you focused and ready to work. However, she is very caring, engaging, and her expectations are very clear. Not too much reading and the class isn't overwhelming but do expect to put in effort, participate, and pay attention in class. Prof Hopper is great!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Super awesome and personable teacher. My writing improved a ton and it is always super clear what she wants from you in your papers. She will give you a few pages worth of explanation for what to do and as long as you don't stray away from the question you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Expects you to basically just write down exactly what she talks about in class. Gives mediocre feedback and is a pretty tough grader. It's very hard to get an A, as messing up on even one essay (5 essays make up your entire grade) will pretty much sink your grade to the B-B+ range.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's pretty good at explaining topics and I learned a good amount in her class, but she's a moderately tough grader though I would say its generally fair. It's important to get along with her in her class, so try to just riff with whatever she says and you'll be okay if you read the books and can contribute in the slightest.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students. Her class is difficult but she's just trying to push you to perform at your peak. She grades the first essay a little harshly which can screw up the rest of the semester, but just continue to work. Conference with her as much as possible.

Professor Hopper made my freshman first semester horrible. She lectures during class about our readings and talks nothing whatsoever about actually improving her students' writing. She did not like my writing but never recommended any specifics to fix it. I learned nothing from this class and ended up dropping UHP. DISC 1313 helped me so much more.

Her class can be interesting, but be sure to read the books. She will call on you in class. GO TO CLASS. Not an easy grader, but if you write exactly what she wants you'll be fine. THIS CLASS IS NOT DISCUSSION BASED. SHE LOVES TO TALK. She can be condescending, don't take it personally, just say what she wants to hear. If you get an A, congrats.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a fan of this professor. She cares more about hearing herself talk then fostering good discussion. Will not let you come into office hours to discuss anything "already graded or discussed in class". There are better professors to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Vanessa Hopper is my favorite professor at SMU. I learned so much from her class and would recommend anyone to take it. It was the hardest class I took all year, but she is one of the best honors professors. She wants all students to succeed but does not hand out many A's. Read everything, take good notes and take adverting of asking her questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Hopper is, without a doubt, my favorite professor I've had at SMU thus far. I am a better writer now because of her. I was lucky enough to have her for both semesters, and she provided excellent feedback and was so encouraging. She's also very intelligent. I learned something in every class and always looked forward to DISC.

Gives a lot of good feedback for your essays. Offers conferences for certain essays, meaning you get the whole week off of class. Helps you improve a lot on your writing during conferences. Will occasionally call on people during discussions so make sure to read. Overall a good professor that is not super hard to make an A with.
If you listen in class and write based on what she says you should be okay. Her conferences are really valuable and useful. She's very knowledgeable and her discussions are in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hopper is knowledgeable and cares about students but can be a bit condescending and harsh sometimes. I still learned a lot from her class. The worst part is the grading. She doesn't give many A's, and your grade is based on just 5 essays. You can't pull your grade up above your average essay score. She isn't too accessible for paper help either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There are lots of notes to take during class, but if you write your essays based on your notes you should be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Assigns moderate amount of reading- not too much. Paying attention to lectures and participating in discussions helps a lot. Very knowledgeable on subject and helpful in interpreting complicated readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Hopper has good discussions in her class and assigns interesting readings, but she gives no option for improvement with your essays. We were not supposed to go to her office hours to review graded essays and there was no opportunity to revise/edit any graded work. It is very difficult to make higher than an A- in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good class. For the most part, as long as you dont try to argue against her points in your essay, you should be fine. She rarely gives out anything higher than an A-. One bad grade can cement you at a B, B+ if youre lucky. I still consider her better than the alternative DISC professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really good professor- easy essay grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class is pretty reading heavy. She's a fairly tough grader, but she gives you a ton of feedback so you learn exactly what she wants. Her lectures were always interesting, and she brings a lot of insight to the table. She also cares a lot about the students and gets to know you! Overall, she's a great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hopper has a very specific way that she wants students to write: economy, clarity, and accuracy. If you do what she says and follow instructions you will be fine. She loves to hear herself talk and does not leave room for too much discussion. Very educated and has great things to say, but not the best English professor I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hopper is a pro at DISC courses. Her tried and true methods is what she sticks to, so depending on the type of person you are, this can be good or bad for you. Follow her instructions and lecture content to get an A on every assignment, including the research paper and the oral presentation. She's a nice person overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing. I highly recommend taking her course. She basically tells you exactly what to do for an A and it really is not that much that she asks for. Listen, take notes, follow the rubrics for essays. That's really it. I plan to take her 2306 course next semester as well because I enjoy her teaching style.

This is her rubric: Very close to what she said in class  A+. Everything else is bad. This doesn't make the class very hard bc all you have to do is take good notes based on what her opinion is and then regurgitate it in your own words. I think she's awesome though. I don't mind repeating her opinion because everything she says is insightful.

Hopper is the most insightful professor that I have ever had.  The topics that she discusses in class are enlightening and will expand your world view.  The class is challenging and demanding, but if you work hard to meet her expectations, you will make a good grade.  She is understanding and willing to meet with her students to help them succeed.

I took Hopper for DISC 2305 and 2306. I wasn't her biggest fan in 2305, but I absolutely loved her in 2306. There are 4 papers and a group presentation. Expectations are extremely clear and you can make an A if you put the work in. She really cares about her students and her job. I highly recommend her.

Hopper is very knowledgable and a nice person, but her class is painful. If you don't repeat her opinions in your paper as if they were your own then she will mark you down. If you say something she disagrees with in the discussions then she will call you out like you're wrong. This was a poor experience and I'd recommend finding someone else.

Although the course description reads like a focused analysis of schools of thought in which discussion is critical, in actual fact the only way to succeed is to parrot her opinion. If your analysis is substantiated, well planned, and well-organized, but you lack her viewpoint, you will be deducted at least a letter grade. Very disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her arguments are very one-sided. She tends to give good grades to students who write what she thinks and poor grades to those who have different opinions; she thinks her opinion is superior. Discussion in class is interesting but be ready to take a lot of notes and come prepared unless you want to be called out in front of the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's pretty arrogant and condescending. Be ready to take amazing notes in class. There are 5 essays and you need to agree with her opinions in the essays and write what she wants you to write or you won't make a good grade. Her expectations are clear, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You have to work and be prepared for every class. Very hard to get an A but if you do what you are told you will get rewarded.

Fantastic professor. Tricky to get an A in this class, she really makes you work for it (as a good English professor should). Very intelligent and knows what she is talking about. Follow her grading criteria, show her you care and you should do well in this class. Will push you and truly make a positive impact on your writing if you let her.

If you are an honors student, you will likely enjoy Professor Hopper. If not, she can be condescending. She has a tendency to treat her students like high school freshman- reads directions verbatim, demands attention, provides strict prompts to baby you through the class, perpetuates clichéd writing, and inhibits class discussion.

If you are considering taking another Professor for DISC, don't. Professor Hopper is by far the best Professor I have taken at SMU. She really is a Professor who cares.  Amazing lectures. Incredible person. Highly recommended.
Hopper may not be a geologist, but she still rocks. #TeamHopper

Professor Hopper is an AMAZING person and a great professor. Her expectations about what she wants in her papers are very clear and she is willing to meet with you to discuss your papers before you turn them in. As long as you are engaged in her lectures and do the reading, you'll know exactly what to include in papers. DEFINITELY TAKE HER!!!

My absolute favorite teacher at SMU thus far. Extremely helpful. Go to her for help and questions it WILL improve your grade. Put in the work and you'll be rewarded. Class topics are a lot of fun and reading assignments and lectures are very interesting. If I could take DISC over again I would in a heartbeat with her.

This is one of my favorite SMU professors! She is clear with what she expects and rewards her students for accomplishing those goals. Going to class and meaningfully contributing will allow you to understand exactly what Professor Hopper wants you to learn and explain more in your essaysassignments. BEST DISC PROFESSOR!!!

I literally cannot say a bad thing about Hopper!! She is the best teacher ever and expects you to work hard, but rewards you when you do! She's amazing and her lectures are so inspirational. She does expect you to go to class and do the reading, but offers great feedback on papers. Absolutely love her, definitely take her for DISC 2305 and 2306
Would take her again and again. She's a little tough on grading but it's worth it if you're at all interested in understanding literature. She has this course down to a science.

Professor Hopper is by far my favorite English teacherprofessor I have ever had. She is very clear on what style she is expecting from her students. English is usually my least favorite subject but she made me love it. She conferences with every students before each paper is due. Very understanding woman. Class requires time for excellent papers!

She gives very specific outlines as to what you need to do and complete. The trick to doing well in her class is participating thoroughly and attending her conferences. She is a tough grader; getting an A instead of an A- will take work; but she grades more for effort than content. Go to the A-LEC, get help from her during office hours.
Fantastic professor. She is so passionate about the material and extremely helpful. I highly recommend.
Professor Hopper is absolutely wonderful.  She truly cares about each student succeeding as a writer, and is very constructive in her paper comments while still grading very gently.

Professor Hopper is so great! She really knows her stuff and wants you to know it too. She makes class discussions very clear and I always leave with a much deeper understanding of our texts. 4 essays all equally weighted, not an easy A but if you work hard, put time into it and meaningfully contribute to discussions, she'll like you
Not too hard of a honors class. One of the easier honors teachers compared to everything I've heard. Kind, fair, and interesting enough. Take her.

Professor Hopper is my far my favorite professor at SMU. I took her for DISC 1312 and enjoyed her so much that I took her again for DISC 1313. This class definitely requires that you work hard, but Professor Hopper is so helpful with everything. All of the papers directly reflect the discussions she leads in class. AMAZING professor!!!!!!!
