Definitely a tough class, but so worth it! Class discussion is great, and Professor Hopper is very straight forward in her assignments. Not a lot of busy work, but a lot or reading. Hopper is young and cool.

I was the only student student in her 2306 class who hadn't taken her the semester before so I struggled at first.  She grades in a very particular way, but she is adamant about students writing the correct way, not just "what she wants them to write."  In the end you can earn an A if you work hard, and she is very encouraging.  Favorite teacher!!

very intelligent, insightful, and willing to help and accommodate. Hopper is definitely one of the best professors I have had in a while. I have been at 2 other schools, one an ivy, the other a nescac, and i find hopper one of the most engaging profs i have had.

Hopper uses a discussion-lecture mix that keeps students involved in the class, while also getting across points we couldn't discover on our own.  From what I gather, she is the Honors Rhetoric teacher that assigns the least work.  Despite that, it is possible to learn a lot from her class.

hate english but her discussions were fun sometimes. she does grade fairly on essays, she can tell when you procrastinate and grades accordingly. she is one of the best honors rhet teachers and she gives class a whole week off when essays are due. you need to put time into this class to get an A, it is challenging.

Had her for both sections of Honors English. Absolutely loved her; discussions were interesting, but be sure to keep a couple of your good points for your papers: she doesn't want repetition of discussion. Very available to help and conference; I even use her as a reference. Fabulous professor/class.
As long as you work hard shell work with you. Not an easy A but you will learn ALOT.

Best professor I could've asked for. She was so passionate about the material and really made it of interest to me. As a goth myself, it was awesome getting to meet another goth on a campus that's majorly lacking in subcultural diversity. Things I recommend: really pay attention when reading the text and take her advice into account when writing.

I have heard some bad things about Hopper, but my experience in her class was great! She grades the fairest out of all the Honors English teachers. She provides interesting insights into the books. Also, when going into conferences with her, I found that she valued originality and only offers advice on a few minor details. Take her class!!!

Hopper is amazing, smart, funny, and she?s the best professor for Honors rhetoric by far! TAKE HER IF YOU CAN! She grades fairly and gives you meaningful feedback on your essays (4-5 each semester). What she wants may be different from your high school English teachers, but you can adapt your writing style to fit what a college professor wants.
if you have her as your teacher and its passed the drop date and your looking it up to find out if shes a good or not. YOUR COMPLETELY SCREWED .....
I thought she was the "easy" honors teacher, but she's not. She expects you to remember irrelevant details, rather than analyze the book.  Also, she really does have favorites in the class.
Very interesting class! Professor teaches the class well and connects all the texts together. Tough, but engaging. Hit or miss

A good teacher. She is really engaging and is passionate about her work. She really tries to help you understand the works. You end up getting a week off for every paper, and edit it numerous times. It's hard to get a low grade in this class if you pay attention and take suggestions.

Shes an excellent prof. really knows her material and always willing to help student who dont understand or have been sick. youll get dropped a letter grade for missing 3 or more classes.so go to class! but she is really helpful and understanding. she's one of the profs you can talk to on a normal/informal level. i wouldnt take eng from anyone else

She is very excited about all the material, but class discussions are usually pretty boring because she just reviews the plot of the reading. Make sure you have read the material before coming to class (or spark notes it) because she sometimes randomly calls on people. I liked her as an honors professor.

This was the worst class I have ever had. She is more interested in checking to see if people read the material than in actually having a serious discussion. If you don't regurgitate her opinions in your papers, they are inferior. Despite that, I still got a decent grade. Don't take this class, it's not at a college standard.
She's very nice and surprisingly knowledgeable based on how uninformative class discussions/lectures can be.  She gives you a week off for every paper assigned - huge plus.  Hit-or-miss with grades.
She is a GREAT PROFESSOR! I LOVE HER CLASS
She's a great teacher! Always cool and ready to chat with her students. She does have favorites, though, but if you're one of them, this class will be a breeze.
The class isn't terrible, but she does pick favorites. And you better be well-prepared before you come to class.
She is a little weird... Sometimes class isn't that bad. I wouldn't recommend taking her though. Good luck!
I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! He's amazing and is such a great professor. I wouldn't take this class if you aren't an art major, but this is a great class.
Terrible teaching style and plays favorites with students. Avoid if possible. Tanks your gpa for no reason.
He doesn't really "teach" you; he leads you.

Easy A. His foundation class and painting class are the exact same. He really likes gouache. Most of his assignments felt like easy, abstract busy work that didn't challenge me/grow my technical skills. When I tried to practice figure drawing in my sketchbook he said it was too academic. He's a nice guy, but overall his teaching style is not for me

Course is a Slow process of intaglio printmaking, I do not recommend for unpatient students.Phones aren't allowed unless for reference images. Final grade is determined by how much effort you put in but no actual assignments on canvas. He can ramble sometimes, but if you show up and do the work you will be fine.

Eccentric guy had him for an Honors class about discussing beauty No homework/tests just reading list you really didnt have to read fully Mostly him talking about stuff very stream of consciousness discussion wasnt structured if you didnt have anything to bring up you dont talk, which is fine by me bc I liked hearing abt how he thought about things

If you're taking foundations, take Philip! He offers so much good feedback because he has so much experience.
Its easy to skip class but he grades on your engagement so just attend class and stay the full 3 hours. There are rules for listening to music but he becomes more lenient throughout the course which is nice

prof philip has a lot of knowledge to offer. Its easy to skip class but its important that you always show and work on bettering you skills. He can go off on rants at sometimes, but they are all kind hearted and its nice to learn about his past experiences. Making an A is easy if you show you care and go beyond normal expectations.

He was nice but is a little rough around the edges. He means well and has a lot of real-world experience. I felt like a lot of the work I did was busy work and I didn't grow my technical skills as much as I had hoped. Made me realize I didn't want to major in art, but I'm thankful I learned that in my 1st semester and not later.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such an inspiring and kind guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His printmaking class is a real gem, he mainly teaches you the basics and lets you work with whatever interests you. Funny to talk to and always is supportive in whatever you want to try, makes a really great learning environment for making art.

Great art professor - he's open-minded and willing to work with you on projects that interest you. He won't just hand out good grades - if you slack off he can tell. That being said, he's not too difficult of a grader so long as you put in the work and show that you're willing to try new art techniques.

While he can go off topic at times, and can be a bit indecisive to what he wants, I ultimately found his class very enjoyable and worth the work he expects you to put in. A very knowledgeable man if you listen to him, has a broad idea of what art is, making any approach seem welcome. Would take again if given the chance.

This class is pretty chill, and you get to work on your own pace in the things you are interested about. He teaches you the techniques, and he lets you go from there. If I could, I would take the class over again. He's funny and he is extremely knowledgeable. He loves to teach you new things and suggests avenues to take in your art.

Easy A, nobody comes to class, you don't have to, he plays for the student crowd and tries to be liked, asked us to nominate him for the hope award so that he can get a raise, all of this is so weird and I've learned absolutely nothing.
Annoying blow hard who cancels class constantly then acts like you should be grateful. Would rather act like your friend than be a teacher. Desperate for a job and it shows.

A poorly designed class & exams are do-able, questions are vague and confusing to understand. He is a professor who emphasizes the importance of good communication, but does not follow his own guidance. Slide decks are old and he snaps at you if you ask questions which created a negative learning environment.
A professor who actually cares. Good class, had a lot of educational fun.

Tries to substitute poor teacher with some strange in class behavior that is enabling to make students like him. Easy grading so there that but everything else just leaves you wondering how he got a job here.
Gives As out like candy which is why people take him. Tries to be cute and fun in lectures. Comes across as desperate rather than knowledgeable.

Great guy. Attendance not mandatory and I still got As on every exam. Warns you ahead of time of the homework and how to do it to get 100s. Super funny lectures. Sometimes gets off track with side topics but you can count on it being entertaining. Would def take again for this class.

Not a good professor and tries to hard to be "popular" among students rather than teach so you learn nothing and then go onto larger projects and classes with no baseline. Do not take him, the other prof will at least prepare you well.

Such a great professor and human. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you honestly get so much more out of the class if you actually attend. While I think his lectures can sometimes go off topic, he does a great job of making them apply to the real world. If you show effort and meet with him if you're confused, the class is straightforward.
H'es not hard but he is overly friendly like he's wanting to be liked by college students and its very sad. Bad teaching too.
He is the best professor you can take at SMU for this class!!!! HE is AWESOME

He's an awful professor who is very full of himself with superiority complex. Tries to befriend students which is creepy. Unorganized and borderline absurd in his antics. Most weird experience I've been in for a class

GOAT prof, some of the most insane lectures simply cause of audacity and connects everything to real life. Unlike other reviews the class gets better every sem and no mistakes made and he's just a very chill guy to talk with.
The Goat of ITOM, take him if you can
Doesn't know what he's doing, desperate for a job given his status, tries to keep it by being the "cool" or "popular" professor, sad.

Does not know the material well, makes a ton of mistakes so he tries to cover up his inefficiency though this weird af golly-gee-willickers affect intermingled with weird ahl cussing, its a crazy experince none of which is fit for academic, weird is all i can say, and sad/desperate, i understand he needs the job but just do your job

Doesn't know how or doesn't care about teaching so he spends the whole class lumbering around trying to be everyone's pal (we're 20 year olds, by the way, it's just sad). Curses at everything and it's a joke we have to pay for this. You will learn NOTHING.

Loser class that you won't learn anything in as he spends his entire time talking about his wife and "bro stories" to be liked and popular among kids, it's weird af and he also loves to cuss af becuase he's hip remember, studpid ahh teachers as this school pmo

He can be really inapproriate in efforts to be "cool" while not even teaching the course well. Low value teacher and you won't get anythign out of the class. If you need to learn for real, take the other option or you'll merely be wasting your time. His language is atrocious for someone so desperately needing to keep his job here.
dude is a total burger, has no knowledge, no connections, can't teach his own topics and tries to hide this fact by trying to be "friendly" 🤡 🤡 🤡

You literally learn nothing. He's so useless and spends his whole time trying to be popular to keep his job but at the cost of graduating students who don't know what they're doing. This is so sad and yet so common in SMU.
WHAT A SAD JOKE OF A COURSE.................... or should i say c&*#&U() course/ would Nils understand that better??????
Don't take him if you actually need to learn.
It's a dumbed down version of code camp for 5th graders but with expletives for no reason, don't take, not worth the $90K we spend here

People pleaser to the highest degree which cna be used to your benefit but also equally against you when your classmates are all asking for exceptions in order to cheat on their work. He's too concerned about being liked and rated highly by us that he doesn't even do his job.
He is a joke and shouldn't it be teaching college. You learn nothing but how many ways you can use the word c@&$.

Outstanding professor. He excels at teaching and breaking down complex concepts. While his style is somewhat informal, it never detracts from the learning experience. He focuses on what truly matters and ensures students grasp the material. I genuinely had a great time in his class and learned a lot.
Should not be teaching college.
The most unprofessional professor I have ever come across, he is not funny, and needs to tone it down. Not what we expect when paying $90K a year. SMU needs to look at who they are hiring.

This is a hard class, but Nils is the best teacher for it! He cares, is engaging, and goes out of his way to support his students. Put the work in, and the material can be grasped. You can just easily tell who puts the work in and who does not care just based on grades! I loved his course! I suggest going to class even though it's optional.
Okay... I think that he's a great professor. He does teach the concepts very well. However, he is very unprofessional. Seriously, why are we dropping the F-word and the CU*T around class?

I love Professor Nils. He genuinely cares about his students and is accessible outside of class. Attendance isn't mandatory but it helps to get to know him and to better understand the material. He makes learning the information fun and knows how to keep the class involved/entertained.
Talks too much ab his personal life when that's not what we're here for

The complaints are fair: he is seemingly not here to actually teach us what we need to know but is here to secure a spot for him and his family. That's fine and all, but you still need to do the job we are paying you to do.

He spends more time boosting his ego than teaching. His constant focus on himself, trying to win approval from students, is awkward and unprofessional. It's hard to respect his lectures when they're so self-serving. His lack of research expertise only makes it worse.

The man lumbers around trying to be all quaint and sheet and can't teach a gd concept if his life depended on it. Do not understand why people refer him as he is the worst thing to happen to our field. Makes a joke of it through his incompetence.

I always looked forward to going to this class. He is very engaging with the class and keeps lectures enjoyable to listen to. I learned a lot in this class; if you feel like you didn't, you probably never attended class. Exams are not crazy hard, if you show up to class and pay attention, they are fairly easy. 1/3 of the class don't show up.

Prides himself on being the "popular professor" when he should concern himself more with teaching skills. he tells random stories touting his experiences and fails to address anything that we will actually use, not worth your time. You learn nothing and then can't proceed in the degree.
Bro acts like he's running a popularity contest for himself. Too busy trying to socialize with us that he not realizing we're not learning anything.
Tries so hard to be liked by STUDENTS half his age, makes everything easy to be like by STUDENTS half his age. Weird fr. Just do your job.
I couldn't recommend him more, I'm always invested in his lectures, there's never a moment where my questions go unanswered.

A man so insecure that he must first try to befriend students then win them over with exceptions for every rule and free As. That's your thing, take him, if you want to learn, take someone else. He is a poor excuse for a professor but easy so everyone takes him.
Highly dont recommend. Class is a joke and u learn nada. i literally have nothing else to say

I can't speak highly enough of Nils! I genuinely look forward to his lecture every week, he's so fun and makes the content truly engaging. The content of his exams is not easy, but as long as you attend class and put in the work you will do well. Take this class if you can!
Students like him because he's nice and an easy a but you learn absolutely nothing and will be useless to industry. We need better professors in this department, he's shameful.
I did not have a good experience. He is more concerned about being liked by students half his age than he is about being a good teacher. Sad.

His lectures were entertaining, especially helpful when you're doing some of the math later in the semester. I'd recommend reading the textbook as exam prep. After every exam, go review with Nils! He might give you points back. You get a one-sided cheatsheet. Oh, and he does take attendance into consideration at the end of the semester for rounding

Nils is a super nice professor who is more than willing to help his students. With the right amount of effort and studying the class is easy and you are allowed to do test corrections and he is super accessable outside of class. Def take for ITOM!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wild he's even a professor with his lack of knowledge.

I loved Nils' class!! Very straightforward grading criteria and you don't have to go to class at all. The homework is really easy and the tests are like verbatim what he says they'll be so can't complain.
Simply put, I don't feel like I learned anything therefore this course did not add to my competitive edge on the market. He tries too hard to be "cool" and liked by children and that alone is cringe.

Simply put, he doesn't know what he's doing. I didn't come out of this class feeling like I actually learned anything and he's just not a nice guy. People-pleaser with no boundaries rather than being an invested teacher.

Avoid, if possible. incredibly vague and his lectures are so unorganized and rarely make sense. Super vague
 and a lot of the time the topics from class are not in the textbook. The examples in class are often 
 off-topic, irrelevant, and not applicable. Wastes a lot of time with off-topic discussions.

Nils was by far my favorite Cox professor so far, amazing lectures, he cares not only about the class but about you too. Had everybody's names in the section memorized by 2nd or 3rd week of class. He does cold call but won't press you if you're just not having it that day. Very chill guy and wish i could take him again.

Tons of drama with limited instruction. To succeed you must mirror exactly what Prof believes. If you do so, you will do great. If you express your own expertise (no matter how well written), you will not succeed. If you seek to improve your skills, take another course.

Great professor, very straightforward. Attendance not mandatory but heavily encouraged to be on good side and know what will be on tests. If you attend, be engaged, and do the homework, you will do well. His lectures are hilarious and very engaging. One of the top professors at this school so if you need to wait to take him, it's worth the wait!
One of my favorite professors at SMU. Truly cares about his students, has great humor, engaging lectures. Def take him!!!!

Love nils. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I still went because you shouldn't go into the tests blindly.... He makes everything easy to understand and wants you to succeed, options for points back on tests too. Definitely take him. WERK NILS!
Got called out for having various tabs open the one time we were allowed to use computers. Very controlling of his class and assigns unnecessary work. Do NOT take him.

Nils is a very caring and straightforward professor. If you get stuck on a test, he will help you work through your problem. He does not have an attendance policy which some people like, but if you go to his class and participate you will do well.

Can't recommend this professor more, he is so nice and caring, he really wants you to succeed. He posts extra help videos online and is always available if you have questions. Attendence is not required but I always went to class because his positive attitude and humor is contagious. Everyone loves this guy! 10000/10

is an easy class with a poor design. Projects & exams are do-able, but instructions/questions are vague and confusing to understand. He is a professor who emphasises the importance of good communication, but does not follow their own guidance.

Nils has been one of my favorite professors at SMU. His lectures were fun and engaging, and he always made the class laugh. Even though it was a morning class, I always wanted to make it to class. He genuinely cares about his students and makes an effort to know everyone.
a joke and a waste
Free and easy A if you can stomach the monotone lectures, attendance not required which helps, but awful experience when attending. His only worth is being SMU's GPA booster.

The problem with him is that he doesn't really teach you anything as he spends his whole time trying to be "fun" and "the liked professor," a real people-pleaser to the max, trying to outshine through juvenile popularity contests rather than through solid, good teaching. If this were high school, he's McLovin.
Avoid this professor. Spends more time on personal anecdotes than teaching. Doesn't respect student time, cancels classes last minute. Total waste of resources.
No idea what he's saying the whole lecture time, not very fun, can't answer a single student question.
Most overrated underperforming professor in the history of professors.

I worked and studied and stressed for hours just to get lousy grades. This is without exaggeration the most stressful class I've taken 
 in college. Class is disorganized full of random jargon.

Useless course, professor seems confused that he is even supposed to be teaching a 
course rather than putting on a comedy show, whole course was nothing but his opinions 
that were not backed up by current trends in the field.
a joke of a course and the professor can't stand to hear or read any criticism
Avoid this professor, doesn't actaully teach, is so insanely full of himself, and he's also condescending and rude to students if they don't understand everything the first time.
Prof. Van den Steen knows how to engage his students and made learning the material easy. You wont regret taking him. 10/10!

Tests are based off HW assigned and powerpoints. Clear and straightfoward class and really nice professor. One of my last classes at SMU and appreciated his passion for teaching as my time here comes to a close. Made a summer class seem like a breeze.
This professor is an amazing guy and I found him to be a great teacher. He cares about his lessons and making sure you understand through participation and positivity.
Does everything to help you succeed. He is an amazing professor.
Really great professor. He makes learning the material easy. Take him if you can!
Useful like a data camp, take it if you need a cred but won't teach you anything meaningful for later application, do not recommend if needing more study later
This professor is a disaster. Can't keep track of assignments. Gives conflicting instructions. Shows favoritism, ignores others. Avoid this class if you can.
Steer clear of this class! Professor is disorganized, forgetful. Doesn't follow syllabus, changes requirements on a whim. An utter waste of academic potential.
Clear expectation. Took time to get to know his students. Was flexible with meeting students after class for help.

one of the kindest professors at smu, makes the class enjoyable for all majors, very flexible with you missing class, great person overall and will give advice outside of class, leaves tons of room for partial credit, exams are very similar to review slides and practice problems with a few twists

Great professor! Made all his lectures interesting and attendance wasn't mandatory. Cared a lot about his students and always made time to meet with them outside of class. Was one of my favorite teachers at SMU

Best professor at SMU! attendance is optional but you won't want to miss class. Class is enjoyable and Prof Nils makes the content very easy to digest. As long as you attend class and make a good cheat sheet, you'll do great!

Such a sad waste of one's time with a professor who is more concerned about being liked than his teaching. If you need or want to learn, this is not your guy - seek out other options. Not even sure he knows what he is doing but do know he cannot tolerate differing opinions here or anywhere.
super nice guy with fair tests. unlimited HW attempts. attendance optional. optional final.

Hands down best professor I have ever taken. Nils allowed me to reschedule an exam during mental hardship which other professors did not honor. Class is not the easiest nor hardest, but if you attend class and prepare accordingly an A is achievable. Go to class, perfect your cheat sheets, and you will succeed.

Whoever doesn't give Nils a 4 or 5 is salty because they didn't go to class and couldn't teach themselves the material. Nils knows his content well, explains it well, and makes an effort to use examples his students understand and relate to. If you go to most classes and put in some effort you will get the grade you want. Take Nils, top 5 prof @smu

One of the best professors at SMU. I have no idea what the negative comments are talking about. His classes are optional but so enjoyable that you won't want to miss them. Definitely take him if you can.

Very chill professor, easy to learn a lot if you got class which is not required. Tests are not incredibly easy but you are given more than enough to prepare with and a front and back note sheet. Highly recommend for anyone
AWESOME
Worst, most useless class I have ever taken in my life.

Prof. Nils is awesome! He's funny and his classes are a breeze if you show up. Tests are chill, just study the slides and ask questions when needed. Linear programming can be tricky but he has office hours to help out.
Great professor, funny and knowledgable about subject. Tests aren't hard if you read through the slides and ask questions.

Professor Van den Steen an excellent instructor as he cares for students and gives engaging lectures. Attending class significantly aids understanding the material. He is generous with partial credit on exams, especially during review sessions so show your work. I'd recommend studying from the lecture slides, homework, and practice problems.

The homework was extremely minimal. This teacher is amazing- he is hilarious and very engaging during lectures. This makes the difficult material easier to grasp. The textbook is required but it is an online textbook through McGraw Hill. Participation is not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! Attendance optional but wanted to go because he gave such engaging lectures. Fun prof and very clear abt what is on tests (with practice problems) so you can do super super well in his class. Cheat sheets allowed for every test, optional final to replace lowest test grade. Best prof I've taken at SMU.

If you get less than a B in this class it is completely on you. Top 3 professor at SMU. Gives real world examples with everything he teaches. Tests aren't hard. Nicest and coolest professor I've ever had.
He was fantastic, with great energy and very reasonable tests!

Prof. Nils cares about all of his students, and makes an active effort to learn more about them outside of class -- there were multiple instances where I noticed him attending other org meetings, just because some of his students asked him. This class isn't hard, and attendance isn't *mandatory*, but it definitely does help you build on concepts!
AMAZING! Definitely take for Itom 3306. Engaging lectures with clear procedures, steps, definitions, etc. Homeworks are great preparation for the exams. Really cares about his job and his students.
There's a reason he has a 5/5 rating.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I truly do not have enough good things to say about Prof Van Den Steen. He is funny, engaging, creative, and truly wants to make sure those who want to learn will- and if you don't want to learn or go to class, he doesn't care and you still get participation points. Best professor I have ever had, wish he taught every cox class!!!

The lectures included example questions that the class worked through together, which was very helpful. The professor is great at teaching the material in a way that helps students understand & is accessible. There is a study guide provided for exams, which helps a lot and allowed me to do well on exams. I enjoyed the lectures, & highly recommend!

His lectures are p hype, you'd genuinely enjoy going to them although they are not mandatory. It speaks volumes when you have other professors that don't mandate attendance with empty classrooms. Regarding the material, it's pretty self-explanatory & putting an honest effort will get you the grade you wish.

Professor Van den Steen may be the best professor that I have had at SMU. Everything about his class is presented in a way that makes sense and doesn't waste your time. Also all of the homework doesn't take a long time and is there to help you understand the concepts discussed in class. He is super nice and actually respects your time.
My favorite professor at SMU. Very entertaining classes that are informative. If you go to class the tests are fairly easy. Would definitely take again for another class.

ITOM 3306 was a really hard course for me in general but Professor Van den Steen took the time to make sure all students understood the content and fundamentals. He really cares  and clearly wants to make sure every student is not only successful in his class but enjoys it as well - great at translating content and putting concepts into context!

This man deserves the world!!  I've never had a professor that cares as much about his students' well-being as well as their academic success. If you go to class you'll be fine, and the information I've learned is some of the most applicable and valuable I've learned in my entire 4 years without being unnecessarily challenging.

One of my favorite professors at SMU. All of his tests are straightforward, gives you weeks/month to complete homeworks that are very manageable to begin with. He teaches things in a way that you can understand what it means in the real world. Overall, he is so nice and fair. You have to study for the tests and you'll do well.
If you pay attention in class you will be fine. His tests are straight from what he teaches in class.

Nils is an amazing professor. I tend to use class time to do homework for other classes (sorry mom), but Nils made it difficult, because I was too engaged with the class. This is a topic that I was required to take and did not think I would enjoy, but Nils made it fun and exciting. He is so nice, and very funny. Success is not hard if you show up.

Professor Van den Steen, where do I begin? To say he cares about his students would be an understatement. He makes it a point to learn every student's name in a class of 55 people. His lectures are engaging (and funny), and his storytelling makes hard concepts interesting and understandable. His classes fill up fast for a reason. Take this class!

Nils is the absolute GOAT! He's truly one of the kindest professors that I've had in my four years at SMU. He genuinely cares about his students and is willing to go above and beyond to help you learn. 10/10 recommend taking his class- he's so funny, helpful, and empathetic!

Guys- he's awesome. Tests are through the connect online platform, so only your answer matters- meaning no partial credit w work. If this ends up hurting your grade- go see him! He's generous with the partial credit and will walk you through where you went wrong. Overall, great class- super fun and engaging guy with passion for what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking his class. He is actually the most hilarious and amazing professor here at SMU. I appreciate his commitment and care to the students and his job. The material wasn't the easiest for me but he help and explained everything in-depth. Best professor!

Professor Nils is one of the best at SMU. His lectures are engaging and he really takes the time to make sure everyone understands the topic before he moves on. Class itself is not too hard but you CAN'T fall behind or you will not succeed. This is by far the best ITOM 3306 professor!

He is such a great professor! His lectures are very interesting. I found the tests kind of hard even though I would study. The multiple-choice questions were confusing. 
But he's so funny and a great teacher. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go to class because its very hard to learn the material if you miss class.

Dr. Nils makes SMU a better place. I've never had a professor more caring and fun. Attendance isn't mandatory, but most people still come because of how great he is. I had little interest in the subject matter going into it, but he kept me engaged every single day and now I love learning about operations. I wish I could take this class again!

TAKE HIM! He is honestly one of the most caring professors I have come across at SMU. He is very fair when It comes to tests and homework and is very upfront with what he expects. You will not regret taking him for ITOM.

Professor Van den Steen is an amazing, genuine, kind, and caring professor. I was able to learn so much in his class while still feeling understood and supported. I also had fun with the in-class discussions they were always very entertaining. While attendance was not required, his class was enjoyable to go to and his lectures were helpful.

Do whatever you can to take Prof Nils. He's super fun and engaging in each of his lectures and he really cares about his students succeeding in class. He's constantly making genuinely funny jokes and is able to relate to students really well. Class definitely isn't mandatory but he makes it fun so it's often enjoyable. Definitely take him!

His teaching style is super interactive and engaging. Attendance being optional is a godsend, but class is never boring and is always informative. Nils really takes the time to explain the intuition behind concepts. As a bonus, he's dripped out in the coolest vests you've ever seen. Definitely recommend for anyone taking ITOM!

Professor Van den Steen makes the ITOM lectures very interesting, and he has a great sense of humor. He is very clear about what is expected on the tests, and he offers helpful review materials. He is willing to meet outside of class to discuss class material. It is clear that he cares about his students. The homework is very reasonable.

Created a rate my professor account just so I could rate him well. I absolutely love Nils. He is my favorite professor I have ever had at SMU, and he actually takes time out of his life to get to know students on a personal level. He never makes attendance mandatory, but he is so funny and such a good guy that you won't want to miss it.

Probably my favorite professor I have had at SMU. He is an incredible professor who really cares about this students and is always available outside of class. Teaches the material in a very understandable manner and makes the classes very engaging. I will recommend Professor Van den Steen until the day I die. Absolute SMU Cox icon!

My favorite professor I've had in Cox! Super engaging and enjoyable class with very relevant material that Professor Van den Steen made it easy to understand. I considered changing my major because I enjoyed this class so much

Prof Van den Steen is a slam dunk for ITOM 3306. I gave him a 3 because the homeworks are easy and he is extremely good at teaching the concepts, but in my opinion his tests can be a little difficult. Nothing too crazy, just harder than the homeworks. However, he's an incredible teacher and lets you take an optional final to drop one exam.

The best professor I've had at SMU. He genuinely cares about every student and wants you to do well. He is always available for help outside class and will even email you detailed examples if you ask. He is funny and entertaining in class and makes jokes to keep people engaged. I wish I could take him again!

Professor Nils was an incredible teacher throughout the semester. His outward passion for the subject and class was expressed creating an atmosphere that allowed students to find interest in the subject. I would 100% take Dr. Nils again especially as a Cox class. His ability to simplify a challenging topic proves his outstanding ability to teach.

Professor Van den Steen is the best professor I've had at SMU. He really cares about his students and tries to make learning fun and engaging. If you don't understand something, he will make sure to explain it a different way. Tests are challenging but if you pay attention you will be fine. If I could take him for every class in Cox, I would.
Amazing! Take his class you won't regret it!

Prof. Van den Steen is a teacher worth building your schedule around so you can take him, plain and simple. The material itself varies in difficulty and how interesting it is, but he always keeps his lectures engaging by including real life examples and humor. He is very clear on his grading criteria, and cares that you understand the material.
Good lectures, give plenty of practice problems.

This class is not my area of interest but this is prob one of the best professors at SMU. Many people make 100's on the exams not because the material is not difficult but because he really sets you up to succeed. Engaging lectures, you can definitely get an A if you put in the work (even though the cutoff is a 94), and not too much homework. 10/10

Professor Van den Steen is one of my favorite professors of all time - super caring and one of the most reasonable, flexible professors. He brings a ton of energy to a dry topic and is more than willing to work with students one on one. Meeting him after exams is also really helpful - you won't regret it. Runs a great class.
Really nice guy and cares about his students doing well

Professor Van Den Steen is a superb teacher. The class was overall easily manageable. The tests can be difficult (the mean on tests is about 80% ish). The most difficult part of the course though is McMillian Learning Game Modules (specifically modules 4 and 5). They are extremely time-consuming and I found it difficult to meet the dollar goals.

I couldn't recommend Professor Van den Steen more highly for ITOM3306. He's an incredible teacher who is dedicated, makes class enjoyable with his high energy and some jokes sprinkled in, and explains the concepts in a succinct way for all students to understand. He is also always willing to meet and help students do well with the material.

Professor Van den Steen is such a wonderful and kind professor! It's obvious he really cares about the success of his students and wants to make the class a great experience for everyone. Not too much homework, tests are straightforward and even the online operations games are kindof fun. If you have to take ITOM be sure to pick his class!

I never really found out how to pronounce his whole name so I call him Dr. Belgium lol, but I would recommend him to literally anyone. Hes an awesome professor that really listens to his students concerns and makes sure we really understand the material and do well on all the assignments and exams. I hope he finds his bike

Dr. Nils is a professor that actually cares about his students' success. He is willing to work one on one as much as needed, and will carefully go through previous assignments with you. He is understanding of your time and always takes you opinion into consideration. He is approachable and respected by all students. However, his can be tough.

Professor Van den Steen is passionate about what he teaches and seeks to ensure that students excel in his course. He more than meets students halfway. He frequently goes far beyond normal instructor deliverables to provide students with resources to assist in their learning. His teaching style is engaging and approachable. Students only need ask!
Great teacher who really cares about his students!

Dr. Wright was amazing and she is so so sweet! She does teach really fast, so rewatching lectures is sometimes necessary. Tests are not too difficult, just don't study the night before like I did. She does drop one test grade, which was really helpful for me. Final exam is a mix of all test questions from past tests with a cheat sheet!

Exams are so easy if you just pay attention in class, and she teaches FAST, so it doesn't get boring. If you watch reels/TikToks on x2 speed, this is the class for you. You can get away with studying the night before.

Dr. Wright was a great professor. Her lectures are pretty fast but she posts them online after so you can rewatch. I didn't take AP Bio so it took a little more for me to be able to understand. Reading the textbook outside of class is really helpful. She is helpful in office hours and gives points back on tests. She gives extra credit too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wright is a true gem in the bio department. The grading criteria is very fair, as even if you don't end up doing too hot on the exams (and she is a very lenient grader), you still have an opporutnity to make a good grade as homework/attendance/final project make up half of the class grade. Above all, she is very caring and passionate.

Dr. Wright is a great professor. Although she speaks a bit fast, her lectures are somewhat easy to understand if you go over the textbook and your personal notes afterward. She truly is passionate about science and makes content digestible. She gives curves on all of the midterms, and is super nice in office hours also! def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is the absolute worst and any positive reviews must be her or sarcasm. Terrible teaching horrible grading. Unfair af

Dr. Wright was a great professor! Always very friendly and willing to help me out each time I went to her office hours. She does go through lectures pretty fast, so I would recommend doing the textbook readings before class. She also gives out extra credit and final exam exemption opportunities. Tests are pretty straight forward!

Dr. Wright was wonderful - don't be scared by negative reviews. Yes, it is definitely helpful to stay on top of the readings, but they aren't too bad. Having taken AP Biology also helps. She changed her intro lectures to a sketchnotes style, which I found very helpful. She offers opportunities for extra credit and final exam exemption.

Good professor for bio 1301. Lectures are fast paced, but not her fault as there is lots of content to cover. I would recommend reading the textbook even though it is long, bc it really helps you understand the topics. Have to work for the A, if you took AP Bio should be a breeze. Also gives extra credit and is understanding if you talk to her.
Good teacher, if you put effort in, you can definitely get an A. Make sure to actually read the textbook, though, because that information is on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rachel is the most condescending and rude teacher I have ever had. I did well in the class, but I had to fake being woke in order to squeeze by. If she likes you, your golden. If not, pray.

She provides the resources needed and teaches all the content that is on the test. This is a foundational biology class, so she does have to go through a lot of content, so that isn't her fault. She could interact closely with students to make it more engaging. Take it if you do not mind studying/taking notes, or if you actually like biology.
AWFUL SO AWFUL. do not take her you'll regret your entire life.

This class was one of my favorites at SMU and it is largely because of Dr. Wright. The overall class is based on problem sets, exams, and participation and her exams are very fair. Everything she tests on she goes over in class and she offers a lot of partial credit because her exams are largely short answer. She's great! Fav professor at SMU!!!

Does not care if you pass or fail and contributes nothing to your success. Didn't do anything but lecture nonstop about nothing that would be covered on the test, speaks too fast and won't slow down no matter how many times you ask, and questions are ridiculously specific on tests that were never addressed.

Professor Wright provides all her materials on Canvas, and is very accessible outside and after class. The course is very difficult like all Biology courses, and the class is extremely lecture heavy. Overall she did a great job explaining all the concepts very clearly, albeit it got a bit boring sometimes.

I really enjoyed Dr. Wright. Yes her class was lecture heavy, but no more than any other STEM class. Her tests are extremely fair and material is straight forward. She even lets you have a take-home portion of the exam that is very similar to the homework sets. The best way to study for exams is to just go class, pay attention and take notes.
Lectures are hard to follow because she goes super fast. Tons of information but if you memorize the slides she gives, tests are manageable.
Lectures are very broad and tests are very specific so it's so hard to get a good grade on the tests and that's your whole grade. Wouldn't recommend if you actually want to get a good grade
Hate her sm. Ultra specific tests you will never do well on and she doesn't care.

The lectures were unpleasant. The test questions were too specific. It's hard to ace a test without knowing the material backward and forward and every detail of what would happen in hypothetical situations. Spent much time studying yet did not score higher than a C on a test. Other than that, she is very nice and cares about what she's teaching.

She is a good lecturer and person, however lectures go by really fast and are confusing in the moment. But, she posts all of her lectures online and they are similar to the textbook so it's helpful to read the text and rewatch lectures. Some test questions are very specific so that makes it hard but mostly okay and tests reflect lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Wright as a person and as a professor. Lectures were interesting and exams were very straightforward and fair. Attendance wasn't exactly mandatory, but she took note if you didn't show up for extended periods of time. Worst part of the class was the poster presentation that gave me anxiety all semester, got an A though.

Dr. Wright is a good lecturer and explains things well. She talks very fast and theres tons of content, but she does record lectures so you can watch later which is seriously so helpful. Tests are multiple choice, very content heavy (like any bio class). Bio is tough regardless but Dr. Wright was great
Dr. Wright is a great professor. Her class was engaging and educational, and I learned a lot. She is also easy to reach and responds to emails quickly. I enjoyed her class and would recommend it.

Professor Wright is a wonderful professor, I was very surprised her rating wasn't higher. Her class can be tricky and she goes fast during lectures, but she is very easy to reach and is very kind. She provides good feedback if you ask questions and is super approachable during office hours! If I could take her for bio 1302 I would!

Displays dismissive and defensive behavior and outright rudeness when confronted with dissenting opinions, clearly can't take any criticism, I would say worst professor at this school by a long shot, and does not help us learn and has an attitude and is sarcastic with students specifically those of us who are nonmajors...

I took Intro Bio 1 with Dr. Wright and could not help but notice that the class was not well put together. She would just read off of the slides, which were not very well organized. Because of this, the lectures were incredibly confusing, and I didn't feel like I learned anything in the class. And on top of that, she was not very approachable.

She needs to find another job: confusing lectures, inconsistent scheduling, and hard grading but all at the end of the semester so you can't complain on her evals. There is no structure in lectures and she does not know how to teach. Worst course I have ever taken and tanked my GPA. Rude attitude in her persona too, just a lousy experience.

It was her first time teaching BIOL 1301 and you could tell. She is a great person and is clearly knowledgeable, this level of bio just isn't her specialty so I think she just needs some time to work out the corks. Her slides are very long but tests are multiple choice and not crazy hard. She's always available for help.

I took her for Intro Biology II. She was a little disorganized in her lectures as they were a little hard to follow. I also thought the mandatory attendance was a little harsh. She is super understanding and kind, though, and she provides an amazing amount of resources for test studying.

I had her for Bio 1301, and she was AMAZING. Very clear guidelines and exams were very straightforward. She provides practice exams and other resources. After every exam, she makes a solution document that has every exam question and explanation. I learned WAY more taking her compared to dbrot.

If u want to go to a class where the teacher really doesn't care and reads off of her slides and doesn't act like she wants to be there, this is the class for you. She is horrible to talk to outside of class and has the worst attitude about everything. I wouldn't take this class if you could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wright was amazing for Genomics. Her tests were kind of specific, but after the first test, you kind of understood what her tests were going to be like. The problem sets got easier as we got used to completing the assignments, but because you get to work in groups, you struggle a bit less. She is nice and clear with expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a kind woman but she does not explain many topic clearly - she mentions things in class briefly and then expects you to read up and research on your own. Exams are hard and specific and she is very picky with your wording, and she includes material that was not talked about in class but is 'related' to the subjects. Very hard to make an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wright is one of the best Biology professors here. She is a tough grader but makes expectations super clear. Problem Sets(homework) are great for learning concepts before exams. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Wheeler is one of the most caring professors I've had at SMU (and thats saying a lot since I'm graduating this semester). She is incredibly knowledgable about the topics she teaches...she is very passionate. It's refreshing. Her teaching style is relaxed and entertaining. 100% would take her again.

Dr. Wheeler is an incredibly knowledgeable and caring professor! It is evident that she's not only passionate about medieval studies and learning, but also teaching and building up her students. Pay close attention to readings and come prepared to section with clear questions and ideas. A great course and professor that will expand your world view!
B needs to retire. Can't even give exams anymore use standard tech. Grades ridiculously. GPA tanker.

This class is one of the best at SMU! You will learn a lot, so be curious and work hard in the class. If you put effort into each assignment you will do well. There are weekly reading assignments and these, along with the lectures, will build the foundation for the class. Dr. Wheeler is a passionate and knowledgeable professor, engage in class!

Don't take! Our midterm: she showed up 20 min late, supposed to take online but she couldn't figure out lockdown browser, gave half the students the questions and the other half had to wait 20 more min, and did not give us full time for test and expected us to write 4 one paragraph responses, 3 paragraph essay, & 3000 word essay in 80 min.

Dr. Wheeler is a good teacher who genuinely cares about her students. You have to do the readings and be able to understand/analyze the content in order to do well. I won't lie, this class is hard, and I did consider dropping it, but I'm glad I didn't. She wants the best for her students and wants to see them succeed, but she won't hold your hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think she should genuinely resign for her own sake, as she is very old and it's reflecting in her classes. Nonsensical lectures, insane amounts of reading, and she never tells you that the class mainly consists of debates. She left us with no proctor on both of our tests. She once had Covid and instead of staying home, she came to class anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For King Arthur, you will be graded around 60% on debates (there are 4), make sure she likes you to get a higher grade because she has favorites, so go to the office hours, etc... There will also be a midterm exam and final exam so make sure you memorize the stories. She can be rude in a joking manner, so don't let it get to you. Lots of reading.

She is a nice professor and cares, but Please do not take Chaucer unless you have read/enjoy reading middle English. I was confused the whole semester; this is honestly the hardest course I've ever taken, the only way I passed was due to AI, and even then, it was challenging. Some students even dropped the course near the end of the semester.

reviews.comment: Have meaningful things to say during class & put real effort into assignments. She's a strange person but just go with it. Heard MANY troubling things from other students so keep a safe distance from her personally. Not good w/ tech be prepared to help set up a zoom. At least skim reading materials there will be a lot. You'll pass if she likes you

reviews.comment: She fits every bad criteria I could list on this website, the word count is too short to describe. Someone please fire her for our and her own sake. You will likely pass the class at the cost of your own sanity from endless readings of the worst stories I've ever read. I entered the class ready to learn about Arthurian legend and now I despise it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She knows what she is talking about. If you are an english major or truly interested in the class she is teaching, you will enjoy her. If you are taking her for a cc, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wheeler is a deeply passionate professor who cares greatly for her students. Her lectures encourage participation from students, and delve into myths and symbolism found in the readings throughout the course. Success is found in staying up to date with the reading, participating in class discussions, and showing passion for the material.

The subject itself was amazing and I loved her lectures as she's very entertaining. The class itself was stressful because there was so much to read and she gave random pop quizzes that were incredibly specific. The final exam was incredibly stressful as it was over everything we read over the semester and we couldn't take notes in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wheeler is a great person and was probably an amazing professor in the past, however, she asks students sometimes uncomfortable questions during lectures and is very rigid on enforcing the syllabus.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. IT HAS BEEN ONE OF THE WORST COURSES I'VE TAKEN AT SMU. Zero instructions, zero information on what the exam looks like.

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Genuinely the worst class I have ever taken.

reviews.comment: AVOID CLASS Should have been fired a long time ago, or at least retired. Makes students uncomfortable with personal questions that don't relate to the class. reviews.comment: Bonnie Wheeler might be the worst thing at SMU. Her inability to teach is coupled by the fact she has no idea how to use technology. (Students have to set her canvas up daily) Her lectures make no sense and don't relate to the readings. She Conveniently withholds grades until after add/drop, and is unwilling or unable to help with the final exam

I think Professor Wheeler was perhaps a great professor 20 years ago, but times have changed and she is not a modern college teacher. There is zero instruction and grades are seemingly pulled out of thin air. I took this class solely for the hours, and it has turned into a nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you absolutely have to. We were not allowed to take notes in class, and she lectures for the whole period and it is very boring. She is a nice lady outside of class, but tends to ask obscure questions that should not be asked in a classroom, leaving many students to be uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class, take the other professor if you can. This class has made me extremely frustrated and upset on multiple occasions. Bonnie is a very callous person and tends to make students feel uncomfortable in the classroom. Maybe she used to be a good teacher but no one in my class has felt that.
bonnie wheeler asks difficult questions on her pop quizzes. You had better study the reading assignment instead of just reading the required pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took this class during my senior year. After the first class, I tried to drop. I couldn't see how I was going to get through all of the reading, papers, etc. I am no Chaucer expert, but I managed. The reading is heavy, the expectations are high, but if I could do it, you can do it. Bonus: every other class will feel like a breeze after this one.

She may seem intimidating and difficult early in the term but by the end of the semester, the whole experience is worth it. She will make you work for your grade but do not have early doubts because by the end of the semester, you should be satisfied with your final grade. She is also very insightful in terms of feedback and explaining the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The reading is intense. The class are all discussion and she goes in circles and goes of track fairly often. She asks random questions and even when you give a response, she doesn't always acknowledge you. Overall its a fairly hard class that i would not recommend

Not only is this woman an amazing teacher but she has a heart of gold. Some of the past reviews are negative, however I must account this to an inability of the student to approach Dr. Wheeler as well as lack of initiative. At first, Dr. Wheeler can be intimidating. She is so intelligent! But get to know her and your world will be rocked!

I completely disagree with the previous reviews. She has a voice that is hard to understand; she talks in circles and contradicts herself constantly. Her tests are poorly written and her expectations prior to tests are not explained. I can appreciate aspects about most subjects and professors but this course didn’t have one redeeming quality.

Dr. Wheeler is, hands down, one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. She's terrifyingly smart and knowledgeable about her chosen specialty (Medieval Studies) and has astounding charisma when she's teaching. If you show interest and are willing to make an honest effort she'll do all she can to help you, but DON'T expect an easy ride.

Bonnie Wheeler is the smartest woman I've ever met...and I consider myself a darn smart lady.  I learned SO much from her and had a really good time in her class.  She expects a lot from you, but you'll gain a lot in return.

This woman is brilliant, but her teaching methods are not great. Stay away if you don't like public speaking - team debates and presentations are the bulk of the class. And she conveniently omits this information until the ADD/DROP date passes.
The absolute best two classes I ever took at SMU.  Not because of their ease, but because of how much I learned and grew through them.

Wheeler's courses are demanding, but rewarding. She always teaches with enthusiasm and a focus on the students. If you ask for help, she will give it. If you don't and do poorly (or don't do the work) she won't like you, but that's a Good Thing. If you want to learn, take her courses. If you want an easy grade, why are you in college?

No grades/notes posted online ever, always paper. Refused to post answer keys/review material. AVOID
