reviews.comment: DROP his course if you could. SCREENSHOT this comment because He is DELETING negative comments on this page. If you are in the core course, you can choose other core courses. He persuades the class to DROP his course once you cannot get any tuition refunded. I dropped his course because he said it's okay and I was terminated by ISSS (<9 hours)
tough

Professor Gao is amazing! Don't get me wrong, the class is still quite difficult and required large amounts of time. However, Dr. Gao is a genius and it's very obvious he knows what he is talking about. He is truly passionate about engineering and cares about his students. He's been available whenever I was confused or lost and was very helpful.

Go to class, learn the material, and you'll be good. She makes the class fun, but can also challenge you - shows she cares. Mad respect for Hu Lao Shu - not only as a professor but as a mentor type. Hands down one of my favorite classes from my time at SMU.
No no. Nooooooo

She teaches you how to speak casually and the meter of her speech is quite accurate to a native speaker. She does cold call on you, but you learn that way. She helped increase my speaking and comprehension ability. Def have to review outside of class, but if you want to learn on the of hardest languages in the world, it's necessary.
Professor lacks basic teaching skills. Doesn't organize lectures, goes off on irrelevant tangents. Unresponsive to student concerns. Avoid this class for a headache.
Such a great teacher. You need to take this class

Hu Laoshi is goated, so are all the other Chinese professors they're literally amazing. 3311 isn't an easy class but it doesn't feel overwhelming either. Hu Laoshi cares a lot about helping you succeed and the class keeps you on your toes but is honestly kindof fun. Lectures are awesome and you get a lot of practice speaking Chinese.

Best teacher ive ever had. She makes Chinese super easy and we learn so much in class. The only problem is the second semester is a little difficult because it involves writing characters. All the chinese teachers are great professors. I actually learn in this class more than any other class. Quizes every M/W/F that are short.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Hu is a great teacher who really takes the time to explain everything clearly and concisely. Really nice person who is basically like an older sister figure than a teacher. If you ever need to skip class or miss something, as long as you talk to her about it, she'll be fine with it.
Hu is the GOAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You'll probably find Chinese to be intimidating but Professor Hu and Professor Xia make the experience enjoyable. Professor Hu tends to play some videos at the beginning of lab that'll make you question some things but you'll appreciate them. She's caring and respectful, and by the end of the semester, you'll find her to be like an older sister.
Best Professor
Hu Laoshi is one of the best Chinese professors at SMU. She is funny and caring. She is also very encouraging and respectful.
Great Professor!! The class material is super interesting.   Have learned a lot of Chinese history knowledge through the different films.  Love it.   Attendance is MANDATORY!

Prof Hu is a fun and caring teacher who is from China and has understandable English. Chinese is in its nature hard for an English speaker, but Hu makes it easy and takes the class at a good pace. The homework is often but very manageable. Only complaint is very little emphasis or practice with characters in class.
Hu is awesome!!! adorable teacher and super nice. makes class as easy as possible and you learn a ton!

BEST teacher ever. Chinese is definitely difficult to learn, but Hu teaches in a way that makes the subject easy and fun! She is very passionate about what she does and cares a lot about her students. Hands down one of the best teachers I have ever had.

One of the best finance professor I have taken. Jinming is super nice and cares about the development of his students. His exams are pretty straight forward. The one thing I didn't like was that he picks and choose who to give back points after the exam.

Xue is a quality professor. Lectures are easy to follow, and homework sets are not too difficult. Participation matters slightly in this class, and he's mostly engaging with his lectures. Most of the grade is weighted towards exams. The better you do on an exam the higher weight that exam is (50%-40%-10%). Helpful if you mess up once.
Avoid at all costs. Professor is condescending, lacks empathy. Makes learning a chore, not a joy. Don't subject yourself to this educational torture.

FINA 4326: Jinming smiles a lot and makes the class very interesting. The content is very relevant and engaging. Exams are very similar conceptually to review slides, but he throws in curveballs to make sure you really understand the material. Exams are graded by TAs and higher exam scores are weighted more (30%-24%-6%). The final can be 6%

Xue is great! He can be a bit hard to understand at times but he always has an amazing attitude and wants his students to succeed. If you put the work in, an A is very achievable. Going in to ask him for help and working the problem sets are also very helpful.

I highly recommend Professor Jinming. He was able to communicate complex financial concepts in a clear and understandable way. He was extremely approachable and had a great sense of humor, making class both enjoyable and engaging. Also, his real-world experience and accomplishments made concepts even more relevant. Take him if you get the chance.

He is not only knowledgeable about the subject matter but also knows how to present it in a way that is easy to understand. He makes himself available for questions and provides additional help whenever needed. He genuinely cares about his student's success and it shows in the time and effort he puts into his teaching.

Investments was difficult and the material wasn't interesting but I appreciated how Jinming is passionate and knowledgeable. The problem sets helped, but the tests were difficult and most don't finish. I enjoyed being challenged since I didn't have much prior knowledge of the subject & Jinming is generous with grading so it ended being very fair.

I think hes an incredible professor. We get 3 free absences, and he was very understanding if we were going through something. He gives a lot of extra credit in class, if you answer a question you get a point and so on. Exams were challenging but it was honestly fun. It truly does depend on the professor, and he loves teaching

Attendance is good for the twice-a-week class, but you get 3 free absences. Rounds every exam so that the lowest grade is a B-. Class is hard across the board, but HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR TO TAKE COMPARED TO OTHERS. No quizzes and a few easy HW. Take him if you can.

You cant avoid him but classes are unbearable. he goes so fast, its chaotic cause no one can keep up. you have to take it for fina labs but waste of time, difficult for no reason. he goes so fast and is so mono tone you spend more time trying to get the answers right and copy down the screen than learn
Labs never ran for the full time. You have in class work, but the only thing that is graded is the Final Exam at the end.
Great prof, made FINA super easy and give tons of extra credit

Pay attention, study the MyLab and lecture slides, and you will do well.

You got one point!
You get one point
Just not a good teacher and would rather hand out As than do his job.
Informative class, to the point. Labs never run the full time, and are well managed. Problem is the final is the only thing that is truly graded, so you need a 95+ to make an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Daniel is an amazing professor, especially for business minors at SMU. He really takes the time to explain concepts, understanding that not everyone in the class has the same level of background in finance. His tests are straightforward and you know exactly what to expect. Tons of opportunity for extra credit - "You get one point!!"
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super kind and a great lecturer. As long as you know every homework problem and the lecture problems, you will be fine. Make sure to do good on all of the exams, as they average in the 80s. Score too low, it's hard to catch up to the top 25%. Also, joke: when you enter the class, take a shot every time he says "yOU GeT oNe POiNt!" Love this guy :)
i will have "you get a point" ringing in my head until i graduate.

sweetest person ever. walks you through all the labs and what will be on the final step by step (doesnt explain it the best, but its all excel). gives 30 extra credits points out each time if you say something thats already answered on the slides. goes through labs really fast tho. usually out of lab early. redo labs for final

Dr Yang has been a great addition to the Cox school. He has been so helpful during each lecture and office hours I meet with him. You get a lot of unexcused absences but engaging during class will get you extra credit. He is super knowledgeable and I am not afraid to ask him sometimes dumb questions.
She seems like a good person, and the tests are harder than the lecture material, but nowhere near impossible.
Her entire course is nonsensical and she doesn't even know what she is doing. What a joke, not for real business majors.
Such a sweet person with very intriguing lectures. You have to participate in class and be prepared for long test which are harder than the class content. I would take her again.

She's not my favorite but I would take her again. Participation matters but you just have to speak up throughout the semester. You get a notecard for the exam but she writes "trick" questions that can be hard if you don't actually understand the concepts. I learned the material instead of just relying on my notecard and easily got an A

I agree with the other reviewers that even though the course material is super easy, it can be harder to get a good grade based off of the way she makes the exams questions not very straightforward and does try to trick you (even though she says she doesn't). Overall easy prof and the class is pretty "common sense," but participation def required.

I think Professor Kimmons means well, but her tests feel like the ACT and are so hard and confusing for no reason. The class is fun and interactive, and the work is manageable, but the tests can be really challenging (even with a cheat sheet) since she tries to trip people up. You also have to participate in class to succeed and gain credit.

She makes it really hard to get a good grade. Some assignments don't make sense and hurt your grade. Efforts to seek help or clarification are often met with pretentiousness rather than genuine support.

Dr. Kimmons is articulate and organized, but I found her to be inflexible and very pretentious. While dealing with a parent's loss, I received minimal support—a two-day extension on an assignment graded harshly—and felt my struggles weren't considered in participation grading. More compassion would have improved my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought she was good just make sure to turn in all your homework. Only take if you are good with participation points and lots of interactive class activities ( nothing bad at all, just a lot of socializing)

Listen, I think shes a very nice lady and a good teacher. But I don't know, something just rubs me the wrong way about her. I don't know if its a tiny superiority complex or the way she conducts questions or feedback but there is just something I cannot stand about her. I would not take her again.

Kimmons is a pretty easy teacher. Her tests are a little tricky and she can be hard to know what she wants, but overall if you do all the work you should do well. She is very nice, but can be hard to get in touch with outside of class.

I loved Professor Kimmons! She made the lectures very engaging and uses a lot of good examples. Participation matters and there are 3 exams and a group project and I found the exams to be very easy if you take good notes. Highly recommend her.

Professor Su is awesome - he is very knowledgeable in what he is talking about but makes the content super palatable and provides a lot of data and real world examples. The class is graded off of 6 problem sets and 3 tests. If you study the problem sets and the reviews he gives you, the tests are super straightforward. Definitely would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved Yichen. Willing to sit with you and help outside of class during office hours. Make sure to see him when you're struggling with the material and he'll be sure to help you out. Learned a lot and would take this again.

Yichen is an extremely smart man. He explains things in a way that is intuitive and easy to understand. homework is extremely helpful. If you do the homework  you will get an A in the class. Not only did I learn a lot I retained what I learned. Highly recommended.

Really nice professor and is very educated in his field. Has 6 problem sets that are usually do on Thursdays at 5pm and post the solutions right after. 2 midterm and a final, for the midterms just study the problems sets and you'll be fine. Tough class to understand but you do learn a lot. New professor but I wouldn't mind taking another class.

New professor. Hard to follow in class so you have to go to office hours. A little rude and difficult grader and class average is a 70%. But he does genuinely like to teach and wants you to understand the material. If you show you care, he'll take care of you.

Hard to understand due to accent. Practice tests are previous year's tests that are near identical to the exams. I thought it was hilarious that the required textbook for the class that you work on homework out of was written by Dr. Xu. I missed class frequently, taught myself how to complete the homework and relied heavily on the practice exams.
This guy is like a father figure to me. Truly one of the best math teachers I've ever had in my life!

Dr. Xu is a wonderful professor. Scientific Computing is a notoriously hard class and he managed to explain it in a highly intuitive way. His tests are very similar to his practice exams, but challenging enough to make you think rather than struggle. He's also very understanding and lenient with grading and will make time to review with you!

Clear lectures that explains the concepts in detail (with useful examples). Lecture notes are posted on Canvas for each unit, so you can learn on your own if you want. Practice Tests are nearly identical to the tests, but the tests can be difficult since they take more time than you are given. 3 tests with no final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A decent professor who is clearly passionate about the course. Tries his best to make the material easy to understand. His accent really isn't too hard to understand and you get used to it pretty quickly- the people complaining about it are exaggerating. The course is graded by 3 midterms, one final, and a lot of textbook homework problems.
This guy can barely speak English. He brings a lot of energy to lectures, but it gets old and irritating after a while. Take at your own risk, not recommended.

DO NOT TAKE HIM!! He is the worst teacher I have had at smu. He doesn't speak very good english and I could not understand him. His lectures were very unclear and very unorganized. His tests were so bad. They were nothing like the homework or anything he taught. He would also blame the students when we wouldn't't understand something.

Dr. Xu is very passionate about teaching and is always full of energy for each class. His lectures are always organized and interesting. He has occasional quizzes which are easy as long as you pay attention in class. Make sure to study the practice tests and do the homework ahead of time and you'll be fine.

He is a very caring & funny professor to have, would take his course again. His tests are a bit heavy but you just need to study daily. He is very passionate and wants all his students to succeed, which is one reason he makes the content difficult. Overall, 5/5, one of the few professors I genuinely love!

Super sweet guy, I think he is the best option for scientific computing. If you have a coding/MatLab background you'll probably do well in this class. Gives good lectures and posts all lecture notes, attendance not mandatory but show up anyways, passing is a 55 and grades are adjusted accordingly. Good luck!

Professor Xu didn't care how hard he made Calc I compared to the other teachers. You can still pass if you stay on top of it but he never curved and he never took credit for any of the tests the class failed - always the classes fault for not studying enough. Stay away if you can. He's not completely unreasonable but he's clearly not concerned.

Professor Xu is a great guy and often pretty funny, but I would not recommend taking him for Calculus 1. If you have never taken Calculus before this class will be very difficult. The tests are not what we would expect from the lectures. He did buffer our grade a little with homework and easy in-class quizzes but majority of the grade was exams.

Professor Xu expects a lot from his students and does not explain calculus topics very well. It is possible to get an A, but you need to spend a couple hours a day learning calculus on your own. Would not recommend

I just recently dropped this class taking calc 1. I had never taken calculus before, but I'm fairly good at math. Many of the people in my class had taken calc before and on our last test the high score was a 69. He doesn't curve or give extra credit and makes passive aggressive comments about how students aren't understanding. I do not recommend.

Professor sheng is a caring and wonderful man. You can tell he's passionate about calculus and wants you to suceed. there is a lot of homework and the grading for it can be tough. the exams are also difficult but he provides practice exams that are somewhat similar to the exams. Show up and try in class, he truly notices it.

Scientific computing is difficult. Dr. Xu clearly explains concepts and does Matlab demos in class. Those will come in handy when working on homework. He does give quizzes every so often, but you only get 10 minutes to complete it. The tests are difficult, too. Dr. Xu does care, and he was (I think) the best option for teaching this class.

Very focused on the WHY and HOW of what we learned(honors course). Offered many visualizations of concepts to help. If you don't understand his teaching style he is not great at rephrasing/giving a different POV. Heavy accent but understandable. Listens to students' input (ie. cancelled HW due before test). HW every class. Easy quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is super hard regardless of the prof but Shang really tries his best. His practice tests are almost exactly like his actual exams, if you do really bad on a quiz he can drop the lowest grade, always accessible outside of class, doesnt take attendance. Quizzes are a bit difficult but they're online so you know the deal

the three tests are some 57% of your grade which is insane considering how difficult they can be, and he makes them super long and doesn't give enough time. projects aren't too bad, but the write-ups are tricky. at least he grades homework on completion I guess? that was the one good thing. Tbh I just finished and I couldn't tell you a single topic

This class was bad to take online b/c it was really hard to understand over zoom. TAs SUCK- no help at all. weekly HW for completion grades (all on chegg), 3 tests that are pretty hard, and 3 projects (code + report) that take a long time so START EARLY and really put effort into the write-up or he takes off a bunch of points. curves at end of sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is really hard, but Dr. Xu makes the best of it. His office hours are super helpful, and his test are easy if you study the material. He never asks anything he didn't go over. TA are terrible, but he knows that and makes up for it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: By far one of the best teacher at this school.
Class average: 76.016. A bit over half the class received a B or higher. Pretty stereotypical college class.

TAs are complete idiots, but Xu knows that and makes sure to curve grades at the end of the semester by a whole 5 points (!!). You can skip class all semester and do fine as long as you have previous (GOOD) programming knowledge.

If you don't go to class, you better read his notes which can be hard to follow without explanation. He does not curve any assignments but the overall grade is curved. He wants his students to succeed. His TA's gave wrong information, leading to low scores on exams. One piece of paper for each test. No final
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's really chill with attendance and gives practice exams that are extremely similar to the actual exams. He gives all of the necessary resources to get an A and has a very lenient grading scale. I can't see how anyone would find him bad!

Had him for Linear Algebra over the summer. Great professor who is VERY flexible and understanding. Lectures are a bit dry, but he's chill  you can come and go during lectures. Overall would recommend again. Grading is particularly easy and practice exams are SUPER helpful.

This guy is one of the most relaxed Professors I think I've ever seen. He's not one of those guys that loses his mind if you never show up to class; as long as you're doing well, he'll be perfectly happy with you. I hope I'll be able to take this guy again :-)

it started out like he was going to be some ordinary run of the mill prof, but especially during the week before finals he did his best to make things as flexible as possible for everyone. truly a caring prof!

Such a fantastic professor! He's really chill, and you can come and go to/in class as you please. Got papers? Lots of exams? He'll let you reschedule exams, he won't chop off your head or anything if you need an extra day for homework, etc. He is a phenomenal choice, and I'd take him a thousand times over again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took him for Diff Eq. Let me reschedule my tests when I felt swamped when no other teacher let me. Truly the MVP. Has an accent but I think its funny af and you can understand it. Dont have to go to any class but its helpful. Really good at explaining things. Only thing was that the tests were hard but I studied and did well.

Attendance is completely optional, and because the textbook does such a good job explaining the material, if you're a be-in-class-to-learn person, you can do that, and if you're a book-person, you can just skip. He lets you use old exams to practice, and he has a very lenient grading scale. Has an accent, but it's fine. Overall, a great choice!
Optional lectures, I just stop by to turn in the homework and go to class when I feel like it. 90% or above is an A, not that difficult. Has an accent, but it isn't that bad.

Do not take Xu for Scientific Computing. This class is supposed to be an easy A but with him it will be one of your hardest courses. You can't understand a thing he says during lectures, and if you try to ask a question he won't understand you and will just repeat the thing that you didn't understand. Projects are insanely hard, & im a cse major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He would be a great teacher if you could understand what he is saying in his lecture, he could actually give feedback during class instead of just writing on the board and making hand gestures. Also his grading scale is weird which can help with grades but the tests are hard kinda similar to practice exam but very little partial credit given

3 tests open book, 4 projects. Coding for the project does not take long if you have some relevant experience, but writing the reports takes forever. Tests aren't too bad, not too different from what he posts for practice or what is already in the lecture notes. Never paid attention in class and got a pretty decent grade, without too much effort.
He loves to test on theorems.. l would study like a crazy person and still had no idea what he was asking in the tests. lots of homeworks, and doesn't translate to doing good in test.
Good and helpful

mediocre linear teacher mainly because he is so hard to understand. the class has a great structure to it though with mandatory homeworks due most days, 3 tests, optional class attendance, great video lectures online, and the book is very helpful.

had him for linear algebra. he was a very good teacher. teaches very well and cares about his students. you just have to go to him to show you are doing the work. check hw with him, go before tests. do need to study from the book too and pay attention in class. practice exams help too but does not subsitute studying. does have an accent
good prof.  accent, so sometimes hard to understand.  really easy tests.

very nice guy. has an accent so difficult to understand. If anyone thinks hes too hard they have no idea what the other professors r like. I had Williams and dropped and XU s test r SOOO much easier and his class is alot easier. Calc in general is tough but if u have him hes so nice and will give u hw answers if u really ask for help
I have a hard time understanding him because of his accent. If you take his class, rely on teaching yourself

very nice man but has an accent and talks a million miles an hour... extremely fast paced and  difficult exams... class average for the whole year was a 50 so he had to change the grade scale so that a 50 was a C.

He's a nice guy but his accent is terrible! He's not clear and he's class is fast paced. He provides many opportunity for people to pass otherwise everyone would've failed his class. Overall I won't recommend him if you have another choice.
He's really a nice and easygoing person.........no final....3 inclass exam, open book open notes..

This is a class that if you do NOT go to very often, it will bite you. If you go to all of the classes, then the open book and open note exams are very easy. Labs are a breeze also, just act dumb and ask tons of questions and you can have the TA do it for you. Great teacher and a really good person! I highly recommend.  PS ~ NO FINAL
all my comments got flagged. just saying do not take this course

This class sucks. I've never had a professor that teaches material in such a poor manner (be prepared to teach yourself everything), with such painfully boring lectures, and tests that are extremely challenging and require more studying than any other cox class. Half of the class is memorization you'll forget the moment you finish.

Homework is easy, but the lectures are long and boring. Very grey class that is hard to pay attention to. You need to study a lot before the tests--the classwork to test layout is similar to prior accounting classes. VERY SMALL curve on tests (into 75% avg). 4 tests, 1 drop, and an easy final project. **get ready to teach yourself most of it**

Lectures are so dense and unorganized. the amount of JEs that you have to straight up memorize for exams is insane. I spend 20 plus hours studying for each test and still somehow manage to do so poorly. Even the alts kids sit in office hours and struggle. shes a nice teacher but just the worst class ever. i just want to pass at this point.

Provides detailed slides and lots of practice problems AND drops lowest exam, lowest quiz, and lowest 2 hw. All very crammable, but prioritize slides. Take advantage of OH, I went one time bc I didn't understand a concept and she dedicated 20 min re-explaining it to me. Not sure why ppl hate, she's a sweetheart and the other options are WAY worse!

It feels like every week you have to study something new in this class. This class is very overwhelming. She drops lowest exam out of all 4 you take. They are all equally as hard average exam grade was a 70 for the last exam. Office hours are not that helpful she seems burnt out from teaching. Lectures are stone cold.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is very overwhelming multiple pearson hwk some that have 20+ parts due every week, 4 quizzes and exams, paper and project due all in the semester. She is a nice prof but the averages on the last 2 exams was 70 and 73. She does drop one but she doesn't curve and the exams will go until the last min(18 MC/short math + 2-3 conceptual) in 50 min
Very nice person, but cannot write a test. Dumbs down lectures so I self taught everything. Tests sucked (don't put multiple choice on accounting with no partial credit on actual accounting problems)

Some of these reviews are a bit dramatic. Cox is a tough school at SMU, however, this class was by far one of the easiest accounting classes I have taken. She gives you a lot of material to prep for the exam and you should be fine if you study. She also drops a test, quiz, and homework. If you work hard and study, this class is an achievable A.

This is a very difficult class. Even though she is a very nice lady, the tests and quizzes will all come down to the last second. She provides study material to help you prepare, but she'll pick the most obscure questions to test you on.
Probably hardest class in your major and she makes it more difficult than it already is.

Insanely hard tests that you must study a minimum of 10 hours for. Purposefully makes the tests harder by picking specific parts of questions that you likely did not study and makes the test about 75 minutes of work with a 50 minute time period.

Nicest professor, very flexible with missing class, an entire letter grade of extra credit available. condenses difficult/lengthy subject matter into simple/concise. her exams are identical to in-class problems. her quizzes are nearly identical to in-class problems with a few curveballs

ACCT 3312 covers pretty tough material, but the lecture slides (all posted on Canvas) covered pretty much everything you need to know, and there are no curveballs on the tests. Prof. Yoon also gives a ton of extra credit opportunities for participation, end-of-class questions, etc. Honestly a really achievable A.

This teacher experience has been nothing short of disappointing, both in terms of time and money invested. It's hard to justify the expense when the quality of education falls short. I strongly advise against enrolling this instructor. Her demeanor is consistently rude and unhelpful when it comes to answering questions.
A complete waste of time and money in this school and for what we pay. Avoid. I do not understand where people enjoy this professor as they are very rude when you ask questions and most unhelpful.

Great professor who is very smart.
Do the work as required and you will learn a lot!
Remember, this is a Cox Business School class so the standards are very high.
To do well, be very diligent and do your best, not the minimum required.
Take her! She makes learning accounting easy. Grade criteria is clear. Go to class and study for tests and you will make an A.

TAKE HER! Intermediate accounting 2 is not a fun thing to learn. However, she does a great job to make it easier. Her lectures are clear and easy to understand as long as you listen. She explains the concepts well and all the needed materials are available in a timely manner. Her tests are straight from the lectures. You won't regret taking her!

Take this class, this will make your life easier. She tries to make the concept easy to understand and gives specific textbook pages to read. The exams were very straight forward, so if you know the concept and how to do it, you will get a good score. Just take this class, I guarantee you won't regret it.

Dr. Yuruk is an extremely kind teacher. She actually tries to make sure that every student understands what she is talking about in class, and her in class assignments on Friday really help comprehension of the topic. Attendance is a bit strict, so just email her. Homeworks are pretty tough and are not really on what we learn in class.
Helpful instructor,

Dr. Nurcan is an great instructor. She makes complex topics in Algorithm Design clear and approachable. Beyond classroom, she shows great care and understanding, especially when it comes to supporting students through family-related issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Note to RMP. The course number is not correct above. It should be 5350 algo eng. She covers many important ALGO topic you have to learn in CS.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Sweet woman who cares deeply for the success of her students.

I took CS 7350 - Algorithm Engineering from her. It was very engaging, and the algorithms (merge sort, I like) were presented in clear and enjoyable fashion. Be ready for practical examples for abetter grade Her explanations were effective. Active participation boosts your grade.
I not a non-cs student. I like her style of teaching. She solves many examples from the books before the exam. Overall, she is a nice person to interact with.

This class was just a mess; she didn't care about the students, but I feel like it's because the Intro CS courses at SMU are a bit of a joke. It's super easy; everyone should get an A if they do the homework. The "participation" tracked labs are sent to you, so you don't even need to go to class, and no lab either.

This class was honestly just a disaster. She does not put ANYTHING on Canvas except for exam dates. This makes it pretty confusing to know what's due. If you are missing an assignment in the class, good luck finding out which one of the 1000+ assignments in the textbook you are missing as she provides 0 feedback when she grades anything.

Nice professor but the lectures didn't really help. Used zybooks to teach myself the concepts and vocabulary. Focus on reading the book and definitions to prepare for exams. Coding sections are easy. Attendance wasn't mandatory until halfway through the semester. Final project was unexpected as it wasn't listed on the syllabus.

Never made it clear that attendance was mandatory but made a lab due each Friday that she coded in class throughout the week and would take attendance this way. She is very quiet so sit in the front of the room to hear better, but to be honest the class was a waste of time. Just buy a subscription to Zybooks and teach yourself.

Yuruk is charismatic and caring outside of class, but her lectures are impossible to follow and I didn't learn anything in class. The entire class is taught by a premade online course and the tests were really hard. However, I talked to her and she was lenient on my grade so I went from a B to an A. Also, she doesn't do minus grades, which is nice.
Attendance isn't mandatory. Make sure to study for the midterm. She's very quiet but very sweet. Make sure to not sit in the back, you wont be able to hear anything.
One of nicest professors at SMU. Wants you to do well and does a solid job at bridging the gap between complex concepts and your personal goals.

Bad professor. Disrespectful to students and rarely teaches. I have no clue how he still has a job. Attendance isn't mandatory for everything, but the final, and all lectures are just online videos. He makes Linear Algebra seem way harder than it should be.

This guy barley speaks English. His lectures are very hard to understand, long, and can be summarized in 15 minutes. You are forced to sit through them as you're scared of missing something important. I don't understand how his English has not improved after 20 years of living here. Class is asynchronous and easy to fall behind. Try to avoid prof.

All lectures are online and pre recorded, very hard to understand and doesn't care about you. He also spends more time figuring out how to proctor the final exam than he does actually teaching the material. He is also xtremely rude and condescending. Do not take him.

This dude's teaching style is so abstract, I highly advise taking this course somewhere else. The entirety of the class is online with online exams, homeworks and quizzes. The final is nothing like the previous exams and is so beyond harsh in material. With how conceptual and theoretical Linear Algebra is, you won't learn anything in his class.

The teacher could clearly care less about students. No in-person classes, no real homework or assignments, and the final was nothing like the rest of the class. Insults and belittles students' intelligence repeatedly when asked questions.

All his lectures are online and well thought-out. However, he teaches Linear Algebra in such an abstract way that his lectures only have ~15 minutes MAYBE of important stuff. It is far better to take another section or pay for an online lecture set. His final is in person in with a lockdown browser with only physical notes and harsh.

You learn via pre-recorded lectures and only go to class if you have questions and for the midterms and final. I only went to class outside of a test once and he was pretty rude/patronizing about students not knowing things. you have multiple attempts for HW & tests and everything is auto-graded. Not the hardest class, but not a helpful professor.

Took Professor Zhou for both MATH3304 Linear Algebra and MATH3302 Calc III. Homeworks, 2 midterms, and the final were all online with multiple attempts. For Calc-III, the midterms and final were all in-person. When I took LinAlg in 2022, just the final was. Pretty straightforward to do well if you spend enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GPA tanker

Entire class is take home open note except final, which is still open note. Never went to his office hours but heard he is very tough on students who attend. Final is pretty tough but he ended up doing a curve. If you can do the homeworks without using online you will be good for the final though

The overall class is not bad. Everything is online/take-home except the final. This is a good thing because you want to stay away from the professor. He is extremely condescending and rude to students. His hour lectures can also be explained by a 15 min Khan Academy video. If you need a professor to teach and explain things, don't take him.

Great professor. He had a flipped classroom so you watch his lectures outside of class and you can come to class if you need help but attendance isn't mandatory. He's very caring and wants you to succeed. Homework and tests aren't hard. Make sure to come to class at least for a little so that he knows you. Then he'll especially want to help.

Weekly homework assignments, the two midterms, and final are all online assignments, and you have multiple tries for all of them. You have three 1-hour online video lectures per week. Only time you have to go to class in person is the final. Easier than other MATH 3304 courses taught by other professors, but it requires a decent time commitment.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Literally the goat. 2/3 of our class got solid A's. Teaches asynchronously where he sends us video lectures and then has a small coding assignment due Sunday night every week. You get 12 tries to get a 100% on the assignments, and HW is 40% of the grade. Only time you go to class is for tests, and they're coding prob's similar to HW

This class is for people who already know the material. My class once raised an issue with him about the difficulty of the test, and he lectured us for 30 mins saying we were lazy and that the math was "elementary." The test average was a 68%. He later emailed us with "evidence" of one problem in a 400 slide presentation saying we needed to study.

Prof. Zhou was easily the least helpful professor I had this semester. He used class time to lecture with slides, but wasted time going on and on over unimportant material that wasnt helpful toward the tests. The only reason I passed this class with an A- was because I had already taken AP calculus and knew most of the material.

DON'T TAKE HIM unless you are a math major, or VERY familiar with calculus already. He doesn't explain things well, doesn't care if you fail his class. Doesn't answer your questions, and always says "this is elementary math and you should know this" 0/10 would not recommend
Weekly homework which was not too bad, but the tests were way harder than the homework. Hard to contact outside of class, and doesn't care whether students fail or succeed.
Do not take him. He is terrible at explaining things and skips slide full of integral information.

Do not take this class unless you are already very skilled at math and are familiar with the material. The teacher is disrespectful to anyone struggling in class. When the class became optional, he wasn't even in class most of the time (one time, he wasn't even on campus yet). His accent is fine, but he organizes his lectures strangely.

Scientific Computing is a hard class in general, but Zhou made it a lot easier than the other professors who teach it. Your only grades are the exams and the labs. He does in class examples that you can adapt to match the labs and the exams, so if you can do the labs, then you can do the exams. The entire class is just coding python.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although Professor Zhou has a pretty strong accent, it can be gotten used to with time. He seems to create a very intense classroom dynamic with few students feeling comfortable to answer questions. As a professor he seems rather unapproachable and can seem irritated when students do not understand content. Overall indifferent to student success.

Professor Zhou does have an accent, which took time for me to understand. I had the MWF class and it was the most intense note taking I have ever done. He speaks very fast and writes all over the whiteboard. Most of the time I did not even understand half of the notes I wrote. You have to put in work to do well. There are three exams and the final.

Not a good professor at all. Mostly didn't stop in lectures for questions, and when he did, he was visibly upset by the answers. Disrespectful to students' time. Grading criteria is only four things: test 1,2,3 and final exam
he has accent, but clearly understandable. if you don't miss classes and do homework and practice exams, you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class average: 82.135. A slight majority of the class received a B or higher. Pretty stereotypical college course.

Terrible prof. Extremely hard to understand (not just the accent, but he literally doesn't pronounce half his words correctly), the four tests are 100% of the grade, doesn't seem to care about the students. Goes very fast, does not stop for questions, making it difficult to keep up. Also mentions things from Calc 3, not a prerequisite for my class.
I wouldn't recommend going to class because he lets you use the Internet and textbooks on the exams. If you can do the projects without much help, you'll nail the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good prof, but doesn't seem like he cares either way how people do in his class. Accent is difficult to understand, so it will take some getting used to. But anyone who is having difficulty in the class is having difficulty because they just don't understand anything. Projects are free 100s.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He has extended office hours and provides all of the necessary resources to get an A, but he is very indifferent with regards to his students. He doesn't seem like he minds either way if you get an F or an A. The grade breakdown is clear, but due to his curving and awkward letter scale it isn't clear what you need to get what grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really poor professor. Very hard to understand in class due to accent. Not overly carrying towards student - will "teach" and that's it. Tests are a dumb 95% of your grade too. Take him at your own peril, would not recommend.

His accent can be hard to understand. Very focused on proofs and not application of the material. 95% of the grade is from tests. He would have to backtrack a lot because he forgot to mention things in class. Does not collect homework. Tests are pretty easy because he tells you what the problems will be but you have to learn the material yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He gives very boring lectures but you can use any notes you take on the exams (and sometimes problems are exact duplicates). He is a nice man and helps you during office hours. Homework is completion. Exams are 95% of your total grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a caring professor, who truly wants students to succeed. His extended office hours are super helpful. His accent doesn't interfere with my learning. The practice tests are great tools for exam preparation. THE material is DIFFICULT, EXPECT TO DO HWs and UNDERSTAND FULLY. MUST ATTEND LECTURE TO PASS

Yunkai Zhou is very hard to understand, and very hard to get clear answers from. Calc 3 is difficult material and his tests consist of theoretical questions that are not related to practice tests, homework, or the text book. One of the worst professors I've had at SMU, and the worst math class I've ever taken.

I took Zhou for differential equations and it was a very doable class. He teaches in a way that encourages students to think for themselves about the math they're learning as opposed to straight up telling you the formulas and answers. I see how this can be frustrating to some, but regardless of this he provides all necessary resources to get an A.
Professor Zhou's class was a great experience. I took him for Diff EQ, and I will definitely look for his classes in the future. His grading policy is very fair.

I'm not certain as to how one could complain about this class. The material is tough, but the class is a classic case of having to put the time in to do well. Homework is only 3%, but students should definitely do it. Some test questions were extremely reminiscent of the homework questions and the practice tests given. Accent is understandable.

One of my favorite professors at SMU. Is really helpful and genuinely wants students to succeed. Walks through proofs clearly and makes sure that test questions are consistent with lectures. he may not be the easiest professor, but his teaching style makes sure that you know the material. I have taken him for Calc 3 and Dif Eq: both good classes.

One of the worst math professors I've ever had. Blatantly embarrasses students in class by sharing failed grades and consistently makes rude comments towards students about "stupid questions." Avoid at all costs.
Can barely understand a word he says, can't believe they allow him to teach here.

I am a hardworking Math major. However, I would not recommend this class. He is not very helpful for those students who have trouble w/the material. His tests are not only on material but on abstract concepts dealing w/class material. The class material is NOT HARD. It's the tests w/abstract concepts that are hard. Practice tests minimally helpful.

He was definitely my favorite math professor so far at SMU. He lets you bring notes to the test, and if you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. He also curves all of his tests and has three practice tests online for each test. He also lets you bring notes to the final. I highly recommend him.

Professor Zhou is awesome. He does have an accent, but it only takes a few days to decipher it. He gives you 3 practice exams for each of your exams, and they are very similar to the actual tests. He gives a ridiculous amount of partial credit, and he always has at least 10 bonus points on each exam. Take him!!! You won't regret it!

Dr. Zhou is just the sweetest man! Once you figure out what a "prane" is, his explanations are perfectly clear. Also his graphs are well-drawn and easy to interpret. After the very first day you get used to his accent and he's very clear and helpful. He wants his students to learn, but the tests are still fair and he gives generous "pasha" credit.

If you remember absolutely everything you learned in cal 1 & 2 your golden. for those of u that dont he expects u to and counts major points off if u dont even when the new stuff is all right. he also makes from inappropriate comments about "american students". i would never take him again
No Comments

Sometimes he's a bit hard to understand but i didnt really go to class and never studied and i got a B+ easy; if i had gone to class i'd've prolly gotten an A. my bad. he gives daily hw and tests are a little difficult but pretty simple if you study.

Dr. Zhou is really smart. It took a while to get use to his accent, but he speaks very good english. His practice exams are exactly like the actual ones and he grades very fairly. He curves and even offers to push back homework due dates!!

Had to withdraw from this class to save my GPA. His lectures are hard to follow as he doesn't explain the steps he is taking to solve a problem or explain concepts thoroughly. He is friendly/encourages questions but his responses are often confusing and don't clarify anything about what you're asking. Exams were much more difficult than homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super responsive to emails and in-class questions. Drops some homework and stuff at the end to help with the grades. Obviously super smart, can sometimes go fast or move on when people are confused but if you aren't afraid to ask him to go back and explain he will. Super chill in class but diffEQ is still a tough class so outside work prob required

Absolutely awesome teacher. Can be a little tough to follow in class but overall great experience. Textbook is free he gives the link to the class. HW is 45% of grade so it should be pretty easy to get a decently high grade.

Sometimes hard to follow during lectures. If you really take the effort to watch videos on the topics taught in class to review and attempt the homework you should be good. I averaged about 6 hours of studying per midterm because testing is the main bulk of the grade. Definitely recommend going to office hours he's super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doesn't do a great job of answering questions and skips steps on the board because he does them in his head. Tests are generally harder than homework. Survived a semester of this class but be prepared to do a lot of self-learning after class.

he's nice but you WILL have to teach yourself the content. he would often run out of time and not go over concepts that would be on the exam, or there were very detailed questions on things we went over for a sec in class. there's a presentation and a few quizzes. only upsides are the extra credit and him dropping our lowest exam score.

information overload. prof is nice but not the most direct or clear with teaching content. Lectures are hard to follow and 80% of the information isnt relevant to the tests. tests are hard and its impossible to know what exactly to study because there is soooo much random information presented.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the best!
Professor Wu is incredibly kind and friendly, however he's not the best at presenting information (sorry

He is a nice professor, but he is not a great teacher. I spend a lot of time outside of class teaching myself concepts because he is not very great at explaining. He also requires us to present on scientific journals with lots of jargon without teaching us how to understand them. Not a hard class but have to work hard to understand what's happening

He is a great professor! His tests were fair, and there were plenty of opportunities to improve your score. He provides quick and helpful feedback on any questions, which really helps students stay on track and understand the material better.

AVOID HIM COMPLETELY!  I worked in his lab and he is the worst human being I have ever come across, worst teacher I know, and all he does is talk nonstop all lecture about stuff thats not on his exams

Such a kind professor who genuinely tries to make a hard topic easier to understand. Pay attention in class and learn the slides and making an A in this class will not be that difficult. He also has a bonus opportunity and really wants all his students to succeed! i really enjoyed his class.

He is a very kind professor and is trying his best. I relied heavily on the textbook because his slides seemed chaotic and badly organized for the first 3/4 of the course. Going to him 1 on 1 was very helpful, and he always responds quickly to emails. His tests were pretty fair, and there are a lot of opportunities to beef up your score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great Instructor who wants his students to succeed! One of my favorite instructors at SMU!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took his bio of the brain class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The first test the whole class bombed at it was also 20% of the grade. Man goes on for an entire lecture and says not going to be on the examination.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a true expert in his field and is one of the best in the biology department. He goes through stuff quickly but make yourself pay attention and you'll have the notes you need for the exams. If you understand the material you'll be fine on tests.

Best biology professors Ive taken. Respectful. I highly recommend. You must put in effort and do your part in order to pass the class with good grade as usual. He gives breaks during lectures, & asks every student if they have any questions over the material. The textbook is not needed, but I do recommend getting it.
Very unprocessed in demeanor and how he approaches teaching. Uses the time to talk about himself rather than the material. Does not know the material well and maybe that's why.

Yoram is one of the few professors where the framework he teaches actually rewires how you think. Fall in love with the problem, not the solution — sounds simple until you realize how often you've been doing the opposite. That alone can save you years. He genuinely cares about his students. Would take him again without hesitation.

Yoram is one of the most impactful professors I've had. He pushes you to think deeply about evaluating businesses and not take ideas at face value. He truly cares about his students' success. I'll always remember his mantra: don't fall in love with an idea. He's always willing to engage, challenge your thinking, and help you grow. Highly recommend!

Professor Solomon's class is engaging, interactive, and practical. He challenges your thinking, encourages participation, and emphasizes resilience. The group projects and final pitch deck are fun and valuable. He's a great mentor outside of class, knowledgeable, approachable, and I'd definitely take his class again! Wish he taught other courses!

Yoram Solomon is one of the best instructors I've had. He gives practical feedback, emphasizes real understanding, and uses hands-on application. He is direct but respectful and generous with his time. Great for students who want to learn and improve.

Dr. Solomon is a fantastic teacher and routinely makes himself available to help students outside of class. His Evaluating Entrepreneurial Opportunities class was group project heavy and required a lot of time to complete assignments, however, it was a great class from which I took a lot from. I am applying many class lessons to my own business.

Favorite class at SMU! Lectures were engaging and made the 3-hour sessions fly by. No quizzes or tests—just a semester-long group project with checkpoints, which let us really absorb the material. Grading can be tricky, but Yoram is super helpful if you meet with him. Highly recommend to anyone even slightly interested in entrepreneurship!

Dr. Solomon was the best professor I have had at SMU so far. His course requires meaningful time outside of class with your group, but the work is engaging and allows for real creativity. He truly cares about his students, gives honest feedback, and makes the class really enjoyable. I looked forward to going to this class each week.

Yoram Solomon is a great man and professor. The class at the time was undergoing a transformation of sorts where in the structure was shifting to more of a hands on approach. But if you want to learn more about the journey of an entrepreneur and want to test/validate your ideas, this is the best class to do so. I recommend taking this class.

Yoram was the best professor I had in the program - this class was extremely immersive & engaging, & the high participation made for a tremendously productive 7wks. This class contributed to the job offer I recently received and I am very grateful for my time with Yoram. I know everyone in our class feels the same with regard to Yoram & this class.

Taking the Corporate Entrepreneurship course was an amazing experience. The professor was very present, attentive to detail, and always willing to support students. I learned excellent frameworks and received valuable feedback on my work. He also took the time to help me with a challenging project from my internship.

Professor Solomon's energy, humor, and practical exercises keep class engaging. Workload is reasonable with weekly readings, discussion posts, and group projects that build to a manageable final group paper and presentation. Stay on top of deadlines, use AI wisely, and you'll succeed. Fantastic class with real-world insight and practical takeaways.

Professor Solomon is an engaging lecturer who uses real-life examples to teach entrepreneurial evaluation. He ensures fair grading, accepts no late work, but provides ample warnings. He's highly accessible, dedicates time to help students, and inspires through his teaching. Highly recommend taking his class and leveraging his support! An SMU Gem!
He's rude and dismissive making learning difficult. His lectures don't stay on track and he's terrible at answering questions, Would not recommend his class seek other options.

A lot of work and unnecessary lectures that he makes SOOOO boring. Not as nice as he seems either when you see 
him in office hours. Phony.
So. Hardcore. For what. NEVER have I made a B in my entire academic career. When there are YEARS of patterns, the problem isn't me, it's you, professor (if that is what we can call you).

Professor Solomon's class was highly engaging, and participation is essential for developing creative ideas. He provides useful tools that have real-world applications, making the course both practical and insightful. I also appreciated his encouragement of AI tools, which added a modern, innovative approach to learning.

Yoram's class is very difficult due to the HW time-commitment. His goal is to prepare us for starting our own business, which is arguably the hardest thing someone can do. I would have preferred the class to be a full semester long, because the deliverables were due on a very rushed schedule, so try to make a team where everyone pulls their weight!

Yoram is the best CISB prof I've had at SMU. Extremely impressive background, interesting, & always available for help/advice outside of class. This class involved weekly readings & quizzes (open note), discussion board posts (100% if you submit on time), group assignments, and a final group pres. Easy A and 10/10 recommend getting to know him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would never take his class again and warn ALL OF YOU not to either. Studied for 10 hours for each project and never got an A. He ruined my GPA.
Adjunct level teaching.

Doesn't have any actual business knowledge or connections in the field. An embarrassment to cox. Take someone who has prestige with the business community as you will need it upon graduation. Yoram is not it.

Yoram's class was excellent. His hands-on approach makes learning entrepreneurship both exciting and practical. He's always supportive beyond the classroom, offering guidance whenever needed. If you're looking for a safe, average path, this class isn't for you. But if you're ready to innovate and take risks, his mentorship is truly invaluable.

All he does is lecture all class, make non-funny jokes, over complicates vocabulary to TRY to confuse you. He IS NOT willing to help. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS - It will cause an IMMENSE AMOUNT OF STRESS.

Yoram is an amazing professor. He has years of experience and is always eager to help his students both in and outside the classroom. While an A is highly attainable if you attend class and do the assignments, the weekly assignments can be time consuming. Overall, I would highly recommend any opportunity to take a class with him.

Very unclear grading criteria,, absolutely boring "discussions" where he expects us to teach the rest of the class. His snarky comments to people who disagree with him are unprofessional DO NOT TAKE (he's a bad teacher). I couldn't wait for her class to end.

You have to work harder to get a B than to make an A. His instructions are clear and direct. You don't get to choose the topic but if you want to learn how to make a business plan or start a business, take this course. Yoram is so committed to his student's success even outside of the classroom. SIGN UP FOR HIS COURSES.

Professor Solomon is knowledgeable about starting businesses and knows what investors seek in a pitch. He provides great resources throughout the course and gives a fair opportunity to increase your grade. His lectures are interesting and informative; he is very enjoyable and passionate about the subject and inspires his students to succeed.

I have learned a lot and also had a lot of fun from this class. It was very practical and used all the different concepts and knowledge I learned from my other classes. The focus on creating a business plan has a unique perspective compared to the typical strategic case studies. The class was engaging and we had a lot interesting conversations.

The program emphasizes logical thinking, active class engagement, and extensive home practice in executing various business plans. The experienced professor, a seasoned entrepreneur, serves as both instructor and mentor, offering valuable insights from founding to financing companies.

His class is a waste of time, he teaches only through his own self-published materials, he is ridiculously concerned about his online reputation (he reads these and uses class time to talk about them), and he's an adjunct yet with the confidence of a Nobel prize winner. The course is like a self-paced internet course except somehow less useful.

I highly recommend this course for anyone looking to start their own business! Dr. Solomon was very engaging, always relating back his lectures to real world examples and to each student's industry/firm.
Pros: Clear grading, extra credit, great lectures, writing & presenting a business plan
Cons: Weekly group work can be difficult to coordinate

Yoram is a very knowledgeable and engaging professor of Entrepreneurship. His analogies and examples for class concepts make greatly illustrate how some key business practices work. Also, his grading is fair and a leans toward the easier side. A very good class. Highly recommend!

Professor Solomon does an excellent job creating a class designed for first time entrepreneurs and well beyond. There was no point where I thought, "I shouldn't ask that now". The flow was well designed. Workload was completely manageable as I was working fulltime, finishing my MBA and launching my own business.

Arguably the most meaningful class of my academic career! This class brings the value an MBA to life through practical application of core business/finance concepts. Professor Solomon is incredibly engaging, cares deeply about students and forces you to think strategically about products, markets, business models, and competitive landscapes.
Received feedback from the professor that prepared me for the practical world of entrepreneurship and the projects we did gave confidence and prepared us to face the real world setup.

Very practical, hands-on class! Professor Solomon wants students to learn concepts, ask questions and succeed. That's why he makes himself available after class hours.  Highly recommend this class if you're interested in the steps to starting a business -- especially if you like classes based on real-world experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Since I've been at SMU, Professor Solomon has definitely been one of my top graduate professors at the University. He clearly defines all expectations for assignments and gives a rubric to eliminate any confusion. His in class assignments made the class exciting and engaging. He actually cares about his students!

Professor Solomon provided an amazing learning experience in the Corporate Entrepreneurship course! He is extremely personable, cares deeply about all his students, and tailors his lectures very well to professionals that want to advance their careers. Very discussion based, but the questions posed really exercise your brain in the best way.

Professor Solomon is hands down one of the best professors I've had throughout undegrad and grad school at SMU. He teaches practical applications of key concepts and frameworks that can easily be applied and he brings a unique perspective given his background includes experience at both enterprises and startups. HIGHLY recommend.

I learned a ton and had a very positive experience in this class. The professor continuously challenged our assumptions to teach us how to think critically and launch strategic business initiatives within organizations. He brings real life experiences that help you understand how to navigate your way through the corporate environment.

He inspires a lot of creative thinking and uses more of his own experience, as well as fresh news or cases just happening, rather than the 1990s HBRs. He has logical methods and teaches practical skills!

Yoram's class was interesting and his humor helped relax the class. The big group project (Final) of creating a business plan was broken down into sections for each week and he provided helpful feedback each time. The effort needed and grading were fair, not too easy or hard. I highly recommend this class for anyone wanting to learn business plans.

I absolutely enjoyed having Yoram as a professor! He made the class exciting and engaging. From the first day, he makes his expectations clear. The only way you will not pass is you do not make an effort. He is more than willing to offer meaningful feedback as you work on projects. He truly cares about his students & I appreciated that!

Yoram's approach in class is like an advisor/mentor. I prefer this approach because it helps create a space of understanding and helps you obtain the necessary knowledge for starting a business. There are golden nuggets of information that can help you and this class is a must take if you want to pursuit a business.

This was an elective credit I took for my program. We had fun during class and everyone was very engaged. The atmosphere was relaxed; the pressure of some vigorous business courses was off and you actually learned something you'd retain and apply to your professional decisions. I do recommend this course!

He is straight forward and grades fairly. Some required classes you wonder what is the point of this class more than likely I will never use what I learn but not this class. If you are looking to start your own business one day I strongly recommend you take him. His classes are very fun and interactive you won't be bored and will learn alot.

Yoram is a great professor who is able to use his own entrepreneurial experience to provide quality lectures and transparent feedback on classwork. don't take his class.
