reviews.comment: Thinks he's funny and cute and he's annoying ahl
Doesn't teach at all, gets by on "quirkiness" and trying to be cutesy...
Very nice and explains well for an intro class
Doesn't really teach well. Performs. Not the standard we pay for.
Pretty hard to learn from and hard to get in contact with.

Weird af and into dinosaurs for some reason. Doesn't really teach and gives everyone As which is why he's popular. Not learning anythin so you're basically paying for an A and that's it. Basic SMU I guess.
literally the easiest class ever. funny professor, super lenient, as long as you turn in your work, you'll get an A. he also brings a dinasour to class which is kinda weird
Calc 1337 Easiest class of my life. Got a 105 and never once listened in class. no homework. mock test was the exact same as real test.
You will learn nothing on his class and he acts like an overgrown child.

This professor is great!! Easiest calc course ive ever taken! He his so caring about his students and making time if you need help! Very easy grader and wants his students to succeed! 100% would take again! The lectures are very boring tho but he trys to make it fun!

He is the sweetest teacher ever. Honestly one of the best math classes I've ever taken. He offers a lot pf extra credit on tests and homework. He truly loves math and has the best dinosaur collection ever!! He is also super funny!!

A professor that does it for the love of math, hilarious, kind and encouraging. Do your work and do your best, don't be scared to ask questions during exams he does his best to clarify questions to give you the best success chance. Wish I could take him for Cal 2 and 3! Loved his dinosaur collection!

I had him at Tarrant Country College for Calculus 1. Hands down the best professor I've ever had. He gives lots of opportunities for everyone and always finds ways to make you feel good at the end of the lecture because of his jokes and life advice. Teaches with passion and makes the subject come alive! 100% recommended!
A complete joke and waste of our time, disrespectful.
The academic equivalent of a broken elevator: unpredictable, frustrating, and always going down. Assignments are booby traps, feedback is insults in disguise, and lectures are just noise pollution.
LOVE LOVE LOVE PLEASE TAKE HIM IF YOU WANT THE EASIEST A TRUST ME!!!!!!!

Never went to class and ended with a 108% in the class. he made all the tests take home and offered so much extra credit. really really easy i suck at math and this was an easy A. Def recommend him!!!!!

This man is pretty interesting to say the least. He refers to us as young padawans, makes multiple anime jokes, and calls me bro in the hallways. That being said, he is caring and strongly curves all of his test grades. If it weren't for the curves, I would have a 50 in the class. If you are actually good at Calculus, this will be an easy A.
unhinged and you won't learn anything

i'm writing for math 1303. This was the easiest class I have ever taken. There is so much extra credit, I haven't attended class in 2 months and I have well over a 100% in the class. The pratice exams are like the actual tests and it is just such a free class. He is super funny too, he loves dinosaurs. Makes me laugh all of the time. Awesome man.

At first I though he was extremely cringe which he is with his toy dinosaur that he shows off every day, but a lot of the stuff he does is also hilarious. He's not that great at teaching the material, but he's such a generous grader and lets you use notecards on your tests. His easy grading got me through the class and i'm not that good at math.

In terms of teaching, not great, but he is a really nice and funny person. Although, please if you've never taken calc before like in high school, don't take his class because I promise you won't know what to do. He does do everything in his power though to give literally everyone an A, so take that as you will.

If you want a chill professor who gives lots of partial credit and is generous grading, then take him!

But if you work best with strict professors, then maybe not for you.

Yea, he's a bit narcissistic and full of himself, but who at SMU isn't lol?

This man's a saint. He's literally like the math Jesus. Gives you too many opportunities to redeem yourself and do good. Almost too much for his own good. If anything, I suggest he be harder next time and not give so many opportunities. Don't be afraid to give Cs, Ds, and Fs.

Lectures seem to focus on his personal need for validation rather than the material. He talks endlessly about himself, aiming to gain approval from students half his age. It's cringeworthy and distracting. His counseling background shows a lack of academic depth, making the lectures increasingly unbearable.

I took him for pre-calc for business. You don't need the textbook or show up for class. His tests are just like the mock tests he provides, and he also allows you to have a "cheat sheet" on the tests while also giving insane amounts of extra credit. This class is an easy A, but I'm worried about business calculus next semester.

Such a sweet and funny guy and grades very easy. Tests are the exact same as reviews and homework is pretty easy. Only 7 homework assignments due in the whole semester and he gives out A LOT of extra credit opportunities. Also he didnt make us buy the textbook. Would def take him again!

This dude is hilarious. Always making pop-culture references and LOVES to bring in toy dinosaurs. While it's not genuinely funny, more people should laugh at the jokes because he really is trying to make the class laugh. Class is pretty easy with weekly homework assignments and a few tests that are EXACTLY like the practice tests.

Probably the most chill teacher I have ever had. You could skip every class and still do well because the study guides are the exact questions on the tests with the numbers changed. He is very understanding and if you tell him you wont be in class he doesn't really care. please laugh at his jokes though.

I took him for Calc 1. He is super funny and incredibly understanding. I wish he posted his notes or lectures online, as he does not post any of his lectures so if you miss class you miss out on it. He is clear with grading and makes lectures intriguing.

This guy is quite a character, a bit quirky but in a good way. I like how caring he is and super flexible with homework and deadlines. Make sure you do the review questions!!!

He also has dinosaurs in his desk who "help" him grade and answer emails , lol...

The guy cannot teach.  I usually love my professors and school, but this professor is the worst. You have to do so much work to even pass this class and some of us are only here for the credit. Absolutely the worst teacher I have ever had and is not as funny as he thinks he is. Spend less time with the jokes, more time teaching.

It was his first year teaching the class and his lectures had room for improvement but he's very clear about what he expects and he doesn't surprise you with things on tests. If you can follow along homeworks and study guides you can easily get an A. Not an easy class at all but he doesn't make it harder, he's a nice guy and wants you to do well

He's one of the very few professors who can actually make calculus funny and interesting at the same time. My favorite joke was "extended hospitalization" made to refer to applying L'Hopital's rule more than once. That and "Dormammu, I've come to bargain!" for integration by parts more than X2. Completely approachable in office hours too!

This guy is hilarious. I didn't understand a single topic in this entire course, however I had a really good time. I would recommend his class to everyone. The homework is light as long as you space it out from lesson to lesson. If you're actually trying to learn calculus, maybe steer clear, but as a science major, I loved the class.

Very sweet guy, very smart always tries to make jokes and interact with class. Easy grader and always tries his best to make everyone pass. I always got extra credit for doing little things on my test or even attempting to do a problem that I had no clue. I do not like the textbook the calculus classes use, the Openstax overcomplicates things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
He loves integrals a bit too much, especially Gaussians and can integrate them in more than one way. Also makes Star Wars and Dragonball Z jokes lol

I personally thought he was caring and had lots of empathy with his students. Very patient and will explain things for you thoroughly if you ask him. Go to his office hours!

Personality aside, this man does not know how to teach calculus to save his life. He has a hard time breaking down the concepts to students. Mans is way too smart for his own good but very kind hearted and the curves plus extra credit opportunities are amazing, however, tests are more difficult than in class practice.

Josean has proved to be the GOAT of Calculus 1 at SMU. He gives ridiculous amounts of extra credit, and curves tests up to a 100 if you get an A- (most of the time). You can also get 120% on exams. Take him!

Best professor I've had at SMU, is more concerned with you actually grasping the math and wants you to do well and get a good grade. If you need help he is always available and is always talking with students before class giving them help if they need it. He is also a great guy and extremely caring about his students!
Bro calls himself the math terminator. His lectures are hard to follow so it's helpful to use your textbook to teach yourself the concepts. He curves pretty generously though.

Professor Alberto-Cortes is a sweetheart. He's almost too smart for his own good and sometimes it can be a difficult to follow the lectures if you haven't taken Calculus before. He is very considerate and will explain anything you need. He is very straightforward about exams and homework is very light. I would take him again. !!

I had this guy as my diff. eq. TA back when he was a PhD student at UT Dallas. He is the G.O.A.T.!!!

Thank you Dr. Albelo-Cortes for making diff. eq. not suck!

P.S. He's kinda cute and very funny!

He's sweet and quirky, I think he's still getting used to undergrad students. I found him hard to follow but Calc II was fairly easy to learn on my own outside of class. He is very clear about what to expect on tests and quizzes were take home. He is also very understanding about schedules and he curves tests.

The course places heavy weight on group without clear guidance or accountability. Expectations shift over time, and feedback is too brief to be constructive. It becomes difficult to understand how performance is measured or how to meaningfully strengthen your work.

One of my absolute favorite teachers I've ever had. There's definitely a lot of reading for the class, but it's interesting stuff. Also be prepared to actually talk and discuss things in class. The grade is mostly essays. She is a tough grader, but she made me a much better writer. I would take any class she taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person and the in class discussions are engaging and interesting. The class is difficult, and there are quizzes over readings so make sure you pay attention and do your work in order to succeed. She is strict on grading, but her office hours are extremely helpful!

She is so caring and engaging in class. Yes, she is a tough grader, but her feedback is very helpful and allows you to grow. Her class is definitely my favorite and she makes our class discussions very interesting and enjoyable.

Professor Amsel is not a bad teacher, but grades harshly and doesn't have clear grading criteria. If there's a minor thing she doesn't like about your essay, she'll knock you down to a B. Also VERY nick-picky about MLA. She's nice and will make you a better writer, but there's significantly easier professors that are equally good and interesting.

Professor Amsel is really nice, and makes the class engaging. She is a tough grader and makes you work for an A, but gives good feedback and is always available if you need help on your essays. Would definitely take her again.

To start things off, I'm a STEM major who was poor at best when it came to English. Dr. Amsel is one of the best professors I've encountered. She genuinely cares, will make time for you in office hours, and is an amicable person overall. She doesn't mention it much in the course, but definitely ask her about her poetry if you like creative writing!

I highly enjoyed Professor Amsel. She cares about her students and will give as much feedback as she can on your papers, but is a decently hard grader (but that's helpful in the long run). If given the opportunity, I would definitely take one of her classes again.

I had her freshman year for DISC and she really tried to make it so everyone participated and got good grades. She was available to meet to go over essays and always offered good feedback. I actually enjoyed her class. Attendance is mandatory because DISC classes are so small but you get a few excuses abscesses
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsel is absolutely amazing. DISC classes are small so you need to show up and it's obvious if you didn't do the reading. You really need to work hard on the essays, but just drop by her office and ask her questions and she'll help you. Show you care, work hard, and be open to criticism. She's a really great prof. Totally take her.

Dr. Amsel is by far the best teacher I've had at SMU. There is a lot of reading and daily quizzes over the readings but they're not hard as long as you've read. She's a hard grader when it comes to essays, but is very nice and more than willing to spend extra time with you as long as she sees that you're invested in the class and want to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Honestly a really accessible and cool person. She's boring at times, but is a really good professor and I would definitely take her again. If you do what is asked, you shouldn't have a problem getting a B and if you work hard you can grab an A- or A. If you don't do the reading and slack off, you will have a harder time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Amsel keeps the class pretty casual, but don't let that fool you. This class is extremely difficult, and it's really easy to permanently damage your grade by making a small mistake on an assignment. She is very approachable though, and is willing to be flexible if you have conflicts. Learn her style of writing early on, and you might do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I was scared going into this class because I heard how difficult she was, but if you do your work and take her critiques during conferences for your essay, you can get an A. I got an A on every paper simply by doing exactly what she told me to do. Participate in class and show up with your reading done. Hard work, but any DISC class is.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. She helped me immensely with my writing. Read the readings and show up to conferences. Also, the class discussion is always interesting.

Very nice and quirky lady. Sometimes goes off on random tangents regarding the books during discussion, but also has interesting insights. Will help immensely if you conference with her for each paper. Ridiculously tough grader and likes a very particular style of writing. Learn this and you may get an A-.

Get ready to read 200 pages in a few days while also trying to do work for other classes and maintain a social life. Then, once the 200-page book is done, prepare to write a 3-page essay on a ridiculously specific topic concerning 1 paragraph of the book, leaving you wondering why on Earth you wasted your time reading the whole thing. Then get a B-

Professor Amsel was one of my favorite professors this semester. She truly takes an interest in each one of her students. The class isn't necessarily about the grade you make but rather making yourself a better writer. Make sure to do the assigned reading and journals. Also,  participate in class and go into her office hours.

She is a hard grader. Do not think you are immune. Kids who got fives on their AP Lit and Lang tests got C's and B's on their essays. It's especially frustrating because kids in other DISC classes get A's on their essays. She does not cancel classes for a week for essay writing like some other professors do. You have been warned.

One of my favorite professors of all time.  Go to her office for individual help, she is very knowledgable and happy to help you improve your writing.  She challenges you but I give her full credit for improving my writing confidence.

Hurt my confidence in my writing. Once she decides if she likes you and/or your writing style or not, it is difficult to change the grades you receive. Always did well in English and writing until this class. Nice individual, but avoid as a professor.

If you have to take Disc 1313, look to taking other professors before taking Amsel. Clear on instructions, but expects your life to revolve around her class. Grades very hard and has a lot of thorough material. Overly excited for medieval literature, thinks it's "fun." Do not take.

Amsel made medieval lit interesting even for those of us who aren't medievalists. Not easy to make As on papers, but it can be done if you put forth the effort and visit her at office hours. She's so nice and very willing to help you if you show interest in her assignments. Will work with you one on one to improve your writing. Recommend
If you like Medieval works, you will like Amsel. She's a good professor and is always willing to work with her students during office hours.

Amsel is a HUGE MEDIEVALIST, so if you are not into that sort of thing I don't really recommend her. She overall is pretty understanding and while attendance is important she lets you miss 3 classes for free. She is very helpful with writing but it is not easy to score a A on her papers.

Dr. Amsel is such an awesome professor! I know some people didn't like her very much, but she knows what she is talking about and she is on top of her work. She is easy to access and very helpful. She improved my confidence in my writing and is an all around amazing professor!

Amsel is a good teacher, and is especially helpful with writing, but you need to keep up with reading the books and articles in the class. It is not very dificult to get a good grade in her class, you just need to do the work and put effort into the writing. I recommend her for DISC 1313
Such a wonderful professor! Taking her class made me a better writer! I would recommend her!
LOVE LOVE LOVE HER!!!
She knows the material very well, but has trouble evaluating students' papers fairly. Tough to get a B+, nearly impossible to do better.

She is my favorite professor at SMU.  She helped me improve my writing tremendously, and has a real interest in helping you. I cannot say enough good things about this professor and I look forward to taking another one of her classes. She may grade tough at times but this is college.

She teaches how to learn from a text and how to write. She will like you if you put in effort to improve. Easiest class if you don't treat it like a blow off class. You learn beyond the class subject (what you learn applies to other classes), which was nice since my interest in medieval lit was nonexistent. Great teacher, greater person.

Dr. Amsel is extremely helpful and insightful. I was having trouble with my writing and it improved a lot in this class. She cares about her students and pays a lot of attention to each individual. I highly recommend this professor, the class was fun and interesting!
The lectures won't help at all.

Class consists of 6 HW's, attendance, one midterm, and a cumulative that's 50% of the your grade. Class is extremely boring but some good topics here and there. Tests aren't really difficult. It's more math than finance. He's a really nice guy. Pretty easy class just study the slides, HW's, and go to class.
Loved his class. he is the best. You have to take his class.
Great course and well presented.  Provided lots of real-world examples which were relevant for my subsequent internships
Not the most interesting teacher and a decent amount of work, but he is a very fair grader and if you try, you will do very well and learn a lot.

She is a very picky grader with papers and nit picks everything. Will tell you to fix one thing, once you fix it she drops your grade in another way. This class is interesting but take another class because you need to put a lot of effort into her assignments if you want to do well.

Not my favorite teaching style, but it's hard to make a three hour lecture over a narrow topic every week interesting. A few small 3-page papers throughout the semester plus discussions of readings every week, and one big 20 page paper for the final, with a first draft due waaay before it should be. Not a bad class tho esp if you like art history

reviews.comment: Has an unprecedented B+ threshold of 88.5 and uses it to cushion her own ego and statistics. Would not instruct anyone I cared about to take her course. Cannot even fathom if I was a bad student and didn't participate in class. My least favorite professor behind Rachel Ney.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly not a hard class in terms of homework. The tests are annoying because they are super unclear. The professor is useless and just down right annoying

I'm echoing another comment when I say a quality professor in a bad class. Because it is akin to a survey course, she has to teach to students who may be in it just for the CC. If you genuinely are interested in the Art History major or minor, I wouldn't recommend this class due to its simplicity and lack of depth. If you want an easy A, however...

Dr. Freund is an alright professor in a bad class. The class is graded on a few things, all of which are easy. No slides are posted online, so you have to take notes every class. She clearly cares about the subject, but there is not enough time to display a meaningful amount of content on the topic. No printed tests, everything is in blue books.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This lady is a piece of work. Only a couple of grades: midterm, visual analysis paper, exam. Midterm and Exam is graded pretty tough and requires study, but visual analysis paper is easy. Class not required, you can just log on Zoom. She gave everyone a 96 in the grading category "masking" (literally wearing a mask) simply because she felt like it.

Not terrible, but much too opinionated to be a fair professor. She's knowledgeable about her subject, but she injects her own modern political opinions into her class, which is supposed to be historical. It's not like she's not trying to push an agenda either, she brought in a guest speaker who talked about critical race theory. It wasn't relevant.

Overall, a pretty easy and straight-forward class. The three exams are open-note and directly pulled from the lectures. She has very clear criteria/rubrics for each assignment  if you follow it, the class is an easy A.

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and boring but sometimes the info can be interesting. The professor is very nice and accessible outside of class. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Freund makes lectures fun and engaging. Shes a fun person and really wants to help. Not many grades so make sure to do good on the exams and papers.

She's very sweet, but her class is extremely hard. Makes you memorize about 30 different art pieces including the artist, location, exact date, period of when it was painted, and even the materials used. She then only shows about four on the test. Tests are really tough and pretty much the only grade that matters. I wouldn't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: tests were an odd format, but once you got the hang of them it wasn't too bad. lectures were kind of pointless, though, and attendance was mandatory which wasn't fun. i felt as if the TAs did more of the teaching during the weekly lab sessions, honestly. but all in all, not a bad option for an arts credit.
Does not help you succeed in the class. Blames the students rather than his teaching for poor class performance on a test. Not accommodating and lacks any understanding.

His lectures and homework fail to align with the content of his tests. Has a dismissive attitude towards questions and lack of response to critical emails. Grading is harsh and includes material not adequately covered in class, making the learning experience unnecessarily challenging.

Meir is probably the worst professor I've ever had. He is quite disrespectful when answering questions and it's hard to follow along in class because he goes in circles. reviews.comment: He's not as harsh as many of the other reviews claim him to be. He's not the most amazing lecturer or anything, but as long as you pay attention in class and do the homework, you'll be fine.

Terrible and horrible. He was just reading the powerpoint all the time, and was not really care about whether you had got his points. No practice exam before the test. After we begged him for extra credits, he only added us few points regardless the average was 67.

Dont know why he has such bad reviews... he was a great professor, just do the homework and study and you will succeed. Got an A.

Worst professor you can ever take. If you avoid him do so. All he does is rambles on about theoretical stuff and doesn't have a concise way of teaching you the subject. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Meir is very knowledgeable. He can explain higher level concepts and make tough material easy to understand. If you don't enjoy math, or want an easy A i would not recommend not taking his class. Take his class if you love math and aren't afraid to ask questions.

Professor Meir always thoroughly explains each concept. He moves extremely slowly and wants you to use his specific terms when describing something which is a pain. Force yourself to come to class, listen, and check your work and it will be an easy enough class.

I don't usually write reviews but this is guy is worth it. Hard to understand what he says, no pattern of teaching just constant lecturing without any order. Explains all theoretical yet expects practical during tests. TAs grade so hard. You will have to ask for a lot of help and self-study a ton to make a solid A. Pray for a curve and good luck.

reviews.comment: Boring.

Although Professor Meir definitely knows his math material, he is simply not a great teacher. reviews.comment: Meir is unprepared for lectures, rambling/repeating topics from previous classes. If you feel unsure about coding and are dependent on lectures, his class will seem impossible. If you've taken math/coding classes before, it's a waste of time. Covered three of the book's topics at most. Learned more from the substitutes when he was at conferences.

Only reason I got an A was because I read the textbook. This is the only way you'll succeed. If you do the hw problems and do the textbook examples you should do well. I never showed up to class after I realized I was learning nothing. Unclear/confident speaker and gets flustered, meaning you won't learn much.  Condescending when asking for help.

Worst teacher you can ever have. you will be better if you switch out at the first opertunity!! if for some reason you stay in class you will learn more by not going to class and just looking at the book. I am a Math major and I think he is the worst math teacher I have ever had. You will do yourself a favor by switching out. if you have him RUN!!!
Lots of homework. Tests are pretty challenging but not crazy.
I learned a lot. She was available for students who needed extra help. For me, it was a challenging class, but I did fine because she helped me and I was happy with my grade.

Amy was extremely difficult to work with. In lecture she was unwilling to assist me without having done the ungraded assignment (even if I had no idea what to do)

Her grading criteria was unfair we were not given a midterm exam to benchmark our grades.  

Unfortunately my program would not let me have other professors so i was stuck with her 3/10
Amy is the worst professor
Exam is tough but reach out to her and keep in touch throughout the class.

This class was three hours once a week, so hopefully that will be changed. She is a good professor, but lectures can be slightly boring and tedious. The 2 quizzes, midterm, and final are open note, but they're your only grades. Final and midterm are 85% of your grade, and she doesn't decide grade breaks until after the final. Would rec if 2x a week
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher and fair grader. Be prepared to work on the highly recommended, but not mandatory, practice problems to help prepare for the class subject materials. The class was once a week and very long, 3 hours, but she nicely planned class time and gave us breaks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was a class that was extremely hard

Professor Puelz knows pretty much everything about statistics you'll ever need to know. But if you've never taken a stats class, it'll be hard to get an A. She drops the lowest quiz and adds the weight to the final, which saved my grade. DON"T GET THE TEXTBOOK! Just practice for tests using her exams from previous terms--that is essential.

Dr. Puelz is one of the most clear professors on campus in terms of her lectures. She can explain things in different ways so no one gets left behind. Her intro stats class was challenging for some, but overall the grades were solid for an honors class. Test averages were around 92. Take her and you won't regret it.

Homework is not graded but very helpful to prepare for quizzes/exams.  Professor is very helpful in answering questions outside of class. She returns your quizzes/tests with thorough feedback, which was great. Fair exam and grade.  Overall would recommend her.

I find it very difficult to pay attention in class, however, that has not effected my grade. Quizzes, the midterm, and the final exam are all open note and open computer. Everything is done on Excel so a computer is required.

There are no tricks to this class. She 100% has your best interest in mind. If you do what she asks you are guaranteed to get at least an A-. Thats it. Do the recommended problems (she gives you the answers so you can check your work), study from the old exams and quizzes (you can also check your work here), and show up to her class.
She is the worst teacher I ever had. Not forgiving at all!! Smu can find better teachers than her
Terrible, terrible teacher.
If you show up everyday for this class, you will get at least an A-. She is very helpful and very organized. I am glad I took her.

The class consists of 7 assignments that are extra credit, 6 quizzes and one can be dropped, 2 midterms and a cumulative final. Don't buy the book. She is helpful and a great professor. Class is not super easy but if you try you can get at least an A-. Quizzes and tests are tricky at times. The good thing is that you can have a couple cheat sheets.

She's vague and grades inconsistently, holding ridiculously high standards for such a meaningless subject. All in all just a bad teacher that goes too fast and is often contradicting. Avoid at all costs. Take Collins instead, he's easier and more entertaining.

She teaches everything through powerpoint slides but explains everything in detail.  Her tests are very fair, she just tests to make sure you have learned the material, plus you get a study sheet for each quiz.  Made statistics pretty interesting, would recommend.

For a class about spreadsheets and databases, she's probably the most engaging teacher you could get. Very helpful and clear in class when people ask questions. You get one piece of paper, front and back, with whatever you want on it for both the midterm and final. You take 5 in-class quizzes using your computer and get to drop 1. I recommend her.
Amy is a quality instructor who is tough but fair. My only knock is that sometime she talks to quickly and you have to ask her to slow down.
Amy is a good professor who is clear and mostly concise in her teaching. The only knock is that she talks to quickly and you have to ask her to slow down.

Honestly, this class is really easy if you pay attention and don't go on facebook during class(we use our computer the whole semester). Tests are not hard to get a good grade if you prepare your cheat sheet well and there are 5 quizzes that she tells you exactly what's on them. She kind of reads off her notes, but all quizzes are open note/book

She is a one of the WORST TEACHERS i had in my college years. She is sloppy and careless. Her grading system is IMPOSSIBLE. Final is 50+ percent. PLEASE, stay away from her!!! She goes SO FAST during lecture, it is HARD TO FOLLOW HER!! She EXPECTS you to know every single detail said in class. Exams & quizes are very TRICKY!! Not helpfull at all!!!
She is a good prof but not very clear during class. She seems to skip over things and when you ask her she continues.  2 tests and 4 quizzes that are worth 40%

By far my least favorite class I have taken at SMU! The tests are extremely difficult and she puts material on the test from random videos shown in class that do not show whether or not you ACTUALLY know the material. Take Jim Collins!

Puelz presents the material pretty well, and it's not too difficult if you follow along in class. The paper tests (midterm/final) can be tricky because of their form and rather vague questions. Other than that the course was fairly good.

Puelz has gotten a lot easier. She explains everything really well and is a great professor! As long as you do the homework and follow the powerpoints in class, you'll be fine. She's not as specific on her tests as she was in the past, and they come straight from what you do in class.

I do not recommend this professor. We never used our textbook. She goes through instructions quickly, so if you miss one step, you're completely lost the rest of class. Some questions on the test are irrelevant to the majority of the class material and ask for detailed answers or numbers I wouldn't remember unless I had written it on my notecard.

Really nice lady. You get to use a study sheet on exams, and I highly recommend going through all the articles and powerpoints and cramming everything you can onto that sheet as her test are VERY specific with numbers that you didnt think would be important. Aslo, go to class everyday/take notes. If you do those two things youre likely to get an A.

Amy is a great teacher!  I had little interest in statistics before the class, but now I'm interested in it because she made it interesting.  If you have trouble in the class, meet with her during office hours.  She will help you; you can do it! Don't miss any classes. You will like Amy's class!

The material is fairly straightforward but the tests are very detailed and difficult. Definitely attend every class and take notes on what she says because she rewrites her tests every semester based on what is discussed in class.

Pretty easy class if you make a good note sheet for the exams. Make sure to read the text and powerpoints as well as understand excel and access very well. She is not the most helpful professor when you have a question but luckily the material is not overly difficult. I would reccomend her

The class was really easy.  here are a few tips: Take notes in class, do not rely on looking back on her powerpoint to make your cheatsheet for the test.  MAKE NOTES DURING LABS- step by step of how to do each thing.  if you do that and look at old tests, you will have a bomb study sheet, and you will ace the course.  obvi go to class.

Likeable professor and the topics in class are interested and very current (as a class on technology should be) But the tests are irritating because they ask questions about the smallest details covered in class. If you want an A take detailed notes and make a great cheat sheet for the test. Thats how I did it.

Incredibly nice professor but her teaching style was not very beneficial to me. You must take incredibly detailed notes to do well in this course. There're only two written tests the whole semester, which seems absurd to me. On the bright side; she does allow a typed cheat sheet.

If you are an insane note-taker, this class is for you.  She is nice and lets you have a cheat sheet but on the down side, you are responsible for EVERYTHING she says/does in class.  Don't space out in class because she will say one sentence about something and then it'll be worth a lot on the test.  I heard the other itom teacher is easier.

Prof Puelz's class is a A if you do these things: go to class because that is how you will know what will be on the test, make a great cheat sheet for your tests (i usually just copy/pasted all of the slides from the section), and show up to lab.  Every lab should be an easy 100.  But what I've heard from other ITOM teachers, she is the BEST!!!

I don't know what these other posts are about. This class is easy if you go to class and pay attention. If you have a hard time or don't see the point of this class then you probably don't belong in the business school. She allows a cheat sheet on all her exams and posts old exams on BB that are extremely similar!

Awful, Awful Prof. The worst I've had ever! She can only answer 50% of your questions. She's disorganized and her tests are so specific! Some of the details she barely goes over and expects you to know every minor detail. Some of the questions have nothing to do with ITOM itself. Everyone I know that have taken her class says the the same.

what on earth is a teacher such as Amy doing teaching at Cox??? She is so useless, and also why on earth is anyone subjected to learning how to create html coding on a "machine" if they plan on majoring in marketing??? when am i ever gunna use any of the stuff i learnt ever again.. literally.. the class is boring, slow, confusing and totallyrubbish

Listen, if you go to class and take notes on the powerpoints with your computer, type up all the little facts she says, you will make an A. Guaranteed. This class is not difficult if you just go and write down what she says. Easiest class of my semester.
she lets you use cheat sheets for every quiz and test. quizzes are really easy, but the tests are impossible. class average on them is below 80, and they count for most of your grade.

I really enjoyed this class. Biggest piece of advice is to MAKE APPOINTMENT FOR CONFERENCES. They are optional, but she will destroy your paper if you don't go, she gives good feedback. She lets class make questions for midterm and final. She is a little frazzled, but a very nice person. 2 short papers, a longer final paper, and weekly reflections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I had a hard time with a tiny assignment in this class. She met me on zoom and walked me through the entire thing. Once she did this she realized it was too hard and felt bad she hadn't experience it more. You write a lot of papers but she is understanding about deadlines and truly cares about her students. I loved taking her class.

She's not very organized and her feedback isn't as helpful as most of the other professors for Hon DISC. Her grading is highly dependent on how well she agrees with your point. She's a doctoral canidate and it shows.

First and foremost, the Honors disc class just suck. They are too difficult and harm bright students' grades without reflecting the difficulty on the transcript. The university needs to fix this. This teacher specifically doesn't give great feedback on your papers. Classes are what you would expect. Not a horrible choice.

Prof Atkinson is an amazing teacher and I loved her DISC course. She's funny and open to discussion, letting students lead but guided us when necessary. Her papers were challenging, but she was happy to help and was a very fair grader. If I could take another class by her I 100% would

Classes were 95% discussion based. We had five essays as the only grades. She would grade pretty hard on essays but not teach us how to write. She was accessible for essay conferences but she would just tell you what was wrong, not how to fix it. Sometimes she would tell me what to change and then take off for doing exactly that in my final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unprepared

Mrs. Atkinson is amazing. I despise english and writing. She didnt make me love it, but she was super understanding about it. She grades more on the effort you put into your paper rather than the skill level of the paper itself. which is great if you arent good at writing. She is insanely helpful and its not a boring lecture. we laugh and have fun.

Definitely loved being in Prof Benson's class. Super chill, caring prof who wants you to do well. Several reading responses, tests are pretty straightforward (lecture/PPT based), design journal that you work on throughout the course, and a big group project at the end. Pretty easy class, just stay on top of due dates. Take her if you can!

reviews.comment: I love her!! She's so much fun and really enjoys what she's talking about. She only lectured once a week, meaning the other two class periods were asynchronous, which was super nice. Didn't have that much homework, mostly just a few projects that were worth most of the grade. Exams were straight forward.

I am honestly shocked at how many good reviews she has when she is one of the worst professors I have had. She grades ridiculously hard for assignments that are not explained well and have little relevance. She tells you not to complain and then tells you it's your fault for not speaking up. Save yourself and take a different professor
Tougher grader than I expected, but overall not too difficult. I would not take this if you are not an ad major or minor / don't need the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Would 10000% take again. She really cares about her students.
Amber Benson is literally amazing. Take her if you get the chance!

Professor Benson makes class fun and easy to understand. She is really funny, and has a unique perspective on media and even college students! If you do your work, and put effort into it, the class is more rewarding and you get the grade you deserve! Take this class if you want to be an ADV minor or are considering the major!!!

I loved Professor Benson's class! I can honestly say that I learned new useful things. Would definitely recommend if you're an ADV major. Her lectures were really interesting and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. Tests are not hard if you study what is taught in lectures. Great class! :)

Amazing lectures!

Overall, he is an outstanding professor.

Profesor D'brot is very chill, kind, and fun! He makes biology even more interesting and always relates difficult concepts in a more understandable way. He always offers office hours and is super helpful! Anyone who gets a poor grade in his class is purely not putting in the effort.

Already managed to tank the majority of our class's grade, and it's March. reviews.comment: He is super caring and intelligent. Really wants his students to learn and do well.

Such a good teacher. Super cool and helpful. Does everything to help his students. Would love to take another class with him!

Professor Dia is amazing, I am so thankful I had her as a professor. SMU hired an approachable, helpful, and competent STEM professor. I really enjoyed her and her class, she is realistic and honest. Organic chemistry is hard and she makes it a little less so.

She is one of the most wholesome kind professors. Makes it a point to know everyone's name and is curious about the well-being of her students. Absolutly do not take. Shes not even worth me saying more

Objectively the worst professor at SMU. And a chair. Hilarious.
If you want to waste your time in class that you will learn nothing in, this is the one for you. A joke of a course and we shouldn't have to pay for this. Bad teaching to boot.

reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's amazing! This class is mostly discussion based and the content is relevant to life. Most of my class didn't read the texts and she knew it, but was understanding. The only work is our essays and all text are provided by her. It gave me the small elementary school feel & relevant information about myself and my service .

Honestly one of the sweetest humans alive!! She did cancel class a couple of times but if you just show up and participate it's an easy A. The best professor I have had at SMU so far. She really cares about what she's teaching and making sure you understand the material and make a good grade. The class meets so many requirements too! Love her.
This class is so laidback, and she's seriously one of the nicest people you'll ever meet. TAKE HER!! Participate a lot, no tests/quizzes, and go to her office hours for feedback on your papers.

Dr. Anderson is super sweet and caring, but she rarely responds to emails and cancels class often. Super easy A, just show up to class and listen and you'll know what to write about in the papers. Recommend this class because it covers a lot of requirements

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

While PRW is a show up and pass class, Caitlin takes it to a whole new level. She is absolutely wonderful and caring and lovely. Her adoration for her job rubs off on all of her students and makes PRW so much more enjoyable. I can not say enough good things about her.
Caitlin Anderson is the best and nicest teacher I've had at SMU. She has a true passion and interest for the subject matter.

You might just see PRW as a UC required class but it is so much more than that. Caitlin teaches you things that prep you for life. She is such an amazing professor and I'm lucky that I had her. If you have the option to take Caitlin, do it!
Caitlin is so nice! She truly cares about what she is teaching and your well-being! Don't buy the textbook because you only use it once and you don't really need it - she even says that herself.
Caitlin is the best PRW prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

Professor Anderson is one of my favorite teachers! She's so sweet and really tries to improve her student's lives outside and inside of class. She's really understanding and will work with you when needed. She seems like she loves to teach which makes her a great (and easy) teacher to have.

Prof. Anderson is great. She is super caring and an awesome influence to have. She is so passionate about teaching and even understands that most students do not want to take the class. Not a super fun class, but if you go in with a good attitude, you will have a good time with her.
Caitlin is a model teacher. She's extremely kind, and makes a relatively basic class truly meaningful. I never want to see her leave SMU.
Caitlin is a great professor and makes class fun and entertaining. Just make sure to show up to class and participate in the conversation.

Caitlin is a great PRW professor. She cares about the material and her students and is more than willing to spend extra time with students if they ask for her. She gives 3 excused absences and since PRW is a pass/fail class, just show up and the class is super easy.

Caitlin is by far the best professor for PRW I. She understands that it is a blowoff class and tries her hardest to make it fun. She is passionate about what she is teaching and very personable. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

the sweetest prof I've ever had. PRW1101 was mandatory and a blow-off class but really truly enjoyed her class and felt like I actually learned a lot from her and what she taught. super easy p/f class that I actually looked forward to going to.
Super Sweet!!!

She cool

Caitlin is a very cool, fun woman who is genuinely interested in her students. While PRW is kind of a joke class, she keeps things interesting and fun with a wide range of activities and topics.

she grades soooooooooooo hard!!!!!!

She also kind of expects students to blatantly mirror/repeat her ideas in papers and assignments. Her grading also isn't super clear so go to office hours.

Joan is a classic Honors Teacher. There is a negative stigma around her class, but she just wants hard work and has high expectations. There are 3-4 papers, readings, and discussions. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

nice person, wants to help.

Arbery is a tough teacher.  Her quizzes are very detail oriented to read closely.  If you read, participate, and make adjustments to papers according to what she says in conferences, you should have no problems getting an A.

do not take him! the notes he gives in class do not answer ANYTHING and he makes it so boring. worst psych class i've taken so far

great guy, easy class to sit through.  tests are decent...you'll do well if you study his study guides.  attendance not mandatory but he does give a pop quiz every week.  you'll pretty much catch on to when the quizzes are going to be though and you dont really need to be in class if theres no quiz.  all notes are posted online.

Great Professor. Very helpful if you meet during his office hours.

Prof. Austin Is great!

I loved Professor O'Neil! She is genuinely a kind person and wants her students to succeed. She will tell you exactly what to correct and essentially guarantee a better grade. Overall good teacher, she definitely helped improve my writing ability and the class wasn't harder than expected.

Professor O'Neill was a very friendly and sweet professor while I took her for WRTR 1313. She was very forgiving in giving homework in advance as well as extensions with proper evidence. If you put in effort to contribute in class, you will be just fine. Be sure to thoroughly answer and complete her essays according to her feedback. Although this class takes work, it is well worth it.

She is so hard, she grades way too strict compared to other WRTR professors (definitely take a different one). She also gives little to no amnesty for being late, missing classes, or turning in late homework. Not a good first professor to have in college, pretty much any other WRTR teacher will give you a better time.
So take her!

She's super nice! Homework's rather meaningless, but it's quick and easy. She gives good feedback on essays (be sure to meet with her with specific questions). Granted, I'm a decent writer so never got below a 94 on my essays. As long as you turn in what you need to on time and attend optional conferences, you'll probably get an A.

Favorite professor for WRTR. There are weekly readings with a 300-word count response requirement - but they help SO much with the essays. She does not accept late work but I found that more motivating to do the work. Just show up, read the readings (or most of them) and turn in your work - you will get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Full warning, I'm a writer so I may be a little biased. You need to communicate and put effort into this class. But if you do, Prof. O'Neil is a great teacher. Her assignments felt relevant to the material and she was engaging in class. She's a tougher grader but if you meet with her and reach out, chances are you'll do fine.

She's really nice but is very strict on grades. Absolutely no late work is accepted and good luck trying to get her to round up grades. Make sure to do the homework. It's tedious and boring but it'll save you from her essay grading.

O'Neil is a hard grader as far as essays but there are lots of other assignments she gives so it evens out. She also has kids of her own so she is understanding of the workload. I would reccomend her if you want a challenge and learn lots.

Professor O'Neill was a good professor for the specific class, and was for the most part very caring. She got upset if people didn't come to class in-person on their assigned days and would count off points if you didn't have a good reason to miss. Communication is key with her, she will help you if you tell her you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Neill is really nice and really cares about making sure her students understand what she is teaching. There's usually a Discussion Prep Sheet due before every class which is kind of annoying, but it does come in handy during the actual class. She gives you plenty of time to work on essays and is easy to talk to/understand. She's super nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader on essays. Buy all textbooks for her class, you will need them for reading. Not many homework assignments, mostly easily graded notes worth 10 points. Great lady, has teenage kids and understands circumstances of students. Do all assignments and don't miss classes.

She is an extremely tough grader. Go to her writing conferences. She would tell me my paper was fine and suggest few improvements, then give my paper a C.  I only made 2 B's on papers. I think 3 students in the class got an A on at least one paper.  Nice lady: not afraid to give a bad grade. She favors a students who speaks in class.

it was pretty hard.  she would give us an outline of what she wanted before the paper was due, and i would do exactly that, and i would have her read over my paper, and i still make C's.  i dont really get it...

Professor edison was arguably the worst professor I have ever had. First off her lectures are completely pointless because they are impossible to follow. Her exams are very similiar to online practice exams however she puts every practice exam on lockdown. So what is the point of having outside resources to practice if she is going to use lockdown.

This was the easiest class I have taken I ended with over an 100%. Every test has extra credit and she drops your lowest test score. She gives practice tests and learning curves before tests and the texts are exactly the same so it is good prep. If you pay attention in class and follow her notes which she makes for you it will be great.
Pretty rough class, the averages for the Exams were in the 50-60% range, so obviously the teacher cant teach. She speeds through the notes as well

Lectures are very quick so prepare to spend time learning it outside of class. Tests are very similar to practice exams and if you actually study you will get an A. She gives extra credit opportunities and drops your lowest test and lab score.
Actually love her she has a great sense of humor and explains concepts clearly. You will have to try obviously but take her!!

She's very accessible outside of class, but the lectures are also very fast. Homework is a bit hard because it's attached to the very expensive textbook that she does not really use, but she gives a lot of extra credit on exams. She's such a sweet lady and really cares about you. Pay attention and ask questions and you should be fine.
Lectures only, does not care about students, moves very quick for an intro class, she does not care (love the TA for lab though)

People who complain about her, just don't try in her class. She is very sweet and helpful. The content is easy if you stay on track and try to understand. Seriously, this class is not as bad as people say it is.

An intro stats course truly doesn't need to be this difficult. Most of the difficulty doesn't stem from the coursework but rather because she moves insanely fast during lectures so they're mostly useless. I only showed up to the lectures because they were mandatory. Only take if you are ok with self-teaching.
Doesn't care about students or being helpful. Find different teacher

this class does not need to be this difficult lectures are boring and she is very judgmental. if you ask a question she gives a sassy response back and your even more confused than before. not flexible for students' time, especially when outside factors happen that are out of your control.
This class was so light and she's a good professor, people don't study and blame her for it

It is an extremely fast paced class and the exams were never like the practice exams, 10x harder. Average test score on one of our exams was a 60% so that tells you all you need to know about her as a teacher. Not the most approachable professor but try to go to her office hours and that can sometimes help. She also never replies to emails.

Great professor and she makes statistics seem easy. Offers plenty of extra credit plus the exams aren't hard. Always encouraging students to go to office hours and is open to answering questions during class. Most of the labs are easy and quick. She's very nice and approachable, highly recommend taking her

Overall class is fine, one notesheet for exams, curves are usually around 4-5 pts and 5 pts extra credit. Notes in class are fill in the blank, test questions are fairly similar to practice test questions and examples on notes. But she's not the most patient, so don't expect her to fix things for you or give you second chances on missing things

This class was an easy A. Her tests are easy, multiple choice for the most part and we can use a cheat sheet. Also we get an extra credit opportunity before each test to have up to five points added to test, plus the test is also curved. She provides fill in the blank style notes. Overall great professor

This class is just overall difficult regardless of the professor you take. She is nice but I did not like her teaching methods, and she moved at a very very fast pace, so I didn't really learn the material in class and had to do a lot on my own. Get to bring a sheet of notes to tests. Provides no extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the rudest if not the rudest professors I've ever had. Would not round my grade up for a B- by .10%. Terrible at teaching. Do not take her. I asked her a question once and was so shocked by her rudeness and disregard for another human let alone one of her students.

no attitude, just one of those naturally sarcastic gals. she was nice, goes around class and helps if you got questions. Fill-in the blank notes and you get a cheat sheet on tests, which is nice. Barely payed attention to lectures, just taught myself later on. work and effort will get you there, and she's got office hours if you need.

I really liked how she taught her classes. Difficult class but if you spend a lot of time on it and go to office hours, you'll be fine. Attendance was only mandatory for the labs, but there were a few random in-class assignments that were a part of the participation grade.
WHAT THE $#%! IS A P-VALUE?!

I don't know why other reviews say she's rude/mean--I never found that. However, I did not like her style of teaching. It was lecture heavy and the homework was grinding. The lecture did not help me learn/apply the info and her tests are 10x harder than her homework/practice tests. There is a cheat sheet, but it rarely helps-take her if you'd like.
Biggest ‘TUDE I've ever met. Horrible. And even worse teacher. Straight As and this is going to tank my gpa. Horrible. What a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She goes over everything in class very well. Just do the homework and you'll be fine. The one page front and back you get for every test is super helpful and she's also just a nice and funny person.
Terrible bad attitude what a joke hardest class I've ever taken AVOID

Probably the worst and rudest teacher I've ever had. I took Stats in high school and did very well and I could not grasp this class due to her teaching and expectations. Tests are SO hard and she does not prepare you well. Take any other teacher she is not worth it.

This class is difficult but not impossible. Edison allows for one cheat sheet every exam (front and back), drops your lowest midterm, curves all exams (about 10pt), and allows two cheat sheets for the final exam. Notes were fill in the blank. Nightly homework assignments that you get three tries for. The class is lecture heavy but Edison is helpful

She is a good professor and knows a lot about statistics. She provides the notes to her class before the lecture. Print them out and use them. The homework and labs are not hard & you have multiple attempts. The exams are from the same test bank as the practice. Is a super easy class if you pay attention and know what you are doing.

This class was pretty hard, at least for me. She goes over the materials very fast but thats because their is so much of it. If you can do as many practice tests before the tests that is the most helpful thing. If you go to class and do the practice test that should be good, Mrs. Edison is a nice lady but can have a bit of a attitude at times.
You do need to show up to class because lectures go fast but you get a cheat sheet on each exam.

This class is just super boring, but not that hard. It's not very hard to get an A if you study, especially if you take the practice tests. Attendance isn't mandatory. If you go to every class and take notes you'll definitely succeed.
Horrible lecturer and teacher but the course is easy compared to the alternatives. You get a cheat sheet too.

I don't know why the other reviews are so bad. Her notes I thought were pretty good and the practice tests were pretty much identical to the actual tests so if you just study and go over those well, which wasn't too hard, you can easily get a good grade in this class.
She's chill and the class isn't too hard. To study i recommend going over every note and putting that on your test sheet rather than trying to put down a test bank.

Do not take her. Her class was all lecture. The lectures and the homework questions barely help on the exam. The only thing that helps are the practice exams, as they are the questions on the exam. Only lets you take the practice exam one time though. Have to spend hours working a cheat sheet even though half the time it doesn't even help.

Professor Edison wants students to succeed. She was always available for extra help, but I often found myself just going to the ALEC. The TA Yin Lu was horrible and condescending. The practice tests are really helpful because the same questions appear on the exam. If you see a tutor and ace the practice test, you'll do well on the unit tests.

Not the friendliest lady and mediocre teacher. Fill-in the blank notes, weekly homework assignments follow the notes and you get three tries. Her practice exams and cheat sheet are what saved me when it came exam time. Practice before the test and get above the average (65 normally) and you'll be sure to get on the curve (10 pts normally).

Class is super easy, exam questions literally come from a test bank and you get a cheat sheet so you don't even have to learn anything, just write down the questions/answers. If you are looking to understand the material, don't take her, she's a horrible lecturer and you have to teach yourself the material. But if you want an easy A, go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take her. She switched to lockdown browser making the class nearly impossible unless you want to spend 5 hours making a study sheet with the questions from the test bank. She also limited the practice tests to 6 even though that is the only tool she gives you to study for tests. Her lectures make no sense and are extremely boring.

Edison has note sheets to use during lectures, and it can get really boring and hard to learn any info. There are nightly homework, huge exams, and some attendance points. The exams are mostly from a test bank but take place on a lockdown browser. I did not learn a lot in her class because she just was not a great teacher, but I slipped by.

Professor Edison is a great, respected, and kind person in general. However, I would not recommend you take her for STATS. I found myself extremely lost throughout the course and though I met with her and a tutor, still got a 67 on my final exam. Tests were purely guesswork for me, and I often left class early because of how lost I was.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not too difficult of a class, but the teacher is clearly new and still learning because she goes so fast. Put in a little effort and you will get a good grade but probably easier options.

Professor Edison is kind, but generally seems to lack experience. 
She goes over important concepts too fast, doesn't fully show all steps when working through problems, and generally doesn't give enough resources for her students to succeed.  
Had to reteach myself most of the content outside of class, which was extremely time consuming.

STATS is hard, and frankly, it does not favor well to anyone uninvested in it. If you can dedicate the time to practice tests and the readings and engage w her: you'll be fine. Fall 2022 was her first collegiate sem, and she has more to improve. But she cares; before I dropped, she would engage in office hours and all. I hope she gets better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you can teach yourself material, this class will be okay for you. Honestly, just read the textbook before class so that the lectures make sense and pay attention to the practice exams because the tests draw heavily from them. The material is not really difficult to understand but more just difficult to organize because it's so much information.

This class is very difficult if you do not know how to teach yourself. She writes long paragraphs on the power points and moves way too quickly for you to write anything down, not posting them on canvas. As long as you take her practice tests a lot you should do decent, they are similar to the test. She also drops your lowest grade out of 3 tests.

I had to drop this class- she does not post in-class notes to access if you miss class, and if you ask for it, she will tell you to talk to a classmate. The lectures were not helpful and barely correlated to the labs (the lab instructor was much more helpful). Would not recommend

So.... she's not the best. If you took statistics in high school, you will be fine in 2331. If you didn't, she speeds over the material and doesn't exactly make it easy to remember things. On a good note though, her tests are the exact same as the practice tests (so do them) and you get a cheat sheet. I'd say she's fine.
An average professor, homework is online and 3 test make up most of your grades

She is really bad at teaching the material, she reads definitions and off the slides without really explaining anything. I have to do a lot of external research to understand concepts and get formulas. However, she is pretty lenient with curves, she drops the lowest of your three tests, and she lets you have a formula sheet/excel file for tests

The other review is misleading. Pf. Edison is very sweet and lectures well. I feel bad because she tries to be nice and get the students to engage but let's be real no one wants to engage in class. Two homeworks a week and three test (one dropped with a final). Do the practice tests over and over because it is the same as the tests.

Where do I even start. This woman literally doesn't teach the material. She throws an abundance of words on the screen in massive paragraphs, reads it word for word, and skips to the next slide before anyone can even write a full sentence down. Every student that I knew in that class had to reteach themselves the entire curriculum before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'd take his class again for sure. He made a really good environment with the class where everyone felt comfortable speaking up and even making jokes with each other. The quizzes are lowk hard if you don't actually read the materials but like you will do well in the class if you put effort overall. He also gives lots of extra credit and trade-offs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Sepulveda is one of my favorite professors I've had at Babson. I took his Art As A Visual Language class and I have learned a lot. I don't considered myself being an "art person" but since he is very passionate about the subject, it made the class very enjoyable. He cares about his students, and I recommend taking his class.

He is the BEST I have ever taken at Babson. I see this often on this website, but i'm not that good of a student, so you can take my unbiased advice. He is the nicest, kindest and most caring professor ever, really, I felt like him and I were friends in class! He really does his best for his students to succeed and makes everyone very comfortable!

I implore you to take a course with Professor Sepulveda, he will make the course seem more difficult than it is upfront, and you will have to work for it but you will learn so much because of how passionate he is about Art History. To get a good grade, read the assigned text (key to participating in discussion) and be engaged in writing assignments

Professor Sepúlveda is an amazing teacher- he is so passionate about his subject that it makes students excited to learn. While there is a lot of reading, it is 100% worth it to take any of his classes. I took Art in the Age of Revolutions (ARHS 3348) last semester, and Im taking The Epic of Latin America with him again this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As an elective class, I would stay away from the course. A class you have to study a lot for unnecessarily. She grades on a 1000-point system, where 930 points is a 4.0. Due to bad performances, she added 10% (or 100 points) if you completed all extra credit work, which is the only reason I ended with an A in her class, somehow lol.

The class isn't that hard but she makes it so annoying. Like most people I'm only doing this class to fulfill credit for another major but she acts like we're all going to be Nobel prize winning geologists. It's doable if you study hard, but if you can avoid her, you'll regret not doing so. Be advised she runs this 1000-level course like the Navy.

Asiye is the worst professor in the history of professors. She doesn't speak english, you cant understand her, her instructions are very very unclear, and her grading makes absolutely no sense. Her tests are also impossible to study for. Unless you want to jump off of Dallas Hall I suggest you stand clear of her.
She has changed every single grade and rule she made. She is truly lost and is on a power trip for grading. Tests are in the 60's for averages, and she could care less. Stay away

By far worst professor I have ever had at SMU. Extremely disrespectful to every student, does not answer questions, only reads from slides, tests unnecessarily hard. tests hard and always have errors, as if she made them the night before. assigns too much work, descriptions never are clear. Recommend to never take a class with this professor

I don't even know where to begin with this one. This class is extremely difficult for an intro. The professor is completely incompetent to teach, as she reads directly from the slides with no emotion. Extremely rude to students, and will make fun of you for asking questions. Your grade will fluctuate daily in this course. DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!!!!

Its honestly shocking to me that this woman has a job. She clearly has no clue what she is talking about and reads straight off of her slideshow. Tests are impossible no matter how you study, all the average grades are failing for every test and she doesn't curve. She is the worst teacher I've ever had and do not take her.

She was GREAT! Taking her is like signing yourself up for an A+ on your transcript!!!! TAKE HER, LOVE IT AND LEARN!


P.S. NO TALKING!!!!!!

Honestly, she's buns, I don't know what else to say about this. Tests are awful and nothing like any of the material she gives her students to study. She reads directly from her slides and I can never understand any of the points she is trying to make. I'm still fighting for an A because I'm goated, but this has been terrible.

I have always been a good student and SMU is tough academically in most courses this is the worst teacher I've ever had. Average exam grades are in the 60s for every exam  and she's made no changes. The project we are doing is also graded rigorously while it has impossible tasks. Somehow I am still fighting for an A- but never take this professor.
This prof is pretty awful. Doesn't know how to use canvas, and the class averages are in the 50s and 60s. Stay away

Do not take this teacher!!! Does not know how to use canvas and gives quizzes that have the wrong answers and you have to prove to her that you answer is right before she changes it. Also very lecture heavy.

NO TALKING!!!! Every class she is disruptive because she stops her entire lecture to yell NO TALKING every five seconds and it is really annoying. Also, don't take this class unless you hate yourself.

I was excited to learn about Geology this year, but this has been by far the worst course I've ever taken at SMU. The test averages are 60s, and this professor seems like she never has an idea of what is going on. I would never suggest this professor to even my worst enemy. Her tests also cover an impossible amount of information to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is legit the worst lecturer i've ever had, she just reads off the slides and does a very poor job of explaining and when you ask a question she ridicules you for it. Assignments are pretty easy, but quizzes and tests are VERY tough. Do not take this class unless you want to dread going to class every day.

Asiye Zanjani is awful. The book that is required for the class is not used. She is hard to understand and rude to her students. To succeed in this class, do all of the extra credit and take note of the pole everywhere questions for tests. Don't be fooled, this class is NOT an easy A.
She is one of my favorite professors!

Rose is fantastic! Easy to pull an A in this class, just read over the lecture notes a time or two before every test. There's extra credit questions on every test and one test grade gets dropped; that test can be the final if you're happy with your grade. Rose's lectures get a little dry, but she'll throw in a witty comment that makes it worth it!

Take this class!! She is a great lecturer and makes the more dry material fun by watching videos of people with the disorders. Also, she gives great answers/responses to difficult questions students ask and is so well versed in psych. She tells super interesting stories and exams are relatively easy if you take good notes.

I respect Professor Ashraf because she is always willing to help during her office hours. However, her multiple choice exams are hard. Most teachers at SMU who see you put in lots of effort will bump up your grade a bit. However, she was NOT willing. Take GOOD class notes, and audio recordings. A 93 average  exempt from final

While the class is discussion based, your grade depends on four essays throughout the semester. If you don't write well, don't take her. There is little focus on writing and improvement is unlikely. She is always available for help if needed and when asked. Participation is essential and the discussions are interesting.
Fun and awesome teacher, but to be honest I only paid attention because she's smoking hot.

Really great Discernment and Discourse professor! She is extremely knowledgeable and makes all of the material very interesting. There are two in class essays and two out of class. She is willing to spend time outside of class in order to help you succeed. There is short homework on the reading (only short stories/articles). Take her class!

Dr. Avey definitely knows his field.  Overall, I enjoyed taking his class.  2 tests and a final, 4 discussion essays that are about 3 pages long each.  He is a fair grader, his tests can be a little tricky.  Fill in the blank (no word bank), ID questions, and essay questions.  His lectures can run over, so try not to have a class right afterwards.

Very good professor with a great academic background in international relations. Textbooks are completely unnecessary, I didn't open any of the books a single time. Attendance not mandatory, all PowerPoints are posted on Blackboard. Grades consist of tests and a handful of short essays. Fair grader, you get out what you put in.
For his first year teaching, Dr. Avey did a great job at engaging the students and making the lectures interesting. I highly recommend him for anyone needing an intro-level pillar requirement.
Ayala taught well, but he took a long time to give feedback in CS 3330. The lecture also did not line up well with the concurrent GUI/DB lab.

Caring and pretty funny guy. The lecture moves pretty fast but not bad if you pay attention. He doesn't grade anything though and rarely puts in any grades. Definitely better professors than him to take if you're a CS student. Only 2 exams and both take home.

Professor Ayala is a very nice person and truly cares for his students. However, he doesn't put in grades until the end of the semester, so you really don't know if you're passing the class or not. He rarely gives tests and they are usually take home.

Really nice guy and incredibly helpful if you ask for assistance. He just moves through lectures super fast so it's important to keep up. I wish he would break down concepts a little more and go through a few more examples of each before just moving on. He did however mention it was his first time teaching this class so I couldn't expect much.
Best class you will ever take at SMU!
Prof Chris Ayala is an incredible person as well as instructed for the Robotics class. He is a great resource to have.
Fantastic class! Fantastic professor! It was hard, but I learned more than I ever thought I would!
He's awesome and super helpful
Best professor ever. You will not regret taking him
He's amazing! Would take again
