Professor Ayala is a wonderful person, a brilliant computer scientist, and really puts forward the extra effort to get to know his students.  He is super easy to talk to and knows what he is talking about, so be sure to ask him if you have any questions, you won't be disappointed!
Professor Ayala was very helpful when he was a TA for my class before becoming a professor. He's really nice and makes every effort to help you succeed.

Prof. Ayala is one of a few professors for KNW 2300: First Year Engineering Design. The class is tough, but worth it. Prof. Ayala is very helpful if you make the effort to ask him questions during class and office hours. However, he won't just give you the answer. He is going to help you to discover it for yourself.
Prof Ayala is an awesome professor who is alway there for you and really cares!!!!

Cool professor that knows his stuff. Class can be slow but perhaps it was just my lack of interest in the topic. Tests are essay based but are very fair so as long as you understand the main concepts, you will do fine. Good class to take if you need history credit and are tired of taking US history, etc,etc

Professor Moin is pretty great.  Class can be a bit dull, but if you do even some of the reading before class and participate the slightest bit each class you're guaranteed to do well.  Pretty easy grader and you do actually learn a lot.  If you're looking for a good grade definitely take him
This professor was so good, that I ended up taking him 3 times.  Enjoyed his class and he doesn't overwork you with papers and tests.

This guy is your cool uncle. This is the kind of dude you want to grab a beer with. His class is so easy, you get two pages of notes (use your review test) for every exam. Just go to his review sessions to fill out your packet and you'll get an A no problem. Plus, I learned quite a bit from this class. It's a good time, take this course.
Highly recommended!! Cares how you do!

Kenneth Berry rambles on and on. His lectures are so boring, and on TOP of that, the lectures do not match the labs as well. His teaching style makes no sense, and he jumps from one topic to the next. One day we would learn about something, and the next day we are talking about something COMPLETELY different. TA and Professor don't communicate.

Be prepared for his mood swings. He rambles all class and the content discussed in class doesn't align with test material. Overall, he's a nice enough guy but if you're on his bad side, you're on his bad side.

Prof Berry is a pretty nice dude to take for ECE 1301. The class itself isn't the easiest thing in the world, but he gives lots of material to help you do well, including two full pages of notes as a cheat sheet on every test, that you can put anything on. He also provides a ton of worksheets. Labs are a little wack but they are easy to do well in.

(Took 2229/2230) He's extremely knowledgeable and brilliant, but his lectures can be hard to follow and his idea of clarification is re-explaining exactly what he said before. That said, he's accessible and his grading is extremely lenient. Though it seems intimidating (especially the composition project), you will succeed in his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Scheer is extremely knowledgeable about his chosen field, it's just his delivery that can be rather monotonous at 8:00 in the morning twice a week. That being said, he is an extremely forgiving grader and he will get you through Music Theory. His piano playing skills are incredible and sometimes he'll surprise us with a joke or two.

Dr. Scheer is clearly a very nice professor, but his lectures are hard and complicated to learn and even difficult to listen to. If you take his class with no prior knowledge of music theory, be prepared to read the textbooks multiple times or watch videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable but assumes his students have an advanced background in theory so his teaching is very technical/confusing. Difficult to transfer lecture info to complicated assignments (class would routinely fail tests), requesting clarification is unhelpful. Would probably be brilliant to work with as a composer, not as a basic theory student
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Scheer has his days. This is his first year teaching, but he is still very good. He doesnt explain in a very detailed manner unless you ask him to. He assumes you understand certain concepts given youre a music major of the sorts. His tangents are him making sarcastic jokes about composers and playing music at random. Still learned, thx Scheer!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dow is amazing. I feel like I am not only learning for the class but for myself. He also often lets us out of class early. If you pay attention in class, you will do great in this course.
Take his class!!! He has 4 exams and provides cheat sheets. As long as you show up to class and pay attention, you'll do great.
This is such a bad classs bad professor.
Professor Dow is amazing, one of the better Cox professors I've had. His lectures are entertaining and he's a normal guy and very understanding.
he's really smart and chill guy!! Take him
This guy is soooo overrated. Nobody likes him.

Very easy class, he's very understanding if any students have needs and he's overall fun to talk to. You have 4 exams, no final and can bring a sheet to each exam. You also have 3 group projects and class participation that factors into your grade but it's not that bad. Pretty much no homework either. Would recommend him over other MNO professors.

This class is such a breeze. Attendence and participation in clas matters a lot. There is 4 exams, 3 group projects, and no final. You are able to use a cheat sheet on all 4 exams so test's are pretty much a breeze too.

Dr.Dow was a life changing experience for me at SMU Cox personally and one of my favorite professors. He doesn't only just care about his students but also inspires them by giving them a real world skills. Very engaging lectures and he's one of the most knowledgeable professors out there who will do anything for his students to succeed.

He is a good man who puts his students before any bureaucratic red tape. He recognizes effort however is not overly generous where it is not deserved. He is clear in his expectations and if you meet them you will do extremely well. 

Bravo Benjamin!!!

Literally one of the most relatable teachers, he cares and has his opinions on how students should be treated and knows he is a 100's style class. Uses a lot of movie clips to showcase examples of management, big group projects, a couple of tests but they are with a cheat sheet

Dr. Dow is a very easy grader. There are three group projects and one individual project. He never makes you present or write a paper. There are four tests throughout the semester which you can have a cheat sheet on, which makes the tests very easy. He is a very engaging lecturer and often times lets us out early. He was a great professor!

if you need a chill business class, take MNO 3370. so chill, barely any outside work. two tests that are open note and 20 questions. you can make your consulting project as intense or chill as you want it to be. fantastic guy and really cares about his students. you WILL get an A

Favorite professor I've ever had. Lectures are super interesting and you get a front and back cheat sheet for every test. Not the easiest grader but if you put in a little time you will do well. Not very responsive to emails so make sure to talk to him in class.

I took him for MNO 4330 Consulting and I highly recommend. He was a consultant and knows his stuff. You work with a group throughout the semester and act as consultants for a real company. Couple tests but they're open note. Must participate 7 times throughout semester.
take him, his exams are so easy and he basically gives you the answers on the exams.

Dr. Dow is by far one of the most kindest and compassionate professors I have ever met! He genuinely enjoys teaching and always has a smile. He makes the class entertaining and fun, which is why I always looked forward to going. No words can describe just how amazing and special this bro is. Dr. Dow is a legend!
He is the sweetest ever! super helpful with reviewing tests and for the group projects! Theres only 4 exams and theyre pretty easy and you get a cheat sheet. Love him, take him hes great

He was the best business professor I've had so far, and his class was super easy if you studied. Don't be discouraged if you have a B because he gives extra credit and grades the group projects generously. He also curves the class at the end of the year. I loved his class last semester!

Amazing professor. His lectures are fun, interesting and useful in everyday life. His group projects are enjoyable and easy, and the tests are super easy if you studied. Get tasks done ahead of time so you don't have to worry about the class. He cares about students and will help anyone, take him for management.

GOAT professor. Dow always lets you out early, has us watch movie clips during class, and gives little to no homework. Tests are easy because he lets you use a cheat sheet. Get a good group for your group projects and your set.
Best teacher for management, straightforward tests with some questions that are completely free. Only real effort you have to put in this class is for group projects.

Professor Dow was awesome. You were are allowed Cheat sheets front and back on every quiz. Only 3 Group Projects, so make sure you get a good group for that. He isn't a tough grader on Group Projects though. You barely have to do work outside of class. Definitely recommend him if you want a more chill class.

Professor Dow is great! Made the lectures super engaging and was my favorite class this semester. There are three group projects but he's not a tough grader. He quizzes on more conceptual aspects of the content rather than definitions, so pay attention to the main takeaways, and you get a cheat sheet. Definitely take Professor Dow if you can!

For a required class, he made the material interesting. The lectures were engaging. Be ready for group projects. Allowed a cheat sheet for quizzes (front and back). Class participation consists of sharing some thoughts on material or opinions. Many opportunities are given to participate. He is also flexible and willing to work with students.

If I could have Prof. Dow teach every class, I would stay in school until the day I die. He is seriously the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares for his students and does an incredible job teaching the material. I have never loved going to class more. TAKE HIM!! You won't regret it. I can't say enough amazing things about him.

Such a sweet guy. You get a whole page, front and back, for cheat sheets. With an hour of studying and a good cheat sheet, you'll get As on the quizzes. Class isn't boring, and he'll finish early if the lectures are short that day. No midterm/final, just a few group projects so pick good people. Ask him for feedback on projects before submitting!

Very nice and helpful! He was accessible outside of class to help solve problems with the group project and was open to feedback throughout the semester. He allows a cheat sheet for quizzes which are easy if you read the slides. Take him for a fairly stress free and interesting class!

not the worst but not the best. new teacher so listens to student feedback. class is just boring, common knowledge, and not necessary but still is. lots of quizzes that can be tricky based on slides. large group project at the end. fine if you have to take it , but i wouldn't recommend otherwise. he's a golden retriever unless he's over the class
Would 100% take him again, helped me decide I want a MNO major. Love prof. Dow, no question take him for MNO whether you need it or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's a great guy who cares about his students. Quizzes were pretty easy and the little homework he assigns is very manageable.

Show up to class as participation is graded, weekly quizzes are a little difficult but he made them easier later on in the course, 2 group projects that are pretty easy. Really great guy and professor. I definitely recommend him.

Most adaptive professor I've ever had. Genuinely wants feedback to be a better instructor and adjusts to the class's needs. The quizzes started out hard and when he saw the average grade was not very good he asked for our opinion on them and changed them. It's hard not to get an A in his class let alone to fail. Genuinely cares about his students
Loved this class with Professor Dow! Would 100% take again.

Professor Dow is the sweetest professor I have met at SMU. This man genuinely cares about his students and wants them to grow. He is funny and his lectures were always engaging. Quizzes are generally easy, just make sure to study the slides. Love this man, take him!

Quizzes in this class are painful and can easily bring grade down. A lot of answer choices on the quizzes have very similar answers so I just wish things could have gone different in that area. There is a group project though that is fun and typically helps grade out.

Professor Dow is awesome! If you participate in class and pay attention to lectures you will be perfectly fine. Professor Dow is understanding and adjusts the tests if they turn out to be too difficult overall. 10/10

Professor Dow is a straightforward teacher with a well-structured class. Every two weeks we take a 10-question quiz on the material studied. You'll likely get a good score on the quiz if you review the slides a few times. We had a midterm group project paper and a final paper in the same format. Very doable and the class is very enjoyable!
Take this class! Benjamin Dow is a great professor and you will likely pull an A with little to no effort. The content of the class is also very helpful and informative.

Dr. Smith is such a wonderful professor! Her class is easy, and she is good at explaining material when asked. Labs aren't too difficult, but practicums do take some time to study for. But, you will be well prepared for them when the time comes. She does teach all freshman biology labs, so learning her teaching style is helpful.

Dr. Smith is an amazing professor! She is really funny and always helps answer questions. If you are sick and miss a lab she has open lab hours and will let you sit in on one of her other labs. Her quizzes can be confusing but they are open note. She drops the lowest quiz and lab grade, and is genuinely always excited about biology. Great TAs!
Super easy class if you pay attention, and she puts in a lot of effort to make sure her instructions are clear. If you put in a bit of time to prepare for the practicums, you're in the clear.

Smith is a funny and caring professor. The labs depend on who you get on your table, but they were fun for me. You get three hours to do the lab, so you really should not be worried about not being able to finish or do well. Some post-lab quiz questions are not explained fully, but are not difficult overall. Straightforward if you do the work

Took this class as a May term for my Exploring Science CC and the course was amazing. The test are on the material presented in class and is very self explanatory. If you pay attention and show up, you will do well.

I LOVE DR SMITH. She is so funny and helpful. Final exam was the hardest part of the class, but def manageable. She was kind of a harsh grader with post-labs but it was fine. You get a lot of grades so everything evens out

Dr. Smith is the best! She is one of the most helpful professors in office hours and the classroom and she really cares about her students. She takes the time to get to know them and tries to make a positive atmosphere for everyone. Her classes have been great for molecular genetics and biochem lab. Definitely take. So fair, so nice, love her.

Tests were way harder than they shouldve been and the class overall is just too annoyingly time consuming for a bio for liberal arts class. Shes nice and helpful and willing to guide you on what to study but you really have to fight for a good grade

She does not know how to teach students and has favorites. I heard that she was talking poorly about students to their classmates. Exams are hard and lab reports are graded super harshly. She has dry humor that comes off as rude. she messes up experiments and puts it out on the students, the quizzes are insanely hard. Avoid at all costs!
extreme views
Bad teaching and very biased. Way too much work and vague grading.
She's chill the people that are hating are exaggerating, she cares about participation for sure and rubric for assignments can be vague but overall not bad

Professor Berk is an expert on the healthcare in the Middle East and has a ton of experience in that part of the world. She uses that to make the class really interesting, which is great. The class is not very hard and she gives helpful feedback. Would definitely take again.

Extreme left radical who believes and teaches 1000 gender ideologies, not the right fit for smu, many of us have complained becuase she's not onlya bad teacher, shes proselytizing her personal beliefs as if they are fact and your grade depends on your ability to repeat them.

Besides having some vague terms set for grading that I wish she told me about before, she is an amazing and very kind teacher who stays very on topic but also tells us some interesting stories sometimes. I love that she always uploads slides before class, which teachers rarely do for some reason. I'd love to take her again.
Extremely left viewpoint and not afraid to show. Must agree with her for a good grade.

Dr. Berk has been one of my favorite professors at SMU! She is so sweet and makes the course really interesting. You have to read before every class, but it's a humanities class so it's kind of expected. Her lectures and discussions about the reading in class are super insightful, I haven't met anyone who has taken her who doesn't like her class!
super vague when grading "be more specific" is thrown around way too much. I have gone into office hours it was so useless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Berk is super chill, understanding, and nice. Her classes were straightforward and a great introduction to the topic. She is an engaging lecturer, gave barely any homework, and was a generous grader. Easy money

Professor Berk is an amazing professor whose expectations are very clear. As long as you keep up with the reading and participate in class you'll do great. She is extremely insightful and covers interesting topics as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Speaks nonstop for hours, offers no good visual aids, and she will not repeat herself so its imperative to listen and write quickly. She uses terms than the ones provided on your textbook and she never clarifies that either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the least competent professors at SMU, doesn't have a grasp on the material she is teaching, course was horribly organized if you could even call it that, she tries to be everyone's friend rather than a professor, tolerating bad behavior and had no class management skills, just do not take her, like being taught by a middle school coach.

Dr. Berk is one of the most kindest, inspirational people I've ever met! She lights up the room with her vibrant energy and is easy to talk to. I took Health, Healing and Ethics with her over the Summer and it was fascinating. Her feedback on our essays was excellent and made me a better writer and was a chill grader. Take Dr. Berk, she's amazing!!

Lectures are great. Homework perfectly reflects the content learned in the lectures. The exams are tough but doable. Dr. Lee is super passionate about the material and explains it in an easily understandable way.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Barry Lee is nice and will walk you through the problems if you visit during office hours. Lectures are confusing and topics are hard to grasp. Averages for exams are low and he grades on a curve that you will not know where you stand until the end of the year. I don't know how other professors are in Lin Alg, but this class was hard.

Hard class, regardless of the professor.
Need to study on your own, tests are hard and lecture/concepts explaining is not very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not address questions very well as he expects students to grasp the content immediately and is slightly condescending. I struggled the most on the first exam due to the learning curve with linear algebra concepts. The test averages are poor, but he will curve at the end of the course. Show him you're putting in the work and you'll be fine.

I have never gotten below a 78 on any math test in my entire life + while I have been a student at SMU. This has been the most difficult and stressful class I have taken in my life - because of prof. Lee. To put things in perspective, the average on the first test was a 52%. He leaves no room for questions during lectures. Get him out of this dept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He wants everyone in his class to succeed, and he begs his students to put in as much effort as he does. I struggled the whole year, but he appreciated my willingness to work harder, and he bumped my grade up. The class is extremely conceptual, and I think he teaches them well. Random attendance checks, scales exams to high, cold calls often
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was tough. He flew through lectures and asked if anyone had questions and would be met with silence from a class unsure of even where to start. Nice guy, and seems to be doing his best. The lecture materials made so much more sense when I read the non-required textbook. Test averages failed consistently. Do homeworks and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and he is always available to help. Cares about students success and it very helpful. Exams can be tough so make sure to study ahead of time.

Professor Lee is a sweet individual, but his teaching style is not helpful at all. He rushes through the lectures and gives a bunch of abstract concepts with little to no info on how to apply them. I would highly recommend avoiding this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy and you can tell he wants you to succeed but he's just not that great of a professor. He talks to the board while teaching and makes it hard for you to see what he's writing. Also he goes super fast in lectures and doesn't really explain the huge concepts that he throws out there. Wait to take another professor, trust me.
It is a super super hard class but he is always available to help and answer all of your questions no matter how many times you ask!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but very disorganized. Did not follow the book. Made everything more complicated than necessary. I went to tutoring center & the tutors were even confused. Class average was like a 70 at the end of the semester. He did curve a little bit at the end because everyone failed his tests. Wait a semester to take another prof - it's worth it

He's a sweet professor who wants you to understand the material, but he doesn't understand how. The test average is roughly a D to C for any given test. In class is fine, but the tests are nothing like the notes or homework. I genuinely don't understand how he makes his tests so disconnected from the rest of the material. Tests are 90% of the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: *Attendance counted as bonus credit for us.* Office hours: he can talk you through whatever you need. In-Class: he goes at the speed of light. Tests are hard as hell. Know vocabulary really well and know the mechanics really well. All-nighters will be how you get a C- (see my grade). Study at least 2 or 3 days beforehand. Formulaic class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lee is a caring prof who doesn't want to fail his students, but he assigns difficult problems for exams and makes them 90% of the grade. Complex Variables are also annoying as hell to learn. I think I could've gotten an A in a different course he was teaching, but MATH 5331 is just... ugh. Do not take MATH 5331 (no matter who is teaching it) at SMU

Professor Lee moves way too fast for Complex Variables. His class felt impossible no matter how hard I tried to do well. He does not want to make you fail and hell work with you, but its hard to keep up during lectures. He talks to the board and makes it hard to see what hes writing. Also super proof heavy. Proofs on every test.

His lectures are too fast and he throws out terms that he never really explains. His tests are tough, especially the truth/false portions, because the answer is often subtle. A nice enough guy, but not a great professor. I gave up on a math minor after this class because no matter how hard I tried, I was always left frustrated. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 25% of this rating is on Lee himself. He usually just throws proofs up on the boards; however, he has review sessions and very open office hours for people who need help. He is caring, but his grading scheme is way too exam heavy. Now, the 75%: DO NOT TAKE MATH 5331 EVER, NO MATTER WHO IS TEACHING IT. Complex variables are so hard and useless.

Three exams constitute 90% of your grade, and he gives almost no partial credit on them. The homework is 10% at like 10 assignments, they're 1% each but they take like 4 hours to finish and the TA takes off points for retarded reasons. He has to make his grading scale nice and let us use a reference sheet because the grading system is braindead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Barry Lee is a classic Math professor in that he thinks that just by throwing proofs on the board his students will just "get it" and understand it. He doesn't explain anything very well at all, expects students to just figure it out. Textbook isn't any help either. He is a genuinely nice guy, and he isn't that strict, but far from easy. Dont take.
If you're someone who relies on the professor 100% to teach you the material, you may have to put in a little extra effort. Otherwise it's very possible to make an A.
speak quietly and it is hard to read his handwriting. Don't take him unless you really need.

He's absolutely adorable. Sometimes hard to understand but he writes clearly and is always available for help. He encourages class participation so be ready for that. He has review sessions with sample problems before the test and allows for a full page of notes for the exam.

He speaks quietly, making him somewhat to difficult to understand and his handwriting is bad. Other than that, there is homework every week and he allows you to have a full front and back "cheat sheet." There is no restriction on what information you include on that paper. He encourages classroom engagement and offers out of class help.

Oh boy, oh boy. One of the worst courses I have taken. I thought it would be more MATLAB oriented, but most of the work was by hand. Lectures were long and confusing. He did not articulate and wrote in extremely tiny messy font on the board. No numerical examples. Kept telling us it was "easy". Avoid at all costs.
Lectures are not clear at all.Notes do no have any correlation to problems on test, homework or projects. Does not seem interested in the concerns of the students.

Extremely difficult, doesn't use numerical examples in class.  a lot of coding that is not discussed in class, ta is not allowed to give any help on code.  test averages were around 50s always.  doesnt curve till end of semester

Professor Bhattacharya is a great professor that breaks down difficult concepts well and encourages students to ask questions. 4 tests (including final), 4 quizzes, and 1 mini-project. Lowest test & quiz are dropped. Do the MyLab first and then practice problems on the lecture slides (most important) and you'll be good for the tests and quizzes.

Neil is the teacher to take for ACCT 3311. He breaks down the topics in class very well. Homework is not graded and helps a lot for tests, top 3 tests are graded out of 4 and lowest test is dropped including the final. Unfortunately grades are made up of all quizzes and tests and test often cover a lot of information. If you prepare you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything already said about this professor is true. either him or the class being very inconsiderate, such a short amount of time to learn, how are we supposed to remember 1,000 formula's for one test, and 7 articles each 10-15+ pages, and ONLY get one small notecard for notes. This class is dumb and the professor don't make it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is incredibly hard for no reason. It's not an accounting class, so I don't know why it's required and labeled ACCT. Group project is so hard because he gives little to no instruction for anything. Gave a final presentation, paper, AND exam. Lectures are really confusing. Seems really arrogant. Nice-ish guy but avoid this class if you can

Actually for ACCT 6244. This is barely an accounting class. Classes involve rational investors rather than actual accounting. Writing assignments arent bad. Class project/presentation is hard because he doesnt give any helpful instructions. Final exam is cumulative with no notes over very specific content. He barely uses canvas. Hard for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything is backloaded with very unclear expectations on literally everything he gives you. Terrible at his job

I really enjoyed him.  Homework was very helpful and working stuff in class made stuff click.  Very fair on exams and I would totally take him for other accounting classes.  My only complaint is it was a guessing game on the grade cause he refuses to use canvas.

Bhattacharya was an excellent professor, and in my opinion, the best of the Intermediate 1 group. His lectures are clear and direct, and his explanations are incredibly useful to not only prep for exams, but to also understand the concepts as a whole. The exams themselves are weighted highly, but it is easy to score well.

Mr Neil understands accounting and the concepts very well and hes good and dumbing them down and using examples to make sure you get it. He doesnt make the class overall difficulty and if you struggle with Acct the class will be hard but if Acct isnt bad then this class will be pretty easy and straightforward. overall good class, good teacher

Professor Neil is probably one of the best professor you could possibly take for Intermediate Accounting. It is hard material but he makes it much easier than how other professor are teaching it. He could be hard to understands sometime but he explains material in a way that everyone can understand.

the most unhelpful, unorganized professor I've ever had. He gave no clear expectations, makes ppl feel stupid for answering unless it's what he wants to hear. He also writes down everyone's name that speaks in class very obviously. The lectures are dense and he doesn't do a good job of engaging the class. Assignments backloaded and grades very hard

Neil is an amazing professor! He is great at lecturing dense topics in an easy manner and his exams are pretty easy. He has no homework and he is very clear with his expectations; his group-project is difficult given the time but he provides enough guidance for you to ace it! He's one of the best I've had in college. GET YOUR NAME ON THE PAPER!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easier option but won't learn real world application as much.

Professor B. is fantastic as a professor and a person. Very kind, very accessible, and much more straightforward than other intermediate accounting classes taught at SMU. ~weekly homeworks, 4 quizzes, 4 tests w/ the lowest dropped. He cares about his students, and wants you to succeed. I cannot write a more glowing recommendation of him.

For Acct 3311, allowed a notecard for most tests, had frequent quizzes. But overall a great accounting professor. He explained the material really well and genuinely cared about what he was talking about. Encourages class participation, but not required. Tests are pretty difficult but not impossible. Best intermediate accounting professor.

This is for ACCT 3311 because it is not populating as a choice. Yes this is a hard accounting class, get ready to study for the exams. 4 quizzes worst one is dropped. 3 exams that are hard so be prepared and study. I think he is a good professor he is very professional and polite.

Group project is very important - do NOT start late, start ASAP. He obviously cares for his class & students, just pay attention, ask questions, and make use of office hours & he'll like you. He is extremely smart but a good professor, given the difficulty of the class/subject. VERY important to understand what he is teaching saying in class!!!

Accounting Theory is an extremely heavy class given the extensive amount of reading materials in a short period of time. Team work is important so make sure you can work well with your teammates. Class participation is a must. Do the homework problems, read his slides and required articles to prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: a great professor take with him

Class is relatively easy if you do the work.  Either he likes you or he doesnt.  Is not very helpful when you meet with him if he does not like you.  Prolly one of the better acct. 2311 classes because hes one of the easier teachers.
Awful professor. Class lectures offer no new information and do not relate to the homework/exam. I like the subject matter but found this professor to be completely ineffective in teaching it.
Very detailed and is a great help when you ask for it.

The class was quite challenging, but not impossible. It's an introductory-level course, so I didn't expect it to be this challenging. However, most of the content is covered in class, so make sure to attend. The professor explains the material well, but moves quickly, so you need to keep up. Ensure you achieve a high grade on the labs.

Honestly, Idk why everyone is rating Bhatia so harshly. Her class was tough but she was nice. She's hard to understand but the lecture slides explain everything. Tests are open note + a curve on all. The labs if you attend will get a 100 and those are a heavy percentage of the course grade. I wouldnt take her again but the class was not impossible

Worst experience at SMU. DO NOT DO THIS TO YOURSELF. The exams are no longer open computer and do not cover anything in class. She is rude and and does not respond to emails. I took this class for credit and took my first W ever. Her exam average after an alleged curve was 50. Take any class other than this.

Worst experience at SMU. I have loved every professor I've had here except her. Her tests have almost nothing to do with the material she attempts to teach us during class. Slow to respond to emails and does not seem to care if her students understand the concepts.

Good lecturer and attendance was only taken once. However, most material covered in the tests were learned only in lecture since there was no textbook available, so make sure to not skip class too much. Tough tests but open note (unlimited pages) and no final. Do not underestimate tests, this is still a science class. Math and memorization are key.
She is very hard to understand, but her class is fairly easy. All exams (3) are open computer. Show up, listen to lectures, and have a good study guide and you will get at last a B
Her tests are meant to trick you and she constantly contradicts herself so you don't go in with strong knowledge anyhow.
This is one of the worst professors at SMU. Does not seem to understand how to grade or teach.

A poorly designed class & exams are do-able, lectures/questions are vague and confusing to understand. She is a professor who emphasizes the importance of good communication, but does not follow her own guidance. Slide decks are old and she snaps at you if you ask questions which created a negative learning environment.

Love Prof. Bhushan she's super sweet and gives good lectures! Beware of tests, 3 tests worth 81% of your grade. A lot of questions with limited time. The questions have really tricky wording. Also gives short quizzes that have similar questions to the test. My advice, study questions similar to the ones on the quiz and you'll be fine on the exam

This class was painful. She is super nice and a good enough teacher, but she'll put the most random stuff on the tests that are sooooooooo difficult and meant to trick you and definitely came out of NOWHERE. Get ready to work. Accessible outside of class and super caring and understanding which is great but her tests make no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Bhushan really cares about her students and does her best to make sure the class is keeping up with her. I took her over the summer, so the classes were long but she gave us a short break every day. As long as you do the homework and study the slides closely you should do well. Also, she brought in coffee for the final - so sweet.

This professor is by far one of my favorites at SMU; she makes an incredibly boring subject much more accessible. Despite this, these class is incredibly tedious and I cared so little for it. I recommend trying to review the learned material each week. I left the final exam in tears, not because of the professor, but because of the difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's the best teacher for financial accounting. Very clear and fair. Usually very nice too but occasionally can be moody. If you try you'll get an A. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She'll tell you that an A for this class is 96% but she actually gives the final grade on a curve. Lectures are decent, she clearly knows her stuff. The problem is that she doesn't have much interaction with students outside of the classroom. Top 30% of the class will get an A- at least. If you wanna earn an A, this summer class can be intense.

Dr. Bhushan is very sweet and genuinely cares about her students doing well. Expectations are fairly straightforward and your grade is almost entirely comprised of 3 tests (at least in the summer course). She is willing to work through problems to help make sure everyone understands and I feel that taking her class has prepared me for the future.

I took this class during the summer and really enjoyed it, even as a Biology major. Her lectures are super easy to follow so as long as you stay on top of the homework and read the slides before class you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Take her class in the summer! Seema is the absolute best! She is available for extra help during office hours and will answer any question you have. She made me want to work hard and earn my A.  She really wants you to succeed!

She was hands down the best professor I have had at SMU. Took Acct 2301 with her in the summer and it was great. Without her there is no way I would've learned the material so well. Almost everyone I know did well in the class and enjoyed her teaching style.
If you have the opportunity to take one of her classes DEFINITELY DO! Great teacher and so helpful.

One of the best professors I've had at SMU! She genuinely wants her students to do well and is more than willing to help them. If you go to class, do the homework, and study the slides, an A is achievable. I feel more than prepared for the next accounting courses after having her as a teacher.
go to class---she tells you what will be on the test. very helpful, very smart, and caring.
Great professor! Pay attention in class and study the slides. She will tell you exactly what is on the exams.
Amazing professor. Best teacher ever I had at SMU. Teaches well with powerpoints and her class is easy to comprehend. If you study you will make an A. Otherwise you can make a B or less.

Gotta go to class otherwise it wouldn't make any sense.  If you listen in class and do the homework, class is easily passed with B or higher.  She's really nice, and actually cares about her students performance.  Can be boring, but she makes things pretty clear.

Seema is the best, she is so nice and helpful. I took 3301 and 3302 with her and both times the whole class just loved her. If I could have taken her for intermediate 1 I definitely would have, but she doesnt teach it. She is always willing to meet with students to help them out. Personally, Im not an accounting person, but I got an A, love her!

Graded on homework, prelab, labs, post labs, quizzes, and exams. She said for future classes she will only allow 1/2 of a 3x5 notecard for quizzes. Hope you can fit 80 slides of content on that. She changes her grading and criteria frequently. Not too much time and effort though.
Do not listen to other reviews this class is not an easy....

Very easy Class easiest class ive taken, she is nice, and the class takes up little time, labs are only once every other week and all the outside work in class can be done in 10 mins. theres only 2 exams and its very easy material with basic level stuff

The professor will have 80+ slides on her PowerPoint, but only lets you use one side of a 3x5 notecard for her weekly quizzes. The professor is a joke. It is impossible to do well in her class. DO NOT take this class or this professor. She treats chemistry for liberal arts like it's for chem majors. Her expectations are absurd. She is delusional.

This class is excessively demanding, requiring pre-lab, lab, post-lab, homework, and quizzes weekly. It also demands memorizing over 40 slides of information for each quiz. The professor's high expectations and condescending attitude make it difficult for non-majors to succeed. Worst professor at SMU.

my biggest problem is that she simply just reads off the slides, but other than that she is caring and gives extra credit chances. Lectures aren't very engaging but as long as you learn the slides one way or another you will likely do well. Labs are easy, simply just a matter of following instructions closely. Tests make up most of grade so study
So easy to get an A with the extra credit and the quizzes being based off hw

She is actually so sweet and funny and cares about her students. We were like friends by the end of the year. She was very available outside of class for office hours and let me make up an exam that I missed being sick. She just gets annoyed if you talk during her lectures which is understandable. You have nothing to worry about if you have Helen.
Just not a good teacher but an easy A which is why everyone takes her and calls her "sweet" - she is anything but

She is such a sweetheart. I thought the class would be easier than it was, but I really enjoyed it. The material is applicable to the real world, which makes understanding the material easier. on my first exam in her class I got a 55 and the second one I got a 95. Listen in class and do the homework, and it shouldn't be too difficult.

Such a sweet lady! Go to class and lab and you'll do just fine, she has up to 10 extra credit points available per exam. Exams, quizzes per chapter (in class, closed note), homework, and labs make up the grade. You will need to study for exams but she makes obvious what you need to know in class. Definitely take for ES credit!!

Dr. Babbili is a great professor pverall. Chem for liberal arts is not that difficult, the work just needs to be put in. Read the notes and do the extra credit assignments. She lets you skip the final if you have an A- in the class and her grading scale makes an 86 an A-. She is very sweet and understanding. Take her if you can.
Awful everything, so unprepared, so horrible at helping, so rigid and old in her technique.

Doesn't teach well, and makes the class harder than necessary by not having a cohesive syllabus or other materials. The material shouldn't be difficult, but she makes it difficult by limiting your available resource. Blatantly rude when students ask questions, answers with sarcasm.

She can be a little scary if you mess up during the lab, but she will help you get back on track. She's really nice, don't worry about it. Do the homework before the labs problems and the quizzes won't be too terrible.
She can be a little scary, but she cares a lot and is easy to communicate with outside of class. As long as you are open about what is going on she'll try and help you out.

She is a very sweet person, but can be condescending when you ask questions about the lab. She rounds sig figs at every step rather than the end. Be sure to do the homework before the lab since there are quizzes at the beginning of each lab over the lab you will be doing. The prelab writeup is easy and you'll be given points if you do it.

She is an amazing professor. Lots of information to study but it is extremely manageable. Go to her office hours, she loves it when students go to office hours. She will help you if you go to the office hours. Tests and quizzes are straight forward, if you work hard you will get an A

Professor Babbili is so sweet. If you have any questions about the lab, she is always very happy to help. She has very clear guidlines on the lab writeups, so it is easy to get a good grade. Make sure you do the homework before each lab because it is similar to the quizzes.
Such a wonderful lady! So kind and sweet.

Professor Babbili is incredibly sweet. She may not seem like it at first but she will warm up to you and you'll see that she is actually so nice. She is really helpful during lab and will guide you in the right direction. Definitely take her over Adams for lab.

She grades very easily and the tests are just like homework and quizzes, so you can actually focus on just learning the stuff for fun. She makes it easy for liberal arts ppl bc she teaches about how chemistry works in the world and doesn't make you memorize stuff. Such a kind person and makes the class super interesting, take if you ever can!!!

Professor Babbili is very understanding and kind, especially towards students who may struggle with math. Her lectures were enjoyable because she knows how to make chemistry interesting for non-STEM majors. Highly recommend this class!

Honestly, this class is not as easy as expected. There is a ton of work and quizzes almost every week, but she is super helpful if you go to office hours. The workload is a lot so I would only take it if you have time to study for all of the quizzes. Her grading scale makes an A a 90 and she has extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do the homework. The lab quizzes are very difficult so do the homework and read the entire lab very closely. Labs themselves are fun and the lab reports are easy to get good grades on. The labs use things you haven't learned in chemistry yet, so it can be difficult. Check for sig figs and rounding, she rounds at every step instead of the end.

Babili is a gem. She really does care about her students, and she makes you feel rewarded by asking her for help. She talks slowly, so it is easy to keep up. One knock is that sometimes it gets a little rough and monotonous, but she really tries. I did Jan term, and she made me love chem (although people say to not do the next lvl so I did not lol)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I took for Chem lab and I really liked her. She loves when you stay after class and asks questions she appreciates the effort and I feel like she graded me more leniently after that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Labs online and only met once every other week. She gives you all the information you need for the labs (because COVID we weren't able to meet in person and do the labs). Really nice. Take her for class or lab if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Babbili is so kind and helpful. The quizzes can be tricky sometimes but the labs make up most of your grade. This class was entirely online so the labs are just videos and you do the reports on your own. She grades fairly and will tell you if your answers are right or not if you ask.

Professor Babbili is the sweetest! She is very patient especially with answering questions since the class moved to an online format. She explains the labs very clearly. Definitely take her class if you get the chance!

She's just a joy. Got to know her pretty well from the first lab and it paid off, we had a great relationship from there on. Super friendly and caring. Smart and knows her way around the lab. I absolutely adore her and would recommend her for anyone taking chem lab. Favorite professor in college so far and it's not even close.
She's the sweetest. She really wants you to succeed and loves when you go to office hours. I made sure to take her for my next Chem lab

SO MANY QUIZZES. For a chemistry class for non-majors, Professor Babbili made the course quite unbearable. Do not take if you plan on not attending because she only allows 3 misses before deducting from your overall grade. Although the material is not difficult and is an easy A if you don't miss class, I would not recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mrs. Babbili is the sweetest professor I have ever had. She really cares about her students and will go out of her way to make sure they are successful.  I took her General Chemistry 2 class over the summer, and although it was a lot of material in a condensed time frame, she made it manageable. I would undoubtedly take a class taught by her again.

She explains things really well and is easy to understand. But if you take her course over summer the grade is based primarily on your test, but she communicates well and seems understanding, just don't miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! The professor who truly cares about her students. DO EVERYTHING to TAKE HER CLASS!

Professor Babilli makes chem. interesting in applying to everyday life. This class I actually learned things I will use forever.  I was in Gen Chem 1 prior and was failing so I switched and finished with an A. She genuinely cares about her students and is avail. for office hours. Show up, take lecture notes  and study you'll be fine. Quizzes weekl.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed her in lab. Clearly explains directions and is willing to help when needed. She is also really funny!

Good prof, easy class, largely just a repeat of basic high school chemistry. Labs are fun with her (generally), but lectures at 8AM are hell. She is painful to listen to at that time of day. Drops final if you have A going into it, and provides a good amount of Extra credit. Take!

This class is SO ridiculously easy. Anyone who says otherwise just didn't pay attention. Most of the material is stuff you should have already learned in high school. Easy A. Just review the notes with the "topics" she assigns for each chapter and you'll ace the quizzes. The tests are just variations of the quizzes.

she will never stop testing  you. you will have quizzes every week and never stop. she frequently  test you too because she maintain that test and quizzes help you study. if you don't like or not good at test do not! take! her!classes! Also, your grade  is build according to your grade.
She is very nice and passionate about Chemistry. She understands that it is not for everyone and will help you. Her quizzes and homework definitely prepare you for the exams.

Her class is very straightforward. If you pay attention and study  the lecture notes, you will be fine. It's easy only because she is so straightforward. Overall, great class for a non major, especially if you've never liked science much. She's super nice also!

Professor Babbili is a great professor and really wants all of her students to succeed. If you talk to her (before the last day homework is due), she will definitely help you out. Attendance is mandatory, or else you lose 3%. If you have a 92.5% or above before the final (which isn't that hard to do), you don't have to take the final!

Babilli was extremely helpful and her tests were easy and straightforward. She was always available for office hours and was happy to explain difficult topics. If you do the homework and review power points, you will do well on exams. She drops a quiz grade and tests were out of 108 points.
Take this class!  Easy A.  Professor Babbili is very nice and approachable.  3 exams and if you have an A average you don't have to take the final.  6 very easy labs (every other week).

I love Professor Babbili! She's so helpful and very clear. She speaks slowly in class and repeats herself. She goes out of her way to make sure everyone understands. The labs are easy and she's always there with the TAs to help. The quizzes are a bit difficult, but you can use them to study for the tests. You get out of the final if you have an A.
Great, helpful teacher. Study well for the tests and you will get mid to high A on them. Quizes are tough but only 10% of grade. Most get As on the labs. I recommend her she is a great teacher!
Every word she says comes in tests and quizzes so take notes. She speaks slow so her accent don't get in the way of her clarity. Great teacher definatelly recommend her class.
Babbili is the easiest teacher ever! She is very helpful. The only A I received in all 3 years was in her class. TAKE IT!
Lab every other week. Extra credit offered. Study for the tests. She cancels class every now and then. And the comment below is very true.
She is super lit all the time. You will be repeating the phrase "You Know" after every class. Overall pretty lit with a couple elements thrown in
Awesome, amazing teacher. It was a super interesting class. Definitely best science class I've ever taken. and she's super sweet.

Her lectures were interesting and easy to understand. She does have an accent but she's easy to understand. Labs were easy, quizzes and tests required some studying- but even though I got B's on most of these, she offers to much extra credit that I got an overall A and I did not have to take the final. Good class if you need a science credit.

I did not do well on two exams, took the replacement final which was complete multiple choice and walked out with an A. Labs are easy and were every other week. Attendance was taken at random. I recommend this course, she was very helpful to me.

SUCH AN EASY CLASS!  If you take good notes in class you don't even need to look at the textbook.  The class is also really interesting and the topics you learn about come up in every day life.  If you have a 93, you don't have to take the final & she drops the lowest quiz and test grades. TAKE THIS CLASS! Also labs aren't every week (every 2 or 3)
She is one of the nicest people I have ever met! Take her class because she will go out of her way to help you!
Class has nothing to do with chemistry, but I did nothing and walked away with an A. Can't complain.
Ridiculously easy. The textbook is unneccessary. Part of your grade comes from her random attendance checks. She drops your lowest test and your lowest quiz. Homework is extra credit on the test.

Hard to understand, and the class has absolutely nothing to do with chemistry. If you were hoping for a class where the chemistry would be easy I guess you're in luck because it has NOTHING to do with it. It's all about hippie environmentalist essays. Oh, and she's VERY condescending. I personally liked her, but like i said...she's very condescendi
Awesome professor!
Class and lab are easy when you go.  She's hard to understand and she's tricky on her questions but A's in the class are attainable.
I love the class. It's very easy and about the environment and protecting it.
No Comments

She was helpful when you asked questions, but is difficult to understand. She makes you feel stupid at first, but will help you eventually. She changes the assign alot during class, and gets frustrated with you from time to time. Take O'Brian if possible.
she was very helpful, and chemistry for the liberal arts is a pretty easy class.

Prof. Babilli is a very helpful professor. I missed the first 3 weeks of class because I had to have surgery, and I had trouble with getting caught up, and she really help me when I went in to speak with her. Also she drop 1 test 2 or 3 quizzes and a lab.

Strengths What she teaches during lectures will be on the test. The chapter review sheets are very helpful when studying. The labs are interesting and help you to understand the concepts taught during the lectures. Drawbacks Although you may not always

I still have no idea what a p-value is. She does not take attendance, so only like 20/100 people ever show up to class. All homework is online and easy. She graded on an insane curve where anything above an 83% is an A. Not a good teacher at all, you can't understand a thing she says, but at least you'll get an A if you can do math.

Never have I ever seen such a horrible professor. It is absolutely insane to me that she even made it past elementary school, and that's putting it nice. Her voice is heavily accented and super soft, I sat in the front and couldn't understand her. She has a microphone but doesn't know how technology works. Easy-ish class, just do practice exams.

I couldn't understand the professor in class or pay much attention to the lecture, but the class was still easy. She gives practice tests that are very similar to the actual exam.If you do the homework and practice exam you will be fine. She also give a lot of extra credit in class if you answer questions.

Pay so much for smu and for a math teacher, she is the worst. You have no idea what she's saying, all she does is read slides, no one goes to class, and the tests are a waste of time, tutors don't even help. total shame this is what you deal with when paying so much for education.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take her if you also want to spend $k on a tutor to actually teach you well and in an understandable interpretation of engligh.

Y'all need to chill for real. The professor is certainly trying her best and she makes the work super easy for people. She gives practice exams prior to the test and 3 attempts on the homework, I mean come on, what other professors you know that would do this for you guys?

She may be hard to understand, but she doesn't deserve a bad rating. The homework is easy, and you get three attempts to do each assignment. The labs are simple and not time-consuming, and her Ta always helps. She also lets you have a double-sided cheat sheet for the exams. Gives extra credit every class for participation. Good stat professor.

Horrible representation of smu teaching. They wouldn't have her answer a phone but they're gonna have her teach us math? She speaks English in a heavy Indian accent, you never understand what she's saying or writing. When you question what she's saying she gets offended and pretty much blames the lack of understanding on the student. Do not take!!!

she makes smu seem desperate for teachers or something. There is no excuse to hire a teacher like her. She barely speaks English and her handwriting is trash. I have a tutor that I pay $100 a hour, the only reason I understand what's going on. Do not take this class. Arizona state offers online classes that the credits transfer over btw!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she doesn't speak english. get my boy zoltan instead. her handwriting is awful. like i mean barely any english
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Biyikli is a very respectful person in general. Her class is pretty straightforward, as shown in the syllabus. She presents practice questions in class, so preparing for the materials in advance is definitely helpful. Assignments and exams are graded leniently, which I believe reflects her desire to see students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bing is the rudest professor I've ever had. He rolled his eyes at me when I simply said "hi" to him, will constantly cut students off when talking, and called me an “incompetent student” in a 1:1 (despite my 3.9 GPA as a pre-med). Very disrespectful. The fact that he graduated from Harvard is genuinely terrifying for our society. DO NOT TAKE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Will insult you to your face and its his way or the highway all the time.

I took him for his Pandemics class and he very very clearly has a certain way that he wants things done, how YOU do it, and he is an atrocious communicator. He also treats you and his TA especially very poorly and dismissively. When working on your project he will insult you, cut you off, and straight up told one kid he should not be in college.
UUUUGGGGGHHHHH and nope your way out now.

While being one of the most accomplished professors on campus (or possibly in the state), he's very friendly and always makes time for students. Classes are designed in a unique and engaging manner that keeps the class interesting but highly useful; many of the skills you'll refine in his class will be useful now and later on. Take him if you can!

HOURS of homework each week, majority of it is irrelevant to the actual class
Multiple in-class debates and activities that have nothing to do with public health
Most of your grade is based on a group consulting project 
Everything is graded harshly because expectations aren't communicated properly
Just a strange prof in general
This is my second time taking her and she's amazing this class though not my favorite. Just a lot of busy work especially towards the end of the semester but overall she's a great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SPAN 1502 is a lot of outside work in VHL but the class itself is fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor and is accessible for students but attendance matters and it is difficult when you have her everyday. You will have homework everyday from the textbook and it would take me up to 30 minutes. She puts in a lot of grades but the tests count for a lot of it and the tests were difficult and so much to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Binkowski is great teacher but, I had the most work by a country mile in this course than any of my other ones. The class is "Monday Wednesday Friday" but you have something to do every night of the week. So much busy work didn't learn much. I didn't learn anything knew this year and I would only *maybe* take for getting CC requirements.

You will do something EVERY. SINGLE. DAY...I wish I was kidding. I had her at 8 am, and she went asynchronous a lot of the time, but the amount of homework didn't end. This class is time-consuming, but as long as you complete all the VHL work on time, know the vocab and all class assignments for the tests, and go to class, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She tries her best to help her students get good grades. The test's are hard but I think a lot of that is regulated by the department. She did a really good job managing the online course structure and taking feedback from students to make it as smooth as possible.

Professor Binkowski is a gem she gives a lot of homework but most of it is just completion grades. The tests are hard but everything else is not and she is very understanding and helps her students a lot.
Have to really pay attention to vocab and reviews arent helpful. Professor was nice and helpful but wish I had tutor for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Binkowski is pretty chill and tries her best to make her students get A's. Her class was a lot of busy work and the tests were pretty hard, but because of all the minor assignments I was able to make an A.

Super easy Spanish teacher, if you just want to get your credits over with, she's the one to take. Wants everyone to get a good grade and helps as much as she can. Homework load isn't bad, and tests are fairly easy. Also funny and engaging in class. Super nice lady, great professor

Dr. B is one of the sweetest professors I've had at SMU. You have this class every day, and it turned into something I looked forward to because of the personal relationship we all formed. Some people cried when they left the final because she's amazing. Just put the effort in, go to class, do your homework, and show you care and you'll do well.

Dr. Binkowski is an amazing professor and human. She is warm and understanding; knowledgeable and encouraging. She is mindful that foreign languages do not come naturally to everyone, so she doesn't expect too much for students that haven't studied a lot of languages. She has interesting stories about her travels and life, and is well-versed.
Dr. Binkowski is one of my most favorite professors. Do your homework and take notes on the grammar and you'll do fine. Quizlet is HIGHLY recommended for studying vocab.

Professor Binkowski is one of the greatest educators I have ever encountered. Her passion for the subject and for her students is evident and has made learning a difficult subject genuinely enjoyable. Spanish is something I have always struggled with learning and Professor Binkowski made sure that every student, including me, succeeded.

Prof. B is amazing. She's funny and really cares for her students. To be fair I wanted to drop this class the first few weeks bc it can be very confusing but it gets better trust me!! Once you get a good understanding of phonetics its really easy (go to class). The only downside is she speaks in English A LOT and I feel like i lost my fluency

Easy grader and easy going.  It's not a blow off class but the work is minimal and not hard.  Study for the tests and you will be fine.  As far as spanish teachers go, very laid back. Would recommend.

If you're going to take a spanish class, she is the professor you want. She understands that not all her students are amazing at spanish, so she'll talk in spanish and english for the class. She grades very nice compared to my other spanish teacher. She loves giving side stories and makes spanish fun!

Binkowski is a great professor. She is there for all of her students, doesn't play favorites like many profs with a small class. Most of her material is available to review through Blackboard. Speaks a good amount of English for a Spanish class. Likes to tell funny side stories, takes a personal interest in her students. Highly recommend her!
She is a great professor. Teaches very clear, but doesn't grade very hard. Not super easy, but definitely would take her again. You get three absences and she is flexible with excused.

She's pretty hard to understand with her accent, but the class is easy enough. You get a cheat sheet on midterms and the final and the practice tests use the same questions. It's pretty easy to get an A, but if you actually want to learn stats I would recommend a different professor as this one is really hard to learn anything from.

Quite frankly one of the worst professors I have ever had. I just dont understand how SMU with all this money, could hire someone with such poor handwriting, and english. She is very rude if you email her about ungraded assignments. She says: "Dont teach me my job". I hope she is removed from the university for being so rude. NEVER take her class.

Class is easy, Homework and Labs are easy 100's. However she is crazy. She crashesout at the class for attendance being low when she doesnt d0 attendance. She gives random quizzes for extra credit and attendance, if you complete the quiz not in class she will drop you from the class. She also refuses to accept students in my class sick notes.

She is very nice and willing to work with you. She offers a lot of extra credit if you participate during the lecture. Her lectures are not the strongest, but they still get the message across. Overall not an especially difficult course and easy to obtain lots of extra credit points!

I never thought attending a semester's worth of classes and learning nothing was possible—until Biyilki's class. With a poor accent, projection (she mumbles a lot), and calling the class "trash," she's the worst Stats professor at SMU. Homework is easy with extra credit opportunities, but it's just memorization that's forgotten after the exam.

Crashed out daily over attendance. Didn't know english and also sucks at teaching. Never take her class. If you have an option of her and nothing, do nothing. Take literally anything else. Textbook is borderline useless, but some utility can be found. Avoid at all costs.

Not super difficult. I had to teach myself most of the material. Don't read textbook, she posts slides w/ all content. It is not hard to get an A or B in the class, you get three attempts on all homework and on the labs. Lab attendance is not mandatory. The practice tests had the actual test questions. She goes over practice questions which helps.

Overall, it is an easy class; attendance is barely mandatory, and you can get away with having your name signed in. She had a massive crash out over that, though, so idk how well that will work. A group chat will do you wonders. Be ready to lock in and cram for tests, she gives you one double-sided sheet for all exams, including the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A C- in her class is a 33% so passing is so easy. However, she has a thick accent so is difficult to understand the content. If you need to get the credit, she's fine, but if you need to learn the material do not take her class. You get 3 attempts on each assignment, 2 per week, so it can be figured out by process of elimination/doesn't take long.

She is the easiest professor at SMU; you only have to show up to class 80% of the time, can have your computer out all class, and work on something else; her labs are not mandatory to attend. You will have to teach yourself the class, but she posts practice tests a week before the exams with all the answers to the test. Her slides are accommodating

I don't understand why so many freshmen dislike her. As a sophomore, I think she's a good professor. Her English isn't great, and she can be harsh, but her grading curve makes the class worth it. My test average of 75 will still get me an A. You'll need to teach yourself the material, but if you memorize the practice tests, you'll do fine.

Don't get me wrong Professor Nurten is a terrible teacher and will crashout over the slightest inconvenience. However, homework and labs are multiple attempts with feedback and hints to guarantee you 100%, the tests are straight verbatim from the practice tests and she gives extra credit. So if you have the patience to deal with her, take her.

no, just no. if you take her get ready to learn everything on your own. she does give practice exams which are helpful but they won't be unless you teach everything to yourself first. she also goes crazy over attendance, seriously. its not the end of the world if you have her but it is definitely the harder route for this class.

She is so strict about attendance, it takes away 20 minutes of actual class time. If I am not learning anything by her, then I shouldn't have to show up. She is also really hard to understand. HOWEVER, the only reason I would recommend this class is because of the grading curve. I have an 85 but have an A- so do what you will with that.
Do not recommend. You can't hear or understand anything. You basically have to teach yourself. She gets mad out of nowhere and every one is just staring confused because literally what is going on.

She can barely speak English you can NEVER hear what she's saying, she gets mad at random things. She can seem chill at first  but then snaps out of no where and starts threatening ur attendance even if you were there. Strongly do not recommend idk who hired her. If u want to learn stats by yourself then take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really don't get the plethora of bad reviews -- her accent IS tough to understand, mostly because of how quiet she speaks, and it's a lot of self teaching, but the class itself is immensely easy. Her grading scale is immensely in your favor. In her class, a C- is 33-42.5 Homework is googleable too. Do the homework and you'll be fine.
Professor Biyilki's class is light on the schedule, while the material takes time to learn you won't be overwhelmed with workload. She is kind hearted and wants to make everything work
Easily the worst professor at SMU. My dog speaks better english! Certainly a diversity hire! Her classes are useless and you need to teach yourself the material. Avoid at all costs.

I don't really understand why everyone is complaining about her.Yes, she has an accent. no I cant understand her very well. However, this is quite literally the easiest class ever. Tests come straight from practice exam question bank. You get a whole piece of paper front and back for cheat sheet. can earn EC by participating in review days.

Do not take this class if you have the option. STATS isn't that hard on its own but when you have to learn everything on your own it becomes stressful. I have bad hearing and am not good at understanding accents but even to someone who is she is still hard to understand. Idk why I'm writing this when I should be studying. I'm sure she a good person
Be prepared to teach yourself everything, teacher speaks broken English and the lectures are so hard to follow yet takes attendance

She is not a good teacher. There is no arguing this but her class is easy if you are capable of reading and studying. Questions of tests are drawn from a bank similar to the ones on the practice exams she gives. Easy A.

You have two tests worth 20% and a final worth 15%. The rest is hwk which is easy. She sucks at teaching but the class is an easy A. Sat on my phone for most of the class and still got a 100% on the first test. Just keep doing the practice exam questions cause the test pulls from a similar question bank.

The worst professor I have had. Not only does she have an accent, but she mumbles what is given on the slide. She responds quickly to emails but 9/10 does not give any useful answers to your questions. I have no idea how to study or do well in this class as you don't even have access to statistic performance in practice exams. Horrific course.

She is super sweet but she does not speak good English at all. You don't have to go to class or pay attention but you will have to teach yourself everything. The Data Science majors struggled in the class more than the Stats majors. Test averages were VERY low but if you learned the material and did the practice problems you could get 90s.

While sometimes hard to understand, Professor Biyilki cares about her students and their learning. She wants to see her students succeed. Unreal curving. The difficulty of the tests is very dependent on the quality of the preparation, if you study and pay attention you'll do well.

She was so awesome, cared a lot about her student's success, at the end curved everything and gave everyone the benefit of the doubt. I never went to class and or studied - everyone else around me was struggling so much with stats but this teacher's grading system was so overpowered a 58 was still a letter grade of a B. Unreal clutch.

smu kids can't understand any accent that isn't southern. she primarily did read off of slides but did draw some graphs that were helpful. the lab is useful in that it teaches mathematics in excel. she talked about her kittens

however, not a single exam went smoothly in the semester i took.

She is very hard to understand, and I had to teach myself the entire class. During tests I had to ask for sheets that should have been given to every student. She has a hard time ensuring lectures and exams run smoothly.

She only reads off the slides the whole lecture and she only gets through like 5 max. She has a very heavy accent and speaks super quiet so it's hard to understand her. She only took attendance for the first two weeks but then after that attendance wasn't mandatory. You basically have to teach yourself the class.

Prepare for a language barrier due to the professor's Turkish accent. This made understanding the lectures nearly impossible. Forced to utilized the textbook and tutoring to get an A-. You'll spot discrepancies between the homework and the textbook early on. She actually uses a different older version of the textbook from another stats professor.

Very nice lady, not the greatest teacher. Entire class is essentially her reading from a powerpoint--very little actual explanation of the concepts. Hard to understand what she is saying because she talks quiet and has an accent. 

If you can teach yourself from a book, take this class. If you need more hands on help, definitely do not take.
