Great guy. Overall grade is based on a bunch of mini homework assignments, 2 papers, 4 tests, final is cumulative. Get ready to write an hour worth of notes each class, I wish he'd be a little clearer on what goes on the test. It's not an easy A but I've learned a lot that's actually applicable to real life. Worth the slight GPA reduction tbh.

Prof Barnes is generally a good professor. He cares about his job, and is obviously very passionate and knowledgable about Philosophy. My only complaints are his grading practices, he is very picky about wording on quizzes and papers, and will take off several points for it. Has a no devices policy, even phones. Overall, I would recommend him.
Great guy, take his classes.

This professor is easily one of the worst instructors I have ever had. Save yourself the time and energy and do not take this class. Lectures are long, boring, and repetitive, gives no leniency or grace under any circumstances and has absolutely no understanding for any issue you may have outside of class. Ruined my 4.0 and will yours too.

You either parrot back everything he says as he says it with no opinion of your own or he will be rude while doing it to your papers. Class far too difficult for an elective, a ton of reading and note taking. Also, very detail oriented to some things and not others. Not very helpful at all, nor is he available, never responds to emails.

I have taken two classes with Professor Barnes now, and they have been two of my favorites during my time at SMU. He holds his students to a high standard, but he provides them with all of the necessary information, opportunities, and tools to achieve that standard. If you are seeking a true understanding of philosophy, his classes are for you.

Great Professor to take for philosophy and fun class! Lecture heavy, but exams are straightforward as well as the papers. There is a lot of reading but he covers all the important points in the lecture so it's not necessary to read everything. Would highly recommend!

Great professor and cares about his students. Simplifies complicated concepts. As long as you put in the work and pay attention in class you will do fine. He makes time for office hours and accepts emails for drafts on papers. He likes class discussions and accepts questions/comments during class, which is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: The essays are graded decently difficultly and the exams are fairly difficult, if you write down everything he presents on in class you'll do well but otherwise the topics are complex enough to get wrong on your own.
Have to show up to class to get notes because the tests are straight from the notes. Lots of memorization. Send him rough drafts of your essay before you turn them in.

He makes everything very easy to understand and his lectures are super interesting! As long as you copy the notes down well you can get easy As on the quizzes. There are 4 mini essays and one for extra credit, take advantage of his feedback on the rough drafts because they almost always guarantee an A on the essays too

Professor Barnes is an amazing teacher. His class is graded by a few quizzes, a couple short papers, and the final grade. He provides a study guide with quite literally everything that you will see on the test for all the quizzes and the final. As long as you take notes in the class, you will have all of the answers to the tests.

If you take this class, attending every class will be very useful because all the information on the quizzes will be there. He explains everything very simply and easy to understand. He is strict about his policies.

Professor Barnes is well versed in the course material. His quizzes are tough but there are tons of Opportunities to lift up your grade through writing assignments. He also offers help on rough drafts before they are due. I got Ds on every quiz but got a B because of the writing assignments! Attendance heavy!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Barnes is a good teacher who cares about his students, however if you are not a philosophy major or have interest in philosophy I dont recommend this class. He takes notes throughout class and covers interesting topics, however the tests are cumulative, closed note, and are 3 essay questions out of 30 full essay prompts and graded harshly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barnes is one of my favorite professors! Liberty- is very interesting and engaging. It talks about concepts like the first amendment, free speech, and political correctness, which are very relevant. He encourages different viewpoints & discussion & is very caring. There's a lot of reading and the tests are a bit hard, but not bad if you prepare.
everybody loves barnes!! just a cool guy who teaches a class with cool and interesting content. i recommend this class to anyone
Lots of reading, but nothing arduous. Well-structured lectures and explains course material well. Available outside of class for discussions on papers.

Very well-spoken. able to present material in an easily comprehendible way. facilitates and fosters great discussions too and will have you questioning and truly thinking about particular topics you learn in class.

I honestly love Professor Barnes. As long as you put effort in he sees you! While the readings are mandatory, his lectures contained all the information needed for the tests and essays and the readings just bolstered your knowledge and made you feel prepared for class. It wasn't hard to get a good grade as long as you put at least some effort in!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Barnes is a great professor with interesting lectures. Attendance is mandatory and important, as he writes all of his notes in class. There are two papers and a final, and a few homework assignments. He allows you to send drafts of your essays before they are due, so use this and you will do well in his class. Stay on top of readings and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very selective in grading but gives good feedback on papers. Definitely send him your essays before you turn them in because he is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take notes of what he writes in lectures and participate in discussion and you'll do great.

Professor Barnes is an excellent philosophy professor. I took this course only with the purpose of fulfilling a curriculum breadth credit, but I ended up learning so much about philosophy in the process. Barnes does a fantastic job of making the subject matter engaging and the assignments thought-provoking. This is the best class I've taken at SMU.

Barnes makes his class pretty enjoyable, and lectures weren't unbearable. He types everything he says, so be sure to have everything he writes down in your notes and you should be fine. Many written assignments, but he lets you submit multiple drafts to him on email and will give you feedback on them. I highly recommend taking advantage of this
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Barnes is a great person, but I didn't enjoy his class. As a black-and-white thinker, I knew I would struggle with any Philosophy class. He grades insanely harshly for a course that is taken by most for credit and you can't just memorize since the class is entirely essay-based. I only recommend this class if you have a passion for Phil.

I took this class to fulfill a cc requirement, but because of Prof. Barnes, I'm now considering a minor in Philosophy! Although the readings and lectures can be heavy, he re-explains everything in class in an engaging way and is always available for office hours. Super chill, very genuine. Make sure to talk to him, and your grade will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. I would recommend sending in 2 drafts before turning it in. It helps significantly. On top of that, he is very understanding and willing to help his students when needed. Always ask questions when you are confused because it helps.

This class was difficult if you did not take good notes or attend class. Before lessons, you are assigned something to read, which he doesn't check and won't randomly call on you. There are 4 papers and 3 quizzes. The quizzes were in-class papers over 1 of 5 outlines you created outside of class. The final is an extreme version of the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR EVER. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Incredibly light-hearted, experienced and entertaining professor. As long as you take notes in class and participate you should receive a good grade. Lectures are not boring because you can tell how passionate he is and he covers really interesting topics. He wants you to do well and learn, and he will help you if you put in the time.

Barnes is the BEST professor to take to learn about philosophy. He is passionate about his topics, you can clearly tell he has a LOT of experience. He CARES about helping you because he responds to emails quickly, you can email him an essay draft and he is more than happy to correct it. I have never enjoyed a college class more than his!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will definitely need to attend lecture in order to understand material, but worth it if you do, especially if you have an interest in philosophy. Led me to understand much more about ancient Greek philosophy, even in areas I thought I knew much about already.

He's a solid lecturer and makes the material understandable, and if you ask him to slow down or explain something else he's great about making sure everyone understands. There's a lot of reading and lecture, but the writing assignments are pretty easy. He lets you send in drafts for feedback which  guarantee at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnes is very knowledgeable, and his class is very manageable if you attend lectures. Grading is based on small writing assignments, term paper, and a midterm and final. If you attend lectures and keep notes on what he writes on the board in class you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor barnes is great if you have done the reading before class. If not he will expect you to pick up the slack

This is a tough class, but Barnes is a really smart guy and has a passion for what he's teaching which makes the lectures really interesting. Grade is 3 tests and 4 papers which he grades strictly but fairly, and they are all very doable AS LONG AS YOU TAKE NOTES IN CLASS. Make sure you email him drafts of your papers he gives great feedback.

He is a great storyteller and explains concepts well. If you want to succeed in the class, write down every single word he says in lectures. I don't recommend taking this class to fulfill a credit since he is a harsh grader. I had to work harder in this class than I did in my actually difficult classes, and it still ended up being my lowest grade.

Barnes is a fantastic lecturer and fair grader. He allows for drafts to be sent and if you participate, you will do fine in his class. The subject matter for this class is very difficult, but if you come to him for help he is there to support you. Make sure you do the readings, and send him drafts of your papers to suceed.

Professor Barnes is an incredible lecturer with a knack for storytelling that really transforms a classroom. He is kind, a fair grader, accessible outside of class, and even looks over drafts of your papers prior to submission. If you care about your education and actually put in the work, this class is no harder than any other. Truly a fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnes is an excellent lecturer. He allows you to submit drafts before essays are due so definitely take advantage of that. I'd recommend doing at least 2 drafts. For the quizzes, it is generally a good idea to give him exactly what he says in the notes verbatim. If you make a sincere effort to engage with the material you should do just fine.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! He solely bases grades off of what he thinks of you, and you will be punished for not sharing his passion for philosophy. Grades consist of roughly seven essays total in which he grades harshly. He is rude and condescending, and if he doesn't like you he treats you like a nuisance. Take any other class.

Prof. Barnes is great! I took him for CC credit and it was a super interesting but pretty easy class. Grade is 4 papers and 3 quizzes and he gives good feedback if you email him drafts. Attendance is required, but he is pretty understanding is you give him a reasonable excuse.

Definitely read for this class. You will have to read around 50 pages per week. This was a FLEX class, so some students were strictly online and some students attended class in-person. Thus, to prevent cheating, he made the quizzes difficult. He'd assign 5-6 essay questions, and only grades one of them. Only his opinion matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While the class is difficult, Barnes makes it easily passable if you take notes during lectures and do the readings. Papers can be confusing but he allows you to submit drafts as many times as you need and always gives great feedback. He wants to see students succeed and if you put in the work an A- is not difficult to get.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although I received a C in his class and philosophy was the hardest class I have ever taken, I think this is the most brilliant prof I've ever had. Plus, Dr. Barnes wants to see his students succeed. I fell very behind and he was understanding and worked with me. If you want to succeed, write down every word he says in class. MY GRADES SKYROCKETED!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Defintely what I wanted from an Intro to Phil class, plus some! Professor Barnes is friendly, respectful and truly cares about what he teaches and the education of his students. The reading is frequent, but not extensive. Participation in class conversation is important. Overall, not unreasonably hard if you really want to learn and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Extremely boring and grades purely based on his opinion of you. Not a good class if you want to get into philosophy. You will be reading and writing all day. He seems to think his opinion is all that matters. And if your view on a paper doesnt match up with his, then its automatically a bad paper. Take another class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I do like Barnes - he's kind, brilliant, and helpful. He does grade papers fiercely, so be ready to work on them to make them excellent. Don't make super aggressive arguments on them, be balanced. He had an extra credit paper opportunity which saved me, so I made it out okay. Do the readings, show up to class, be respectful, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: So hard. Hardest professor I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Chair of the department for good reason. Brilliant professor. Excellent moderator for class discussion - always ties it back to the relevant topic at hand. Very clear in lectures, open to questions. Informative comments on graded papers, tests. Scary intelligent but approachable, office hours don't seem intimidating. NOT EASY, but would take again!

Nice guy. Pretty helpful and very prompt with communication. Fair grader, he really wants you to understand the philosophical material and be able to argue. Not with high expectations but at a reasonable level. 4 Short papers, 2 long essays. 2 tests which aren't too difficult.

Prof. Barnes was pretty good. The reading wasn't excessive and there was a good bit of class discussion, but the material did get a bit repetitive. Grading on short homework papers was confusing and difficult to decide what he was looking for, but was fair on longer papers and tests.

(Elementary logic) Not bad as a whole, but was annoying how he wasn't willing to note the controversial philosophical nature of some test questions. Lots of busy work. This class is more like a math than a philosophy.

This man is the epitome of an average philosophy professor. I had never taken philosophy before, so I was hoping to be engaged and challenged by interesting ideas. That didn't really happen. He grades pretty fairly, and it's exactly the type of class set-up you would expect when heading into college. Neither good, nor bad.

Professor Barnes is a great teacher who is really interested in what he teaches. Plato is his passion and he makes the class interest. If you do your part, he will make sure you get something out the class. Well recommended.
A wise man. Written a book on philosophy. Took his class on Plato, he enjoys the subject. homework was Q and A based. I love philosophy, and I enjoyed the class discussion. A nice humble guy.
Strong professor.  Serious about class.  This was a hard class for me, but I enjoyed it.  I would def. take him again.

Intro you'd expect to be something to get you excited about the topic. Not the case with this guy, expects way too much, especially in a summer class. Totally unprofessional (came to class in jean cutoffs and t-shirts straight out of the 80s) and class is not organized. Quizes/Tests/Essays are difficult, grading is unfair &subjective. DONT TAKE HIM

Attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is graded (I didn't go to class and got a 90% in that category). The tests are straightforward and all learnable from the slides and readings. He's a new teacher and seems to be learning the best way to teach his classes, and I think there are improvements year over year.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I adored this class! Reading heavy, but that is because classes are lecture and discussion-based (participate! It helps.) This class was not hard in the slightest if you paid attention. Midterm and Final were very doable and Prof listened to feedback. Loved the class and was excited to come in and learn. Plus you get to listen to lots of music!

Great professors. Really cares about class and subject. Readings can be really long but you really just need to skim to do well on the quizzes.Not really sure why some say the tests are hard, really easy even if you pay half attention. Midterm was harder bc review was vague but gave better one for final, even gave short answer prompt beforehand

Dr. Schmidt is a very nice guy, but I did not love this class. He assigned 40 page readings for homework before most class periods with a 3 question quiz that had a 5 minute time limit. Attendance is not mandatory which is nice, but most of the class failed his midterm. Only take if you are truly interested in foreign music, not for CC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt is a decent professor. He's nice, mature, and seems to genuinely care about what he is talking about. However, he does give us very little time to prepare for the exams, and almost never correctly covers what will actually be on the test. This is because the content we learn differs from what is actually on the test.

I am currently taking Dr. Schmidt for MUHI 1237. Music is not of interest to me but every lecture wasn fun and it is even better if you participate. If you show up and listen you will do well on the midterm. He is very passionate and knowledgeable which makes class even better. He is quick to respond and great in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt is awesome! Those who did not do well on the midterm clearly did not study or pay attention in class, it has been one of the easier midterms I've taken. He's super friendly and understanding. This class is a good option for a CC credit.

It is not that the class is hard, it is the fact that the course is not taught well for the exam and everyone does horribly. Do not take it unless you want your GPA to tank. Also, he is a first-year teacher and does not know how canvas works.

Honestly, he is a nice guy, but he is a very bad teacher. He only grades on a few assignments and one of them is the midterm. It is genuinely the hardest midterm and I have taken Econ and Stat. The guidelines are NOT clear at all and the test was nothing like the review. SO RIDICULOUS!! It is unacceptable how this is my hardest class. DONT TAKE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Evers is easily the nicest teacher I have ever had. He grades super nicely. He understands that this class is a ton of lectures, but he grades with a lot of leeway because of that. He also gives students snacks during some classes. Just an upstanding guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. The way the class is, you do not have to go to class since you can read off PowerPoint, but I recommend still going. Very generous for making test corrections. I would recommend him!
Not good at explaining things, thinks he is. He's wrong.

Definitely take this class if you can. Professor Evers is so kind and teaches in an easy-to-understand way. Attendance not mandatory, but I would go just because I loved the class environment. Material is very straightforward and you get multiple attempts on homework assignments if you made a mistake. 10/10

Professor Evers is so kind! The class isn't too difficult as long as you complete all the assignments. Attendance isn't required but he's one of those Professors who makes you want to go to class because he cares so much and wants to help students learn. He brings snacks to class often!

Professor Evers is one of the best professors I've ever taken - his exams are straightforward (2 attempts and open book), he lets you resubmit assignments if you missed points, and he brought us snacks once a week for the whole semester. He is a gem of a man and his lectures are enjoyable - take him if you can !!!!!
Do not recommend. Negative behavior, extremely rude

Disclosed private medical information about a student in another class. Asking questions is looked down upon and they won't be answered, you are expected to know everything. Case studies take hours and are extremely vague, do not reflect what you learn in class. Edits out the rude remarks she makes in class before she posts the recordings.

Disclosed private medical information about a student in another class. Edits out the rude comments she makes in class when she posts the lectures. Case studies are about such random topics that we don't learn about in class. Asking questions is looked down upon.

Dr. O is a great professor and very knowledgeable about the material she teaches. She is a tough grader and looks for very specific answers on the case studies but she does give lots of partial credit which helps your grade. It's a tough class but very manageable to get an A if you put in the time and effort.

This rating is for the LAB and the lab only (lecture was incredibly difficult). This was one of the easiest labs I've taken at SMU. Very little time spent working on it outside of class, and the first lab practical was very easy... second was slightly more difficult. Not sure if it's worth it bc the lecture is so hard, but the lab was nice...

She changed the class completely and now your grade is based on one case study each week. The case studies are insanely hard, she is looking for a very specific answer and even if you are right if you don't put exactly what she wants you lose points. Impossible to know what she is looking for. Unfortunately the only anatomy prof at SMU

She started making it all take home tests- which is awesome but they are very difficult and she is looking for a specific answer. it takes a lot of time to find the answers. Definitely not a blow off class

60% of this class is 4 tests where you will be asked to edit and write code on a piece of paper without a compiler. Although open book those tests can be very hard. The 4th test is basically inclass activities over 12 weeks which you do not want to miss. I did bad on 2 tests and couldn't make it up to pass the class.
Best CS professor ever!

Professor Etchison is a very solid teacher. I came into CS1340/DS1301 with no experience coding in Python, yet I didnt find the class very difficult. Her assignments are very helpful for learning the content and usually not too hard. If you ever have trouble, she will respond to your emails almost instantly. I learned a lot, glad I took her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A classic 'I've never written a ratemyprof review'. But Judy made me. For a class called 'intro to computing concepts' it is hardly that. If you do not thoroughly learn python code you will not pass the class. impossible coding projects. labs take forever. For someone who needs a single CS credit for a major to graduate.. avoid Judy at all costs.

Prof Etchison's class has so far been the hardest class I've ever taken. I have received a 100% on every assignment, every lab and every quiz, but I don't know if I will pass. Her tests are incredibly difficult and her grading is very unforgiving. Lots of people drop because of this class. Take a different professor. She doesn't do online well.

Professor Etchison gives a good intro to C++. Although the participation assignments in the online textbook were annoying, they were very easy. The lectures were repeats of what was in the textbook but I guess that helps people new to coding. She is very good at responding to questions about the programs so don't be afraid to ask for help!

She will respond to your emails so fast and is always willing to help you program! She is so caring and although sometimes lectures can be boring since this is an intro class its because she really takes her time to help everyone at every level. There is no reason to fail this class if you utilize her resources.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class becoming online hurts the quality of this class. You are forced to buy and use the online textbook and she is the type of professor that cares about tests. Her tests are worth 60% of your grade so if you're into that she's the professor for you. If you're a bad test taker be prepared to study big time for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Etchison! She's very helpful and available outside of class, and she explains things in an easy way to understand. Some people think her tone of voice makes her sound condescending, but I truly think that's just how she talks. Some of the concepts are hard, so just be ready to dedicate yourself.

Lectures are super useful and she explains everything in amazing detail and helps you understand it all. If you don't pay attention and don't take notes you won't do well. Always (even right before midnight deadlines) accessible by email, and always willing to help you. Test content is always made very clear, and explained in detail in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Etchison was by far the W O R S T professor I've ever had in the engineering school. Unless you did super well in Java and have an extensive background in computer science, she goes way too quickly to understand anything. She's also just flat out condescending and rude if she thinks you're not catching on to things. Def DON'T recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Etchison is the perfect person to teach C++. Everything is explained in detail, and she's always available by email (even for the midnight deadlines). The quizzes aren't hard if you took notes and paid attention in class.

Professor Etchison is the best computer science professor I could have hoped for coming into my first semester. Not only did she make learning C++ easy and enjoyable, she is always accessible to students through office hours and email, even on short notice. She has inspired me to continue learning computer science even though it isn't my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took her for CSE 1341. I really enjoyed the class. Assignments were spelled out easily. In my opinion you have to try to fail this class. If you do all the assignments and turn them in on time you won't have any issues. Professor Etchison is amazing with replying to emails instantly.  Anything above a 90 is a solid A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took C++ this past semester and had a great experience.  Pay attention in class, do your assignments on time and you will do well in the course and be well prepared for future courses.  The material is interesting with labs and programs that ensure you have full understanding. She encourages questions in class so make sure to raise your hand.

She is a great professor who clearly presents the material in class and is always encouraging questions.  While attendance isn't mandatory she makes it clear that your attendance is typically directly correlated to your grade because her lectures cover more test material than the readings (I went to nearly every class).  Start you programs early.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Both in class and during office hours, Professor Etchison is helpful, enthusiastic, and patient. Tests are open book and correlate directly to reviews, weekly homeworks, and programs. Lab quizzes provide more than enough time and come with lab aid to help ya out. Programs are time consuming but doable. Overall, a caring and competent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Etchison is always willing to help you and clarify any questions you may have, especially when debugging code. The open book policy is nice, but you should only use it to double check your answers; don't get too caught up looking up answers in the textbook.

Her test policy is open book because "in the real world, if you don't know something, you can look it up". Having said that, doing well in the class still boils down to how well you understand the general principles of CS (since the syntax you can look up). Do the homework even though it's worth like 1% each, it helps. And speak up if you're lost

Very clear lectures and always wiling to help. The class wasn't hard for me all all but may prove challenging to some people. Test were very easy plus she lets you your book during it which can be a life saver. Responds to emails quickly and will at times give out extra credit for her exams.

I took her C++ class, I found that she presented the material rather well. In addition,  she goes out of her way to ensure that you understand all concepts at a high level. Tests are about average difficulty, know what you're doing and you'll do fine. Fantastic professor and wonderful person, I highly recommend her.

A decent teacher. Very friendly & fairly helpful. She answers her emails very promptly. Tests are not too hard if you study & HW is always easy. Still, she does not present the material extremely well, and she uses weird, abstract examples. Sometimes it gets confusing. She's a LOT better than some of the CSE teachers! I'd recommend her.

I took this class Spring of 2008. She is a nice lady but the class sucks. The labs arent hard but the class sucks. Tests are VERY hard. I had to take this for my major, I would NOT RECOMMEND this class for anyone unless they have a good amount of programming knowledge beforehand. She is nice, but its a hard class. Dont get fooled like many of us di

Prof. Etchison does not present the material well. I took a java course in high school and aced it, but when I attended her class it just confused me. Many non computer savy people tend to struggle in this class. She may not be good at presenting the material, but she is always offering review sessions and is always available for questions.

Super nice teacher and woman. The class itself is boring, but very basic and slow-paced. If you already know java, try to not take this class. You could teach yourself on the internet what she's covering in this class.

She's definitely a nice teacher. Although her class is boring sometimes, her class is slow-paced. But the lab hwk is sort of hard, and you have to be really careful to prepare for your exam. You can get many bonus after every exam. I like her- A helpful teacher.

she is a completely unfair teacher. take kahn! they gave the same test and when they found out about mistakes and stuff, judy didnt do anything while kahn gave his class at least 20 extra points! ridiculous. she seems nice but her lectures are so pointless, yet you HAVE to go because she gives pop quizzes. tests are impossible.

I hoped to learn some advanced stuff from this class but she taught all that I already knew. Her teaching style is really boring. She just pulls out code from the textbook and goes over it so slow as if she were teaching JAVA for dummies. There's nothing to learn from the class that you can't learn from the JAVA Tutorials.
She is an OKAY teacher. Her class is easy and you don't really need to go to the lecture. The material she covers in the course is simple.
No Comments

Only about 50% of her lectures are helpful and relevant to the programs you have to write.  I was especially put out with the lecture designed to introduce object-oriented programming by relating it to using an elevator.
No Comments

DISC revolves around having a good professor rather than actually being a good writer. It was actually impossible to get an A in the class. Whether you spend 10 hours on a paper or 1 hour, your grade will be the exact same. Avoid her at all cost if you want a free A/A- instead of putting in a lot of work to get mediocre grades.

reviews.comment: she's nice, but a really hard grader and her feedback isn't really helpful. to be honest i have no clue what you have to do to get an A on a paper, even after meeting with her
Grades way too hard for a class that should be an easy A. Other Disc teachers give A's to average papers and she doesn't give them at all.
Very nice and helpful. Clear grading and expectations. Long lectures but worth it.
Fun class, but don't sign up if you get grossed out by touching bugs, worms, fish, etc. Dr. O is really great, and she definitely enjoys the subject.
A-MAZING! Interesting lectures. You'll actually enjoy going to class! Take good notes and you'll make an easy A.

Very nice and funny, interesting lectures. BE SURE YOU TAKE NOTES AND STUDY THEM because a lot of stuff she puts on the teast is not in the textbook, and she actually makes correction to what's in the book.

His lectures are so dry, it's incredibly difficult to stay focused. All he does is read from the online textbook or read from a powerpoint that is made solely from textbook pages. We never coded together in class. Tests are open book which is cool, but it isn't cool that I could've not come to class and done just as well.

I took java and received a 4.0 . In C++, I found Professor Evans rambling in his monotone voice reading examples from books and expecting full mastery. It is like a math teacher reading a solved multiplication problem and expecting you to solve them from scratch on the test. Assignments are poorly written. Never want to do C++ again in my life.
very hard in operating system.. a lot of homework and code..

reviews.comment: Professor Evans knows what he's doing and has a passion for Assembly. That being said, he's not the best teacher. Be prepared to ask questions and read on your own time. The LAB is the only reason I passed the class. It's' boring, but go to class, take notes, ask questions and you'll survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Well, this class is not friendly to people who is changing their major to Computer Science. The homework is too hard. If you get a wrong result, the grade would be lower than 50. It's just like, the class is teaching you what the pencil is. And the homework required you use pencil paint better than Da Vinci!!!!!!!Test is also very hard. No reviews
He's a truly beautiful man, inside and out. I'd let him toggle my bits any day of the week ;)

He can be a bit monotone at times but I still really enjoyed having his as a teacher. He's available outside of class and very willing to help. Tests are difficult but he lets you use your book as long as you have a paper copy.

Dr. Evans is really nice and really cares about Assembly language. He's really good at it and is willing to help you if you ask questions and go to Office hours. Lectures can be boring but the tests are usually mainly stuff covered specifically in class.

Lectures may be boring, but they are key to passing. He cares about his students and is super helpful both during and outside of class. Tests are open book, but really difficult. Lots of work involved between reading the textbook, bi-weekly programs, weekly labs, and quizzes. Even with all the work, be ready to do extra to understand the material.

Professor Evans really knows his stuff and he's willing to put in a lot of time and effort to help students understand, especially outside of office hours. His lectures are pretty boring, though, and his tests are open book but difficult.
Not helpful at all outside of class expects you to know a lot of material coming into the class and doesn't help you if you start behind.

this dude is booooooring. he cares about the material and you can tell he's really good at what he does but he drones on and on in his southern drawl that puts half the class to sleep. i didn't do well on 2 of the tests but did well on the programs and ended up fine in the class, those are the key

Its very easy to fall behind, so make sure you are grasping the material from the beginning. Evans is really helpful in office hours for projects and test prep if you go in with questions. Tests are difficult but doable if you redo class examples and homework multiple times. Do not expect to be able to use the book much during the test, no time.

Evans is great because he's so helpful, especially if you ask questions. He genuinely wants to help his students and cares about them. Yes, he is kind of monotone but as long as you keep up with the textbook and go to lab, you should be able to get an A.

Prof. Evans really knows his stuff, but can put you to sleep in a matter of seconds. Do go to class, though, he gives a lot of helpful info about programming assignments and things that are covered on the test. Tests are open book, yet he throws in a lot of the details he mentions in class.

Evans is a decent professor, but he is monotone and it is easy to drift off in class. His quizzes and tests have questions that are worded poorly and can easily trip you up. Sometimes it's better to learn from the textbook than from him. The tests are tough with an avg of 70%, and the quizzes are weekly and tricky. The programs aren't too bad.

Professor Evans is a really sweet man, and he is not trying to make you fail. However, he has a tendency of being monotone and it is hard hard hard to stay awake in his class because of that. Besides the first exam, his tests and quizzes  are really tough. Class is fast paced. If you already know Java fairly well, you'll be fine. If not, good luck.

I did not enjoy taking Java with Professor Evans. His lectures are very boring and and sometimes tries to trick you on the biweekly quizzes. The first exam, however, was rather clear cut, and most of the grade is from the exams, not the quizzes, but still, I do not feel as if I have learned much in this class because he almost puts me to sleep.
He is a great teacher.  His tests are pretty difficult, but open book.  I had a great time in his class.

I took his OS class in summer (DO NOT RECOMMEND) long lectures, several assignments and Project + Research paper. But he is helpful and willing to work with you if you show hard work. Grades fairly and he makes sure students understand the concept. Definitely recommend him but not during summer.

While Don Evans may not be the best professor, the class itself is not too bad. Tests are decently tough and averages around a 70% because people don't know how to study. As long as you build a good habit of reading the book and doing the programs wo help, you will get an A in this class and be decently prepared for Assembly and Data Structures.
His lectures are monotone and dry, but overall, he'll get the info inside you.  FIND THE TEXTBOOK ONLINE

Don't understand why he is getting so much hate. Funny guy who knows material well and presents it clearly. As is college, you do need to do some work/studying outside class, but nothing unreasonable even to achieve an A. Only complaint: he is pretty monotone and does seem boring initially, but if you just pay attention you will like him/do well.

Good Teacher. His tests are open book and they are not very difficult. He is not against giving back points on the tests and quizzes if you go and talk to him. As long as you finish the labs, you'll do fine.

I was nervous to take Professor Evans after reading the comments on him, but his class really isn't that bad! He's a really nice guy & is helpful when you ask questions. The material is decent (not too challenging, I'd say). But you do need to do the homework and practice exams to be prepared for the real tests.

He knows his material and explains it clearly, but tends to assume that you've learned to think like a programmer; and Java does NOT teach you to think like a programmer. If you like Java, you will HATE Assembly: be wary of this class if all you've studied is OO languages. You will need Windows to do the assignments in the text, which is annoying.

He expects you to already know C++ when you go into the class.  He doesn't help you if you don't know it.  He isn't available for office hours and wouldn't answer emails.  I do not recommend taking his class.

I've been coding c++ for nearly 10 years and I still didn't understand a thing he was talking about. Many questions on the tests were irrelevant vocab questions that were maybe mentioned once in class, but since I stopped going half way through I guess I wouldn't know. Avoid if possible.

Don't take him if you can avoid it. His classes are super boring and totally unhelpful when it comes to doing the labs (and I'm a CSE major).  Always felt like I understood the material well and could do the labs easily but did pretty bad when it came to the tests. Seriously would not recommend if you can avoid him.
He rocks

Overall good professor, but kept changing his requirements for the class.  I took him for OO and for fundamentals class.  In the fundamentals class he spent a half hour on one topic and had 2 difficult questions on the exam.
He is a good teacher but makes it very hard to stay awake in class. He knows his stuff very well, but it doesn't show. Despite all this, he is very good about giving good grades.
No Comments
Great lectures.
The best teacher possible
Trying to do y'all a favor, just skip the class and trust the other reviews.
Terrible professor. Hard to understand during class, he is all over the place and does not teach well. Communication with students is nonexistent. Would avoid taking at any cost.

Fun on class, funny enough on grading. Every class Faradonbeh was only reading the slides from Pearson, and almost no similarity between the lectures and tests. Everyone got super low grade on linear algebra since no one really understood the concepts. Highly recommend using YouTube tutorials, this will save you.
No office hours. Bad at teaching. Watched Youtube videos to survive. Super generous with the grading.

Funny guy, but he cannot teach. Syllabus was unprepared/disorganized, poor communication regarding exam dates/schedule, no review for exams, covered less than 5/10 of required chapters, not receptive to feedback. I only did well bc I taught myself. He made sure people passed his class, but the credit doesn't matter when we don't know the content.

Lots of reading, a book every week. Lectures are pretty useless in my opinion. Prof Greenspan will talk all class about the book and what he interprets from it, but nothing he talks about helps you on quizzes or essays. I'm not a great writer but the way essays are graded is demoralizing, it's very hard to succeed. Expect low grades on all essays.

reviews.comment: I’ve always been told I’m a good writer & have thought so myself, until this class. This professor will make you feel downright stupid if you don’t write in a style he likes. Be prepared to read an entire book over weekends and write about extremely specific prompts. Would give this man 0/5. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you join his class is prepared for condescending feedback if you aren't on par with his expectations, unclear instructions during quizzes and essays, extremely hard grader, reading 2 books minimum per week (sometimes 3 books and 3 papers), and being expected to write 6-page essays after each one in (1 week to do 4-6 page essays).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class for a graduation requirement, dont take it if youre not an english major. He gives feedback but a lot of it is difficult to understand. He tends to talk a lot in class which makes it hard to know whats important for the quizzes. Lectures are kind of disorganized. He also expects you to read A LOT before class, novels and textbook

Dr. Greenspan is a caring, intellectual man. However, this does not necessarily make him a good professor. There is tons of reading for this class, so be prepared to read a short novel before class begins. Extremely lecture heavy and often will speak the entire class with only one or two chances to ask questions/comment. Only a few grades though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is the reason I came to SMU. His lectures are profound. Outside of class, he helped dissect my writing, identify all its weaknesses, and then make it stronger with changes.

Dr. Greenspan is intellectual but cares deeply about students. He respects and praises students' ideas. He will often be delighted by a comment and go off on a related tangent. He gives everything serious thought including his own teaching methods. It can be intimidating, but he thoughtfully considers everything you say and write for his class.

This class was the worst. He doesn't listen to his students and grades very harshly. I thought I was the only one but once I talked to other people in the class I realized that no one was enjoying this class at all. Maybe it was online teaching but I would avoid this class until it's in person again.
so condescending and makes you feel like you can't write anything. feedback is very rude with little to no constructive (and positive) criticism. avoid!!

Although I can respect the amount of knowledge this professor has, I cannot respect the way he speaks to his students. I had an extreme passion for English before I took this class. I know I am not the best writer, but I love English and I understand the content given to me. He made me feel like I did not have a place in the English major at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Greenspan is my fist college English Professor. I love English and want to be an English major and Dr. Greenspan reaffirmed my desire to major in English. Wonderful Professor

His American literary history class was amazing. I didn't know anything about American history, but I took the class because I was being adventurous. He was understanding and exceedingly helpful!!! Need
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: avoid taking this class if not absolutely necessary. He is a very smart guy, but his lectures are unorganized and confusing. He goes off topic all the time and assigns a ridiculous amount of reading. I've always been a A+ writer and good test taker and I've gotten C's on everything he's graded in this course. DO NOT take

He is a typical english teacher. I am a great student, with a business major and around a 3.7 GPA. I took this class to fulfill SMU requirements and it was a mistake. I read the books and went to class and was still unable to get the grade I wanted. Granted I am not the best writer but I know I am not a C+ level. DO NOT TAKE!

He is the best professor I ever had. His subject is extremely interesting and he doesn't mind veering from his lecture to answer a student's questions. Plus, he makes you feel like your thoughts matter which spurs great conversations in and out of class. Essays easy, Final exam was tough but not too hard if you did the readings thruout the semester
If you make an effort at the beginning of the semester to come to class and participate, he'll like you and be way more lenient the rest of the semester.

He is a very intelligent person. With that aspect, he expects a lot out of his students. He is a very hard grader on essays and assigns large amounts of complicated reading. During class discussion he easily goes off topic. If you are not an English Major do take the class!!
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. I loved every day in his class even though I did not do as well in his class as I thought I deserved. He is still an amazing professor!

He's a brilliant professor. Very old school in his methods. Show up when you want, write 3 essays throughout the year, take notes on whatever he says during the class. Simple. He's a great guy in general, very interested in the students and the learning experience. I highly recommend learning from him
He’s great if you like condescending professors.  Avoid.

Dr. Greenspan is a brilliant teacher, but the course material isn't the greatest at first. He was always very helpful and eager to discuss after class. He's also very fair when it comes to grades. Highly recommend this class.

Prof. Fanning is a caring and amazing teacher. He sets you up to succeed and gives amazing feedback during conference week. He gives the books needed for the course online so you don't have to pay for them. Highly recommend because you will be able to take a lot from his class and apply it to next semesters writing course.

Gives good feedback on all of the papers. Very accessible outside of class through email. Any reason to miss class will be excused if you email ahead of time. Laid back atmosphere in class. Would take again.

Kind, laid back, high expectations but not strict. I learned a ton and my writing improved tremendously but did not have to struggle to get there. He understands students' lives and works with individuals' situations (eg. student-athletes). He creates a positive and collaborative environment where everyone is treated respectfully and equally.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fanning is an easy-going guy and is a very understanding professor. He is helpful with one's papers and truly listens to input from the class to determine how to lead the class.
Best Prof I've had at SMU so far. Super funny and class goes by fast. Very helpful with his students and their papers. Overall great guy and great class. Would take again 10/10 times.
Very chill prof and will work with you. Wants everyone to succeed. 10/10 would take his class again.
Fanning is a stand-up guy, a real good man. Mr. Fanning will do great things in the future and I know he is a generational talent. This is a guy you want on your sideline.
Prof. Fanning is super chill and a great guy. Ever need to miss class, email him, and he'll excuse you. Works with you and wants you to succeed. Overall, 10/10, 100% would take again.
He's an awesome professor who is down to earth and loves to joke. He's a straight shooter and very good with students. He's been my favorite professor so far.
SHE CANT LECTURE 50 MIN EVEN W PAPER IN FRONT OF HER AND NO TECH ALLOWED BUT CANDY RUDE B FTS

No tech rules are R in this day and age. Her 3 questions is R ahl and she grades down w no reason given
Not sure why Prof. Faglie gets a bad rep, she is very kind and helpful. Read and take notes from the textbook before class. Be sure to show up to class and participate every now and again.
She will give you a horrible grade on the writings and give you little to no feedback. She's extremely rude to students and becomes defensive when you ask questions.

Easy A but not a good experience. Class felt tense and condescending, with constant scolding about phones or note-taking. Lectures were just reading from the textbook. Feedback was vague on essay questions and written assignments: "write more". Worth it for the credit, but not a class I'd recommend.
Worst professor ever. Her grading makes no sense and she will yell at you in front of the entire class if she feels you are going against her bias and her thinking.

She is a super sweet woman with a really positive attitude. She presents the material well and moves at a steady pace, so we normally get let out early, which is nice. I really like her as a person, and the class isn't too hard.

Nice lady, but she doesn't seem to entirely know what shes talking about. She can barely lecture for 50 minutes WITH a paper that has all the information on it in front of her. If you like to talk, cant stay off your phone, and laugh too loud or too much, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS because she WILL let you know that she doesn't like any of those things

Easy class but she teaches it like we're in elementary school. She throws constant temper-tantrums when there aren't class-wide convos because she expects people to participate when most people just want to get the work done as it's not a class we're taking because we actually are interested in the subject. Very far-left and loves to show her bias.

She makes the class really easy but she's sort of infantilizing and doesn't seem to know what she's teaching. Attendance is mandatory but feels useless to go becuase she literally gives you the test questions before the test so rewriting the notes is pointless when you only have to memorize the questions. Doesn't know how to teach but candy.

reviews.comment: An easy class if you do your due diligence and listen during the lectures.
I'm dropping this class because of her no technology policy and because she lectures off a piece of paper. Feels like I transported back to middle school.

She is very sweet and very easy as far as class material and assignments go. Kind of a hard grader but not too bad. The class itself was almost too easy though and I feel as if I didn't really get anything out of it. She kinda treated us like we were still in grade school.

reviews.comment: course material was dated and unhelpful like we had to learn about a theory about men and women before women could vote and it was sickening and unhelpful. she shoud use disclaimers in and not just talk about the info.  The class was boring and on nothing that matters. she moved questions offline midsemester, beware

class could be condensed to 10 days total you do nothing all week after when she literally reads definitions to you on monday which we can look up on our own, nobody pays attention and then she gets grouchy and snaps at us for not paying attention, a lot of the questions we got on quizes and games were sort of dependant on the person or subjective

1 day lecture, 2days questions and jeopardy. She talks ab her kids too much and treats us likewise bringing candy and yelling at us for not paying attention. Tests are randomized from a bank you pray favors you knowing others are cheating, mine were way harder than my friends but still easy

literally like middle school and she is angry all the time with the way she constantly talked about people being on their phones and talking, lectures were her reading terms to us from the powerpoints, randomly would talk about inappropriate topics like gender stereotypes as if they were true and you had to repeat them, also very boring

This class was managed like a kindergarten class. nice lady and all, took her for the cred, but she is so infantilizing it is gross, needs to get a job at a middle school rather than trying to work with college age adults who expect effort, easy A, no reading needed, but not worth it, get chegg

She's actually a lovely person and has a very organized class, she also does weekly Jeopardy games over the chapters which is good practice. Took her to fulfill a breadth but would take her again. Her class is very straightforward and organized.

Do not take her, she is an extremely difficult person, the only assignments you have cant be dropped, and the whole course is textbook materials, no point coming to class, exams full of random factoids she never talks ab then she schedules them at break but no makeups even with docs, she blamed the students for "clearly not studying enough."
the class is wack, chegg is your friend
Pathetic. Take her if you want to waste your time learning nothing.
Horrible teacher, she is not clear at all. The syllabus is totally differnet from what she requires us to do. Every class she changes her mind about whether its a take home or in class test.
I don't recommend anyone to take her. Take her and you will regret it.
Terrible teacher. Absolutely terrible. She makes simple things confusing. Take this class if you are looking to learn nothing and recieve a less than satisfactory grade.

Professor Nibbs does not grade any assignments, your TA is entirely in charge of your grade. There were 3 essays and a final paper as well as super easy flashcard quizzes in the discussion labs. Overall pretty easy but I had 70% of my grade outstanding going into the Final. Got an A- with minimal work. It counted for my human diversit requirement.
Great Teacher. Makes simple demands everybody can follow. Makes class intersting with films. J- Term easy A. I highly recomend her.

This professor is awesome. I rated 4 on easiness because you do have to put a little time into the homework. Just get on your TAs good side and you will receive an easy A. Also go to class cause she gives you everything you need for the HW and follow directions. No tests just weekly short essay and a final paper that is on a movie. SO EASY!

TAKE THIS CLASS IN J-TERM. Prof. Nibbs is wonderful. Stay current with the homework during the J-term and you will ace the final which is over a movie in which you use the ideas of cultural anth to analyze the movie. Easy easy.
really intelligent prof and really thorough, but nice. not bad to look at either.
Good in general. Very good at explaining things, but can be real demanding
Not helpful outside of the class. Talks to low and didn't seem to know what he was talking about
Awesome
Good.
Good professor. Tells it how it is.
Learned a lot in this class. Really seems to care about students. Was flexible with deadlines when class didn't understand something.

A poorly designed class, lectures/questions are vague and confusing to understand. She is a professor who emphasizes the importance of good communication, but does not follow her own guidance. She snaps at you if you ask questions she doesn't think should be asked which created a negative learning environment.

I loved Jax! Definitely a strict professor but if you make it clear that you are trying, then she will do everything for you! Super patient and made me realize how much more I can get involved as a student at SMU. If you come to her with your problems when they first happen, she will help you!! An A is a 95 which can be tricky.

If you let her, Jax will be the best professor you've ever had. She cares about your well-being and wants you to succeed. You will do well in this class if you put in the effort. She made me realize that I was much more capable of success than I ever thought possible, and I am very excited to be enrolled in another course with her next semester.

Professor Jax is very understanding and patient with her students. She presents the content perfectly for beginners. Needs a calmer attitude about cell phones and laptops but I loved learning with camera cause we got to do stuff outside of class that was fun. She was nice about absences.

Professor Fellows is one of the best teachers I have had at this school. She is very caring and wants you to succeed. Assignments are self-explanatory and do not take too long. This course is lecture heavy, though. If she can tell you are genuinely trying, you will get a good grade.
Very available to students, you learn a lot about podcasting and videos. Show up and stay off your phone. Students love her, the ones who don't probably failed.

She is so awesome but a tough grader. You need to pay attention and show up for class, which was brutal on a Friday with a lab that was 3 hours long. But you do learn a lot of valuable skills and it can be fun if you make it fun.

Jax is an amazing professor who wants her students to succeed. The class is focused on video and audio production, and she makes sure that everyone understands the content (even if it takes a little longer). She is so caring and I went to her office many times just to chat or for a hug. If you have the chance to take her, definitely do.

Jax wants every student in her class not only to pass and get the content finished but to learn the integrity and ropes of Journalism through various means. In 2304, which is focused on projects and video editing, she was super helpful and encouraging to get stuff done. Talk to her, make a relationship, and be honest. Will take again! Thank you

reviews.comment: She's great, class is very straightforward if you stay on top of your work. Can be a bit boring, but nothing to get caught up about

Encouraging teacher. She helped me through a tough semester. She wants you to succeed and really cares about her students. The work can be hard, but she lets you choose your own topics to write about.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this professor; she is super sweet and really does care about how you do in the class, but the tests are really hard and a lot of information all at once, so a lot of memorization and study ahead. She does give extra credit if you don't do well on exams. However, her lectures are very good. I did struggle in this class though
