reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I have ever taken at SMU. She is smug, uncaring and grades hard. Thinks too highly of herself. Makes things harder than they are just because she can. Avoid at all cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher with a lot of knowledge in this area!  Super nice and super clear instructions.  Memorize, memorize, memorize and you will do great on the tests.  Make sure you study hard for all of them because if you don't your grade will tank!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved her and this class. However, the tests are a lot of information thrown at once. Also, the reading checks are very surface-level details that I never remembered. Interesting class overall and she is super nice.

La Ferle offers good information in her lectures, which is great if you truly are interested in advertising, but she grades harshly. TIP: For the written answer portion of the tests, write very detailed responses or she won't count it, even if your short answer response is correct. Had I known that sooner, I would've passed with a higher grade.

This class is hard. La Ferle is no cake walk. She provides study guides but you must memorize everything on that study guide word for word. She assigns a lot of reading under the guise that it provides 'context' for what is being taught when in reality her powerpoints are just watered down versions of the readings. Extremely difficult grader.
Worst class I've ever taken at SMU. She makes this required intro class way harder than necessary.

Love La Ferle! She gives 2 extra points on your overall grade if you attend every class and she gives extra credit opportunities. Only 3 tests, half multiple choice/ half short answer. They can be very tricky and you must know every slide and read the text book! Interesting class, great prof!

Dr. Feezell is very good at teaching and is available outside of class in the morning. He also offers extra credit points if you take an exam for musicianship before 8am. He makes sure that you understand material and that he answers any questions you have. He provides reviews for the final as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've had Dr. Feezell for 2 semesters and all I can say is that he is the most laid back music professor ever. He genuinely cares about you learning something and will give you so many reminders about assignments. Super organized and not an overwhelming amount of work the 2nd semester. Gives tutors for the1st semester. Sweet and understanding guy.

Dr. Feezell is the professor you want. He is the best teacher for theory and musicianship by far. He teaches well, is super caring, and is kind with grading. The only thing that matters is attendance, as ALL of the test material is reviewed in class.

As a music minor with little basics, I survived two semesters of musicianship and theory fine. You really need to spend time practicing, but it's worthy. Talk to Dr. Feezell if you have any trouble or worry and he'll help you. He made a very good web site so you can learn theory for free, and everything is explained very clear.

Dr. Feezell is amazing. He is the most caring person, and is always willing to help his students out. Not only does he care about your grade, but he cares about each and every one of his students well being. Definitely one of my favorite professors
Hes cool

Dr. Feezell is the best professor I have had in college so far. I have taken Music Theory and Musicianship with him for 4 semesters, and I have loved every second of it. Dr. Feezell has been more than just a professor but has been a mentor. In all of the chaos of being a freshman dual major in College, he has always been accessible for advice.

Dr. Feezell is a very mediocre professor. The majority of his class time is wasted with him talking about random, non-music things. He is one of those teachers who desperately wants to be friends with his students. He is a little self-centered. Easy A if you show up and pay attention.

The whole Music Theory I class is centered around the placement tests; once you pass them, you're out. Also, the class is Pass/Fail. I wasn't in the class long, but Prof Feezell was funny and encouraging, and I hope that I can take him again for Music Theory 2.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: this could be really difficult material if you don't like music or analyiss, but as a music major, i must say that dr. feezell makes these concepts pretty easy to understand and his style is very clear and straightforward. he's very responsive to questions and often makes humorous comments about composers and the music we study. highly recommended.

Great professor!  Very helpful and sweet.  He assigns a lot of homework, but is very lenient on due dates. If you don't understand the material on the homework, he'll give you an extra day to turn it in.
Fantastic teacher
I love Dr. Feezell! The class isn't easy-- but he will help you and if you do the homework and study a little bit, you will ace the class easily.
Awesome professor! He is the most helpful prof I have had yet. Go see him during office hours. He likes to see that you try even if you dont get it! take with him if you can!
First year Music Theory (MUTH 1229) and Aural Skills (1129) are demanding classes. You have to work hard to earn the grade you want.

Extra credit saved my grade in here, but I wish I would've taken a different class for science credit. Tests were so hard and everyone would fail them. Ended up not going to class after spring break because lectures felt pointless and attendance wasn't mandatory. This class just felt very eh.
This class was ok. I wouldn't take it again and you should try to find another way to get you science credit. His exams are very hard and not based on the material that he says will be on it.
Absolutely impossible, tests are horrible, hard to understand.
He is a really good professor, very chill. But the test and the lab, especially lab, is extremely hard.

Such an odd course. Tests were awful with big curves. Feng is smart but a poor lecturer, often mispronouncing words and unaware it's an elective. Reviews skipped key topics, and labs were irrelevant and tough. Cold-calling students added stress. Took this for a science credit at SMU, but it was the worst choice. Avoid if possible.

I am very conflicted about him. Most of my classmates and I averaged a 60 on his exams, but by the end of the course, we all managed to raise our grades to around a B+. His final exam replaces the lowest grade and consists of only four sketches. Because of this, I ended up with an A in the class. So... idk lol.

Class is not easy at all.
Good professor, but his slides are not very good.
Need to study on your own and don't miss classes.
Lot of extra credit though.

super chill class and professor feng is funny and awesome! soooo much extra credit it makes it really easy to get a good grade w/o all that much effort, and 1/4 exams get dropped. i thought i was going to end with a b but extra credit brought me to an a at the end of the semester. my only complaint is labs were kind of tedious and annoying.

Barnaby is the man. Even if you have no painting experience (like me) you shouldn't hesitate. Just paint and trust yourself to keep going. Barnaby will always be there to guide you and pick you up. He'll even dabble in painting a little on your easel if you're lucky! He is a beacon of truth in a world of posers. A lovely man whom I miss already.

I don't understand why y'all rate him so low, he is the best professor I have met in SMU. No he did not pay me or tell me to write good rating about him, I just wanna say that he is a good wonderful awesome and amazing professor!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
You can really learn a lot from him

I cannot thank him enough for his instruction in my work and study. He is very dedicated to his teaching and his students. Always give good feedback, and you might not get him at first (an abstract thinker), but that's the whole point of learning. He has a personality and is funny. Absolutely recommend him if you are serious about the major.

Very tough, but also a very rewarding class. Barnaby is very blunt, if your work isn't good you're gonna know, but he encourages you along the way. He's very well-read and listening to him talk is incredibly entertaining. I recommend him for anyone who's willing to put the work in and grow as an artist, don't take him as a throw away.

Barnaby is one of the reasons that I came to SMU. He is talented, well versed, funny, and a joy to have studied under. He is passionate about both art, teaching, and his students. I am not sure what the complaints below are about. Don't take an art class thinking it will not be challenging. I cannot recommend him enough.
Choose another class and avoid him!!

He doesn't sugarcoat it. If your work sucks you'll know. He encourages you but expects you to grow mentally. Don't take this class if you just need a throw away class.  Very Bohemian. Expect wild artistic rants.

Professor Fitzgerald and I did not get along. If you are not an art major then I suggest a different class. The assignments had to be worked on for 10 hrs every week. In general his comments are super vague and I did not find them to be helpful. I encourage if you have another choice to avoid him!

Great professor! Nice and helpful in office hours; calm demeanor; fair grader; flexible with office hours and will walk through every problem with you if that's what it takes for you to succeed; definitely recommend!!

Ana Firan is a good professor. Her lectures are clear and the problems she works in class are really helpful. The tests are true to what she teaches and is not too difficult. However, the final was definitely a struggle. She is a generous grader and gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. Definitely take her!

Firan is a professor who really knows what she is talking about. However, communications skills are not her specialty. She has a heavy accent and a soft voice. If you wish to learn, sit near the front. If you wish to surf the web or what not, sit wherever else, because she allows mobile devices in class. Homework is weekly, and due electronically.
she is really nice professor. if you go to her office she will explain everything to you. take her definitely.
Professor Firan is a nice teacher and is very helpful. The lectures are boring, however. If you listen and do the homework you should get a decent grade especially if you took high school physics.

Professor Firan, is not a bad teacher, but her lectures are very boring. As long as you do the hw, take the quizzes, and look at old test for practice you will get an A in her class. Drops 2 lowest quizzes and hw's. 2 tests and a final. Tests are really easy, but the final is difficult. If you have an A going into the final you will get an A.

Professor Firan is the sweetest lady I have ever met! Although the lectures are boring, she knows her stuff. She will help you with hw questions if you go to office  hours and will even sit with you for 2 hours straight if you need the help. Lots of extra cred as well. Love her, take her!! I HATE physics but I got an A in the class. Shes the best:)

She is very boring in her lectures and doesn't teach the material well at all. Her accent just adds to the confusion. Her tests, however, are somewhat easy if you study. Take her if you want an A, and could care less about the material in the course.

Professor Firan is not a great lecturer, she doesn't do a good job of explaining concepts clearly. Her accent can also be very hard to understand. I didn't learn much of anything in this class, I just got as much of the material to pass the exams... overall physics was disappointing considering I need to know this material for the MCAT

Prof. Flores passed away on July 6. She gave a strict first impression in the placement test with the 3 chance policy, but her kindness was also simultaneously apparent. She really cared about her students like we were her children, and I'm truly grateful to have studied with her for 2 years. The Japanese program at SMU is not the same without her.

Very hard emotionally to start your day with this kind of professor. She CAN be funny and nice, but most of the time will yell at (literally yell) & berate for any small mistake, demands respect but does not give it. She makes the class much harder than it needs to be on purpose, and takes pride in it. MINIMUM of 5x quizzes & 5x homework / week.

Go to class, do the HW, study every day and it will become less difficult. She gives out a lot of quizzes and HW so it will help boost your grade if you do well in them. Study for the tests and ask questions. Your classmates are also good study partners. Don't skip a lot of classes cause you will fall very behind.

Even though she's been teaching for years, Sensei has a hard time understanding why anyone would ever have trouble learning Japanese. I believe she is a good person deep down, but she yells at students for misunderstanding or making even slight mistakes. It is very difficult to be in her class every single morning. Hardest class at SMU, for sure.

I've taken all her Japanese classes in SMU. Initially she might seem strict, but her lectures are always organized and passionate. She does allow you to make mistakes, as long as you show respect and apologize. She pays attention to each of the student and spend time to know our problems. We all enjoy having her and even celebrate for her birthday!

I would say that Japanese is the easiest language to take at SMU. The tests only make up 20% of your final grade and the final is worth 10%, and the bulk of the grade comes from attendance and HW assignments. If you go to every class, and perform decently on the tests, should be an easy A. Just go to every class and do every HW assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You will learn so much in such a short time with Flores-sensei, but be warned that she expects respect and you absolutely cannot miss class. Homework, class participation on the speaking checks, and the written quizzes everyday make up the majority of your grade so don't worry about chapter tests. Really great teacher, but a lot of studying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sensei is by far the best professor I have had at SMU. She is not easy by any means - she'll yell at you at the drop of a hat and holds high standards for student performance. She makes class fun and interesting and as long as you genuinely are trying and it shows, she will work with you toward your success. Respect her, be on time, do your best!

Although knowledgeable & well-prepared, her style is ultra-Asian and is sharply unforgiving. Mistakes are met with ridicule more often than forgiveness. Praise is not infrequent, but if you miss class, she will have your you-know-what. If you are accidentally rude, you will be punished with shouting and rampage. Scoring an A is easy earlier on.
I have been taking every Japanese class since my first year in SMU. As long as you participate and do your homework, you will learn much and score great.

Sensei is awesome! She is one of the best professors at SMU. As long as you don't slack off and you study/attend class, there shouldn't be any problems. She is extremely helpful, and posts class notes on iTunesU, as well as audio recordings of the classes. Excellent professor.

Schneider-sensei is a very interesting teacher, and she will try to scare you for the first couple weeks to weed out slackers. She gives homework and a quiz every day, but they're not too hard. Just be sure to come to class! Teaches mostly in Japanese so you get a feel for the spoken language, but she is always willing to explain what she means.

This teacher is awesome.If you want to take a language class don't do something boring like Spanish or Italian, take Japanese with this teacher.She makes class fun and you learn a lot.There is HW and a Quiz everyday, but they are very small and they really help you keep up with the class.If you do your work and study you will get an A no prob!

Really cares about her students and their wellbeing
Understanding and willing to give extensions if necessary
Easily accessible outside of class via email or text
Genuinely wants to see her students succeed and tries her best to help them get there
Not a tough grader, only expects full participation, effort, and attendance

This professor is amazing. She genuinely cares about her students, knows how to teach, and is all around a great professor and teacher. She might move around dates and scheduling stuff a little too much, but other teachers rarely adjust their teaching for the students in their classes. If you can take a class with her, you should.

She is amazing!!! Take any class she teaches. She is the most laid back ever and so kind and knowledgeable about her craft. It just felt like a time set aside every week to practice with cameras and learn about production in a non-judgmental environment. ALL work is done in class, and she pushes dates around to make sure you are never stressed.

Rebecca is an AMAZING professor. Easily the best professor I have taken at SMU. She cares about her students so much and the class is fun. You will learn a ton but even if you aren't into film, like I wasn't it is awesome and super enjoyable. Would recommend her to anyone and everyone.
Best class on campus. Professor is so lenient and understanding. Never will have a test. The final is given out to you with answers provided in the review. No homework or studying. All in class work

The only test you take is the final exam which is open note. The work is all class work, never any homework or studying. Highly suggest taking this class or any class with Professor Flores! She is so fun and she is very happy all the time. Never expects an unrealistic amount of work, she is very lenient!
Definitely one of the best classes at SMU. You actually LEARn what you need for the real world. It's helped me in my job more than any other class.
Professor is often hard to read. She is tough to please but once you are on her good side you are good to go.
Awesome Professor! Made me love my major!
love her... shes is real and you will feel comfortable moving into the field when shes done with you
No Comments

She is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is extremely understanding and always willing to lend a helpful hand. She tells students how it is and sometimes that is hard but for me it only made me that much better. She knows her stuff and is dedicated to the success of her students. I recommend taking her, you will learn alot!
She basically forces students to write controversial articles and encourages them to submit the articles to the student newspaper.  She definately has a feminist agenda.
Not understanding & very uncaring & unfair. Not looking out for students' best interests.  Not helpful with struggling students. Class is mostly females.
grading is ruthless. she loves to humiliate so-so work during class

He is a good guy, but he does talk a lot and I usually zoned out after a certain point. He lectures AND then he talks during discussion time meant for students, often relating things to his personal life. I did get a good grade in the class overall though, once I figured out exactly what he's looking for in the essays.

Dr. Foley is extremely intelligent and provides interesting discussions. No tests, just some essays that are relatively easy. This class was not a huge time commitment compared to other history classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loves to hear himself talk. He will ramble for an hour, and whatever twenty minutes is left for discussion (for which participation is graded), he will also talk through large chunks of that time. His instructions are painfully vague but he has very specific grading criteria. Despite being repetitive himself, he will hold it against you in essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
SOOOOO boring. i cant emphasize that ENOUGH. take another teacher if possible.  
  it wasnt THAT hard as it was BORING. just avoid it, ppl were falling asleep all 
  around me ALL the time in class including me.

Lecture is pointless, it's just him rambling on for an hour and twenty minutes. One weekly 650 word essay due every Tuesday at 1 pm, he grades really tough and never explains his grading just says "look at the rubric" which is not thoroughly helpful. Attendance is crucial, but other than that the only grades are the weekly essays (60%) and an essay
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class time is generally speaking pointless, but you have to show up or else your grade gets hammered. Luckily, he wants you to use your laptop in class, so you can just do whatever you want on it. Getting below an A- in this class requires you to be... special.

No exams at all, not a lot of papers either. Half of your grade comes from the twice-weekly reading "analyses" (which are basically just summaries of short readings) and just showing up to class. Half of what is done in the lecture is stupid and useless, but beyond that he is very knowledgeable and communicates information well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! Foley is amazing  (used to teach in the UT plan 2 program) and SMU is lucky to have him. Lectures are interesting. The earlier comment is right though.. only complaint is that writing assignments can be vague. Do the readings/go to class and you'll be fine.

Dr. Foley is the man. Has seen so much in his life. He is a respected historian who has written many books. Despite his successful career he still likes to teach and see kids understand concepts. If you go to every class and read you can get an A (as long as you know how to write)

Keeps the lectures relatively interesting and the readings easy. On the whole, I'd say he's a great professor except for one fatal flaw: he keeps his writing assignments vague. Doesn't even give prompts. Never done a prospectus or document  analysis before? Tough luck, although he's a pretty reasonable grader. So far pleasantly surprised.

BEST PROF EVER- He is extremely caring, understanding, and so funny! There is HW everyday for this class but it's not difficult. Participation does matter bc thats like majority of your grade, one project, and 2 written exams. Not a harsh grader, gives great feedback, genuinely cares for your wellbeing and just an amazing professor overall. 11/10

The best class to knock out your literary analysis and a few other credits. Highly recommend, but only if you actually agree with the content taught or at least come in with an open mind. Grades are mostly done based on participation, but are made up of project, essays, & homework too. The in class essays are not that hard only 2. Funny guy too.
He refused to give me any flexibility to finish the course after I had a family emergency. Told me since I wasn't studying enough beforehand, not to expect any breaks now.
When I needed it most, he was incredibly understanding and flexible but also very harsh when grading.
He is an awesome professor! When I needed it most, he was incredibly understanding and flexible. Would 100% recommend. He is also very knowledgeable and an engaging lecturer!

Such a great professor! Would definitely take him again. He is so kind to his students and caring and he creates a positive environment. He leads in-class discussions where you have to speak at least once per class which isn't too hard as long as you read. The homework is doable and tests are graded generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Funny, sympathetic, and knowledgable! Engaging "lectures," heavy discussion/participation. Do the reading, even if it can be heavy! Open-ended essay prompts, no wrong answer, lenient formatting and requirements. Moderate grading, but gives good feedback. Worked with me when I had personal setbacks, allowed late grades, not strict at all. <3

Dr. Foerster is an absolute gem!! Take his class! Most of these reviews are for french, but he taught an honors history/human rights course this semester that changed my life. He is so caring and loves teaching. He adjusted the work load when he saw we were stressed and was always there to help. Pretty easy grader if you put the work in.

a great class, a great professor. Good class content so you probably won't be bored. Professor is understanding. If you read and participate you'll do just fine! I definitely recommend him. One of the best professors here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy who's passionate about the subject. The class is reading heavy, but not a lot of work. Participation in class is the most important thing to him and you are graded on if you participate at least 2 times a class. He's an easy grader overall.
Maxime is the sweetest guy, and loves his french classes. Smile and you will get an A

He is so nice and so laid back. I'll admit class is a bit boring because we are rarely tested on the material except for two in-class, open-book essays. However, this means it's pretty easy for the most part. He obviously cares about the material and about his students. He is so sweet, funny, and reasonable.
Really enjoy taking classes with Professor Foerster. He's very passionate about the material, and it shows in his lectures.

He is not only an easy professor, but a really nice guy. There's readings assigned every day and hw to supplement, but he tells you before if he's going to collect the hw or not. He loves teaching french vampire lit so it's easy to do well. Go to class, take a bit of notes, do the readings, and you'll be fine. He is a very easy grader.

Best French class I have taken at SMU thus far. Professor Foerster was always available for help and you could tell he really wanted to help and loved what he was teaching, which made the class love it too. Only two tests (in class essays) and then a final essay. Class participation is important and homework is not difficult if you do the reading.
He spends the whole class time confusing himself and us.

Super sweet guy! Lots of kind of boring lectures, attendance is mandatory but he grades exams so nicely it makes up for it. I took him for ECO6354 (same as 4354 with extra project), the material is so difficult but he's always happy to help. This is one of the few econ classes I feel like I'll use after college.

WORST experience of my life and this prof does NOT know how to teach. In fact,  doesn't teach, never have I been more lost in a class and have a prof too lazy to  help or actually teach. Talks poorly about other previous students, lectures are a mess, intentionally is unhelpful outside of class to embarrass you.

His teaching reflects his mastery of the forecasting material, and he's a nice and funny guy. With the curriculum being so advanced, the exams are really difficult and long, so expect to study a lot for them. Studying with classmates ahead of time can help prepare for them. Most of the coding HW is easy and helps too, along with the free textbook

Professor Fomby is very knowledgeable about the course content and does a good job of explaining it, despite the difficult subject matter. He is always available for office hours, and his homework exercises give you a good idea of what the exams will be like. He is a really nice, caring guy.

Fantastic Professor who is exceptional in the field of applied econometrics and forecasting, as well as predictive analytics. The homework assignments are difficult but you can go over questions you may have in his office hours and get great help. Would definitely take this class for the rigorous experience the knowledge gained.

I enjoyed the class time with Dr. Fomby, even if this class is very hard. Sometimes I cannot understand all materials covered in a lecture but his class notes and quizzes are very helpful when I study after classes. His homework is also very helpful. He gives a sample, which is very similar to but also different than the homework.

Fomby is an incredible teacher with an exceptional background in his field.  The class covers profoundly difficult topics, but he does a great job of making sense of them.  Make sure to come amped and ready to learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you are actually wanting to learn the topic that Professor Fomby teaches, and you're willing to learn, you will for sure learn. Professor Fomby is one of the most knowledgeable professors on campus and he is a gem to the economics and stat departments. Not an easy class, but its definetly doable. I had little stat knowledge and did fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is of course not the easiest professor you could expect, but this class is worth taking. His classes are hot topics and Professor Fomby himself was a part of Nobel Prize (he didn't get it though, but he joined the composition of that paper). however, this is not a easy class, but it's really satisfying if you work for it and get good grades.
Instructor seemed confused about the course subject and spent quite a bit of class time trying to understand the material.  Often times could not understand issues and resolutions.

Prof Fonner is truly the kindest man and professor. He was so understanding of we were having trouble with an assignment and would change due dates. He was always willing to have office hours rather than a set office hours schedule.
Such a great professor who is so understanding and just the nicest dude ever. He really does want you to succeed in his class. Best CCPA professor I've had yet.
The most understanding and kind professor I've ever had. He knows who he's teaching to and tries his best to make the class as manageable as possible. If you're lucky enough to take him, you should.

Professor Fonner is super sweet and understanding. He wants you to succeed. However, his classes are pretty boring and we do not do much other than listen to him teach. I will end up with an A or an A- depending on how he grades my final research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: super sweet lady but had a lot of quizzes. Same assigned group for all projects throughout the course so if you get stuck with a bad group, it sucks. She wants all her students to succeed and will put in time to meet with you. genuinely cares but can be a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Such a sweet teacher and very willing to help in office hours. However, there are only 4 tests and the questions are trickier than you'd expect, so it's more difficult to make an A than you'd think a core class would be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Foxman is very sweet, but boring. She's a very strict grader, doesn't give any leeway or extra credit. She sets her expectations clearly, but participation/attendance matter to her a lot. It's not too hard to get an A, but it's kind of an annoying class. I liked her, but there could be better teachers.
Very kind teacher but class graded on only a few things, so one grade can significantly impact your final grade. Helpful in office hours but no extra credit offered.
Very sweet lady but pretty boring class

This class was not the hardest class by far, but you have to show up and pay attention. Prof. Foxman is a good professor and the class is enjoyable, but there are very few things that cause your grade to go up or down. So do your best on the tests and you will be fine, but you don't have to overwork on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice lady, but class is harder than you may expect. Do well on the quizzes because they are worth a lot more than you would expect. Tests can be tricky, so make sure to know examples and not just memorize the definitions.

Really cool professor with lots of professional experience so get to know her. The tests are very challenging so make sure to memorize every detail of her PowerPoints and take notes on examples of concepts. MIA quizzes are really easy and interesting. Overall I enjoyed the class but it definitely made me realize that Marketing is not my thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great experience. Print PowerPoints and take additional notes in class and study those to do well. 3 tests and 4 small quizzes. Attendance is mandatory and you have to participate (participation grade starts at a 77.5 and goes up or down). Very nice lady with clear expectations. I recommend her.

Excellent choice for required marketing class. Has put a lot of effort into her lectures and I think her tests are less subjective than in past years. Basic intro class, easy to do well in, a lot of it follows common sense. No projects, homework, or consistent reading required (besides MIA articles). Highly recommend!

Sweet lady who cares about Marketing, but really boring class. Her tests are very tough, even though the material is easy: it is application-driven and more of those "A and B could be right but C is MORE correct" type of tests, where there are not very many points.  I recommend taking her if you are a Marketing Major. If not, take an easier prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Foxman is a very sweet lady; however her lectures are very boring. I don't think I've been more bored by a class in Cox. Overall the class is pretty easy. Don't underestimate the tests; though if you study the details well, you should be fine.

Foxman knows her own small field in mktg, but her qualifications in academia are nonexistent. Her teaching and tests are poorly constructed, and trying to point out the lack of clarity in her test questions is like arguing with a brick wall. Nice lady, but grossly illogical, and, academically, rather unintelligent. Lectures are painfully bad.

Sweetest lady ever! Very cute and hilarious, and truly cares for her students.  Texts are average difficulty, while quizzes are extremely easy. Really applies marketing to the real world. I am a finance major and now extremely interested in marketing because of her. Class very interesting and fun to go to,

100% would NOT recommend her to anyone. I am an A student. These comments do no illustrate the kind of professor she is. Very vague questions on the test, you can never get them right since you never know what she is looking for. Minimal explanation of marketing content. Surely there are other better marketing professors in the business school.

Marketing is perhaps the worst class in the business school. The material is, at best, intellectually bankrupt and horribly unfounded in fact, so the blame is not all on the prof. Foxman's presentation is boring, and very little is to be learned from attending lecture. Just make sure to study for the test, they are purposely tricky and deceptive.

She is a great teacher. I am not a business major and this is the most interesting class I took this semester because she is so engaged in the subject material. The tests are a little difficult if you dont study application of the material. Shes excited about the material and she makes you interested and makes you want to come to class. Take her.
Exam can be hard, study the reviews.

I took her for the intro marketing class.  I loved the class thought the lectures were really cool, but despite thefact that I would study for days, I always got bs on the exams.  not an easy class, but you'll enjoy getting the b/b+ lol

Pick her for Intro Mktg for sure. She makes class interesting through her stories and all you need to know is her slides and the terms on the assigned pages of the textbook. She also curved me a couple of points in the end. Great teacher and great class.
Great teacher
choose this professor for mktg 3340!
Foxman is the best.  Pay close attention to her power point slides and her lectures and you'll ace every test.  She has had great practical experience.

Her tests are hard, but the subject is common sense with a fancy vocabulary. She tests as to which answer is the best answer when technically two answers (depending on how you argue) could be right. She gives updated examples, which are easy to understand.
Although her tests are a little on the hard side, she is possibly the best prof I've ever had. Very clear, very helpful, passionate about teaching, and she has tons of real-world experience to share.

Lectures are engaging and he really wants students to participate. His assigned readings are really good and very eye-opening, but sometimes the class discussion did seem to get a little uncomfortable at times the subject matter could get pretty dark. Stay on top of the readings and have friends proof read essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Foster is so interesting to listen to. The small sizes of DISC honors classes make it so that he will call on everyone in your class and force deep, thoughtful discussions. My head usually hurt from thinking so hard after his classes, but it was so worth it. Amazing guy, really helped my writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster is an amazing teacher. One of my favorite at SMU by far. Awesome discussions, super helpful, encouraging, and understanding. Not hard to get an A if you participate, do the work, and just try.
makes you read inappropriate, awful stories, nice person though.

If he likes you you will make a good grade. Go into office hours for each paper and he helps a ton. Pay attention in class even if you don''t know the answer when he calls on you if you are on your phone or computer he won''t like you.

I thought Foster was a great teacher, though some classmates disliked him.  From what I can tell and what I've heard he appeals more to those who are scientifically minded (not sure why, maybe just the way he does analysis).  The class is easy too, I had an A with minimal effort on papers.  You must discuss in class, that is the whole point.

This is a discussion class, if you don't participate, he will call you out on it. That being said, discussions are usually interesting and help later on when doing written assignments. Not a class to take as an 8am but definitely a good english class.

Foster is great. Compared to the other Honors Discourse teachers, he's more discussion intensive. I absolutely love the class and his teaching style. Not the easiest grader on essays, but he'll let you re-write if you ask, extend due-dates, literally as flexible as possible.

Dr. Foster is extremely intelligent. Sometimes he has trouble conveying what he's thinking, but discussions are still very interesting. He's a difficult grader, but is always available for office hours. Class participation is necessary to do well in the class. One of the best honors English professors.

Prof. Foster is fantastic:  the best professor I have had at SMU so far.  He's really smart, incredibly nice, and so interesting.  He is very helpful and keeps the discussion going in unexpected way.  He's also very funny!  I wish I could take more classes from him!
Dennis is an awesome person.  Very smart, very encouraging.  So glad to have known and worked with him.  Definitely take Dennis's classes.  I did, twice.

i realized i was really gonna have to work the 1st day, so i tried to make it to class. i didnt think i knew the stuff as well as i should and i thought i was going to get Cs even though i was working really really hard on it, just because of the depth of the material covered was nuts. i ended up with a B+ he sees effort and grades on it!! good!
Dr. Foster is brilliant, and he will force you to see the world through a different lens. I will warn, however, his brilliance, at times, impeedes his clarity, but I promise amazing "braingasms."
he's great!  so smart and so interesting, and very helpful to students.  i recommend him really highly.

Honors DISC is probably one of the most painstakingly tedious courses one could take, but Mr. Forrester made it extremely enjoyable. He's young and hilarious, so it's pretty easy for him to relate to the students. His office hours are pretty flexible and he's always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took his class randomly, didn't know anything about him, and he's ended up being the best teacher I have ever had.  Extremely helpful and really cares about his students .  He is a little bit awkwardly funny in a good way and it's awesome becausee it keeps class interesting and fun.  If you have the opportunity to take his class 100% reccomend.

Really cool guy. Hes super young (23ish) so he is still pretty cool. Easy grader on the few assignments. Only 5 or 6 total assignments with a few homeworks. You can skip 6 classes before you are droppedn from the class but he is generally pretty cool about missing class if you have a solid reason.
Really nice guy who make class fun and interesting.
Such a funny guy. Some people say its sassy but thats what makes his classes so entertaining. Also the group project is insane but he will help you out at every step. Nice guy, wants u to succeed
Not bad, but you need to spend a lot of time on his group project, it will takes few weeks to finish. Big lecture( lots of people), little bit difficult to concentrate at all.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure what all this hate is for Fontenot.  When I had him for Data Structures at SMU, I learned a ton. It was a lot of work, but you just had to put in the time.  If you want to learn useful knowledge, take his classes

Very challenging but great prof. I definitely accelerated my knowledge a ton, just expect summer cs3500 to be a full-time job.  He constantly sought feedback about how assignments were, and made modifications as we went along often times loosening requirements to reduce stress. That being said, this class was absolutely worth taking with Fontenot

Dr. Fontenot rewrote the Object Oriented Design course to teach more practical real world skills and, in my opinion, did an excellent job. He is very helpful and teaches things that matter in industry and I would definitely take more of his classes.

Dr. Fontenot is an incredibly lovely man. His version of OOD is significantly easier and more fun than any other professor's version. He knows this, so he can be snarky when students still complain endlessly about the course difficulty. I feel incredibly lucky to have had him as a professor. Would recommend.

Fontenot isn't as bad as some people make him out to be. His approach to teaching is interesting, and he clearly cares about the students' feedbacks. The class is indeed difficult, but cs3500 is traditionally a difficult class at neu. The class would be better if he spends more time crafting the lectures and labs, and stops hiring unqualified TAs.

Mark Fontenot's teaching skills leave much to be desired. He's dismissive of questions and has trouble explaining complex concepts clearly. Class often felt disorganized and his attitude discouraged open discussion. His lectures were confusing and less helpful than expected. I won't take his class again.

Mark Fontenot is unapproachable and creates a hostile learning environment. His lectures are disjointed, and understanding the material is a hassle. It's frustrating when you ask questions and are met with condescension. His impatience is counterproductive. Try to take the class with a different professor.

Mark Fontenot makes learning a chore. Terrible at explaining concepts, and insanely unapproachable. Ask a question, prepare for berating. He's arrogant and belittles students openly. If you value your sanity, avoid taking a class with him. Learning is hard enough without a hostile professor like Fontenot.

Taking this class with Mark Fontenot was a huge mistake. He's knowledgeable but extremely patronizing and unhelpful. Dismissive of students' questions and creates a toxic learning environment. TAs saved the class; without them, it'd be a nightmare. Avoid if you have other options.

Mark Fontenot is very unprofessional and condescending, making the learning environment unbearable. He avoids answering questions and displays passive-aggressive behavior. He favors certain students and is reluctant to provide guidance or assistance. Avoid his classes if possible, for a better learning experience.

I took a course with Mark Fontenot and it was a letdown. He's knowledgeable but his communication skills are terrible. Rarely answers questions and is passive-aggressive. Creates a negative environment and hinders learning. Choose a different professor if possible.

Mark Fontenot's teaching style is less than helpful. Rather than answering questions clearly, his responses are often patronizing and uninformative. The inconsistency in communication and expectations made mastering the material very difficult. His standoffish attitude made learning frustrating.

Taking a course with Mark Fontenot was a mistake. He's rude and dismissive, making learning difficult. His lectures don't stay on track, and he's terrible at answering questions. He created a hostile environment, and I often felt belittled. Would not recommend his class - seek other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I regret taking a course with Mark Fontenot. He's unapproachable and gets annoyed when students ask questions. Lectures are boring and unproductive, leaving students to rely on TAs. Communication is poor, and he doesn't handle criticism well. Try to take this class with someone else, if possible.

Mark Fontenot is an atrocious professor for CS3200. He habitually delays assignments and changes grading rubrics without warning. He never keeps his promises, making this class unbearable. Unsupportive and unreliable, he's a detriment to students' learning. Avoid his class if possible.

The instructor felt passive-aggressive and students spend more time learning from the TA's than the professor. The course needs to be reorganized to give students sufficient time to work on assignments instead of having students cram endless assignments and projects during the last weeks of school.

Professor Fontenot is one of the few I've had in college that have genuinely inspired me.  He is very experienced in all things academia and will help you to the extent that you help yourself.  I pent roughly 8-10 hrs a day working on his projects over summer, including class time.  I left his class so much more confident in my own ability.

Very unresponsive and often passive aggressive. Prof and TAs were really untimely with grading as well, especially considering how easy some of the assignments were. As of over 2 weeks since the end of the semester, some things still haven't been graded, and I doubt they ever will be. Class is easy enough but you can't rely on him for much help.

Professor is new to northeastern and it definitely shows. He's passive-aggressive in slack, email, and piazza. I have never experienced such an unreasonable professor at NEU. Class was easy and had freebie assignments, just make sure you don't rely on the prof for anything. Get in and out. Very unresponsive to communications, especially towards end

review for cs3200 at neu since rmp hasn't updated that he switched colleges. besides being a little passive aggressive at times (unintentionally i think), my main qualm was how totally unresponsive he was, especially towards the end of the semester. barely answered any questions on piazza/slack about the final project. kinda just a meh prof tbh.

Professor Fontenot is a okay professor. As long as you pay attention in his class, you will be fine. You will need to use outside sources as well though, especially for the programming projects. The final search engine project is also a good project to put on resumes.

Dr. Fontenot teaches some of the hardest classes at SMU. He does it moderately well, but oftentimes you have to teach yourself the final mile of how to complete his programming assignments. This works for some, but it is also extremely stressful in the midst of it.
Amazing Professor, sad to see him leave for northeastern. Also, make sure you refer to destructors as deconstructors in his class.
Ask him if your program is terse enough.

This class is incredibly difficult. The first programming project makes you feel like you were hit by a bus and the programming projects only get more difficult and time-consuming. The final project is extremely stressful. The lectures only cover the conceptual aspects of subjects rather than the application in the projects. Rely on the TA for help

Best CS professor by far! Great lectures and really funny. Classes are project heavy and each one is pretty challenging but you learn so much doing them. Also a fair grader and understands his projects aren't easy

Some people worship him, and others dislike him. To be honest, he’s a good computer scientist, but he’s not a good teacher unlike what some people think. He just reads off some slides and occasionally explains a concept needed for a project. Final project is useful for resumes.
He made it more difficult than it had to be, thanks.

Fontenot is so, so tough, but he will likely be the reason I get a job in comp sci. I've already used skills from class projects on independent projects. He's not great at explaining things during class, but he's incredibly helpful/accessible outside of class. I would highly recommend meeting up with him outside class at least once.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tough but understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely love Dr. F! Took Data structures over the summer. Really intense and fast paced but he is understanding, sets reasonable deadlines and very accessible outside of class (before 8 pm). Passionate in what he does and genuinely wants his students to learn. Graded on 3 coding projects, fine project, midterm and final oral interview

Dr Fontenot is my favorite at SMU so far! Although the class is difficult but his lectures are funny and informative. The projects are difficult but doable if you work on them a little each day. Dr Fontenot and the TAs were always available to help. I wish that I could have Dr Fontenot teach all of my CS courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor you can take. He gets a lot of heat because he's the face of the CS department which separates those who are serious from those who aren't and are simply attracted to the salary of a software engineer. This professor is hard because he cares about you. If he didn't care he wouldn't waste his effort. You better grind if in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have heard such scary things about this class. It all really came down to who was willing to put in the time and speak up/ask questions. If you get on top of your work when it is assigned and ask questions when you need help, you will be absolutely fine. I ended up doing well in this class, as I had been mentally prepared to get ahead and it paid
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fontenot's data structures class is certainly time consuming, however I dont agree with many of the other reviews that the class is overly difficult. If you attend lectures, pay attention and take good notes you will have all the tools needed to succeed. Just make sure to be proactive in starting the projects as they can be very time intensive
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The supreme leader at smu. He controlled half of the department. Barely, teach anything. Some students worship his teaching, but in reality his lecture is mediocre.

took him for Algorithms and Data structures. The whole class is project-based in both of them. He will point you in the right direction and push you to do independent research. Some would say he is the great filter. He separates the wheat from the chaff. Many people complain about him, but it's just because they're bad. He's a force of Nature
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have some gripes with Fontenot, but his strengths really shine. His lectures are good (if a bit slow/distracted), however his projects are the real deal (esp. in 2341). They will seriously challenge you and make you much better at coding. PUT HIS FINAL SEARCH ENGINE PROJECT ON YOUR RESUME!! Classes demand your time and effort, but its worth it.

Those who say he just wants to challenge you need to realize theyre paying thousands to willfully get their lives ruined by this sad excuse for a teacher while learning nothing in the process. You might as well print out his projects in your free time if you want to feel challenged because youll get the same amount of teaching and guidance

Anyone who likes this guy has actual Stockholm syndrome. He doesnt teach a single thing in class and then expects PHD level work. His formula is simple: show up, make some jokes, give a vague, disorganized, unhelpful lecture and then basically ask you to build Google. He is also incredibly rude and lacks basic social skills and manners. Worst prof

Knows his stuff but doesn't know how to teach. Humiliates students who don't immediately understand the material, talks poorly about other previous students, lectures are all over the place so you have to learn everything on your own, intentionally is unhelpful outside of class to embarrass you. Slog through it if you have no option.

Dr F was my prof for KNW and Data structures, both of which are the hardest classes I have taken at SMU. Fontenot has been the best professor throughout both classes. I can walk into his office and debug code with him without a meeting, talk about future classes, etc.. Best part about him though is how much he cares for students and their success.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Im ngl, Fontenot's classes give me depression. He's a necessary evil. His projects are heavy and pretty difficult, so it's great project experience, but it's substantially hellish during the process. I am grateful to be challenged, but he challenges you to reach his very high expectations without teaching in class how to get close to it. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. F is has high expectations for his students, and has no problem asking you if he should fail you come final presentation time. Put in the hours to avoid this at all costs. His lectures are great, and he is usually quite witty. If you're going to fall asleep in his class, probably best to just not go.

Fontenot is a fair instructor that is concerned with his students actually learning the material. I have personally taken him for Java, C++, and for Data Structures. If you engage, pay attention, and put in the work, you will get a good grade. There's often a moderately heavy workload, so procrastinate or slack off and you're not gonna do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: KNW is by far one of the most difficult and time consuming classes at SMU. But if you do the class right and met frequently and work diligently your team will succeed. Fontenot was strict and loose at times so get on his good side.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is designed to be challenged. From my experience, the projects aren't hard but just time consuming. You can find most of the help online so use google and stackoverflow wisely. I don't understand why some people here hate Fontenot. The fact is that he might judge you but he does care about every CSE student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Here's the thing - Fontenot is one of the professors that, if you're a comp sci, you'll have to take him for a few semesters. Get on his good side. Don't sleep in class or act like you already know the material. Not all TAs are super helpful, but the internet exists. Data Structures is a difficult course, but I have seen improvement in my code.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Most of your grade is determined by labs that you will spend 20 + hours a week on. Tests were open book, however, they tended to be hard and long. Fontentot calls his students out on everything and gets distracted very easily- making lectures all over the place. I never learned anything from a lecture ever. Take another intro teacher if you can
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Stay away from him. He cannot teach. I have had much better teaching from my High School teacher. His bedside manners are horrible. He will judge you and it is automatically assumed that the student is bad. Not true. Their entire department needs to be overhauled. I wish I had never come to SMU. They keep him so he can make you keep retaking $$$

I took him for Java and he made the class enjoyable and interesting with his examples and lectures. Make sure to go to class so he likes you and don't sleep/ yawn. Make sure to do the lab projects so you actually learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: When I took this course I didnt know I was expected to already be an expert. His teaching is rare. He judges you from day 1 based on what you look like. I had to get my own help and avoided him as much as possible. I tried reporting him several times but soon found out that its no use. They dont care. Very Sad for SMUs CSE Department.

So here's the deal. This class is HARD and TIME consuming. Start the projects the first day or you will suffer! I was terrified at first but when I put in the work and went to see him if I was confused, it paid off in the end. You learn so much new material so quickly its crazy! Amazing class and will really shape you well for the real world.

Be ready to code. This class is sooo time consuming. Youll spend hours debugging code. Make use of the TAs and prof. Grading was a bit unfair on programs. Hes an alright professor but gets off topic sometimes. He tries to throw a few jokes here and there. Shows little to no sympathy. Go to class, work on the programs, keep up and youll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You need to work hard for this class but Fontenot is funny and teaches concepts well. He can be intimidating and a bit rude to students who don't put in the work but he does care and spends hours debugging students' code. Most interesting and personable prof I have had for computer science.

Fontenot is one of the best professors I have ever had. He really cares about how the students are doing. With that being said, you need to be in class every day as he will remember who you are and where you sit. He is always bringing energy to classes. However, with all of this being said, there is ALOT of work every week that needs to be done.
Expects you to spend more than 20 hours a week outside your class on assignments, and doesn't show a lot of empathy for students.

Fontenot is a great professor who will actually teach you and make sure you understand the material before moving on. He is fair, but this is a difficult class. Granted, it would be a lot worse if it was with a poor professor. Fontenot is very fair, but you do have to put in the work. This is NOT a blow off class. He is also very entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Fontenot is maybe the best professor at SMU. His class is hard and will challenge you no matter your CSE skill level. He has a way of pushing you to your limits but not past them, and can do it for all ranges of skill levels. A truly amazing professor.

You are expected to spend 20 hours a week outside your class for project. You have to actively seek for help both in class and outside the class, from TA and personal tutors(that u'd pay for) if you want to make okay grades.  If you are majoring in CSE, you have to take him and note that half the class ends up failing or dropping every semester.

Had him some time ago! He will make sure that you're completely invested in getting a CS degree.  I've talked about his final project at every interview I've been to. I've landed 2 internships & a permanent job coz of this class. He won't just teach you the material, you'll learn how to think and survive. He'll ready you for an actual job! Love him

He is the professor to take if you want to be ready for a real job! His projects will help you learn a lot. Be prepared to learn on your own and put in the extra effort. The TAs are great and are always willing to help. Final project is something that really impressed every employer I've interviewed with. Put in the extra effort and you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors at SMU. You will actually learn in this class, and get this, without a BOOK! GASP! He prepares you for the industry and will force you to think. He makes you better. It won't be easy (final project will make you cry) but you'll be thankful later.

This is it, folks. The weed-out class of the Computer Science degree plan. This is a difficult class, which is exactly why year after year, Fontenot teaches it. He is a fantastic professor - he makes you think about difficult problems and challenges you to come up with the best solution. Also, DON'T YAWN IN CLASS OR "FRAT SNAP", HE WILL MURDER YOU.
It's gonna be a struggle, but plan lots of time for the homework and you'll do fine. Get his phone number, he's helpful over text.
Great professor but you will have no life if you take his classes especially data structures  NO LIFE AT ALL

I have never had a professor like Fontenot, in a good way. He will make you work, but he will do everything he can to make sure you understand the material.  And with cse, thats what is most important.  Also, one of the best senses of humor i have seen in a professor.

Very very good professor! There is lots of work but it is work that is going to get you ready for industry. And he goes way out of his way to help his students. Over all a very good professor. Take his classes!
Awesome teacher, had a blast learning from him because he keeps it interesting.  Definitely take his class.
Ridiculous grading by the TA's (they are so harsh). This class WILL require a minimum of 10 hours a week on projects, but probably more like 20 hours a week.

Fontenot is a great professor. He was able to explain the material in a clear and fun way. He establishes a friendship with his students that make his class all the more enjoyable. I highly recommend taking any of his courses, just be prepared to work .
Fontenot is a really good teacher. When it comes to 1341 all of the teachers are really good but I guarantee you will have the most fun with Fontenot and learn the most!!!
He expect a lot from you , if you can't keep up with hard work , don't take his class!

I have had a few classes with him now, he treats you as an adult and expects you to work without a lot of guidance as such. His classes aren't easy but he'll teach you more than most professors and keep you interested most of the way. A perfect college professor.
An engaging lecturer, although a harsh grader. Very involved.

Fontenot's a great guy and a terrific teacher, but his class was really hard! He expects a lot from you, but you do learn a lot. I worked harder and stressed out more in his class than I did any other last semester! I'm not a CSE major, but most of the other students were. It came really easy for them, but really hard for me.
Great professor, knows what he's talking about and tries his best to help you learn. Great guy overall. I would take another course with him, if he taught it.
Great guy and fun lectures. Great example of how every college prof. should be.
He's the best teacher at SMU.

He is very helpful. He reminds us what being an engineer is all about and makes you like it. The class is not hard if you pay attention and do not procrastinate on the programs. Even if you do, its still good.
Knows his stuff. Very helpful.
he's super nice and funny.  very easy.
Great teacher, funny, nice to joke around with.  Still kinda acts like a college kid but a great teacher
He makes C++ interesting, but you'll never miss a class because he is too funny
No Comments
awesome professor! easy class too!
i really liked professor fontenot! he is such a funny guy to have for a class. I hate computers but i still really liked his class because he is so fun. its a pretty easy grade too!

He is a very good teacher. I enjoyed his class and would highly recommend him to anyone who has to take this computer science class and is not a computer science major. He makes the material interesting and easy to get through.

Lectures are long and slightly boring--just no effort to make it engaging. Very nice and knowledgable, cancels class often. Tests are open note but worth a large portion of your grade. Posts all slides, some info from test comes from class lectures, but attendance isn't really mandatory. Would recommend as an easy elective

Traci changed the class due to the backlash on the two tests. The tests are take-home and open-note. There is no homework, and attendance is not mandatory, really. She does in-class exercises but not actual attendance. Super nice lady and very knowledgeable in marketing. Fun class where you talk about engaging and real-time topics.

Classes are so boring but both tests (including final) are take home open note open book. Highest test grade was worth 80% of our grade and the other 20% attendance. She's nice and cool but it was just such a boring class and attendance was random so you kind of have to go to most classes to do well in that section of your grade.

As much as I love her as a person, this class will tank your GPA. 20% of your grade comes from participation assignments (12 throughout the semester) and the other 80% is from two exams that are absolutely impossible. There is no hope for a good grade in this class. I wish I would've known this before putting myself through mental distress.

Yes shes really nice, but her entire class is graded on 2 exams. Its take home, open note, however everyone gets a 60 on it because it is absurdly hard with niche random questions she makes up herself. If you fail one exam you will not be able to get an A  or potentially a B in the class. DO NOT TAKE HER.

Nice lady, very little assessments so therefore everything was a big deal. attendance is checked by 12 attendance sheets and she tends to cancel class a ton. I think there was one month where we only saw her 4 times. if you attend class and are a good student, she will help your grade out in the end if she knows that you put the work in.

Worst class I have ever taken at SMU. The guy does not know anythng about economics and goes off on random tangents that make zero sense. The class is a waste of time. He lacks the intellecutal capabilities to properly dictate the material.

Frost challenges students to participate in the academic process. This puts some off. His lectures are clear, insightful, and laced with real-world examples. He's a cool dude too. Unlike all of my other econ classes, the lectures were provocative. Attending class and not being a dil ensures an A. Frost is a game-changer.

I think Money & Banking was harder than it needed to be. The professor encouraged developing persuasive writing skills over grasping economic concepts and sometimes assumed you knew more than you've been taught. Outside reading is HEAVILY emphasized, but you don't review them in class. Overall stimulating lectures with high expectations for work.

I had the displeasure of having Mr. Frost at UTD and SMU. I had him at SMU last and I can say definitely one of the dumbest professors I have had. He constantly goes off topic and is not very familiar with the information he is teaching. I would highly suggest taking with another professor.

This guy is awesome! He actually makes economics interesting but his class is not easy. If you pay attention and read what he assigns then you can definitely get a good grade. He is there to help you but if you don't try then he won't care. Take this class.

Easily one of the most interesting professors that U will ever come across. Highly intelligent, does not suffer fools or slackers lightly. Likes  stimulating and challenging dialog. Employs Socratic method(s). 2006? Texas Monthly Teacher of Year.

Literally the best teacher I've ever had.  My class is at 8am and surprisingly enough I actually want to go to class because I want to hear about what he has to teach me.... not just about economics but about life.  :)
Good teacher who really encourages thinking for one's self.

Ive taken Frost for 1311, 1312, and 3355.  He is the best teacher you will come by at SMU.  He will make you work, but you will come out of the class with knowledge you can actually use. He gives you a lot of food for thought if you take the time to stay after class. Hes the type of professor you will always remember.
my best prof in my schooling career. attend class, listen and actually buy into what he says. all relevent in life and test

If  you want to ruin your GPA then take the class. He teaches very well but what's the point if your end up with a C. If I were to reverse it, I'd take an easy Macro Professor and Audit Mark Frost's class instead.

MOST AMAZING TEACHER EVER. hard but fair. listen to what he says in class!!! take notes on it because his test questions definitely come from the lectures. he doesn't go by the book. he changed my outlook on life i wish i could take his class again. smu is so lucky to have him
