Easy class, 3 papers and in class hw every week. Easy grader, lectures a lot in class but we watch movies so it's nice and easy to zone out. 
She's super nice just show up and talk and she'll like like you.

very nice person, interesting lectures. To do good on essays you must carefully read the readings and attend at least 1 or 2 office hours in the semester. Overall, I recommend this class especially for poli sci majors.
She is a terrible lecturer and doesn't know how to grade fairly. Worked hard all semester for a good grade and only this class is bringing my gpa down of six in enrolled into. Hate her sm.

Doesn't teach at all like in any way just sits there in his as expecting us to talk then throws midsize childish fits when we don't depending on her unpredictable moods which are harsh and wide, only positive is leave early every day halfway through class if you stay quiet
Kind of a lot of reading, and she's a total bore, had a pretty big crashout when she thought people were using AI/ If you are just trying to grab an easy credit, just do something else.
Awful. Awful. Boring. Argues. Lies. Avoid.

This teacher is the worst and is so rude and demanding to her students. Distrustful in nature she assumes everyone's cheating then creates a hostile atmosphere with her weird policies and lectures. Don't know how to teach and literally reads to us. Sad.

I am honestly shocked at how many good reviews she has when she is one of the worst professors I have had. She grades ridiculously random for assignments that are not explained well and have little relevance. She tells you not to complain and then tells you it's your fault for not speaking up. Save yourself and take a different professor
Easy class, good at delivering content, just a bit monotone and boring

Very engaging, informative class with understandable readings. I like how lectures were structured and with daily participation grades which helped boost overall grade. Feedback is helpful on papers and tests. I suggest taking detailed reading notes and lecture notes to connect overall themes!

One of the best professors for Political Science at Smu. As a major I would highly recommend taking her. She's very knowledgeable and it's possible to get an A in this class if you try. People that are mad are the ones who probably thought this class is gonna be just sitting around and doing nothing. Put effort and you will get a good grade.

Dr. Mueller has been great and has developed my interest in international relations. She is very accessible outside of office hours, considers what our class wants regarding grading, and is flexible. While she lectures frequently, the writing activities accompanying them are minimal, and it is very easy to get a good grade for pending completion.
She's alright. Make sure you read the prompt carefully before doing any of the paper.

Dr. Mueller is one of the most considerate professors I have ever had. She is incredibly smart, resourceful, and respecting of her students. Her course wasn't the hardest, but it certainly was not the easiest. Would taking her class to anyone, if given the opportunity.

Dr. Mueller is a fantastic and intelligent professor! Lectures are based on articles/chapters assigned (which should be read before class), and there are some opportunities for discussion in class. Four short research papers comprise the majority of the grading and are about applying course content. She's a great professor, I would recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! I took two of her classes, and she was so nice and accessible outside of class. She was very understanding. Attendance is mandatory, and she assigns many readings but reviews them in class. Grades are based on papers, which she gives more than enough time to complete, and the prompts are very fair. Wish I could take her again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although lectures were sometimes a bit lengthy, the class as a whole was interesting and informative. Grades depend heavily on 4 large papers, and these papers incorporate lengthy political science readings. To succeed in this class, pay close attention to lectures and also read the course material provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She assigns lots of readings every class. She ends of going over them during lectures though so I didn't read that much. She assigns lots of writings but only grades the content not the quality of your writing. Answer questions for participation but overall she was super great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super sweet teacher and easy grader - looks for knowledge, not writing ability. Classes can be pretty boring because lectures the whole time, but got out early almost every day. Lots of assigned readings, but after the 3rd or 4th I gave up and did just fine. Very accommodating, once gave me a paper extension the day before it was due. Love her tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is extremely lecture heavy, attendance being mandatory (only allowed 1 absence), with loads of reading homework. I found Professor Mueller to be a nice grader on Essays and accessible outside of class. However, I found most lectures unitneresting, most people did other things during class.

Great professor! You do have to go to class for attendance. Answer questions somewhat often for participation. If you do not want to do readings, you can take notes during class but definitely skim them to help you with papers. Overall, loved the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor but he is such a tough grader. I wasn't a fan of the way he does the overall grading of things starting from 0%. For analysis quizzes and essays, he will grade based off of what he likes. He has to like the analysis in order for him to grade it well. If it was a good analysis and he doesn't like it, he will mark you down.

Having finished the course materials, the last week of class could have been used to prepare us for the final exam, but he spent it as time to yap more. Only on the last day did he briefly talk about final exam (and make us sit through his singing.)
He cares more about the subject rather than students' academic success with the essay and exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never usually write reviews for professors, but this one really did it for me. The teacher may be a decent person, but as far as lectures go, it's way too much content to be a freshman level class. Throughout the year, you take 12 quizzes worth five points and all are graded bias to him and one paper. The Final's content came out of no where.

Professor Griffin is an amazing professor; he is very passionate about film which keeps lectures interesting. If you're looking for a course to just watch movies in, this is not it. There is a lot of reading, lectures and weekly quizzes on what we watch in class. For film majors, this is a great class to learn analyzation skills.

Sean is one of my favorite professors at SMU. His classes are challenging, put if you talk to him and put in the work (which is pretty much just reading and studying for the midterm and final) you'll be fine. You'll learn so much and he makes lectures super interesting. TALK TO HIM about term papers!! He'll tell you exactly what to do to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Sean for graduate seminar, and he did a new criticism each week like... Communist critique, Queer theory, Feminist theory, etc; and that allowed me to see him lecture across the broadest spectrum, which was super cool, and also he deputized students to present, which was honestly lots of fun. All of us went to pool party at his house later!

The class isn't that hard but it's pretty ridiculous there's a final worth 25% of your grade when there's no prior tests in the course. Also, the final has isn't multiple choice, you just have to fill in the answers. He takes the class a bit to seriously with this being a course most are taking just for the breadth credit.

FILM 2362!! This class was so interesting and Dr. Griffin made all the material so applicable and easy to understand in both the real-world and in film. Only 3 grades though, midterm, 10 page essay, and final. great class and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is a fantastic film professor that is engaging and clear during lectures. He fully understands the material he teaches and can help clarify any confusion on a topic. Labs require a lot of participation, and he does appreciate adding to the discussion but won't single you out. Take his class either for CC or major requirements.

Professor Griffin is a good teacher, he tells you the content clearly with examples. The only thing is that there is no homework, your grade relies on watching movies in class and then taking quizzes on it. Sometimes you watch the movie one week but then take the quiz the next and you might forget key points. Study the notes and each specific thing
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is the best! His lectures are super interesting and you learn a lot. Hes super nice and approachable and cares about his profession a lot. He loves getting the class involved in the discussion and is always open to all opinions. One tip is to start the term paper early (7-10 pages) and email him for revisions. Hes awesome!!

Three grades all semester: midterm, one essay, and the final exam. Sounds really scary, but he gives a study guide for the midterm that perfectly matched the test. If you dont like movies, dont take this class. First half of the semester is all black and white movies and the first quarter is all silent movies. Easy going guy, hell probably sing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class, the professor is understanding--and really doesn't give you a hard time. The class requires less work than regular college classes since there are no quizzes--just two exams and a paper. If you put in a good amount of work you should be fine. I'd take the class again if I had to.

Took this class because I thought it would be interesting and an easy A. Some of the films were okay while others were very boring. Do not take this class unless you're planning on being a Film major. You don't know what your grade is until the end of the semester which really doesn't help when you think your'e doing well but end up with a B.
Do yourself a favor and don't take this class unless your a film major. Took it thinking it would be an A easy but it was terrible. Seemed like he chose films that were purposely bad.

Overall was a good class. TAKE NOTES on all of the movies you watch and take some during the discussion too. Watch out for pop quizzes they're worth a lot more than you think. Has lots of writing on his midterm and final, start the paper early. Wouldn't take if your not a film major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's super nice. The class is interesting and fun. Quizzes aren't that bad, but there ends up being a lot of writing for the midterm, term paper, and final.
Very laid back but full of energy at the same time.  He doesn't care if you walk in late.  He really likes people who voice an opinion in class, and he is very helpful if you go to his office hours.

Awesome professor! Very funny and knowledgable about film.. Likes for you to speak up in class even though its a large lecture class... A couple written exams, that he gives reviews to.. Take good notes during the movie and discussion and you will do fine! I enjoyed his class but I wouldn't take this class if I wasn't a film major
Great teacher but the lecture period of the class is too long. Tests are difficult so study. Start term paper early

Awesome class and awesome teacher. Watch interesting, relevant movies/TV shows and analyze/discuss them. He's also the Chair of the CTV department, so I recommend taking him, especially if you plan on majoring in CTV.

Dr. Griffin is awesome. He's really a fantastic teacher that loves his job and communicates well. I only used the book to find the definitions for the tests. Never had a quiz or pop quiz. Had one paper due at the end of the semester and the final. We watched movies and discussed them. It was killer! I'd take this class any day, Griffin is that cool

history of animation class. hilarious guy & you watch movies and clips every day. make sure to TAKE NOTES he will give you review w/50 names & 30 movies/defin. and 5 essays be prepared to answer all of them. there is fill in blank, matching & essays(must be thorough!!) also 10 pg paper take good notes on specif movie u like that u can research a lo
Awesome Professor, Very Nice Guy, Loves Film/Teaching Film, A Bit Arrogant but Very Likeable
No Comments
Awesome teacher! Absolutely love his class!

Very fast paced class but it is not difficult even if you don't remember anything from your previous french classes. Gives a ton of partial credit on tests and quizzes I got almost every question semi-wrong but would get 95% on tests. Daily homework was very tedious/ time consuming and did not find it helpful. Def take for language credit.
she's a great teacher she can just be a little strict at times but she's really good at what she does

So great! Prof. Grubbs is such a nice and patient professor! Lots of homework, but it isn't difficult. Participation is VERY important! Coming to class is vital! Make sure to study, and you'll do great! I learned so much! Made hard stuff understandable. She really cares about her students! Can't recommend her enough!!

Amazing. This was the first French class where I actually felt like I learned a lot. Workload got a bit heavy at times but that's what you would expect for a 5 credit class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit on tests and assignments are very manageable.
great teacher tests are a little hard, but tons of opportunities for easy other assignments to boost grade.

Dr. Grubbs embodies what an educator should be. She has clear expectations and deeply cares about her students. She is understanding and always willing to help. The workload can be a bit demanding at times, but it's completely manageable. Take her if you have the chance because you will learn so much from a great teacher and person!

She's a great professor, and she made it easy to understand difficult concepts. I took 1502 with her the previous semester and decided to continue with French because of how obtainable she made it. I could not recommend her more!!

Hands down the best French teacher I've ever had! I wish she could teach me every subject for my entire college career. While the course itself does have several assignments, they are all doable and simple enough. She cares about the students' success and will help you as much as possible. Overall, she's just a lovely human being.

Truly one of a kind. I really enjoyed her class and the material we talked about; if you don't keep up with your readings, it's hard to participate or enjoy the class! She gives great feedback but I highly recommend going to her office hours, she helps a lot!! It's definitely a workload-heavy class, but very reasonable for a 4000-level class.

LOVED Professor Grubbs! She was great at involving students in discussions and activities during class. She made the French very easy to understand. She graded assignments and tests very generously and always gave very detailed feedback. She is also very kind and available to help. I hope to take Professor Grubbs again soon!!

Prof Grubbs and Omar split this class, Grubbs talked strictly in french for five min at the begining of class almost everyday and all 15 of us were lost and just nodding our heads. she cares and will help you if you ask for it, kind lady. Will never cancel class insted have another prof fill in. Assignments were easy.

TAKE HER . She is one of the kindest professors out there she genuinely cares for her students and if you put in effort and show up then she will make sure that you come out knowing a lot better french than when you started she is genuinely interested in making sure her students succeed and makes sure that you understand the material.
She strictly talks in French, and makes class hard. She makes papers and speaking assignments easy which makes it easier to get a good grade. Tests are very hard.

This class is work, but it's the level you'd expect from a 4000 level class. She gives you opportunities to be fun & creative, and a lot of the class is discussion in small groups w the people around you. Make sure you have a friend in the class or pick a good seat on the first day. You can find most/all of the books for this class for free online.

She spends about a month reviewing the basics before progressing onto new topics. There is homework every night online and lots of projects and assignments. Attendance is strict so make sure to show up. She is super nice and really cares about her students. I would take her again - you can get an A if you do all of the work and put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Grubbs certainly is passionate about the topics - be prepared to put a lot of work into all paper outlines and drafts. Class is very homework heavy, and you have to put in a lot of research and critical thinking, all while writing in French. Learned a lot, but definitely the toughest French class I've taken so far in terms of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she is an excellent choice. she wants students to do well and is super available. she also gives tons of feedback on everything - goes above and beyond here. shes a decently easy grader and her quizzes and tests are easy if you slightly know the material. definitely reccomend

Nice woman, just a very tough grader when it comes to written assignments. Don't just follow the rubric, but be prepared to go way above what it's asking in order to get an A on assignments. Do your readings if you want to have any idea what's going on in class. Not a bad option just don't think you're gonna just sail through her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Grubbs is incredibly sweet and very proactive. Participation is mandatory but her charisma and dedication towards making sure her students learn makes it worth putting in effort. Not only that, but she is very easy to communicate with and makes great accommodations for hardships. Easily the best language instructor I have ever had.
Professor. Grubbs is such a caring person who gives you a great feedback on every interro and oral. She wants to help and cares for you. Just be ready to do homework and speak in French!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Grubbs is super patient and allows us to think a bit before using people to answer her questions. She explains things very well and she also gives us flow charts or simple guidelines to remember French grammar rules. She was most helpful when reviewing for tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Like others have said, she just reads off a script during lectures and the TA ends up answering most of the questions. Exams don't reflect what's actually covered in class and grading feels harsh. Having been to three different universities, this is easily the worst professor I've had. Would not recommend for any graduate-level course.

The instructor primarily read from a script during lectures, and the TA often stepped in to answer student questions at the board. The final exam, worth 50% of the grade, was a 20-question McGraw Hill test with no partial credit due to its online format.

In my experience, the course was not taught well by Dr. Guler. No accounting course should fail to review calculations in the live sessions. The exam does not match what is taught in class, and projects are graded harshly. She isn't very receptive to student questions or concerns.

Genuinely curious how this lady calls herself a professor. Class average on the final exam of a cost accounting class was a 43…for a decently simple subject, that should tell you everything you need to know on why not to take this class with this “professor”.

Unfortunately, this class has been the worst experience I've had at SMU. This professor does not time manage her class properly. We are let out of class 15-20 minutes late every class. She does not teach; she only reads straight off of her PowerPoint slides word for word. What she "teaches" is not what is on quizzes/exams. Avoid at all costs.
Worst professor of all time and has no business teaching an MBA level course, zero professionalism, zero ability to teach course concept, do not take and avoid at all costs.

This professor was responsible for the worst academic experience I have ever been a part of. This professor's class made me doubt the value of my time at SMU. We were belittled for asking questions, treated like children, and given little to no guidance. 

Avoid at all costs.

The experience was terribly frustrating. I enjoyed the concepts, but the teaching was a disaster. I don't expect a top MBA professor to be only reading off random slides in class and dump the work load on us as pre work. Additionally she did not solve a single calculation problem in class on the board but expects us to do all of it for the finals

The class may be challenging if public speaking isn't your thing, but she is a very fair grader and will give you tips to succeed on the next presentations. Quizzes are open-book and note so if you can lock in before the tests you'll do great.
Great professor! She is so nice and helpful and really wants you to do well. If you actually try, you will do well in this class.
Loved this professor! She's so sweet and accommodating. Get ready for lots of presentations.
HORRIBLE! Such a strict grader for an easy A class. Made it impossible to get a good grade and the workload was so much. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Personally, I loved Professor Graves. As long as you do your work and actually try, you'll receive a good outcome. She's open to working with you one-on-one, she gives great feedback, and overall is a good professor. Slightly hard grader but totally doable to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She treats her class like kindergarten and keeps talking most of the time about unnecessary things. If she were an English teacher, students would loathe her to the end. Grading criteria are awful. Get ready to relive your kindergarten moment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: dumb class but required for cox. all common knowledge on how to present and act in the business world. grades unnecessarily hard and I barely got an A somehow. at least it's only twice a week but just get on her good side even if you don't like her. participate a lot

Meg takes her job too seriously. If your thing is not presentating on random topics, making weird hand movements/ strange eye contact and being graded on a super harsh and subjective rubric then I would not suggest this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is okay, she is an okay teacher, but she is a very unnecessarily harsh grader for a BLI class for both presentations and assignments. Even after meeting with her about one assignment and making all the changes she suggested I received a B. If you just care about passing she is fine, but if you care about making A's it is unreasonably hard.

Very easy class. Prof. Graves clearly states how the class is graded and tells you what you need to do to succeed in the class. Only two quizzes and three presentations. Great class and it did improve my presentation skills.
All quizzes are open book/note which is nice. Presentations are somewhat of a learning curve, so if you take her advice the first one you'll be good for the 2nd/3rd.

Prof Graves is okay, her lectures are boring but you don't have to take notes. Quizzes are useless but they're open book/note. She gave our class the opportunity for extra credit. The main part of your grade is the presentations so just be prepared for those. There's an easy rubric to follow. Not a bad class, just very average.

DO NOT TAKE HER! She is completely disrespectful and dismissive of your situation if u miss class. Attendance is absolutely mandatory and even if you are in class she will give you a 1/2 on participation which will lower your grade by 2%. She grades presentations so hard, you will not get an A in this class. So bad I considered dropping the class.

This class is completely useless and painful to sit through. She refuses to round final grades so if you get an 89.8 it's a B+. Grades presentations on ridiculous criteria: hand gestures and body style. LOTS of busywork. Didn't give any rubric for the final presentation. She either likes you and gives you an A or doesn't. Loves teachers pet type

Prof Graves is a solid choice for BLI. She gives you rubrics for grading before you give a presentation and is always clear about what she is looking for. If you do the work, you will get the grade you deserve. Be cautious about due dates, the layout she uses on Canvas makes it a bit confusing to see when things are due. Would take her class again.

Meg is fine. Her tests are hard though but I never read the textbook and always managed to make like an 80. She doesnt curve grades but theres if you do an EC assignment she will. Shes not the worst option. My experience with her was just decent. I do feel like she assigns a lot of busy work for no purpose.

this class is completely useless and painful to sit through. Meg makes it much harder than it needs to be. She refuses to round final grades so if you get a 92.99, you have an A-. She takes it way too seriously for a complete joke of a class. Grades presentations on ridiculous criteria and doesn't know how to grade so she repeats the same critics

She's really nice and seems easy. Her quizzes are very hard, to do well must read the textbook and memorize the stuff. She is a very hard grader on presentations, so follow all her guidelines / rubrics in order to do well. Counts off for not paying attention / missing class (HUGE portion of grade which is ridiculous).Way harder than I thought; nice
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The tests were harder than I expected, but you can make up by preparing very well for your presentations! I loved the feedback she gave. Truly cared about improving our presentation skills. This was the hardest class to transition to online format, but prof Graves made it as smooth as possible!

This class is so much busy work and nearly impossible to get an A in. That being said, Graves is very knowledgeable about the course and lectures well. She cares about the students. Two individual presentations, a group presentations, and quizzes. No final. Very hard to get an A, but it is a Cox requirement. Graves is worth it.

So nice and is honestly very transparent with what she expects. She offers good feedback after presentations and genuinely wants you to do well and improve each time and is happy to help. For the "quizzes" make sure to read the textbook chapters the night before and you'll do well on them. Start the group project in advance and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Okay you NEED to read the chapters for the exams because the exams pull specific questions from the chapters. Also, you'll do three presentations in this class, and make sure to practice at least a day in advance because she's a tough grader on those. Other than that, she's amazing and the lectures are applicable to real life

Subjective beyond belief. If she likes you, you will end up with a better grade. Gave useless feedback. Such as, "Well done. Thorough research and strong organization led to a readable and actionable article."Let me know how I didn't get a perfect score AKA: Subjective. This isn't Meadows, this is COX LAST I CHECKED!!

Loved the class, honestly couldn't stand the way Graves talked during class (she's very high energy). Class is graded off your presentation skills and how you improve. Easy if you're a good talker. Big project in the middle of the semester, just make sure to get it done as early as possible because it comes up pretty quick and she won't mention it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor that I would recommend to anyone taking BLI. Her grading is very clear, and if you follow the rubrics on projects they are not difficult. She wants her students to succeed and makes this a fun and interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BLI is a class you're going to have to take, it isn't a great class but Prof. Graves does the best she can with the given curriculum. She is very understanding that this class is not your main priority and also clearly outlines her expectations for the course work making it easy to do well. The course does have a lot of busy work but its easy.

Professor Graves is a really cool and chill professor. I took her just this Spring of 2018. I loved her silly in-class activities. All BLI Courses have work that takes time but Professor Graves made it easy. Her instructions are super straight forward. I got an A and so did others I know who followed her instructions. I totally recommend her!!!

Meg Graves is a good professor. This course has a lot of busy work - you'll get an A if you stick to task and rise above the boredom. Sometimes the lectures can get dry, but Meg really wants her students to do well. No hyper frustrating moments and no unreasonable grading, so she's a safe professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: First of all, I think this class should be removed from the cox core classes and should instead be a one week mandatory workshop. I think Professor Graves was great in giving good feedback for presentations, but the one test we had is basically a subjective english test which judges your email writing skills in a time crunch situation.

Prof graves has a lot of mixed reviews. In all honesty her class isn't bad at all, the only thing you have to do is show up. Lectures are simplified and her sarcasm helps. Assignments are probably the easiest ones in cox. Not too time consuming at all. She is clear in what she wants from your presentations. One of the more laid back in cox
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For a class that should be an easy A, Ms. Graves does a great job making it as hard as possible, she seems to think BLI is your only class and that it should be as hard as your finance or accounting classes.  Two  (subjective AF) quizzes per week over a really boring textbook that goes into extreme detail of things that should be common sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ms. Graves will try to go out of her way to help any student that asks for help.  She is very nice and seems eager to teach the subject.  Her class is easy - at least easier than other classes I had.

Really helpful professor who cares a lot about her subject and students.  She spent a lot of time preparing us for internships.  Pushed me to write better for job search and work.  I hate to speak in front of people, but she made this part of the class as good as it could be for someone like me.  Online quizzes.  Group project. Grades fairly.
Great

Did not enjoy this class because everything was common sense. You would think the class would be easy because of this, but it was excruciating.  Projects were pointless (and there were many of them). If you have to take this class, I would recommend taking it on your very last semester. If you don't, avoid.
Very helpful! She was great! The class could be tough. Lots of projects. It was worth taking her class.

This class is stupid in general, and most of the content we covered seems very obvious to the average person, but the tests can be tricky. Teacher is a bit all over the place, moving due dates and deadlines around all the time. Her lectures are pointless, but attendance is mandatory. Not an easy A, but not a demanding course at all.

While I dont think BLI necessarily warrants a semester long class Graves is a good teacher for it and her enthusiasm and helpfulness really made what could be a dull class relatively enjoyable. Tests are not difficult, but also not easy and she is a stickler for presentations. But walking away with a good grade is not difficult with moderate effort

Good professor. She makes the class interesting with her lectures and assignments. A couple tests which are not bad if you read the book and pay attention in class. A stickler about details in presentations, but if you prepare and practice it is not hard to do well. She is good at teaching the subject and cares about what she does and her students.

For a class like BLI, Graves is superb.  She is very clear about the subject matter, and very helpful out of class.  She bluntly provides proper criticism of presentation techniques in a way that is easy to accept and helpful because of it.  All the work is manageable and to get good grades you just merely have to try.  Take Graves for BLI

Professor Gunther truly made SMU in Taos such a great experience. I went to/saw so many new things that I wouldn't have otherwise. Professor Gunther quickly became one of my favorite teachers of all time after taking his health psych class in Taos, NM. He is an incredible mentor and has a lot of wisdom to share. One of the best TAs I've met, loved the labs

Richard is awesome and makes class fun. The class is easy and he is a good professor.

he gets so off topic.. the labs are easy, final is insanely hard (everyone fails) but he makes it that everyone gets and A or B

He is the most helpful teacher ever. Just remember to no skip classes and learn the slides as careful as possible.

he just reads from the slides

Professor Gunst is amazing. His subject is difficult, but he will go out of his way to help the students in anyway he can. If you show him that you are trying your best, he with help your homework and exam grades! Very sweet man!

Not a great professor, he does a poor of explaining easy concepts. Always do the homework! Assignments are given online thru blackboard and he only gives you about a day or two to complete them. Class doesnt cover 1/2 of the material on test.Labs are useless, not an easy class.

good prof.knows his material, is very willing to help. at the beginning of class he always asks if anyone needs help.there is no hw for labs.  His tests arent hard if you study his old tests and the samples he puts in the ppts. I came to class,worked hard,and he exempted me from the final.

Horrible teacher! Professor Gunst has NO sympathy for his students. Went into the final with an 87 and ended up with a C+ in the class. Then when I emailed him to ask what I got on the final, I got an autoresponse saying he was out of the office until Jan 3rd. Horrible teacher! DO NOT TAKE GUNST!

AMAZING TEACHER!! actually interested in students learning and actually cares about his students, you do have to go to class and tests can be a litte tough but if you know the material you are fine (if you dont miss class he will give you extra 4% on tests!!) also if u go to class/lab &do well on hw/lab/tests - u dont have to take the final!!

But at least I can do in 15 minutes what it takes everyone else all day to do because of Prof. Gwinns class. I wish SMU had more classes like this.
