reviews.comment: He's not that hard but how he acts is cringe, a substitute teacher who never left, that's him. Overuses slang he googled last night then smirks like he invented it. Thinks hes "young hip and vibes w genz" and u have to challenge him in person for your points when he should just get it right the 1st time. We shouldnt have to correct your grades bro
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His tests are a literal joke. Class is extremely boring and he has major superiority complex. What's even worse is that he lies and tells us SMU says we can only have 1 day off when all my other teachers give more. Friday before Fall Break, off. Monday before Thanksgiving, off. Every class cancelled except his. Joke and total waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Should be a relatively easy class, only taking this class for a CC credit, so there is no reason I should not receive an A in this class. He makes his midterm excruciatingly hard, takes off 0.2 or 0.1 points for no reason when he should be giving full credit. Barely curves, and then grades harshly on every other assignment. Like seriously dude?

This class is HARD. No matter how much you study it's impossible to do well on the exams with all the “trick questions” and you better do extremely well on all 4 exams because those are the only grades you get

I loved Reynold's as a prof as she made 80 min classes very engaging. Some people think she's rude but she's just a very direct person. Super kind and helpful in office hours. Only thing is that the class is only graded on 4 very very hard exams so you have to do well on all of them but curves grades at the end which is a lifesaver
She's fine, can be quite rude and is dated in her material and knowledge, but there are worse out there
This person is allergic to clarity. Vibes-based grading, passive-aggressive announcements, and lectures that felt like spoken word performances about their personal trauma. Iconically terrible.

Her class is easy, and the exams closely resemble the practice problems. Pay attention, and you should be fine. You can have 5 excused absences, which is generous for a T/Th class. Grading is based on a few exams, so if you don't test well, consider avoiding this class; however, most ECON classes are like this.

Professor Reynolds was fine for Price Theory, but that was due to the department setting guidelines for the course . In cultural economics, the opposite was true as lectures were disorganized and she was unclear over what would be on the exams. Her grading on exams was arbitrary and she rarely gave partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible just terrible. Gets mad at her students when they ask questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She takes attendance for every class and definitely go to class but she is super relaxed on if you show up late. You are only graded by 4 tests but she curved all the grades at the end. If you actually do the work you will be fine. People struggle because none of the homework she gives out it is mandatory/graded but if you study you will be fine.

Graded on 4 tests, each is 25%. Tests are hard, very. She gives out lots of papers, do them all, do the practice tests online and read the textbook if you have too. If you put in the work for this class you will do great. The people who dont like her did not study enough/were not willing to put in the work or should not be majoring in econ.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Helen Reynolds as a person, she was super funny in class and really nice and understanding outside of class. But, tests were super hard and that is the only thing she puts in the grade book. I think she curved a lot because everyone failed the final. Unless you can confidently pass every exam of hers I would take another professor.
Hardest and worst course I have ever taken. She is a mean old woman who hates everyone including herself. Do not take this. She will scar you.
She is absuive to students and bad comments keep disappearing. Beware.

Professor Reynolds is smart, witty, and engaging. The short-term format makes the heavy reading load tough, almost impossible. Homework accounts for 10%, while two exams make up 90%. Her lectures cover a lot, and tests include many outside readings. This course focuses more on memorizing details rather than applying economic concepts to problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Reynolds has four exams and they make up the entire course grade, each 25% of the total. The exams are multiple choice but still difficult. You don't really need the textbook. She gives a million handouts and practice exams, etc. She does her best to make economics interesting by giving random acronyms and stories. She's pretty great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good at teaching econ. Graded on 3 exams and the final, so do your best on them. Mostly multiple choice, so not hard but easy to mess up. Study what she gives you and all the practice tests, its the same test bank. Go to class as it helps learn the concepts. Can easily get an A but also a B-.

Grade is based on tests and attendance. Class videos online. Instructor is witty and explains well, offering many practice problems. Despite students often struggling, I managed >80% exam average using these resources for an A, thanks to a ~10% curve. Beware of tricky exam questions.

Professor Reynolds is a bright and caring professor. She always kept lectures bearable with subtle humor but wasn't afraid to tease us in a friendly manner. The course is graded exclusively by difficult multiple-choice tests with a plethora of trick questions. If you are willing to put the most effort in to learn the most, you should take her!

She was rude when we asked questions and made belittling comments if you didn't understand something like "why can't you get this yet?" right in front of everyone. That's pretty abrasive and not conducive to learning. If you want help, take someone else. Tests are the only grade and they all consist of trick questions nothing like class

Literally the worst class I have ever taken. First exam, instead of owning up to her horrible teaching she said no one out of her 4 sections got an A so, "to prevent people from jumping off buildings" she added 10 points. Every other test after that was just as atrocious as the first. Only tests are graded. I have actual rage writing this review.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not actually teach and is not helpful at all. Doesn't cover whats on the tests, no feedback, couldn't care less about students struggling in her courses, blatantly rude when you ask questions, fails to respond to email.
Love Helen omg. Took her just for micro but passionate, caring, made sure I truly understood everything in office hours which was always sweet i dunno just loved her!
Test and lectures were two different things for me. A warning to all economics majors out there. You're also only graded on the 3 tests and a final.

Helen Reynolds gives out random papers during class and solves example problems. It's a flipped classroom, but no actual lecture. If she was teaching a Youtube class for review it would be okay, but for someone who is supposed to be introducing concepts, her lack of organization and confusing teaching style was a mess. No modules in Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Long lectures, but show up and you will do fine. Hard grading but she was fair and wanted to help

A lot of work which is at the last minute, not respectful of our time either in class or out of it, dead lectures that are insufferable, doesn't have time for you. The most unorganized woman I have ever met, likely worst professor I have ever met, and I hope SMU finally does something about her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Reynolds for ECO 4340 and ECO 43543 over the summer. It is very important that you attend class and pay attention to lectures, as the final grade was based on only a few homework assignments and several tests... But that shouldn't be a problem because she is one of the most interesting and funny professors I have had! 10/10 recommend.

Do not take her for law and economics! I love Economics and do well in economics classes, but this is by far the worst structured class I have ever taken. It is a Monday 3-hour lecture, and she only grades you on 3 exams. She is also unclear about what to study -- basically, we are expected to remember every single thing she has ever said in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching style focused on those who already understood the material. She did not care to teach to those who did not automatically grasp the concepts. Even if you attend every class & all her office hours, she dismisses your attempts to learn as incompetent. It was very disappointing to see her unconscious biases against students as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciate that Reynolds made this class very straightforward and no harder than it needed to be. The exams were fair, and you will do very well if you understand the concepts (which are not too difficult in the first place). I also really liked her as a person since she had a great/funny personality.

Really great lectures, makes the material interesting and isn't very challenging to follow. Your entire grade is basically 3 exams and a final, but if you keep up with the material and do the homework, it's not too bad. She doesn't use canvas which is a little frustrating, but overall a great teacher.

I'll preface this by saying I'm AWFUL at econ. I thought I was gonna major in it but I'm not now just because I'm so bad. Anyways, Reynolds is a nice lady. She is kind of cold but is never rude to students. Only grade is the tests. She lets you drop the worst one. I would take her again if I HAD to take an econ class. Kind of hard to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Takes time explaining concepts, good lectures, fairly easy tests.

As boring as this subject is, she makes it interesting & clearly explains the information during lectures. Great professor and if you go to class/watch lecture recordings, you will do fine on the tests. Never looked at the textbook but reviewed all practice files she posts & got an A. Only thing is is that entire class is based on 3 exams & final.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Reynolds is really cool, her lectures are always interesting and engaging and she really does care about the students. The class is graded on 3 tests and 1 final, one of the three tests can be dropped. She really makes a point that she doesnt want people to fail, and she will give ExCred for those who need it. Grades on a curve. Def recommend

Professor Reynolds is great at explaining things and has a good sense of humor. Grade is solely based on 3 tests and a final, but she ended up dropping our lowest test. Not hard to do well if you go to class and do the practice problems she puts on canvas because she uses some of the exact questions on tests. Never had to open the book once.

Professor Reynolds is the best econ professor at SMU. She is really into the topics that she teaches and if you can take her for price theory. Even though her lectures are extensive, there is no homework. Take clear notes because everything she talks about in class is helpful to study for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is funny and engaging when she teaches which is nice because the material can be dry. Make sure to print out the packets for each class because it'll be easier to follow along. Never used textbook. Tests are okay-do the practice packets and attend review sessions to understand specific questions because they'll show up on the tests

Good choice for econ elective. Just pay attention in class to answer her test questions that do test your memory of little things. Textbook seemed pretty unnecessary- I never cracked it open. Reynolds is cool and an entertaining enough lecturer and often pretty funny; can sometimes come off a bit condescending but she means well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think Prof. Reynolds is a bad choice for 3301, but she's not great. She was pretty rude when asked questions + made passive-aggressive comments ("this is easy right?) in both verbal and email communications. I'm no snowflake and I thought she was abrasive. If you need extra help take someone else. I was fine with her style but not impressed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: entire grade is based on three tests and a final, and each test is 33 questions, final is 50. so not a lot in the grade book, but tests aren't super difficult if you just do the practice problems she gives and if you show up to class and take notes. Def worth taking her!!
Shes great. Your grade is based off of 4 tests and nothing else. All multiple choice (maybe a few fill in problems) and some extra credit if you go to hegi
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brings a lot of energy and I actually feel like I learn from her lectures. A lot of professors are smart but aren't good at communicating the material but she is an excellent teacher. Three tests and a final and they are not easy by any means but I think an A in her class was a 90. For price theory this is by far the best option.

Prof. Reynolds is hilarious, and she gives really good examples to explain her concepts. I feel like I learned a lot of econ from her. What I felt I learned and what was on the tests, however, were two different things. Tests all multiple choice, some very tricky. I think that's on the department though, take Reynolds!

Dr. Reynolds is hilarious and gives really good real-life examples in class. She makes the difficult concepts easier to understand, and if you go into her office hours she is an even bigger help. Her tests are based on the notes and examples in class. You don't have to take the final if your average is a 90+ among the first 3 tests. She's great!

Reynolds is a terrific professor but this class is no cake walk. She's a terrific professor but the material is challenging. She includes interesting stories and explains the concepts well but the material can be dry and uninviting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Reynolds for ECON 5353 (law and econ) and ECON 3355 (money and banking). Both classes were great! I got B's on every test except the final in both classes and ended with an A so there definitely is a curve. She is always available outside of class and is super nice. Definitely go to class and just glance over textbook to do well.

This class was a breeze. If you show up for class and take some notes you'll be set, barely have to study. Class moves kind of slow but her lectures are usually pretty interesting. Annoying that she doesn't use Canvas but otherwise solid class. Textbook is pretty irrelevant. She does track attendance.

I had the chance to take this class during the summer term. Class was very straight foward and her lectures were very well organized. Class was 3x a week and hardly ever lasted the entire time. As long as you pay attention in class you and do a little outside work you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had to pleasure to take several classes from Dr. Reynolds. She is a great professor and makes Econ lectures entertaining and provides examples applicable to real life. No need to buy the textbook but make sure to read the handouts she provides. Absolutely take her if you get the chance!

I think she's a solid choice. She gives interesting lectures and uses good metaphors and examples to illustrate her points. She doesn't use Powerpoint, so notes aren't accessible outside of class. It's also slightly irritating that she doesn't use Canvas. She's a quality professor though, and I'd recommend her.

She is the ideal early-morning professor.  Very energetic, easy to understand, and she illustrates everything with real examples.   Her tests can be fairly difficult, so be ready to study.  She has a few quirks (ex. she insists everyone bring highlighters & rulers to class), but nothing unreasonable.  Great professor, I highly recommend.

If you go to lectures you'll pass with either an A or B, and they're interesting in the way that other profs will make lectures just about the concepts, but she applies them to everyday examples and she's kinda funny. lots of hw but they're easy in the way that she works similar ones in class and u can have 2 drops for hw and 5 absences
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very funny and easy. She's a little disheveled as a person and you probably won't ever get your things back, but an easy A. 3 tests, 2 presentations (which were a completion grade), attendance, no hw - engaging teacher, would recommend. Don't waste your money on buying the textbook, she assigns readings but only class stuff is on the test.

Funny and exciting teacher. For Price Theory, I did not even touch my textbook because I went to all her lectures. Save yourself some money and skip the book. Her tests are a breeze and she makes the class go by quickly. Homework are not for grades and only for your benefit. She counts attendance.
Easy easy easy. You retain all the information from lectures and she tries to make them interesting. Tests are easy if you look over the review and the notes for 10 minutes. Show up, do well.

I LOVE Dr. Reynolds! I took her for 3301 and enjoyed her teaching style so much that I am taking 2 classes with her this coming semester (3355 and 5353). She is very clear on what you need to know and will make sure you know and understand it. She uses great relevant examples. She takes attendance but only to see who's grades she can raise later.

Dr. Reynolds is a vivacious women, and she funnels her energy into her lecture. Her grading system is black and white, as she has only a few tests and mild homework. You cannot breeze by her class, because one bad test grade will make you sink. Keep up with the homework, and visit her in her office. Don't be intimidated by her snarky demeanor.
Very straightforward in grading. Doesn''t play favorites you get the grade you earn.

I'm going to start off by saying that I'm probably the laziest student in SMU. I rarely read, study, and attend class. That being said, Reynolds is my favorite professor of all time. She's pretty funny, she's lenient and it's easy for someone like me to succeed in her classes. Just listen to the lectures. She's awesome. Take her classes, no regrets

Great class and discussion provided a different perspective on economics.  Instructor kept the class entertaining and reviewed concepts from prior classes to ensure understanding of what was being taught in this class.

Very disappointing experience.  No class interaction (discussion) and little to no interest in teaching students to learn the subject.  No learning other than reading the textbook and the tests did not mirror anything in the book but seemed geared towards prior subjects (Price Theory and Calculus).  If you can memorize formulas you're set.

She is a great professor.  She is very clear, and honestly is not that hard.  You need to show up each class period to take notes.  If you write down exactly what she puts on the board and memorize it before the test, you will make an A.  She is very enthusiastic about the subject, and really is a wonderful professor.  This class was wonderful.

Also got the "I only give 2 As" speech on Day 1. Her lectures were fascinating. I did badly on the first test b/c of her ambiguous wording, I even complained and she said next semester she would be more clear. Did well on exams 2&3 despite an awful class avg. on the 2nd. Ended up w/ a B+. HW is completion as she is too disorganized to give it back.

Very enthusiastic about the subject.  Her teaching style is great, she reviews concepts from principles while at the same time teaching you price theory. Her examples are great and are great review problems for her tests.
whenever students ask her questions she cannot answer it. she said she will email the answers but always forgot.

She gives good examples and explains things very well!  First day of class she said she is going to assume everyone knows nothing and review everything you learn in principles.  Exams are not difficult if you know what your doing and she hosts reviews every test

She never responds to email and is not flexible with the office hours and does NOT care if you are passing or failing!  The first day of class she said, "ill only give 2 As this semester., we had atleast 100 students in there.
Dr. Reynolds rules...she is the most interesting professor I have ever met. Her lectures make sense and she is very helpful. Tests are just like homework.

nice, the first review. i may be a little biased since i enjoy econ but i find her pretty easy and intriguing. her tests are not very hard and she gives homework and reviews that very closely resemble it, i would recommend her

Professor Hennum really cares about students and is always available to meet and offer guidance. Clearly passionate about the books and really knowledgable. I feel like I learned a lot! You have to put the work in but its worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ENGL 10803 at Texas Christian University - Would recommend taking this course! Professor Hennum is a passionate teacher always inspiring critical thinking and very understanding. Definitely the course can become a pain, yet you always learn something and thought-provoking. You get what you out in, but participation matters and engagement.

Easy credit, ever since coming to TCU his attitude is not how it is in these previous rates. He is a lot better and a funny and understanding guy. Would totally take again. Never stressed me out. Bless this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took crime fiction with him and it's a class you can do amazing in. Classes can get boring at times, and it is mandatory. I would recommend him though for crime fiction.

I took Crime Fiction.
His lectures are insightful and engaging, urging you to actually think about our system within many different contexts. He will take a hammer and smash your worldview, asking you to put it back together with what he taught you as a thinking and working adult. 
You get what you put into this class. Loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good professor for a core class, I hate English, and he makes it very enjoyable. He is a professor who is accessible outside of class, and if you ask for more constructive feedback, he will give it to you. I really like taking his course, even though there was a lot of reading and weekly write-ups. Def. one of the easiest classes at TCU.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hennum is passionate about the subject and expects students to engage and try. There's tons of opportunities to make up points, you just actually have to do the work and make an effort. If you expect to get an A just for registering, this class isn't for you. If you want to learn and have some fun doing it, give this prof a chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I have no problem while studying with him. I joined Intro to Fiction at TCU this year and I think he really cares about his students IF YOU ACTUALLY STUDY. If you don't and just expect to have an easy A class stay away from this class pls. Oh if you use AI for any of your essays you will fail this class =)))

Worst teacher I ever had. Not sure how TCU hired him. His temper and attitude is so discouraging and makes nobody want to participate. He also sets up conferences where he loves to tell you an assignment is looking good, then give you an F on it when you submit it. Teaching should not be his profession.

was rarely available outside of class, lectures didn't have any relation to the papers, insight was never helpful, all together one of the worst professors I have ever had. I wouldn't wish him on even my worst enemy.

He does not make himself accessible outside of class therefor hard to really understand all the material as each class he reads word for word off unclear lecture notes each class. Unfortunate that TCU would hire an immature candidate like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems as if he may have it out for TCU students considering his past job.

Now teaching english at TCU. Unprofessional teacher and seems to be unqualified for his job. Unfair grading and simply not worth your time to take. Other english teachers here care much more about their students and I would not recommend him to anyone who thinks of signing up for this class.
If you actually care about your GPA, don't take him. Loves giving zeros and laughs at you when you email him about it. NEVER TAKING HIM AGAIN!!!!
Worst professor ever. Talks in monotone, reads directly off slides. Doesn't clarify confusing concepts. Expects us to magically understand. Avoid at all costs.

Awesome class taught by an awesome professor. We explored some really interesting literature in a variety of mediums (essays, short stories, books, films, etc.) Professor Hennum is extremely caring and is happy to assist students when needed.

Prof Hennum is great! I would definitely recommend his class. There is a lot of reading but it's typically very interesting and there's also a few films implemented into the class. Participation is important though considering how small the class is. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hennum is a great person and teacher. He really cares about his students, if you're having a bad week you can email him and he will make sure to help you with the work for the week. He makes the class fun and doesn't have a ton of hard grades. Participation definitely matters though and the class is pretty small in a small classroom.

best professor I have ever taken. He is so caring about his students and wants you to do well in the class! He is very passionate about the readings and wants you to be as well. He is very funny and made class enjoyable to come to. He is very easy to access outside of class and will work with you. Take him if you can I promise you won't regret it!

He is an incredible teacher, extremely kind, and willing to help even with other English classes. Usual book readings with a couple of comics and songs. No quizzes. Fun class and engaging discussion. He is not a hard greater but gives good feedback. Readings are not difficult and if they are, he goes over them during class. I highly recommend him.
Frequently 10 to 20 mins late to class. Does not grade assignments until the last minute.

Absolute stud. Great personality, funny jokes. A lot of the assignments are completion, at least for us this semester. Interesting stories, can get dark at times. Don't take if you're a soft person. Either way, really fun class, just make sure to read and talk in class. Hopefully this exam doesn't totally wreck me, but theres nothing we can do.

Love him. He does in class writings after books are finished but they aren't bad. he is funny and his classes go by quick. would def take again- no computers in class but taking notes in notebook is beneficial but also not the end of the world if u dont take notes one day.

Professor Hermes is so nice, intelligent, and genuinely wants the best for his students. You get 5 absences to use as you please, which is nice. A lot of reading throughout the week, but it's not bad. Keep up w the readings, get ready to participate in the discussion & you'll do fine! Plus, most of the grades were completion grades anyway!

Dr. Hermes is kind and inspiring. It's a lot of work at first, but once I got used to it, it became the class I look forward to the most this semester. The round table conversation is thought provoking and really enjoyable.
Barely grades, not sure he even read anything, doesn't have a kind sense of humor, bad teacher.

Took this course over January term and absolutely loved it. I could not have asked for a better professor to spend those two weeks with. His feedback was always very thoughtful and constructive, and by the end of the course I could see how much my writing had improved. The class was engaging, and he truly cared about my experience. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: If you don't want to know ur grade until they are posted for the semester in my.smu, take him. He loved to talk about creepy and inappropriate content in our class. We read disturbing texts and he was raunchy when I went to office hours. He makes u print EVERYTHING and loves to "joke" in a hateful manner. I don't think he looked at my final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mr. Hermes is a great teacher, he is super nice and cares about everyone in his class. He does expect you to talk in class, and you HAVE to come prepared (meaning you have read the stories). If you like teachers who generally love what they do, and want to hear what you think about these topics, then this is the teacher for you. I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He values participation in class discussions and will get frustrated if the class doesn't participate in them. If you're struggling, he's pretty good at accomadating your needs. He can be a little frustrating at times, but if you engage in his disscussions, do the readings and laugh at a few of his jokes, you should get a B or higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: he grades at the very last minute, super rude and will target people he doesn't like, shows up to class 10 minutes late every class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love him! His insights on our story discussions are really helpful and his sense of humor will make you smile

Prof. Hermes changed my life, literally. He believed in me when I didn't believe in myself. He truly saw us as people and not just as students. Amazing lectures, and I grew so much as a writer with his feedback. Overall a fantastic teacher!

Major assignments were not discussed clearly. 
He said he will be accessible outside of class but rarely answers emails.
When feedback is given, it is not very helpful and office hours did not benefit any. 
Assignments are not graded until after the final exam. 
A LOT of reading but some of them were fun to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hermes makes class enjoyable to come to every day. Our discussions are always enlightening. He helps everyone to feel like we know each other. It's a lot of reading but the books he chose are interesting. He's really good at helping everyone analyze them and see connections. He was also very kind when I was struggling.

Amazing professor! I learned more about writing than I have in my whole college career. A very challenging class, but thought provoking. He genuinely cares about students and created an environment where everyone feels respected.

Class periods were a waste of time. Anything worth more than a completion grade was not discussed clearly. I spent hours each week reading and the writing assignments hurt my grade the most. He doesn't input grades until the last day so there is nothing you can do by then and his feedback, while good, was useless by the time you receive it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hermes is a great professor both in and outside of the class, but this class has a TON of reading. You're expected to read 30-50 pages before each class, which gets exhausting and hard to keep up with as you move through the semester. Takes forever to grade, but is an easy grader which helps a lot. If you hate reading, probably avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a great professor that truly cares about his students and wants them to do well. There is a lot of work, but it is mostly writing fiction stories which can be fun. Put in the effort and you will be rewarded. Took as a may term and had great, fun class discussions, but definitely lots of work.

Professor Hermes is kind, funny, and passionate about the subject he teaches. However, this class will probably be a lot more work compared to other SMU CW professors. Worth it if you have time in your schedule. Not a hard grader. Intriguing workshop discussions. You get out what you put into the class.

Professor Hermes is a super nice dude, but his class can also feel like a burden. There is a lot of reading required on you and he might be the slowest grader I have ever had! Overall if you show that you care you will get a good grade in this class.

Professor Hermes is the best. Super relaxed dude and always fun in class. definitely take any course of his. Not the fastest grader, but an easy one so it's worth it. If you do take his course, always participate and it will help you out.

While I certainly wasn't expecting the workload received for this class, I do think it's been worthwhile. I feel I've learned a lot as a writer, thanks to the great feedback given by the professor and although I think some of the course load could be reduced, it's mostly been a fun experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: For an introduction level class I was expecting far less work. Be prepared for a writing assignment every class. He will call you out if you do not participate. I turned in a writing portfolio in September worth 20% of my grade. It is now almost December and I still have not received a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kind of hard to understand her lectures, but the material is not hard to learn yourself at all. She litterally tells you exactly what questions will be on the exam too.
She didn't even teach real accounting.

went from Amy's class last semester to this one for managerial. WORST DECISION EVER. This woman has no idea how to teach. None of what she "teaches" in class matches what a REAL accounting course is meant to teach. I feel like i've fallen too far behind because this woman does not go by the textbook - she makes up her own type of accounting.
Suffering in Intermediate as she gave me a false outlook of what accounting is. Take Altizer or Hamirani to be better prepared and get the education you are paying for.

This professor is undoubtedly the worst at our school, with a dismissive and sarcastic attitude towards students who she doesn't like. She is the most unorganized professor I have ever seen, is consumed by acronyms that are not consistent in the field, and can't teach.
Do not take her, she will not prepare you for intermediate and you will be in a world of pain like I was. You've been warned.

Biggest regret. Going to be so unprepared for Intermediate Accounting now. It is a lot of acronyms that are not that applicable. Thought this class was an easy A but you weirdly have to work backward and get on her good side for an A.
Very compassionate teacher, lecture heavy but the practice problems she does in class are similar to test and quiz problems. Gives random, but beneficial extra credit. Unrelated: she's a fashion icon

She's the absolute sweetest. LHR's a wonderful professor who gives you the tools and resources to succeed and made accounting seem interesting with her various acronyms and study guides. She really wants her students to do well and has a good sense of humor about things. TAKE HER!! SHE'S THE ABSOLUTE BEST!!

TAKE HER! She is the sweetest lady who truly wants nothing but the best for all of her students. She is a very fair grader and will work with you if you are struggling. Taking her for a whole year (2301 and 2302) convinced me to switch from finance to accounting major! She is the best professor Cox has to offer.
Great professor! Has three tests, a group project, and a final. Is very willing to give extra credit if you go to office hours and show you care.

LHR has a very unique, and at times confusing, teaching style. She has helpful memorization techniques to help you grasp accounting easily. She curves a ton and is an easy grader, but there's lots of grades. More importantly, I have NEVER met a more caring professor in my life. LHR is a tremendously hard worker and amazingly genuine. TAKE HER!

She is awesome! Has office hours every single day, makes herself accessible by giving her personal cell number out so that students can text/call her if they have questions. Her lectures are easy to understand and she's very considerate with grades. She'll bump your grade. There's one group project - easy A if you start early (it's a lot of work)

Hickman-Riggs is very passionate about her students and wants you to do well. Some of the ways she teaches the later content can be confusing, you have to teach yourself some of it, but communicating with her and showing you care goes a long way. Would highly recommend taking her because she is extremely knowledgable in her field.

You should definitely take Hickman-Riggs. She is the most caring professor I have had here. The material is not difficult, but it is not easy either. An A is very possible to make, but you do need to put the time in. 3 online quizzes, 3 in class quizzes, 2 midterms, and a noncumulative final! takes attendance
Absolute beast. She teaches solely for the fun of it and cares deeply about your success. Easily one of the best teachers at SMU. Take her if you can

THE BEST PROFESSOR SMU HAS!! She is the best and nicest accounting teacher. Do not even read any further or think about it but take her!!! It is not hard the class is interesting and she is an amazing professor!

LHR is the best professor I've had at SMU by far. Not only is she a great teacher but she also cares about her students as individuals. She wants her students to succeed and achieve their goals. I could not possibly recommend her more.

LHR is THE BEST! She is so sweet and caring of all of her students. I got a A+ in her class with curves on every exam. She wants you to do well, and is extremely kind. She is wonderful and should be taken over any other ACCT professor at SMU

Took her class during the summer and absolutely loved it. She genuinely cares about her "scholars" and will do everything she can to help you succeed. Whether she's giving extra credit or tutoring in office hours she has a passion for the subject. She also understands her class is some people's last shot at Cox and tries to help you earn the grade.

Tough Course, caring teacher. Professor Hickman-Riggs acknowledges that the subject of accounting doesn't come to everyone, which is why she is so caring and accessible outside of class. If you are struggling in her class, do not hesitate to communicate with her via text or pop into office hours for a one on one lesson. online quizzes and 2 exams

Go to all classes and office hours! She is known to care a lot about students. If you show you are invested in this class, she will be invested in you. Material is hard, reading the book makes it easier. Make this class a priority because it is difficult, but one of the best professors to have for this course.

Great Professor. She gives lectures off of powerpoints and posts them online. You don't really need the book. Her powerpoints teach you everything  you need to know. Tests are simple if you come to class and pay attention.
She is the best teacher ever and is truly invested in each one of her "scholars". She will make you better prepared for a career in accounting than any other possessor.
Best professor you will ever have. Put in the effort and she takes it into consideration more than any other teacher.  SMU is lucky to have her.

I am in love with her she is the best teacher and REALLY wants her students to do well. Tests are hard but she is fair and will curve if necessary.  Attendance is mandatory but there is no HW. Cried on the last day of class--she really does care about her students and she comes up with her own methods to hard topics in the class.  GREAT teacher!

I had her for 2301 and 2302. BEsT professor I have had at SMU hands down. I made A's in both of her courses. You have to work and come prepared but she is so helpful if you go to her office hours. LOVE her!!!!

While she believes that she is the best teacher you will ever have at SMU, she is not. Her test are impossible and you will always run out of time. She teaches out of the book but never touches on topics fully. Do not take this professor I had an A- in ACCT 2301 and worked half as much. I currently have a B-. Take another professor and get an A.

Be ready to read and write. Essays basically every week with a big cumulative essay every three or so weeks. Essays are graded harshly if you don't include at least one quote from every reading, textbook chapter, and something from your lecture notes. If you are not taking him for honors credit, take Mueller instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was the most work I've had in my entire life. The writing in one week was more than a cumulative essay in other classes. All I would do for this class is write, write, read tons, and write more. He's not a bad guy, the workload is just insane. I would never wish this class upon my worst enemy. This class is not worth it/take the other section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. I have learned so much in this class. Pretty much, 3 papers make or break your grade. Yet, you are assigned reading memos, which he gives great feedback. Using that feedback, for papers, combine them into a flowing paper and submit that. Always aim for the max writing count, not a terrible grader. Also writing was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was a scam. Just linked constant reading then graded our essays like we were applying to grad school unless you redid them all and ain't got time for that. The workload is obscene, gave off serious “I hate my life” energy and projected it onto every student.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely not. He's ridiculous to think his workload is even slightly reasonable. He's unorganized and assigned thing that we're never covered. His papers are absurd. He is useless when asking for paper guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and can be pretty accommodating but this is the most unreasonable amount of work I have ever had in my life. So much reading, weekly essays, giant research paper, and more. No computers in class. Pretty much unmanageable on top of other classes. Will give you an extension at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent, passionate, and very understanding professor. He frequently engages with students in lectures and is available in and outside of class. The reading is a bit too much and very dense so its best to read throughout the week or get good at speedreading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Absurd workload and doesn't seem to know what he is doing. Part of being an educator is knowing how to curate material, not just throw everything at us.

I'm sad about the negative comments. He's one of the most understanding professors I've had. Yes, his lectures can feel boring, and he doesn't allow laptops, but he's so lenient with late assignments and lets you rewrite essays for full credit. I've taken 3 classes with him and was happy every time. Try, and you'll do well!
Speaks condescending to you if you ask a question, remarkable unclear in all that he does, class lectures are nonsensical and unprepared ahead of time, not fit to be a teacher.

Yes, it's a lot of reading, but he goes over everything in the lectures. Really kind, caring, and smart. You'll learn a lot if you just try a little.  His intro classes are easy and his upper-level classes have a very typical workload. Amazing person and professor.
This guy has got to be kidding with the workload. Stay away unless you think your gpa is a joke and something to be f'd with.
not as nice as he pretends to be when it comes to final grades, wouldn't even listen to me when i had a family emergency, assigned unreasonable amounts of work
nice guy but awful professor with unreasonable expectorations, not worth the stress at all, take something else trust me

Humanely impossible to complete this course and i also found the guy not as "nice" as he seems, he intentionally threw a paper back at me when I didn't do well and laughed at other student's papers in office hours when the students weren't around, completely unprofessional and unreal in expectations, find another course or drop the minor like i am.

Weekly papers and 4 10+ papers due throughout the semester. Over 100 pages of reading every week. Content in the lectures barely covers the assigned readings. Overall, you can tell prof Takeuchi wants you to learn, but it is a very extensive workload. This is one of the most stress-inducing classes I've taken at SMU

you are expected to read an impossible amount of reading and he doesn't even effectively cover the material in other ways and i don't think he is the "nice" guy that everyone thinks he is. he was blatantly rude to me when i asked for clarification in office hours and belittled two students in my class behind their backs

Look you can be ok guy and horrible professor. Reviews not based on teaching ability, which is terrible. He's not that nice either, people just assume him so.
