reviews.comment: The class was easy, even though I'm an international student. He was always available to help me during his office hours. If you try and show that you care by going to his office hours or engaging in class, he will appreciate it. I recommend professor Hiltz.
boring

I highly recommend against taking this professor. The class boiled down to him going over slides; his quizzes/tests consisting entirely of memorizing specific concepts and terms word for word. Near the end of the semester I could've cared less about the class or the content we were learning. Don't take it unless you want a bore-fest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst and most boring teacher I have ever had. Only take this class if you want to waste 3 hours a week coming to a lecture that will put you to sleep in 5 minutes. Everything "taught" in this could be  figured out by flipping through the readings, and all of his tests/quizzes consist of memorizing over-complicated definitions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the worst professor and class I have ever experienced. Has no assignments to help course grade throughout the year other than a couple tests and quizzes. Lectures the entire time, is rude to students, and acts like he never cares about anything other than himself. Never ever take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, disrespectful teacher.  As long as you never talk, you will do just fine.

The worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. he is so rude and disrespectful. Students are barely able to ask questions because he interrupts because he doesn't care. Class is so beyond boring, he's a horrible teacher and makes the content so much more confusing. Grade is based on 3 tests & final. The points taken off for tests are absurd
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He has a sign in sheet for attendance everyday so you can't skip class. If you don't keep up with the readings you'll be very confused during his lectures. He doesn't let other students participate or ask questions during class and his lectures are very boring. It's an interesting subject though and I enjoyed it.

He doesnt care about his students at all. He is rude every time you approach him with questions. He assigns homework that you will spend hours on just for it not to go into your grade at the end of the semester. He will never admit he is wrong even though he continuously makes stuff up. My only advice is do not take his class.

The class is very boring and goes on tangents. Canvas is super confusing and hard to understand. He never admits he is wrong either. Make sure you do good on the quizzes because that's all you're graded on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class a really long time ago in the summer and it was mind-numbingly boring. He doesn't allow anyone to talk in class, but just talks over you. Think of "The Dude" from the Big Lebowski, only not interesting and much more arrogant, and you have Professor Hiltz.

This class is composed of lectures, quizes, one essay, and two exams. The lectures are boring and often include tangents. There is little to no participation from students during class. Alot of reading is required and the books and articles are not interesting. Canvas page is confusing and unclear and it is difficult to find information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take someone else if you can. Incredibly rude to students and talks at you, not to you. He barely knows how to use canvas, you have to search around to find homework or any info. Makes rude and weird comments about other people and lectures in the most monotone voice. Doesn't involve students in lectures, literally doesn't care about kids at all.

If you arent a fan of politics in class, I would keep away. That said, Im not critical of his views; I just dont think it is class appropriate. He makes you work for everything. You pretty much get a quiz per week. He gets angry if people dont ask him questions, but when you do ask, he has a tendency to shame you for not knowing the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester, he started off being pretty good and helping out a lot. The fact that this is my first time rating a professor shows a lot about what I've been going through with this class. He honestly gets distracted while teaching forgets what he was saying. All of the grades are quizzes and 2 very hard exams. Get ready to read
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: yo this professor is so rude, mans acting like we dont have other things to deal with outta school. he strict as hell anyways he completely shames you if u miss like one class. He makes you feel like a complete idiot. So anyways warning: try to avoid this professor as much as u can. Spare yourself. Word out.

I think the reviews are pretty indicative. Some very interesting material at times, but presented in the most boring way possible. First few quizzes were very tough, but once you get to know his style in the questions they aren't too bad. He is available often, it's just the class itself is quite the bore.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Deserves the low ratings, talks on and on with no interaction, doesn't answer questions and makes you feel dumb when you ask anything, never is in his office hours, and could not be more boring. Uses the same quizzes, so get them from someone and you'll do fine if you don't die from boredom first.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not deserve the low rating, he expects participation and people to do the homework. If you do the minimal homework (15-30 minutes of reading per class) and pay attention in class you will get good grades, he will respect you, and the class will be an easy grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took his class in summer online. If you zone out you're screwed, but if you take good notes you're good. I stopped doing the readings after the first week and did well. His notes/lectures are comprehensive, but make sure to read and listen closely. Read carefully on the quizzes but they're straight from his Canvas notes. Fair grader on papers (2)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shocked to see how low his ratings are. For political/social the midterm, final paper and quizzes are each a third of your grade. Never read the assigned readings and didn't have any problems. Provides detailed notes on the readings and lectures. I can see how some might not like his persona, he's quirky but he's insanely smart and caring guy.

Prof. Hiltz was constantly disrespectful and rude to his students. Would show up late to office hours, and he got mad at us when we didn't ask questions, but if you did, he would just say that you would already know the answer if you paid more attention. A super easy A, but so rude to his students, so don't expect an understanding professor

Probably the most arrogant professor you'll run into in the philosophy department. Says lectures are discussion-based but we've had maybe two all year. Guy definitely loves to hear himself talk and doesn't really care all that much about the students. The class itself isn't hard, but he makes it significantly harder than it needs to be

love this guy. real gem and gets a bad rep bc hes kinda pretentious but not rlly in a bad way, just in a "i went to Princeton and studied a non-subject" kind of way. but a hella chill guy if u show up

Great teacher, who really cares. If you actually do the reading and go to class you will do well. Makes it easy to do well if you put in the work. Teaches interesting stuff and actually knows what hes talking about. He loves participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are confusing and boring, but he posts documents on Canvas that summarize the main points. Reading is manageable and the material is relatively interesting. Weekly quizzes on the readings, midterm, final, and one research paper. He is a fair grader. Attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT take his class for an essay A. Hard grader, no sympathy for grammar. ALL definitions on quizzes and test must be word for word or you get points off. Very lecture heavy, must read textbooks or you wont pass. very opinionated and biased, towards apposing views. Midterm , final essay project ( individual), Final like midterm and essay Q.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: hes fine, kind of annoying but if you show up and review a little you'll get a good grade. no pop quizzes he tells you when everything will be, and we had one test and then test 2&3 were the final and no papers or homework besides the quizzes. never read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty easy professor, I took him 3 times and got A-'s each time. If you read, the quizzes (almost always true/false) aren't hard and he's a very fair grader when it comes to papers. The only thing that keeps me from giving him a 5 is that he talks over people when they try to ask questions or contribute to the discussion - it's really annoying
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hiltz was not a very tough professor. He just expects you to be accountable of your education and to put effort in the class (the usual). You do have to read carefully and take notes, but it's manageable. I recommend study groups or flashcards to study. The quizzes prepare you well for the tests and do not get behind in your readings!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found his lectures engaging and interesting. DO THE READINGS! they're really helpful, especially when studying for quizzes. As long as you read and go to the lectures the quizzes are easy, but he is a tough grader. Available for help outside of class. sometimes goes on tangents but you get through the material you need to in time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is super boring! Lectures always put me to sleep, but his class isn't hard especially if you know someone who had him before to help you with quizzes. He assigns a lot of reading, but you can get away with just notes from lecture if you pay attention. The way he does grades is weird with only one test and lots of quizzes during the semester.

Hiltz expects you to do the readings and actually think about the material covered. When that doesn't happen, he knows. People are quick to judge, but as long as you apply yourself and question things, it's really not hard to do well in his class.

Hiltz is a really nice guy. His class can get boring (especially beginning half) he is very long winded and is old school (writes on a chalkboard, no technology in class). He is a very fair grader for the 8 mini quizzes and 2 tests. The wording can be tricky but if you study the reading and his lecture notes you should be good! He curves!

Professor Hiltz is a great professor, and is definitely a good choice for someone taking an intro to philosophy course. The course is heavily based on the readings he assigns, but he thoroughly explains them during lecture. There are t/f reading quizzes for every essay, and his wording is a bit tricky, but not impossible. Best part is, no essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's okay. The material is pretty interesting although the readings aren't always. He gets up on a soap box a lot.
Hes super boring... the whole class is literally him just blabbering on about philosophy. He really does care about the topic and is willing to help you, but I wouldn't say this is my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: While it is evident that Hiltz is very knowledgeable when it comes to the material, his lectures are not at all clear. Personally, when I ask a question, I come away flustered and unmotivated to engage with the material. The lectures are mainly chalk talks with hardly any opportunity for interaction. When asking questions, I am usually interrupted
If you're really into it, then he's good. Test ain't that hard tbh. He has two tests only. You need to keep alot of track on what he's doing!

You've got to pay attention and keep up for an A.  Readings challenge you and you will need to think about the content to understand the concepts--simply reading and walking away won't allow you to fully understand material.  Ask questions and participate in class and you'll get helpful clarity/feedback.  Good guy but not an easy A.

This was my favorite class this semester and that says a lot coming from a biology major. His lectures are super interesting and insightful. If you show up to class, copy the notes on the board, and do the readings as he asks, you'll be good for an A. In my opinion, people who don't do well in his class overthink it and study too intensely.

Took it as an intro type class but he taught it more like an advanced class.  He spent more time talking and comparing poker and gambling to philosophy so the Gamblers Fallacy was interesting.  Attendance was mandatory. Avoid if possible

Hiltz is super confusing. Everything he says is a riddle that you have to try to figure out. He does not know how to explain the info in simpler terms if you need help. His quizzes are not hard if you pay attention, but his midtermfinal papers are a bit difficult.

Hiltz was a really great professor to take because he gave 3 test all semester, had no final, and gave easy quizzes. If you show up and take notes on the lecture, you'll be prepared for the quizzes, and his grading scale is super lax too. Definitely recommend!

By far the worst instructor I have EVER had!!! I went to him during office hours and was told to ask any questions I have during class, so do not go to him for help because he will NOT help you what so ever! His grading does not mathematically make sense! HE makes up quizzes and does not even know the correct answers.

He doesn't really care too much about his students. He doesn't do anything to aid success. All of his lectures are highly opinionated and leaves no room for discussion. He would rather flaunt his philosophy knowledge than make sure his students are learning.  His lectures are dead boring. However, the tests aren't that bad and he doesn't grade hard

Recommending the Taos course. Philosophy in Taos? No brainer! Take it! It's not much different than other PHIL courses. Show up, read the assigned material, show any bit of interest whatsoever and discuss in class. Notice it's an 'upper level' PHIL course, so do stay away if you're not into philosophy. He was way more helpful than other profs...

I took his course in Taos, and I was one of 3 students in the class. He helped me with an essay, yet he gave me a C on it, which dropped my A to a B. I worked so hard for this class...and I didn't get the grade I earned. He does not help you if you need an A & you try. The course was 17 days, class 3 hours a day. SO BORING. too much reading.

Givin 8 quizzes a semester. Easy to earn at least 90 If you take the notes n. do assigned reading. I was too lazy to read the book, so didn't do well in reading part of 6 quizzes. I got 91 and 100 for the rest 2 quizzes when well-prepared. 1 independent project relate to videos and theories we've learnt. 1 midterm, and 1 final with an essay.

With hiltz, there are 3 or 4 homework assignments that he doesn't change each semester. IF you have a friend that took the class, look at their tests for review. all you have to do is memorize some vocal words and have someone sign you in on the attendance sign in sheet. Its an easy A if you put in a little effort

He is not a good professor at all. He is least interested in his teaching. He has only 2 tests and 2 papers, which does not allow room for improvement. No discussions, boring class. Don't take him unless you have to.

Rambles a lot. Refuses to explain what will be on test due to the fact that he "never had that privilege". Takes attendance. Class participation is 10% of the grade and if he doesn't like your opinion he will mock you in class. As long as you read EVERYTHING he assigns and try to speak up a few times you should be fine.

I don't understand what people are complaining about.Yes, the class is boring, but I don't think thats the professors fault. The subject is what is boring. He's approachable and will be more than happy to clarify things for student when they don't understand something.
The best course I took at SMU

Takes attendance every class.  Rants about us being late but shows up 5 min late every day.  Grade comes from two tests and a final, which aren't hard if you know what to study, but don't count on any help from him.  Class is so boring, and he talks in circles about nothing.
Boring lectures. Rambles a lot. Considered himself an easy grader but if you don't memorize what he writes on the board word for word you get points off on your tests.

I love Prof. Hiltz!  Be sure to take one of his classes.  Don't pay much attention to the whining from those non-majors who took his Business Ethics class.  Hiltz is easily one of my favorite professors at SMU.

Business ethics with Hiltz is awful. Class is VERY boring. Only grades in the class are two huge tests, final, and a research paper. He was fired as a University of Phoenix teacher... Don't take his class

Professor Hiltz really isn't as bad as everyone on here has made him out to be. The class is very easy to get an A in and the quizzes are NOT hard. All you have to do is show up for class, take notes, and read (but you don't even have to do all of the assigned reading to do well in the class). Don't let these reviews on here scare you. It was easy.
Horrible class.  He does not explain his thoughts clearly. Class is extremely boring and you will fall asleep. 8 pop quizzes and they are hard. He loves True/False.

This class was dreadful!  It was not interesting and the content was interesting but the was the professor taught it made the class miserable.  The class includes pop quizzes, two tests, and a 8-10 page paper.  I got an A still but had NO idea what my grade was going to be until final grades were posted.  I would not recommend this teacher!
Practical Reasoning-never met a less helpful uninterested professor. also seems VERY uneducated on subject.

Easy A if you attend the class and listen, his lectures are extremely dry though. For tests I just studied my lecture notes and made high A's, but you have to do some reading for the papers which are not too bad. If you get it done you should be fine. Multiple choice tests, feeds you what he wants in your papers.

Very nice guy but does not demand much of students - which shows in the class test average (C+). If you keep up with readings, you'll be fine. 1300 is an easy course. Prof Hiltz uses Fox News as his whipping-boy but ironically, he utilizes many of the rhetorical devices in class he claims to despise
brutal.

Unless you love philosophy...do not take this class. He talks at you for 50 minutes about the most boring things. He does not help you understand what will be on the tests at all. He merely says "anything we've covered is fair game, and no, i will not give you a review sheet"

uhmm good guy. some of the stuff he talks about will go right over your head and you won't understand. but it is philosophy afterall. doing ok got a b in his class. alot of reading. try and keep up. a couple little papers at the end and an exam. class is so boring.

Not a terrible professor but if you're a conservative/republican, you will not like this guy. Constantly throws out his left-wing liberal views. actually does want you to get an A though. READ THE BOOK.

I got an A in Business Ethics, my lowest grade in the class was a 98. If you work hard and ACTUALLY give the class some effort you can do well. Others in my class did poorly or average and hated it but they also didnt study for tests. He wants you to memorize some definitions word for word, and doing so helps answer his other questions correctly.

he is not a great professor. He doesn't know how to explain things in a way that REGULAR-NOT-PH.D.-HOLDING people will understand or care about. His essay quizzes are bad because half the class doesn't understand what he wants. The only good thing is understands that he is not a good professor so he lets you redo it.

He's an okay teacher. Talks in circles, class is soooo boring. Didn't read the book all semester but would read the chapter summaries and class notes before tests. Only had 2 tests whole year, no quizzes, and one 6 page paper that's pretty easy to bs. Only take if you plan on going to class bc he takes role almost everyday!

hes a pretty damned goood teacher. attendance is mandatory..he gives pop quizes, but u can miss 2 and it wont count against u..the tests are prettyt easy...most people get b's....theres some reading but its all preety basic...hes better than the other bus ethics teacher and plus u dont have to write any papers.
Very difficult, but challenging subject.  This is Hiltz's favorite class, and it shows.  Great recommendation for anybody looking to be challenged.
I didn't enjoy this class at all.  The subject matter only concerned the ethics of war, and I was expecting a much different class with a larger variety of topics.

This class involves constant reading, and if you dont keep up then you'll pull a C at best.  He speaks in circles and way too fast to understand most of the time.  Tests aren't too tough, but the true/false can definitely trip you up because his wording is ridiculous.  He can be funny sometimes.

The first half of the course is extremely boring, but it picks up at the end when the material becomes interesting. His quizes are a bit tricky, T or F stuff as well is his tests, but overall this class is pretty easy and if you keep up with the reading you'll be fine. He's also a funny guy at times
He is very nice and his class is fairly easy if you pay attention, but he is so out there and makes weird sexual comments....
Awesome teacher. He makes the issues we discuss very interesting and always has great stories. The quizzes are tough and so are the tests, but not that bad if you study. Hes awesome.
Take this guy for business ethics
No Comments
good teacher, but not a lot of grades in the end, so less chances to mess up. he gets pretty into it, so he doesn't cover everything he puts on the sylabus.
Interesting and Intelligent Professor. Tests Challenging but Graded Liberally

Fall 2016 was her first Honors section so the first half of the course was pretty jumbled and unclear. However after the first wave of reviews went up, she really took those criticisms to heart and has become more clear in her discussions, essays, and expectations. She is a very caring and happy person who will soon become an excellent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person who wants to help you do well with writing. Very tough grader in the honor's English class and is willing to let you rewrite essays for a possibility of a better grade but be warned, they are very difficult and time consuming. Overall class was enjoyable at times and not so enjoyable at other times..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's a caring person but a tough grader, similar to most English teachers. She's sometimes jumbled with deadlines, but also is considerate about pushing certain assignments back if you talk to her. Classes are always spent discussing the current work, but it's still important to do heavy reading of the texts on your own because it's tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Ms. Hinton is a great person, however her class is pretty unplanned and doesn't follow the calendar. She is someone who outside of class would be a good person to know, but isn't the best as a teacher. Interesting grader, but she does her best to give you good feedback and chances to raise your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Hinton is a kind and caring person, but is disorganized and does not clearly specify what assignments are due when. Her expectations of papers are also somewhat muddled. I would recommend taking this course from another instructor.

Ms. Hinton is a HORRIBLE teacher. She doesn't use Canvas so you never know what you are supposed to read before class, she grades essays without setting clear directions/guidelines (which leads to horrible results), and she will give you advise on a paper, tell you it's great and ready for submission and still give you a low grade. DO NOT TAKE HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Hoedebeck is great. She gave super clear instructions and was extremely kind.
Such a sweet and understanding professor. The class is pretty easy itself so if you do whats requiered its and easy A
joke of a class and program

One of the best professors I've had at SMU, knowledgeable in the field but also laid back in the classroom. Expects you to do the work, but is a reasonable grader if the work is completed on time. The brutal part about her class is the presentations, but that's not on her. She will let you miss class if you tell her ahead of time.

Amazing teacher! Super nice and understanding. Very fun and keeps lessons upbeat. Class does have the COX curve so she does have to be strict on grading per COX criteria but she gives a bunch of extra credit and explains how to get a good grade well.

She is very nice and approachable but also a tough grader. Encourages participation and questions but makes it easy to get points. Class is not a ton of work but too much for a 2 hour class imo. Reading assignments take long if actually done, 2nd and 3rd presentations are decently big projects. Overall nice teacher but not a blowoff class.

Overall very nice person and a good teacher, tough grader but if you review the rubrics and meet all those requirements you will do well. Lots of reading homework but not that many people actually do it. Also provides an extra credit opportunity at the end of the semester.

Hoedebeck was a good professor with engaging lectures, but there were some assignments where the instructions weren't very clear. She's a tough grader, but as long as you spend time on your presentations, getting an A is not too difficult.

She is a really good professor and a great person. This class really helped me develop my public speaking skills. Her lectures are engaging, and you can tell that she cares about her students. It is true that she is a tough grader, but as long as you have writing and speaking skills you should be fine.
Nice teacher and has pretty decent lectures but grading is super unclear and overly harsh for no reason.

Professor Hoedebeck is a tough grader but she makes her expectations clear. Make sure to follow her exact guidelines for assignments and you'll be fine. Her quizzes are very specific to the books she assigns so be careful of that. Overall, she cares about her students and tries to make lectures engaging.

Solid teacher, but tough grading. On the writing assignments, everyone in my class got a A-/B+. The criteria for presentations is pretty clear, but it's still hard to get a high grade on them. Besides that, she is passionate about her class and I enjoyed her classes. (You only need a 92 to get an A with the extra credit so it's not too difficult)

Review for BLI 1210: She taught 1210 for the first time and you could tell she wasn't used to teaching freshman. She is an amazing teacher and person and you really have to work hard for an A in her class. Going to office hours, practicing, and showing up to class on time are key to getting an A.

There is a lot of work pretty much all semester long. You will learn a lot of important information, but it's all coupled with homework. The quizzes are easy; the essay tests can save your grade if you write well; the presentations aren't as bad as you think; but your grade heavily depends on the group project all semester long.. can be good or bad
Professor Hoedebeck is a tough grader. The Career Management of the portion of the class had lots of assignments with short deadlines. She's a good professor, not exceptional.

BLI, in general, is a really unnecessary course, but Prof Hoedebeck makes it less unbearable. Lectures are a waste of time because the content is common sense, but she's really caring towards students and provides great feedback on grades. Group project is a lot of work but she really tries to help students succeed. Lot of busy work homework.

Probably one of my favorite professors. She's very sweet and the work that she gives isn't too hard. The career management portion of her class is annoying with short deadlines, but overall she is a great and sweet professor.

People come into this class with a wide range of skills, and Hoedebeck does a great job of getting everyone the information they need to be successful. Appears like an easy class but since it's Cox you still have to put in effort for an A. Take this professor to learn something!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class, in general, is filled with so much meaningless information. Presentations are the only real skill you could learn/improve on. Sad that it is required. Hoedebeck herself is a nice person but is so beholden to the curriculum that it ruins the class. As a result, everything is graded unnecessarily hard and the grades are weighted terribly.

Professor Hoedebeck is a great person that's for sure. But her class, well it eventually comes down to a lot of busy work. Don't slack off at the beginning because you will not get an A. The class is based off of tiny quizzes from the textbook, but it is simple and you wont honestly use the book at all. Write good. She is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: You definitely have to work for an A in this class. Nothing is necessarily hard, it just requires a lot of time. Hoedebeck is very personable and always willing to answer questions. Take the time to get to know her; it definitely makes a difference in this class.

Take Hoedebeck for BLI. The class is annoying no matter which professor you take and Hoedebeck tries to make it bearable. For all BLI teachers, it is hard to make a solid A due to the curriculum but based off of what I've heard about other professors, Hoedebeck seems the most reasonable. She's nice and personable and makes you a better presenter.

Professor Hoedebeck takes monotonous course material and makes it applicable to undergraduate students. BLI is a difficult class by nature, but Hoedebeck makes sure to have clear expectations, and, as a result, grades fair to performance. If you are receptive to feedback and adhere to course material, you will do well in this class.

Easy class, graded super hard to make up for it. Wouldnt recommend her, she normally teaches MBA classes and was pulled down to teach undergrad. Overall the class content was real-world based but would recommend taking someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It's possible to make an A in the class if you put the work in. Presentations are hard to make an A on but it is easy to do well in the rest of the class. The BLI curriculum is a lot of work in general and is going to be pretty uniform for all teachers. I recommend Hoedebeck because she is super nice and I honestly got better at presenting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's chill. Required kind of boring class, but it's nice to have an easy A esp since class does not meet every time. All the BLI teachers are forced to have the same grading/material, but Kate is funny and knows this class isn't the end of the world. My presentations have gotten way better. Highly recommend

Nice lady.  Attendance is strictly mandatory.  The material is not very substantive (everything just seems like common sense) and she makes class a fun and talkative atmosphere.
