If uses this site called Piazza to answer questions we have and it's useless. If you ask him a question about something he will tell you to look at the homework problems and in class assignments. Very un resourceful. Not sure why SMU hasn't done anything about this. Just listen to the students!! Do not take this class, take anyone else if you can.

Horrible professor. On the first day more than half the class dropped. It is now December and there is only about 15-20 students. He cannot teach, reads off slides, does not give extra credit even though he is allowed to. Does a different grading system. I am on the verge of failing and I go to his office hours frequently. Worst teacher ever.

I wouldn't recommend taking this professor without having taken AP/IB Chemistry in high school. The tests have have huge time constraints, though doing the homework and in-class problems, especially the math-based ones, will really help with your test-taking skills.

This class was hard material as it is, but the professor definitely made it 10x as hard. The tests are curved but the average was still a C. I am an A student and have finished with A's in all of my other classes. Do NOT take this professor if you can choose.

He is a really smart guy, but probably too smart to be teaching an intro chem class. The 2nd semester is significantly harder than the 1st semester (I had an A 1st semester). His slides aren't super clear and the way he works out problems is extremely confusing. Tests are really tough, and there is never enough time to finish. Going to class helps!

Werner's lectures were dry, uninspiring, and unhelpful. His policies for tests were ridiculously strict and unforgiving, leaving little room for error in his class. If I had the choice, I would've taken any other professor besides him.
BEST PROF. And when he says "youre velcome" my urge to cry vanishes.

Do not take this mans class avoid at all costs. There is very little time given for tests and chances are you will study 3 weeks for an exam and barely pass. I urge you stay clear take the other guy!!!!!! He is nice but an awful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Probably one of the hardest I have ever taken. Do all of the homework, several times, and take really detailed notes outside of class in a way you understand. I had to get a tutor and that really helped. Not easy, but possible to get a good grade if you study a lot and do the homework in the books. Also look at the answer book to get explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pain.

Prof. Horsthemke solves equations like physics problems with variables all over the place. He doesn't use dimensional analysis, so it makes talking about the tests and homework very difficult because he can't help you. Plus, there is a language barrier with his accent. I taught myself this chemistry from the textbook and youtube videos. Don't take.

Chem 1304 is already a difficult class and learning it via podcasts and confusing powerpoints sure doesn't help. I had never struggled with Chem before (got an A in Chem 1303) but this class kicked my butt. Homework and additional practice not similar to test. Also, tests are too long for the time allotted so you must work at an extremely fast pace
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Awful experience! The professor is a nice guy, but his virtual lectures are miserable. I bet his lectures are better in normal in-person times, but it did NOT work to be online. The powerpoints are bland, over-complex, and ultimately useless. My suggestion is just to ditch the lectures and only read the textbook if you want a proper understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There's no reason to go to this guys class. His lectures make no sense. His slides use different variables from the textbook he assigns. His tests are ridiculous, evidently not taking them himself. Only good thing is he curves but even then it's not enough to make up for his lack of teaching. I have never had a worse experience with a professor. NO

I still have nightmares about this class. I took AP chem in high school and did great so I expected to go into this class easily. I would send my highschool teacher pictures of homework and question and he could not even solve them. He hardly knows how to work zoom and is just all around terrrrrible. Avoid this class at all costs.....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not very clear, doesn't explain very well. Just gives you recordings so its basically self-taught chem
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horsthemke is possibly the worst teacher I've had so far. He does not teach anything and does not clearly go over how to solve any problems. His lecture slides make no sense. You're supposed to do problems before class, but he gives no understanding on how to solve them. DO NOT take his class
I want to pull out my hair when I think about this man.

I knew going into this class that it would already be difficult, given that it is Gen Chem. But this is the hardest I have ever worked for a class and I barely made a B. I had to review lessons on youtube in order to understand them even a little bit. Do the homework to practice and study every day to keep topics fresh.

This is definitely the hardest intro class you can take and this professor does not make it any easier. A lot of studying will most likely score you in the B range. Make sure to use other resources because the lectures given in class will not suffice. Not a very personable guy.

Alright. I've never had a professor whose class I have dreaded as much as this class. I relied ENTIRELY on other students here teaching me CHEM1303, when I pay for a tenured professor. The tests are nearly impossible to finish in the time provided, and often times there are 30+ point curves on tests that still end up as failing grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not very easy to follow his recorded lectures, had to study a ton more than my other classes. Chem is difficult no matter who you take it with so if he's your only option just be prepared to work a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry is already a hard class, especially for me since i never took it in high school. The professor makes the class unneccessarily difficult; his "lectures" are prerecorded podcasts where he reads off of slides and does not show how to do example problems. He has a question forum called Piazza, yet his answers are dismissive and not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I followed the schedule the professor gave at the beginning of each module I probably would have done better, He curves a lot on the tests. His quizzes are a nightmare though. If you are good at self studying and sticking to a schedule, this class is for you. Be prepared to do practice problems.

Did not like him. I had to teach myself everything and the way he explained things was absolutely terrible. I had an issue with one of the tests and lockdown browser after killing myself studying so i emailed him and he basically said tough luck. I would have understood more with any other professor.

Chem is a difficult class to begin with, so be prepared to study a lot on your own no matter who your professor is. Dr. Horsthemke's class is difficult and based mainly on test scores, but participation quizzes to count. Do the homework because test questions are usually similar. Friendly and available in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and despite what many people say he isn't hard to understand in the slightest if you pay attention and have a basic command of the English language. That said this is a hard class and if you don't put in a lot of work it is going to be rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst teacher ever. Does not teach, lecture slides make no sense, and gives you podcasts but has a heavy German accent so you cant understand them. Doesn't lecture during class either so he expects you do his four hours of lecture slides/podcasts on your own on top of all the other homework you have. if you have the option, DO NOT take this class!!

He was a nice person but this class is just rough. Don't take with other hard classes because you need to study every day. He has a thick German accent but you learn to understand him better if you go to class. When it went online, it got really difficult because he didn't hold lectures so you had to stay accountable. Definitely a weed out class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you are willing to put in the work, you will do well. There's a very clear distinction between students who work hard and students who don't in this class, but if you're willing to spend a lot of effort on it you'll pass. I found that I had to teach myself often because I don't always get his lectures. Otherwise he's nice and very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst prof I've ever had. Nice man but his teaching makes no sense. I had Dr. Son the next semester and I was able to understand harder topics with so much more ease. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horsthemke is a genius and is actually really nice, but his class is impossible. It is as if he is too smart to teach this to college students. I felt like I understood every unit really well but still ended with C's and B's on tests(with big curves). I could not follow the way he taught material and essentially had to learn through the textbook
Helpful in office hours. Tests have normalization curve. To do well do the hw atleast 2 times and practice problems he gives at least 2 times.

I ended up dropping this class because it was too much. He is a sweet guy, but his lectures are dull and it is hard to grasp concepts since he flys through the slides and his thick accent doesn't help either. You are going to have to teach yourself everything. Good luck, you'll need it if you take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horstemke's been teaching for a while, but that doesn't make this class any easier. His thick German accent makes it slightly harder to understand the already complex subject matter. Your grade is determined entirely by four tests (2 MC/2 FRQ) and a final, so don't expect any homework or extra credit. Expect a LOT of self-teaching and studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry is hard no matter who you take it from. He is a boring teacher though and makes chemistry miserable to sit through and learn. Lots of tests that make up your whole grade.

Sweet man but not a great teacher. This is a pretty standard chem class... test average fell between 50-60 with no curve. I went to lectures and would walk out feeling like I had absorbed nothing due to his dull lectures and boring powerpoints. If you want a good grade study on your own and do the practice problems. Good luck.. youll need it

He's an average professor at best. He lectures off of bland white PowerPoints and doesn't collect homework. If you go to office hours, he'll work problems for you, but largely cannot explain them well. Be prepared to learn on your own. Test grades are usually pretty bad, but this is true for all sections. Generally, not a great class.

All his quiz questions come from the assigned chapter questions, so you HAVE to do rework them 3 or 4 times to do well on the quizzes and tests. His lectures often don't correlate with what we're being tested over (meaning he will be going over chapter 7 in class but the upcoming quiz will be over chapter 4). Overall, he's better than Patty.

Very knowledgeable, but lecture style is pretty dull. His powerpoints are paragraphs on a white background. He reads this for most of the lectures. He gives no hints about how to study or what to focus on for the tests, there are no reviews. Do the homework problems. Look at the Hints & Tips on Canvas, your only clue on what might be on his tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: HARD CLASS. Three exams. Standardized chemistry exam. Final. Quiz Average. That's your final grade. It seems like you are failing all semester, but talk to him and he will personally tell you were you are at with a curve. For no reason, he tricks you. Look at the Hints and Tips on Canvas. Rework ALL the problems twice and time yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Harsh grader, but it seems like he really wants you to succeed

He is a great professor and very straight forward. doesn't try to trick his students and always available to help and answer questions. the quizzes are identical to the homework problems, so do the homework its easy to get 100%. Tests again are straight forward. Sometimes takes questions from book & class and just tweaks them. long, not impossible

He is one of the better Chemistry teachers here. He knows the material is very difficult and will adjust, making test and quiz material clear to his students. The book problems are essential and his hints and in class problems help tremendously. Lectures, however, are a bit boring. Would definitely recommend.

He was a great teacher and a really nice person. Always there to answer your question and help because he knows that Chemistry is a hard class. He was reasonable. Every test was made from homework practice problems and in class problems. Never tricked you. Great teacher

The bottom line here is that he's a good guy. He genuinely wants to see his students do well. He doesn't try to intentionally fail you, and wont throw curveballs on testsquizzes. He encourages students to come to office hrs. to seek help. If you understand the material, his tests and quizzes are fine.

His lectures are terribly boring. you won't walk away with any understanding of physical chemistry, but his exams are exactly the problems he assigns for the unit. Learn the problems and you can get a good grade.
he is awful
Great teacher. The tests and quizzes are problems identical to those in the book, so if you do the homework, it's easy to get a good grade in the class.
Well orgnized ,the quizzes are directly from the book and his tests are not that hard
What a joke and a scam of money.
Huh is the best professor I have had at SMU! I went to class two times and got an A+, do what. is asked on time and you will succeed. He is very clear with his expectations and class is very easy.

Never went to class and got an A+. Huh is a sweet guy and a good teacher, this class is just ridiculously easy at no fault to him. He wants you to succeed! If you are looking for an easy A in an 1000 level PLSC class, take PLSC 1320 with Huh!
One of the best professors I've taken. His lecture are really good and he's passionate about what he teaches, also you learn tidbits about random stuff which is fun.

Professor Hudson is probably one of the best May Term Professors I've ever taken. His slideshows are basically all you need to study for the exams, and it's easy to get good grades on the exams and in class in general if you just read through them before the exam. Definitely recommend anyone take this class, super fun and chill professor!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hudson is cool as hell. I just completed the MayMester today, and the class was quick, and easy to make an "A" due to how much extra credit he gives. I definitely recommend Professor Hudson's MayMester. His slideshows give great examples and stories.

Chill, silly dude who structures the class knowing that students prob don't care about it. Gives EC for essays, taking surveys, or just showing up to class sometimes. Lax attendance and in-class "attention checks" aren't graded. Read slides before your test and you're fine. TAs look for honest effort and accuracy in lab, all nice and approachable!

Dr. Hudson is probably the worst professor I have ever had. Do NOT take him, spare yourself. His lectures put you to sleep and he ends up repeating everything over and over again. The TAs are NOT helpful at all. His exams are way too complicated for their own good. If you're smart, you'll take professor Kucker instead!!!

The professor is simply the lecturer, he was okay. The TAs were interesting, the less experienced one graded everything so harshly with little to no explanation on errors. The other was passive aggressive and annoying. Only one TA helped the me thoroughly. Assignments are doable and there's extra credit, but don't take unless you're a psych major.

I wouldn't have taken this class if I wasn't a Psych major, and I won't be taking another research class. Lectures were a drag and TAs weren't helpful. Dr. Hudson doesn't grade a thing, so he's really a lecturer rather than a professor. The paper is annoying but doable, and there's extra credit to help your grade. I'm so happy this class is over.

I want to start off by saying that this class is mandatory for the psychology major. If youre not majoring in psych, dont reccommend taking this. This rating is not based off of Dr. Hudson but the TA's. They are the ones to grade everything and are by far the harshest graders ever met because everything has to be in APA. Julie Pham is more helpful

Dr. Hudson is clearly passionate about psychology but his class is boring and he just reads off of the slides. The lab section of the class is hard and TA's weren't clear with grading (and took a long time). The tests are OK, all online. The research report is time consuming and hard, but doable. Overall, wouldn't recommend.

He cares about the content and his students, but it is very hard to sit through his lectures. He can spend ten to twenty minutes saying the same thing over and over, and yet still not cover all the exam content. The class was alright, but only take it if it's required for your major. Otherwise, it's a waste of your time.

professor hudson was obviously passionate about his class. however, class is dull since it's read off a powerpoint and tests are really hard. I studied for both and managed to pass but did not do as well as I hoped. Lab TAs are no help as I went to office hours many times. he drops a lab, but I cannot lie, this class should only be taken if needed

Research methods, irrespective of teacher, is boring. He is a very nice but lectures are dense and dull. Exams are lengthy and confusing. The grading criteria for labs and research papers is ambiguous. No professor is particularly worse or better of this particular class.

Great professor! Lectures are very interesting and the tests aren't difficult. Every week we have readings and papers due but, he doesn't grade them difficultly at all. There are 3 extra credit assignments that aren't difficult and it helps with your grade. Can be taken for masters in IO or undergrad advanced research methods class.

Professor Hudson seemed to be knowledgeable but his lectures were honestly dull & hard to sit through. Course material was dense and lectures normally consisted of flipping through slides with limited explanation of concepts. We were required to purchase a textbook that was rarely used in class. Grading on assignments also often seemed arbitrary.

Professor Hudson is well knowledgeable, but the lectures are super dull. It's hard to stay focused because the classes are boring. It seems as if he does not care about the students. He puts no effort into making a good experience for the students. The exams aren't too bad. I would recommend doing the extra credits. It helps a lot.

Dr Hudson is a good lecturer. He seems to be quite passionate and excited when teaching even though he is talking about extremely boring things. He offers a lot of extra credit so if you take advantage of it early in the semester it can save your grade in the end. Its very much possible to get an A if you work really hard and prioritize this class.

I had to take this class, and me and every other person in this class hated it beyond words. We had weekly labs that were so hard, and the TAs were as lost as we were. He takes forever to grade and provides zero feedback. Tests were take home which was nice, but overall, this has been the worst class I have taken at SMU. Beyond disappointed with it

Dr. Hudson is extremely knowledgeable in his field, but is likely at SMU just to conduct research and the University makes him teach a few courses. While not his fault, the material is bone dry. He is an enthusiastic lecturer but he is a lazy exam writer (Canvas MC exams) and the labs are run and graded by TA's. There are better profs RM at SMU.

Dr. Hudson does his best to make it exciting but the material is so boring. For lectures he is fine however, you do have to write a 25-page research report at the end of the year and it's brutal. The TA's were useless in labs and were never available for help. Literally one of the worst things I have ever done.

Dr. Hudson is boring and inconsiderate. His lectures put me to sleep faster than melatonin and his lab requirements are way harder than any other research methods prof. A kid copied my paper on an assignment we were supposed to collaborate on and I sent him proof of this, but he said there was simply nothing he could do. Least favorite prof at smu

You have to memorize the power points in order to even do somewhat well on the tests. The averages on the tests were around 70% with no curve and the writing assignments are graded even harder. Not understanding guy at all. One of the worst professors I've had at SMU.

Easy class. Professor gives great lectures, and his test questions come straight from the lectures. You can skip lectures if you want, you'll lose some points from participation but his test questions are straight from his powerpoint notes. Labs aren't fun but they're not too bad.

The class is easy if you do the extra credit and pay attention to the lecture slides. Just pay attention to his lecture slides and only look at the book if you're confused. You get lots of points from just showing up to class and lab and doing the extra credit. Weekly labs are rough and a lot of coding but not a huge part of your grade.

Dr. Hudson is super passionate about investing in the future of scientific research and because of it I found myself drawn to his lectures. Memorize the slides to get an A and refer to the book only if you're confused. I don't know what everyone else is talking about. This class is easy and interesting if you've taken statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Hudson is nice and did the best he could with the bone dry material, but this class is brutal. Exams are reasonable; the weekly labs are the problem. Incredibly dense (one took me 5 hours to complete) and graduate level in difficulty (intense coding), they caused a mass panic to the overwhelmed TAs office hours every week. Awful.

This class tests your willingness to get a C. I have always wondered why professors who come to smu solely for research try to teach undergrads material and assume they already know it. For a fact, I know that this class could be much easier but the level of difficulty on every assignment and exams makes it impossible. Take this class elsewhere.

research methods just sucks in general. he's fine and while they aren't easy, the tests were fine if you put some work into it. the hard part is the lab assignments preparing you for your research project. they are impossible, had to do with coding and tech stuff, and neither he nor the TA were helpful. you lose 10 its every time you miss a lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Hudson is not very personable and is not accessible at all out of class. He has made no effort to help us succeed in this class and uses an overworked TA to grade all our assignments and teach all our labs. The labs are pretty much coding research data, which is really hard. Even the TA is never available to help explain the assignments.

what I love about Professor Hudson's class: 1. he is really passionate and his lecture is incredibly interesting 2. he is a very humorous guy and explains things clearly 3. his hw is all about essays which lets you truly learn the stuff but objectively speaking: 1. he talks incredibly fast 2. you need to memorize everything in the slides to get A

Professor Hudson is very straight to the point. It helped me personally cause from the syllabus as well you can plan& take advantage of extra credits. He can seem fast paced but the topics are interesting . If you go to class, read the textbook and turn in a good paper you will be fine. He's a very fair& logical professor, unlike most

Hes kinda asocial and goes out of his way to not meet you half way. Im sure he is knowledgeable in the topic but he doesnt teach very well. Its hard to get help from him and he just repeats the same thing to you when you ask questions. Dropping the test helps.

He's very nice but I never met with him as his office is on East Campus. The lecture slides are useful and are posted on Canvas. He drops the worst of 4 tests, so you don't have to take the final if you're happy with your first 3. His tests are hard, even if you study super well, but the extra credit makes up for it. Also, there's no homework set.

He's a very passionate professor and keeps the topics interesting, but his class is incredibly tough. It was frustrating because the material itself is not that difficult but the questions on the exams are hard application problems. Four exams including final for your grade, but lowest grade is dropped. Do the extra credit- it'll save you!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Mr. Hudson is a good teacher, but he's not very sociable so it's hard to work to improve your grade. Extra credit. 5 tests, 1 test drop. His test questions are tricky compared to any other psych class I've taken. I go into each test knowing the material 100% and I still flunk the test. He's not mean. You just have to be ready to study very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kinda tough but thats expected from advanced mandarin. Actually, its pretty easy compared to advanced language classes at other universities. She's enjoyable to listen to and pretty funny. Take!! Highly recommend.
She is great. makes class fun and enjoyable to go to
Tough grader and strongly opinionated but there are not other teacher options.

Super engaging and lectures very well. Very friendly outside of class as well! The tests compared to a lot of other finance profs aren't bad at all as long as you study. Group projects are a bit of a pain as you get stuck with the same group for the whole semester, but he lets you choose your group so choose wisely

Definitely the best professor I've ever had! He is very accessible outside of class and cares much for his students. The material itself is not easy, but his lectures are very clear. He includes a lot of practice problems on his slides which help a lot when preparing for his exams. As long as you pay attention and do the practice, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is my favorite teacher I've ever had at SMU. He does a great job at getting the material across and making sure you understand it. If you study the lecture slides and do the problems in them, the test should be a breeze. The only hard thing about this class is the final so if you do well early on you should be able to get an A in the class.

Dr. Huang is the best professor I've had at SMU. His lectures are so clear and very efficient. He is so nice and so responsive to email and requests for help. His tests are very fair. The class is challenging by nature but he is the best person you could take it with. Absolute GOAT!

If you ask for clarification on things, he acts like you are dumb for not knowing exactly what to do. Did not help build a strong foundation for my upper-level Finance classes. If you are a Finance major I would avoid. If you are a general business major, it wouldn't matter as much.

Very passionate and knowledgeable about what he's teaching. Hard material and sometimes in his excitement he'll move very quickly and skip over some not so obvious parts of problems but besides that a good teacher. Very funny at times too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very interesting course and enjoyable professor

Great class by an industry expert. Do not skip a class or you will miss out on the weekly quiz and the info needed for next week.  Read the books assigned, not hard reading and content is pertinent to the film industry. I plan on taking him again despite it being 630-920 at night.
An industry expert that shares his knowledge.   Tests are based on you paying attention to the lectures and reading.
He's a very interesting guy with a lot of awesome personal stories. He is also very easy to interact with and open to discussion if you make the effort.
He's a very interesting guy with a lot of awesome personal stories. He's easy to interact with and open to discussion.
No Comments
meh

Cares a lot for his students and wants them to succeed. Lecture Heavy but uses movie and tv show clips to help explain concepts. Tests are sometimes difficult but he does drop one and curves. A lot of the information is common sense and if you study you will be fine.He gives extra credit to which is really nice!

Super straight forward class. I would highly recommend taking if you have the chance.Just need to take notes in class and listen to a few podcasts here and there. Tests are somewhat hard but grades can easily be made up with a few light projects near the end that are graded very fairly. Tries his best to make content interesting and applicable.

Nice guy and accessible outside of class. 4 exams are only worth 37.5% of grade (drop lowest) but they are the make or break of if you do well. DON'T BUY TEXTBOOK. Everything is covered in class so go to class. Ended with an 89.1% and he wouldn't raise. Otherwise I recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a subject with pretty unexciting material, Prof. Sessions did a good job of engaging the class. While it can be tedious at times doing all kinds of projects, he's accessible, caring, and always willing to re-explain content. Easy to score well on tests/papers, but class participation is BIG. Be ready for discussion questions on homework!

For a new professor he is great. His lectures are directly from the slides, so pay attention and you'lldo fine. Some of the assignments can be a little unclear on paper, but if you talk with him he always works with you to help you understand. He really cares about his students. Extra credit for doing 3 studies too. Would take again. Def recommend
If you take any management professor take Hudson. He really knows what he is talking about and tries to make the lectures interesting. Study hard for tests and you should get an A.

I recommend this class. There are four tests (you can drop one), that are fairly easy if you review the powerpoint slides he posts (pay special attention to the drawings/diagrams), two reflections that you compile over the course of the semester (100 points so long as you do them), a paper, and a team debate.

Prof. Sessions is a new teacher, and he really cares about his students. He has four exams (you can drop one), which are relatively easy so long as you review the powerpoint slides that he posts (pay special attention to the images/diagrams). I recommend this class, its not that hard to get an A.

I really like Professor Sessions as a person, super nice guy and is passionate about his work. Sadly, his exams are hard and require studying. Besides 4 exams, (you can drop one) there is a paper, out of class work, homework, and a group debate. Not impossible to complete, just tedious compared to other management classes. It's very "meh" for me.

Professor Sessions is new to SMU, and his classes are lecture-intensive and test-intensive. Tests require a lot of memorization and studying to do well, but luckily you can drop one if you don't do well (and has a curve). Compared to other management teachers, this class is pretty tough, but Professor Sessions is a nice guy and engaging teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Professor Session's first semester and I have a couple thoughts. He has WAY more work than any of the other management teachers. The class isn't hard, but it is significantly more work than any other MNO 3370 teacher. Session's class has four 50-question exams (require studying), a debate, a paper, and homework every night.

Fairly straightforward class, goes over a powerpoint every class and expects students to do outside of class preparation. Exams are over the stuff covered in PowerPoints and additional readings. Not my favorite class, but not horrible. Nice guy, just not the most interesting material.

Genuinely loves teaching and cares. That being said, he is pretty inaccessible outside of class. Most of the time I was better off asking other students or ALEC for help. 90% of your grade is 2 midterms and a final. Exams are difficult, but he gives a curve at the end. No formal attendance policy but go to class! Hurmuzlu is a great guy.

Great statics Professor! I would 100% take him over any statics professors. All you gotta do is show up to class and communicate with him, he will always help you out especially if you actually are trying to understand the material.

Go to class!!! Make sure he knows who you are!!! He is a nice guy but the material is hard. If you can take physics before statics, do it! At the same time is difficult. Also, make sure to study homework for tests because he does repeat them in tests. It's boring, but do the homework problems 3x or until you have it memorized inside and out.

Prof Hurmuzlu is funny, engaging with his lectures, and has a large curve at the end of the course. He also cares about his students and is always willing to answer questions. My main complaints are that some subjects were less thoroughly taught than others, he is inaccessible by email, and his example problems often skipped critical steps.

First class Ive ever had that didnt have a syllabus or office hours. Dont bother buying the textbook either, he will teach with an older textbook in mind (and take homework problems from it instead) that you can find online. Not bad teaching style and is entertaining, but his laziness and unorganized class makes it harder than it should be. Avoid!
He's fine, just be prepared to do practice problems to do well.

Dr. Hurmuzlu is definitely very well respected and a staple professor for every CEE/ME student at SMU. DO NOT SKIP CLASS - while there's not formal attendance policy, he will call you out and make things more difficult for you. Definitely would take again.

Had him for both Dynamics and Statics.... Owh boy that nightmare came to an end finally. The only thing he do is talk about "In this country, you should never ..... (you guys will find out)" 
Dont have office hours
He got stuck during solving problems and had to watch his solution manual every time.

I wouldn't be too nervous about Dr. Hurmuzle as a professor. No formal attendance policy, but if you miss class he'll call you out at the next one. He's a funny guy who sometimes makes out-of-pocket comments but overall a solid professor. Forgiving grading, won't be bad if you don't get behind.

He is by far the greatest SMU professor due to his personality, teaching style, and willingness to answer any questions. He walks through questions in class, allowing for a comprehensive understanding of the approach, process, and solution. Highly highly recommend taking at least one of his classes. Don't ever skip class and do your homework.

Hurmuzlu is really great at teaching. He is a very sarcastic person, and his relationship with his students is built largely on his humor. Be prepared to be poked fun at: he will assign funny nicknames to students, harass people who miss class, and so on. However, his jokes do occasionally cross the line into racist/sexist/etc. microaggressions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked this class. Professor Hurmuzlu made the class entertaining and the material easy to learn. Although you have to put in the work to understand the material, the class is well-paced and I would definitely recommend him as a professor.

Doesn't teach well, and makes the class harder than necessary by not having a syllabus or other materials. The material shouldn't be difficult, but he makes it difficult by limiting your available resource. He won't give you answers to ungraded practice materials so studying them is worthless. You won't learn anything, you'll just survive.

He was super helpful in office hours and explains concepts until you understand them. The class had two tests and the final was 40% of your grade so you have to keep up all semester to do well. The way to succeed in this class to do as many practice problems as possible. Overall he's a fun professor who knows how to teach the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ugh. He said thered be a curve at the end of semester. At most, it was one sign. I completely bombed the first exam but passed the second and probably passed the final, as well, but I guess not enough to overcome that bomb. Ugh. Doesnt post any grades on canvas, wastes a lot of class time, doesnt answer questions well. At least hes funny. Ugh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He teaches the subject simply, runs through a few problems, and lets you out early. Not a lot of homework and the book has an online answer key. He gives lots of bonus. The tests are hard, but if you do the homework on your own and and genuinely study well, you'll do pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Hurmuzlu is one of my top 5 favorite professors all time. He demands excellence and curiosity from his students and rewards them with funny lectures and great teaching. He's a respected researcher and has a lot of experience. Love this guy.

Hurmuzlu is great! If you go to class and do the work, you will be fine. I absolutely loved his teaching style. Just know that he does not respond to emails and goes on several tangents during class, especially if peeps walk in late; other than that, one of my favorite engineering professors at SMU! would recommend! extra credit:watch sci-fi movies
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor could not care less about whether or not you succeed. He won't respond to emails and he will not make an effort to meet with you after class. That being said, he is a decent professor inside of class, but is so incredibly lazy that he skips test days in order to watch soccer. Overall, not bad, but not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class time is spent just doing book problems and getting out way too early. He's never accessible for office hours, instead relying on TA's and graders who aren't even there half the time, and when they are, don't want to do anything. He gives out a lot of HW that barely affects your grade, and two midterms with one insane final. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Not only gets through all of the material, but tells some great stories along the way. Never a dull moment. Just don't use your phone or act out- he will call you out. He remembers everyone, so make sure you make a good impression or he'll tease you forever! Tests/homework is a breeze, you will be well prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My favorite professor so far! He's been teaching Statics since the 80's, so do the homework and ask questions in class and he'll make sure you understand it. Study for the tests but also know that the final is 50% of the final grade. But if you keep up throughout the semester then you'll be fine.

Class time is mostly used to work problems from the book. He also holds review sessions before the tests, which are usually easier than the homework. He does not have much of an accent, but he has a ton of great stories.  You must attend class, because he remembers everyone's name and face, and make sure not to come late.

Honestly, one of, if not the best professor I've taken in my entire college experience. Brilliant man, really funny in class, and knowledgeable in his field. Wish I could take him again.  -"Detective Bautista"

He has a charming way of teaching that makes you like learning. He basically hands you everything you need to know - just write it down i.e. don't miss class and practice (do the HW). Yes, that means you have to do work in his class to do well but he makes it easy for you. He's funny, interacts with students and is a master on the subject.

He is a great teacher who knows the material. He desires students to participate and ask questions, and when done, the material is not hard to pick up because he is really good at explaining it. He also won't hesitate to answer the simplest questions. He doesn't respond to emails, so class time and office hours are the only time to talk to him.

Hurmuzlu is one of the best teachers at SMU. You don't have to go to class but you don't to miss any classes with him. He is FUNNY , intelligent and the only professor who doesn't use any notes during the class .He knows what he is doing and he doesn't want you to leave the class without undrestanding every details about the lecture.

Prof. H's lectures were intelligible, funny, and concise.  To me it was obvious that he has mastered the teaching of this course. He knows exactly what concepts students typically struggle with and explains them beforehand. Prof. H is hands-down one of the very best professors in this department. Don't miss your chance to learn from the very best!

I enjoyed going to Professor Hurmuzlu's class. He explained the material clearly and involved the class in the lecture by encouraging us to ask questions.  The homework can be tough, but it is great preparation for the tests. Hurmuzlu makes bonus points available on the tests by asking questions about movies that he assigns. Great statics class.

Hurmuzlu is a good teacher and makes the lectures entertaining. Tests are hard to impossible but he curves. Obsessed with organized crime movies so much that he makes watching them extra credit on tests.

Second time taking this course; but first time having Prof. Hurmuzlu. Definitely best teacher for engineering classes I have take so far. Explained and deconstructed the processes so the students could better understand them. Really wish he would teach more classes

Dr. Hurmuzlu is one of the best professors I've had at SMU. He takes the time to answer your questions during the lecture, and he makes the class entertaining. Only class I've looked forward to going to. Tests are pretty hard and so is the material but he is a very reasonable guy. Only downside is he has a don't respond to email policy.
Great teacher. One of the best at SMU lyle. Took him for control and dynamics. I wish he taught more classes.

I really like this professor. He does an outstanding job of making sure you understand what's going on in each chapter so what starts out seeming very complicated turns out to be not as bad. I looked forward to going to class everyday. His lectures are all example problems which is the best way to learn the material.

Hurmuzlu is by far my favorite professor at SMU. He can relate to almost everyone, shares his opinion (whether its on topic or not) and knows how to handle his class and environment efficiently. If I could select him again, I definitely would. Be prepared to work for your grade, but I assure you he will teach you what you need to know.

Overall, one of the best professors at SMU. I never needed to teach myself anything. He is willing to help and always willing to answer questions, no need for office hours it is always very clear in class. Don't skip class or have your phone out ever, and you're golden. Just pay attention.

Hurmuzlu will be one of my favorite teachers by the time I graduate SMU (I'm a freshman right now). You definitely need to do the homework, take thorough notes, and solve problems on your own time from the book. It may be intimidating at first to ask questions, but he genuinely wants students to understand, so he will help you. He's also hilarious.

He's a great professor. Sometimes hard to reach, but will definitely answer questions. You must go to class, and he's super strict on punctuality. sometimes deviates topic and starts to talk about evolution.. but great professor. very helpful, and you can tell he actually cares about his students.. taking him right now, and definitely would again.

Hands down the best professor you will ever have. His class is by no means easy but he is fair. If you want your grades given to you without working for it, then 1) switch out of ME and 2) you will fail. I don't know why you would skip class because he is the most entertaining teacher ever. Only annoying thing is that he NEVER answers emails.

By the end I absolutely loved his class, but I will admit that in the beginning I was totally lost. Be prepared to ACTUALLY STUDY. You will learn a lot if you keep up. It helps to redo the hw at least twice before the tests. Always go to class. Ask him to clarify while working problems on board, otherwise he will assume you understand.

I took Statics with him, and i understand it well now, but he was no help. He skips steps when he demonstrates problems, and he doesn't explain the concepts well. I had to work my a** off to get an A; he just doesn't explain things well.

His lectures suck. When asked questions, most of the time, he didn't know the answer to it. His tests and quizzes were difficult, because there were trick questions and tricky wording. And his group project wasn't graded on time, so when he misunderstood our project, we got a bad grade that couldn't be fixed.

Loved Professor Park's class. He is knowledgeable, caring, and intelligent. Always available to help outside of class and gives quick feedback. Tests are straightforward if you study the material he goes through in class - there are no surprises.

Cost accounting is a very interesting class. Prof. Park is friendly and helpful. Tests are difficult if you do not know the materials well. For the final group project, you should ask prof. Park for feedback before submitting.
Literally the most amazing teacher in Cox. friendly, helpful, and he teaches really well. Definitely take him if you can.

Prof Park is awesome. Prints off all notes prior to class, so it is really easy to follow along. Tests can be hard if you don't understand the material. But if you don't understand and go in, he will help you. PAY ATTENTION and show up, and you will be fine. Awesome class to take.

Professor Park tries very hard to help his students understand the material, and knows it can be confusing for a lot of people. He is also pretty tricky on his quizes, but they don't count for too much. If you need help, he is happy to answer questions in class or during his office hours.
Professor Park is very willing to help students learn and perform well in class.  His lectures were very clear and helpful: I felt little need to read the textbook.   Overall, a great professor!

Park is a great teacher and explains accounting well. The tests aren't too bad, but be sure to study for the quizzes, as they cover more than you might think and can catch you unprepared. If you take the honors sections, you'll have an additional project at the end of the year, but it's not too much work.

Park is one of the best professors I've had at SMU. He's super sweet and really does his best to explain everything well. He goes over the material at the beginning of class each day, and is very accessible if you ever need help. The tests are usually harder than the practice ones though, so don't be fooled!

Seriously the sweetest professor ever! He truly cares and wants you to understand the material! If you show you're the least bit interested and that you are putting effort into your work you will get a good grade!
Great class, one of the best professors I've had yet. 2 midterms and a few quizzes. Always willing to meet with his students and very helpful. Highly recommend his class

If you have to take intro accting then take it with Park. He is an understanding, intelligent, clear professor who cares about his students. Go to class everyday and take notes. He talks a little fast but you get used to it. Awesome guy!

He's a great guy & he really respects his students. There's homework but seldom picks it up. Hes a great professor because he teaches w/o using the book as a crutch. The exams are straight forward & in the class before each exam he gives u a practice exam that is EXACTLY like the test. tho his quizzes (once/mo) are kind of challenging. Take Park!

Highly recommend!! The tests are more based off his notes than the book (but it's still helpful to read). He challenges you on tests, but wants you to do well. He is usually flexible and is very helpful in office hours. He also talks about what's happening in the economic world and applies it to what we learn.

A very professional professor. Very nice and personable too. Lots of multiple choice, he only collects homework twice, and will tell you when he does. Can't really complain, but be aware that there is a severe curve in this class. The average has to be at a specific point, and so will raise or lower your grade to meet this average.
Great professor who is always willing to meet with you but the tests can be difficult. 2 exams, 3 quizzes, 1 final
Very good teacher. Always willing to help his students. Tests are hard but doable if you study and understand the material.

He's super friendly and he really wants his students to do well in the class. I think this is his first year teaching and I thought he did a pretty good job so I'm sure it can only get better. 2 midterms and a final exam. Study his practice questions and you will do fine. Go to his office hours, he will help you a lot.
friendly and nice teacher. sometimes we don't understand what he says. no mandatory homework. it's a fairly good class.
Not a bad class, but sometimes it is hard to understand him. Also, he misunderstands questions fairly often. However, he is very friendly and really loves to teach and help.

I am talking about the advanced managerial economy class this guy teaches at UTD. this guy should be fired absolutely. never understand why UTD hires him. maybe because his wife is hired by UTD? read ppt (copy from textbook) off, no explanation, it is totally waste of time to go to his class

"If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough." - Albert Einstein.  This quote says everything about this class.  Confusing poor explanations on the topic, then would give homework over those topics every week.  He gave off the impression that he didnt care at all about the students.  He was no help if you went to his office.
His explanation is unclear
he can't convey his point clearly. I have his class.
Ask him questions!! Very helpful
Boring can't hear and acts like he has no idea what you're saying when he does. Useles course.
He lectures a lot and sometimes is hard to hear, but he is great and very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Richards is such a great guy. Class based on 4 tests and lowest test grade is dropped. Make quizlets based off exam reviews and you will do great. Labs are 25% of grade so make sure you go to those as well. I think Richards is retiring though...

Professor Ian is awesome. He is very funny and entertaining during lectures. Always willing to meet with you outside of class if needed. Only downside is the review guides he puts out for exams are just combinations of lecture slides. Tests aren't too bad but you'll need to do your own review work.
Professor Richards was amazing. He's really kind and his class is fairly easy. The tests can be tricky, but they're easier if you go through the slides and skim the textbook beforehand.
Great dude. Cant stand science but had to take a breadth. Very easy grading structure that is favorable for the students and does not require work. Take for breadth credit. Go to labs

I really enjoyed Earth Systems with Ian. His attendance wasn't mandatory but he really appreciated everyone that did show up (and gave extra credit). The lectures were somewhat interesting and he's pretty funny too. He cares a lot about his students, especially the ones that really show they care. Go see him during office hours, it'll help you.

Ian is a great professor. There are only three tests then the final, and then the lab. He values participation, and he makes a few jokes in his lectures. He has dry humor, so I valued that. He also offers an extra credit assignment that will add at most 3 points to your final grade. It's not an easy A, but it's attainable.

Prof. Richards is easily one of the best professors I've ever taken. He is super funny and always makes class entertaining. You can tell that he really enjoys what he teaches and he makes lectures very engaging. He is always available for office hours and if you review the study guides with him, you'll do amazing on every test. He's a must take!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. Quizzes every week are easy and sometimes he helps and sometimes he just gives us answers. Tests are not bad if you study. Research project is basically participation grade. He's hilarious and a genuinely good guy.

Dr. Richards co-taught this class, but really it felt like it was led by Deshon and Dr. Richard was there to lead 5 or so lectures. I'm not sure how the class would have went if he led the course, but Dr. Richards does have the special talent of learning names very fast. He will know your name by the end of the first week. He is a very nice guy.

Great professor! Gives 10 extra credit quizzes that allow you to boost your final grade up to 3 full points, and is willing to help you prepare for tests outside of class as well. He understands that for many this is just a class taken for a science credit; I would definitely recommend taking this class!

One of the nicest, caring, and helpful professors I have had for an intro class. Almost always available to help outside of class and is super flexible with all assignments if you get sick (like I did). The final is optional if you do well enough on the first 3 tests (which are fairly easy to get an A if you study) and he makes grading very clear.

Not only one of the nicest professors, but nicest people I've met. Super passionate and intelligent. Only has 4 tests/semester including final. No homework or attendance. Tests are easy multiple choice, but if you don't study you wont do well. Lecture is more difficult. Allows computers and class is curved.

He is really helpful and really wants his students to succeed.. he offers extra credit. You will do well depending on how much you study for the exams, but they are all multiple choice. He is seriously so incredibly nice- I didn't even like geology as a subject but this has been my favorite class all semester.

Class is what you make of it. Professor Richards really enjoys what he teaches and knows what he's talking about. He's really funny and helpful. Tests depend on how much you study and pay attention in class.

Nicest professor I've had thus far.  He knows everybody's names by heart and wants his students to succeed.  Attending class is not mandatory but definitely helpful.  He posts his notes online and lets you know what to study for tests.  If you do bad on a test... no worries b/c he lets you drop one (best 3/4).  Definitely recommend his class.

I have him for Intro to Environmental Science, and this class is very easy. Definitely not as interesting as the env class I took in high school, because this one is more focused on Earth processes/env changes, but it's one of the easiest Gen Ed science courses to take. Boring power point lectures, but he's really nice & helpful & he's Australian

The epitome of a theory based lecturer. Terrible at conveying the material in a manner comprehensible to 98% of undergraduate students. Prepare to do an excessive amount of self study to remotely grasp the material. Don't expect clear concise notes, or even example problems for that matter. Welcome to Ouchtown, USA. Population: you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had him for Heat Transfer at NYIT. He gives a lot of quizzes, but they're quick and easy. He encourages class participation and asking questions. The assignments are never required but if you don't do them you're pretty screwed for the tests. Overall a fun and engaging professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures aren't always super interesting, but he goes over a lot of example problems in class. His tests are exactly like what he says they'll be.

Professor Iopollo is really funny and he's a nice guy. There were a lot of tests in this class but that made it easy because each test only covered like 1 chapter. None are cumulative. Also basically drops the lowest one. His lectures can get a little confusing but he will certainly clarify if you ask, and the book is great at clarifying
Just understand the homework and you'll get a 100%. If you ask questions he'll love you and if you don't understand something he'll show you how to do it no problem

DON'T take this professor!! He'll make your life miserable with back to back tests. While most classes are on there 1st exam, you'll be taking your 3rd or 4th exam. On his exams he'll only have like 2-3 questions only. Hard grader. It's not worth it. He also doesn't teach well either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Be sure to ask questions or he'll get upset and give an impossible quiz

Not a good teacher, the accent is really hard to understand. Never hands back quiz or test grades--I thought I was on track for at least a B before the final, ended up with a C-. Semi-helpful in office hours, but without grades to indicate progress, students are totally lost.

Chill guy but horrific teacher. Very unclear grading and test procedures.  Most of the class didn't have a clue what was happening throughout the semester and didn't know their grades until the end of the semester. Make sure you do the hw accurately or you will because you have to have higher than 80% on hw/quiz category to pass the class.
Terrible teacher but he gives take home tests sometimes and his tests in class aren't too hard even if you don't go to class

I took Prof. Ioppolo for Thermodynamics and made an A. Excellent teacher but has typical European accent, which is VERY understandable though. Funny person too :) Make sure to attend the lectures as they are very informative. Tests are hard so make sure to do HW. Talk to him after tests in his office and he'll give a good grade! :)

I'm currently a student in two of Ira's classes in the brand-new MA in Creative Technology program that he's spearheading at SMU. While I came into the program with zero-to-no knowledge about coding or programming, Ira has made the program very accessible and fun while sharing his vast knowledge of the space with all the students. Love his classes!

Very good at explaining and lecturing on material (better than any other computer science teacher I've had). He is very helpful if you meet with him about any issues you are having in the course as well. Tests can be tough, but he reviews plenty and tells you what to study or what will be on the exams. Allows cheat sheet as big as you can make too.

Ira is a great professor. It's clear he loves creative computing & knows what he is talking about. We did really fun and interesting projects in his class. However, we didn't go through very much material or learn much C++. If CSE is your major, I would not recommend this class. Any other major, I would say go for it! Its is fun and not much work.
Good professor! Really helpful on the labs and makes sense in class.

One of the best CS professors I had at SMU. Professor Chow is very easy going and gives extra credit, and his labs/homework are self explanatory and easy. He is very caring, and tries his best to make sure everybody gets a good grade. Heavily recommend taking this class so you can have at least one relaxing class during the semester
Easygoing professor and you can earn extra credit by doing more work

Absolutely riveting class! The level of energy in this class as the professor goes through his awe-inspiring 100 PowerPoint slides every lecture. He is the only lecturer for this class, so you will take his class if you are a CS major. Just focus on what the professor emphasizes loudly in his slides to prepare for exams (open notes).
Teaches mostly off of the book and his powerpoints, which does not fit well with 3-hour night classes. He is extremely kind and willing to answer questions if you are present and paying attention.

Worst professor I've had in 4 semesters at SMU. His 3 hour class never goes beyond the slides, so you're better off just reading the slides and taking notes on your own. Tests are open book/open note and rely on it. Overall, class is a joke -- It's up to you if you want to learn anything -- either way you'll probably get an A.

He's super slide heavy and really doesn't explain things clearly, I walk out more confused than not and we end up watching YouTube videos in class for way too long. He has good intentions, but shuts down discussions and can't seem to find a way to concisely explain anything without going into tangents or over complicating very simple ideas.

Here's the thing: if you're not a computer science major and just want a class to boost your GPA, take it because you're guaranteed to make an A+. BUT, if you are a computer science major and want to REALLY LEARN SOMETHING, do not take his class! His lectures are horrible and he speaks with a heavy accent! You'll NEVER learn anything in that class.
dude gave us the entire first test in class. what a legend

Easiest computer science class available at any college. This man will give you the code on labs and as long as you change it up a little he wont even doc points. 100% take his class if you can. I'm not a CSE or engineering major and if your looking for quality teaching this is not the class for you. Turn in work on time and completed, thats all.

Awesome class. The professor is very clear and helpful in explaining the programming concepts. I now know more about OOP in Java. He uses multi-media such as videos in explaining stuffs. The labs are very organized and easy to follow. The last two labs get more complicated but they are fun.

Great professor. He is very enthusiastic in teaching and helping students out. I was not good at programming but he used a lot of examples with great videos. The lab assignments are great and help me understand the programming concepts. If you go to class and listen to the lectures, you will get an A.

This class is a joke. Dr. Chow doesn't teach.... the majority of our class time is spent watching projected YouTube videos on the screen. Just learn the material yourself and take the tests. The TA's in Caruth 484 are incredibly helpful with the lab and lecture material. Just make friends with a TA who's working the help desk and learn it yourself

Easy class, but waste of time to attend. The majority of "lectures" were actually watching YouTube video tutorials on the lecture topic. Attendance was 5% of the grade, but if you admitted you never went you still got 4%. Don't go to class, just YouTube the material yourself. Tests are simple, I never went to class and got 98-100% on all tests.
He's AWESOME chillest professor and genuinely wants you to succeed. You will get a good grade unless you just don't deserve it and he gives homework points which is amazing!! Take him he's awesome!!

Professor Bosch is a phenomenal chemistry teacher. He really cares about you learning and less about a simple letter grade. He is willing to meet and go over any questions during office hours and the homework he assigns, although optional, is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super chill. He has his lecture pre-recorded so you can work at your own pace, whether its faster or slower. His quizzes and tests are free response but as long as you know the material and do his practice problems, you should be fine. He also offers extra credit through the homework. It's 2 points per homework, 10 homework total so 20 extra points

I loved him. He was so funny and made chem fun. This class is HARD so be ready to do the work. He is good about office hours and does review sessions for exams. Homework is extra credit so make sure you do it! All exams are free response but make sure you know what you are doing because you will use the whole time given. Overall amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is super unprofessional. I have been cussed out many times for trying to correct him on something he wrote down wrong. His test questions are written unclear and he offers no help to understand it. He also hates being told when he is wrong, and does not accept feedback.
He is a great professor with a good personality. He gives a lot of extra credit and wants his students to do well. Straight forward tests form examples he does in class.

At first, it was hard to understand what was going on in class, but I put in the work and reached out to the professor for help. He was extremely kind and helpful, and he explained everything to me. By the end of the class, I felt that I had a good understanding of the material.
Dr. Isaac is a great professor, especially in the upper levels of chemistry. He's hilarious, which makes learning about inorganic reactions and molecular symmetry late in the afternoon bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A really funny professor that does tend to cuss a lot, but it makes class very entertaining. Exam questions were mostly textbook questions that were either covered in class or in the homework. Offers a lot of extra credit to boost your grade. As long as you pay attention in class, this class should be relatively easy to do well in.

Terrible professor. Does not explain things thoroughly and will ruin you on the test/quiz by asking about an obscure formula or a type of problem that wasn't demonstrated in class nor in the textbook. Half the time he does not attend his own office hours and makes his TA teach them. Curses so much that it's disrespectful.

Great professor. Explains well. Prepares you for exams thro HW problems. He's very caring and would give u as much time as u need for office hours. He is extremely nice, but he gets really IRRITATED if u skip class, so don't do that! Attending class is definitely mandatory, and you won't pass if you don't attend or do the HW. All HW is extra credit

Favorite class and professor at SMU. Really helped grow my knowledge in entrepreneurship and excel my own business, receiving funding/investment. Learned how to pitch, develop businesses, legal structures, methods of development, and how to do use your personal power to the fullest and smartest potential.

Professor Hart is excellent if you want to explore the intersection of mindfulness, creativity, and business. You collaborate in groups to develop a concept, applying real-world ideas. He keeps the class engaging, practical, and balances conceptual teaching with hands-on implementation

Prof. Hart is genuinely nice and the class is pretty easy, but he often rambles and drags lectures out longer than they need to be. He also tends to contradict himself when giving instructions, so it's always a good idea to clarify what he really wants

Professor Hart and AMAE 3387 single handedly made my semester this year. He is an awesome teacher and if you are even somewhat passionate about entrepreneurship, this is the class for you. There's a few tests in which he gives you everything needed to study for them efficiently and the rest is group work! I overcame my fear of public speaking here!
Tons of dynamic excercises and team-based projects. all assignments were project based and we explored many different entrepreneurial methodologies.

Professor Hart does a fantastic job teaching the class and keeping you engaged with real world skills that will help you be a successful entrepreneur. He wants you to be successful in his class and he will show that by checking in with you on your projects and making sure you are on track with your work. overall he is a fantastic person.

Creative Entrepreneurship was the best class I had this semester. Mr. Hart gives themes that can be useful for entrepreneurs. The class was relatively easy and super direct. He explains the materials for the exam, as well, what he is expecting of your team's project. Looking for something fun, interesting and business related take this class.

Professor Hart is a very motivated teacher and loves the subjects that he teaches. His classes are enjoyable and his activities are fun if you put in the effort to participate. He isnt a hard grader on projects, he wants to see you put in the effort and he genuinely cares about your ideas and your work. He has really helped me grow as a student.

He's a nice guy, and it's a good class to knock out a breadth requirement. There's little to no homework, and half your grade is just attendance. The only downsides are that he tends to ramble about himself, and sometimes your grade feels like it depends a bit too much on the random group you get assigned to.

his lectures are incredibly boring. He's also a hard grader. Always says he'll give us guidance for an assignment then proceeds to make instructions incredibly difficult to follow, leaving you more confused than before.

Professor James Hart is easily the best professor, teacher, and mentor I've ever had the good fortune to learn from. His entrepreneurial spirit is contagious, and his knowledge and wisdom are given freely to all of his students. If you are curious about this class I recommend you listen to your intuition and take it. You won't regret it.

The class was not overly difficult and had material that can be used in real life. He cares a lot about his students and helps you wherever he can. Much of the class is attendance and participation so just show up and you should do well.

Honestly not really sure what to think of him. Nice guy, and seems like he cares, but also such a random course that I wasn't really sure what we were being taught half the time. Some of the quizzes he gives are strangely challenging/vague so beware. Overall, easy class. Haven't gotten my grade yet but would be surprised if it was below an A-.
Very engaging class! Many opportunities to put skills learned into practice. Professor Hart is kind and always willing to meet for extra clarification and assistance!
Professor Hart is always willing to help you succeed! Pay attention and participate regularly! Overall wonderful class - 100% recommend.

Professor Hart's AMAE 4390 fosters an environment of learning, encouraging participation in both the classroom and group projects. In class, I saw my team members from our project grow as entrepreneurs. The lessons I learned in class will be incredibly useful in my career. Professor Hart was an amazing teacher and everyone should take this class.

This was my favorite class I have taken at SMU . Professor Hart has designed the course so well. You will gain so much from this course. Attendance is mandatory and you have to put in work to get an A+ but it is all very relevant material you will be able to use in the real world. Take this course!

I really enjoyed this course. Professor Hart is a great professor who really wants his students to succeed. The class is only what you make of it. Be prepared to show up everyday and you will gain awesome insight and practice to starting a real company and being able to speak fluently in an entrepreneurial manner.

Prof. Hart excels as an educator, blending expertise with an approachable demeanor. His course uniquely applies theory to real-world scenarios through dynamic exercises and teachings. With substantial experience and a kind personality, he's a standout in my SMU experience, offering not just education but inspiration. Looked forward to class evryday

Test are easy, quizzes are hard. Attendance is mandatory, but most classes are spent working in your groups on projects. You spend majority of your class time throughout the semester working on your pitch decks which gets kinda annoying and super repetitive but its not a hard class at all. The material is beneficial and he is nice

I found this class to be very beneficial for those who have interest in taking an entrepreneurial route. All of the material in this class is applicable for postgrad. Professor Hart was very helpful in office hours willing to help me brainstorm when it came to my own ideas of starting a business.

This class is easy but also thought provoking, the information and material you learn will help you in the future but it is not that difficult because it is mainly common sense and getting the hang of the terms and definitions. A lot of your grade in this class is participation so if you show up you will get a high grade. There are a few quizzes .

I have found this class to be very applicable to my everyday life. Professor Hart equips his students with the materials they need to succeed in the "real world," specifically when it comes to entrepreneurship. Additionally, I gained more confidence in public speaking in this class than in my actual public speaking course.
Extremely caring guy with a lot of great insight. Class is structured on "play" and exercises which makes it very enjoyable

Professor Hart remains the best teacher I have had while at SMU! He truly cares about his students and all material is extremely engaging and enjoyable! If you have the opportunity to take a class taught by professor Hart, do your self a favor, and take it!!!  After back to back AMAE courses I can strongly say, I will miss having him as a teacher!

Professor Hart is the best teacher I have had in my college career. I have taken him for AMAE 3387 and AMAE 4390 and enjoyed both of them. He is extremely intelligent, kind, and understanding. I would recommend either of his courses to anyone regardless of their major.

Professor Hart really cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. 

There's quite a few assignments and reading quizzes in this class, but you can easily use them in your midterm business plan. 

If you participate and put effort into this class, you'll do great.

I genuinely enjoyed taking his course. You do not need to have a background in business to succeed in his class. He is always willing to help and wants to see you succeed and grow as a person throughout the semester. He also gives extra credit opportunities and listens to student feedback. I would recommend taking his course! You learn a lot!

Professor Hart's incredible teaching is what inspired me to pick up my minor in AMAE. He is direct with what he expects and is very respectful. I have had him for one class in person and an independent study for another class and he couldn't have been more helpful and flexible. I am very grateful for his commitment to building the AMAE program.

Mr. Hart was the best professor I had outside my directed music studies. He was the most impactful and inspiring professor I had during my time at SMU. I still use the things he taught me even 7 years after I taking his classes. Definitely a must for entrepreneurs and motivated people alike.

Professor Hart personalized this course to fit my needs and met me where I was at in term of my business knowledge. He assigned me relevant tasks that pertained to what I wanted to accomplish in real life and I learned a lot from every single lecture he gave. Be prepared to take notes and participate to get the most out of your time with him!

I took Professor Hart's class and a year removed it is still impacting my life. He is particularly thoughtful, caring, and wicked smart. If you are looking for a blow-off class, look somewhere else.

No matter your major, but especially if you're not majoring or minoring in business, take an entrepreneurship course with Professor Hart. Hart is a great mentor to have

Professor Hart cares about the success of his students. He pushes his students to take risks. If youre interested at all in arts entrepreneurship TAKE HIM.
