This is without a doubt the most frustrating class I have ever taken. While professor Ozak is knowledgeable about the material he is horrible at sharing that knowledge with his students. His tests are an absolute nightmare and he does not curve. If I could give a future student any advice I would say avoid this professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: SUPER hard class but the professor is very helpful if you have meetings with him and/or go to office hours. He has a PhD so he is obviously way smarter than undergrad students & the content is already really hard. Tests leave you sweating at the end, but if you go to office hours it is much more manageable overall (required class for econ kids)
Lack of feedback and empathy and sometimes can get passive aggressive when asked a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I haven't heard a single student say a good thing about this professor. He does NOT care about his students, and sometimes refuses to talk to them if they ask for help. He does not provide reviews or ANY assistance for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE. BY FAR my least favorite Professor I've had at SMU. Avoid at all costs. He doesn't care about his students, is a cruel grader, and makes economics way more complicated than it is.

Lectures are very straight forward and taught through powerpoint slides that are accessible at anytime. The lectures may seem intimidating at first, but if you put in the time to study the review before the test and visit him in his office you should do well in his class. Reasonable amount of homework through connect learning. Also curves tests.

Dr. Ozak is intense. Make no mistake that he loves to scare his students from day one. He wants to rid the class of the slackers, and he succeeds. If you stick around, then you will discover that he cares about his class and the subject matter. The class is not impossible, and if you keep up with all the assignments, you will be fine.

Dr. Omer's class seems like it will be terribly hard at the beginning, but it is actually very manageable. His quizzes are based on the previous class's lecture and he usually gives half credit for putting your name on the paper. His reviews cover everything on the exam, and in the end he ended up giving our entire class a huge curve.
His practice tests are often similar to his actual tests.  Take him!

The lectures can be confusing sometimes but he makes an effort to encourage questions and he takes the time to answer them. He's also helpful if you go see him. Unlike the previous person, our TA was terrible. I left the study sessions feeling worse about the test. He ended up curving the exams so it worked out. Nice teacher who cares.

INTERMEDIATE MACROECONOMICS, he is new this year (I think), he is a nice teacher, but his lectures are very confusing and boring, he makes things so complicated. I cannot understand a thing he teaches, good thing there is a TA, the TA is the best, I wouldn't have passed the class without the TA's help. There's a lot of homeworks.
Objectively a horrible teacher and wholly unorganized with everything to the point where your grade suffers.
Not a good professor and not very nice when you need help or understanding when stuff goes down in life as it do.

I only took this class for credit. And I absolutely hated it. Professor is not nice. If your work wasn't what she wanted, she would get mad at the students instead of  taking the blame for herself. Very boring class, don't waste your time.   I would never take her again.

Dr. Mueller is good at what she does and is obviously passionate about her classes. Make sure you read what's assigned otherwise it makes for an awkwardly silent class. Very discussion-based so hope for a talkative class. Shes really helpful on papers and her expectations are super clear. Definitely one of the better Disc classes.

Mueller is a fantastic lecturer, and I was hardly every bored in her class. However, she gives little to no feedback on any papers or writing assignments. She conferenced once and it lasted four minutes. If you are historically good with English, I would highly recommend her, but if you struggle with writing, steer clear or prepare for frustration.

Decent. She leads good discussions, and if they aren't interesting it's cause nobody read the material. Reserved character and very calm. She came 5-15 min late to every class this semester, make of that what you will. Really vague as far as grading and doesn't give very clear feedback on essays. Nice and deceptively funny at times
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pros: Very nice lady and professor. Does not lecture incessantly like Hopper or Arbery and does not constantly talk about sex. Very conservative/reserved in character (I'm not saying politically). Good for those who like class discussions. Cons: Does not hold regular office hours and must make an appointment. No clear grading criteria on papers.

Took her literature of the holocaust class because it was the only disc class available. The topic of this class is dark but she did a good job of making it somewhat interesting. Class can be boring sometimes but she is actually a great teacher. My writing definitely improved over this semester. She is a nice person and a decently easy grader.

She's really nice and approaches the topic in an interesting way. She's chill. The papers are not difficult, and she has one on one conferences to help you. You have to write one page analysis over readings, but you get to choose when out of multiple options. The final is a paper that she helps extensively with and gives class time.

At the beginning of the year she seemed fairly reserved and even pretty boring, but as the semester progressed she definitely became more colorful and at ease with our class. If you dont know how to write, you are going to learn in this class. She is a fair grader, but you have to give her what she wants i.e. cater to her style of writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Uses a textbook that is out of print, so getting it was a little difficult. Has slowly become more comfortable in class and started making jokes and loosening up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really liked her, she made class interesting and we did many in class workshops that helped my papers greatly. I thought she was a fair grader. Very nice too
she's totally a nice and caring woman, but grades a little bit too harshly. not crazy harsh, but definitely could've taken an easier disc professor.
If you take the "The Role of Rhetoric in Social Media and Academia" you don't read a book all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's a great teach and explains concepts thoroughly. She is passionate about the subject she teaches and always finds a way to make class lectures interesting and relevant to our lives as students. She is funny, nice and gives good feedback. I highly recommend her as a DISC teacher.

If you have any self-respect, DON'T take her class. She has hard assignments so kiss your grade goodbye. I showed up for all lectures, studied, attended office hours, and still barely got above a C. Last 5 min of class and she is scolding us about
 how we have 10 min left and that it's "our grade" because we were packing up, horribly condescending

Dr. Murphy is genuinely the best professor I've had at SMU. She explains everything very clearly and genuinely wants her students to succeed. She is very smart, straight forward, and helpful. A+P isn't an easy class, so studying is necessary, but if you put in the effort, you can get a good grade.

Took Prof Murphy in Jan term, best decision I've made at SMU. She is really good at explaining material, gives you lots of time for in class assignments, and an open note quiz at the end of the day but no final test/outside homework. Only other thing is a paper on a topic you choose and it's not hard. Just DO NOT be late or skip and participate!
Super smart and nice teacher, but extremely fast paced class with hard test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are extremely difficult for an introductory course. She will not curve it or round or give any form of extra credit. No matter how much work you put into studying for this class, your exam score will most likely not reflect it. The tests are unfair.

Honestly a huge you know what. Incredibly condescending and makes the class harder than it needs to be. Im convinced that she wrote all of these good reviews herself. Everyone Im in a group text with hates her with a passion & so does everyone I know thats had to take her in the past. Bad person, bad teacher, hard subject. Only take if ur forced

One of the worst classes at SMU. DO NOT take unless you are a Pre-Med or Bio major. There are no prerequisites so it will trick you but this class is very very very difficult. This class has the most info you will ever have to cram in your college career and it is just an all around horrible class. Save your GPA and do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loved the class. A&P is a difficult subject as is but Murphy does a great job of getting you interested in it. Tests are really difficult - lots of information and systems to memorize. Pre-med kids (most of the students) will have no problem but other students will just because it's so much info - but it is definitely doable! Take Jen for lab.

Dr. Murphy is awesome! The material of the second semester of A&P is slightly more difficult than the first, but still very manageable. She is a wonderful professor who really cares about her students. Can't recommend enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Anatomy is a hard class in general but as long as you care about the class you'll be fine. She really cares about the class and all the students. The class is all memory but that's what A&P is. Lab practicals are always the same week as tests. Practicals are super hard (ie memorize all the bones and muscles) but the lab teachers (Jen) are great

Dr. Murphy is awesome! She makes the class (anatomy & physiology) as straight-forward as possible and makes lectures interesting. The lecture is relatively easy; the lab practicals are what can bring your grade down, but Dr. Murphy doesn't teach lab. Overall would highly recommend!

LOVE HER!! My favorite professor at SMU. The subject was a little hard but manageable and this is not my major so trust me. She was one of the nicest professors I have ever had and so smart. I wish I could have teachers like her, truly invested in our growth, in every part of the class. Tons of different assignments so if you mess up one, no biggie

I LOVE Dr. Murphy. I had her for anatomy and exercise physiology simultaneously and she was amazing. She was thoughtful, excited about the material and helped us learn by powerpoints and in-class labs. Barely any homework, listen to the lectures and pay attention and you will do well.

Dr. Murphy is my favorite professor. I've had her for exercise physiology and anatomy- highly recommend taking them both simultaneously. She is so fun and outgoing, it makes the tough content of anatomy more interesting. Definitely a lot of work, and study hard for the lab practicals because Dusty is tough. Love her and love the class!

She was an amazing teacher, always went over material multiple times in class to make sure it was understood. Anything that is not on the power points she writes up on the board and goes over it at extreme length to make sure you understand it. If you go to class, turn in the HW and simply meet with her when you are confused you will get an A.

Great Professor! She's very sweet and helpful. Tries to make class fun and interesting. It's a difficult subject, so it takes effort! Exams are taken from PowerPoints. Didn't buy the book and got an A. Final is cumulative. Take her without hesitation! Bonus: Very pleasant to look at

She's nice, but she never posts the powerpoints onto blackboard until after we're done going over notes in class. It's really frustrating because I like to write on the slides while I take notes. Read the book and study hard, and you'll do well. It helps if you've already taken chem and bio.

Sid is one of my favorite professors at SMU. His class requires a lot of reading and test prep but if you work hard, you will do well. He doesn't try to trick you on exams and they are straightforward if you're willing to study. His lectures are very clear and he provides examples and emphasizes certain concepts that are going to be on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely cares about his students and wants you to succeed. The lectures are AMAZING! He is genuinely a great person. The class is seriously so easy as long as you actually show up. One of the best professors at SMU!
a rule follower and doesnt not have any sympathy for his students

Sid is an amazing professor. He is knowledgable and very friendly, which makes him very approachable for out of class meetings and questions in class. He makes himself available for his students. His tests are dense, but adjusting the level of studying after the first one makes the class a hard earned A. lots of students complain, but don't study.

Sid is very fair. Not an easy class, but put in effort & you will do well. Some test questions are tricky- be familiar w material. He's readily available for office hours (highly suggest) and responds to emails immediately. Gives study guides & clear slides. Take in Summer if possible- ask for guidance and participate and he will help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Unless you enjoy unreasonably hard tests, not having your opinion validated, or unclear grading policies, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!! Avoid at all costs. 0/10 would NEVER take again.
Don't take unless you have too. His tests are unreasonably difficult. Class average for test one was a D yet he still didn't curve.
Lectures very laid back although sometimes boring. Tests (unnecessarily) harder than I anticipated. Sid is great though!
Sid was a super helpful professor- especially after the course finished!  He helped me to review my resume.
Great, Friendly, Iand nteractive!
Makes tests too complicated. Avoid unless advertising is your intended major.
Avoid if possible

All powerpoints, which I personally liked. There are 4 tests, last test is the final, not cumulative, pretty straightforward if you study. Gives study guides. He is really helpful outside of class and appreciates students who go to office hours. So many extra credit opportunities, attendance is mandatory. Take the class!

Enthusiastic and interesting lectures. Laid back class, although the tests can trip you up if you don't study for them. 4 tests, no final. Memorize the review he provides and you will be fine on the tests. $ extra credit opportunities, and extra credit given for having 0 absences at the end of the semester.

Loved this class. The readings were really well picked, and Prof Myers led to some great conversations. I also have to say, their feedback was awesome. They gave really specific advice that helped me improve my writing, which not ever professor will take the time to do. Honestly, I learned a ton and would take again.

I found lectures to be wordy and hard to follow. Along with this, she assigned about 80 pages of reading per class. The assignments given were worth a small number of points but equated to a high percentage in the grade. There is very little room for error. She also is not understanding of family emergencies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Instructor is difficult to deal with. No class plan, no interest in hearing other opinions, and no set method for grading. Hostile class environment.

Myers is an amazing teacher she is really open about personal experiences and teaches culture through an accepting lens. Definitely has pop quizzes and group pop quizzes plus attendance policy (policy is very fair with multiple misses). Really interesting lectures and quest speakers! She cares a lot about her students as well.

Neely Myers is a perfect option for Anthropology credit. She is open to help students, her lectures are extremely interesting even if you aren't into anthropology, and you'll learn a lot+ get a good grade.

Neely is very passionate about what she teaches. She posts rubrics and as long as you follow it, you'll get a 100. Op-ed instead of final. If you are easily triggered by mental health issues, don't take her 3303 class. She talks about every issue under the sun and sometimes laughs in uncomfortable situations. Overall, nice lady - easy, fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Easy A. Dr. Myers is so passionate about what she is teaching that you can't help but be just as passionate. Cares for your well-being and success. Essays are graded with ease and presentations are fun (on interesting cultural syndromes).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the best professors you can get in the department. We had easy projects instead of tests and wrote an op-ed for our final. however, you will learn so much she is such an amazing and kind professor and I learned more from her than many other professors. TAKE HER

A class that doesn't feel like a class because the material is very interesting and inclusive of the class. Includes discussing with other students and the readings are also very interesting. One of my favorite classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: GREAT !   Long tests
Very interesting woman with lots of great stories to tell. Keeps students engaged. Tests aren't too bad, pretty straight forward.

Literally so amazing. He's kind and understanding, just make sure you go to class and are paying attention. He's very nice about late work and is a super fair grader. He always let my class out at least an hour early.

LOVE. LOVE. LOVE. Fantastic professor, lectures were so fun, especially towards the end of the semester. I took this as a night class and he always ended 1-1.5 hours early. Take him!! Class is incredible, learned a lot.
Hands down the best teacher I have ever had in my life. He is extremely authentic and makes you feel comfortable in his classroom. Only downside is that he doesn't teach more classes at SMU!

His lectures are super super boring and so is the reading. Don't do the reading just buy the textbooks (he wrote all of them) and pay attention during class because he explains the reading anyways. All of the tests are take home open note, so do the study guides using your textbooks and you'll be fine. Don't miss class, it'll impact your grade.
Such a great professor. He is laid back and understanding of conflicts. Highly recommend.

He was such a great professor. I had him for a night class and we would normally get out an hour early. He was very engaging and relatable I looked forward to his classes because they were very interesting.

Loved this teacher he is so funny! Super relatable guy and makes you feel relaxed. I will say - do not turn anything in late and make sure to go to class. He does not accept late work and there are only 2 project papers, a midterm, and a final. One zero and you fail the class. The tests are a little hard - just take notes in class and use them!

My favorite professor here! Even though his class was online, I learned a lot. It's a bit of reading, but really interesting subject matter. He was also very kind when I had to quarantine and treated his students like equals. I thought the class was on the easier side.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at SMU!!! So understanding and kind. Hes a bit of a hard grader but you usually have opportunities for growth and he will let you make up to a higher grade. I wouldnt say its an Easy A but if you are on top of your work and actually try its not challenging.

One of my favorite professors I've had. He cares so much about his students and their success. He is so passionate about what he teaches and is sooo funny. As long as you do your work and turn it in on time, you'll be successful in his class. 10/10 recommend

Definitely recommend taking Jour2310 with Professor Lascity. Some of the lectures can get a little boring, but on presentation days the class has group discussions that are actually really interesting and fun. He's a funny guy and super nice. Gives tons of extra credit and is always available for help.
Professor Lascity is the best! Class in enjoyable and so interesting. Participation is absolutely necessary, go to class and talk! If you do, easy A. Would reccomend for everyone.

This was Lascity's first year at SMU and he was not bad at all. Attendance matters as he has you sign in everyday and if you do not participate in class that affects your grade also. Mostly lectures but you do have 2 presentation and 2 papers (like one page or two). Gives lots of extra credit and will help if you go to his office.

Show up, participate, and you will be known as his "star student". He does care about the success of his students, but only the students who prove to him they are willing to work hard. He has an enormous amount of work experience and incredible connections. He was a very hard teacher, there are def easier ones but overall I loved him!

Avoid Professor Mysore at all costs!!! Lectures are long, boring, and confusing. Asking questions in class just leaves you more confused. His tests are nearly impossible since all the answers are practically the same and he doesn't give any study guides. The project assigned has no rubric, examples, or explanation. Run far away!!!

AVOID AT ALL COST His test are impossible and they make zero sense. He says he cares about his students but then tells you that if you get lower than an 80 its your fault even though you spend days studying and he doesn't give you any helpful advice on how to fix it for next time. Group project isn't bad but his instructions are extremely unclear.

Professor Mysore teaches with the attitude of Robin Williams from Dead Poets Society, but doesn't teach the actual material. An actual quote from him, "I am trying to teach you without being descriptive". He would say he would give rubrics, then change his mind and take points off for stuff he never said we needed to have. There is better out there
Questions on the test are way harder than what he taught in class. Good guy just not a good teacher

Forming a relationship with Mysore is essential to success in this course. Participate in class, email him about the material, go to office hours, etc. The tests are really hard, but he is super knowledgeable about the field and has really amazing experience in marketing too. Definitely not an easy A, but I would take this course again.

He is a really good teacher, you just have to put in the work. There are tests and quizzes but the course revolves around one group project. If you see him in office hours and shoe him youre trying he will help you out. I think people dislike him because you actually have to try and apply yourself. Having him isnt the end of the world

Mysore is a good dude and clearly a great marketer but he can't teach. Spends the entire class reading the textbook/slides and doesn't cover the right material for the tests/quizzes half the time. Didn't give any sort of clear guidance for semester-long project either. Only saving grace was curving the overall grades. Avoid if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: nope...
Honestly, SMU should fire this man I AM NOT JOKING. I have encountered a lot of professors in my time, and I cannot even say he is the worst because that would be giving him to much credit.

Professor Mysore is a decent guy but his lectures are beyond boring. The tests are very hard and are 100% textbook-based. There is a major project that is weighted highly yet we barely discuss it in the class. I learned some concepts from this professor but truly disliked his teaching style. I wouldn't recommend this class.
Avoid at all costs. If you have to take marketing a semester later, do it. You do not want to take this class with Nick Mysore. He has great experience but is simply unqualified as a professor.

Tests are very hard and are made straight from the textbook. If you pay attention to the lectures and answer questions you should be fine. It is clear he knows what he is talking about and is very experienced in his field. Unfortunately, most of your grade in the class is dependent on a semester project but if you are well prepared you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and boring, tests are nearly impossible to pass, does not help students receive better grades even though he knows everyone is struggling. Giant project looming over the whole semester with lack of guidance. Test averages have been Ds and he doesn't curve.

The worst professor I've had at SMU. Do yourself a favor and do not take Nick Mysore's class. He has plenty of real world experience but is incapable of making sense of the material to any of his students; Not a real professor. Cannot lecture and oddly cannot answer his own exam questions without double checking. Failing avg on exams and quizzes!
You can not understand him. His test makes no sense. He grades weird and difficult. He expects you to know things that no one would ever know.

Lectures are ambiguous at best, weekly HW assignments take at least an hour each (+50 questions minimum). Group projects are rarely discussed in class leaving it entirely on the hands of us students. Not sure how he's able to teach at SMU... I'd strongly recommend NOT to enroll in his intro course!

He's not mean but he's not a good professor either. He will give lectures that always go past time and will give tests about things he did not teach. His powerpoints and documents are unorganized and its hard to look through his canvas. Even if you try, you might not get the best grade; and he will definitely call on you if you have an easy name.

Mysore was a good guy but he is simply not fit for this line of work. You can tell that he is very knowledgeable about the subject but fails to keep students engaged throughout his long lectures. The issue with him is really just the tests. Not only are questions ambiguous, but but he also throws in random facts about companies from his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Mysore is good at marketing but he teaches it like it's 1990. It's just a very boring lecture heavy course with a gigantic group project at the end. He tends to pick a handful of students and always call on them (I feel so bad for them). Just avoid this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am still baffled that this man teaches at SMU. Do not take MKTG with Mysore. This man has no idea how to teach an intro class. This might be his first time teaching, ever. Huge group project, hours of homework, and extremely hard tests. No rubrics. You could study the lectures and textbook and still only earn a B on the test. So beyond unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: take any other professor. so many people have dropped mid way through semester. long boring lectures that dont correlate with the test. you need to teach yourself to succeed in this class- even then its beyond hard to get an A. Approximately 500 questions a week for homework on top of extreme group project. absolutely terrible. not an intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: good guy and good marketer but the class is sooo boring. Almost nothing from the lecture is on the tests or quizzes, everything is from the boring textbook. The homework is also like 300 questions each time and everytime he assigns anything else his instructions are vague... have fun tryna figure out what to do. i gave up with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Mysore is very experienced in the field of marketing, but he cannot teach. Long boring lectures that have no specific purpose and are hard to follow along. Group project with no rubric (legit marketing proposal) in an intro class. Most students performed very poorly on the Midterm. First test average was a C and not curved. Hardest class.

This man is an incredible marketer, but his talents just do not translate to the teaching field. He drones on during class and expects you to listen to every second, as any word he says can be on the tests (which are too hard, and filled with trick questions). The classes, project, tests/quizzes are all just much for this level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He questions are vague lectures boring. The assignments take so much time. About 300 multiple choice questions and 2 chapters of textbook reading per week. I feel like I didn't learn anything because it is all busy work. Tests are hard to because you have to know everything in the text. Group project is so intensive. Too much for an intro class

Dr. Nam, although she was nice during office hours, was not a good teacher.  Condescending. Mistakes on exams (the correct answer was not an answer choice...), ambiguous wording, and no partial credit. I would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is nice overall but please do not take her. You will learn nothing in the class and the test just get harder and harder. Basically no partial credit on problems that should have partial credit and the wording of the exam questions can be ambiguous (She does not answer any questions during the exam)

overall terrible teacher, lectures are very difficult to get through, her exams are hit or miss depending on if she can write them correctly, grade distribution so close for Cox curve, would NOT take her if you don't have to, 0/10
Awful lectures, had incorrect answer choices on her MC questions so you would have to write on

Her lectures are a little dry, but she's a nice woman. Just do the slides a bunch of times for practice. The first exams are easier than the final, so prepare extra for the final. Nice woman, and she's passionate about the material. More conceptual concepts than corporate.

Very sweet, cute, nice in OH, and receptive to feedback! Tells you exactly what to study, so tests (except the very hard final) are straightforward. Worst part is that everyone does well so the curve is ruthless; A cutoffs on tests are at least 61/62. She teaches content well but inadvertently encourages a zero-sum environment for students.
Boring lectures and she makes exams pretty easy which ends up making the grade spreads super tight which can be frustrating at times

One of the most boring lecture classes I have been in before. She just rambles and half the class ends up zoning out and needing to relearn it for the test. The final project wasn't explained too well and so there was a lot of overall confusion. Also first test is much easier than the second (which everyone was freaked out after).

Clearly a very smart individual but has extremely boring lectures and will cite unimportant niche topics for a multiple point question on her tests. For projects, even when meeting with her repeatedly, she gave extremely low grades after very vague prompts. Disappointed with the quality of Cox professors.

I think Prof. Nam gets too much hate. Her lectures are super boring, but the tests are fair and half the class is just like HW and participation which is an easy 100. Her class really isn't that hard overall
Professor Nam was regularly available to meet via zoom for review sessions/group assist.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Nam, she's really nice and is always willing to help you. There's 2 exams and 2 group projects with some homework and quizzes in between. Her exam are fair and she prepared the class well. Very detailed and clear when giving instructions.

She was so great, im not sure why people hate on her, I loved her and the tests were pretty easy. She tries to make the class light and fun and seems like a really nice person. Take her if you have the chance

Horrible! Worst finance teacher in Cox! I would not recommend her to anyone. She is very condescending and does not answer questions. Her exam reviews are nothing like the test and are a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nam is undoubtedly the single worst professor I've had in my four years at SMU. I'm sure she excels in her academic research but the fact that she holds a lecturing role is deeply embarrassing for SMU as a school  someone with such a condescending and demeaning attitude towards her students belongs nowhere near a classroom
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nam is a brilliant person, yet her success in academia has failed to transform into a teaching role. She is incapable of adequately explaining the contents of the class to her students, alongside will either dodge questions asked or laugh at them. She is a sweet person, but SMU needs to understand some people just weren't meant to teach.

Worst Cox professor. You can't understand a word she says, and when you ask a question she just laughs and gives no help. Boring lectures and will keep you the WHOLE time, even if the lecture is done. Tests are curveballs with multiple-choice A-Z (26 possible answers). Took the final 2 weeks ago and don't have my grade yet, no idea what I have.

Jayoung is probably the worst professor in the finance department. We have no idea what our grades are going into the final. I haven't learned a single thing during class because Jayoung can't explain anything. I can't express how much I've hated this class

One of the worst professors I have had at SMU. You cannot understand a single word she says due to her poor English. Half of my notes I leave "___" because I am not sure what she said. She will also laugh in your face if your question is "too dumb". Additionally, office hours are useless and good luck with the exams, many curveballs.

IDK how you nicely tell someone you can't understand squat coming out of their mouth bc of their accent. Even our ppts have broken english . I spend more time trying to decipher in my head what she just said in English rather than learning the material. Additionally, she's one of the worst explainers I have had in Cox. Gotta teach yourself here.

Her English is pretty bad, and she talks very slow. Her exams are insanely long for the time given. However, the class itself and the material covered are hard, so she can't make it easier. Expect about 42 questions for the cumulative final - a combination of multiple-step questions and essays.
She is forcing you to learn by yourself instead of teaching you to learn!!! Just take another professor's course

One of my bottom 5 profs at SMU. She's difficult to understand, and useless in office hours. I did a lot of teaching myself in this class. Tests are monstrously long and so hard to finish on time. To be fair, I had a super busy semester and probably should have dedicated more time to this class, but overall frustrating and disappointing.

She cares about the students as long as they reach out to her and pay attention during classes. It seems like many students don't pay attention during the lectures and then complain when it comes to exams/homework. This is a course that you need to study and participate in to make the most out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She isn't clear about what is expected from you on homework and tests. She doesn't accept partial credit for tests either and makes them way too long. She tests you on material you have never learned. I would absolutely not take this teacher- she has no experience teaching and doesn't know what to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down worst teacher I've had while at SMU. Her lectures are confusing, she never finishes them, she is not accessible to students outside of class, and her tests cover concepts not taught. On top of all of this, she makes it clear that she does not care about her students. Take in spring with different teacher 100%.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS ANYWAY!!!

She goes over on every single lecture then forces you to teach yourself the problems she skips outside of class by watching videos she makes after-the-fact. Her tests are way harder than the homework, which makes no sense because you have to teach yourself how to complete all the homework anyway since she can never get to enough examples in class.
Overrated and impossible. Didn't explain things well. Is rude.

Professor Walcott is difficult, but by far one of the best professors I've ever had - if not the best.  I genuinely learned the material.  He's just a great teacher, breaks it down in a way you can really understand.

I loved Professor Walcott! He is definitely a tough grader and the tests are hard, but if you pay attention and study with the past tests with enough time to feel comfortable with the material you will do well. He appreciates students coming to office hours with genuine questions.

He is a very harsh grader when it comes to exams and projects but goes well into depth for each concept. His exams are all short answer, 3-5 questions. Cares about the explanations behind each finance concept. He is not an easy professor, but if you want an easier professor, I suggest taking a different one. If you want to learn, then take him.

Probably one of the best professors at SMU. He is very organized and is REALLY good at explaining things. Very helpful in office hours but also a harsh grader (since there is a curve it does not matter that much) Pay attention to the "why?" behind every concept and you will do well. Tests have a lot of conceptual questions.

The class is run exceptionally well and is almost exclusively based on exams, with a small percentage coming from HW and participation. If you can do better than the average, you will do well. He gives you almost all exams he has ever administered for you to have ample material to practice on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Felt more like a power trip than a class. Lectures are rambling nonsense, and grades are just weapons. Half the class dropped or failed. Expect no support, no clarity, and absolutely no accountability.

Unorganized and doesn't explain things well but sure ah thinks he does. Huge ego with nothing to back it and the worst teacher I've ever had. Curves to make sure he gets only and only the right number of As no matter what you really earn. Worst class I've taken.

He is a nice person and is knowledgeable about finance. His exams don't cover every concept and have 6 questions, which can be tough. But there is partial credit and grading is adjusted on the bell curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Walcott is a good teacher and very knowledgeable about his subject. That said, this class is very difficult. You HAVE to pay attention to lecture, take notes, and make a serious effort. 

One thing that does help is that the class is so hard that you only have to do slightly better than average on the tests to benefit from the curve.

Midterm and final were HARD do not be fooled this class is hard but to put on top the slides were unorganized and there was not enough examples to understand the material. The class and Walcott did not make me feel comfortable to speak up in class and ask questions. Not a terrible professor but Ive had WAY better. This class is hard, PREPARE!!!

Mr Walcott is really smart and gives great lectures, great class to learn finance topics. His test are really hard so study in anticipation, but if you study enough the tests arent that bad. If you a finance major i recommend taking him if not i say take someone easier. Overall great professor, class is structured clearly and well, great class.

As someone who struggled like hell here & also not a finance major, I can tell you that you're gonna have to grind to live & breathe this stuff to perform remotely well before a curve. The man himself has the voice & passion for the subject, like the narrator in a crime show, unlike the kangaroo mess that is the lab... Just like any other @SMU.

I am not a finance major and struggled in this class. Professor Walcott was ok, but I wish we had done more practice problems to understand how to apply the material. His exams are HARD do not be fooled but he does it on purpose and then curves. The class is difficult as it is but Walcott makes it even harder. It was ok but I would never take again

I would not recommend Walcott especially for non finance majors. He goes on long tangents about topics in upper level finance classes that have nothing to do with this intro finance course. He grades extremely difficult and makes his tests really hard and brags about that. Not the worst SMU prof but don't take if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Like everyone else he's gotten a lot harder and frankly ruder. Can't teach worth a damn and yet acts like he's gift to academia. Stay away if you value your gpa.
Terrible teacher and bad at preparing us for exams. Should have stayed in CO cuz we don't want him.
This guy will fail you with a smile in his face.
Terrible teacher, no help, no useful examples, DO NOT TAKE. DO NOT TAKE. DO NOT TAKE.

Amazing professor! His slides and lectures were extremely helpful! Test are difficult so definitely make sure to study. He provides you with everything you need to study in order to be successful on the exams. DO NOT procrastinate studying for his exams!!! He actually cares that students understand and learn from his course.
Best finance professor, top notch lecture, just need to pay attention in class and take notes, not much extra reading needed. Would recommend to anyone

He did a good job with real world applications, the course was very case study and group project based. This means the final has a lot of weight and creates the grade distribution - it is a very hard exam. Walcott really prepares you for the real world and I enjoyed the class. It's not an easy A, but you learn.

Nice guy, but his way of lecturing at students for over an hour with 0 examples. Class isnt productive and it's hard to retain anything. Really only graded on group projects which are almost impossible to get above a B- on if you arent already a finance genius. Grading criteria isn't clear, Avoid him at all costs if u rly want to learn and succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Walcott is genuinely a nice person. He expects every person in his class to have an advanced understanding of the course material and presents lectures on concepts with no practice or application. Group projects are assigned and you must work with the same group again. The course is not well laid out to foster growth in Finance.

Professor Walcott is extremely passionate about the material he teaches. The projects are difficult, but rewarding, and in general if you provide sufficient care and attention to the material, you will do well.

Professor walcott provides confusing lectures and you will have to do tons of work outside of class if you want to pass. He has strict policies and often you will feel as if he is annoyed with his students. He gives random pop quizzes every 2 classes and expects you to have knowledge of calculus already. Not a good teacher, you will need to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Provides no help on hw and lectures are confusing. Why did cu hire this guy

Professor Walcott is a genuine professor of financial knowledge, and in my experience at the university, one of my favorite professors (I am a Marketing major). He speaks clearly and in an entertaining manner. His lectures are good, his exams are also 'challenging' as they should be, and his approach is caring and understanding.

Put in the work, and you'll succeed. Walcott's going to push you to truly understand the material. By far the class I've learned the most in. Tests are hard, but he gives his old ones to study. If you go to lecture and take good notes, study 3 hours a week, you're going to get an A
Perhaps the greatest professor I've had here at SMU. Class is tough, but rewarding for those who put in the effort. Not much else to say, great guy!

Walcott's class is challenging but he is a very good teacher. You have to pay attention in class if you want to do well on exams. His lectures are extremely helpful and he answers questions thoroughly if you have them. He has office hours multiple times each week. MyFinanceLab homeworks are pretty easy. Exams are difficult, study in advance.

Walcott is a really great guy and an excellent professor. He is probably the most difficult Intro to Finance professor at SMU, but there is a department-wide curve for the course so it doesn't really matter. He posts all of his past exams which is incredibly helpful for studying. If you are willing to master the past exams, an A is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredible professor! Genuinely wants his students to learn the content taught, and is very fair with his grading and feedback. Definitely one of my favorite teachers at SMU!

This professor is one of my favorites at SMU! He makes you work for an A (based on a curve), but gives you all of the resources to succeed. His lectures are a great mix of theory/problems, is very helpful in office hours, and gives you past exams for midterm/final review. Definitely take this professor!!

Walcott is the gem man, he is so good at teaching!!! I took his FINA 4125 because I had him for FINA 3320. 4125 really helps with advanced financial management and you get lots of practice with financial modeling. This class is an easy A as long as you don't get lost. If you are looking for an easy course just for credit and learn a ton, take it!

It's a hard class forsure, but I loved this professor. He teaches well and uses analogies to help connect you to the problems. You have all the old tests so if you want to do well in this class, do about 10 of the old tests for your upcoming tests. Its stressful and a lot but he clearly knows what he's talking about and shows that he cares.

Hardest thing about this class is that you're graded on a curve with 25% making A's, 25% A-, and the rest is "up to his discretion." Really great prof; got me really interested in finance. Knows his stuff and does a great job explaining it. He gives you old tests to study, hardest part is competing with the finance tryhards for a good grade.

Walcott's exams (and the class in general) are not a walk in the park. Your overall grade is on a class curve and he makes you work to earn your spot, wherever that may be. However, as a finance major, I am glad I took his class. As stressful as the exams are, they prepare you well for anything you do in finance. Provides plenty of practice exams.

Walcott is known for being hard finance professor. Heads up he is extremely picky when it comes to grading quizzes and exams. He does NOT post powerpoints. Again, his class is so hard, it is based on a curve. Beware, take another professor

Walcott is the best professor I've taken in Cox. The testes are extremely hard and studying for them is so stressful, but I actually learned a lot from him and I believe that he is the best professor to take for Intro if you are majoring in finance. He gives you all the old tests and quizzes to help you study too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very tough class, but I think Walcott does a great job of making the material as easy to understand as possible. Grades on a curve.

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Explains concepts very fully and expectations are very clear. All old tests/quizzes and answers are online for studying. Its definitley hard but you are given the materials to be successful and will remember what you learned in class. Relative grading scale with top 20% making an A.

Walcott is by far the best finance professor at SMU. Take him for every finance course that you can if you want to learn. His tests are hard, but he gives you the tools to do well and actually remember the material after the class is over.

reviews.comment: Walcott is the best professor I have taken in Cox. His lecture pace is fairly slow and he makes sure everyone understands.

Professor Walcott has been by far the best professor I have had at SMU so far. He is so straight-forward and thoroughly explains the concepts that he lectures on. His tests are difficult IF you do not prepare thoroughly for them. He gives you more than enough practice material to do well on his exams. If you prepare then the tests aren't bad at all
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His tests are very thorough and difficult, but he has all his past exams which makes them easy to study for. He is an absolute wizard in explaining complex mathmatical concepts. I  enjoyed his class very much and actually felt like I had a deep understanding of the subject.

He wants us to LEARN the material. Assigned work is an assessment of our understanding. If you just want to get the grade and move on without growing in finance, then yeah- take a different professor.  BUT, if you want to learn finance, entering the job market with conversational level understanding, then you'd better take Walcott!
His tests are extremely hard. That being said, he gives a lot of partial credit on tests, and is available to help you. You will learn and remember so much from his class.
Tests are very difficult, but he is an excellent professor.  He reminds me of Ted Mosby from How I Met Your Mother, sounds just like him!

Walcott is a fantastic teacher as long as you pay attention and really commit to learning the material. Yes the tests are just as difficult as everyone says, but he curves them heavily and dishes out partial credit on problems wherever he can. He gives you all the material you need to do well and is extremely helpful at his office hours.

Walcott really knows what he is talking about and makes finance easier for students to understand.  For corporate, he gives you lectures in between case study topics but majority of classes are discussion based .  Expect to speak in class if you are taking 4325 seeing as he graded participation and to devote time outside of class doing cases.

Professor Walcott is one of the best professors I have had at SMU. Investments is not the most exciting subject to teach, and although I would not say the lectures are exciting, he did a great job at teaching the material, and the class is really not that difficult. If you are somewhat of a good student, you can expect to do well in his class.
I am a senior and took Walcott for into, international, and investments. As long as you go to class and can follow along you will do well. Great professor that I would highly recommend.

Definitely one of my favorite professors at SMU. Took this class for the Business minor over J Term. Classes are meant to be 6 hours long and most days we got out after 3 hours. He has a great personality and is very easy going.

Walcott has hard tests, but he gives you the resources to prepare for them.  He posts practice tests and quizzes online for each test and each quiz that give you an idea of what to expect.  You have to understand the material and go to class, but he will never cold call on you and require you to participate if you are confused.  Great guy.
Don't expect any sympathy from him for extenuating circumstances that keep you out of class.

FINA 3320 is a tough class in general, but Walcott is a great professor. He's organized, clear, concise, not condescending, and kind. If he knows you're trying hard, he'll take that into account. Have to go to class otherwise you won't get all the notes. Tests are hard, but practice consistently and you'll be fine.

Walcott is a great guy. He does a good job of explaining tough concepts and makes himself available during office hours and via email. Does take FOREVER to return assignmentstests back but overall would recommend him. Attendance is mandatory in that he doesn't post his completed notes online so either go to class or get them from a friend.
loved him! so helpful and definitely fair. would suggest him to anyone in Cox!!

I really enjoyed him. He challenged you to apply principles to problems without the fear of failure. VERY generous grading scale (top 20%=A, next 20=A-, next 20=B+, next 20=B). Cutoffs for As on the tests were normally around 78. He makes the class pretty stressfree with two midterms, a final, and 3/4 quizzes counting toward grade

Do not take Walcott. Attendance is not mandatory but he doesn't post notes online/makes you write down everything (he removes everything important from his powerpoints before posting them) so you're screwed if you don't go/miss a class. Tests are insane. All I ever did in his class was copy notes

Took portfolio management with him this spring- his tests are crazy hard but you get a notecard that can have anything on it and huge curves made ~70% a B+ even in a class full of alt asset students. Homeworks not too easy but can (and should) do in groups
Fantastic. His exams are crazy hard, but they are curved so much that a 70% can be an A-, easily. He is really clear, and always available to help students. Take him! I loved his class!

His lectures are okay, can be a bit confusing at times. He helps who he wants to help & tends to be a bit cold towards others. His tests are extremely difficult. If you aren't familiar with finance jargon then get acquainted with it before taking his class or you'll be lost. There's no required textbook but buy one ANYWAY.

Advanced Financial Management (corporate finance) with Walcott was fantastic.  The class is entirely case based with a few assignments to apply what we learned.  He also lectures a little bit to introduce topics.  You must speak up during the daily case discussion to get an A.  His class is a must for Investment banking interviews.

Does he really know his field? well, I don't think so. 
Does he have good quality research in his area? I don't think so

Computer Science Professor who is not checking his emails, and students lost Financial aid, and couldn't take class for a semester. The art is for what ? For the people/humanity or for the artist him/herself ?  We need you Leonardo Da Vinci the greatest engineer in this era...

good personality , I like it. the course is fun. exams are good (not hard + not easy) . the problem comes with communication and appointments. not involved with students or researchers deeply. not welcoming new ideas and sticking to what he learned in books (stay with standards, no need for new ideas in this area !!!)

Good course structure, homeworks lot of learnings

reviews.comment: Terrible professor for a terrible class. Expect lecture to be nothing but monotonous slide readings. Homeworks are all ripped from the internet. I love his style of teaching. He is from the industry and got lot of real world experience. He always gives examples from his experience and it helped me understand the material better. He is very approachable and available to help. His exams might be a little tough, but gives good grades. He is one of the best teachers I had at SMU

thick, monotonous accent. long boring lectures and just read the slides without explaining. this course could've been interesting and helpful for landing a decent job but we didn't learn anything. total waste of time.
the best professor I have ever had at SMU. Actually cares teaching and does it out of pure passion. very nice and will always be willing to help.

Wonderful class about sports, but it mainly focused on the legal side. Prof Newberg is very knowledgeable and got me interested in law school. The lectures are long, but the guest speakers make it worth it, and there are only two exams. Overall, I would take it again and I recommend Professor Newberg to everybody!

Great professor! The guest speakers were always the best and made the class really engaging. Some of the lectures can get long-winded but he always does a good job of tying them into relevant topics. Very caring and very approachable for anything. 10/10 recommend his class.

One of the best professors I have had at SMU. While he has long lectures, he tries to get the class to interact and they are interesting. You have to stay engaged the whole time and take notes because they will be helpful for tests. Not that much homework, two tests, some extra credit opportunities, he also curves a lot. A lot of guest speakers too

reviews.comment: all around stand up guy. Doesn't post lectures so you have to pay attention the entire 3 hour class but he is very intelligent and passionate about teaching. Not a blow off class but not difficult to receive an A either if you study a little and make a effort. Great guy makes his class as interesting as possible, alot of good guest speakers

take professor newberg. his class is amazing and it teaches you so many things. he is not a tough grader at all and he genuinely cares about his students. I wish the class wasn't a 3 hour class because after some point it can be tiring.

Let me put you on Professor Newberg. BY FAR the best professor I've had so far during my three years at SMU. I've never rated a professor before, but I had to hop on here to make sure the certified goat gets the respect he deserves. Lectures are heavy, but I've never seen a professor so dedicated to helping his students succeed.

Is a lawyer and comes to SMU to teach night class. He is very passionate about what he does. A few assignments, midterm & final. Do the extra credit. Take good notes in class, powerpoints aren't posted. Goes the full time class is scheduled, speak during discussions to get a good participation grade. Class made me interested in law school

He was extremely helpful when it came down to extra assistance on an assignment or group project. His lectures are set up well with many visuals. The best part is he has some great guest speakers throughout the course that were very intriguing!

She lectures the whole time but confuses herself, since she dives into so many unnecessary topics, therefore at the end of the class period I questioned what I was learning. No more than 3 absences, and the way she grades papers/essays is ridiculous, be ready to get no more than a 90, and even then its close to impossible. Pick any other professor.

reviews.comment: This professor is impossible to please unless you align completely with the extreme and unnatural beliefs expressed in class disguised as core material. Rude, condescending, irritable and makes a terribly uncomfortable course environment with her personal beliefs on full display.

Beth is a super sweet, passionate, and funny professor. She loves poetry and has an abundance of knowledge that she is excited to share. While class time is relaxed and gives the impression of an easy course, the papers are held to high standards that cater to her understanding of the poems. Not hard, but harder than expected. Go to office hours!

Took her for Brit Lit II. She does not organize her lecture very well so I feel like we are rushing every class and can barely scratch the surface of the material. But she is very funny and kind and grades fairly. So pretty good overall. She also tries to make class interesting by discussing student's writing or having us act out a play, etc.

Dr. Newman's class fosters excellent discussion. She is extraordinarily passionate. Also very accommodating of students' schedules. Dr. Newman helps you see how a rigorous dive into literature can be fascinating, fun, and rewarding. You will get lost in the Victorian era in the best way possible.

Great professor, highly recommend. Unaware of issues the negative reviews suggest. As an English major, I appreciated how she was always willing to help. She is also a very clear and entertaining lecturer.

I enjoyed class time, lectures and the readings. I took this class as the only freshman among juniors and seniors and often found myself embarrassed by the professor. I received nothing above a C+ with terrible feedback. The professor made me feel completely unqualified to be in the class as an English major. Very rude & inconsiderate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I just had to rate Professor Newman after seeing her score. Despite some prior negative reviews, she is an amazing teacher and individual. She is open to all beliefs and wants to explore different viewpoints. She grades fairly and tells you what she expects. Sometimes gets off-topic, but only because she's passionate about her subject!

Professor Newman is great. I took her Victorian Writers class over the Brontes, and had a great time. We discuss interesting things within the novels at length and have some entertaining-yet-still-productive class conversations. There's a pretty normal amount of reading homework, but nothing crazy if you pace yourself. Only 3 four-page papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Newman is incredibly difficult to deal with. She has no class plan, no interest in hearing other opinions, and no set method for her grading. It is near impossible to please her unless you align completely with her extreme and unnatural beliefs.
incredibly disorganized and scatterbrained...worst professor I've had at SMU by far! she is also a raging feminist, liberal, and agnostic. if you don't agree with her completely, you're screwed.
A joke of a course and an excuse for a teacher.

She's great! While the FRQs were hard, the rest of the test was usually easy. However, our class had FRQs and free response questions while other sections didn't. I'm not sure how fair that is. It was an enjoyable class overall.

Jamie is a younger prof so she is super understanding and caring about the needs of her students. Your grade is based on 3 tests and a group project in which you design a dating profile for a theorist (super easy). The tests are lecture and textbook heavy but they are pretty easy as long as you keep up with the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is young and fun. She makes her lectures engaging and listens to the concerns of her students. She cares deeply about each student and is a pretty great prof. keep in mind. TEXTBOOK READING IS A REQUIREMENT! She tests heavily on book content that isnt covered in class, but if you read and pay attention an A shouldnt be too hard

There's a lot of material to learn quickly if you don't have much coding experience. His quizzes and tests look for very specific details, but there are so many opportunities for grades in other ways like in class exercises, assignments, and a project. If you aren't procrastinating he really wants to help you succeed and is easy to communicate with

Definitely a solid choice if looking for a STAT elective. Came in only having took STAT2331 and did fine. If you're looking for an easy A, this is NOT the class. He does evaluate your work compared to other students in the class, so you don't know exactly where you stand until the end. Go to office hours. Utilize the TAs. Go over the powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. He has your peers rank your work for your grades (as if they're not biased...), average on first test was a 57, and moves the syllabus around. He hands out 100+ slide powerpoints (1-2 per class) and any minute detail within SAS or R is fair game.
Taken three times now. Intro class is fine enough I suppose. For any higher level class, he is a complete mess. Would avoid at any cost.

Dr. Ng is great! Quizzes every class easy, but tests hard, especially multiple choice, short answer easy bc he tells you what type of q it will be. Will check hw in office hrs b4 it’s due so you get 100. Witty, has a “statistic of the day” interesting and funny. Lab is blow off class but have to show up bc attendance taken, usually get done early.

Took STAT 2331 for J-Term and got an A.  One of my favorite teachers so far at SMU. Knows Stats extremely well, explains everything clearly, and very willing to help (gave us phone number). We had breaks every hour or so and got 2 hours for lunch and to complete in-class assignment. Had take-home quizzes (easy) and practice tests. Great teacher!
His tests are so specific and tricky. You have to read every little detail. And his grading scale is hard. An A is around 95!

Tony gives quizzes every class to keep attendance high, but they're very easy and a grade booster. He repeats things a lot to make sure you understand the concepts and is great. Best stats teacher for sure!

I took Stat 2331 with Ian Harris and got a D-. I dropped and took Tony and got an A. THE BEST PROFESSOR. Really helpful, review before the test and do a couple of homework and you get your A. DO NOT TAKE WITH IAN HARRIS. TAKE TONY IF HE'S EVEN AVAILABLE.

Very nice man. Mispronounces some words, but you get used to it. Tests can be tricky and were only out of 50 points which meant a couple of wrong m/c could throw you below a 90 quickly. He certainly does take the class average into consideration with final grades and does curve when needed.

Attendance is mandatory; there are quizzes every class, but it's easy to make a 100 quiz average. Lab is also attendance based. Homework due once a week from the book, usually 3-7 problems. Tests are SPECIFIC. Spell out every detail or lose easy points. Sweet professor: wants you to do well, but also requires you to earn the grade.

Professor Tony is really nice and helpful.On the other hand his exams are very hard. They are not like practice exams at all.Sometimes there are a lot of questions and many students run out of time.So overall he is a fun and helpful teacher but his exams are hard and attendance is mandatory. Plus there is weekly homework
Hard to understand sometimes but the lab helps. As long as you take the quizes and do the hw then the test will be easy.

Easy class, daily quizzes used for attendance purposes (not hard at all) Tests are easy, about 12 multiple choice that can be found by studying lecture notes given to you online and 3 short answer that are straight from the practice test with different numbers. Plus he lets you use a formula card. REALLY REALLY EASY A!

Great Professor!  Gives homework straight from the notes.  Gives a mock practice exam before every exam.  Is very willing to help his students and offers several help sessions before tests.  I would HIGHLY advise anyone to take his class over any other Statistics professor at SMU!  You'll do great!
He puts notes on the web, which are very helpful it is not necessairy to go to class if you have the notes.  His english is a little hard to understand but he really knows the material.

Long list that I cant put here. Put simply, avoid. She attempted to refuse a doctor's note for an excused absence, she doesn't use her own rubric to grade, is extremely harsh on grading, offers next to no extra credit opportunities, extremely strict attendance policy so much so you're screwed if you miss more than 3 classes for any reason.
Very nice professor and gives decent feedback on papers but almost never gives A+ on papers. Only way to get A+ on papers is by doing extra credit

The absolute worst teacher I've had in my entire life. It's impossible to get an A on. Your grade matters on 3 essays, and she's the strictest grader ever. I doubt she reads the essays in depth because I've gotten the same grades for these essays. She also rarely gives extra credit, but they are usually like presentations or talks, late at night.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Newton can be a bit hard to understand at times, and her class can get boring, but overall, she is a good teacher. She is a super sweet lady and will let you make up quizzes if it isn't a repetitive thing. I'm taking her again next semester. She isn't a crazy hard grader, plus she tells you most problems with your writing in conferences.

(WTR 2304) Very nice lady, really hard to understand at times. We have like 3 paper grades all semester and that's it. i would say she is a pretty tough grader. I still can't manage to get an A on a paper even though I consider myself a good writer. Painfully boring class. Take someone else if you can.
She graded really harshly and made it absolutely impossible to get an A

Great professor but classes were very long and boring at times. Be ready to read 3+ texts before each class and discuss them. Not a super tough grader. I found that once you understand her grading style you can easily make an A on papers. I wouldn't suggest that you take her, but if she's your only option the class isn't terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: AVOID!!! Pauline Newton has singlehandedly made me consider transferring from SMU. Thank God I didn't take her WRTR1312 course because I would have transferred. There is a complete lack of motivation, an impossible rubric, and a predetermined grade for all papers. Do not get sick because she will show no compassion attendance wise. THE WORST PROF!!

reviews.comment: Unable to give constructive criticism

reviews.comment: WRTR1313 Pauline Newton was the worst professor I have had at SMU. This was a writer class but would have been better classified as a study of subconscious bias. She was mostly unreachable outside of class but when she was, she was unhelpful. She would literally take away points for suggestions she offered if you were even able to reach her.  Awful

AVOID! Pauline is the worst. Especially if you decide to be involved in greek life. She seems to have a personal vendetta against her 1313 course. Don't expect an A, because you wont get one. Her criteria for papers share no similarities with the rubrics given. I am convinced that she has a predetermined grade for you before you submit your paper.

Don't take Professor Newton. This class is the longest class on campus, and she never ever lets anyone out early. Even on days when everyone finishes their work early, she will find some sort of assignment to make sure everyone stays the entirety of the class. If you miss more than two classes, you automatically fail...

Still did not figure out what she really wants. Her expectations of writing papers are out of this world. Avoid her at any cost if you like to get a good grade. Her classes are super boring and annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst Teacher At SMU hands down

Nice lady but she's tough to reach out of class and even if you can then she doesn't give helpful feedback. I went to the ALEC 3 times per essay and everyone I talked to got the same grade for every one so I don't really think she reads them. Not engaging in class. Only graded on a few essays.
DONT TAKE HER!! SHE IS THE WORST

Unbelievably hard to understand in class, doesn't post her assignments on the canvas calendar, never ever clear about what we are doing in class. 99% of the time I have absolutely no idea what is happening in class. Stay away from this prof. if you can! If you get her, expect to do a lot of work for a measly wrtr class that won't matter ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst teacher. Does not know what she is talking about. In class, the discussion is held by the students doesnt give input of her own. She wont give personal feedback and just asks you what you should fix. Gives poor grades without reason. hard to understand her when she talks.

Dr. Newton is a nice lady who cares about her students and is passionate about her classes. She doesn't assign a lot of reading or random assignments. Your grade basically comes down to 3 major essays. She grades these essays EXTREMELY hard. She won't fail anyone, but to get above an A-, you have to be an ELITE writer. Don't expect an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Newton might have been my least favorite teacher Ive taken. She does not teach much in class, but you are only graded on writing. She is very hard to access outside of class. Dr. Newton is a nice lady, but I wouldnt recommend taking this class. She is a very hard grader and she doesnt forgive any grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this DISC 1313 class. Professor Newton grades super hard for no reason and her grading makes no sense at all. She spends way too much time rambling in class over the same two topics. I put in my best effort and was only given a B+, because she rarely gives As. Overall, would never take a class from her again. Nice woman though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is the such a sweetheart. She gives you the grade you deserve. As long as you complete the assignments and participate in class discussions, you will do well. There are several class readings, but they easy reads. There are three essays, a presentation and a bibliography. She gives you a grade for attendance and participation.

Dr. Newton is really nice. If you are a decent writer and go to her for help often, youll make an A. I made the mistake of thinking I would be okay without her help on my first essay and got a bad grade. Even if you dont have a question, make up a question so she sees youre trying. She answers every email and make sure you go the writing center
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Her class is so much harder than any other 1313 disc. She's also an insanely hard grader considering she doesn't teach anything and has a rubric she doesn't stick to. The classes are a majority of open discussion over the excessive amount of articles, passages AND books we have to read. Don't take this class if you're looking for an easy grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Prof. Newtons class. Our lectures about the course theme of travel were interesting. Make sure you read because she does random pop quizzes. She is a tough grader but wants you to do well. If you talk to her, ask her questions, and participate you will do good in her class. Just work hard and she will help you to succeed.

Prof Pauline is a very caring professor. She is not the easiest grader and your grades are almost all from your essays. I am not the best writer but I pulled out an A- so it is definitely manageable. Biggest advice would be to ask for her help. She will respond to any email with a question you might have about your essay. Work hard on the essays.

Pauline is a very interesting professor in that she has opinions on all of the material. I took her for the American Identity section. Very boring section to be sure and many of the readings were awful. She's a very nice and relatable person, but she has a bit of a strange voice. Not too much reading, pretty fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: she is quite good. I really enjoying her class .though English hasn't been my farvouite, she has really encouraged me to read and improve my writing. she also has a great sense of humor !
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So many other Disc teachers you should take. Dr. Newton doesn't really teach you anything and is no longer an easy A like she used to be. Not a lot of work but the class is extremely boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Newton is a great option for 1313 at SMU. Her lectures are discussion based so as long as you do the readings and come to class prepared with something intelligent to say then you'll be just fine. Go to her office hours throughout the writing process and she'll give you great pointers on your papers and ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Newton's class isn't particularly noteworthy, and most of the time you actually go to class it feels like nothing happens. There are three essays in the year, so once every month or so you will have to put in a lot of work, but other than that the only thing you have to do is show up. The books she chose were good at least!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Newton is a very good professor. Despite what everyone says here, she isn't a tough grader. All you have to do is read, analyze, and make sure you're writing at a college level. She is very accommodating if you can't make her office hours, and the ALEC is always available to help! She can be boring, but just do your work and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Newton is really nice, but she's not an incredibly intriguing professor. She is an incredibly hard grader, and does not use a rubric on her papers, so its hard to know what she is taking off for. She has even said herself that she is one of the harder 1313 professors. She is nice though, but I would not take again.

Really cares about her students. Had a few family things come up and she was really understanding about going to a different section of her class or seeing me for extra help.
