reviews.comment: While this class requires a bit of effort, it is amazing and worth your time. I have learned so much about the different religions and my perspective on religion has truly been changed. There are weekly readings with notes, however these are essentially a completion grade. Aside from this, there are 2 exams and 2 papers. Overall a great class.

Lectures are pointless and the class is a joke that will ruin your gpa. I copied down her lectures word for word and recorded and copied everything perfectly, all useless. Course way too difficult for an elective, not helpful at all, rude and condescending toward students, fails to receive any constructive criticism at all. New but still no excuse.
Professor Arratia really surprised me and I found a love for photography in this class. I wish SMU would keep their good professors more often. Great class!

Easy class as long as you do the work and participate. If photography is your main medium as an art major might be disappointed, didn't learn anything I didn't already know. SMU needs a better photography department overall.

Way too much work for an intro to photography class. Additionally, you are required to provide your own camera for the class. If you are looking at this class as a fun way to learn about photography or fulfill a cc, this is the wrong class. Put more work into this class than anything else last semester.

Prof Arratia was great at challenging artists to think differently through the use of narrative. I enjoyed all of the projects in this class. Her insight was helpful during workdays and great during critiques. Im not going to say much on attendance bc you really shouldn't be missing your art courses, she does grade on it too. Overall, chill class.

Great Professor! I was hesitant taking this class because art is subjective, but this professor works with all subject matter. There are a lot of assignments and photos you have to take so there was no room for slacking but good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Olivia helped me to fall in love with photography as an art form. I didn't think I would like doing photography as much. I took her summer class.
I learned alot in this class and created a nice portfolio in the class. Professor is super kind and will go out of her way to help you on a project. Will take again!

Guy's a piece of work. Lectures are slow and monotone, and he legit just reads off the slide as if we can't read. Test reviews are vague af, but then tests will ask specific ?s like stats, DSM criteria, drug types, etc. Not accessible for office hours (TA's a real one). He seems like a chill guy, but he can't teach. If you like psyc, avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know how that person has an A+ because he explicitly told us the highest grade in the class was a B lol. He is monotone and might be the least helpful professor ever, but if you study long and hard and meet with the TA often, you'll do fine. It's a hard class regardless of who you take it with but he definitely doesn't make it any easier.

It is true that his lectures are insanely boring and monotone. But with that being said, the exams are not that difficult and If you study the slides/textbook you should be fine. there is a curve that helps as well. Have an A+ right now without being in class in 3 months so I think the other reviewers are a bit dramatic

Lectures are boring and not engaging in any way, he just reads off of the slides. It is a guessing game as to what will be on the tests but you are expected to know everything from lectures and the textbook.The class is comprised of 3 exams (you can drop one) and 1 cumulative final. It is very challenging to score well on exams, do not take.

His lectures were unbearable (a painful 1 hour and 20 minutes), so much so I dozed off every class. If he enjoys teaching, I wouldn't know because he's monotone and lacks enthusiasm. Your grade is comprised of three difficult exams. His "study guides" (general lists) and the specificity of the exams don't align. It's impossible to succeed. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE ANYONE ELSE. Straight A student and I am struggling to make a B- in this class. He is so rude and says things are "above his pay grade". Grades super hard, everyone is averaging a B- rn. No grades besides 4 hard tests that he does not give a study guide for. Tests us on specific statistics and percentages that no one knows. I am so upset
Pass/Fail class. All you need to do his pass your Excel certification test and you'll be fine
Professor Trevino was super helpful outside of class, but she doesn't teach the course. This class isn't very difficult at all. Just do all of the assignments and show up and you will pass the class.

There isn't much to say about the class because it's mostly workshop and presentation based. Trevino serves more as a moderator than a professor. At times she can be preppy and standoffish, but the interaction is limited.

Super easy pass/fail class. Just complete the assignments and you're good. You get two absences per semester and there is one required class. Professor Trevino doesn't teach any of the classes, as guest speakers are brought in.
You have to try really hard to fail this class. Just show up! There are very few assignments. Trevino just monitors and gives announcements, she is not teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BLI is easy if you don't miss more than 2 classes and do the CMC assignments. The professor doesn't really matter.

Just show up to class and do the few assignments in this class to pass. The bulk of the class is hearing from all the departments at Cox, so Trevino is hardly ever teaching anyways. The biggest assignment was the paper at the beginning of the semester but its basically just a completion grade. BLI is a free class and Trevino is a fine choice.

Trevino is a solid choice for BLI 1110. Only assigns a few things which are spread out across the semester and as long as you do it, you will pass the class (the one credit section is on Pass/ Fail). You are allowed to miss 2 out of the 14 classes (one of the classes is mandatory). Each class is just a presentation from a different person in Cox.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WORST BLI PROFESSOR EVER!!! Do not take for BLI. She takes it waaaayyy too seriously for a class that you learn nothing. Will make you write a whole essay with 3 sources cited if you miss class, even if you have doctors note. Take a diff professor!!!

Orlovsky is the sweetest old man at SMU. He's awesome to chat during office hours with, and is genuinely interested in his students doing well. One of the only downsides to his in-person class is that there is absolutely no agenda, powerpoint, lecture notes, etc. The reading can be dense, but honestly, you don't have to do all of them. good luck!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orlovsky is a really nice guy who knows a lot about Russian history. His class was easy: I took online Russian history and had a midterm, a final, and one other assignment. The only problem is that he is a (really) boring lecturer who gets lost in tangents, making it hard to pay attention and take notes. Still-good choice for an easy history class!

Professor Orlovsky is a brilliant man and knows everything there is to know about Russian history. He tends to run off on tangents, but he's a really nice guy. It is really difficult to understand what he is actually teaching because of how deep in tangents he gets. He also does not organize his syllabus. It is a pretty confusing layout.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof! Cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed, only grades were 2 papers, midterm/final, attendance matters but classes are interesting. Got 12 books for the course but never read a single one, which is why the lectures are so important bc he tells you what he wants in the papers. Sit in the front bc he's hard to hear

No canvas page, all assignments are given out on paper with no other way to access them. Does not even remotely follow the syllabus. Incredibly boring lectures. Angry mean guy. Fades out at the end of all his sentences so good luck taking notes. Assigned 10 pg midterm over spring break.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Epic professor. has a great sense of humor. took his european diplomacy class. Ask him anything about Russia.... he will start talking non-stop cuz he is passionate of Russian history. honestly an Easy A class if u just come to class, listen and take good notes. lots of opportunities for extra credit !
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: There is nothing good about this class other than it doesn't matter if you pay attention in class and the essays are very straightforward. He is an extremely boring lecturer and is not personable at all. Kind of a miserable man, but is relatively easy to get a good grade.

Do not buy any books! It seems like you are going to use them all the time but I used the books once . You do not need to read to pass! The entire grade is two papers and attendance. Papers are not difficult but I recommend going to his office hours for help. Class itself was boring but extremely easy to get away with doing nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the greatest professor. That is not just a figure of speech, so take it literally. Just shows up to class and you will know everything about whatever subject he is lecturing on. Very knowledgeable and laid back. Pay attention and you will learn a great many things.

Prof. Orlovsky really knows his stuff. Make sure to sit near the front though because he mumbles and assumes you're not paying attention if you sit in the back. Grading scale is a bit off, wants very specific answers but only asks huge, generic questions. Hard to know what he actually wanted you to write.

Great professor at sum! really enjoyed his class. As funny as a professor can get, so do not expect too much. We got 3 grades, two take home exams (really easy) and a take home final (even easier). Both were essays and he gives you plenty of time to finish, we got 2-3 weeks! Makes the material interesting as well, TAKE HIM!
Best professor at SMU. Really knows material and cares about his students. He wants you to get a good grade. A lot of reading and in class note taking, but very clear expectations from the beginning.

Great professor!  Really knows the material.  If you pay attention in class, the tests aren't that difficult.  The hardest thing was figuring out what he wanted for the papers, but just go to his office and ask.

I had no interest in Russia whatsoever until this class. One of the best professors i have ever met.  knows material like his own childhood.  FANTASTIC!!! I was surprised when I got an a, i figured he'd expect more, but all you have to do is prove understanding of his class and youre good.

An insane amount of reading required for this class, but it's worth it. Excellent at helping you get the big picture while he remembers the most intricate details about his subject. Makes you WANT to pay attention and write notes until your hand falls off. Loves to get to know his students, and long memory when it comes to SMU politics. Great class
great teacher
Very nice man and knows his stuff.

Orlovsky is a GREAT person/professor. He is so knowledgable and really enjoys his job. Usually assigns a lot of reading, but grade is generally based on take-home midterm and final exam-maybe a short paper somewhere in the middle. Get to know him during the class-he loves getting to know his students
Do NOT take this class if you're expecting an easy A. He's far too sarcastic and full of himself to care about his students. The group projects are terrible as well because he's tedious.
Tests are easy if you memorize the review packet. Essays are a little harder but he gives out good grades on them. Class can get boring but he's a good teacher!

This class is the worst. The professor is extremely vague and even though its an intro class, you would never know because by the end of it you won't know what you have learned. He says that he doesn't like to teach the traditional way, but by not teaching that way you don't learn. There is also a miserable film project at the end.

Dr. Olsberg keeps his lectures intersting, and very converstional yet he never forces people to talk as it is tecnically a lecture. He's young and interesting, knows a tons about culture, human behavior, and what's happening in the world today. The study guide is exactly what is on the test. I skimmed it and got a B on the first test.

I scored 100s/125s across all of Orr's exams even though I worked really hard for an A. Do all the suggested problems twice for Orr's first two exams (for FRQ). Pay careful attention and read the chapters twice (for MC). Then, you'll do better. 70/30: MC/free response. Get good at MC. Each question is 5 points! Don't miss a class; take audio rec.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Genetics at SMU is definitely a mess. Dr. Orr teaches the first half of the semester and Dr. Jones teaches the second. My advice is to do well on the first two tests that Orr makes as they are based off the book problems and what he does in lecture so they aren't too bad. Also, do as well as you possibly can on the homework as it can help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Orr's half of the semester is much more math-based, and he is good at conveying such concepts during lecture. His tests can be tough, but with enough studying, they aren't impossible. Make sure you do well in his half of the class though, because the second half gets significantly more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He goes off the powerpoint to do problems a lot. His homework is tough but if you do the suggested problems you should be fine in the end. Whoever grades the homework is a tough grader so make sure your little mistakes are fixed before turning it in. You have a week for homework and exams are pretty much like the previous years' exams he posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are sometimes very confusing and he goes off on a tangent often. The homework problems are a lot different than what he teaches in class, so you'll have to skip the chapters to find out how to do them. The tests are mostly like the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I don't know why the ratings for Dr. Orr are so bad! I thought he was a wonderful professor. He explains concepts and problems pretty clearly and is always happy to go over things again. Tests aren't hard as long as you've done the suggested problems and you've kept up with the readings. The first half is heavy on problem solving, so practice!

I don't know why the ratings for Dr. Orr are so bad! I thought he was a wonderful professor. He explains concepts and problems pretty clearly and is always happy to go over things again. Tests aren't hard as long as you've done the suggested problems and you've kept up with the readings. The first half is heavy on problem, so practice!

He teaches the first half of the semester. Look over the text book and do practice problems, definitely go over class slides on your own. A typical science teacher, lectures can get pretty boring but he is a very nice person, does a lot of examples and always willing to answer any questions. A lot of learning will have to occur on your own time

He teaches the first half. He is not that helpful and the tests are not comparable to what is taught in class. over all all of the work needs to be done by the student. Read on your own, Learn on your own, Do Not Count on Him.

Dr. Orr teaches the first half of the genetics course. He is a good lecturer who spends part of each lecture working through example problems, some of which come from or are similar to the homework he assigns. If you can do the homework, you can do well on his tests. He is very helpful and approachable if you have any questions.
He grades coursework very late, a tough grader tbh. He does not explain concepts thoroughly
Very intelligent and knowlegable. A lot of work but was very fair in his grading. Learned A LOT !!! Very challenging

Took forever to grade assignments and projects.  Didn't use the book, all from his powerpoints.  Excellent knowledge of the material.  Knew what he was talking about, lot's of real, practical examples, discussed in class
Helpful

I had this guy for one of my graduate level courses. He put the whole class to sleep with PowerPoints. He also ignored emails from the students and took weeks to grade homework which he never explained what you missed or why. I really wish I could get my money back on this one.
Excellent communicator, great class content, very organized. Lots of homework...but homework good prep for tests.
Very informative and helpful
Truly informative. Sometimes the lectures are boring.
Very informative with lots of practical industry experience to illustrate important points.

Took this class to satisfy some common curriculum breadth requirements (IT SATISFIES 3 BTW!!) and ended up totally loving it!! I took it as a summer class in June, it met MWF from 12:00 to 3 but really only goes until 2:30. Before each class you have to watch a film and write a page and half on a prompt, usually really not that difficult. ESSAYS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had her for North African Cinema. She's a very knowledgable teacher and really helpful, and her lectures are interesting. Though there's a ton of writing and homework, she's a relatively easy grader and lenient with due dates. I came away from the class feeling like I had learned a lot, and I have a new appreciation for foreign cinema.
She's a great teacher and expects you to do the work. All classes are discussion based and there are sometimes quizzes on blackboard. If you do the work and participate in class you will do well.
I thought this class would be easy. I mean, who doesn't want a grade for watching movies. I had to read and work more than I thought, but it was a great class.
He is such a nice person. His lectures are kinda boring but he really wants you to succeed. He made a point to get to know his students.

Volkan is like your dad. He wants to teach you and this is his passion. I had a really small class so it might be different when there for people but he learned all of our names and made it a super positive area to learn. Half way through the semester he started cold calling us to problems, which seems scary but it isnt, its actually  fun.
the GOAT

This was a very fun class to take with Dr. Otugen. You learn really important things about professional engineering. Graded by 2 presentations, 2 write-ups, and 1 final report. Guest-lecturers shared really valuable and relevant experience. Applies to many different fields of engineering. Dr. Otugen was an easy grader and a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Otugen is hands-down one of the best professors at SMU. He made fluids extremely easy to learn, and gave easy homework and tests. He has a great personality, really tries to connect with his students, and wants to work with you. I wish I could take the rest of my classes here with him. Go to class and study, as tests are 90% of the final grade.

What a nightmare. I can usually get by A's even with a bad professors by reading the book and doing extra work on my own, but he really takes very, very, very horrible teaching to a new level. Avoid him like the plague. Wastes most of class time writing every word he utters on the board instead of example problems and equations.
He would ruin my day every time I would have to go to his class.

I am not a math person but I enjoyed his class and the material. He provides a lot of notes and examples that are similar to the ones on the homework and exams. The class is very straightforward, attendance isn't required but it helps to go, and the subject matter isn't extremely difficult to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pf. Ozerturk was a solid professor for Strategic Behavior. Three exams worth 30% of your grade each, and three HW's worth 10% of your grade. He was very unclear during lectures, however he was extremely helpful in his office hours. The exams are very similar to the HW and he will tell you exactly what's on the test. Just go to his office hours!!!
Great professor ! Straight forward
great prof,
Not a super easy class but he tells you what you need to know for the tests. Go over the practice tests and make an effort to understand the material and you'll do fine.

Pr. Ozerturk presents exactly the things you need to know with out any fluff. If you schedule office time with concise problems or issues, he will go above and beyond to what is expected, and help you figure out any aspect of the course you do not understand.

OTURK IS THE MAN  3 classes with him.  2 tests, 2 open note quizzes.  His class is focused on test material, go to class + redo the quiz and example problems = A on tests.  This guy is so funny, also knows a ton about whats going on in the finnancial market.
Knows a lot about what's going on in financial markets. Worth taking his class only for that

tok 4368 and 4378. class periods  focus on what will be on the test. review before test tells you what exactly will be on the test(just different numbers) gives 2 open note quizzes a midterm and a final. not helpful outside of class but if you go to class you willbe bored but you will be successful. no reason why an A shouldnt be made. i made two

great professor! gives test review which is VERY similar to the test. i have not made an A in college in about 5 semesters...and i made an A in his class. go to class, take notes, get the review, practice the review over n over for tests and youll make an A. also gives 2 open note quizzes

Excellent! Don't be thrown off by his accent. Doesn't say much but knows a lot! Explains so carefully and clearly that every one can understand. The course work is not overwhelming. ATTEND CLASS! I did not open the book AT ALL and got > 100 average in the class. He writes on the board all you need. Copy and read. A great guy!

Professor Ozerturk is a good professor. You will have to try but Money and Banking was quite simply informative and not overwhelming hard to obtain an A. Overall, I would take Ozerturk for Money and Banking!
the guy is a genius!
Worst professor.  Cant understand a damn thing.
She made many errors during class and on the answer keys for exam practice problems. Tests and the cases are hard. She puts the last thing she taught on the exams without going over it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Brutal. Shes nice enough but man, she cant teach. Lectures are filled with errors, and she is usually unable to answer a question that isnt directly from the slides. shocks me that she has such great credentials.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the most divisive teachers in the business school. I took her for two classes, and they were both that I could rely on to get a solid A. Some people get it, some people don't. She explains each concept with plenty of examples but I guess it just doesn't click for some people.

I am honestly confused why people rate her so low. I took her for International, am currently in her Investments class, and am taking her for Derivatives next semester and am excited. She honestly works hard to give students decent grades, asks for feedback constantly, and cares about the students. She is chill to talk to too. Would recommend her.

Professor O was heavily misunderstood. She gives upwards of 50% of the class A/A-s grades. Did I learn much? No, I agree to an extent with the other comments, but did anyone who participated in class get an A? Yea pretty much. Also all homework is done in groups. Attendance is crucial and sometimes gives extra credit participation quizzes.

I have never had a teacher at the college level that has been so poor at relaying the information to the students. Her tests were nothing like the work done in class, or the "study" pieces. She requires in-class attendance, however class time is not spent effectively as she is good for a few mistakes each lecture (don't use a pen). DO NOT TAKE.

This class was one of my worst experiences at SMU. Professor Ozuguz is unhelpful and does not know the material she is teaching. She constantly makes mistakes in class. Her exams do not cover what the lectures or homework cover at all. Avoid her class like the plague

I think he gets a lot of flak due to the flipped format, but as long as you pay attention and study - you will be fine. The homework does have guidance and he does have office hours. Also rely on the tutors at school for help that are free. It's not a class you can skate by in, but it does pay off for prep throughout the rest of the program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: First half of the course is tougher than the second half. If you spend time to understand the concepts in first half, the rest of the course is a breeze. The group project is also a significant part of your grade and is time consuming. Professor Park is funny guy and generally grades generously. Although, he can be difficult to hear at times.

Graded with AI, assigned work with AI, probably answered emails with AI. But if you use AI, it's war crimes and academic dishonor. Got a zero for “suspicious phrasing.” No receipts, just vibes and hypocrisy.

Dr. Park was a great professor, it was a lot of material but he made it so that we understand the concept and not specific formulas. He was also entertaining and took time to help us understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Park is an excellent professor. The class material is challenging, but he wants his students to be successful and gives them the necessary resources. He does offer some opportunities to earn extra points throughout the course as well. I highly recommend Professor Park for MAST 6478 as an MBA student.

I blame the class structure more than the professor here in that the structure and content of the course was just bad. There were 3 class presentations and all groups had the same presentation! My understanding is that the course is more or less "set" by the department. Bad and confusing lecturer. Gives ample amounts of bonus points though.

Professor Joon is a very caring professor. He is always happy to help you inside and outside the class. The class was extremely heavy on assignments and projects. It was definitely the most time-consuming class I took this semester. He gives several extra credit opportunities so you will have a chance to make up for some poor grades.
Demanded a lot from his students. However, if you show up, participate and take good notes, you will get a good grade in the class.

He demands a lot from his students but if you show up to class, participate and take good notes you will have no problem doing well. He doesn't want you to fail... he wants you to do well and gives you all the tools to do so. He also has really interesting career experiences that he shares

Hard to understand, not helpful, even participating in class by raising my hand and answering at least a question per class is not enough to get the full participation grade, exams are challenging. If Foxman's classes are full, he's fine - he just teaches straight off the powerpoint, but you have to be in class in order to get participation credit.

Literally the worst professor I have ever had. I'm Phi Beta Kappa/Beta Gamma Sigma, I doubt I can even get an A-, AND I TA FOR STATISTICS! He can't speak english, doesn't know how to teach, and grades totally unfairly. He loves trick questions, and doesn't understand curving or partial credit: 3 points off for doing part A wrong (worth 2) is "fair"
All in all, good class. As long as you go to class and listen, the exam are not hard at all.

This professor should be let go. The entire class is confused and really has no idea what his lectures are about. He reads directly from the slides which are useless for studying, and his tests do not fairly cover the material in the slides. Grading is objective; no way to find correct answers-if you ever recieve the tests back. Very poor English.

let me give everyone looking at this a piece of advice.. do not go anywhere near this prof... hes from korea and does not speak english.. in finance or acct thats one thing, cuz u can just study hard, but u need to kno what hes talking about and if u cant hear him, how can u learn.. his tests are tough, and he is completely random.. one of the wors
No Comments
Calling in her job she doesn't even care to teach.
Literally the best prof for WRTR. Easy A. You never need to come to class. No homework, no final, no tests. Just 2 essays throughout the semester. TAKE HER!!!
Well I quite liked Kate! She's cool and charming which is so helpful especially when it comes to alleviating awkward moments. She's a good professor.

Professor Kate was one of my favorite teachers in a long time since early high school. Out of all my first semester classes as a freshman this year, her class was definitely my favorite. The discussions were very inviting and thought-provoking and allowed me to grow a lot as a person and as a writer. You need to take one of her classes!

Kate's an incredible teacher that truly cares about her students. She assigned fun essay prompts that give you a lot of freedom. She's a bit of a tough grader, but gives great feedback and is always willing to help you. The class is very discussion heavy, but she always tried to keep it relevant to us and fun. I couldn't recommend her class more!!!
This professor waits until the last minute to enter in final grades. She gave a whole letter grade below what I was expecting and what I had all year. Do not take her. Bad attitude.

I would best describe Kate as a very amiable and conversational professor, with her class rooted on relaxed  discussion of topics among your peers. Oftentimes, the atmosphere may feel awkward, but she's great at easing this with her charm. I do suggest reading the assigned material to enhance your class experience and your academics on essay time.

She is very helpful and clearly cares about her students. Her class is very conversation-based and you become pretty close with your classmates. She makes it fun and it is not lecture-heavy at all. There is a good amount of reading homework but nothing super challenging or lengthy.

Great professor but the grading is pretty tough. Even if you have had experience with upper level English courses in high school you still might be at risk for a B in a supposed "easy A" class. Petsche says that participation is most important but regardless if you participate in the awkward lectures, she can still be ruthless with the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ms. Petsche is one of the nicest and down-to-earth professors I've had. She was awesome from day 1 and was super nice. She grades essays fairly but it is not easy to get an A on an essay. She engages the whole class all the time and makes going to her class fun. You have to write a one-page response paper weekly, but they are easy and fun.

Kate really cares about you as an individual. She tries to make class fun and gives us choices in what we want to analyze and write about. She is there to guide us but doesn't baby us. Wish I could take her next semester but all her slots were taken!
She is the best WRTR teacher. Definitely take her class if you can

Kate is fantastic. Even with awkward class seminars she works really hard to keep the conversation flowing. Make sure you schedule appointments with her to discuss what you will write about for your essay. She is relatively young and relates to college freshman. Very understanding and caring. You will learn a lot from her class. Just participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. She always gives excellent and in-depth feedback on all essays and she is always available for help. In class, she keeps things very personal and comfortable. If you put in the effort, you will get an A.

I 100% recommend taking Professor Petsche, she is amazing. She is very understanding and is very accessible outside of class. She has helped me improve my writing skills a ton as well. I definitely got a lot out of the class. The work load really isn't bad at all either.

Petsche was awesome. She cares about what students think and what they are interested in. Discussions are very interesting. When there is an essay assignment she talks to each student individually to help them brain storm and organize their ideas. Definitely my favorite professor teacher in the department.

easily one of the most caring and thoughtful professors i've had here at SMU. always finds a way to stay interesting and keep everyone involved. put in effort, participate, and you'll have no trouble with this class. i'm a CS major and Prof. Petesche made me consider pursuing english. definitely take her if you can.

Professor Petsche is the best! I always looked forward to going to class. She is very organized and clear about the class schedule. She has office hours many times a week and genuinely cares about her students. If you put in the work you will do great! There are 4 essays and a weekly one page assignment to write about a topic from class.

Professor Carton has easily been one of my favorite professors. This class is not a normal course, so it was interesting navigating it. I am so glad that I took this class with him though, he is the BEST professor for it! Seriously, if you have the opportunity to take Professional Development with Professor Carton, I highly recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do no recommend this class under any circumstances. At this point just cut the APSM program, if this guy is this one in charge. What a waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Highly dont recommend. i literally have nothing else to say
Terrible Class. All he does is talk about himself and he is a harsh grader for no reason. You will learn nothing and it is so boring. Lectures are mandatory. Assignments are a waste of time.

Prof. Carton may seem intensive to some students, but a lot of the work done in his course will benefit you long term. Really stresses real world application in the assigned work, which is a positive as it might help you network with influential people in the sports industry.

Carton is a great professor who cares about his students, especially in a small class environment. His midterm and final exams are pretty random, but it makes you think. Learned a lot about the sports industry and even had a project where we presented to the CFO of Mavericks. Gives you real-life work experience. Overall great.
Professor Carton is one of my favorite professors. I have learned a lot. Do the work and you will do well. He respects and cares for his students . Overall awesome class.
Professor Carton is a nice guy and has lots of tools available to help you succeed in the job world. His class work is tough however and requires major amounts of work.

Carton is awesome - really wants the best for his students and wants to provide you with real world application in class. Pretty solid guest speakers with the opportunity to network. Loves to cold call so make sure you're paying attention in class - other than that, he's a pretty solid choice for APSM
Great teacher and mentor but you have to put in the effort

This professor is very unprofessional. She will get all up in your personal space and is very biased with certain students. Her grading is most likely based off of if she likes you or not. She tends to make uncomfortable and inappropriate questions towards students depending on their ethnicity.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Professor Peng's teaching fell short of expectations. She struggled to engage students or earn their respect, delayed posting grades until the last two weeks and provided no feedback throughout the semester. If you want an easy A do not take her class.
Very unfair and tough grader. Hard to communicate with and is just not understandable in class. Very biased teacher.

She's extremely biased, she openly said she hates men. She gets upset when students express views that differ from hers. Her behavior is invasive and inappropriate she'll rub your shoulder, get in your face while talking, and call everyone “cutie.” It's uncomfortable and completely unprofessional.
She's just a lousy teacher.

The readings were really well chosen. not too much, but super relevant and interesting. Our discussions were probably my favorite part of the class. Loved hearing what everyone had to say and it felt like our views all mattered.

I am a straight-A major, I have a high GPA for whatever reason that only the prof knows, 
I can't get out of teh B-range. Do not take this class. She is passive aggressive and rude when
you ask questions and many people write on here the same experience but the remarks disappear.

Dr. P is my most favorite professor of all time. Not only is she brilliant, but she truly cares about each of her students. The way she facilitates conversation makes her classroom a safe space for all opinions, and my most favorite thing about her is that she treats her students as equals and is willing to learn from them. Took her all 4 years!

Dr. Pergadia is a great professor—thoughtful, encouraging, kind, with helpful feedback, great reading selections and creative assignments.  She lets you write on things you're interested in, and fostered a sense of community among students.  Plus, she's a safe space if you need to talk about something that's affecting your schoolwork.

Dr. Pergadia was one of my favorite professors at SMU and my favorite English Professor. She gave clear feedback on papers and was available outside of class. Her classes made me a better writer and her lectures were very interesting and added value to the texts we read. She is open to other interpretations of readings which is often rare.

Dr. Pergadia was one of my favorite profs at SMU. So intelligent and kind, and she really made me think differently about everything we read. She has high but fair expectations for essays. Definitely would recommend taking one of her classes, especially if you're an English major!
My absolute favorite professor. She was nice, supportive, and kept the class interesting. Attend her lecture, engage in discussion, and you will not only get a good grade but enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Pergadia is a walking encyclopedia for me. She has so much knowledge about EVERYTHING that it blows my mind! She's incredible with her lectures and her ppts are so engaging! She encourages her students to do better and gives amazing feedback. If someday I become a teacher, I'd want to be like her. Absolutely the best!

Professor Pergadia gives her students an insurmountable level of support, which in turn enables her students to reach their highest potentials. She dedicates her time to helping students craft research questions that best suit their personal needs without compromising their own scholarly vision. She's a staple of SMU English, and a true gift.

Dr. Pergadia is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is incredibly knowledgable of her field and is a genuinely caring and encouraging person. Her course was one of the formative steps in the development of my research for my dissertation.

Dr. Pergadia is a brilliant and inspiring professor. Her seminars are always engaging and thought-provoking, and she brings the real world into the classroom through her pedagogy. Outside the classroom she prioritizes connecting with students through the topics they are interested in, meeting each person at their level and offering encouragement.

I have taken several classes with Dr. Pergadia and she has become one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are engaging and the discussions in class made me think in new ways. She was always very respectful to students' views and their interpretations. Fair grader and gives helpful feedback. Her class helped me grow a lot in my writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is amazing and lectures are fun and entertaining. Never a dull moment, and topics are always thought provoking and challenging. Caring and respectful to any situation that may come against you, always talk to her about it. Any issue you may have outside of school or with class she will always try to accommodate!

Dr. Pergadia is a brilliant professor who challenges students and believes in them. She gives thorough feedback, connects literary study to real life, and is always willing to provide help or clarification as needed. I have taken three classes with her and would take more if I could. Truly a wonderful person and instructor.

Truly an amazing professor. She can take the most complicated obscure thing ever, and condense it down, flipping it in a way that matters to every student in the classroom. She makes it relatable and is completely open to whatever you want to do for your final paper. She gives insightful feedback and is always willing to listen and help you.

Dr. Pergadia is a brilliant and passionate professor. She has high expectations of her students and really makes her classes enjoyable, interesting, and will absolutely do her best to help you succeed. She is also extremely supportive of your ideas and comments in class. Absolutely take her!

Took her for distinction seminar. Very good if you do the readings & apply yourself. Had small class size so it's obvious when you aren't engaged with the material/conversation. This is the second time I've had her as a professor and am very happy to have taken a class with her again. Be ready to read quite a bit but reading material files provided

reviews.comment: You get what you put into get classes. Do the reading and show up to office hours and you'll do well.
Objectively a very bad professor who can't teach concepts well.

Pergadia is AMAZING at what she does! Just read, consistently participate, and meet with her outside of class to discuss your paper. Even if the reading or assignment criteria are confusing, speak up!! She clarifies anything you need + it counts toward participation, which is 25% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pergadia was very sweet and kind and cares about her students. Her class however is a bit difficult especially if you haven't taken literature before. Her assignment instructions for the final project and annotated bib are unclear and ambiguous. So it'd be hard to do well if you don't email her for further instructions. my peers were quite odd too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: The readings and discussions were tough, but Dr. Pergadia is a great professor and she supports her students so much. She is easy to talk to and provides helpful guidance for assignments. I would love to take one of her ENGL classes again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Pergadia is brilliant. She changed how I think about almost everything'. We did some group projects that were pretty cool for doing a deep dive into a topic

Professor Pergadia is very nice and you can tell she cares about her students. Class consisted of some in-class writing assignments, two papers, and a group presentation. Not a free A but it's def possible if you put in the effort and show up to class. Her class was pretty disorganized and she would cancel often, but she is super sweet.
One of the best professors I've ever had. She opened up my ability to read everything from Shakespeare to Get Out. Never been so intellectually stimulated by a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Pergadia is one of my favorite professors at SMU. Her knowledge about the subject area is endless and I left each class with an enriched understanding of the readings and feeling inspired to study more literature. She helped me learn how to read and analyze a book for it's deeper meaning.
