reviews.comment: She's really nice and pretty funny too.
A brilliant professor who is truly passionate about her subject. I walked away from every class with a deeper understanding of the books we read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Pergadia is my favorite professor at SMU. The mini-lectures she posted before class were fascinating deep dives into the material. She also strengthened my ability to analyze film and literature. There is a lot of reading for the class, so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Pergadia is kind, intelligent, and accessible to students. She is really well-versed in her topics of teaching (racial/societal injustice, African American literature, etc), a lot of the grade is participation/discussion posts which are p easy. She isn't a strict grader if you put in the effort. One of my fav professors, take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is extremely degrading. She gets annoyed very easily about questions. She gave a lecture on the first day of class that we would not do well in this class and refused to encourage us. I do not recommend her.

Dr. Patty makes General Chemistry unnecessarily hard. She gives you twenty minutes to do quizzes which simply isn't enough time. She is extremely rude and intimidating in lecture and belittles students. She tests you on the hardest material and will make you wish you had never taken chemistry.

She makes chem MUCH harder than it needs to be. I always felt worthless leaving her class and office hours. She insults students that struggle and expresses her emotions by throwing objects across the room or pulling papers out of student's hands. She is just downright mean. I spent hours doing homework & going to every office hour op to only fail.

Look, here is the thing, you will either LOVE or hate this professor. I just happened to be on her good side. I honestly thought I would dislike this professor, but I realized that with a bit of hard work and enthusiasm, it is possible to get an A. If I can do it, then anyone can. I used to be awful at chem (got a 2 on the AP test) but I made it!
Rude to students and almost no office hours. The tests have very little partial credit and are your entire grade. As a student who has always gotten A's, this class is extremely hard.

My experience with Dr. Patty was definitely not as positive as many of the ones posted here. I did my homework, and emailed her questions as often as I could (since her office hours changed mid-semester). I still failed, she posted none of the grades we made in the class, and emailed days later. I found her teaching to be rushed and ineffective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Patty is an extremely tough professor but very thorough with her teaching course. Attend office hours, do ALL the homework she assigns although its not graded it will tremendously improve your grade on her tests. Great professor but do not take her if you're not up to putting in a great amount of outside class work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Patty's students do better in every other science class because they are so well prepared. She's a great teacher and you will learn the material forwards backwards and sideways. Worth the effort! Go to office hours and actually make an effort to get your questions answered to get that A.

If you're willing to put the time and effort into this class, you will do well. But time management and understanding your own learning process is essential. If you're good at math, it will help you tremendously. If not, that's okay, just plan in some extra time to grasp the concepts. Do all the problems at least twice - three times if you can.

If you're a pre-med student and you're thinking of not taking Dr. Patty, just drop pre-med now. If you can't handle Dr. Patty, no way you'll make it through med school. Dr. Patty is amazing and pushes you to your limit. Your grade will look terrible for a while, but she curves at the end. Be at every office hours and get all your questions answered
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely the hardest but most rewarding class I've ever taken. I put in at least 12+ hours of work per week outside class but it really paid off in the end. This class is a must-take for pre-med students. Truthfully I think everyone in Patty's class is going to do much better than everyone else in O-Chem. This class is not for the faint of heart.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken, but would 100% take again. She makes you work for your grade, but if you are willing to put in some time you can do well. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! It gives her a chance to know you. The class is on a MAJOR curve so don't stress during the semester, but work hard. She taught me so much and I'm happy I took her for Chem 1&2

Hardest class I have ever taken. She makes it very clear that her course is one of the hardest at SMU and that she's going to make you work for your grade. With that said, if you work hard, go to office hours, and truly understand the material you'll do just fine. She curves and wants to give good grades to hard workers. A must take for pre-meds.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: No quizzes mean no checks on if we comprehend material before tests. Grading curve is PURELY SUBJECTIVE, even after the final. There is no sure way of knowing if you are failing because she changes her curve to accommodate the students she is failing after every test. "Has hours" but not approachable outside/in class for questions if youre confused
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It is not impossible to do well. If you have taken AP chem, are taking fewer than 18 hours, and have a very math-oriented brain, you will be fine. However, I have none of these advantages, and I am failing halfway through her Gen Chem 2 course. I do all of the problems twice, put more effort in than I have for any other class ever, and I have an F.

Dr. Patty is hard. That's a good thing. You will actually learn Chemistry in her class. Your grades will not look so hot, but if you put the work in and go in for office hours, you can make it out with an A. Be ready to work for your grade. I respect Patty's students more than any other profs because they didn't take the easy way out.

One of the most difficult and rewarding classes I've taken. She is tough -but fair- and extremely helpful in and out of class. In order to pass, homework, practice quizzes, and reading are a MUST (I spent 4-6 hrs/week). Providing you have a good work ethic, I would highly recommend Professor Patty for an in-depth understanding of chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Absolutely brutal class, tests, quizzes, everything is rough. You will learn, but it will be forceful
Dr. Patty is an amazing professor.  In class she can seem a bit cold but go into her office hours, she is so helpful.  She definitely makes you work for your grade but you will learn so much.

Absolutely no. Would recommend taking a different professor if can. I took her class first semester got a C- then redid the course because unsatisfied with my grade. With 2 different teachers sharing the semester I redid, I got an A. Terrible teaching style, and will yell at you in office hours. She's terrifying.

Dr. Patty is terrifying, confusing, and goes far too quickly during lectures. However, if you go to her office hours and catch her at a less busy time, she is very helpful and you will actually understand the material. Old tests and self-made practice tests are the best way to study; as well as doing every problem repeatedly.

Dr. Patty is a difficult professor, but in her defense, Gen chem is hard EVERYWHERE. I had her for both 1 and 2, and did pretty well. I did not go to every lecture. But if you study about three or four nights before each exam/quiz and understand every hwk problem AND how to do it quickly, you WILL make an A. But this is no blow off class.

I had a background in Chemistry, yet I found it hard to keep up with the workload. Weekly Quizzes that might mess up your grade, so be careful. She likes to live up to what everybody says about her, so do expect a hard semester.

I used to hate chemistry in high school and sucked at it. For some reason Dr. Patty somehow made me want to do amazingly in chem, and I work really hard in that class. Take her class if you want a fantastic, rewarding education. If you just want the credit but don't care about chem, don't take her class. You will definitely "earn"  an A here.

I have incredibly mixed feelings about Patty as an instructor. While this class is way more stressful than it should be and requires an extraordinary amount of dedication to do well, I am still choosing to take her for 1304. The stress and requirement of dedication has made me learn this stuff like the back of my hand.
WORST PROFESSOR AT SMU!!

Easily one of the worst teachers at SMU - do not take her class if you need a good grade want to learn. She is not knowledgable about the subject, as evidenced by her teaching an introductory, General chemistry class and nothing at a higher level. Her class is basically just large amounts of tedious, banal homework and impossibly difficult tests.

She's really not that great of a professor. She continually makes mistakes and makes the tests unnecessarily hard. Furthermore, she justifies her difficulty by talking nonsense about medical school and how "harder" the other professor(s) is. I took this class without planning on going to medical school and I definitely do not recommend her.

I absolutely LOVE Dr. Patty. Gen Chem is probably one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, but its worth it. Do the homework (at least twice). Go to her office hours and get to know her! She's very scary at first but if you actually take the time to meet her, you'll be surprised.

It's definitely a weed out course but if you take the time to do EVERY single homework problem at least twice you can do well in the class. The toughest thing about the tests is the time. Everybody could do well if they had longer time but in her class you can't hesitate. You either know it or you fail.

Hardest class I have ever taken so far! You REALLY have to study and practice, practice, practice for this class (unless you're already pretty good at general chemistry from AP background). However, she is one of the sweetest professors I've met. She will answer all your questions during office hours.  She's difficult and challenging in a good way.

Very... thorough with the material. I literally spent hours a day to try and understand the material. Her virtual office hours are a good source of Q&A and is a better alternative than going into her office hours, in my opinion. I'm performing poorly because of stupid mistakes on test. If you know the material, you should be fine. Study hard. HARD.

Would NOT recommend taking this class. Although she tries to be a "good teacher", Patty is horrible at teaching the material and then grades it to an impossibly difficult standard. Class will suck away ALL your study time just to pass. Additionally, has a rather unfriendly attitude in general.

Very difficult. Her exams are very intense with little writing space, completed under 50 minutes. If you are successful in her class, then it prepare you for something like the MCAT. I would definitely not recommend her if you just need to get through a semester of chem for a Geology or MechEng degree. Your cortisol levels will definitely increase.

She's literally the best. The class is super tough, and you have to do all the work required twice, but if you need help, she's always there for you. Her office hours are SO helpful and she really wants you to succeed. It's a tough class and she isn't going to just hand you an A, but if you work hard and put in the effort, you can get a good grade.

If you hadn't taken AP chem in high school this class will be very, very hard. good class to take just for the sake of learning how to put forth effort in college, if you didn't have to do so in high school.

Dr. Patty has a bad rep because of students who aren't willing to put in the work. The woman is literally a saint. If you go to office hours she will literally sit there with you until you understand. One of the greatest professors I've ever had. She  does everything she can to prepare you for higher level courses.

Easily one of my fave teachers at SMU because she genuinely cares. It is a very challenging class. Unless you are naturally good at Chemistry, this should be your only difficult class in a semester because you have to dedicate a lot of time to it. Go to office hours, even if you don't have questions. Someone is bound to ask something that you didn't even realize that you didn't know! If you are looking for an A without putting in all that much effort, don't take the class.

The most challenging chemistry teacher at SMU. She has high expectations for her students: you cannot simply memorize and regurgitate information, all her exams focus on applying information in new situations. It's a challenging course, but by the end you'll know the ins and outs of gen chem.

Take Dr. Patty's class if you really want to know the material and be competitive for MCAT.  It is very difficult and she is a tough grader, but if you go to her office hours and do all the homework problems (as everyone else has said, twice helps), you will do well.

Patty's course is the most difficult of the intro courses. I struggled to earn my grades (doing the hw 2x every week and going to her office hours.) If your schedule is already difficult, I would consider going to the easier classes. Patty is much nicer out of class/one-on-one than in class, so go to her office hours and establish yourself early.
hard, but you ACTUALLY learn.

Even though I got a C in Dr. Patty's class, I believe that she is a wonderful teacher. You really need to do all of the problems (at least) twice to do well in the class.  I normally couldn't get through them all twice though, which is why I got a C.  This class taught me how to study well, and I encourage people to take her class.

Ok the only good comments are coming from those who can naturally comprehend chemistry well and prly got one of the two A's in her class. For those, which is most, who are not prodigies at chemistry, avoid this teacher at ALL COSTS. I am premed and got all A's this semester, accept for Patty's class where i received a B-.

Don't believe bad ratings; I read them and was scared to death of her, but my experience was the complete opposite. Patty is a wonderful professor (my favorite in fact) who loves to help her students in office hours. Yes, it?s hard BUT manageable. Take Patty. She is the best gen chem professor. I got an A both semesters with no background in chem.

Professor Patty is a WONDERFUL professor who really cares about what she teaches as well as her students. Unlike other CHEM 1304 professors, she actually teaches the material and does not hand out free grades: everything is earned. Tips: pay attention in class, do ALL homework problems, and ask questions. She is an amazing prof overall; I would rec

Chemistry is a hard class that requires most of your time. I put so much effort into this class, but it's paying off. She tells you what to do: do homework, go to office hours, study every day. She's right. She doesn't WANT to see you fail, and office hours are worth it! She's nice and approachable. She's not necessarily harder than others

This woman was honestly the worst professor ever. The only reason a few people did well was because they had their noses shoved so far up her ass, she magically graded their exams much more leniently. Her lectures are useless and she belittles everyone with 2nd grade level practice problems. The exams are nothing like the practice exams and she puts emphasis on minute things and exceptions to rules. I can believe she still teaches at SMU.

Contrary to those what those who support her claim, Dr. Patty can not teach. Her lecture style is incomprehensible to most students and she grades harshly for mistakes she frequently makes in class. This class is very text book dependent, meaning you have to read alot of tedious chemistry rather than learning it in lecture.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! YOU WILL HATE YOUR LIFE AND CHEMISTRY!!!!!!!! if you remotely like yourself you will NOT take this class!!!!!
You have to know everything! And if you do, you will get an A in the class. You have to study more for this class than any other, but it is not impossible.

she is an amazing teacher.  chemistry is very hard, people don't like her because she actually makes you learn it and know it.  i would recommend her because you will be MUCHH better off in organic chem, which is EVEN harder! so if your whining about dr. patty, dont bother taking any more chemistry.

im not sure about the massive amount of hatred going on, her class is hard, chemistry is hard, she tells you how to succeed and shes right, it takes a whole lot of work outside of class but she has plenty of office hours and a one hour help session night before every quiz, its just hard though

DO NOT TAKE GENERAL CHEMISTRY WITH DR. PATTY!!!!!!!  I don't know how much stronger i can say that.  I am currently enrolled in her class and failing.  She just reads the lecture notes, curses at the class, uses unhelpful stupid analogies that insult your intelligence, and yells a lot.  She enjoys watching people fail and ridicules those who do.
Not a good teacher at all

Worst professor here at SMU. She puts the chapter outlines on her website to print and feels like reading them out loud to you will make you understand. Her examples are fitting of an elementary school level. She loves to see her students fail because it makes her feel better. Going to her office hours don't help. DO NOT TAKE CHEMISTRY WITH PATTY!

The worst professor I have ever had. Her constant childish analogies make you feel like your back in kindergarden. She likes the select few who do well, and hates those who fail, which is the majority, and she takes pleasure in their failure. Quizzes are difficult, and tests are impossible. AVOID THIS PROF. AT ALL COSTS!! Take Lattman instead!
What the heck is going on here!?

Doesn't bother with attendance after the first few weeks. The weekly quizzes are easy, but a pain  If you do the homework and go to the study session the day before. The tests can be difficult.  She treats you like you're kindergarten kids and uses retarded analogies that make it hard to learn unless you have the thought process of a four year old.
I really liked her, she is always there to help and really wants to see everyone succeed. An extremely intelligent, caring lady, her class is HARD but you can do it.
Great professor who is always willing to help! Learned a lot in her class and if you put in a decent amount of effort you can make an A!

Hated It!  She is the worse chemistry teacher I have ever had.  Loves to watch her students fail and jokes about how they will not pass her tests.  The only quiz the entire class passed was when Professor Lattman came and taught lecture for 2 days.  I would HIGHLY advise you NOT to take Dr. Patty; Your GPA will drop significantly!

The worst class I have ever taken. The chemistry was fine, the professor not so much. The classes are useless, disjoint, and confusing. The only reason I attended was because she throws in random bits of information that will appear on the test. Unlike my other professors, it seems like she could care less whether or not her students do well.

Claims to be helpful, but really is not. She seems to get a certain pleasure out of seeing kids drop/fail. I'm an engineering major, and all my other classes are As right now, and an F in this one. Surely that says something when I can ace calculus and honors rhetoric. Warning: Stay out of her class! Very important.
Fantastic teacher!

I was in class every day and still barely passed.  I even went to the tutoring session.  She grades the tests in alpahbetical order and my name ends in a "W" so I always got nasty little notes on my quizzes from her.
Pre Med Students did not pass the class, she's tough and her tests have nothing to do with the quizzes, nor practice tests, believe me she'll change your career after you fell her class.

Dr. Patty was great. I agree with most who say the class was a little challenging but only if you dont go to class or do the homeworks. The tests are challenging but she gives you more than enough opportunities to make up for mistakes on tests. her grading system was great. how people did that poorly i do not understand! Dr. Patty was great!
to be honest, i'm just glad that i somehow managed to pass that horrible class...

The quizzes had nothing to do with the Tests and Exams!So even if you have a A+ average in the quizzes, you can count on failing the tests. Class was very challenge, and screw my gpa up.  She tricks you, and does use exception of rules regardless of her comment in class that she doesn't. She is cool,and even funny, but stay away!Take Adams.

Worst teacher I have ever had. The exams and quizzes are insane and have every imaginable exception to the rules possible. I hated her so bad I just quit going because of my personal dislike for this woman. She is B****y! Nobody take her EVER! take ADAMS or MAGUIRE. She will ruin your GPA and turn you off of pre-med

I took Maguire's class in the fall and I was bored out of my skull; it was so easy. Dr. Wisian-Neilson's class was a bit more challenging, but nothing that I could not handle. Her class went over the beginning parts of organic chemistry, which was very helpful when I formally took organic chemistry later.
She is insane with the quizzes and exams. Do the homework or fail.

The class isnt easy, but just do the homework and you will be fine. If you have any questions she is SO easy to talk to... just dont be a total slacker and you will get a B or higher. Besides, she prepares you for the rest of the chem faculty.
No Comments
she's impossible
Good Teacher but extremely hard, no mercy on grading and you never knwo whats gonna be on tests/quizzes, know everything especially exceptions to rules
good teacher but extremely hard...
Hard course, but if you do your work, you will know chemistry when you are done.

This is the hardest class i have ever taken.  I ended up having to drop so i wouldn't make an F.  She is very unclear and it is a VERY fast class. 1-2 Chapters a week; hard quizzes every week; and test every 2 weeks or so..
No Comments
No Comments
A very tough teacher, but not too bad. Don't expect to make an A unless you're a chemical genius.

This is a VERY hard professor and it is almost impossible to make an A in her class. She is not very willing to offer help without some sort of criticsm towards you.  However, if chemistry is your major, I would recommend this teacher.  Otherwise stay awa

If you are a Biochemistry major, take Physical Chemistry of Proteins! It is 100% the better option over Molecular Biology. Dr. Tao made this a fun research class. No exams; you just research a topic related to proteins that interests you. As long as you show up for attendance and do the weekly research updates, you'll be fine. Dr. Tao is awesome!!!

19 of 40-person class finished the year, but he does give about 11% extra credit to everyone. People complain that exams are hard, but they are directly from optional homework, and I mean exactly from homework. 6 short quizzes, drops 2 lowest as well. He gives his students every chance to succeed, and this is not a hard class if you actually try.

The class is hard and a weed out, but is not impossible. Most people who didn't do well spent all their time complaining instead of studying. As someone who failed exam 1 and ended with an A, your grade reflects the effort you put in. Exam questions are very similar to hw. Tao is very available outside of class and wants his students to succeed.

HORRIBLE! All chem profs here are but he's actually awful. Ruthless grader, cannot teach, unfair policies,etc.The list goes on. Only gives 15 min for extremely difficult/time consuming quizzes, and exams are too long/too hard to even finish/get a PASSING grade. Cherry on top? Never curves(even w/ 30%-50% aves) and wont say what to study. DONT TAKE!

Gen chem 1 is a hard class, I won't lie. He is such a kind man though. He provides a set of "most important" homework problems which are almost identical to his tests. Also provides many opportunities for extra credit. Can be a tough grader, but as long as you study this class is hard but not impossible.

Dr. Tao will give you all the resources you need to be successful. Those who struggled did not put in the work, as chemistry comes easy to very few people. Lectures can sometimes be frivolous, but just ask him to go over problems and go to office hours. Quizzes are similar to exams. He wants you to succeed! Just put in some effort and you will.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While you can tell he tries to teach, you have to memorize insanely minute details that are on tests and most of the learning must be done outside of the classroom. While there was some form of extra credit, it didn't compensate for how ridiculously difficult this class was for an intro. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have had at SMU. His lectures are super hard to follow and disorganized. I emailed countless times, and never got a response. For a general science class, he makes it a lot harder than it should be.

His class is very hard to get a good grade in. There is no curve or flexibility to his grading. You can tell he tries his best to teach, but most of your learning has to be done on your own time outside of class. He is very scattered when trying to teach.

Really wanted to like him and he's a nice guy but it's so hard to learn from his lectures. Went to office hours regularly and ended up having to drop because the class is only graded from a few exams and quizzes and I bombed the first exam because the homework and quizzes were nothing like it! Be prepared to work a lot.
this guy gives you 15 minutes to write a quiz. awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Tao is a caring professor. He is more than happy to help his students. He really cares about his students. If you put in a certain amount of work, he will work double that amount of work to support you. You are lucky to have him as a professor if you ever have the chance.

Professor Tao foremost is a professor who cares for his students even in such a large lecture environment. The effort he provides is obvious and he always tries his best to explain the relevant material. He teaches in a typical manner for lectures, but he is clever with how he keeps the student engaged. Good Professor just get ready to work.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. He explained chemistry in a way that confuses me to this day. I withdrew from the class to take with a different professor and easily understood the material. He also routinely shamed students for asked questions. He makes gen chem way harder than it needs to be and made me hate the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were exactly like the homework or questions covered during class. Gave plenty of extra credit opportunities. Really great guy, you can tell he's very passionate about chemistry and making sure every student understands the material. Super helpful with answering questions and breaks down everything clearly.

I love Dr. Tao!! I took him over the Summer for Chemistry 2 and he's amazing! A lot of students don't like him because he's so test heavy and complain that his test are hard! But if you ask questions, do the homework, and understand the materials it's not hard at all. He's amazing and anyone who doesn't like him just didn't work hard enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am going to miss Professor Tao & I'm not just saying that because I got an A. I took both 1303 Spring semester & 1304 Summer 2 with him. Chemistry is a tough class, but he truly cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. If you work hard for him, he will work twice as hard for you. You'd be lucky to have him as your professor.

After I took chemistry in this class. I hate it so much to the point I will never ever take another course in Chemistry again. Such a disgusting subject and un-followable. Everything doesn't make any sense. Why are we even need this as our requirement. I learn nothing from this class, absolutely waste of my time. Do not sign up for this class.

I am a junior in college, and this is the first class in my entire life that no matter how much I studied, it would not positively influence my grade. This is partly because of the comically short amount of time allotted for both quizzes and exams. For the online portion, we had 15 minutes to complete 20 complex word problems. Avoid this guy.

Transition to online was a nightmare. His rules are way more complicate than other teachers. It not like all of us going to pre-med field like jeez. I don't need a perfect angle for the phone cam. Not many students have a phone handler. Like what do you even expect ????, he did not curve either instead he removes some test to make up grade.
He is good but there are way too many people in the class. You won't learn anything if you sit all the way in the back.

Dr. Tao is a nice man, but he is not a good professor. Passionate about chemistry and cares for his students, but his lectures are chaotic and difficult to follow. Hard to understand because of his accent. Inflexible. Tries his best but I find he is not very useful in office hours. Tests are very challenging. Has the potential to be better for sure

I took chemistry and calculus in the same semester and couldnt keep up with all the homework from both of them. Roughly 60 questions per week, many of which contain up to 8 sub-questions, and theyre hard. Quizzes are basically the last (and hardest) handful of quizzes from the homework. Posts PPTs online and is fun and perky. Would take again.

Dr. Tao is a great professor for anyone who just needs to take one semester of Gen Chem. He gets through the material and gets to the point. He gives lots of oppurunties to prepare for the tests. The class is a easy A if you work. BUT, if you need to more semesters of Chem, the class is too easy and you will struggle a lot later.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tao is a fantastic professor for general chemistry at SMU. However, if you're a pre-med/biology/chemistry major and you plan on taking higher level chemistry courses in the future, take Dr. Patty because she'll prepare you better. I had him first semester for 1303 and did awesome but had to do some catching up in 1304 because he was too easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tao is outstanding in the effort he puts; he will find time to help you understand the material and even offers extra review sessions for anyone to participate. He genuinely wants to see students excel, but you still have to work for it. There are no free or easy grades in this class, but, if you put in the work, he will help you learn & succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Tao is very knowledgable about the course topic, however in lectures he goes though the information very quickly and it can be very difficult to follow. If you have to take him, do the homework and chapter readings before class to be prepared for his lectures.

Totally enjoyed the whole class. He completely changed my view of chemistry.  I liked the way that he went beyond the content of the textbook and tried to encourage us to think deeply. Warning: Only take this class if you are planning to do the homework.

Dr. Tao is an enthusiastic teacher! He clearly cares about his student's understanding of the material. Doing homework is a must, because many quizzes and tests problems are very similar to the homework.

He gives A LOT of homework and grades one of it so you don't know what you got right or wrong. Won't go over any extra problems during class says theres no time. During office hours he's not too helpful said " either you know it or you don't".
The lecture is unclear, too much homework and got quizzes and tests frequently.
Hired for a reason and not because of their teaching skills.
so rude and a bad teacher

Very unclear grading criteria, unreasonably high expectations for assignments, absolutely boring "discussions" where she expects us to teach the rest of the class. Her snarky comments to people who disagree with her are unprofessional DO NOT TAKE (she's a bad teacher). I couldn't wait for her class to end.

Genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Apply yourself and listen to feedback and you will do well. Go to class and make sure to stay on top of the small homework assignments as I forgot some and lost a few percent.

So easy I literally went to class 3 times ever and have an A. He also doesn't grade the assignments I just write a random sentences every time not even to do with reading and get a 100. So easy take this class w him if u can so so easy almost forgot I was in it.
Respond to a couple of prompts on a handful of days and thats the whole class, literally do not even have to show up in class, highly recommend

He does not teach, just repeats things about his life, is no curriculum so you don't know what to write about on assignments though you somehow may scrape by w a decent grade on some things some times depending on who you are. Heavily docks attendance, nonsensical course with no direction or point, exams a mixed bag again depending on who you are

Every single assignment was so unclear. We never had homework except for a presentation on a social problem of your choice. We had three in person exams which were timed 30min prompts that literally made no sense. They asked theoretical questions and even if you went to class it was impossible to know what he was expecting. A 93.4 is an A-

Easy class; attendance isn't mandatory at all. There is a presentation worth most of your grade; otherwise, only three exams 1 question each where you write about your topic, which relates to your own presentation which you do throughout the semester. They are easy and on lockdown no camera.

I took this class to fulfill my cc and his classes are lecture heavy so write everything that he says. He grade really harshly on participation, if you show up and talk every now and then expect a low grade. If you want a high participation you need to talk in every class. Do not take him.

As others said, some people really should not be teaching. Pierce basically rambled for an hour and a half every class, going over the same lecture but teaching nothing new. He's nice and class can be easily passed, but papers are extremely vague and you'll never know what to write. They're mostly open note and can be bs

In 4373 "Class, Race, and Gender" is a really nice guy and I can tell he means well but some people are just not meant to be teachers. A lot of talking without teaching anything. His writings are easy and mostly open book/note, if you're good at bs'ing you'll do fine on the writings but you still have to get through his painfully long lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pierce's course does not teach any of the content outlined in the course syllabus. In fact, he repeated many of the lectures, and it came across like he did not prepare for every class. Did not enjoy the class at all - papers have way too little direction. Had no idea what was going on in the course, do not recommend.

This class required intellectual thinking. The professor is sweet and open minded about new perspectives. Be present in class and participate to show genuine interest so he knows the way you think thus understands your writings
Horrible professor - only 3 grades throughout the whole semester. do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Has a terrible attitude and does not care about her students doing well in his class, it feels like he 
purposefully ensures you do not do well. Terrible professor who just throws answers at you and makes you learn EVERYTHING on your own. Has a terrible attitude too and is rude in office hours.

Up until the midterm, taking notes is highly crucial to studying. Afterward, taking notes is optional, and you can write your papers from online sources. After the mid-term, everything is technically optional, and if he cancels class, then it is to no detriment. Take this class if you are willing to learn about random things in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was incredibly disappointed with this professor. He was disorganized and honestly had no idea what he was talking about. He was not helpful at all when it came to questions and could not answer them due to his cluelessness about the subject. I would not recommend this professor.

Reviews are arbitrary. If you are committed to getting a good grade, you will get one. It is much simpler than made out to be by these reviews. I put in a much smaller workload than I thought I needed to after first reading the reviews and still got an A-. If you pay attention in class and know how to write a paper, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take him. The only people who did well in this class were the kids who live and breathe philosophy. He is not interesting, and halfway through the semester most people stopped listening to the lecture.His grading involves just highlighting random sentences. He never responds to email. Take another class.
Almost impossible to stay awake during his class. It is always lectures, almost zero class involvement or learning diversity. Very mundane and not what I expected philosophy to be.

Not a bad teacher or person at all, just hard for an intro class. 2 papers and a quiz make up you whole grade. I would not take just as an easy class, if you are interested or majoring in philosophy you will probably enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely nothing in this class made any sense. Expectations were often unclear, and the course material was incredibly dense and next to impossible to understand. This man has an unhealthy obsession with zombies and a complete lack of self awareness. Save yourself, and your brain cells, and avoid taking this useless class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chuard is a super nice guy, but does not set out clear criteria for his papers. Attendance is mandatory but he is forgiving with deadlines. He is super smart but his lectures can be challenging to follow for those not interested in the field. The class is much more empirical than theoretical, and not geared toward philosophy majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never gives feedback and expects you to just know how to write a good essay. Avoid at all costs.

I didnt miss a single class and still ended with a low grade. This professor doesnt teach you how to write a philosophy paper and expects you to just write a good one. Hes a tough grader that never gives feedback on how to improve your writing. PLEASE dont take him, you will end with a bad grade especially if you are a math/science driven person.

Do yourself a favor and do not take his intro class. One of the hardest professors for philosophy imo. Lectures are long and boring. I found his teaching style to be extremely unclear. Class is graded on 4 papers basically. GO TO CLASS and take notes on every single word he speaks or you won't be able to write your 4 papers (half are 5 -7 pages)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most boring class ever. Just sits and lectures the whole time, and expects us to do the readings, but don't have to participate in class, so easy to skip over the homework. Only 4 grades, being midterm/final exam and 2 papers (one being written with a partner which sucked).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Other reviews are a little harsh. Professor Chuard is really smart and I liked his lecture style, but the reading material is dense. 4 papers and a presentation and he grades pretty fair. Accepted my final paper a few days late. The class challenged me but I learned how to write a good philosophy paper

His lectures are not clear to follow and the papers are painful because his research is in consciousness. Be ready to work the hardest you've ever worked on papers to even pass. I cannot even count the amount of times I've cried over these papers.

Professor Chuard is very passionate about his teaching, but he is an extremely tough grader. He uses a weird grading scale to compensate, but the majority of students in the class will have low grades. Do not take if looking for an easy A elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not many major grades so doing well in them is important. The readings for class are pretty long. Teacher is super nice and understanding, he grades papers pretty fairly but if you dont read or pay attention there is no way you will do good in this class. The topics are pretty interesting. Tests are hard. Read, take notes, go in with an open mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class average: 79.2. A slight majority of the class received a B or higher. Pretty stereotypical college course.

Very difficult class. Everything wasnt too articulated and was challenging to follow. If you miss class a few times you will be completely lost. Long lectures and class participation is almost impossible since the class material is so challenging and abstract. Used students names in the quizzes and only called on a few kids.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was very interested in Philosophy even though it wasn't my major. I absolutely detest this class. Only take him if you like philosophy or if you enjoy sitting through the most boring lectures of your life. The only homework is to read. They're also boring. You have a midterm, two papers, and a final. No room for error. Way too hard for an intro.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He grades on a curve, so that's a nice aspect of his class (86 is an A-). He is a nice person as well and is passionate about philosophy. The readings are hard and there are pop quizzes on them, and he is very particular in his grading. Metaphysics is a really hard subject & I wish I didn't take this class, but Im sure his other classes are fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Classic case of just needing to show up to class to get a good grade. Show up and pay attention and you'll be fine. Skip class or look at your phone all period and you'll fail. Simple as that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very fair professor in his grading. He drops the lowest of five quiz grades, basically tells you what the exam will be in advance, and has a scale of >90 A, >85 A-, >80 B+, etc. I can see how this can be hard to some, but he explains concepts clearly and provides all of the necessary resources to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes are an oof, you genuinely have no idea when they're coming. But he does a good job teaching difficult introductory material and has an extremely generous grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Instead of being one of those guys that takes a hard subject and just gives everyone easy test questions, he changes the grading scale outside of the normal one -- which really makes a difference!
