reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: took prof chuard for PHIL 1305 in the fall, took this one with him in the spring. he is really interested in and excited about the material he teaches, and he was so flexible when it got super loaded during the week before finals since other profs were loading us up with assignments. i would definitely recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is not an easy intro class. However, if you come to class every day, take good notes, and study, you'll be fine. He is a hard but fair grader and makes you work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: pop quizzes keep you on your toes - i got screwed by one and got a 20%, but he drops the lowest of 5 quizzes. he has a weird accent, but i found it funny af. he expects a lot of regurgitation, but the grading scale at the end really bumps you up a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Chuard is a French-speaking Swissman who speaks English with an Aussie accent. Combine this with his poor, unclear explanations of the topics and learning the already tricky subject of philosophy becomes that much harder. On top of that, hes a tough grader who uses a huge curve so that the class passes. Nice man but would avoid if looking for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class can be difficult at times, but his grading scale makes all the difference. Upper 80s is A-, anything in the 90s is an A. Definitely makes up for some of the harder stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was the longest hour and 20 minutes I would experience. Philosophy is hard for math-brained people (and even for some abstract-brained people) and I am not sure I ever completely understood any of the units. I would only suggest this class if you plan on majoring in philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chuard's intro class isn't too bad, there are five pop quizzes so you should always try and do each reading before class but they are short so it isn't stressful. Your grades may look bad at first, but he uses a different grade scale that turns 86 into A-, 76 into B-, etc. The topics can be hard but not much work, and he is a funny prof

This professor is nearly impossible and expects students to be fluent in all things philosophy on day one. Awful pop quizzes, I would spend two hours a night on readings and still get a 3/10 MAX. Half of the class should not have to be worried about Freshman-Forgivenessing an intro level philosophy class. Enough said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Chuard means well and is a good guy, but a lot of topics seem very specified and extravagant for an intro philosophy course. The main thing he's looking for is regurgitation for tests and especially essays - just write based off your notes from class. Fortunately, he does have a nice curve at the end of the year that bumps you up about 5-6%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Attend class, pay attention, do the readings, and ask questions to clear up any misunderstandings. If there's any class that is a predictor of your overall academic ability, it's this one. Are you a C student? You'll get a C. Are you an A student? You'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Not understanding, terribly boring lectures, not enough graded items in the garbed, confusing class with no other resources available aside form his own lecture. Ruined my entire GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. class is hard but worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a blow off class, don't take his class.

Took his intro class which was fine because he was okay at explaining things and the material was pretty straightforward. I WOULD ALSO NOT RECOMMEND ANY OF HIS ADVANCED CLASSES!! The lectures were hard to follow. He was extremely disorganized and a much more difficult grader. Does not explain why he takes off points.

Chuard's class began well, but unfortunately went downhill near the end. The lectures, upon reaching the most difficult material, became a bit rambling and difficult to follow. The class, topically, was also a bit disorganized. Chuard is always willing to help in or out of class, but can be a harsh grader.
Good teacher, funny and witty. I really enjoyed his class even though I have no interest in philosophy. Readings and quizzes every few weeks, few grades but attendance is taken every class.

Dr. Chuard is nice and lectures clearly, and is helpful in office hours for assistance on papers, etc. The tests are fairly easy; he is looking for the arguments discussed in class written verbatim. If you learn them word-for-word, you'll do quite well on the tests and in the class as a whole.

Prof Chuard taught Metaphysics for me which is hard as hell to begin with. He is very intellegent and makes MP understandable because it should be a grad level course. He grades rough drafts harshly but also curves. His quizzes are easy so long as you read the material.

ALL I CAN SAY IS GOOD LUCK!!! :(( THIS TEACHER IS IMPOSSIBLE!!! You know the key word to this class is Intro to Philosophy not some graduate level class!!! anyways like i've said before good luck in this class (luck and prayers are needed in this class)!!!!
Hardest Philosophy class i've taken.  For the tests you have to memorize the arguments of each philosopher and if they are not word for word he takes off.

He is good, but u need to pay attention in his class or u will get extremly lost, keep asking questions. He loves to give examples, notetaking is not allways necessay, he gives handouts on all his note, just write down his exaples to help with note rembering.

For this class, it is essential to focus on the labs and troubleshoot any issues during lab time before the TA leaves, as many students procrastinated and could not finish. The essay and presentation are graded leniently. Create a detailed cheat sheet for the tests so that you do not have to remember every little thing discussed in the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. If you are not good at test-taking, don't worry. Make sure you do well on the labs and the homework. The professor and lab TA are both available for feedback and they are pretty good about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Doesn't help students effectively prepare for exams. Slides and example programs don't reflect what is on the tests.

Dr. Phillips is a wonderful conductor. He has many years of experience and deserves respect. If he's conducting, the orchestra is in good hands. He seems very scary and intimidating at first, but if you talk to him in person and get to know him, he's actually a nice guy.
Good guy, very talented man. Total tool sometimes. This class really makes you grateful for life when you're not in the class because it's the driest part of anyone's day.
Dr. Phillips is strict and scary. Good musician but unnecessarily mean at times.

He's a wise conductor, he knows what he's doing and he's been around the block. He can really pick out how things should be and how they sound. He does this thing where a week before the concert he'll get mad at how the orchestra sounds bad so we run through whatever we're playing one more time and then he says it's exponentially better.
A wonderful conductor. Clear in what he wants out of the orchestra and does not spoon-feed. He helps us make beautiful music.

Great teacher and conductor that knows what he wants and doesn't stray from it.  I think he is great for the orchestra because he holds the orchestra accountable and makes the musicians all play to their musical ability.
If you get on his good side, then your time at SMU will be great- if you get on his bad side, you might as well plan on transferring!

Dr. Phillips has great knowledge of the field but is always very negative in rehearsal. This negativity is not constructive nor does it provide for a good working environment. In addition, he does "play favorites" which proves very frustrating. Though he does have good ideas, his attitude gets in the way of having effective performances!

Whoever said Milnes was a better conductor should be shot!  I myself made up the rhyme "Dr. Milnes, gets paid more than I do, but have no fear, he'll be gone next year" and "altho he sux, he makes the bux"--(for the main theme from Strauss's "Don Juan") back in '93.  Milnes can't keep an orchestra together, rhythm-wise.  Phillips can.
Very organized. Helpful. Knows what he wants. Clinically clean of musicality.
The Maestro is amazing.  He knows exactly what he wants, and he knows how to get it out of you.  Playing in his orchestra is an unbelievable experience.

Dr. Phillips is a wellspring of knowledge, and he is very clear in rehearsal.  However, he lacks fire and passion in his performances.   He is clear and easy to follow, but he lacks the power to inspire in performance.  His style lends itself to a good orchestra and is not appropriate for such a conservatory style environment.  He's an excellent teacher for the classroom,  but his conducting does little to prepare Orchestra members for the professional world. Far less competent than David Milnes.

Dr. Phillips was the best orchestra conductor I've ever studied under. Orchestra was the best six hours of my week, and the most stressful! He pushed me to be the best musician I could be. I'll never forget him!
Wonderful musician, wonderful person, a wellspring of knowledge, charming, kind, honest; the best conductor I've ever met in my life!!!
This guy is a boss. I would do whatever needs to be done to take him.

First anthropology class I've ever taken and it was very interesting. A pretty easy class with two exams, a 10pg paper and dream diaries. I would definitely refer this class to anyone who needs the credit.
He was pretty easy although its hard to keep up with note taking since you never know what to write down. Ask around for past exams, his tests are pretty similar.
What a joke of a course.

Took his Judo course. It was fun. I got to legally rag doll students. Take a gym bag and shower after class to not get Staph; the mats are not the cleanest and since you grapple, one will notice others hygiene.
Very nice teacher, I took his judo class and there wasn't too much work. He is very passionate about what he teaches and its a fun start to my morning.
Professor Chelstowski is awesome. He's very knowledgeable in the areas he teaches and really cares about his students. Take his class and you won't regret it!
Awesome guy, just participate and come to class as much as you can and you will get an A. Learned a lot in self defense and it was enjoyable
I am taking Judo for my 2nd PRW. Professor Chelstowski is a very nice professor. He gave many extra credit opportunities. He never cancels the class.

Professor Kelly is one of my favorite professors at SMU. She is so caring and truly wants you to succeed. Her course is heavy with material and exams. Her exams are very difficult honestly, but the other assignments keep your grade balanced. Her lectures are great, she uses kahoot, and is funny. Take her but expect to put effort in!

Really kind person and seems very smart but her skills do not translate well to teaching. The tests often have material that was never mentioned on the study guide. She switches between lectures and group projects in a disorganized way that really confuses the students.
TAKE HER! She is so lovely and makes class fun. All tests are take-home lockdown with no mic or camera. The workload is definitely manageable, and it is very easy to get an A. Slow but easy grader.

Dr. Kelly genuinely cares about her students and wants them all to succeed. She is very attentive in answering emails and finding time outside of class to help. The class was essentially one big group project, so it's important that you like your group. She is very detail-oriented, which can be frustrating for things like citations and Excel.
a bunch of homework and assignments and we do not meet regularly in class so it throws a lot of students off guard. I wish we did not have many assignments/projects all at once.

The sweetest professor. She is very lively and caring. She wants to see everyone succeed. None of the assignments are very difficult and she grades easily. I loved her class and hope I can take her again in the future!

As a junior, she is probably the best professor I have had at SMU. She is funny and kind and genuinely wants the best for her students. She set clear guidelines for expectations and learning material which made the course much less stressful. I love Dr. Kelly!

I can not recommend her enough. If all of my classes were taught by her I would love going to school. Truly my favorite teacher I have ever had. Course is fun- just a partner project with a couple easy tests. There are some papers- but you get to chose what you want to write about. Highly recommend

While the class itself is on a bit boring/difficult topic, Dr. Kelly is the KINDEST PERSON EVER and will meet with you outside of class and help you out! She wants everyone to succeed and gives bonus opportunities. She spends so much time giving feedback and if you show her you care and listen/participate in class, she will recognize that. Take her
She is the best.

I love love Professor Kelly!! Her lectures are actually interesting and interactive even in a zoom setting. She's super accessible outside of class and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. if you get the chance to take her class absolutely do!!

I loved Dr. Kelly's class! She is super nice and very easy to talk to. She genuinely knows her stuff and cares about the students. Lectures and assignments are easy to understand and follow. 100% would recommend for CCPA students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kelly is a great professor. She is super sweet and cares about her students. Everything you learn in her class is super useful and applicable to the real/professional world. There is consistent work, reading, and projects, but they are all pretty manageable and easy. I would definitely recommend taking this class.

Pop quizzes. Hard tests. Professor who expects you to know all the basics already. If you are NOT an accounting major, do NOT take this class as an elective, you will suffer like me. The workload and learning curve is so heavy for someone not invested in an accounting major that it is not worth it. She's alright, but extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Pizzini is a great professor. If you do your homework and practice the powerpoint exercises you will be okay. Accounting is hard but Dr. Pizzini is always willing to help. she is straight forward when answering questions, so do not get offended. She cares and will help you if you ask. Put the work and you will survive 3313.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took her for intermediate accounting at Texas State University. This class is going to be extremely difficult no matter what professor you take. However, she posts filled out notes from the lectures and gives solutions to the HW problems that will be on the test and always tell the class when there will be a quiz. Best ACCT prof I've had so far

I'll repeat what was said in another rating. She's just not a natural teacher, and to be honest, a bit meanspirited. It doesn't appear she even likes her job. The classroom feels like a dictatorship. It's 100% regurgitating the textbook creating no real reason to be in class other than the fact it's mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prints out lecture outlines.  Very organized.

She is a horrible teacher. Probably the most boring of any I've had. She writes her notes on one of those computers you can write on and her writing is too hard to read. She tries really hard to explain it but just isn't a natural teacher. She makes no sense and I would never take her again. Her tests are much harder than anything she assigns.
Great Prof, test are hard but she is very helpful.

Very nice professor but a tough class especially for first year students. Lots of homework and project deadlines. Projects were pretty interesting but most of the work was expected to be done outside of class so expect weekend and very late night studio work. Almost never given rubrics making it hard to determine what to do for best scores.

If you are not an art major and this class is not required for you, do not take it. It is EXTREMELY time consuming. The homework paired with major assignment workload is immense, be prepared to pull all nighters with your entire class. Expectations are high and rubrics are non-existent. It is a challenge to do well, and favoritism is significant.

No rubrics provided
Participating in critiques is very important for your grade
A good portion of the class stayed in the studio until 2 in the morning on multiple occasions because of the heavy workload that we were expected to complete
There's also a good bit of research required for some projects
Tests are difficult but as long as you study and pay attention in class you should be good. Go to office hours and he explains the information well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His exams are actually hard. Other assignments are much easier. Gives opportunities to earn extra points through in class quizzes. He is always available if you have questions and responds to emails quickly. I think this class in general is just hard conceptually and he tries to make it as easy as he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot of material is covered in this course. You have weekly homework and with no textbook, it's a bit hard - however, the professor is very helpful during office hours so take advantage of that. Study the notes and homework, and you'll be ready for the test. The TAs are hard graders - get points back by going to office hours. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The class is not something to take lightly you will cover a lot of martial in a semester. The homework is very hard, harder than tests in fact. Go into his office for hours to help he is very helpful. The test reviews are very similar to the tests. Your grade in the class is very based on TAs grading so make sure you get partial credit.
He's really nice and helpful when you ask questions or go to office hours, but don't slack off on doing the homework and make sure to attend his review sessions before tests

Class is easy to follow with plenty of examples. Tests are mostly multiple choice, and you receive zero partial credit on such problems. Enjoys giving quizzes when students are least likely to show up (after exams). Quizzes and Homework are short-answer and easy if you come to class.

He is a great teacher and is able to keep the attention of his students by providing examples in class that allow us to practice using the formulas. He does not take attendance but there are pop-quizzes and the information in class is very valuable
Intro Stats class. Quiz at first of class to insure attendance. Easy. Content is easy if you pay attention. Allowed a note card of formulas for test.

What an awesome professor. Clearly loves what he does. Is very helpful with the material and breaks it down so everyone can understand. I'm not a fan of math but I would take any math course if he was the professor! He reminds me of the boss from the movie Yes Man! Funny and chessy(but in a good way!)

Very nice guy.  Attendance and doing the hw is mandatory to do well.  You have a short quiz over the reading every lecture class so you must go.  He does a good job of explaining the material and even squeezes in a few good jokes every once in awhile. If you study for the tests you'll do well.  You also get to drop one test which is nice
You MUST attend, there was a 2 question quiz at the beginning of every class. He is VERY fair and very interested in the material. I definitely recommend him.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. I am usually an A student,but I really struggled in this class. He gives practice problems before the tests and then puts a few completely random questions on the tests. The lectures are boring, but he does explain everything. He must have curved at the end because I had a better grade than I expected.

This class was pretty easy and basic if you paid any attention at all in class, read the few page assignments before class and did the simple homework.  The professor is nice enough and answers even the dumbest questions in class. The labs are easy.

He's really nice and is thorough with the material.  His tests are hard and there's required homework assignments about every 2 weeks.  He gives about 3 quizzes, but they only counted if they helped your grade.  If you go to class and do the homework, he really helps you out on your grade.

Definitely recommend this class for an easy math credit. It's wise to show up because missing a lot of the daily quizzes can tank your grade. Definitely a manageable class if you do the readings and go to lab sessions. Missing daily quizzes and labs are really the only thing that can hurt your grade.

Easy class and nice professor. He drops your three lowest quiz grades, your lowest test, your lowest homework, and you lowest lab. Practice exams given prior to the test are very similar to the test. You are allowed to bring a "cheat sheet" to all of the tests and exam. I would take him again.
This class was really boring. Quiz every class so attendance is mandatory. Tests are okay, gives practice exam beforehand so not to difficult. Also plus that Professor Potgeiter is really cute.

Ive had this professor twice now and both times were great experiences. He cares for his students and teaches well as long as you put in effort he puts in effort with you. Favorite professor at SMU so far
Class average: 89.66. A large majority of the class received a B+ or higher. A decent bit easier than the average college course, but not overwhelmingly so.

I highly recommend taking Pr. Polanco for SPAN 3355. All of his expectations are very reasonable regarding homework. You definitely have to go to class to get a good grade but he is very enjoyable and I have had more laughs in the class than any other. He is a great professor but more than that he is a great person.

Taking Pr Polanco for 3355 right now. All of the work that is expected has been very reasonable. I enjoy going to his class, usually a good amount of laughing - its really been a good time. As long as you show up you should do fine if you have an above average understanding of spanish. He is a good professor and a better person.

Great guy, funny, tests aren't hard, very fair and accurate reviews, and not difficult at all. BUT THERE'S SO MUCH HOMEWORK. You know the whole "two hours outside of class for every hour in class" thing? Yeah, this dude takes that to a whole other level. Not hard to get an A, but way too much busy work. Tedious.
So much homework. Online and book every night. Quizzes weekly. A difficult class unless you have much past experience with spanish. I have learned a lot, but it has come at the cost of lots of time.

He is a very caring professor who grades fairly easily, but the amount of busywork in this course is INSANE. You will regularly have >5 hours of homework per week on top of any studying that you have to do for it. The material is easy, the grading is easy, it's just so tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sr. Polanco is THE MAN! He's a great guy who genuinely enjoys teaching Spanish to students. His lectures can get a little repetitive and his grading criteria is not always clear, but he is very helpful with test reviews and general information. He will definitely like you if you put in some effort in his class; he rewards hard work.

Sr. Polanco is the best professor I ever had in my life! He is the cutest thing ever and cares about the well-being of his students. I had a really hard week and missed class and he emailed me and made sure I was ok. The exams are pretty hard so not an easy A, and there is a lot of hw (online and book), but it is an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: I took two semesters with this professor: SPAN 2401 and 2302. Both were amazing. He takes time to explain things and is always open to questions during lectures. He is understanding and knows that second languages aren't for everyone. He has made me prepared to continue my degree in world languages.

He has to follow strict curriculum guidelines by the department, but he definitely makes the class as fun as possible. You must participate in class, or he will call you out for answers to force you to do so. I highly suggest making sure the homework is completed everyday, or he will hassle you. Really great guy and I suggest taking, for sure!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As long as your Spanish isn't horrendously bad, you'll get at least a B in the class. VHL answers can be looked up online. As long as you memorize vocabulary for tests, you should be good to go. Great professor overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lenient grader on oral presentations and writings. Tests and quizzes are very straightforward. The curriculum is pretty much the same across the Spanish department. I highly recommend Polanco. He is a super nice Peruvian man and he honestly made class fun for Span 2401
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of the VHL answers can be looked up online if you have no idea what you're doing, which means since VHL is 18% of your average, that should put you off to a good start. Writings are graded pretty leniently as long as you proofread. Quizzes and tests WILL catch you off-guard if you didn't spend any time studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Essays are very easy if your proofread. Tests are easy if you study. The cultural presentation is also easy if you memorize your presentation.

Not a Spanish 1 class, more like an advanced Spanish. You will never get full credit for participation and he definitely picks his favorites! You will learn a lot, only because you are forced to understand him considering he only talks in Spanish... Expect homework every night and pop quizzes. I do not recommend!

I took 2 years of Spanish in high school and this class was easy for me. Answer the question when he calls on you, do the online homework that is due once a week, and review a bit before each exam and you'll be fine. If you've never taken Spanish before it'll be more difficult because he speaks in Spanish often and theres no platform he starts from

He's a very funny, adorable man. Polanco is a chill professor that will gladly clear up any questions you have. His tests are moderately difficult and he gives random quizzes but you can easily pass with some work. You also get 3 unexcused skips.

Prof. Polanco only speaks spanish in a Spanish 1 class, which is frustrating and difficult. He speaks quietly and mumbles. However, the exams are easy and you can get an A without any prior Spanish knowledge.

If you're afraid of answering questions in spanish in front of the class/teacher, don't take his class. He makes you feel dumb if you can't understand his questions and won't help you if you don't understand. Otherwise, the tests are easy if you study but the homework is tedious and he always adds more onto the already long assignment

Tests do require studying but they are quite easy. Essays are graded very easy as long as you proofread them. His little review sheets outline everything on the test that you need to know. Coming from high school spanish I found his class very easy.

Such a sweet man. Class is terribly easy but has a lot of tedious busy work. Really funny, genuine, little Peruvian man. If you're looking for a good grade, take him. If you're looking to learn a lot, don't.

Don't take this professor! He's horrible. I had him for Spanish 3358. Class consists of him reading from the textbook. He never answers any question; he just talks around them. He was so frustrating when it came to exams. He would give us wrong answers on the review and then graded them ridiculously hard. Also he has his favorites.
This guy is great. Best Spanish professor out there.
Good guy
I LOVE MY POLANCO!
great prof!  so nice, helpful, and the work isn't too bad either
he has his favorites, and no matter how many time you go in to see him for help, it doesn't help, he'll blow you off...

He was such a sweet teacher.  I would definitely recommend him for this class over other teachers.  He was really nice, and he made the class interesting by keeping everyone involved.  He was awesome!

Would you like a free 100? Take this class, bam, that is a swaggy 100 added to your GPA. Do you care at all about actually learning anything about philosophy? Avoid this dude like the plague. He never shows up to class, doesn't care at all about his assignments, and is honestly not fit to be a professor. But hey, that easy A makes it ok
Easiest class offered at SMU if you take it with Popovic.  One night a week and you don't even have to show up except for on exam days.

Took as a pillar course one night a week. The lectures are overwhelmingly boring but there is absolutely no homework. Only three tests and one paper. Tests are free response and truefalse--you must study lecture notes to do well on tests but studying the night before is plenty preparation. Extremely easy class, I would definitely recommend it.
There are only three test and not very hard. The debate project was super easy because you can choose your topic and you have a team. The final paper was only 5 pages and totally reasonable.
Confusing and boring teacher. Presentations for half the time. Clear waste of time and didn't learn anything.
Took this class over J-Term. Class was cash. money. Easiest thing ever.

Attendance IS Mandatory. Went to every class, he takes attendance randomly once a week. Has a really thick accent and hard to understand. Have to rely on the textbook 100%. Tests are true/false so you have to know things word for word. Would not recommend this class.

Awesome professor. The textbook is basically the class notes, tests are a breeze, etc. Keeps the subject matter interesting. Oh, and what most other reviews state about the difficulty/his grading is true.

any of his classes are easy--10 quizzes and 1 final paper. doesnt care for attendance but you should go to the 3 classes prior to the quizzes thats how you will know what will be on them. quizzes arent hard. very easy professor. go to class and you will make an A.
Easy A if you study and attendance is not mandatory!

He is great. Very easy! the textbook he uses are his lecture notes. If your not going to pay attention in class then you have to read the book, but the textbook is very interesting. He put it together, but definately overpriced. his tests are fill in the blanks with no word bank and true false. I studied the night before the exams and I did fine.

A good professor. He is very easy, and the textbook he uses are his lecture notes. Incredibly overpriced for something he made at Kinkos, but by far the most useful textbook I have. His lectures are straightforward and well structured, but it never seems like he is looking at you, he appears to always either be lecturing to the ceiling or the floor
Very easy class, and I found his presentation to formal logic especially helpful when taking my Kaplan course for the LSAT.
Easy class! Plus he doesn't read the final paper!!
Definitely TAKE HIM!! It's an interesting class if you pay attention and the quizzes are easy!
this guy is the man. take any class he teaches.
Excellent professor, very understanding, easy grade but effort is semi-involved, take his classes if you can!
SO EASY.  TAKE HIM FOR ANY CLASS HE TEACHES. YOU WILL GET AN A UNLESS YOU HAVE NO BRAIN

EASY A! weekly quizzes that everyone gets A's on which is worth 50% of your grade. There is also a 10 page paper or two 5 page papers that is 50% of your grade that everyone gets an A on basically. His attendance policy is that you must be there for more than half the classes and it is not a big deal if you miss.
SUPER EASY CLASS

Extremely easy class. Making up quizzes and papers is never really an issue. Going to class helps getting A's on all the quizzes. A little difficult to understand and at times can be boring. Otherwise an easy A!
Its an easy course! take attendence and the exam is really easy! btw he is nice toooo

I had him for Contemporary Moral Problems.  The class was extremely easy. Two long papers that he gave almost everyone an A on and eay quizzes that take 30 seconds to study for. Easiest A you'll get! Not really clear in talking but after a while you start to understand him and he says you have to come to atleast half the classes: attendence is open

Elementary Logic - Most people I talk to don't like him just because he seems like a shifty guy with a thick russian accent. He's really nice in that he wants you to understand things, but ya know... There's no point in taking this class unless you have to or you like formal logic.

This class is impossible. Dr. Prasanna isn't fit to teach this class. Right when lecture ends, he bolts out of the classroom every single time. Topics are confusing and class is very unstructured. Hopefully you are good at teaching yourself or you have a different experience. Lab is at a terrible timing but TAs are great.
how the sequel to this class easier than the introduction

One of the worst instructors I have ever met. Homeworks do not match the material covered in class, and you're expected to grade your own homeworks despite the fact he reviews them anyways. Quizzes are random and unannounced. Material is difficult even in a vacuum. Class average for midterm was
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Keeps it simple and does not overwhelm students.

Prithu is not the kindest professor and does not like his job (he ends class very early and gets angry when you ask questions). At times, he is funny but his lack of enthusiasm makes the class boring. You get 100 on every assignment if you follow what he does. ILP and Final are graded pretty harshly by the TAs with minimal partial credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you are looking to take Investments lab, he is way better than Vivi Zhu. He isn't amazing, but I learned more than with Vivi and I thought the final was more manageable. He knows his stuff and is very kind - even brought pizza in for the final!

Probably the worst professor I have had at SMU. He didn't care at all about this class, one time gave a lecture from a coffee shop on zoom that we couldn't even hear him. Basically had half the class buy a new computer and didn't give any alternative options. Also the videos are so much more straight forward than his actual lectures.

Whole grade is virtually final exam. Does not teach during labs so prelabs and labs are taught through videos. Clearly a good professor when you get one on one time with him but the class by nature is poorly structured.

This class is ridiculous. Professor comes to class and offers no help and when he does makes you very uncomfortable. He should not be allowed to teach at this school. I would never take this class again, even if I was paid back all of my tuition. I found it very difficult to learn in a class I feel could have really helped me with my major skills.

Professor Vatsa seemed very out of it every class period. Half the time he explained assignments in 10 minutes then left. This class made me incredibly doubtful in the talent I have in my major. Final was a 3 to 3 1/2 hour assignement that we only were given two hours for. I would never take him again
Prithu is the boy, dude gets too much hate. Just literally copy everything he does and you'll be fine.

The class is optional to go and he would not teach you anything, and I don't see any meanings for this course. Video is better than his teaching, recommend this course to be online or change another professor.

Dude...we just started today! No one and I mean no one understood the material.  Professor Vatsa gets a zero on teaching us the material.  How do they expect us to learn if the Professor doesn't teach it in the first place.  Class is suppose to be until 4:50, professor left middle of class. It costs us too much to not be learning the material.

You HAVE to have a Windows computer for this class for this specific plug-in for all of the assignments. He tells you to get "Box" installed if you have a Mac to run Windows & I almost threw my computer every week because it never works. I had an A all year then final came and I ended with a C+ because my computer wouldn't work & I failed the exam.

Dr. Vatsa is fantastic. You must attend class to understand the material, but he moves fast. He will provide a recording of the lecture if you ask for it, which is helpful to review. Tests are open notes and are similar to what you review in class. He provides office hours every day and replies to emails quickly. I learned a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Vatsa is a good guy. He tries to make class stress free, but it can be difficult. There are 2 exams, 6HW (1-2 weeks for each), and a final. All are open note. He moves fast, so it can be easy to fall behind bc the topics are second nature to him. Edit: He's a real one. My grade went from a C to a B+. Put in effort and you'll do well.

Do not take this class for WRTR. Lots of homework which sometimes seems unnecessary, papers are graded very strictly and there is only one extra credit option the whole semester which only boosts your grade by a percentage or 2. Take someone else for WRTR if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As long as you try and she can tell you will be fine in the class. She gives a good bit of work like any other writing professor, but it is very manageable. She is also extremely understanding about the work load.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is definitely one of the harder disc teachers.
Worst teacher I had at smu. Her disc class is extremely harder than my disc class first semester. She is a way tougher grader than all the other disc classes. Take anyone except for her.

His class has to be easy because everyone would fail if he made it any more difficult. You can learn if you can understand him, but it's pretty difficult to figure out the concepts he's trying to get across. Teach yourself from the book and check the answers on all take home quizzes with the internet and everyone else in class.
Hard to understand but makes the class really easy. Take home quizzes and you can use your notes on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pradhan's class was pretty great,  he makes the class super easy. All of our quizzes were take home, we had one assignment every week, and our tests were completely reasonable, and curved when applicable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You will get an A in this class if you read the chapters, and go over the slides before the tests. Also, go to class bc she gives a lot of examples that might show up on tests. She announces quizzes and exactly what pages they will be over. I reccommend.
the attitude, donot care!

Professor is too random in approach to grading. Test will cover obscure references to HBR articles or other reading assingments that are not discussed in class. Other than that the class is good and the tests are very hard but fair. She does test on the information discussed in the class and the reading assingments. If you travel your are screwed.

Great professor who is the epitome of professionalism and clarity. I agree that lecture seems very common sense but the tests are difficult. In my opinion the only reason they are difficult is because of the amount of material covered - not because the material is complex. Only study the portions of the book that are mentioned in her powerpoint.

She is a nice professor but the tests are tricky and arbitrary. If you want an A in this class be prepared to memorize A LOT of worthless definitions. While you are in the class you feel like it is all common sense (which most of it is) but then the test comes and is too difficult. I believe this is another example of a simple subject in which the

Fun and relevant class. She uses examples that you can relate to. Tests were too hard... If you want deep analysis you should make the tests open-note. Oh well. Other profs are easier but you feel like you didn't learn anything useful. I loved her class because I actually learned a lot.
Awesome. Very clear. Understands that class should be relevant!

In her class right now...I don't know who was teaching this other commentor but this is probably the most boring class I've ever had, she made me hate marketing.  Also its inVesting not inWesting (if you take the class you'll understand)...

She is so nice and helpful. She teaches throughly and speaks clearly on what she expects.  I took her for intro to marketing and consumer behavior, she uses the same teaching style throughout and she likes to get the class involved.  She is a fun teacher. She made me want to be a marketing major.
One of the best professors in the Econ Dept! Very caring and very helpful! His lecture slides are extremely useful. Strongly recommended!
he cares about his students, and will help you if you go to his office hours.

Avoid at all costs. Impossible to  understand and very clearly hates teaching.  Gets sassy and asks why no one is participating but yet is very condescending to those who ask questions and seek to understand.  If you must take him, a tutor will be necessary to get through this class

Fantastic professor.  The things he taught me helped form my career.  I thank God that I had the opportunity to learn from a professor that loved his subject matter and encouraged his students to succeed in their studies as much as he did.

brilliant professor.  Dr. Pulte is outstanding nationally in Linguistics, bilingual education and American Indian languages.  He is fair, polite and helpful to all his students.  He is a professor who can change your attitudes for the good.
The nicest person you will ever meet. He is passionate about his subject matter, but will repeat himself and forget things (due to age). He is very personable and is understanding. Excellent!

I love this man.  He's just so nice!  His class is so straightforward.  He's one of those adorable professors that seems kinda absent-minded...but in an endearing way.  He's very proper and very gentle and well-mannered.  He always comes to class in a suit.  He loves what he's doing and he loves sharing it.  His tests are so easy and really adhere to the lecture.  He has review sessions where he actually gives you the test questions basically.  He's that willing to help.  Whatta great guy!
No Comments
Pulte is great -- good class to take.

Dr. Pulte was one of the best professors I have had.  He was patient and treated us with respect, knowing that we all had full-time jobs outside of school.  He also was passionate about what he was teaching, yet welcomed scholarly debates about issues.

This class is straightforward. If you have ample Excel knowledge and like being taught by one guy's opinion, just take something else anyway. I don't want to manage my finances the way he told us to. He is aloof and unwilling to help students. I think he didn't like me at all and my grade reflected it. The stock game and project were decent though.

Hardest professor I've taken at SMU by far. Many of these reviews say you'll be okay if you attend the class even though attendance is not mandatory, but this couldn't be further from the truth. Professor Puelz is unnecessarily harsh on students, has a major ego, and should not be teaching. Do. Not. Take.

Professor Puelz is sincerely the worst professor I have ever had. I honestly hope he reads these reviews to grasp what his students think of him. He makes you subscribe to his finance blog and pushes his book. This class is clearly an opportunity for him to push his unsolicited beliefs. It has nothing to do with the course description.

Dr.Puelz is a sub-par professor for Cox. The class itself is based on his opinion of financial planning compared to reality. In addition, he pushes his textbook and substack onto students to bolster his own gains and reputation.

Super sloppy, lazy, and rude. Poor at lecturing, teaching, and grading. I would avoid Dr.Puelz at all costs.

Confusing class overall, guidelines were not always clear for grading and I'm not totally sure what I learned. He can be kind of a jerk to students and doesn't seem to really care much. Insurance game made little sense and is 25% of your grade, and he doesn't break down how you are graded. Overall just eh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Puelz is a pretty blunt but good teacher. He assigns homework for every class that is due that night, but if you go to class and complete it, you will get a good grade on the assignment and won't have any homework. Attendance is not mandatory but he keeps in mind who is in class and who is not. Not an easy class, but very manageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't understand why so many people hated him. Yeah, the class was hard. Yeah, he wasn't my favorite professor, but he at least was fair and was willing to work with you if you were willing to work with him. From what I remember, most of the people who had problems with him didn't go to class.

Homework assignments after every class -- pay attention to lecture & you will do great. They are not hard & don't take long. Really interesting class. 6 quizzes/tests, takes best 5. Class is about financial planning, not super intriguing but I enjoyed the class and would take it again! If you ever have any questions, ask him or his TA!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor simply assigns way too much homework. An excel assignment is due after almost every class and he doesn't even give you until midnight for some of them. Would finish often class at 5pm and have an assignment due within a few hours. Pretty rude to students and not understanding to any problems they have. Worst class I've taken at smu

this class was a huge waste of time. you learn nothing and this professor is the WORST. you spend all your time trying to figure out random excel assignments and the quizzes make no sense. worst teacher, worst class, so disappointing.

Does not respect his students at all, have never seen a professor like this one. However, don't skip class and do your work and an A is not impossible. Assignment in every single class throughout the semester, but you'll get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a really great teacher who cares about risk management and insurance. Quizzes aren't bad if you study for 30 min. Assignments are tough but they really help you understand the concepts.
Great class with a lot of real world application. I would recommend that anyone graduating with a business major should at least know the basics of risk management.

Professor Puelz is an amazing lecturer, he will make sure you understand the important issues. Sometimes because the topics are new to most they can get confusing but overall a really beneficial class and I would recommend it to cox students looking for an elective.
Extremely strict on attendance. Not willing to help his students out at all.

Great class, great professor, show up, do the assignments and turn them in on time, post questions on the blackboard discussions, visit his office hours for help, and ask him about risk management and insurance. The work is hard, but very useful in real life.

Prof. Puelz is a great professor for those who are serious about understanding the material. The knowledge he shares is very much useful in real life. He goes great lengths for those specifically interested in risk management and insurance and has really contributed a lot to the successes I have had with scholarships, internships, and a career.

Puelz is awesome. Yes, it was one of the hardest classes I've taken, but I learned so much. The trick to getting an A is to simply DO THE HOMEWORK PROBLEMS until you get it and KNOW VOCABULARY & general concepts. Not too difficult. The homework problems are a lot like the test/quiz questions. Do all the problems he posts on blackboard too. Fun guy.

Lectures are worthless and unorganized, and you will have to teach yourself much of the material. Puelz is blatantly rude to his students in class and will single you out for it. Quizzes and tests are unnecessarily convoluted and unrelated to lectures. Take someone else, or you'll be at a disadvantage in future Fina classes b/c of a bad intro.
As long as your somewhat inteligent you should get an A. I still dont understand how some people still hate on this guy hes not that bad

This professor is terrible!! Not only is he hostile in class, but he makes the tests as difficult as possible. The first exam is much easier than the last so if you want to make a decent overall grade, study hard for the first one because you will need that to be the 30% test grade. He curves a LITTLE at the end so don't depend on it too much.

You will go to class to hear him ramble. You will try and teach yourself the material from the book. Then, come test time, he puts such problems that are much more complex than anything he taught. His curriculum mainly surrounds the formulas, and not much more. If at all possible, take another professor. You will barely learn anything with him.

Took Dr. Puelz's RMI course as an elective. Glad I did. He ended up being one of my favorite professors at Cox. Very clear, articulate and has a way of making the subject more interesting than it is. Additionally, I found the RMI game to be a great real-world experience.Only two exams and 6 quizzes. Optional final at end. Class average was B+.

Terribile professor. Laziest and sloppiest man teacher I've ever seen.  I love most of the COX professors but he is awful.  Two of my friends dropped the class because he was so rude and sarcastic to them and he made an entire group of girls cry.  I think his sarcasm and attitude are terrible and he and his wife are both terrible teachers.

For some unexplained reason he makes the test as hard as can be.  Even those who study hard and spend hours reading/doing homework, quizes...struggle with his tests.  I agree the material is hard but he doesn't have to make the tests that complicated to see who is studying and hwo is lazy.  Take the class with someone else...

Prepare to spend a lot of time on this class. Make sure you do good on the in class quizzes. Tests are diffcult. Read text book and do all HW problems - similar to in class quizzes. FYI If he doesn't think you are working on the class he will make you show him your work. Make sure you are studying if you want to get better than a C.

Tests are not easy, class average is mid 70s however he curves. If you want an B+ or higher, you gotta rely on those quizzes and self-online quizzes because the 2 exams represent 55% of your total grade. The 8 quizzes, he drops the 2 lowest, represents 35%.  The 12 self-online quizzes are easy 'cause you only need a 60% overall to get full credit.
Great Prof. if you can think for yourself
BP Is awesome. Most bad ass teacher in COX.
I agree. He's nice but it is a very hard class. And please don't ask questions in his 80+ person class. It's annoying to everyone else.
Very difficult...has a really messed up scoring system....not helpful at all...if Aduku is teaching take her instead...would never recommend him to anybody
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. PUELZ GETS OFF IN MAKING EXAMS & QUIZ AS DIFFICULT AS POSSIBLE. I QUESTION HIS QUALIFICATIONS...
This guy was one of the worst teachers I had at the Cox School of Business. He thrives on making tests hard as hell

He's approachable, available and helpful during his office hours. However, during class, he can be a intimidating and unclear. Don't be afraid to ask questions or slow him down if you're confused. His class is tough.
He's a nice guy and he tries his best...but he's very hard and you constantly have to stay ahead if you want to get a passing grade in his class.
Think she's ffunny and cute and is annoying ahl can't teach worth shte

This was Dr. Shudde's first year teaching STAT 2331 and she did awesome. There's so many extra credit opportunities, your final replaces your lowest grade, she drops lowest homeworks, your TAs do the lab with you (easy A)..She is great and accessible outside of class too. If you can't get Wickersham, do Dr. Shudde!!

Best stats class, she takes time to explain she will stop for questions and give more examples. She wants you to get a good grade. She doesnt grade hard on tests, they are on paper and you get a notes page. The labs feel pointless but thats the only downside i found.

Her lectures are clear, and she will stop the whole class to answer your question fully. A hw assignment is given after every lecture but it only takes 20-30 mins. Her tests are on paper and you can bring a full sheet of notebook paper as a cheat sheet. Just pay attention and you will be fine.

He doesn't input the proper calculations for grades, and we have to calculate our grade throughout the whole semester. He is the first professor I've ever encountered at SMU in my four years here who does this. He doesn't seem willing to help students after class, as he has a very cold attitude, and is still confused why students don't attend OH.

His lectures and HW are only loosely connected to the written problems he creates on exams. He will make up a problem and claim it's from the HW, when in reality it was very loosely based on the HW and requires additional knowledge which he doesn't teach in class. His exams are only 8 questions which make this even more detrimental to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very understanding and accomodating. Lectures can get a bit boring but in general was able to learn a good amount from this class. Would recommend redoing the homework assignments to study for the test. Wish he posted his notes from class
Seems strict but super accommodating and a lenient grader. If you review the lectures and homework problems, you'll have no problem on the exams.

Hard to understand and talks for the entire class period every time. Very boring class super hard to pay attention. Even if you try to pay attention you can't even really know what's going on because his explanations are very bad. Doesn't really teach the concepts well. Each test is only 8 questions so if you miss liked 2 questions you're cooked.

If you are a stats/ds major, this class should be a breeze. Homeworks, projects, and exams are graded very easily, just make sure you have a basic understanding of the material. I stopped going to class a quarter thru the semester and still got an A but take that with a grain of salt. Seems like a nice guy but i never interacted with him lol.
he was a bad professor. super difficult, hard to understand, and didn't adequately prepare us for the tests.

I enjoyed the way the professor presented the material and was very quick to reply when I had a question. I do wish there were more grading criteria other than 2 exams and homework, as one mess-up on an exam would cost you dearly, however I think he did a good enough job where that didn't matter. 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor is one of my favorites. I have never taken a statistics class before and was nervous about taking it this semester. He made it very easy to understand. I love the way he conducts class and his notes/presentations are super organized. He explains things extremely well and always does many example problems. Would recommend!!

weekly quizzes on readings. We read an entire book in 5 class periods. She doesn't use canvas, so you have to show up to class to have any idea of what is going on. Everything is handwritten including the two essay midterm and final. She will go off on tangents about weirdly intimate activities. I would take this class if you care abt gothic stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unfortunately just not well organized. An obnoxious amount of reading, assignments are unclear, and it is impossible to know your grade until it is too late to do anything about it because Sudan refuses to use canvas. reviews.comment: super disorganized and refuses to put grades in. didn't start using canvas until a month into the semester. doesn't answer emails or communicate deadlines. very knowledgeable and passionate about literature but does not operate the class well. don't take this if you're not an english major/minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She doesn't put any grades in canvas at all. If you miss more than two classes, you will get marked down points, even if you are out sick. Honestly one of the hardest graders I have ever had and we had to read like 7 really long books. For non-english majors I 100% would not recommend because she is such a harsh grader with VERY strong opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gives really engaging lectures. Not too many papers, but we have weekly quizzes. Found her to be a very fair grader.

Really enjoyed her class. She made the class discussions very interesting and engaging. Apparently, she liked my writing style, so I had no trouble with the class, but I had friends who said she was unclear about expectations in the writing assignments and graded harshly. The load is fair, but be prepared for lots of reading and class discussions.

I feel sorry for this person. He spends almost every lecture talking about his wealth. If you're really that rich, why waste your time at this age on a university campus? Every lecture is basically just an explanation of the next assignment, which is expected to be completed in a week!! The course felt like a waste of time and unnecessary stress.

LITERALLY THE MOST CONEITED MAN IN THE WORLD. It is disgusting, spends OUR class time talking about how much money he has and how amazing he is not at all teaching anything content-related. SMU needs to re-think who they're hiring.
Not worth the hassle and stress
Does not really care about his students just more about talking about himself or his companies. Talks about how much money he has constantly
Finally, a latino faculty member I can relate to! Rene is the best professor I ever had. Insightful, inspirational, and a true intellectual!
Rene is the man!! Very type B, unlike the majority of professors at Cox.

Very inspiring entrepreneurial spirit, I learned more in his class than in most COX courses that's fs. With that, be prepared to work, I wasn't able to put my best effort with my courseload; but here's some tips for success; keep your group if they put the same effort as you & take good notes as his expectations for assignments aren't too clear.

You are graded on your group project and basically nothing else. The expectations for the deliverables are sometimes unclear but Rene is willing to meet with you outside of class to discuss. Definitely not an easy A class, but you will learn a lot of useful skills that other classes do not address.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The whole semester is basically a long group project, you work with your group on everything which is nice but it's a lot of work. Professor Larrave is a really nice guy and he's teaching you useful materials for the real world but he's a tough grader so get ready to work.

Professor Larrave was an amazing teacher. The class/assignment was really challenging, but he was always willing to meet before class to tell us exactly what to fix etc. Although this class has a lot of work, I am so glad I took it. I learned more in this class than I have in most of my other business classes

Professsor Larrave was absent for a lot of lectures due to his other businesses. He is a tough grader and even meeting with him outside of class various times does not guarantee that you will do well on the projects.He spends most of his class talking about his experience but then grades on quantitative items that he does not go over in class.

All of these reviews are pretty spot on. Honestly, if you do the work/plan when you start your group project you should be fine. It is a lot of work but organizing the work within a group is paramount. Expect to do up to 3 hours of extra time outside of class a week. Overall, I have learned more in this class than most of my other classes combined.

Awesome professor. Not an easy A - the project is definitely difficult, but at the end you really feel good about it because youre using different skills from your degree. He gives great advice and his lectures are spot on. Put in the work and youll get a good grade. Not a class you can wait til the night before to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class if you are an independent worker. You are basically forced to work with a team of 3 people to do your MKTG, Financial, etc and all of those combined are worth 60% of your grade. If two people in your group start to go against you, it becomes a "them vs you" situation and the group decides how to allocate % points ie: 50/30/20

Rene is a good teacher and very successful businessman. His class is the most work of any class I have taken at SMU. At the end of the semester you end up putting together a 50 page business plan. He is a tough grader, you have to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: ok
Difficult class compared to other sections of ITOM 2308, but you learn a ton more than with other professors! Final project worth 40% of grade, midterm 20%, final 30%, and homework 10%.

I recommend taking Professor Rees very much. She is an extremely sharp woman that cares about her students' success. Although the class is textbook heavy outside of class, the information is very interesting and her teaching is very thorough and engaging. If you keep up with the readings, you will be set. An amazing professor, get to know her.

Dr. Rees is a caring and fabulous prof, but It is almost impossible to get an A in this class. She gives everyone the same grade for group projects and almost no group gets an A. Too many group projects for class during Covid. This class is probably amazing when it's not on zoom. I would not take her until after Covid. Also attendance is mandatory

Her lectures were really helpful and she tells you what to study for the exams. She is nice but a hard grader and her class is fun and insightful but sometimes her grading really doesnt make sense. If she grades you unreasonably though you can go to her and contest the grade.

Lectures were super informative and I learned a lot, BUT the group projects were ridiculously graded. There is no peer review so you're stuck with a bad grade if that's what the group gets. Impossible to get an A and the rubric doesn't tell you anything. Tests (due to COVID) are way harder than they need to be. Take someone easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Rees is an extremely difficult grader. Tests questions are based off of unclear hypothetical questions. Group projects are graded extremely unfairly and she doesn't take individual work/peer reviews into account. Participation is worth a lot of points and you have to go to every class.

Rees seems to make it as hard as possible for students to get an A. Course content isnt difficult but Rees is difficult. Her grading on group projects is completely subjective and based on if she likes you. Almost no one gets an A on the projects. Test questions are made to trick u. Dont take her, save yourself the trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Rees is awesome. She is tough but fair. She responds well to asking for help and genuinely cares what you do in your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor! Is very clear with grading requirements and doesn't give unnecessary homework. Good with feedback too!

Rees was nice, but a boring lecturer. She is very strict on her grading criteria, but she doesn't tell you what she wants beforehand. She pushes group work a lot, and there are two presentations. She does provide extra credit. A fair amount of reading and outside work. You have to participate in her research labs. Not bad, but not the best

Dr. Rees is a genuinely kind professor who is interested in the welfare of her students. She was more than willing to meet with me and discuss how I could improve my performance. Participating in class and setting aside time to study for tests are essential for an A. You wont like her at the beginning of the semester, but you will by the end.
Dr. Rees is awesome. I learned a lot, but more impressive was how much time she spent with me out of class to help me. I wish she taught more.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best MNO professor! Everyone is complaining about participation, but that part of class is easy and fun if you just do it! She's really helpful if you meet with her too. The tests are too bad, it is just memory so if you study, you will be fine! Take her!

Dr Rees is a good professor. She listens and she is fair when you go see her about your grades or performance on an exam or assignment. You do have to participate, but she makes that really clear. I went to see her about half way through the year to check on my participation and she helped me understand what I could do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr Rees expects a lot, but she cares about us. If you go and spend time with her, she will help you out on multiple different areas. She gives great lectures, and tests fairly on the content that has been talked about in class.

Dr Rees is great. I learned a ton in her class. She wants you to be there and participate. Her tests were tough but she let you drop your worst. Id definitely take more classes from her. Nice to look at as well...

I really love professor Rees, her class consist of 4 test( lowest one can be replace if you do extra credit) 4 homework, 2 group projects with presentations, you will have high participation score if you raise your hand and speak up in class. Its easy to make 100 for in class participation just speak up. I would take her class again anytime.
It is the day before the optional final and my grade just went from an A to a B because of in class participation. I think that says everything you need to know.

Take anyone else but Dr. Rees. a 94% is an A, which is already absurd, and Dr. Rees's grading is nonsensical. This is management 101 yet it seems as though she treats it as an MBA course. This is a very high-maintenance, high-effort class, and the reward is very low. How ironic, granted this is a management course.
If you enjoy being humiliated for asking questions this is the class for you. Zero support, zero empathy, and a massive ego.
This professor is undoubtedly the worst at our school, with a dismissive and sarcastic attitude towards students who he doesn't like. Bad teacher too.
Don't take this class. he doesn't like teaching and it's pretty clear throughout the semester that he fails at it

I'm sorta bad at math but Dr Reynolds is great. Took both 3302 and 3304 with him, definitely one of the better options for math! He provides all his notes that he lectures off of which helps a lot with focusing on in class examples. Open note/book exams but you have to be organized beforehand. Hard class imo but would def take Reynolds again
Steer clear of this class! Professor is disorganized, forgetful. Doesn't follow syllabus, changes requirements on a whim. An utter waste of academic potential.

Took Dr Reynolds Spring 2020 for Linear Algebra. He's probably the most organized prof I've had in 4 semesters at SMU, even with COVID. He teaches fast, but he's honestly really good. Tests were moderately challenging but made easier due to being open book. The final project was amazing! Proof heavy. Take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor! He has a great knowledge of Calculus and will help you though any trouble you are having. The class is difficult but he makes the class easier through how he teaches and how the grading is laid out. You need to participate and work a lot outside of the class.
He's a great professor. Keeps the class engaging and is available for help outside of class (and is actually helpful). His tests are open book/open note and are pretty fair. Overall, great guy

Dr. Reynolds is by far one of the best (if not the best) professor at SMU. His lectures are extremely clear and cohesive, and super informative. He conveys the material very well, and he is just such a nice guy. He really wants you succeed, even though the class is tough he makes it super understandable.

Prof is a great teacher, but grading was difficult in this class. Homeworks were graded brutally, and was super nit picky on exams. Oh, HE BELIEVES IN PROOFS. Probably best linear algebra prof, but also probably hardest linear algebra prof. Pick your poison.

Dr. Reynolds is an exceptional professor. His lectures are engaging and he's a really kind and funny guy. However, what others have said about his exams is true - they are really difficult despite being open-note. The final is weighted very heavily. I recommend him if you want to learn something, but an A won't come easily.

Wonderful professor! Try to understand the readings and warm-ups before each class. It'll make his lectures, which are fantastic, easier to follow. His tests are pretty d@mn hard, even though they're open note. Fortunately, he makes himself as available as possible to his students and is very helpful during office hours.

Best Math professor at SMU. His lectures are always interesting and he is great at explaining the concept. Test are open notes and books, but I still recommend studying and understand all the homework problems. He is always willing to help outside the classroom.

Prof. Reynolds is a nice guy, good teacher, and cares about the material and his students. Despite this, I busted my butt in this class and got great grades on the homeworks and out-of-class stuff. The tests were way more difficult than expected though and he wasn't an easy grader. Beware, nice guy, but tough class and grader.

He is wonderful. FINALLY a good math teacher I've found at SMU. Class started out really hard for me, but I went to see him and things immediately changed. He is so helpful. He wants you to understand the material. The rest of the semester was almost a breeze! And he has an awesome sense of humor. He is the best teacher in the math department.

He is the best teacher in the math department hands down! He is so helpful in and out of class. I had no interest in the material, but he was so great at explaining the topics in class that it made the class so easy to understand.
Awesome professor!  Always willing to help students excel.

He is such a great professor. The class material may be  hard, but he is great at explaining things in class. There are class quizzes every week, but they are short and doable. He wants you to do well in his class so he will help you in anyway he can. He is a must take professor!

There can't be a better professor than him. Out of all of my math classes I've taken he is the best. Material can be hard, but he puts so much effort into the class that it becomes very interesting. You can tell he truly loves what he does. Highly recommended.

This guy is seriously one of the BEST mathematics professors I have EVER had. He cares about your comprehension and learning and extends his office hours prior to exams to help you study. He also posts a very helpful review before every mid-term. Simply the best!!!

Dr. Jones is very clear on what you need to know, but you NEED to put in the work.  Very important to study little details and know the practice problems front and back.  Otherwise, he is a very caring professor and as long as you know the stuff and know it well you will succeed.

Tests are hard and are your whole grade, hw doesn't help, professors are vague when it comes to questions about the test and hw and want students to fail.
They need to curve this class bc majority of the class failed and reevaluate the teaching department.

Does he really think he's making a difference in the biology department here? it's a genuine question, he has the worst reviews, takes no accountability, and doesn't know how to teach. Having a student come once a week to tutor you for less than 2 hrs does nothing with the amount of students there are.

It's funny that Annika Wylie isn't on rate my professor, but since the class is a flipped class for god knows what reason, (all that does is make the course more unbearable because we're stuck with learning a new professors style), we're stuck with both of the worst professors. She sits on the chair in the most monotone voice and reads off slides.

Feel bad giving a bad review but if more than half the class failing, maybe something should be done. New prof isnt better either. Review sessions r useless, HW isnt engaging, and you have to read the whole textbook to pass exams since lectures arent recorded and slides are just copied from textbook.
If you're a bio major, good luck.

Is he the best professor? No. Is he good enough to get by? Yes. The other reviews are a little extreme. Just take notes and pay attention in lecture. Start studying a week before the tests, do the practice problems from the textbook, and make a Quizlet. The class is hard but if you put in the work and study well in advance, you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: The dude isnt a bad guy, but he is a terrible terrible professor. I do not know why smu has a horrible biology department. If half the class fails the 1st test, hmmm maybe its you and not the students studying weeks in advance for a test just to fail it? Lectures are boring, says right or okay after every sentence, he makes this class unbearable

Literally have been doing good in every other bio class except this one, I have a D. Blamed the students for the mean being a 65 first test, then gives no extra credit or anything. Rounding it up 4 points to a C does barely anything. Homework weight does nothing, it's basically just the tests which is so unfair. Homework should be weighted more
He is nice but the lectures are very boring and hard to understand. Even with studying a lot the tests are tricky and there is no real way to be completely prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel bad giving a poor rating because Jones is very kind, however his lectures aren't the best. The homework isn't intellectually stimulating or helpful. It's pretty difficult to navigate how to do well in this class, and by the time you do, it's too late to get an A. Wish they offered extra credit, it wouldn't hurt.
He is very nice and a good teacher if you can get through his lectures which are boring.

His lectures weren't the most interesting thing ever but they were at least easy to follow. He was a fine professor and I didn't think he was as bad as his rating suggests. The tests were tough and didn't have a lot of questions so you do have to study a lot to do well.

Dr. Jones is a very nice man, I just don't believe he is the best professor. He talks quietly and can be quite boring in the lectures. I struggled to stay awake during the first half of the course. His tests were difficult and I did not feel prepared enough for either of his two tests, despite studying extensively.

It sucks that this is the only option for genetics professors because it's already a challenging class and the unhelpful professors make it worse. I have to say that Dr. Norris was slightly better at teaching even though his tests...Tests are insanely hard and no amount of studying will help because of how questions are worded to trick you.

5 points for a MC question is crazy. (out of 25 questions) Could not care less if you get clapped by the exams. Homework and practice tests are truly useless to the highest degree. I hope you read this Dr. Jones and I hope you know you are only slightly better than Norris.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a very good lecturer, he fails to keep the class motivated during his presentations. The presentations barely have any writing and you would be better off just reading the textbook. The practice problems are super helpful.
