Few assignments, but make sure you do your best on them in order to get a good grade. They arent hard though. Tests can be difficult as they cover a lot of material, but just study his ppts!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very nice, passionate, funny guy. Very few assignments so no slip ups! Tests are hard because he has very specific concepts on them. However, if you go through every popwerpoint slide for studying you can do well on tests. Getting an A is very doable, just have to work for it!

Sedman really cares about what he teaches and makes class really interesting. There's not a lot of grades though so you can not slip up. 2 tests,3 short papers,1 large project, and a final. If you memorize the powerpoints you're fine. He tells you in class what he's going to put on the test as essays, so as long as you go and study, take this class

This class was history of animated film and it was by far my favorite class at SMU. Sedman is hilarious and truly enjoys everything about animation. Every week we would have a "monitoring project" which basically meant we went to the movies for the class period. HIGHLY RECCOMEND

not clear what matters and what doesn't in his lectures, questions on tests are often random side notes and not the bulk of the important material. took the final and still don't have 3 of the grades from previous projects and big assignments, makes it hard to know where you stand in the class. funny, but needs to be more serious
David Sedman is the funniest and most fun prof. Great lectures.

Great Professor, if you need to take a Pillar class TAKE THIS. Has attendance checks but going to class is not a chore. He makes lectures fun. 3 Writing assignments and 3 Tests. If you go to class and study the slides, making an A is totally possible
He's a really funny guy, and he keeps lectures are intersting. His tests are alwyas from his lectures, and he puts his powerpoints online. I would take him again.
very interesting professor. one of my least favorite classes. first test was very confusing. 3 papers throughout the year

(Summer 1) Took this as an 8am and he kept me awake. He's super hyper, moves fast, talks fast. Really easy straightforward material. Working with powerpoint, excel, etc.. We made an iMovie and song on garage band. So pretty easy/entertaining. Tests are straight from the notes, so study slides and pay attn. to his hints.

He's super funny and interesting and really enjoys his job - you can tell! Make sure you show up and take notes and study before exams and you will be fine! He makes you do presentations but they are short and everyone has to do them so they aren't bad at all! I definitely recommend him to everyone!

Great guy. He's funny and enthusiastic about what he teaches. The tests are a little difficult, so you have to put in a little effort towards studying. Other than that, great professor! Highly recommended!
Professor Sedman enjoys teaching and makes classes really fun. Totally take his classes

He was the best professor I have ever had. Professor Sedman is hilarious, but also knows a lot about film. I would suggest taking his classes! The only thing is, is that you must attend class. His exams are all about the lectures.

Professor Sedman might be one of my favorite teachers at SMU. Not only does he know the material, but he makes the class fun and interesting. He's easy to understand and talk to, and he really does have a passion for it. An awesome professor
Great professor, manages to make a sometimes-boring subject interesting because of his effective teaching skills. If you are willing to put in a little work it is an easy A.
He is such a quirky professor but class is really fun to attend. He knows what he's talking about and clearly has a passion for it, which makes it better for his students!
He's easy.

He was really chill and understanding probably the best professor I've had. He gives tons of extra credit opportunities. I definitely recommend him. If it was possible I would give him 100/10 rating. He goes above and beyond.
Never even talked to the guy and he's the best teacher I've ever had. Made me seriously consider switching my major to history, all around great guy.
Weekly readings are interesting, there's flexibility for your final projects and there are tons of opportunities for extra credit.

One of the best professors I have ever had! Personally, ITOM is hard, but his lectures are so engaging, and he is very generous when it comes to grading. He is hilarious, kind, and overall a wonderful professor. 10/10 would recommend!

Clearly an academic with little understanding of application and execution. Low self-esteem makes him ill-equipped to be candid and straightforward with adult students. Intelligent on subject matter, but poor instructor, theory heavy with implementation.

Fun class, an easy way for  an A, the professor gives you the exam during the review session and solutions. If you have good memory you will receive an A. I did not learn much, was not important for my Finance classes
Fun, insightful, and very helpful in describing a very complex subject in ways that make mathematical modeling accessible to those that may not have a strong math background.

The absolute WORST Professor ever! I have never had a Professor so unwilling to help students and actually not want us to succeed continuously beating us down. If I did not need this class to Graduate than I would have dropped, but we'll see if I even Graduate not with a professor that had my A in the class drop to a C-.

Passive aggressive, assigns more work than is needed, takes months to grade, and doesn't communicate effectively. No rubrics, deducts points he "feels" are best, and is truly an unreasonable grader. A quote by him: "To put it simply, no one should be passing this class or getting a degree without learning this basic academic skill." AVOID HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Harshest grading professor I have ever had. For an ONLINE class there is an absolutely ridiculous amount of work. 4 textbooks. Assignments take hours to complete and he provides no rubric, but will never tell you what to fix. Takes forever to grade, literally WEEKS. Teaches at multiple universities and probably shouldn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor refuses to grade papers on time or post exams at the previously announced time.  As I speak, at 5:55 pm, he still has not posted our final exams, which were to be posted at 5 pm.
kept the class interesting! Fun projects.. class isn't mandatory, but go - he gets a little upset when too many students repetitively don't show up

He was very nice, and the the intro class was not too boring. But the classes went all over the place. What he taught pertained to the book, however it was out of order, so it was often hard to study. If you go to class and put in effort you'll get a good grade. The book are interesting and the project for the project you get to choose the topics.
Terribly biased for a sociology teacher. Completely boring class with uninteresting lectures and discussions. Do yourselves a favor and avoid at all costs.
Confusing and poorly grading. Don't take his class!
Taught us almost nothing and then expected sophomore CS level projects every single week. Not a bad guy, terrible professor.
The slides he covers are super simplified and show no code examples. When it comes to the programs you'll have to do a considerable amount of self teaching.
I learned more about his travels than data structures.
Loves talking about travels, but not the class.

This professor has no clear structure, spends class time on irrelevant topics, and doesn't provide helpful code examples. Assignments are far too advanced for the course level, and there's no clear syllabus. If you want to learn data structures, I strongly recommend finding a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shaibal is an extremely lazy professor. He always shows up to class unprepared and proceeds to yap about irrelevant topics for 20-30 minutes before quickly skimming over important course concepts. He barely ever shows us actual code and he encourages us to use LLMs for our projects. If you want to actually learn, do not take this professor.

Honestly a very lazy professor. He doesnt really teach any material and only ever goes over slides that cover very minimal information. A lot of projects and assignments where you have to teach yourself how to implement everything because he doesnt teach it. Didnt even have the class material prepared so he just comes up with it as we go along

Prof Storer is the best. He cares abt his students and does his best to make class interesting and engaging. He also memorizes everyones name by week 2. His lectures are pretty interesting and he likes to hear our opinions about things too. He also makes it very clear what you need to know for the 2 major exams. We also did a few group projects.
All the reviews are true, he is great!! He's genuinely very nice and wants us to be good people and succeed. He is very respectful to all his students of different backgrounds and cultures.
Most overrated professor. He does literally nothing.
Such a nice guy. He really cares about his students so talk to him if you need help. Homework load wasn't bad at all. Definitely a chill class to take.
Agree with all the reviews. Definitely take his class. Very chill and he's a super nice guy!

Professor Storer is by far the best professor at SMU. He genuinely cares about his student's success. He is very understanding. His lectures are extremely helpful and goes over every concept clearly. There are 2 presentations (1 team, 1 individual) & 2 exams (midterm, finals). Quizzes are open note taken remotely. I 110% highly recommend taking him

Genuinely cares about his students and is very understanding if circumstances arise. Will take his time to get to know you and help you out. His class is based on assignments and group projects. His lectures are pretty fun to follow along and applicable to the real-world. As long as you put in the work, you will get a good grade.

Overall awesome professor. Just wants to see his students do well in his course and build relationships with them. Not too difficult but you're still going to learn in his course. Can't reccomend him enough. Would take him even if his class wasn't required for my minor.

I would 100% recommend this class to anyone. Professor Storer is great and very chill. The class consists of open-note quizzes, two exams, and two presentations. If you put in the work, you will get a good grade. A lot of the material is real-world stuff for when we graduate, so it is good to learn about these topics.

Truly a great professor and person. Although the class may not be super enticing for some, just having this professor in your life immediately makes it better. Truly cares about everyone, loves what he does, has great stories, and really aims to inspire others. The difficulty of the class is exactly on par for what you are learning.

Professor Storer is the best!!!!! Easily one of my favorite professors at SMU. He created such a positive and welcoming environment. I usually get nervous presenting, but felt totally comfortable in his class. He's so supportive, accommodating, and genuinely cares. Highly recommend!

Dr. Storer is amazing - the way he explains concepts is engaging, and my favorite part about this class was that it what we learned is actually useful in real life. The guest speakers we had were interesting and especially helpful as I was negotiating salary for my first job after graduating. I would recommend this class 10/10
One of my favorite professors at Cox. He makes the material more interesting and gives feedback where a lot of other professors don't.
Not for me.

Dr. Storer's class is pretty easy if you attend class and pay some attention. He can be a bit tough when grading participation, group assignments, and presentations. He keeps is interesting for an HR class. Quizzes are open book and tests are relatively easy/curved.

He has a passion for teaching and genuinely cares for his students. His class makes you think critically and put concepts together for practical learning. I tell all my friends to take his class. Highly recommend!

ritiques feel more nitpicky than anything else and will just tell you to 
"specify" when your ideas are right there. Would not recommend.

Professor Storer made the material more interesting by getting us involved during class. He gave positive feedback on assignments and also helped me find summer internship opportunities. One of the most caring professors at SMU.
He is awesome! Really chill and friendly, super resourceful. Gives days off of class to work on group assignments and tests aren't crazy hard.

Professor Storer is an inspirational professor who is well acquainted with the Human Capital and Talent Management industry and class materials. His lectures are extremely engaging and his feedback on group projects is meticulous. I really enjoyed his class, and highly encourage everyone to give it a try! You won't regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Storer is a great professor and his knowledge of the subject material cannot be beaten. He has years of hands on experience in this field which is something that makes this class extremely relevant to the business world. I would 100% take his class again and his professionalism and respectful demeanor make him a pleasure to work with.

Professor Storer has been one of my favorites thus far at SMU. He genuinely cares for his students so much and is willing to help you extensively. He is super passionate about what he teaches and the course is extremely relevant, engaging and interesting.

This was one of my favorite classes this semester. Professor Storer is a great instructor he truly cares for his students. The information taught is all very practical and he presents it in an interesting way. Your grade is based on 2 big exams, 2 projects, reading quizzes, and in class assignments. Such a good elective!!

Professor Storer CARES about his students while they're in his class and even after. Not a blow off class but its highly engaging. He's a fair professor, what you put in is what you will get out. Regardless of your major, this class will be of value if you care about working with people. One of the most practical classes I took in my 4 years at SMU

Shawn is hands-down one of the most caring professors I've ever met. He'll make the time for you, and really make you feel supported. I'd never considered HR as a career path, but his class was so engaging that it changed my perspective on the HR field. Plus, a lot of his content is useful for anyone who works a job. Super fun and helpful course!

Not a college-level course, it was more like a paid seminar you get at a hotel when attending a business conference, basically a dumbed down version of the real deal. I mean that's fine but by no means is going to help one's career. Take him to pad your grade, he's boring but fine, take someone else if you want real connections/career.

GREAT Professor! He care about his students and can make even boring material fun. Lots of different types of work in this class: projects, group work, quizzes, and presentations but all tied the material together.

One of my favorite professors at SMU, he's hilarious, open-minded, and caring for his students. Group projects are straightforward and exams are based right from the lecture material, the textbook also helps a lot. Talk and get engaged in class for participation points. Can't recommend him enough!

Professor Storer was one of the best professors I have had at SMU. I implore all of my friends in Cox to take him. He truly loves the material and cares about his students. It is clear that he wants the best for them and makes the material so interesting. I have great respect for him and wish I could take him for the rest of my experience at SMU.

Prof Storer is one of the best professors in Cox. He is amazing lecturer, and he is super passionate and knowledgeable about HR. He really encourages participation by requiring two individual presentations from each person throughout the semester, so be prepared! If you put in any effort in the class, you will get an A.

Amazing professor! Class is fun and dynamic. You will have presentations throughout the semester on interesting topics. 

He is an absolute must, take him it will help you get prepared for your career.

This professor is unorganized and dismissive. Lectures are purely conceptual, offering no practical examples to prep for exams or homework. He avoids questions, gives unclear guidance, and leaves students to teach themselves. Avoid if you value your education.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 50% of the class is an easy 100 and you only need a 90 to get an A; however, tests are a time crunch and are much harder than what Dr. Dalley teaches in class. He makes class entertaining, but you have to spend a lot of time teaching yourself the material. Test averages were in the 60's (he doesn't curve). Online practice problems will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!! I struggled from the beginning because I hadn't taken Calculus 1 beforehand. I constantly emailed him for help and he did nothing. He merely recommended that I do more problems and attend class (I came to every class and sat in the front row). TA wasn't there and in-class problems were way easier than the tests and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. Nothing that he explains in class is remotely near whats on the homework or tests. In class, we are taught the most rudimentary skills, then have to learn everything on your own while doing the homework. He doesnt guide you through problems, and doesnt explain why youre wrong.
He genuinely knows his stuff, and he teaches his material well. You do have to give effort into the class, but he is fairly understanding.

Professor Dalley speaks within his own frame of knowledge. When you ask questions on homework and labs, he enters the room to answer everything except for your question. He is not empathetic towards personal circumstances whatsoever. I would highly recommend taking another professor or take bio for credit all the way. This class was not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He requires the students to buy the textbook he wrote, which also contains all the quizzes. The lab session is the only difficult part, but if you ask him he will provide hints. There is only one exam which is the final. It's open booked and all multiple choices, and he will provide the questions (without the choices) before the exam.
Dr. Dalley displays his passion for Physics throughout the semester but he doesn't prepare the class well for exams.

If you attend lectures and take notes you'll be fine - he wants you to do well! Two 4-Q online quizzes per week plus a 3-Q written homework, but they're easy and if you get a quiz Q wrong he lets you redo it. Only 2 tests (not worth much of grade) and he gives the test Qs in advance. The only hard part is the labs. Plus, it's only 90% for an A!

Took his janterm physics class and it was definitely worth it. Quizzes everyday wasn't ideal, but it's only 8 days of class and you can redo any wrong answers for partial credit. There was a lot of reading for the class, but with the condensed janterm schedule it makes sense. He gave interesting lectures and genuinely enjoyed teaching physics!

Dr. Dalley is a decent professor. Not the best, but not the worst. Weekly quizzes with the chance to re-do them. One midterm and the final. Online survey due before each class. Really not too hard of a class if you do the homework and do well on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his class but he's not at all understanding about extenuating personal problems of his students, don't expect any sympathy from him. After all he is British. It seems like he deliberately avoids interacting with students out of class and prefers to pawn them off on TA's.

A small test and homework every week and multiple choice quizzes every day, does an ok job explaining things and he gives you a formula sheet. If you're good with math you'll be good with this class because you can get through the testfinal problems if you keep relationships between things in mind and work through them. He takes roll by asking Qs

Doesn't teach topics thoroughly. Went to help sessions with TA's every week to get help on HW and still would receive less than perfect grade back when he encouraged us to go to them for help. When the regular monday tests come around you will be left confused and feeling like you haven't learned that topic to the degree the question is asking.
He makes thing much more confusing and he speaks at a really low voice! I cannot learn anything from his class! And test every Monday.
Great Guy, very helpful and will teach you everything he tests.
Good teacher but his tests are there to bring down your grade and nothing more. The test averages are between 50%- 70%

Dr. Dalley is extremely hard when he grades. He grades everything with so much detail. I find it really difficult to get all of the points on a homework. I never got an A no matter what I did. The labs are most of them extremely long and consuming. His explanations are really confusing and he never helps you.
He is a good teacher but the tests are killer. HW and quiz due everyday.

Dr. Dalley is the only person I know who can legitimately teach physics. His class is structured in a way that if you do the reading/quizzes/homework/attend lectures, you really cannot go wrong. Just meet him halfway and you'll do find. His tests are difficult, but not unreasonably.

Dr. Dalley hates teaching students who are not actual physics majors and expects  his non-major students to understand and explain things in the way physics students would.  It seems like a blowoff until you write the two essays and take the final exam when the essays are so broad that it is difficult to even understand what is being asked.

Took this over the summer (absolute mistake). The grade was exclusively tests (and 5 of them in 4 weeks is awful). He actually teaches very well, and if you go over the problems in the book most of the tests will be fine, but the final is EVIL. 10 questions, no partial credit; dropped me over a letter grade.

This was honestly my favorite class to attend last semester. The class is a liberal art's introduction to physics, so there is almost no math involved, save basic algebra occasionally. Dalley makes the class enjoyable, and as long as you take notes, it's hard to make less than a B+ in there, honestly. Take this one for GEC, you don't regret it.
Hands down, amazing english professor. inspiring, thoughtful lectures. class is extremely well organized. shes also a great person. i recommend her completely to anyone, take her class if you can!

I really enjoyed Professor Siraganian's class, and her as a professor. She is a fair grader and doesn't give a ton of assignments. The class mostly consisted of in-class discussions, with a few papers. I highly recommend her!
Insightful professor and helped me improve my writing significantly. Just do not be late or else it's scary!

She is a great professor. I really enjoyed her lectures. The nly bad thing is she gives almost daily quizzes, so if you miss class then you miss a quiz. She did drop two, though. She also assigns almost weekly 2 pg papers She grades the kind of strictly but it shouldnt affect your final grade(I got an A) if you do good on the quizzes. I reccommend.

Good teacher, but didn't enjoy the class. With different material, I think I would have actually enjoyed her teaching style greatly. There is a lot of in-class discussion, a collection of 2-page essays (in contrast to a few big ones) and no tests except the final. I'd say take her, she's nice, relatable, and helps in any way she can to clarify.
He is a bit strange, not typical teacher but its a doable course and I got a lot out of it.
His grading is a bit strange, and you give like 10 business presentations. The class was not hard but he def graded a bit tough at times

Professor Mak is such a fun teacher. If you want to learn the basics of entrepreneurship then I recommend taking him. You have to come up with a lot of business ideas throughout the semester and it's mostly group work. He also brings in professionals to judge "pitch contests" and tell us about their careers. Fun class not hard grader.

Professor Mak is a very easy grader, but overall the experience was lackluster. Students invest heavily in getting an MBA from SMU, and this was not a good use of my money or time. There is nothing I got from this course that I couldn't have gotten from joining the entrepreneurship course. Ultimately, this course is all bravado and no substance.

Mak is a good professor, but be ready to create 20 business ideas throughout the semester. This class has a lot of busy work and presentations. You don't learn much of anything about running a business, more just how to come up with an idea and see if it is doable. He is passionate and knowledgeable but this class gets old and work-heavy.

I can't in good faith recommend to anyone with self-worth or entrepreneurial goals. Poor design and outdated examples (10+ yrs). No rubrics or feedback though grades are compounding. Highest so far is an A- for class. Doesn't post instructions for GROUP projects until 2 days before due. ADHD slides. Expects you tomemorize lists but won't warn you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Decided to do Entrepreneurship for my concentration and was excited to take Mak's class but was let down. He has a very narrow insular mindset when it comes to a strategic approach and creation of ideas. He uses his "entrepreneurial" career, being a professor, and leverages it to prove his credibility. Albeit, he is well liked, I wouldn't recommend

Dr. Mak is awesome. He is incredibly enthusiastic about entrepreneurship and really shows that he cares about his students learning the material. Usually assigned one small homework each week, occasionally some larger projects but always gave enough time to get them done and ask questions if needed. Highly recommend taking his class!

Dr. Mak is an enthusiastic professor. There are a lot of small assignments and three group projects. You don't really learn anything about the business side of entrepreneurship, only the ideation aspect.

Awesome professor! Easy assignments. Grades easily on group projects and presentations. There will be two "midterm" quizzes that are on RANDOM topics and you'll probably fail them but hey those are the only assignments that will drop your grade a little. I got As on everything but the quizzes and ended with an A- in the class

Disclaimer: Dropped the class after a few weeks. Very smart and experienced prof. Thought the class would be about how to raise capital for your business and other practical issues. Class is really about how to come up with new business ideas. Poor lecturer and unrealistic expectations. Project heavy class and strict grading.

Took this class because I want to be my own boss some day, Mak has the mind of Einstein and can help you out but he has unreal expectations. His class is interesting and he has real life examples and experience, I enjoyed it but he needs to cut back on a few things. I just feel that there is a lot going on and he grades SUPER strict on assigments

A lot of people are super critical of Mak on here... Let me set the record straight. Professor Mak is a super kind, positive professor. He has a lot of small assignments with deadlines. I took 18 hours and worked a part-time job and got an A just fine. He has a million bonus opportunities too, and will ALWAYS make time for you if you need help.

This class is the worst class I have taken at COX. Professor Mak has "experience" but he lectures not on our level. He kind of takes away from creativity from assignments by grading them unreasonably hard. I like the concept of a class for being entrepreneurship minded, but I can learn more by learning it myself and attending seminars.

Kind of wishing I had dropped this class, the class itself is not hard but he expects way more than what is necessary. Also, he grades super strict for no reason. This class is not making me want to be an entrepreneur! I could learn more by researching about it not taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Horrible might as well be an MBA class, not an elective class. He's a smart guy but doesn't know how to teach effectively. Also, requires Facebook page, twitter, and other assignments. just too much going on at once. You get to do a couple of field trips which are fun but If you want an interesting class look elsewhere!!

The rudest professor I have taken at COX, the course is interesting but could be taught better if it were a different professor. His ego is too big for his britches and when people speak up in class he is rude if its not the right answer. Has unreal expectations for his assignments and a short time frame to complete them. Also, an elective class!!!
Amazing professor

like his new mustache...awesome professor.. I feel the best professor i ever had in my graduate school

There is a lot of reading, and he is not an easy grader but he truly cares about his students. He stayed up with our class till 3am the night before our research papers were due to help us.

Sloan is easily one of, if not the best teacher at SMU. He's always available to help you with papers and it will make a huge difference on your grades if you take advantage of that. He keeps lectures and course material interesting. The research paper is long but the rest of the papers throughout the year are quite short. Great guy!

Sloan was an excellent DISC professor. He was hilarious, easy-going, but still held standards. That being said, Sloan was incredibly slow on grading assignments. We would have our next major assignment due before we would receive our first assignment back. Sloan,if you see this, keep up the great work, but please grade things within a shorter time.

The best English teacher I have ever had! I recommend doing the reading because quizzes are detailed, but not hard. For papers, email him your rough drafts and he will provide great feedback. He even ended up writing most of my thesis statements for me. Good luck trying to get into his class, but if you do, lucky you!
AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING! His class is filled within 30 seconds of opening so good luck scoring him! However, if you do CONGRATS!
Love Sloan, enough said.

Greatest professor I've had thus far. I hated writing and reading until I took this course with him. It took a lot of work and time to perfect my papers, but the end result was satisfactory, and I got the grade that I deserved. He connects with all his students and makes English an exciting subject.
Without question, the best professor at SMU. I grew immensely as a writer and as a critical thinker in his class.

Professor Sloan is an amazing teacher. He keeps class interesting with good books, and engaging discussions. He is always willing to help students. He responds to emails at any time of day or night! I highly recommend him! He has made me enjoy going to english class! One of the best professors at SMU!

You would be a fool not to attempt to score Sloan as a professor. He's absolutely brilliant, and by the end of the year, a tiny bit of that will have hopefully rubbed off on you. This class is an A if you try, and your writing will be improved by the end of the year. Guaranteed. His assignments are clear and he is extremely helpful.
One of the best professors at this university. Such a great guy, his class will fill before any other at the entire school. Helpful, great knowledge, great material... he is a must take
One of the best professors ever. He's really hot too.

By far the best professor at SMU. Consider yourself very lucky if you have the opportunity to take his class. Willing to spend hours working on your papers to help you get a good grade, and while it is by no means an easy A, it is a very interesting course and well worth taking.  Improved my writing immensely and am grateful I was able to have him.

Ross Sloan was my favorite professor at SMU during my freshmen year. He's funny, caring and very helpful. If you ask for help on paper and ask him to edit it before turning it in, he will pre-grade it, then u an edit it and turn in a better paper. Overall fantastic professor.

Best english teacher I have ever had!!! I despised Discourse last semester. This semester it was my favorite class. Make sure you take him at least once! Super funny, super cool.A lot of reading and writing but the class discussions are a blast.
Probably my favorite professor. He loves making fun of all the little SMUish things that happen and he makes the class really fun.

I had professor Sloan for 1301 and 1302.  He is the BEST professor at SMU by far! He loves his students and his job. He is willing to help day or night and will even come to campus in the middle of the night if need be. He is a fair grader, so his class is not an easy A, but with all of the help that he offers, his class shouldn't be your hardest.

Professor Sloan was extremely helpful throughout the semester and always available by e-mail, office hours, etc. He truly loves his job and it's obvious. If you go to class, do the super short readings, and speak up you will be just fine in class. Work on your papers and he will know....the grade will pay off.

One of my favorite classes this semester. Sloan makes this class fun, and improved my writing A LOT! English is  my second language, and he helped me in every way possible. I really respect this man, and you should definitely take with him. On the other hand, this class was not easy for me. But it was so worth it because Sloan will fix your writing

Honestly, hands down,  the BEST teacher I've ever had here at SMU. I put a 4 on easiness because if you're a good writer he will appreciate it and give you an A. But, if you're not, he will help and grade based on effort. You can't go wrong with Sloan.

Love love love! He is the most amazing teacher I have ever had! Makes you work hard but at the same time is very enjoyable. Very funny sense of humor and always made class super interesting. Consider yourself lucky if you get this class because people fight for this teacher
omg! I love professor sloan. one of the best! Not only is he raw in the classroom, but outside of the classroom too. btw he's a cutie! <3
I loved Dr. Sloan! If you are willing to work, then Dr.Sloan will love you!
Best English professor I've ever had. Challenges you,but an A is attainable with hard work. Gets to know each and every one of his students and his class is interesting. Great sense of humor.

Best English teacher I've ever had hands down. He made me want to write, and I pushed myself to produce the best writing I possibly could for him. Interesting, caring, hilarious, and witty. I've never seen a teacher work so hard to make his class such a success. There is no class I would recommend more at SMU than a class with Professor Sloan.
BY FAR THE BEST PROFESSOR AT SMU. CAN EXPLAIN THINGS VERY WELL, AND OVERALL CLASS S FUN.

Great prof! English classes were not my forte throughout my scholastic life, however I thoroughly enjoyed 1301 and 1302 with professor Sloan.  It was fun having a young teacher, especially one who brings enthusiasm to class.  Read the readings and bring them to class.  Bring your syllabus to class too, just in case.

Really good professor as long as you do the readings. He's pretty good at picking interesting stories.  He's a fair grader and is always open for extra help or to read over an essay.  Very quick at responding to e-mails. Really nice and wants his students to succeed.

really awesome prof. all he wants is that you read the material and participate. he hates it when people plagiarize. But he is extremely helpful with assignments, very quick to respond to emails and his quizzes are very simple and straight forward as long as you do the readings.
This class is exhausting for no reason. Endless nitpicking, unclear expectations, and zero consistency.

I never rate professors on this site, but after seeing all the negative ratings I thought I would weigh in. Yes, his classes are difficult. His target audience is students who are actually going into statistics/data science and want to put in the work to do so. Don't take him for required technical credit towards a completely unrelated degree.
DR. SOUTH IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I EVER HAD! HE IS SOOOOOOOO GOOD!

reviews.comment: A packet of slides with two legs, definitely not amounting to what we were promised when applying for this degree, certainly not what we're paying for.

He just reads slides and running pre-prepared code during lectures. He was tough with grades. I expected the class to be practical since he is a Professor of Practice, but it ended up being neither academically deep nor practical.
Guy's a piece of work. Lectures are slow and monotone, and he legit just reads off the slide as if we can't read.
he's difficult becuase he's not a good teacher and a very difficult human being, avoid.

Straightforward class going over syntax for R and little bit of SQL.  Homework and labs are basic applications of the syntax.  Participation is 15% of your grade.  You can have at most 2 absences and 2 tardies before your grade starts to drop.
Am a 4.0 student and I have never gotten grades like these even looking it up and you find nothing. its impossible to ace this class and he's not setting you up for anything for good grades at all

Dont take this professor. This was the worst experience of my life. Absolutely everything 
is excessive. Take literally anything but this professor.

Hardest statistics class I've taken (I've taken almost all undergrad classes). Extremely technical coding in R with 2 major data assignment projects that take over 40 hours each. The exams aren't awful but if you aren't good at coding you will seriously struggle.

Initially appears manageable only to unravel into an ordeal of excessive advanced concepts, unclear grading, and point deductions galore without any explanation even when you try to find him in office. An unrelenting barrage of busy work that'll have nothing to do with your graded work, is extremely unclear in his "lectures" or whatever unorganized stuff that was falling out of his mouth, and unless you have a mastery of the course already before taking it,  you will do poorly like i did. Lowest grade I ever received. Take literally anyone else.

Teaching consists of methodical lectures and corresponding ungraded in-class practice directly related to homework and exams. Took the class during a half-month semester so highly fast-paced. I would come into class already knowing introductory/intermediate R not to be overwhelmed. Exams consist of a conceptual paper portion and programming portion

Great professor as usual. Most useful class if you want to get good at using R in all facets. Best professor. Always answers questions whenever you have em. Easy to learn from and the data assignments and homework were very relevant and quite intense. Still, he gives you all the booster code to work with.

reviews.comment: Took him for 6301 as well. Excellent professor. I'm usually not not thrilled when I come out of a class with a B but this class was so beneficial to me that I didn't even care. The class can be a lot of work, but it's not unreasonable and you will get your money's worth of knowledge from Dr. South. Highly recommend

3300 class was pretty hard for me because I was not familiar with R studio and the whole class evolves around it. After getting pass that it was okay. reviews.comment: Extremely helpful during office hours. Lectures are clear and organized. He gives practice exams before exams, and they're literally the exam with different numbers. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. HE IS AMAZING. YOU WILL GET A SOLID A.

South is really a chill professor. It is so funny that he always tries so hard to find some good memes and hopes the memes would make the lecture fun. I had him for 4 semesters in a row. Definitely recommended. He is a very easy and fair grader!!! Talk to him and he will try to help you.

He's a good speaker which makes the class much easier. We spent the first 8 weeks covering old material from 2331, honestly a pretty easy class and it's really fun with him. He's super chill and is super forgiving when it comes to grades. If you bomb an exam he'll replace it with a final if it's better. Top-notch professor.

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend Dr South enough. He really cares a lot about his students and does a lot to make himself avaialble outside of class to help you learn and enjoy the experience. Stat's isn't always the most enjoyable subject, but he adds a lot of examples and pretty comprehensive slides to help you understand concepts and enjoy the process.

Dr. South is probably the best professor I've had so far at SMU. Really nice, great at explaining things. If you come to every class, pay attention, and actually follow along and do the examples, you'll have a great understanding of stats and barely need to study for the exams. I like that he drops two labs and homeworks.

Dr. South is a fantastic professor. He really cares in office hours and is willing to help work with you until you understand the content. His tests are not bad if you study the powerpoints. The only thing to be wary about is that there is an open note quiz every single class to prevent people from skipping.

Go to labs & do all homework. Stats is pretty boring, but he really cares and tries to do the best for his students. Do the reviews he gives for exams. Doesn't offer extra credit, but he drops the 2 lowest lab & homework grades. He's available outside of office hours if you need him and responds to emails fast. Genuinely a caring professor.

Dr. South is an awesome professor. He really gets his students and is really nice about everything. Statistics is pretty boring but he tries to make it fun. The material is easy and if you do the homework and practice exams you'll be fine.

The lecture is mostly just him reading off a PowerPoint so you can easily just skip and look at the PowerPoint on Canvas. There are weekly homework assignments that usually require the textbook and the lab is graded on attendance.

Tomar is generous with his time and is v.responsive to email - albeit they sometimes come in at 1-2am. Class participation is key so if you're a little more introverted, be aware that he will call on you and ask you to contribute. If you want to keep up in class, make sure you watch the pre-course videos, do the fill-in notes, and ask questions!

Sorabh is a great guy who really cares about his students. He is very responsive and always around to help if needed. The subject he teaches is difficult but he does a good job explaining it as simply as he could.

Professor Tomar is fantastic. This class is not easy but he does a great job making things clear. He gives great feedback through email and in person and always has time for students. The homework can take a long time and the exams are difficult, but as long as you understand the homework and practice exams you should be fine.

Tomar is the Man! Highly recommend

Professor Tomar works very hard and wants his students to succeed. The tests can be hard because of timing but he curves them and there is extra credit at the end of the semester. My favorite professor at SMU so far. If you get the chance to take him, do!!

reviews.comment: Tomar is a newer prof and really refreshing. He's the reason im majoring in acct tbh. I wish he taught more acct classes bc his energy isn't intimidating, but still respectable. The hw is essential for understanding the material, and this homie will help you if you show interest. He's been my favorite business prof so far (it's still acct tho lol)

Tomar is a great professor. He makes accounting lectures enjoyable because he is funny, engaging, and charismatic. He cares about his students and is accessible and understanding outside of class. Accounting is never going to be the easiest class and an easy A but very doable 100% would recommend Tomar. HW is great review for exams
Professor Tomar is always helpful and explains thoroughly. Hes made learning fun with his natural charisma. Nice and warm guy, definitely misses him.

Hes not a bad teacher at all. Very nice guy and he explains the material well. I loved tomar! Tomar is a great professor and sincerely wants his students to succeed. An A is not extremely easy, but if you do the test reviews before and pay attention in class you'll be fine. Great teacher. SOOOOO Underrated

What I love from a class! You go to lecture and listen and take test great! Every lecture is great because he works everyday in the business he teaches. So he can relate real world applications to the class which really helps. Highly recommend him!

Not good looking. HE is a nice teacher and willing to help but if you don't want to spend 20 hours on each program weekly I suggest don't take the class. Computer science is hard no matter who teaches it.
great professor. very precise and clear. good looking. helpful.

reviews.comment: Spiegelman's the kind of professor you go to college for. Simple as that. I'd also note that his course is as close to a "writing class" as I've found at SMU. He expects us to write one-paragraph responses to the day's material, which he then marks all over and returns the following class. A semester with him will make you a much better writer.

His Romantic poetry class was the best English class I ever took at SMU. This man is a genius, but not such a genius that he's detached from his students. He has a gift for memorizing the texts he's teaching, and sees the world in a unique way. He's also like a father to his students, and is very accessible outside of class. 1010 would take again!

Dr. Spiegelman is one of the gems of SMU's English Department. A more erudite gentleman would be hard to find. He can be a little intimidating at timeshis force of personality can take some getting used tobut he's never unfair or harsh and his usual charm makes up for it.  Take him at least once. If for no other reason, then for the experience.
One of the best classes I took at SMU. Professor is engaging and fun and the subject is very cool. Be prepared to write a lot, though.
Had her form DISC 1313: Film Noir. Really helpful when you have questions about the writing or the readings, really nice lady! Decent amount of reading, not too much homework though.

Not a bad teacher but a fairly bad class. 1313 is all specific classes that have marginal relevance at best. I wasn't really interested ever in the year.  Its an english class that is all about film. Not bad movies, Batman, Fight Club, etc.  A good amount of homework and tough essay grading.
I took her film noir class over the summer. She's a really nice lady. I would definitely recommend.
She will tell you your paper is great in the conference meeting, but still give you a low B. She marks you absent when you have a certain number of tardies, and the class gets very boring.

Professor Park is very helpful and I learned a lot in her class. She is so nice, and I loved having her. Make sure you do the homework...it is super easy and cushions your grade. Also, go to the conferences, they are VERY helpful in you getting an A paper.
She is amazing, she will help you with all of your papers and she makes the class so interesting.  Take her for sure.

Very good teacher.  There is no textbook, but the books she chose to use were extremely engaging.  The rater interest means interest before the class started.  Now my interest in the stuff is through the roof.
Very good teacher.  There is no textbook, but the books she chose to use were extremely engaging.
So sweet. You will definitely get an A if you put in work.

There are quizzes every week but she provides homework and practice quizzes to help prepare. Her class is tough but structured very well and she has great lecture. You have to work for your grade but it is a very good class where you will learn a lot. Very good and nice professor.

Dr. Riffe is a great proffesor and explains topics very well. The class has a lot of reading so make sure you plan your week and complete the assignments before class. She is available outside of class during her normal office hours, but you can email her to schedule a different time. I would take her again.

You will be expected to watch hours of videos to prepare for each class and then she will present her lectures in a monotone fashion while randomly calling on students to answer questions throughout class. Her emails are often condescending and she treats graduate MBA students as if they are first year undergrads.

I found that the class wasn't overwhelming and was well-structured. She sets clear expectations and there are no surprises on her exams. She calls on students but it's not a big deal if you don't answer it correctly. Overall, her class was very organized and the workload wasn't bad.
