Her. Study. Materials. They help!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: has a cocky sense of humor. having said that, i think she is one of the most overrated professors ever. take someone else for intro for bio. she can be very sassy at times. very arrogant when it comes to her research on embroy
Boring. Her lectures were very boring but occasionally she would say something funny. Nice enough lady but her lectures were so boring and dry and did not make bio 1 fun at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class can be hard to get through, but she goes over all of the material thoroughly.

I don't have a lot of sympathy for people who complain about her. Her class isn't hard. She's super nice outside of class and gives good lectures. She knows the material inside and out and you'll learn something in every lecture. She has clear expectations, just don't be an idiot, study a little, and you'll be fine. 5/5
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Strecker is a pretty good teacher. Biology is hard so the class does requires outside work. If you follow the instruction in the syllabus on how to get an A you'll have no problem. Attendance 5%, Online open book quizzes 10%, 4 multiple choice exams 15% each lowest dropped, Final Exam 40%. Utilize office hours and you can email questions too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy and takes attendance. As long as you take notes, review material, and pay attention in class you should easily make a B or A. She lets you drop one test and is really helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She literally gives you test questions during her lectures. Shes a little boring to listen to but sometimes shes funny, and its not hard to get an A if you try. Also her son is in med school and she knows most of her students are pre-med, so she does a lot to help provide pre-med resources for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is extremely rude and condescending to students. The worst part about this class is the weight of the final. I went into the final with an A and came out with a B+. The average for the final was a 70 and there was no curve.

solid professor. knows the stuff and really passionate. DO NOT SKIP CLASS!!!! - YOU WILL NOT PASS!!! quizzes are literally a joke if you just listen and pay attention. not hard to make an A if you just put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You must attend this class - do NOT have your friends sign attendance for you; just show up (she has photographic memory or something seriously she will know). Take notes, do the reviews, & do the practice tests. Don't try to cheat either - she isn't dumb, she has a PhD and she will notice. It's a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Strecker is one of the best professors in the biology department. I had her for intro bio, so was glad to take her again for developmental bio. Definitely a difficult class, but her powerpoints and study questions give you everything you need to know. You can earn up to 6 extra credit percentage points added to your final grade.

Good teacher with a structured organized class. Tests are straightforward but still have some pretty specific questions. The final is hard enough to bring your grade down though. She's not that nice when approached though.

The tests are just like the quizzes and the previous year's tests, if you can get ahold of some older tests from a student who has taken her class before then you should be set for the tests. For the final she wrote new and very specific questions, so it can make or break your grade. Personally, the final dropped my grade from an A to a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She's very straight-forward in lecture, as she has very easy to follow power-points. However, lecture is mandatory as she takes attendance and this factors into your final grade. She is very anti-extra credit though, so beware if you ask for it! Overall, if you study the material, you'll do well since all exams are multiple choice, online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In general, she's pretty rude to students. Tests can be tough and the final is 40% of your final grade. If you don't study, you won't do well.

Professor Strecker was a good professor to me and I took her my first semester of college. Her lectures are a bit boring because they are all the same, but she is very straightforward about what she expects from you and tests are directly from powerpoint, textbooks, and quizzes. You have to study a lot, but if you put the work in you'll get the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great choice for intro bio. Just show up to lectures and take advantage of the study guides that she gives you in order to get an A.
I love her! Really goofy and nice. Gave the whole class an extra 3% to our grades and drops one test. She really notices attendance.

Attendance is mandatory and Dr. Strecker will call you out if she sees you on your phone or talking. She's more than willing to help you, especially if you go into her office hours. The second test took a lot of people by surprise in a bad way; it is possible to do fairly well just by studying the powerpoints, but the textbook definitely helps.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Strecker's lectures are reading off power points that can all be found online, but she takes attendance so you still have to show up to class. Don't talk in class and always show up and you won't have any problems. I never even opened the book, just learned straight off the power points. Study hard a day before each test and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't bother purchasing the textbook. I never even opened it because her powerpoints and study questions cover all of the material that you need to know for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is nearly all memorization of the material presented during the lecture. While attendance is mandatory (she checks every day), she gives test questions during the lecture at random to reward those who come regularly. Dr. Strecker is enthusiastic about the subject she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are easy to understand and tests are very straight forward. If you attend class and pay attention, you shouldn't have to study too much before the test, especially since you can drop one.

Dr. Strecker gives very clear and concise lectures. Do the study questions, go over old exams, and actually pay attention in class. There are people doing rly poorly but that's because they sleep in class or just don't go. Don't cram, start reviewing notes about 1-2 weeks in advance for the tests later in the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really not too hard of a class. Attendance is mandatory and she checks nearly everyday, but she also throws in a few test questions during lectures, so it's beneficial to come. Material really comes straight from the slides. Thoroughly answer the study questions she makes for each chapter and you'll do fine.
Honestly, if you're studious, this is an easy class. Study the lecture slides. Memorize everything. If you do that (which should only take 3 or 4 hrs) before each exam, you'll make an easy A.

She is such a pleasant professor to have. Her enthusiasm radiates and she is just too cute. I love her and her lectures are extremely helpful. I did not even end up using the textbook I bought. Her overhead slides and notes are so helpful and is a great summary of her lectures. She is a must take. Study and you will do well.

She is one of the best teachers I ever had. She helps you in every way possible. She give us test questions during lectures and old exams keys that help you to pass her exams. Exams are extremely hard. No textbook needed, lectures are enough.
The class is tough since there's a lot of information to learn, but the study questions that Dr. Strecker provides are useful when for tests.
Really enjoyed Dr. Strecker's class.  She is lenient with attendance and she posts lectures online.  Class was  overall enjoyable.

She really cares about her students and has lots of office hours for you to ask questions. Strecker answers all questions clearly and thoroughly even if they are stupid questions. She treats everyone really well and occasionally throws in some jokes.

Dr. Strecker is the sweetest!! Fair grader and sets appropriate expectations for class; very kind lady who loves biology and makes class fun and fair (i.e. won't make students stay after just bc an experiment runs long); class isn't too hard especially if you have research experience. She's a MUST-HAVE professor!! Can't recommend her enough!

Molecular Genetics lab is a really good class. Dr. Strecker is a great teacher - really knows her stuff (she coauthored our lab manual) and is very easy to understand. All in all an easy A if you try. I would not recommend skipping class or tardiness because she takes points off. Just show up for class, do your work and you'll do well.

She's super sweet and loves biology. She records her lectures but takes attendance so skip wisely. During lecture she will show a few test questions that will be on the midterm so pay attention! She also gives study questions for every chapter. Do them. All in all the class isn't too bad!

I took Professor Strecker for introductory biology first semester of freshman year. The class structure is entirely lecture-based. She uses Powerpoints and overhead notes to lecture (she posts these online so you have access to them before class). Tests are incredibly difficult, studied at least a week before tests and still couldn't make an A.

Dr. Strecker knows her stuff, and it occasionally seems as if she is going too quickly in class. However she has a large amount of office hours (8+ hours per week) and her grading criteria is relatively relaxed. Attendance is not "mandatory" but keep in mind she takes off points for "professional conduct" (talking during class, no shows, etc).

I really enjoyed this class! The material is interesting, and you only have to write a short paper each week. The reading is alright, most of them are interesting. I recommend this as a CF (with human diversity credit)!
She is so scatter, and can get snippy if you ask questions.

Dr. Strecker is very nice and has a funny wit about her, however the person who left the comment about her making the Developmental Bio class harder was right. While I really like Dr. Strecker, I almost feel like she went out of her way to present the material in a less than straight forward manner. It was also a pretty dry class, but informative.
Take her class! She is very nice and will help you understand biology. Take her class

Strecker is incredibly easy and such a sweet lady. There is an attendance sheet you have to sign in on and she makes a point of making you sit in the same spot so she will see if you're missing. I took two years of bio prior to taking this class, and I found it extremely easy. There are only two midterms and a final though so make sure you study.

Easy A if you read the book, go to class, and study. Tests are identical to the in-class quizzes and extra credit assignments are available. If you're struggling, Dr. Strecker is easily approachable and loves meeting with students during office hours.

Extremely helpful teacher. Professor Strecker is also very nice and laid back. You can get an A in her lecture class or molecular genetics lab by paying attention to what she says and visiting her office hours

I took Dr. Strecker for Developmental Biology. She is a very nice lady and I really do like her.  That class, though was something else. Most boring class I have ever taken in my life. Also as a warning, she told us that she is making her class harder because kids in the past took advantage of her being too easy and straightforward. BE AWARE.
Dr. Strecker is amazing. I was unsure about the class because it is reading and writing intensive but she makes it manageable. She grades fairly and gives out plenty of extra credit. Love her!
Easy. A but not a good teacher   Can't take criticism well either apparently.
best teacher I have taken throughout my time at SMU. Super passionate and easy to work with

Prof Tirado was extremely kind and made everyone comfortable speaking French. He does call on you in class but it is very relaxed and he is always encouraging even if you make mistakes. He's so sweet, he makes jokes, greets everyone, available for questions, and makes it easy to understand the concepts. I would love to take him again.
Objectively a terrible professor.

I really enjoyed FREN 2302 because of Prof. Tirado and his energy. He's laidback, funny, caring, dedicated to seeing his students succeed, and always able to put a smile on people's faces. The course is heavy on grammar and history, so be ready for cold calling and essays. But, he's a great, lenient teacher who'll help you every step of the way.

Mr. Tirado is a good professor! He's very easygoing and gives a fair amount of work. He is also very encouraging when it comes to presentations and mostly wants to help you and make sure you understand rather than nitpick every mistake you might make.

I had to take this class for my second language credit but ended up having a good time in this class. He made me less nervous about speaking in French and helped me during office hours a lot. He is such a sweet professor and I would definitely take him again.

I love Prof. Tirado! He made me feel less nervous about speaking/participating in class, and I'm so glad that I took him for this course. He made it very clear in the beginning that he doesn't want people to feel judged when participating, and I encourage everyone to take him if possible.

Professor Tirado is one of my favorite teachers I've had so far. There is a fair amount of work, but he's a nice grader and extremely encouraging. You never have to worry about messing up speaking in class because he will only help you. I hope to take more classes with him in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tirado is a caring teacher who helped me learn positively. I enjoyed coming to class and learning from him. French is a heavy workload, but he makes it as smooth as possible.

Liked the class, it wasn't super hard. Only annoying thing was how much homework we got each week. We would watch a movie and have like 4 essay assignments on them. Easy to get through, just a lot of busywork. Overall, he's a super cool and funny guy though, and tries to get kids engaged and laughing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The tests can be hard sometimes, but the homework and everything else is really easy. Just participate in class, write down the important things he says, and practice a few minutes everyday and you will get at least a B+. He will try and convince you to get a French minor
Best french professor ever!!!
One of my all-time favorite professors at SMU. Knows his stuff, very accomodating, loves his students. Would take his class again in a heartbeat
I'd never had a French teacher like Tirado-- he's so forgiving, and yet also actually teaches you the language. I've learned so much.

I've had Tirado for 3 semesters now and I'm so sad that I won't be having him next semester. Tirado genuinely cares about his students, giving extensions when asked. He's a pretty easy grader. Usually there are weekly homeworks, a few essays, and several quizzes. Tirado is such a bubbly gem and one of the sweetest professors I have had.

Professor Tirado was one of my professors in France while studying French abroad.  He is SUCH a good teacher.  He empowers you with the tools you need to master French.  He is an amazing professor that truly cares about his students.  Plus, you will never be bored-so funny.
I really liked Tirado. He is a funny guy who usually gives his students the benefit of the doubt on tests, so he is a fairly easy grader. I didn't enjoy taking French, but he made it not so bad

do whatever it takes to have tirado as your teacher! he is so nice and fun. he's even convinced me to minor in French. classwork is easy and he is always open to answer questions. occasionally gives tips about tests and quizzes. expects exceptional in class essays. final was easy and take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tirado is great! 80 minute French classes are very rough, though. He is a good teacher!
He was the best professor for lab and he made the subject material easy to understand. Will definitely be taking him again

You're going to want Tirado as a French teacher at some point in college. He is hilarious and very sweet (he sometimes also likes to get sassy, at least with me). Class is very easy and he's an extremely generous grader. You will actually look forward to going to his class.

Tirado is one of the best French teachers I have had in my years of French. His grading scale is relaxed and he genuinely cares about the material. He has a good sense of humor and is a good teacher for an otherwise hard class.

The online homework is terrible. But Professor Tirado is genuinely the best. This class is a breeze. He juices down the whole lesson to about 2 mins, which is ample to understand everything there is to understand in every module. Listen to him for 2 minsclass and you'll make an A+. Honestly, this class is so easy, you'll have to try hard to fail.
Nice guy, fair grading. Pretty boring teacher, but could be worse.

Prof. Tirado is the best! He has a good sense of humor during class which makes it less boring. He tries to engage and help everyone during class. Grading for assignments was really easy and it is easy to earn a good grade with him. Definitely take him if you can, best french professor!
Absolutely love him! Professor Tirado is extremely helpful and forgiving when you're having difficulty. He's also hilarious. I hope I'm able to take him again someday!
I love him! He's super sweet and understanding and teaches French really well! He's also really entertaining. Take this class! I hope I get him again.

Monsieur Tirado is one of the best teachers that I've had. He is hilarious and such a good teacher. His class is so easy and even if you struggle, he will help you through it. Truly enjoyable class...I hope I get to have him as a professor again.
Cutest teacher ever! He is so nice and if you were placed into this class with the online exam it will be so easy. Never had to do homework because we talk about it in class. So easy!! Take him.
literally the sweetest guy, he helped me so much when I wasn't doing well. He really wants you to understand French. He is very funny and makes class entertaining. I hope to have him again
Definitely one of the most helpful French teachers there are. He's from Marseille, and teaches the subject extremely well.
This class is insanely boring and will put you to sleep. The one good thing is that he canceled class a l

Great teacher, you can really tell he's passionate about philosophy. However, as someone who types notes, there are absolutely no phones or laptops allowed in class which makes his lectures (which are very long and repetitive) more difficult to follow. Also takes a very long time to grade any tests.
Very nice guy
Nice guy but lectures are a bit sporadic. Takes long to grade assignments and rarely responds to emails.

Professor may be knowledgeable but he is incapable of teaching it. Spends so much time on the simple things and run out time or super rushed going over things that are complex and technical. avoid at all costs

Grading on tests is kinda harsh, but adds a curve. Lectures were boring, and most of class was him over explaining the same concepts repeatedly. Long readings assigned after every class, but I didn't do most of the readings and did good on tests using summaries, his ppts, and the study guide. You get 4 absences. Overall nice professor and easy A!

I enjoyed this professor, he was necessarily easy and you didn't have to go to his classes, but he is nice and cares about what he does so I would say to attend some of them. Quizzes are mostly online besides the last few and the lowest quiz grade is dropped. The hardest part I would say is the final paper he gave, he let us choose the topic though

His lectures are scattered and free flow which can make it difficult to follow along but he provides PowerPoints which are helpful for studying along with the readings for exams. Overall an interesting and enjoyable professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brad Tompson has very boring lectures that are hard to pay attention to. He then has canvas quizzes that we are given 7 minutes to complete it. When it comes to the test, he is a extremely hard grader so its almost impossible to receive an A, he always curves the tests because the entire class always fails no matter how much you study

Long and loosely structured lectures made it easy for me to trail off into thought but it was nice bc every class felt more like an open discussion. Overall, I found the class very interesting. Also a lot of reading and only a few papers/assignments.

Horribly boring class. I could barely sit through the lectures without falling asleep, but Professor Thompson is genuinely a nice guy. He grades a bit harshly but if you do the quizzes, the class is easily manageable. You honestly don't even have to go to class and can get a decent grade. Recommend for CC breadth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Long lectures and tough grader for no reason even when my essay answered all aspects of the prompt. Wish I tool a different teacher. I will never take Philosophy again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thompson is one of the more intellectual philosophy professors at SMU. If you chose philosophy to try and learn more about current topics that our relevant to the near future, he is your guy. Just communicate in class and ask questions right when you get them, and you'll end up with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Super easy class, he's a very chill and nice prof. He doesn't expect a lot, but you actually learn a lot! I literally just took this class because I needed hours, and actually enjoyed it.

He grades based on 3 tests making up 90% of the grade + 1 quiz grade (all the quiz grades you've taken before.) Lectures are dry and boring. He missed more than 4 classes while I took his class and it really made lost. My time spent on this class was prepping for the test bc the reviews are the tests. Class is interesting at first but becomes borin
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a hard class, but oh my god it is boring. Professor Thompson is a nice guy but his lectures consist simply of him talking about philosophy. No powerpoint, and very little writing on the board so it's hard to take notes without falling asleep.

If you can past some very dry lectures, this class is worth it. He really knows his stuff, and responds very clearly and concisely to questions. Reading is very manageable, and expectations for the paper are quite clear. Doesn't push his views onto students at all. Again, the lectures aren't exciting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is interesting, but very difficult to understand if you didn't take the intro course. Philosophy of perception was very challenging to understand all the initial concepts, but he is helpful and if you actually ask him to clarify things, it helps. This is definitely not a class for non-majors.
Boring lectures but he's helpful if you go ask. Easy grader.

The class is just 3 papers. That's it. They were supposed to be in class, but he moved all of ours to take-homes. The lectures can be super boring sometimes, but if you participate they can get marginally better. It's him talking for about an hour and a half and he does not let out early ever. That being said, he's an easy grader.

By far the worst professor I've ever had. Very unclear about his expectations for test questions. Very unorganized and scatterbrained during class so you end up leaving class more confused about the textbook material. Make sure you keep up with the reading because all of his lectures are from the textbook. I would not recommend taking this class.

He's a really cool guy who holds open-ended discussions that sometimes lead somewhere,sometimes dont. There is a reading for every class (they are REALLY short, but can sometimes be hard) he said he was going to give us random quizzes,but he always told us about them. We only had 2 quizzes& 1 short writing assignment and he dropped one. I recommend

Avoid this class. He is very boring, and it often seems as if he doesn't know what he's even saying. If you don't like walking out of a class wondering what you just did for an hour and a half, don't take this class. Class uses a couple books, but you don't need to read them to do well. He assigns a couple papers that require them though. Avoid!

Thomson is a fantastic prof.  He's really smart (really smart), nice, and completely down to Earth.  I don't know why the people below are complaining that Thomson is a liberal.  I'm a conservative, I did fine in Thomson's class, and we had really good discussions in class.  I think some people are just pissed that they're bad students...

takes attendance, boring classes, even worse reading.. extremeley liberal, hates conservatives although to your face he will not admit that, he'll just take it out on your graded papers.. as the first comment suggested take littlejohn, this guys not fun at all and the midterm is ough to study for because he gives little information, fire him smu

Absolutely AWEFUL.. the MOST BORING CLASS AT SMU.. no idea what he's talking about, yet he's a raging communist that seems to think comparing Nixon and Bush to Hitler and Stalin is a wise thought.. he is terrible.. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM, take it with Prof. Littlejohn who's a joker

he has no idea what he is talking about half of the time. if you're a philosophy major don't take this class because it will just make you mad. he tries to be open and have discussions, but ends up not having anything to talk or argue about and no conclusions. so half of the time you're sitting there in silence while he tries to gather his thoughts

Good teacher -- very unbiased and open to everyone's ideas.  He doesn't seem to grade very hard on the papers or the "shorties," which are little short papers he assigns on occasion.  There are no tests or quizzes in this class and he didn't take attendance with our class.  I'd recommend him.
Loves to teach, and brings an openminded zest to the topic of "Contemporary moral problems." A good teacher.

By all means I would recommend not taking this professor. Means well, but the expectation is not explained well. Entire class is based on incredibly hard exams that are impossible to study for because he gives no material to study off of and the few homeworks you can use to practice end up being nothing compared to the questions asked in the exams.

This class is without a doubt the most difficult course I have ever taken. Before finals I am sitting at an A. This course is very difficult but curves make up for bad text grades. The homework is difficult and takes along time. Prof. Salmon himself gives great lectures but the content is difficult. Overall hes a good professor, just a hard course

Game Theory is an extremely challenging class and Professor Salmon is extremely knowledgeable in his field. It will push you and is not an easy A but is very interesting. Go to class and office hours if you need and he is more than willing to help you out and explain things. The grading at the end is semi unclear but he will explain if you ask.

Extremely difficult exams. Be prepared to make ugly grades in this class. I made 50s as an A student. Material tested goes beyond the level that's learned during lectures. Problem sets can be VERY difficult and time consuming. Don't waste your time taking this class, avoid it at all costs unless you want your GPA to drop.

Game Theory is hard. This class was extremely challenging. It helps he curves a lot on tests but you will notice many drop the class after first exam. Professor is funny and entertaining, even adds humor to his test problems.

Dr. Salmon's behavioral course is easy if you pay attention for most of his lectures. The midterm has a pretty hefty curve, and the proposal summary is graded extremely fairly. The grading for the final proposal, however, left me a little confused when I saw my grade. No rubric and little feedback on what exactly he wants. Super nice guy, funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Salmon is a very knowledgeable man who has a lot for you to learn from, however, the structure of his class is an absolute nightmare. His lectures are painfully boring, and his grading is EXTREMELY unclear and objective to his opinion. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid game theory at all costs. Its the most useless class I have ever taken. The material is worded in ways that make no sense. Professor salmon is a nice guy, but he takes pride in making his exams hard. I highly recommend taking a different advanced econ course.

Salmon is a really nice guy who knows a ton about game theory. He's very approachable and it's crucial to go to class and office hours if necessary. This class was tough; for a non-math person this class was difficult and very frustrating. The material is presented in an overly convoluted way. Worth it but only if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING class to take for CC. Such interesting lectures during class. Tests are so easy if you pay attention in class, you dont need to study if you go to class and listen to him. Tim is so sweet and understanding when it comes to having to miss class and fosters an amazing environment where everyone can share their POV. 10/10 class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: SO AWFUL AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! A is impossible, expect almost 3 hours of reading per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brought big “you should already know this” energy while explaining nothing. This class gave mental illness and not the cute kind. No useful rubrics, no mercy, just bad vibes and careless teaching meant to showboat his inflated sense of self worth. Made me question my major.

My favorite class and professor I've taken at SMU. Incredibly engaging and fostered an environment in which we were all extremely comfortable. Hilarious classes while also maintaining full engagement with the material itself. 350 characters is not nearly enough to encapsulate the incredible experience of this class and Dr. Cassedy.
Super rude. Gross behavior.

Don't know why he has an average rating. He's awesome. Super interesting lectures and readings. Lots of them, but it's an English class. As long as you're willing to participate in class, you'll do fine (won't force you though, just gently coax). Very understanding and flexible. Fair grader. Love him! Best class I've ever taken.
Bad attitude too deluge the mister nice guy persona. It brews beneath and changes when you ask questions he deletes things that aren't nice ab him

My favorite professor in all my time at SMU. I took as many of his classes as I could. Comes off as a bit standoffish, but very understanding if you approach him. His classes literally changed my whole way of thinking and writing. I'll forever be thankful to him. 

Don't take if you're looking for an easy A. He is an extremely a tough grader.

Prof Cassedy is my fave English teacher, he's always open to meet & gives great feedback. This class exceeded my expectations. The workload was light: reading assignments, weekly Canvas task (not based on readings), final paper, short presentation. Paper is 15-20 pages but you basically work on it all semester so not too bad. Loved him & this class
If you're taking ENG 3346, do yourself a favor and switch professors. Given that the class average was a C-, this says more about him as a professor than about students' learning abilities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really tough grader. Super rude and it will show through discussions and email. Makes attendance mandatory, but doesn't follow his own guidelines regarding the absence policy. Save yourself the trouble and find a different class/professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tim Cassedy is passionate about the subject material. He is, further, deceptively kind and a bit of an eccentric, but not in a good way.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Yes, professor Cassedy is a harsh grader. I was excited to take this course until three weeks in. That's when I realized there was blatant favoritism and biases shown toward students. He ignores you if you happen to be one of those students, he will belittle you if you're a minute late, and this treatment will also be in emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grades harshly on papers
He is very vague on what he wants in essay papers and you have to read an intensive amount of books. Would not recommend it if you need an LAI requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Cassedy is a hard grader for sure. My last essay which he said was my best was still only a 91. But he gives a lot feedback even if the rubrics are not super clear. The reason I like him a lot even tho I didn't get an A is because discussion is great and he is very nice and approachable I think he wants really well thought out essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Funny, engaging, and intelligent who leads great discussions. With that said, I wouldn't take it unless you're an English major or minor. It is a ton of work, with about an hour of reading or more before each class. He's also a harsh grader and doesn't outline his grading expectations until he hands the essay back.

Professor Cassedy is a nice and funny teacher. However, his grading system is both unfair and ridiculously harsh. I took a junior-level English class at the same time and it was much easier to pass. His grading rubric is vague; the first essay's highest score was a B+ since he said that he would be surprised if we knew what he wanted us to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is just way too much reading in this class. You have to read like 80 pages of a book for one class. The discussion was interesting though. He is a harsh grader too. For the first major essay assignment, the highest grade is 88.5, with an average of 82. I wished I didn't take his class for the UC requirement.

Attendance is mandatory and his tests are impossible. Tests consist of 6 small paragraphs from the many readings; you give the title, author, and explain what the reading was about -in detail. He gives 6 and you answer 5 of them. His essay instructions are ambiguous and he says you will understand after the graded paper with comments are in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cassedy is one of the best professors I've had at SMU. He is passionate and hilarious. I actually enjoy going to his class. He cares about his students and what he is teaching and it shows. His lectures are interesting and go above and beyond that of an average teacher. If you have the chance to take one of his classes do it.

His class has been my favorite non-creative writing English course so far! He's incredibly passionate about what he's teaching and it shows. I never thought I would find books about book making interesting, but here we are. Class discussions were always fun and free-flowing; I never felt like I was just waiting for the class to be over. 10/10

Professor Cassedy was definitely one of my favorite professors at SMU. He leads incredible discussions. Hes hilarious, smart, and spends a lot of time giving detailed feedback. Ask him about his games Bards Dispense Profanity. Dont take as a blow off class, because he expects you to always be prepared.
Coolest professor ever! I need to say no more!

Professor Cassedy is one of the most driven people I have ever met. He is insanely dedicated to and passionate about what he does. I have taken a few of his classes and they are always engaging and never boring. His 3000 level class was not too demanding, but he really makes you step up to the plate in his 4000 level class.

Do reading in order to be able to write a strong paper. First paper is20% and second paper is25%  Please attend classes and participate because it's 25% of your grade Drops 2quiz grades 3 inexcused absences (then each will cost u points) Give extra credit throughout the semester (one towards midterm and others towards quizze)  strongly recommended!

Funny! Make class very interesting! Discussions in class are very important and WILL help you with exams, so take notes! Participate in class, say what's on your mind, don't be shy, and get good participation points. There's no right or wrong. Average of 35-40 pages reading per class. Give pop quizzes (10%) exams are easy if u read and attend class

I would definitely recommend taking Cassedy's classes.  He has a great sense of humor, and he makes the readings interesting.  Also, he's adorable.  However, I was never to get an A on any of his papers.

Best professor at SMU, hands down. Not an English major and I enjoyed this class more than any other course at SMU. Encourages students to think outside of the box and discuss. Never taken anything like it. He is the man.

GREAT teacher! Very helpful inside and outside of class. Obviously brilliant and passionate about what he teaches. My competency in writing improved vastly under his direction. If I were an English major I would take another class of his in a heart beat!
For his very first year of teaching he did well. Not too sensitive to what he says to students and he didn't really prepare for finals, but he's interesting.

I highly recommend taking any course taught by Professor Cassedy. He assigns interesting books,and leads really involved class discussions. He's very enthusiastic about english, and is very helpful in office hours.

She is really sweet and funny in class, and makes knowing ASL a breeze. You never even have to study outside of class if you just participate and have fun with ASL. Outside of class, she is really tough on grading and attendance. No late work or makeup work is allowed, which can be rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor McCray is not the best professor. She is a harsh grader, and you must submit things timely. She will not have grace if you forget to do something, so make sure you stay on top of your work. She seems to hate her job. I just wished McCray had taken more interest in helping her students succeed than in wanting them to fail.
Not a terrible professor, I've had worse. Very strict late policy, won't let you submit anything late. Attend class and do the homework, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly, I don't think she was as terrible as most of the reviews say. She's pretty nice but there are some minor annoyances with the class. She will take off a couple of points on assignments (not very many, 2 or 3) but doesn't tell you why. She doesn't respond to emails and there are several (anywhere from 6 to 12) homework assignments weekly.

Professor McCray cares a lot about her students. She tells you how it is the first week of school and if you don't go by her rules then that is on you. You must come to all classes and there is no late work. She is always extremely helpful during office hours if you have any questions! During class she is inclusive and you do learn a lot of ASL.

Professor McCray is a teacher who wants you to learn. She makes it fun and a class you look forward to going to. I have loved getting to learn so much ASL in a fun and active way rather than just listening to someone teach and lecture. As long as you give her the same respect she gives you, this class will become one of your favorites in college!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Never responds to emails. At least 6 homework assignments a week. A book report, unit 5 test, final exam, and presentation all within the last week of school. McCray is a nice teacher but it's as if she's teaching a HS class. She is an extremely harsh grader and you will never make a 100 on an assignment.
Do not take class! Awful professor and class
Does not care about students at all!!! Literally take anything else.

Professor McCray is a nice person, but she is pretty strict and gives a ton of assignments. Every couple weeks there is a test AND a pop quiz, and there were 3 different "final exam" assignments. I would only take her classes if you really want to learn ASL and are willing to work hard.

She as a person seems pretty cool but as a teacher, its like she is teaching a high school class - strict. The class isn't hard, she just doesn't provide resources outside of class to help you "study" for exams/quizzes. There is an exam every other week and pop-up quizzes. She is strict with grading, late assignments, etc. Take only if you have to.

She's a great professor who wants you to learn ASL. I think many students that this class because in the past it was an easy A, not anymore. ASL is a beautiful language and should get the respect as the other languages, therefore you will need to study, do the homework, participate in class and ask questions if you are confused. Just ask for help.

She's a reallu tough grader. She will count points off for any little mistake. She's alright but very "try hard" teacher. So many assignments and exams (exams are every 2/3 weeks). Attendance is mandatory and she will not help you make up the material you missed even if it is excused.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader and will take points off for minor things. I don't hate her, she really tried to make the class interesting (and it was) but if you miss class, you miss so much content that she won't really help you catch up to. She is really strict on late policy as in you get a zero. She's nice and tries but also just very though in the end
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have came across. Unfair grading scale, late to respond to emails, extremely vague assignment descriptions. Do not take her class.

DO NOT TAKE!! Prof. McCray is a nightmare. She sprung tests and hw on us VERY last minute with no warning and never provided rubrics for major assignments, so you were always unsure what you actually missed points on. She either didn't answer emails or replied extremely late. If you need ASL for a language credit, take a different prof or language.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking this professor's course. He is awesome! Shows respect for students and provides straightforward instructions. Dedicate time and you'll find a successful outcome.

A really great professor. He cares for his students and is very reasonable. He wants you to succeed, so put in the work, show you care and you will be just fine. Everything is straight up, there is no confusion on how the class will go. You can complete the homework super easy with the helpful notes that he provides. 1000% recommend!!!

He is a great professor. If you read the notes and the slides posted by him, you can complete the homework easily. He gave the students an option to retake one of the tests as the grades were low for most students. He is very prompt in replying your emails. He also allowed to use the notes in the finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class for the math requirement breadth and am not a math person at all. While he is a nice guy, he is NOT a good teacher when it comes to explaining content. I had to pay for a private tutor outside of class just to be sure to pass. I failed every test except final. If you're a math person - it will be no problem. If not - good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Jacobbe is a super nice guy. His class is hard, but so are all the stat's classes. He loves when you go to office hours and may even bump your grade up for it. He isn't the best teacher but he does want his students to succeed so he is very lenient. 3 tests throughout the semester and one final. I recommend him!

Tim is great. Ignore the other reviews. If you actually pay attention, then you will understand the material. The homework is designed to be challenging and you actually learn a lot by using your resources and figuring it out on your own. This class is an easy A if you complete the assignments bc he is an easy grader.
Tim is very passionate about his class. If you don't go to class or pay attention you won't leaning anything though. Wants everyone to do well.

Tim enjoys lecturing us during his class. And we truly enjoy our time watching a Thursday Night Football Game. As far as I know, people don't do his class for credit nor knowledge, they do his class for inner peace and anger management. P.S You will be struggling doing his homework. I promise.

Professor McDonough is probably one of the worst professors I've had at SMU. His lecture is tedious. AND we have to stay the entire 3.5 hours. His homework is NOTHING related to his class. As I am currently doing his data mining homework, I feel nothing but being violated.

Tim is probably the worst professor ever. He rambles for hours and teaches content that is totally irrelevant to the homework. All the quizzes can be found online and the answers are given most of the time. I was sitting at the last row in the classroom and saw four different guys have 4 football live streames on their laptops
Doesn't teach anything, and not willing to help.

His class is a disaster. Avoid at all cost. Classes are boring, hard to follow, homework never matches what he teaches in class. Don't waste your time and your money here in his class.

The lectures were read verbatim from the presentation downloaded from the publishers website.  No final exam so instead of paying attention in class most students cruised the web or texted the entire time.
No deviation from the book.  Lectures were simply reciting what was in the text but if you read the book the tests are straight forward.
Not worth showing up to class - had to teach myself using text book. He is not willing to help or answer questions, either, even after numerous attempts.
Worst lecturer I've seen. Makes everything confusing. I aced all the exams, but not the hw and the dude just penalized me for that. Don't understand anything he's saying.

Very nice guy and brings a smile every day. Class is easy, he usually does 3 examples in class with you and they are from the text book. Tests are basically the homework problems and he will tell you how many problems there are on the test and then does very similar examples before. Curves the tests as well.
A really bad lecturer but he curves alot
The professor is nice, I had some fun taking the course

What most people have been saying, I agree with; he is nice, but hard to understand. Statics is an easy class as long as you do the homework and actually go to class. You do NOT need the textbook. I wasted money renting it and it just sat, unopened all semester.

I would say it is absolutely pointless to go to class however there is an attendance check everyday.  This guy is absolutely impossible to understand so expect to teach yourself this entire class. He talks directly from the slides and never does examples. Homework is long and very time consuming. Take a different teacher for sure.

The class is completely useless. Understanding and following him is very difficult. Because of this nobody pays attention at all, yet everyone still goes to class because there is an attendance check everyday

Prof Tong is a really nice guy, but he is very hard to understand. He becomes more incomprehensible as the semester goes on. Fortunately, Statics is a very easy class. Do the homework, using your textbook, and come to him for personal help. You should be fine. He grades very generously. Not looking forward to Materials with him though :(

There is no understanding him. I know now as much about Materials as I did going into the class. You want to root for him, but there is nothing. What really makes me mad about materials is that it is more or less the only reason Gen Chem 1 is pre requisite for ME's.

Absolutely unintelligible. He gets a few good ratings because he is slightly endearing and you want to like him, but to no avail. This will be a self taught class that is a pretty easy B at worst, when in doubt write stuff down and you will be fine. If you care about learning more than just the grade, take deform with someone else.

I also took Prof. Tong for Deform. He knows his material very well. Lectures are IMPORTANT, but you need to have studied the material before the lecture or else the lecture becomes useless. Sit in front seat. Tests are HARD! But just write the correct equations and do SOME working, and you will hopefully get high grade. Highly recommended! :)

Prof. Tong is a nice person. His lectures are nice, but you DONOT need to listen to them to get a decent grade on exams. A whole lot of people had past exams of this prof. because of which they made high grades I think. His tests are CRAZY but he is a very easy grader. He has accent but is very understandable. I made a B bcuz I didn't had pastexams

Easy grader, Very helpful and nice. Eventhough its hard to understand what he is saying, you can catch some things if you can stay awake in his class. Do the homework problems over and over again and your good to go.

I loved Dr. Tong; he wasn't the best teacher but there is just something that makes you smile about this guy. Its not hard to get an A in the class, although you feel like you are failing. He only does the example problems in the book, but is willing to explain any questions students have. He curves tests and throws outs your lowest homework grade.

The only good thing I can say is that he is an easy grader.  He teaches straight from his slides without variation but is difficult to understand through a thick accent.  No example problems were worked in class.  All homework was from the book, which had poor explanations and very few examples.

He is very difficult to understand and does not explain the material well. Never works examples. Homeworks are time consuming. Not worth showing up to class - had to teach myself using text book. Worst. Professor. At. SMU. Do not be fooled.

Super awesome professor. took her for writer 1312 and every essay you can submit 2 class periods before for feedback that basically gives you an A. Just showing up to class matters. A total waste of class of time and money and she can't tech worth shute

One of my favorite professors at SMU. Pretty easy class with 3 papers; you can submit a rough draft to her beforehand and receive feedback before the final submission. Rarely any homework, and many class discussions on fun topics like pop culture, music, and movies.

reviews.comment: Loved taking her for this class. Taking WTRT 1313 next semester with her as well. No HW, 3 essays in the whole semester, and she has workshop days during class to work on them and also independent study days were class is cancelled. Has a fun personality and has discussions and debates about music, sports, and everything you can think of. 10/10 fun
Participate in discussions and turn work in on time you'll be good.
Woke professor who grades you based on how work you are.

Professor Carey is one of the best. She truly cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Don't know how she has a job here. Incom

worst professor at this school by a long shot, does not help us learn and has an attitude and is sarcastic with students specifically those of us who are nonmajors, the course is so unorganized, do not take unless you want your gpa to take a hit from a course nobody cares about,..

There are three essays a semester, each taking around a month to complete. She also allows you to send her a completed first draft, and you will most likely get an A if you change what she says. reviews.comment: Very clear instructions and assignments/ projects given have a proper timeline/ due date. Very good, kind, caring person overall. Enjoyed going to her class.

This professor is hands down the worst I've ever had. Instead of teaching, she rambles about her opinions, grades unpredictably, claims expertise in writing despite evident flaws, and responds defensively to any criticism.

Had her both semesters. If you send her a draft of your essay, you will more then likely make an A. The people who waited last minute and didn't send a draft before submitting the final are the ones complaining on here. Only graded on 4 essays. lectures don't stay on track, and she's terrible at answering questions. She created a hostile environment, and I often felt belittled. Would not recommend his class - seek other options.

She was great for WRTR 1313! She can be a tough grader at times but if you put in the work you will be fine. Barley any homework which was nice. Just make sure you talk in class because participation does matter.

I've had some terrible professors, but this one takes the cake. Instead of teaching, she goes off on tangents about her opinions, grades inconsistently, supposedly teaches writing despite lacking skills in it, and becomes incredibly defensive when criticized.

The professor I'm referring to is undoubtedly the worst I've ever had. Rather than teaching, she rambles on about her opinions, grades haphazardly, claims to teach writing despite evident deficiencies in her own, and reacts defensively to any critique.

Among all the professors I've had, this one stands out as the absolute worst. This professor ranks as the worst I've encountered, constantly veering off into personal opinions instead of focusing on teaching, assigning grades arbitrarily, lacking basic writing skills despite purported expertise in the subject (her examples are available on this page), and reacting defensively to any form of criticism.

WRTR 1313 was a journey for me. I didn't know what to expect but I left a better writer and feel like I have a better understanding of what it takes to write in college. I could not have asked for a better teacher.
There are four papers but no final. She takes roll but you'll pass the class if you do well on the essays.
The class was easy and she lets you send drafts. A lot of class discussions but only four papers.
I took both semesters with her and I would take her again. Professor Carey really cares about her students and worked with me through a hard time. Really glad I took her.

This professor ranks as the worst I've encountered, constantly veering off into personal opinions instead of focusing on teaching, assigning grades arbitrarily, lacking basic writing skills despite purported expertise in the subject (examples are available on this page), and reacting defensively to any form of criticism, a very immature reaction.

Worst professor I have ever had in my life, goes on tangents about her opinions on everything rather than bothers teaching, grades randomly, can't even write yet supposedly teaches it (you can see her samples on this page), and is SUPER defensive to criticism. Hi Triauna!

By far the most treacherous experience of my life with a professor who not only doesn't know how to teach but uses the classroom as her personal stage for any and all opinions she feels compelled to share and share she must. Horrible grading, you have to parrot back her diatribes to be successful.
Easy if you show up and try. Attendance matters. Assignments are super easy. Discussion days aren't bad. Would take again.

What a great semester! Dr. Carey is thoughtful, approachable, and made me like writing for once. Writing is hard for me but this class was super easy. Not a blowoff class. You have to attend but it was totally worth it. Highly recommend if you want to learn something.

Great teacher! I had her for WRTR 1313, and she gives clear guidelines about the essays and lets you send her a draft before it's due. Doesn't take late work, so be on top of the deadlines. Also, she doesn't force you to participate in discussions if you are shy:) Definitely recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's understanding and gives you lots of time to complete essays. You can send her your essay's a day early for feedback and is accessible outside the class. Mostly, class discussions and four essays, plus important discussion posts for the majority of her classes. Participation is important, but she won't randomly call on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Carey is an amazing professor. In class and online discussions are easy, all you have do to is participate and try. Essays are very straightforward and she is always available to help. Take her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Goes off on lots of tangents, overly political. She doesn't have a very defined way of grading and I've seen A papers get 75s and C papers get 92s, so you really never know.

Dr. Carey is an AMAZING teacher. She lets you write about the things that interest you, and she fosters really interesting discussions in class. The grading is also very fair. She always allows you to send her drafts before you submit for a final grade. At the end of the semester, she said she would count a 90 and above as an A.
Literally loved him! Sweetest professor ever and you can really tell he loves doing what he does. Makes lectures fun and engaging! Wish I could do more classes with him.

Professor Stuckey is the best professor I've had at SMU. He's clear, supportive, and makes every topic interesting. He truly cares and gives amazing feedback that helps you grow. He's the kind of teacher who makes you love learning. Truly one of SMU's best, take him!! I feel so lucky to have been able to learn from him so take advantage!!

Dr. Stuckey is an amazing professor. This course had nothing to do with my major but I really learned a lot and enjoyed his class. He is very engaging and if there's not much left to do, he will let you out early. Really easy A and a great professor to know!

He uses a slideshow for his lectures and posts the notes on canvas after. Its alot of material but he does a review day where he tells you whats going to be on the test. There are only 4 labs during the semester and they are all very interesting. Honestly my favorite class I have taken at smu.
Professor Stuckey is so kind and is very passionate about what he teaches. He is a very understanding person and the best professor I have had at SMU so far!
Great professor! Take him as many times as you can!

Dr. Stuckey is awesome, i definitely recommend. Everything for tests is based off the lectures, so dont worry about the textbooks. Tests are pretty straightforward and there are two papers. Overall he is a cool guy and also a pretty easy grader; he always tells you what he's looking for so that there are no suprises

Take professor Stuckey!!! He's very kind and easy to reach for questions outside of class. The class is 100% lecture with PowerPoints. It does get dense, and there's a lot of information to study for tests. BUT there are literally 2 tests, 2 papers, and a final presentation. The class is very straight forward, and you should get an A...

Took in person during COVID, so semester experiment covered mask effectiveness with air samples and having to look at slides and count particles with final paper and presentation (the most tedious part of the class) midterm was pretty straightforward short answer, precis paper on climate change(have to read entire textbook for) LOT OF WORK but good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Stuckey is very knowledgable about env policy and passionate about his job! Some lectures are a little dense especially for a night class but the material is super interesting. He's not very tech savvy so a bit of confusion with assignments and exams but also a pretty easy grader so doesn't matter anyway--you'll probably get an A.

Stuckey's class about air quality is informative, easy, and he is very passionate. The last half of the class makes it one of the best you can find. Lectures finish, and you spend the time collecting and analyzing air samples, writing a short-ish science paper at the end. You learn lots of great real-world skills, making this class uniquely good.
Professor Stuckey is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about environmental policy. Favorite class at SMU so far.

Such a nice man. I didn't have much interest in environmental science, but after I had a class with him I had a change of heart. I decided to take another class with him and I'm glad that I did. Totally relatable and approachable. What a professor should be.

Take this class.  You will love it!  Dr. Stuckey brings considerable experience to his class.  This may be the best class I've ever taken and he is a super nice man.   It's a long class, but his lectures pass the time quickly.  Hard A, easy B if you come to class.

Dr. Stuckey is one of the most caring professors I have met at SMU; he literally puts his cell phone number on the syllabus. Anytime that I had a conflict he was speedy to assist me. Dr. Stuckey is not shy to mention his extensive experience and incorporates his knowledge in lecture. His personal stories make the lecture so much better.
One of my favorite teachers at SMU. Maybe THE nicest man ever. Take his any of his classes and you'll be glad you did! Tests aren't too bad a come right from the powerpoints.

great guy. tests are straight from the lectures and very straight forward. Environmental policy can be a dry subject but he makes it as interesting as can be. Three hours go by fast, lots of tests though

Just a nice guy. The first half of the semester you have to get through a lot of lecture, but the air sampling project over the second half is much more interesting, and he'll help you every step of the way. He seemed boring at first but he knows his stuff and it's really funny to hear him talk about his kids. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Stuckey is one of the coolest professors ever. He loves his job and loves his students even more. He is always there to help you no matter what. The 3 hrs FLY by. He is also very generous with grading if he knows you try hard. For his exams, study the power points and you will get an A. Take this class!

Tests based on lectures 99% of the time. He puts reading assignments on blackboard, but they are usually not on the test. His lectures are 3 hours long, but the information is really interesting. He doesn't give out a lot of A's tho :/
This teacher is very nice and helpful!

This professor is awesome, although the lectures last 3 hours, you will be so enthralled that the time will fly by. He is one of the nicest men I have ever met and is willing to review any information you do not understand with you before or after class.

hes such a chill professor. the tests are lowkey hard but he gives out a sheet w potential questions so if u go thru those and the answers every day, then u will recognize on the test. take him hes so nice and passionate abt sports and loves to yap
Kind of a joke of a course, can't believe he gets paid to do next to nothing, worse teaching i experienced in all my life.

Prof. Troupe is a very knowledgeable person in sports. He does ramble on about himself sometimes but if you're a sports nerd, you'll love him. His quizzes are about current sports events, and his exams are roughly over the material he lectures over. If you know sports well, you shouldn't have to study too much but his grading can be a little odd.

DO NOT TAKE, his class is so boring you will want to sleep. Dont ask any questions if you are confused. He loves to publicly embarrass students, he is extremely rude, and has no filter. His teaching is all over the place and get ready waste your entire 3 hours a week.

Very chill guy, who is very knowledgeable and genuinely wants you to learn things that are useful in the sports industry. Most of the class is lectures that can be long and boring. However, you have plenty of easy grades to get an A- or A.
my favorite professor. cares about the students and he actually teaches you helpful things. I always take him when I can. tests are easy and there is not a lot of hw

Professor Troupe doesn't seem like a nice guy, but deep down he is. He's an easy grader, but he does have pop quizzes every once and awhile. There's a bunch or projects and presentations, but it's not a difficult class. I would take again!

Professor Tran's class is extremely easy to follow with copious amounts of extra credit. His homeworks are short and to the point, while his tests are practically given to you before you even take it. He is very much willing to explain anything that you may have questions on. My only con is that he is difficult to reach outside of class.
You can tell he really cares and wants to make sure everyone understands the material. His lectures are very clear and engaging. Lots of extra credit

Take him if you want an easy A in Diff Eq!! If you participate in class you get extra credit points. His lectures are amazing and make the concepts easy to understand. He goes over exam questions that look just like the exam the class before, making the exams easy if you understand those. Each exam also has an extra credit problem.

reviews.comment: Dr. Tran is an amazing lecturer. He is very clear and is careful to be sure we understand. His homeworks are useful and not too difficult. I won't say that his classes are easy, but he makes it easy to succeed. I will take his courses as often as I am able to, he's amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty clear and he hands out practice tests before the exam that are very similar to exam problems. He encourages participation and gives you extra points every time you answer a question in class. Not super helpful in office hours, but if you're willing to participate in class, it's an easy A.
awful. dont take this class. i was so lost the entire time.

Dr. Tsarevsky is the kindest and most difficult chemistry professor. You have to put in the work to yield the results. He genuinely cares about his students and his availability outside class shows. He frequently held 5+ hours in office hours and delayed his lab time and graduate students for me. 

TIPS: 
Do NOT fall behind.
Attend office hours.

Dr. Tsarevesky is very difficult teacher, but if you really want to learn and understand chemistry, he is amazing. He is super nice and is always available during office hours for further help. Even though its a lot, do all the homework and study the examples from class, it will help a ton for his tests.
If you care about learning, take him. He is the toughest and the best chemistry teacher for gen chem. You will learn so much more than with any other teacher.

Professor Tsarevesky is a very very difficult professor. Tests are extremely difficult even for biology and chemistry majors. If you didn't take AP Chem, this professor is a big no. Test averages are always below 60 (no curve). He is very nice and knows a lot about his subject. He will teach you a lot, but it comes with a prize.

Very nice guy and wants his students to succeed. His exams are VERY difficult and there is a lot of homework. Encourages you to come to office hours and does his best to explain things clearly but this is an extremely difficult class.

Tsarevesky really wants his students to do well and understand his class. He has lots of times he is available outside of class to help you better understand the concepts. His tests are hard, but they get easier as the semester goes on. If you are choosing between him and another professor, take Tsarevesky.

reviews.comment: A caring respectful professor with an enjoyable personality

He has some of the hardest tests because they're unpredictable, but do the homework and ask questions and you'll be fine. He really wants you to do well, and if quite helpful. The homework is a lot, but good to do if you want to do well. Go to class, it's hard to teach yourself unless you've done chem before.

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsarevsky is so hot. Yum. What eye candy

Like pretty much all sections of gen chem, Dr. Nick's course is difficult. Do expect tough tests and plenty of homework. However, he is very willing to help when you have questions. Going to his office hours are extremely helpful especially the lecture-style ones. He really wants to see his students succeed.

BOTTOMLINE: This class is difficult, but if you put in the effort, you will do well. You HAVE to go to class, take notes, do the homework a few days before it's due (you won't be able to do it all the night before), and go to office hours. If you really try to do well and show you care, Mr. Tsarevsky will help you get an A! In the end, B+ A

Dr. Tsarevesky gives the hardest tests and quizzes of the first semester gen chem professors but what he cares about is people trying. There is usually a big curve at the end of the semester because he knows how tough his class is but for those who go to office hours and his review sessions, it is very helpful. Very logical in problem solving

Nick is literally the best. I'm sad that he doesn't teach CHEM 1304. His office hours are ESSENTIAL to understanding the material. Chemistry is a difficult subject, regardless of the professor. He drops a quiz and replaces your lowest test with your quiz homework average! Heavy curves on the tests at the end of the semester. Tough, rewarding class.

I was not in AP Chem, so my chemistry knowledge was limited. The class was ridiculously hard. I would read the book, go to every lecture and take notes, do all the assignments, and study hours every night, and still couldn't do well in his class.  The testsquizzes are confusing and hard-average was around 65%. Office hours were helpful though.

Tough accent to understand but its decent enough.  Impossible quizzes will make you wish you took Professor Z. instead.  Hard material that he flies through and expects way too much from the class.  If you did not take AP chem in high school get ready for a bumpy ride, lots of people dropped.  Semi-helpful but get ready to work
He says he gives the hardest quizzes/tests of all gen chem teachers. Heavy curve (82->B+) on final semester grade. Extra credit for going to office hours.

He makes gen chem very difficult (more so than other profs at SMU). Be prepared to do A LOT of independent studying. His exams and quizzes are pretty hard. All that being said, he is extremely helpful and goes out of his way to ensure you understand the material if you see him in office hours.

The class itself isn't hard, you get a lot of credit. She is just so annoying and will always argue your opinion. You have to give a presentation to the class and she always interrupts and tries to prove you wrong or question you if you really know what you are talking about.

She was honestly a fine teacher but genuinely insane on attendance for some things. She was easy to work with if you were sick and had a note from a doctor but she required attendance before a long weekend even though she skipped, got the class a sub and gave us no extra credit for being there while she wasn't which was bs

Avoid if you can, she is harsh and overwhelming. Seems to favor some students over others based on their ability to understand the language. Took during May Term. easy but she wants you to heavily participate and be engaged. you have to buy all the books that are read during class so you can use them during the in class essay. in class essays, final essay, homework, and presentations are graded based on if you know what your talking about and follow the rubric. 10/10 recommend. easy A.

Pretty easy A class if you participate and do the readings. The one major thing I didn't like about this class was the in-class timed essays we had to write for the "exams". Prof. Williams-Tutt is very nice and willing to work with you when you need help. LOTS of reading and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mme. is the kindest soul and an awesome French prof! The class can be tedious with the all the homework and readings, but she's lenient if you show that you put in effort and is accessible outside of class. Overall, she's very patient and has a genuine dedication to seeing students succeed. Also she has A LOT of energy...make of that what you will.

Took this for a breath credit and absolutely loved this class & professor. If you put forth a little effort an A is definitely attainable. There is a strict attendance policy & short homework assignments before each class but only 2 "tests" and a final which are papers. Discussion based class on a series of books so participation does matter a lil
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Williams-Tutt is amazing. She inspired me to minor in French, and I really enjoyed her class. If you are someone that can stay on top of work, you will be completely fine. You do have to go to class because you only get a few absences, but she's super understanding if you are sick or anything. All around LOVE, LOVE, LOVE !!!!!!!

She is very kind. There is a lot of homework, 4 talk abroads, tests every other week (not too challenging) - but it is very manageable. Make sure to do the homework (you do not have to turn it in but she does cold call when reviewing in class). The only negative is that she is slightly unorganized so follow the calendar from the syllabus

Patient, kind, and understanding! She helps students even when they don't understand a concept the first time. I was hesitant to take her because this was her first year teaching at SMU, but I was quite satisfied with my choice. One thing to be aware of is that FR2401 has a LOT of homework and quizzes, but it's the same for all french profs at SMU

reviews.comment: prof Tujin teaches such a hard class and he knows it. That's why his end of semester rounding is pretty generous especially with a final that can only help your grade. However you will be lost in class A LOT. Be prepared to study a lot for his class but he does offer plenty of office hours

Liked the guy more than I thought I would based on past reviews, don't understand the hate. AI homework was enjoyable. You work problems in class and he gives direct feedback. Tests are long, but the majority of the material is directly from managerial. If you understood that class, you'll be fine here.

reviews.comment: Not the best, not the worst. Positives: Uses AI driven HW, provides lots of study material for exams, final exam is optional. Negatives: exams are difficult, group projects are confusing and he overcomplicates the easiest concepts. This is an inherently difficult class and you will need to put the work in to get a good grade.

The class is very challenging and his method of teaching is not the best. He reads off slides which can be difficult to understand. He is very strict and the exams are very conceptual heavy make sure to study the concepts. I a lot of double negative T and F. Lots of teadius group projects but help the final grade.
He is very kind however the class is very hard. The entire class is slides and the exams are very hard (50% conceptual - extremely hard).

This class wasn't my cup of tea.  I thought he was super nice but it just didn't click much for me. Group projects were not fun because the case studies I thought were difficult for little guidance. I also thought the homework did not help at all. Very different than in class so don't rely on that. Best bet is to study the practice exam material.

The way he explains problems is also very confusing. He encourages students to use chat GPT as a “tutor” to help understand problems but half of the time it's wrong.

Tests arent impossible if you use the extra help that he posts
Final Exam is optional
Homeworks easy if you use multiple tries

Cons:
He isn't the best teacher
For more complicated topics you are on your own
Cases can be really hard if you dont have a good group
Before class quizzes are brutal since he makes you read entire chapters for them
