reviews.comment: He was not as bad as the other reviews say. Sometimes, the way he explained things did not make sense. However the extra guidance practice problems he gave out before the tests were extremely helpful for reviewing for midterms and made a lot of concepts clear. Some of the group projects throughout the semester were hard.

I was nervous to take this class in light of the bad reviews. The common criticisms (mistakes in slides and unclear lectures) are just not true. There was 1 mistake in the class slides which he promptly corrected when he reuploaded the slides after class. His lectures are clear but may be a little confusing if you've done 0 of the assigned reading.

I hate to give him this ranking since he's so kind, but Tuijn teaches his course in the most unproductive way possible. I've managed to maintain an A in his class simply because I just study the practice material, but his lectures will confuse you so much that you're better off not listening. I'm sorry professor Tuijn, but you're not that guy.

Tuijn has no idea what he's talking about. He is unclear in lectures and explains everything so poorly. You will be confused for the entirety of the class and even when you ask him to explain you probably will have to ask 5 more questions for it to become clear. His grading has mistakes along with the slides, and case studies: IMPOSSIBLE. awful

reviews.comment: One of the most difficult and frustrating classes I have taken so far. The lectures were very confusing to understand and there were lots mistakes on practice exams and lecture slides. He did not work out problems in class and could not explain the material well, so the material was mainly self-taught. Also, tough case studies and long homeworks.

Least favorite SMU professor and class. Tuijn, no joke, has probably made 50+ mistakes in his powerpoints, reviews, etc which is incredibly confusing. Makes class material very hard because he doesn't know how to teach it and doesn't seem to know it himself. Case studies are impossible. Tons of work. Would never recommend to anyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Professor Tuijn was amazing! He was great at explaining the more complex/boring stuff and keeping the class engaged. Loved his lectures. I actually use what he taught us at work now. 

Ten out of ten, would highly recommend this knockout of a professor.
He is the greatest. Do the work, youll get an A. Honestly an awesome, brilliant professor.
didnt learn much and prof tuijn was not my favorite. Tests were nothing like in class work it seemed like

I've never rated a professor before, but I felt like it was necessary this time because he was so bad. Everything about this class was confusing and the tests were extremely difficult. I tried to get help from him multiple times, and he just confused me more.

Doesn't explain the material well, homework is worthless, test questions are nothing like we covered in our long practice problems we cover in class. He should stop being lazy and write his own tests.

Not a fan of professor Tuijn. His teaching style revolves around PowerPoints that do not help us understand the material. He also never told us that there is a participation grade until the end of the semester which hurt a lot of people. Concepts for case studies were not covered before they were due.

Marcel is a novice professor that simply does not know what he is teaching. You ask him a question in class only to find that he doesn't know the answer himself. The case studies are horrendous and the tests are bogus. We have barely any other materials to practice with before the test. He really needs to change how he teaches this class.

Material itself is easy and Tuijn is so nice, but truly not a great teacher. He'll start answering your question before you finish asking it, and his slides were sometimes messy and unclear. If you had LHR for Managerial, think the EXACT opposite for Tuijn. You'll be fine but you'll be teaching yourself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm a big fan of Prof. Tuijn. There was a lot of negative energy around this class being difficult, but it seems like some very effective changes were made to create a still hard, but very possible class to learn a lot in. Lectures are good, case studies are hard but just plan ahead.

I really enjoyed Tuijn's class! He has transparent criteria for what topics you need to know for exams (from the PowerPoints and read the textbook if you need extra depth). There are short reading quizzes for some chapters that if you read you'll get 100% and group case assignments that align with each major topic. Normal amount of Mylab homework.

He is just not a good teacher. He is nice and tries to make the class interesting, but every time he answers a question it just confuses everyone 10x more. Teaches off of a powerpoint which is extraordinarily boring in a 90 min class, and the homework is so confusing. You'll survive if you have to take him for cost, but won't be fun.

Lots of group projects that are way more in-depth and require more than his examples in class he gives to teach the material. He was a nice guy and I respected him, and he is a good teacher but his teaching just did not fit my learning style. Tests were average, I always thought I did better than I actually did. Read textbook, follow along in class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: 3 midterms optional final. The tests were not too hard very straightforward. For the first two tests, his lectures were fine, but the lectures for the 3rd test were unclear and hard to understand. There are group case studies, they were fine google will help you. There is a final group project (20%), and it needs some dedication for a good grade.

Take anyone else. Tuijn ignored university policy regarding Covid, and he usually refused to answer questions. His lectures make no sense, I had to teach myself this material. Lots of homework, case assignments, three tests, and an optional final. He will curve people down to make sure not too many students have an A. He may be my worst prof ever.

One of the nicest guys you will ever meet, but he is not a good teacher. These concepts should not be hard, but the way he teaches makes everything confusing and you will be teaching yourself a lot before the exam. His case studies are not clear, the averages are very low and he is not good at giving feedback. Often messes up his in class examples.

Dr. Turner is dedicated to all students in the class. He spends enough time to make sure we understand the topics. Even when a difficult subject has to be repeated, he stays calm. Also, his grading system is fair and not too easy or too hard.

Great teacher who really cares about his students succeeding. He's always willing to meet with students or hold study sessions. Homework and tests are very straightforward, and the material is easy if you attend class.

Best teacher ever!  Explains things well.  Always available to help.  Cares about students doing well.  Tests are just like practice tests.  HW is out of book but pretty simple.  With a little effort and if you pay attention this class is really easy!

Professor Tunks is literally the most kindhearted man on the planet. He's super quirky and adorable and you can tell he loves the material so much. He is super understanding with grading too and his class is incredibly laid back. Don't listen to a single negative review! He even took out the final and midterms from the course.

He is a good lecturer and is clear about what are going to be on his daily quizzes. However, his midterm and his final exam include very very tough listening components. Attendance is basically mandatory each day because of his daily quizzes. The concert papers aren't hard but the exams are ridiculous especially if you haven't taken a music class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tunks is a very knowledgeable and fun professor! Sometimes the lectures get a little dry but he knows what he's talking about and is great at explaining the course material - he also uses demonstrations and examples every class to explain the material! I have no music experience but still probably one of the easier classes I've taken at SMU.

I took this class for Musical Acoustics. I barely used the textbook and I ended up being okay. I could have done better by just dedicating a lot more time to studying for the tests. Class is pretty interesting, but hard to really pay attention through the whole thing. This class isn't so bad so just do what they ask and you'll be okay

Don't take this. It should have been an easy A but after the final, my grade dropped to a B & I went to every class, did well on all of the quizzes and papers and didn't even think the final was hard. I even have music experience. He's also super boring and I can only imagine how hard this would be for people without music background.

Hard to describe. He's charismatic and talkative in class, but he seemed kind of cold when I personally approached him. But he explains terms pretty clearly and gives the class as many examples as we need. Just pay attention and you'll be fine. If you've ever taken any kind of music class before this class is an easy A.

Extremely difficult professor, very careless towards his students. Exercises power over the class body and gives very unfair grades. Unfortunate that this class is required- I really loved classical music, now I just feel bitter after the experience with this professor. Be prepared! Out of all of my difficult classes, I got the lowest grade here.

This class is ridiculously hard for an introductory class. Not only is it the most boring class ever, but he may as well be speaking in Chinese if you don't know much about music. His way of grading is also extremely difficult to understand. This is my least favorite class I've EVER taken.
This class is extremely hard for a beginner. If you want to get B or B+. Do not choose this class. Professor just speak and never use ppf in class. I hate him.

This class was way too difficult for an introductory level class. Dr. Tunks' expectations are ridiculous and he should really think about making the class easier for the students who are not music majors.

Such an easy class if you've ever done anything musical before. Tunks is super sweet and genuinely cares about his students. A few of the TAs are good, but the rest aren't the best. But Tunks is great and the class is so incredibly easy.

Great class for a mandatory perspective! Professor Tunks is really straight forward and you can tell he loves his job. Midterm and Final were straight out of the notes. Be prepared to come to class everyday because of daily quizzes. TA's aren't that great at teaching but Tunks makes up for it.

Professor Tunks was great! He loves what he is doing and the class is very interesting. He is very helpful and will work with you. Attendance is mandatory since we take a quiz every class but it's 3 questions that are very simple. Take his class!!!

Hey was a great teacher with Professor Olness!! I LOVED this class!! The first time I took it as a freshman I was not prepared for the challenge of the course but the second time around I got it right.

This course is a full price course but they have non PhD people on their staff teaching it.  David is someone who tries to be nice but fails to know how to teach and grade fairly for all. He biased again some students and grades accordingly.
A total waste of class of time and money and can't teach worth s. For what we pay we should be getting actual professors not staff to teach courses.

Professor Tylicki is a nice person, really liked taking his class! There are several assignments per week but they are all easy. He also provided good information about all of the departments that offer support at SMU. Seems to genuinely care about his students.

Lectures are ego-driven rants. Nothing is taught, everything is judged, and students are just props in a self-obsessed monologue. Grading is chaotic, and any confusion is blamed on you. Avoid unless you're into humiliation.

Bro is condescending to people who don't think like him. Can't teach worth ahyte is disorganized, rude, conniving, and won't listen to student concerns even when serious health issues arise. Need to find another job and shouldn't be around young people
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lack of leadership, common courtesy in emails, and disrespectful attitude towards teaching.
I also took the summer class it was very easy.  He said its harder during the semester, but I dont think he would be that bad of a teacher during the semester.
Good teacher class was easy.  Took it for summer so he watered it down.
he is a ****.
This is a graduate level seminar for the Co-Op program. Grades are earned by completing a report based on your internship experience.
Best adviser ever!
Mr. Valerin is very helpful to international students. This internship program gives us great opportunity to learn.
Contradicts himself often, very misleading, delights in manipulation.

One of the worst professors that I have experienced at SMU. Disrespectful and rude to students when answering his questions. Awful learning enviroment with no homework, quizes, or tests outside the midterm and final. He should be retiring soon which is a blessing for everyone. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

Prof. Vetsuypens is an expert in corporate finance and valuations. I found his class exciting where he explained complex concepts in simple, relatable ways. I still remember some of the cases we discussed in valuations class. He expects his students to come prepared and that helped me in learning deeper concepts in finance.

He retires after this year but be aware that if you have no financial background you will struggle. He expects everyone to already know about finance which is not always the case. He is a nice and blunt guy but the only grades are the midterm and final and it is so hard to have to teach yourself to understand the material.

He has no rules, no boundaries he probably doesn't flinch at the hint of torture or genocide. He is not loyal to a flag or a country, only thing he is loyal to is the set of ideals that are making his students suffer as much as possible. This is coming from a Graduate that got a B+ in his FINA6212 class. He will laugh as you suffer. DO NOT TAKE.

To be honest, this is the worst experience I have had throughout all my years of school. Not only does this professor blatantly call people out and make people feel stupid for not knowing something, he could not care less about your feelings. The final exam is your entire grade. He does not curve, he does not care if he fails anyone. good luck

reviews.comment: Great professor. He is a tough grader and expects you to be prepared for every class, but you will benefit greatly by taking him.

He is by far the best professor I’ve ever had - includes every professor I took while I was in b-school,  law school, and as an undergraduate student. Expects students to come to each class prepared to discuss all assigned material. Extremely knowledgeable and does a great conveying that knowledge to the students.

Hes one of the best professors Ive ever had. He teaches so well. I understand how some students may get rubbed the wrong way as he makes some hilarious jokes, but its all in the context of finance and applicable to the material so it helps in learning. He is very knowledgeable an expert really.
Lot of knowledge.  Tough class.  Funny Stories.
Long rants with little clarification on important topics.  Has some funny moments, but overall is kind of a jackass.

Easily, the worst prof I've ever had.  He is arrogant and rude.  He seems to revel in the well-known fact that he is not well liked.  He is a lazy professor and doesn't go out of his way to help.  There were a couple times when he called out fellow students berating them for not knowing the answer to his rambling question.  Worthless.

You will learn so much in his class; however, if you really worry about your grades then look out. He does not curve much and has no problem giving out C's. He is very organized and knows the material well but is somewhat intimidating to approach. Grade for this class was 100% based on final, so it was sink-or-swim as far as the grade. Final-tough.

He is a pretty standard professor. He's a nice guy, but is bad at responding to emails. If you are a studious pre-med, the class is easy. Like, NGL, I stopped showing up to lectures for the last two months and crammed the night before and still did well on the tests, of which are open note. No extra credit unlike the other professors, though.

Lectures are hard to follow and super monotone. Tests are difficult but there is always a curve. Three attempts on all homework assignments which is nice. Overall he is a nice guy but you will never be able to reach him outside of class so if you have questions go to him directly.
He was pretty monotone and doesn't understand when people don't get it

Sweet guy and soft spoken. Lectures are kinda boring but attendance isn't mandatory. Gives 3 attempts on each homework which is huge. Tests are very similar to homework and open note. Even if you skip class, it is very very manageable as long as you figure out what's going on before the tests.

Lectures can be confusing and lots of remedial learning needs to be done outside of class. Professor Vega is a nice guy who is clearly very bright, however, he is hard to understand and frequently goes off on tangents. He really does know what he is doing, but this course is poor and I would avoid taking it unless you are truly interested.

To do good in this class you have to conceptually understand what he is teaching. The biggest tool to preforming well is doing the homework consciously, which means actually trying each homework problem after the studying the material, and if you get a problem wrong, make sure to understand why. Some problems will make you look into the textbook.

This professor is beyond a doubt the worst teacher I have ever had at any school. I could write an entire essay about how awful this poor excuse of educator is, but I'll keep it short. Vega talks in circles, shows no respect for his students or their time, and has no idea what he is doing. Homework is useless, and the book is awful. DO NOT TAKE HIM

reviews.comment: He is verbally abusive in office hours and calls students stupid and idiots one of the most unprofessional professors I have ever met or learned from it's really sad SMU thinks he's worth something

Terrible TERRIBLE professor. Classes were a waste of time because he never covered anything of substance. Homework did not follow from lectures. For some reason during a pandemic he gave insanely harsh grades after himself missing the final exam for "personal reasons". So you get a pass but students are expected to perform perfectly? BS!
Worst professor ever

reviews.comment: Dr. Vega is nice outside of class, but he really shouldn't be teaching an introductory physics class. The textbook doesn't correlate to the class at all. He doesn't make his own homework, so it is usually different than what he is teaching. And the tests are 15 mistake-filled multiple choice questions with little chance for partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If I could give a 0 on here I would. Count on errors on exams, on quizzes, or in lecture costing you in the long run. Professor Vega's inability to teach an introductory physics class astounds me. If you want to maintain your GPA don't take the class, or if it's too late, master the concepts on your own. Nice man, but shouldn't be a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He definitely knows the material, but it doesn't translate well until his lectures. He's a very nice man, but lectures are almost pointless but you  have to go for the pop  quizzes.  Not to worry, your grade will be better than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What makes his classes so difficult is that he tests on understanding and comprehension rather than just your use of math. Plus, I feel like because he eat sleeps and breaths quantum mechanics, it's easy for him to forget that this is all new and strange to us. But he makes up for it. He will always help if asked and he's very genuine.
The guy knows what he's talking about and absolutely no idea how to explain it

Like others have said, Vega's a caring, brilliant professor who just can't teach that well. He does tend to go on a tangent sometimes and derive formulas which leaves everyone blank-faced. But, participate and listen in class, and he'll acknowledge your effort. He's always available for office hours and very helpful in there.  Study a lot.
NEVER TAKE HIM

Vega is a nice and brilliant professor who unfortunately is utterly incapable of teaching physics I. His lectures are disorganized, confusing, random, non-sequential and contain unrelated tangents. He makes everything so much more difficult than it has to be. You must read the textbook and teach yourself the material throughout the course.

Simpy put, Vega is a really great guy who cares about his students. However, he just isn't a great teacher. His lectures are often full of rambling, tangents, and confusion. The homework isn't too difficult and is a good portion of the grade but does nothing to prepare you for the tests. I just find myself reviewing old tests and saying a prayer.

This teacher is the worst teacher you will ever take. STAY AWAY FROM THIS CLASS. No matter how hard you study you will still FAIL the tests. It is a impossible class, the teacher does not teach it well and it will kill your GPA. AVOID VEGA at all costs.

Probably one of the hardest courses I have taken, but if you apply yourself, read the book and do the homework consciously you will do well in the course.  The exams are multiple choice and conceptual understanding is emphasized.   The homework problems are hard unless you have a solid conceptual understanding.

Lecture leaves you clueless and he is disorganized, but, in office hours, he's extremely helpful. And his disorganization allows him to be the most flexible prof and he gives extra credit all the time, especially if you prove him wrong about something. His grading Policy is GREAT! If you fail this class, you're very lazy.

There's only two teachers who teaches Physics, and the other teacher is as hard as Vega. I don't know which one is worst, I am just GLAD TO BE OUT, now is your time to suffer, mine is over...lol..HAVE FUN..!
STAY AWAY!!! He basically teachs by deriving formulas. Living you clueless and everyone with blank faces. The test's average were 60's..
No Comments

Absolutely miserable.  He isn't clear or helpful or even civil towards his students.  If you need help out of class, go to the TA b/c he'll tell you nothing that is helpful.  A majority of the class is close to failing!
terrible - impossible, likes to trick students on exams.. average on last test was a 39 and it was a mult. choice test with all premed students........avoid this guy...
Horrible! Gives the grade she wants to give not what you deserve. No feedback in class.

There is a lot of work, and the tests (4) total up to only 45% of final grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Veronica Leon has been the worst professor I have ever had. She's rude, and very demanding. She is not willing to help in class, and is very confusing in her lectures. She speaks way to fast for anyone in a beginner Spanish class to understand and follow what she wants us to do. I would not recommend her to my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Simply the GOAT.
Class is mandatory. class is easy but you do have to practice if you want a A. She's very willing to help in her office. Very sweet and kind. Deff recommend
Love her. She makes class interesting and clear. Very willing to help.
She's great.  Not super easy and don't fall asleep, but if you pay attention and do the homework, you'll learn a lot

Leon is really nice, and is really big on following the syllabus. She's willing to help with issues, and will go to great lengths to make sure her students aren't confusedstruggling if they approach her about a problem. Take her class!

Knows her stuff; kind, engaging, and a great teacher. Not hard if you attend class, listen to lectures, and do the online homework. One easy online homework (takes 30 mins or less) due each week. 6 quizzes and three tests, which she reviews for and is very clear about what she expects. She's great with spanish and sparking your interest - take her!
She takes attendance very seriously. She really cares about her students and wants them to interact. If you do the work and try she will like you.
Profesora León is a good Spanish professor, but is definitely the hardest for 1402.She is department head and kinda does what shes wants. Go to class, do homeworks and you will make an A.

Loved Doctora León! She was not everyones favorite because she does require participations and hard work. However, you can get an A without straining yourself too much. As a Spanish minor, I really felt my time in her class was well spent. She is very understanding and forgiving. Would recommend for anyone who has an interest in Spanish.

She is very strict and gives a lot of homework. Do the homework, go to class, go to her office/set appt, and you will do good in her class. She's always willing to help! Don't eat snacks/candy in her class, makes her mad. She's passionate about helping u learn Spanish. this class isn't easy.
Homework is simply busy work and all you do is discuss different major controversies every week. Vocab quizzes once a week. Does not like incomplete homework. Very personable professor.

I think Dra. Leon is amazing. She has a true passion for teaching Spanish. Your grade in the class is based a lot on how much you improve in Spanish. If you show you are trying and make improvements in your speaking, half of your grade is already secure. I believe anyone majoring/minoring in Spanish should have her as a professor!!
This is a demanding class due to the amount of work assigned throughout the semester, but it's a great class overall. She cares about her students and is very passionate about Spanish.
She's demanding, but genuinely cares about the students. Lot's of assignments and a good amount of tests/quizzes.

Horrible professor , unfair grader and she literally gives you the grade she wants at the end,  AVOID , head of the  department which gives her the advantage to do whatever she wants. WORST TEACHER OF SMU
I learned a lot from her class. She really cares about her students, but she is very demanding
I must say I was very surprised to see this professer get such good reviews. I had her several years ago and I found her to be a very hateful and unfair professor.
She is a great teacher. She may be kind of hard, but you will learn a lot and she really cares about her students.
She's a really nice lady and explains everything quite well.  I wouldn't say her teaching style is the most exciting, but I learned a lot from her class.
Really nice teacher, always willing to explain concepts. Tests are pretty difficult but similar to practice questions posted

Truly a nice guy. Tests are a little hard, but he is always willing to help and the class is graded on a curve like the rest of the FINA ones at SMU obviously. Doesn't give bad final grades. This elective class comes with weekly quizzes but they are short, easy and open note
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I found the class overall slightly disappointing, since the course content appeared to be more theoretical than practical, though I'm sure that doesn't land squarely on him. His tests were a bit tricky, though since the class is graded on a curve it isn't too bad. He is a friendly person and is happy to answer questions if you go his office.

Good professor. It's hard to pay attention in class because he posts his slideshows and doesn't work that many examples. Tests were pretty hard. The first one was definitely the easiest and the second was the hardest. No final. Two simple projects. Weekly completion homework.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ok - Diego is an extremely nice guy and is very approachable. But, he is a rather new professor, and hasn't figured it all out yet. His tests are rather difficult but he is always willing to help. Lectures are ver long and boring but he basically doesnt give anyone below a B so you are pretty safe. not bad

Outstanding professor. Very caring, open minded, and very optimistic about anything. Definitely a person who sees the cup half full. I've learned a great deal from her. She does give a lot of work, but what do you expect art classes to be? Challenging class indeed but rewarding based on the time and effort you put in. One of my favorite teachers!
It doesn't matter how hard you try, if you aren't an art major you won't get an A. Doesn't give out grades you just have to guess what you have in the class. I'd stay away

Relatively easy coursework, but she's not very clear what she wants. Most of the class you paint rather than draw. Teacher is not very friendly at all. I wouldn't recommend her. Also very hard to get an A. You can't miss a single class and she'll never give you grades for your work so you wont know how you're doing until the  class is over.

you'll get 100 on every assignment if you follow what she does, and your entire grade is the final exam. her models do not balance and she gets angry if you ask her questions. it's difficult to teach a modeling class anyway so the best you can do it is to beat the curve. make a good cheat sheet and you should be fine on the final
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: terrible teacher, does not know the material at all, she just posts old videos of former professors talking and expects that to help, she did nothing herself. I'm a 4.0 finance student, I could point out 50 times throughout the class when she was objectively incorrect, but when you point it out she just says nothing and denies it. 0/10 do not take.

This class has good material but the teaching style is awful and you learn nothing. She is not understanding of circumstances that students go through like attendance or late to class conflicts. She is very hard to understand in class and you have to practice outside of class to do well.

If you have an alternative, do not take Vivi Zhu. She is very difficult to understand and hardly speaks English. She lacks any sense of empathy or understanding. Do not take her!!!! On her way to getting kicked out of Cox.

like everyone else says, easily the worst instructor at Cox. She had no idea what she is doing, always does problems wrong (she will clearly be unable to solve the problem and then just shrug and keep going) just does excel stuff using arbitrary, complicated formulas, and expects us to match it exactly in a test setting, 0/10 horrid professor.
Teacher spoke improper English so I learned nothing in this course.

This was a terrible class. All we did was copy the things written down during the lectures without being given any explanation about what was occurring. The final was awful, there was barely enough time to complete everything. I did not learn anything in the class and I feel like I wasted a semester just copying down formulas in excel.

Professor Zhu's lab covers Home Depot 1-5, additional data cases, and attendance. She walkthroughs the data cases, often ending early. She is respectful, supportive, and helpful. I'd recommend reviewing data case work before submitting. The final (35%) covers Home Depot 1-5 and one random data case (i think). She allowed a cheat sheet. It was hard.

I see why people have an issue with her because she doesn't really teach the material. Each class is basically her telling you what to do but not really explaining how she got there, just the numbers. Despite that though, always lets out early and the labs aren't too hard. Final was pretty bad but allowed cheat sheet and there's cox curve.

Entire grade based on the final which is practically impossible via lockdown excel. Genuinley such an awful finals environment and very disappointing to see this format in the business school. All other grades are virtually follow along in class where she is repeatedly wrong and will not explain her methodology.

I beg you to avoid this class. She is extremely hard to understand in class and doesn't teach the material conceptually at all, and then comes at you with a final worth 35% of your grade at the end (which the average is roughly a 65 on). Doesn't matter how smart you are, your grade in this class could be literally anything.

She's the worst. You learn nothing, everyone get's good grades on the labs because you just follow along with her, but when it comes to the final, everyone gets screwed. The lab final is on lockdown browser Excel, which is super glitchy and hard to use. Many people lose their work and you are not prepared by the class. Many 4.00 students get B+'s.

Vivi is a nice person but awful teacher. She expects you to know everything. So you just copy her the entire class. When it comes to the final, you are tested on a semesters worth of material with no idea what's going on. She was absolutely awful be prepared to drop a few letter grades.

Labs are easy, but I almost couldn't sit through them because her voice was so irritating. The final exam is taken on an excel lockdown browser that can refresh and lose your work at any time. Because everyone does well on the labs, your whole grade basically depends on the final. She refuses to take accountability for her faulty final exam system.

Zhu is the most horrid professor at SMU. You can hardly understand her and she does not speak enough english. She was also incredibly unacessible and lacked any understanding outside of class. The jist of the class is following her lead in class then saying a prayer before opening the final, which 1/4 of the class walks out crying from.

This is the worst professor I have taken at SMU. She refuses to help students. In class, if you go up to her asking for help, she will answer "it is there", when "it" obviously isn't. Barely speaks English and will not listen to you. On her in-class assignments and final, the Excel docs are filled with errors, and she won't help. do not take!!

If you want to be miserable and absolutely hate your life, then take this professor. If you want to actually experience some sort of peace in your daily life, then I would suggest a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor for ANYTHING. You will not learn ANYTHING. The exam made no sense because she did not teach ANYTHING. As others have noted, a department curve was written in her syllabus but she did not use to calculate final grades. Extremely unfair since SMU forced us to take this professor as no one else was teaching this class.
Can't speak english, Final is impossible, walks through each model expecting us to understand what she's saying. Just end up copying her and trying to figure it out. I learned nothing in this class

Professor Vokic is great at teaching, she's super animated in lectures and explains concepts well. Her classes are total points so they're pretty tough, and you absolutely need to show up to class (3+ absences = fail). Definitely recommend going to her office hours if you have any questions, she's always open to meeting with students.

For Linguistics it can be difficult to understand, but her teaching and lecture style makes you really comprehend the material. Great teacher who cares about her students and will help/ give good feedback. I have enjoyed her class.

Dra. Vokic is a gem! She is really helpful and knows what she is doing. She values learning over your GPA - meaning that she won't punish you for not getting every detail right. Really values effort too! Her grading scheme is pretty clear, but the weight of all of her assignments is not so clear.

She was very knowledgeable and made the class interesting. Shes very passionate. The class is project heavy with a midterm and final. I enjoyed the class and would take it again. She picks on you to answer her questions, but thats the worst it can get.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Vokic is by far my favorite professor!! This class was so interesting and I learned a lot. Pay attention and take good notes because she does a great job of explaining the material and its much harder to teach it to yourself later using the book.

I very much enjoyed the discussions in her class; I feel like I learned a lot about real world problems. There are several papers to write but they only have to be 500 words. Participation is a must in this class, but it is very informal. I would definitely recommend taking her.

Vokic is a good teacher in the sense that she explains things in detail with lots of examples. However, she is a really tough grader and doesn't give points back. Honestly her grading doesn't make a whole lot of sense. Prepare to participate, or she'll call you out.
Good prof. Knows what she's talking about, and takes pride in her work. Easy class, 30% of the grade is attendance. A few assignments, but all easy. The interships are fun and chill.

Amazing professor! SMU is stupid to let him go! He has a real passion for teaching and really takes time to get to know us as students. He made the class very interesting and engaging! The MNO concepts are really basic, but don't let that fool you. The tests and project can be challenging. But Dr. Vogel will really try to help you succeed!

Professor Vogel was the best professor I've had at Cox. We are all upset that he isn't staying at SMU next year. He was straightforward, fun and easy to understand. He spent time getting to know his students and understanding their interests. Other professors definitely should learn from him.

Good professor. Straight forward, he covered relevant topics in class in interesting ways. Two tests, team project, case studies & participation required (but he makes it interesting enough the whole class participates). One of my better profs in Cox.

Take this guy! He really makes this an interesting class. The case studies he chooses are all relative and he is great at getting the entire class involved. We did a Harvard Bus. School simulation that had us climbing Mt. Everest in teams. Other profs in Cox need to be more forward thinking with their lesson exercises like Vogel is. Best prof. yet!

WORST Professor I had at SMU. After taking AP Calculus in HS and getting a B, I thought this class would be an easy A. I was so wrong! He was so hard to follow. He cared more about theorems then making things easy to understand. He used weird symbols and was overall weird. I took Judy Newell's section the summer after and got an A in her course.
Had lots of time for office hours and was always enthusiastic about calculus 3. Best math professor at SMU by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Viator is very inconsistent. He canceled/shortened his office hours every day and didn't give us our daily quizzes daily. His class was slow moving for a proofs class. He didn't seem to care about wanting to finish the semester strong because he has another job lined up somewhere else. I'm glad I won't have the chance to take him again.

He is a little intense but its only because he is obviously passionate about the subject. His lectures can be confusing but he explains things perfectly in office hours for some reason. Tests are harder than the homework, but the hw does give a good buffer grade. Solid choice for calc, if a little tough

He is honestly the best math professor I have ever had. There are few people who are as passionate and as knowledgeable as Dr. Viator. His excitement is contagious and makes an otherwise boring class exiting. The notes he gives in class are extremely helpful. Do the homework and you are guaranteed a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Viator will be your biggest cheerleader at SMU. He made Calc 3 so easy to understand and he was super supportive. He encouraged asking questions and made you feel so smart even if you asked something stupid. Super clear and engaging lectures, gives tons of example problems. Tests are similar to homework.

He's a very nice person and cares about the subject and his students, but wouldn't take him again. Took him for calculus 1 and had to work hard for a B+. I'm naturally good at math but still found his class extremely challenging. His teaching style is confusing and he makes tests harder than they should be. Hard grader and weirdly strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Viator is a great instructor! He is so passionate for mathematics and he is always open to answering any questions during lecture. He works out examples of math problems during class and he goes through every step in detail. He does give a lot of homework and he is a little tough on grading; so you will have to work hard, but you will learn!

Sorry kiddos, Calculus III was NOT fun with him at all. Calculus III involves lots of sketching 2D-3D graphs, but we never really took the time to understand and utilize. Literally, in this class, he would sketch and we'd be like whaaaaaat. Don't expect easy at all. You can't solve anything in this class if you can't see what it asks you to solve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Viator is super passionate about calculus and it really helps to make the class easier. He wants you to pass and is always willing to help. His course is as hard as any intro calculus class, but there are bonus points on the test and enough homework grades to keep your grade up and give you practice for the tests. His lectures aren't boring!

A nice teacher that really wants you to succeed. His tests, however, are extremely difficult even if you have taken a Calculus class before. Homework piles up and even though it's technically optional, if you don't do it you'll fail. Quizzes and assigned problems are usually not too bad, but tests destroy. Also, not at all lenient with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mr. V's passion for math makes you feel almost as excited as he is, and he constantly encourages us to ask questions if we don't understand. He understands that there is a mix of students who have and have not taken calculus before, so he's always willing to adjust. Best of all, he drops the lowest quiz and the lowest homework grade at the end.

Prof. Viator is the best math professor I have ever had. His passion for math makes you more passionate about the subject. His energy is contagious, and he is extremely available outside of class and loves his students. Would highly recommend if you are a hard working student and want a professor who will make love math.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Passionate and great instructor. Super easy to access for help outside of class.

Really hard class and very time consuming, so if you've never taken Calc 2 before then make sure your schedule is clear enough to devote lots of time to practice problems. The final was almost a copy of the problems on the midterms. Not a bad professor (he cares a lot about his students) but expects a lot and doesn't give much fluff points on tests

Viator is hilarious and makes class fun, but if you miss class you will get so far behind. A lot of homework is optional and he takes a lot of test questions from it, but each night can take more than 6 hours to do. Had to teach a lot to myself as I was always confused in class and office hours weren't help. Lots of people failed. Take another prof

I have never felt so comfortable wanting to ask for help. He truly is passionate about helping students learn math. He is very nice in lecture and loves to answer questions. Calculus can get tricky but he is very clear in his lectures! highly recommend.
I got an A in diff eq and almost failed calc 2 with him. i think that says enough

PROS: Great passion for the subject. Loves math, all the ins and outs of it. Wants you to love math too. Brings great energy. Has very straightforward expectations. Very caring outside of class. Bonus on every test. CONS: Stingy, inflexible grader and he'll even say so. Has a tendency to cancel office hours, although usually for good reason. 4/5

Dr. Viator is hands down the best math professor I have ever had. He is energetic, intelligent, and challenging. He wants more than anything for his students to love math as much as he does so he always encourages questions. He has a funny way of describing concepts like "crunchy" or "juicy" so you'll be dually entertained and educated :) RECOMMEND

Viator is one of my favorite math professors ever. His notes are clear and he gives examples very similar to those that will be found on the quizzes/tests. He has 8-10 hw problems due on mons, a quiz on weds, and 3 exams spread throughout the semester. If you do the hw problems he assigns and understand the topic, that is really all you need to do.

Viator is amazing! He respects your questions even if they are silly ones sometimes, and he truly encourages us asking him questions. Take his class cause you'd sit in his class thinking, "what if I hadn't taken his class? man that would be terrible!"

One of the most toughest graders at SMU but one of many shining stars in the math department. He is enthusiastic and will get you excited for calculus. He will make you suffer with hard stuff first (like using limits to calculate derivatives) which at first may be annoying, but in hindsight, Im glad he made us do it. You will LEARN calculus!

Doctor Viators workload is unnecessary and frankly inappropriate when it comes to his teachings. My entire class struggled on homework with loads of problems. This was made worse by the fact that he is quite frankly a very inflexible teacher. Beware if you need extra help or any special arrangements as he will not be lenient. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Mister Viator is a pretty decent teacher when it comes to presenting material, but the work he gives is what makes the class difficult . Be prepared for tens of questions each week, and study like theres no tomorrow. He gives work that doesnt accurately reflect his teaching, as they include uncovered content and lots of unnecessary work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: If youre a first-year coming right out of AP calc, youll probably get an A. If youve taken a gap since your last math class, dangerously procrastinate, or tend to skip class, youll probably fail. He assumes everyone is already a pro at trig, assigns 80+ homework problems each week, and has something graded every class period. No m/c on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There's never a dull moment during Dr. Viator's lectures. He is so enthusiastic about the subject, and he makes it very easy to understand. He looks for participation during class, so make sure to respond when he asks questions. You can skip one problem per exam, and there are 10 point of bonus possible on each. Definitely recommend!

I love his energy and the way he made himself available to the kids who asked for help. It was calculus, and so I might only recommend this class to people who want a degree in STEM. This class made me feel prepared to take his Calculus II class and this passion was contagious throughout the class.

He's super engaging and just a funny little man! He doesn't take attendance but you have hw due every Monday and a quiz every Wednesday so you kind of have to go, and also he makes it a point to get to know people's names, so he knows when you don't show up. Quizzes and tests are easy as long as you look through the practice problems he assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Viator is everything you could want in a math professor! He makes the subject interesting and he loves math with a passion. Very accessible outside of class and a fair grader as well. if you keep up with the class you should receive an A. attendance was not mandatory but he does give quizzes often.

Dr. Viator was the best math teacher I've ever had. It's clear that he wants to make sure everyone understands the content, and he really likes his subject. His tests are reasonable, and they shouldn't be too bad if you do the homework. Definitely take Dr. V if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Viator is everything I would want in a teacher! He does his best to make material understandable, and he's very down to earth and extremely accessible. He does give plenty of homework and practice problems, and if you haven't taken calculus before, it will be difficult due to the speed of the class. However, he's very quick to respond!
Professor Luan tries to give you many times for extra help which is very nice. It is a difficult class, but at least try to go to him for help! It is manageable if you do the work and study a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Luan always made time to help, and added extra office hours before midterms
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Luan is more than willing to help the students learn and truly want them to succeed. Also, Luan shows enthusiasm towards the material and wants the students to grasp the concepts conceptually, not just memorizing formulas and theorems. Overall, one of the better math teachers I have had, but the class is difficult.

I really enjoyed how Prof. Luan got our class involved with lectures. He has an accent but all in all is a very good teacher and teaches very well!! His encouraging participation increased my understanding of the course. Just got an A+ and be ready for his Calc2 this spring :)
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: If you've taken calc 1 before this class will be more manageable, but for just finishing pre calc it was a lot harder for me than my friends in the class. He has a hard accent to understand and will assign hw and quizzes that are harder than the problems shown on the board. Because he doesn't explain things well, going to office hours does not help
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Luan is a great mathematician. He gets a lot of crap for his accent but once you get used to it, it isn't a big deal. This is a super easy class to take. When making a test, he just takes the study guide and changes the numbers. He also has tons of office hours per week. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Luan is ok. If you are good at math or ready to put in the work, his class should treat you well. Like others have said, his accent can be an issue in class sometimes. Very lenient grader and wants his students to succeed but sometimes his inability to simplify concepts causes students to be confused

He is an extremely smart mathematician. The nice thing is he really cared and wanted us succeed. His handwritten notes and review sessions were very helpful. Overall, great teacher. Already enrolled in his Calc2 class this spring.

Professor Luan was very enthusiatic about the subject. Very kind and easily approachable. He cares and wants the best for his students. Although sometimes the class is silent when he asks a question, the questions are actually well posed. The review sheet and practice midterms were helpful. Definitely my favorite teacher.

I was personally doing fine in this class and it was easy enough, but this was because I was in Calc 1 in high school, so if you struggle with math, this is not the class to take. He'ss very accessible outside of class but his lectures are very scattered, and these lectures were primarily theory-based and examples for homework were far and few.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He shows enthusiasm in teaching and really cares to have us understand the material. He does have an accent but breaks it down well enough so that we can understand. He offers interacting lectures, where students are able to obtain extra credit from answering questions. office hours are really helpful. his tests are fair. Good teacher.

I enjoyed his lectures very much. I havent had a math profess or who is so well organized as he is. His notes are handwritten (not just slides that are copy and pasted from the textbook like many other professors) and he can teach us the concepts in the easiest and most effective way possible. Professor Luan is great at teaching Calc1.

Do not take this dude's class if you can avoid it. He has a super thick accent and you can barely understand him. He teaches completely based on theory not on examples which makes doing the homework difficult and the lectures are extremely painful. Only good thing is his tests are basically exactly the same as the practice test he gives you.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Overall a pretty good teacher. Homework isn't too hard (about 20-30 problems a week and a 10 question quiz). Sometime you will have a quiz in class and that is how your participation grade is calculated. Tests can be tough though. Also, and its not really something that can be helped, but he does have a strong accent and can be hard to understand.

I like her. I took 3320 (not on list). This class is NOT building websites like course description. U do learn html and css basics. She is helpful and knows what she is doing. Lectures are dry and only assigns projects at end of semester; which means ppl don't pay attention in class. Easy A, wish course description matched the class.

Professor Watkins is one of the best professors I've ever had! She quite literally taught me how to code and has always been super encouraging. If you're struggling with any material, she will always go out of her way to help you. You don't need to worry about your grade in her classes because she always gives you opportunities to bring it up!
Good Teacher. Easy A if you follow the lectures. Attendance required for lab and lecture.

Did not really teach anything! lol 
Teaching is a task assigned to a teacher/professor. right?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The professor has exams which have too many problems for the amount of time given, and his in class lectures and examples are not nearly as difficult as the homework or exam problems. He doesn't explain enough of the theoretical concepts and he doesn't explain what he is doing in depth when doing examples so you are left on your own to learn.
Straight from the book Accent A LOOOOT of homework
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: MUS360 best class I've ever taken. Super engaging lectures and extremely fun assignments. The tests were cake online and in person as everything you might need are in the slides provided on Canvas. Extra credit opportunities are available as well. The class average was like a 95. 100% recommend.

Currently taking MUS360 @ University of Oregon Winter'24. He's not clear about pop quiz grading (says they don't count for grade but then says lowest is dropped), punished entire class for some students using ChatGPT on a take home exam and made all exams in person in the middle of the term, takes forever to grade, goes super fast during lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallmark is a fabulous music history teacher. His lectures are clear and the tests reflect exactly what he talks about. Quizzes are easy if you do the homework. Homework can be reading heavy at times. He is funny and caring, and gives tons of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallmark is one of the best professors in the music department at Southern Methodist University. He is open minded and provides students with a tremendous amount of knowledge. His courses can be challenging if you do not do the required work, but they are mind expanding. I highly recommend Dr. Wallmarks courses.

Be ready to listen! The large majority of test material comes from lecture. Take notes on stuff beyond what his slides say - he'll post his slides for you to access before the tests. Listenings are taken from pretty obvious sections of pieces, so don't worry to much about that. There is a lot of discussion during class. Overall, this class was fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everything the wrong. She took a leave for a known reason and never should have been allowed back. Completely not able to do her job and your grade will suffer for it.

While most of the reviews on here bash her, it is a effort and communication issue for most. Accounting is not an easy class, but it was more than doable with the resources she provided. She curved the exams, was extremely helpful during office hours, and truly cared for her students.

She might be the worst Professor at this university, and to be quite honest, I'm not sure how she still has a job. Different/trick wording on assignments, tests worth 70% of your grade, including nuanced material barely talked about, unhelpful office hours, an insignificantly small curve, and terrible lectures. Absolute nightmare, DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice lady, but lacks any ability to teach accounting concepts, often times chatgpt would explain the concepts much more clearly. She also will word every question on exams in a specific way to trick you. No curve, no dropping tests or homeworks. Just an Accounting raw dog. Just take Eric Marrs.
She should not be allowed to teach.

very sweet person not a good prof tho. she is extremely caring and wants you to do well but she can't explain things very well. She was a 4000 class prof but was so bad smu took all her sections away except for one section of 2301 try and take another prof

Shes honestly so nice and definitely cares about her students and loves the material she just lectures very quickly and isn't very good and teaching at all. I had to learn everything on my own even after paying attention in class.

After finding out why Wilson was so disorganized and dishelved every class, it all makes sense. Due to that, it is not fair the grades we received. Avoid her at all costs. Thankfully Cox found out about this issue and removed her from a majority of the classes she was initially teaching, but somehow she still holds a position with the university..

Do not take this professor. Wait until you have the opportunity for the alternative professor. Hardest course at SMU by far not because of the material, but because of the lack of teaching. Class average for tests is usually in the 60s, mind you exams are all you're graded on in the class. Do good on exams or fail basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wilson was awful. She was disorganized, a bad lecturer, and the worst professor I've ever taken. Her "lectures" are her copying/pasting her notes. The homework is on Pearson and completely useless. Her exams are somewhat like her practices, but if you take this class, don't expect her lectures to help at all. No curve, but extra credit.

Wendy is a sweet person but she's not very passionate about the subject. She'll teach you the process in class, but she won't make it interesting. With that said, intermediate 2 is a hard class but the tests have a cheat sheet and she provides a very helpful practice test to study off of. You can also earn up to 2 points extra credit.

There's a fine line between making mistakes that comes w being human vs recklessly disregarding a Summer class.. I get that ending class early might make you likable but when you're making mistakes on end + unnecessarily rushing to get us out :/

Could've flown on Spirit w those $5k to all 7 continents instead & they would've paid me more mind

Worst professor I have ever had at SMU Cox. Not once taken a class and complained about the professor, but Wendy Wilson is one of a kind. If you have to take a class with her do everything you can to get out. Not worth the time, and definitely not worth the money. Horrible at the art of teaching, should be removed from Cox.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she literally does not teach, just makes you watch videos, constantly contradicting herself, and she makes so many mistakes its an embarassment. does not deserve her position as professor when she does nothing
Her snarky comments to people who disagree with her are unprofessional DO NOT TAKE (she's a bad teacher). I couldn't wait for her class to end.

Awful teaching style. She used videos to teach and then worked through problems in-class. The problem is she was bad at posting these videos early so sometimes they would pop-up the day before class. The videos had quizzes attached to them so it was really annoying when I didn't know when the vids would be posted.

I have a serious bone to pick with Wendy. The class format is watching lecture videos at home and doing examples in class. There is limited in-person instruction. She doesn't explain the in-class examples & often makes mistakes, confusing her students even more. Her canvas grades are incorrectly inflated, which is EXTREMELY misleading.

Overall the class structure is helpful with concepts mostly taught in videos outside of class and problems worked through in class. Homeworks were easy. Quizzes were also mostly easy. If you try on the discussions you will get a good grade on them. Exams were challenging due to the amount of rules but not impossible. If you try you'll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Pros:
The videos make what she does in class make sense
The classtime is used effectively to do problems 
Exams, HW, and Discussion Posts are very doable

Cons:
Before Class Quizzes are sometimes hard
The class format (videos at home, problems in class) may not be for everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: watch the videos before doing quizzes. Study the problems & make good notes for test. Her test are slightly different from the material you learn in class so make sure you read the powerpoints too. Class is short because she wants to get you out of class early It would be more useful to use all the class time to work on problems to excel in exam.

This is my 2nd course with her. You must attend class and follow along to do well. She provides ample opportunity to improve your grade. Her only downfall is that she does every example for you so there is not a lot of in class practice. But, she knows her stuff and you learn a lot. Her before class quizzes are crucial so watch the videos and focus

This class was terrible for me. Very long tests that I never finished. Confusing explanations that left me spending hours on the homework without understanding what I was doing. Avoid at all costs, hardest Cox class taken BY FAR
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I only learned on my own from studying, in class she just read off example problems and provided very little to no reasoning behind what she was doing. I attended class everyday and was still not able to learn besides on my own, studying and re learning the material myself. It was an Awful experience and discouraged me from pursuing my CPA

AVOID
other professors are just easier

Not my preferred teaching style. She has example packets with one example of each type of question for each of the chapters that she works through in front of you in class. Before class quizzes on her short videos on chapters. You can use the textbook or her videos (best to use both). Just felt like one of those classes you just have to get through

This class is difficult as it is. Wilson genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. She gives really good notes, but if you don't pay attention and study, you won't do well on the test. Always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I hate this class with a passion. The topics are useful for finance majors but the level of detail is extremely high. I study 30hours for each exam and I'm barely making a C in the class. I want to withdraw but I don't want to be this miserable again next semester.

Corona class** Tax accounting is hard. There's so many small details that you need to know. Wilson doesn't always include these details in her packets, she'll mention them once and expect you to know them. Write down every word she says. Lots of examples in class but she struggles to clearly state the brig idea. That's probably the hardest part

Prof Wilson was great at teaching tax, one of the reasons I chose it! She offered extra credit and always answered questions. Her lectures were amazing and it was pretty easy to transition to online classes. Really cares about her students, very approachable!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pros: amazing office hour help, useful practice problems in class, organized curriculum, fair grader Cons: fast-paced, several hw probs have mistakes, not enough time during tests Tips: Go to office hours to clarify concepts (very important!!), do all the hw, re-do notes before quizzes, do practice exams, be mindful of test time
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily the hardest class I've taken in Cox. She seems very nice in class but is a little standoffish in office hours. Class doesn't seem too bad till you hit the tests, which are impossible and way too hard. Everyone ends up barely scraping by with a C or a D+. I wish there had been another professor available.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class benefits those who will be working in public accounting i.e., Income Tax Provision audit. To be honest, not much of this material will be on FAR exam. Prof. Wilson definitely teaches you more than what you need to know for FAR. Her classes are always challenging but doable if you do the practice problems in the note and sample exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Wilson is a great person and a good professor. The class is not easy and, speaking honestly, I didn't do great, but none of that is on Wilson. She teaches fast, but uses lots of examples. So if you fall behind you might have trouble catching up, but if you can keep up you should get a great grade.

Overall, one of the better and nicer accounting professors. If you go to every class, you'll still need to study a lot on your own in order to do well on the tests. Her class examples are relevant and helpful as are practice tests, but you need to read the book and do book problems or you won't do well on the exams. Overall still a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Intermediate 2 is one of the hardest classes in Cox, but Wendy does a good job with it, lots of class examples, open book quizzes, etc and she is very nice. Attendance isn't taken but you absolutely need to go to every class - not the type of material/tests you can learn on your own

Intermediate 2 is a hard class but Wilson is one of those professor that actually cares. Very accessible outside of class and is a fair professor. Her practice exams help a lot with taking the real thing. Hard content, great professor

Lectures are not very helpful. Wilson moves so quickly through the material that it is hard to get a firm grasp of the chapter at hand. The class is not impossible to get an A in, but Wilson does not do a very good job of giving students a strong foundation in Accounting.

Wilson did not do a good job teaching the material, she focused so much on the small details and completely forgot to explain the big picture, so then when you saw something you hadn't seen before on a test it made it very difficult to problem solve your way to the answer. She's nice, but her teaching sucks.

Had her for ACCT 2301 and she did a great job. Much of class time was spent doing exercises that were a big help. She makes a practice exam before every test and it helps a lot with test prep. Exams are hard but if you study you can make A's. Overall she teaches the class very well and it is not hard to make a good grade if you put in the work.

ACCT3312 is the most challenging accounting class at SMU. If you want to learn and prepare for the CPA exam, definitely take Prof. Wilson's class. She will go in deep about important topics in the book. Read the study materials, rework homework assignments on paper and read sample exams carefully. Final exam is optional.
Great teacher and is very very helpful. Tests are pretty easy and curves a lot!
No Comments

Honestly one of the best professors i've had and a great guy. Definitely a hard class but I learned so much. He is a very tough grader but if you put in the work and the effort you will succeed. He shows you the respect that you show him, if you show concern/need help he will help you. Very clear on how to succeed, lectures are very important.
Very nice professor with easy-to-follow lectures. You do need to read a lot for his class. He is very knowledgable about Russia and enjoys his job.

reviews.comment: Class was rough but doable. The quizzes were based on assigned articles. I hope you can retain information well because it's based on memory. But the Professor lets you know when the quiz is, and you break the articles down in class. Exams are cake if you study and participate in class. He's not bad; some students shouldn't be in college, it seems.

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken. 8am class is challenging as it is, but the professor made it even worse with his condescending and rude attitude toward students. He lectures the entire time, pushes his own political agenda, and allows little to no room for diverse perspectives. I strongly recommend avoiding this class.

knowledgeable. separate quizzes for readings and in-class lectures. lectures are long and boring, but it's the class material not him. suffered from miscommunication on the first exam. will give you a blank stare in class if he doesn't like your answer or finds it uninteresting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wegren is a super nice guy and really likes what he teaches. The issue is that you are graded by 7 things and its hard to get great grades on them. reviews.comment: I know his ratings make him out to be the worst guy, but he's really not. Pay attention, SIT FRONT ROW, and he will like you. Have 4 quizzes which are dense based on readings, but the midterm is not the worse, the final is not cumulative, and he makes dumb jokes and tries to keep the class engaged. For an 8am, it's not bad. Very smart professor too

3 quizzes, attendance, midterm, and final exam. Definitely an unforgiving professor at times. Loathes giving extra credit opps. Lectures are easy to follow with good info and tests/quizzes aren't difficult content-wise, but harshly graded. MUST DO ARTICLE READING OR YOU WILL FAIL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgable about Russia/post communist countries (his area of expertise). My class was graded only on a midterm, paper, and a final, which can be good or bad. He had very good personal anecdotes/perspectives, but it seemed like he was a little reluctant to share them sometimes. Not a warm & fuzzy character, but I learned a lot.
He knows a lot about the topic he is teaching; however, he is very critical when it comes to his feedback and even degrades others' questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not someone who gets on RMP to whine. I still pulled an A- in this miserable class. Wegren is unforgivingly hard, technologically incompetent, and just flat out mean. Furthermore, he does not teach from the book *or* the supplemental readings - the only thing that matters is what he says in class. He is rude, egotistical, and unhelpful to students.

He explain this subjects in a greats ways, you will learn a lot. But he is mean when he is not in the mood! and will give you hard time with grading your papers and exams!!! reviews.comment: Don't let Mr. Wegren discourage you from studying international Studies. There are 5 assignments: 2 quizzes, 2 exams, and 1 essay. I hope Stephen falls into a poop puddle. He is the most uncaring professor at SMU. He treats every class like he hates his job. bestie, if you hate your life just say so. I'm reluctant to continue with my Intl. Studis major because I simply do not want to nor can work with him. There is absolute no leeway nor is there any grace with grading.

The most condescending person who does not care if you want to learn material. Pushes whatever agenda he wants and just watched him tell someone they couldn't make up work they that missed while they were having life saving surgery. Overall this man does not enjoy his job and takes it out on his students grades.

reviews.comment: Dr. Wegren is a very knowledgeable and intelligent professor. I really enjoyed his class, but hes a really hard grader that dosent tell students whats hes looking for in papers. Kinda annoying, but a really fun class nonetheless.

Hes great. I think hes one of the professors that makes you really think critically, rather than ramble off from the readings. Yes his grading is harsh, but gives tons of opportunities for extra credit. Probably the only class where you can passionately demonstrate your thinking on current issues

The class material was easy, but he gave confusing instructions for papers and was not understanding when the students did not complete the assignment correctly. If you do need to take his class, make sure you're COMPLETELY clear on what the instructions are and ask questions to double-check.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Participation heavy class, however, he gives limited opportunities to participate. He doesn't give good or clear feedback on work submitted. And doesn't provide a clear rubric when grading papers.

reviews.comment: He is hard and you have to work to get an A. Having said that, participation is key to get a great grade since it covers nearly 40% of your overall grading criteria. Lots of opportunities for bonus credit (that helped me bump my grade from a B to an A-). Hilarious lectures, but can get dry at times.

Wegren is completely technologically illiterate and does everything via weekly emails. His class is lecture based, but reading the books outside of class is a huge help. Big on attendance and participation- if you speak in class, he'll like you but that won't help on papers/tests which are anonymous. Sometimes interesting, but can get dry quickly
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wegren's senior seminar is fun and not too big of a burden on your class schedule. It is a weekly discussion meeting on readings and then one big final paper at the end of the year. reviews.comment: extremely witty and hilarious. cracks me up in his lectures. best professor i have ever had. inspired me to push my limits and be the best i can be

I have mixed feelings about Professor Wegren. I genuinely enjoyed his class, and he's very knowledgeable on what he teaches. I participated often and he seemed receptive to my comments. However, I was never able to figure out his grading. Even after meeting with him, I received terrible grades on papers, even though writing is my strongest skill.

reviews.comment: Tough grader but if you talk to him he will help a lot. Very respected man and loves to crack jokes. Very reasonable professor.

reviews.comment: This class can be pretty brutal, DEFINITELY do the readings and be prepared for the discussions (participation earns you BIG points with him).
