I actually came into this class enjoying his sense of humor and his straightforward expectations. However, when I would answer questions he would shoot me down. After awhile it gets pretty discouraging. A teachers job is to foster growth and provide a safe community for discussion, no matter personal opinion.

Some are saying that he is a bad professor. He's not. He has a dry sense of humor, so don't take it personally. He's not being mean, moreover, just strict. He knows what he wants and as long as you follow what he wants, you'll do fine. Read, come to class prepared. You're adults, not children.
DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HIS CLASSES. His expectations are ridiculous and he is not helpful at all.

Coming into a class like this with no prior knowledge of communist Europe was a problem. I took this as a CF as outside of anthropology(its my major) they are mostly history and English. He has HORRIBLE handwriting and would actually refuse to read what his notes said aloud. He talks quickly jumps around and you can't read what the board says.

His class is very interesting if you like intl politics BUT his attitude is not the greatest. I hardly participated which was 40% of the grade, even when I knew the answers a lot of times because he was so aggressive and focused on those that had the right answers. He is not a professor that you can create a lasting relationship with. Intimidating!

He is honestly the worst teacher I've ever had. He claims his class is discussion based, however, if he disagrees with your opinion he will shoot you down and tell you that you are dumb without reason. He is demeaning and rude towards his students. He also grades very unfairly. DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER!

A lot of people feel Wegren is condescending and rude, but they simply mistake his dry humor and cynicism. He is demanding as a professor and will let you know if your assertions are blatantly incorrect but he is very knowledgeable in his subject and really fun if you put fourth effort in his cass
Shoots down students. Makes them cry. If you don't agree, be ready to feel degraded and ignorant.
There is a lot of information in the class which makes it hard to study for tests.  He does know a lot about the subject and you learn a lot of interesting facts.

He's great. You just have to come to class & follow instructions and you'll be fine. It's not really anything extra than you should be doing anyway. He's also SO knowledgeable and passionate about the subject that it makes me want to strive to do better. He is over-qualified to be teaching undergrad and I feel fortunate to hear some of his wisdom.

Only lazy idiots would think this guy is mean.  However, he does not put up with nonsense.  That's not to say class is a dictatorship.  So long as people are engaging in class and read on the subject, he is fun and happy to help with anything, its when you have not read or dont show up that he gets down on you.  He's great if you are interested

DO NOT SIGN UO FOR HIS CLASS!!!! This is a warning, do not take Wegren's class. He is extremely adversarial to students and has a horrible attitude towards people who are not in the PLSC program, so much that I question how it can be possible that he is still teaching. He is the kind of professor that makes things difficult just because.
Beware. This guy is a classic narcissist.

You either hate him or love him. I think he's great, he knows a great deal about Russia and eastern europe. Readings for his class are a must, but even if you follow the notes you will do fine in his classes. He takes some getting used to but when and if y

A lot of people don't like him because he's so liberal.  Wegren does however listen to everyone's opinions and is a huge fan of group discussion.  If you're an idiot who doesn't do the work, he will embarrass you.  I really enjoyed him.
Not the easiet; but very knowledgable and loves Russian Politics. Tests are a bit hard, no curves. Take Attendance.

Avoid this man. His class is one of the harder ones, but what makes it terrible is professor. He is temperamental, rude and condescending. Furthermore, his presentation is boring and the lectures seem irrelevant, as the midterm and final did not correspond well with them and are worth 70% of the grade.

This class is tough, but if you adequately prepare, you'll do fine on exams.  Really interesting class - he loves his Russian politics!  Responds right away to email.  Overall nice guy.  Some people don't like him b/c you have to work hard, others think he's a communist (which is not true at all).

Prof Wellman has really interesting lectures and listens to students and their concerns. There is A LOT of reading and participation is very important, you have to write an essay for every class you miss. She's really understanding though, so as long as you listen and participate you're good. I literally bombed my presentation and still got an A.

reviews.comment:
Her lectures don't stay on track, and she's terrible at answering questions. She created a hostile environment, and I often 
 felt belittled. Would not recommend this class - seek other options.

I love Kathleen Wellman so much!! I had her for HIST 1322 and despite the fact that it was an honors course, I didn't find it difficult at all. The course was super interesting and Dr. Wellman is a pretty easy grader. Highly recommend!

Do not take this class unless you have lots of free time. I loved the content but hated the class. The amount of reading you will have to do is unreal. The assignments are very confusing to the point where no one in my class knew what we were supposed to do.

reviews.comment: Wellman lays out the class very clear for junior seminar, refuses to let you slack. She is very blunt and will tell you to drop the class if you need to. On one hand she was SO difficult with required reading for every class, having to write an whole essay if you miss one (1) class, a paper and/or presentation basically every week, and harsh grading. BUTTT on the other hand the material so wildly fascinating that it was kinda worth it? Take her class with caution lol

reviews.comment: If you have previous knowledge of the topics, then take the class. You will have a lot of reading...make sure to do it. She is very strict on participation so you can't be shy. Study for the tests, you will fail if you don't. She is also really funny and definitely is passionate.

reviews.comment: I loved having Wellman for my junior seminar. She laid out the class very clearly, so you couldn't push off all your work. reviews.comment: Prof. Wellman taught this class with Prof. Cogley. I enjoyed Cogley's part of the class way more because his lectures were organized. Does not like when you disagree with her ideas

reviews.comment: Wellman is great. If you even skim the readings & participate in class you will do very well. The final is a paper, so its easy to ace if you take the time. She is extremely intelligent and actually pretty laid back contrary to other reviews. She is stoic, but understands/ can be funny. Her women's history class was one of my favorite classes!

Be prepared to speak up in class for participation grade. She is a very caring professor. I was struggled to keep up with her class because of the extensive reading and writing assignments. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is wonderful!

I only took this class for a history credit. And I absolutely hated it. Professor Wellman is not nice. We wrote 2 different essays and when they weren't what she wanted she would get mad at the students instead of taking the blame for herself. Very boring class, don't waste your time. I would never take her again.

Dr. Wellman is actually in the History department and not the Women's Studies department.  She is an absolutely wonderful professor.  She is demanding but at the same time is very helpful and very engaging. Definitely take her class if you are looking for an interesting, stimulating, and fun history credit in European history.

Dr. Wellman is a fabulous professor.  It is clear that Dr. Wellman has a sincere interest in her studies as well as her students.  Everyday she attempts to engage her students in a vibrant conversation versus a mundane lecture.  She is very helpful! Be ready to write papers, but she is fair in grading!!!
Her Queens and Mistresses class is really interesting (esp. for women) and it is relaxed as well. However, you must be prepared to write almost a paper a week for it.

I had suffered a severe medical condition while I was in her course. I was meet with apathy. Her lectures were boring and I didn't get anything but headaches from her class. She is not genuine nor a true pedagogue.

This was the most infuriating class. reviews.comment: Dr. Whitelaw is one of the best professors out there. She is so kind, gives very specific feedback to help you improve, and lets you resubmit revised versions of your writing. She cares about your learning and always asks how else she can help. She is very supportive and attends every performance she can. She is incredibly humble and caring.

Dr. Whitelaw. I can't begin to describe the outrageous ineptitude and lack of organization this professor brought to the classroom, at the expense of our education, but the other reviews here give an accurate sample. I've heard that she teaches well at the graduate level, but if you're taking the summaries I would hold out for Anderson or Kupfer.

I don't understand the other reviews on Dr. Whitelaw. They sound like a bunch of spoiled HP kids who have never taken a standard college course. This was probably my favorite professor I've ever had. She is engaging, kind, and you can tell she is passionate about teaching. Challenging but fair.I looked forward to her class and will miss her!

Dr Whitelaw is a terrible professor that should not be allowed to teach in any capacity. Terrible Professor, group quizzes

I would rather memorize a shampoo bottle than read from the text.

reviews.comment: As a transfer, I hoped this would've been an easy class. Professor Whitehead was so nice, but tough. This class gave me a lot of stress and I feel like I worked harder to deserve more than a B. Make sure to ask specific questions in your conferences and use the writing center. Overall, she is a great professor to have!

Professor Whitehead is a nice and funny person. Her class is not bad but she is a tough grader when it comes to papers. There's 3 papers and weekly discussion for the class. Take her if you need a WRTR credit.

Professor Whitehead was definitely tough at first, but over the course of the semester she has warmed up to my class. We had three papers, which she graded quite harshly, however she is super sweet and quite funny. If you need to fulfill a WRTR you should consider taking her. Not a lot of homework and she is willing to help you if you ask questions

This class is really helpful in developing your writing if you are willing to put in the work. Professor Whitehead is known for being blunt and sometimes harsh when it comes to critic however it comes from a place of wanting to see real improvement. She is also funny and does not want to waste time in class.

She does not teach anything!!!!!! There is not one thing I learned in her class. She just talks about random things and assigns papers. horrible!!!!!!!!! you will not learn anything and she grades very hard on papers. DO NOT TAKE HER.

reviews.comment: Makes class interactive with group activities. Have a lot ability to create your own narrative for essays. Gives good feedback on essay improvement.

Professor Whitehead is an incredibly difficult grader (thinks a B- is a good grade) on the four essays that make up your total grade, but other than that the class is pretty basic and the homework is annoying but not bad. Class time is super boring, but that honestly isn't her fault. She is a good human and will give help when you ask.

AMAZING!! Honestly those who are giving negative feedback most likely did not pay attention or didn't take her corrections. Catrina is just awesome. I took her for Evolution and she did a fantastic job. The course is difficult, requires some memorization, but it's nothing out of reach. She's also very personable, encourages tons of questions, listens super well. She's a reasonable grader and will help you do well.

Professor Whitley is an expert in her field without a doubt. She knows what she's talking about. That being said, expertise in the field doesn't translate to being a good teacher. He has many dedications to students. Class work was hard but English has very hard understanding to me so he is a very good teacher. a Always helping me. Must take him if your English is poor.
He is an awesome teacher .. show passion to the class and he will do his best to help you!!
He is strict and hard to get a good grade :(
He's a hard teacher.
Sorry, no help at all. This semester, I  received all the scores higher than A- but the grade for this course is C+. It's the most unlucky thing for me to choose her
She will grade you base on nothing other than her personal preference. She likes to give high grades to those students who are flatterers

Pf. Wheeler-Matlock is very into in class activities and discussions, so attendance is pretty important, especially if you want to see the themes she wants you to highlight in your papers. She gives straightforward feedback in her conferences and is very nice.
Do your best to impress her with something other than English because she grades you based on her opinion of you instead of your content.

Professor Willis is one of, if not the most fair, test grader in the entire ME department. For heat and mass, his assignments were projects rather than actual homework, which helped with application and understanding of the material without piling on a ton of work. The tests were difficult but if you actually understand the material, you're good.

Professor Willis is one of SMU's best professors. He is a difficult teacher but only because He expects the most out of his students. You have to pay attention, take notes, and ask questions. Lil challenging but it makes sense. He did a good job and was always smiling so I rocked with him

Great lecturer and a fair (but strict) grader. No final exam; we had a final project. Loved taking this class.  Readily available outside of class for office hours and to answer questions on the homework. Attendance not mandatory but necessary to understand the content.

reviews.comment: Dr. Willis delivers clear lectures, making tough concepts accessible. Homework is the key to success, preparing you for tests and future classes. His fair grading and genuine care for student success shine through. Office hours are invaluable, showing his dedication to helping all students succeed.
Don't know why my first review got deleted. He is the nightmare that a freshman might have to suffer from. He is just terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Willis complicates everything for no reason. Very harsh on grading, and barely gives any partial credit. Avoid him if you can.

Does not help students transfer learning from lecture to exams, his equation sheets are more confusing than the  problems themselves and don't include all the equations you need. you need to study like a maniac to pass, as his exams are super hard and he is happy for the class average in an exam to be 50%, good luck

Dr. Willis was amazing; his class is definitely hard, and I was struggling a lot at first (since I hadn't taken physics before) but his class PREPARES you. I'm in statics (the second ME class) and physics M right now, and they are a bit of a breeze because of his class. Go to his office hours!! He genuinely wants everyone to succeed.

Dr. Willis had everything that I wanted in the engineering program. The homework and exams were very difficult for an intro class, but he drilled us to do things the right way. We had strict formatting requirements for weekly homework, and he graded with a fine-toothed comb. I am grateful for this, since I pay more attention to my work now.

Willis a good professor for ME3332. The content of this lecture is pretty hard and his slides do a good job at explaining these hard concepts. He doesn't assign hw, he just posts a list of suggested practice problems. My advice, do every single one of them to do well. Use Chegg to check your solution. The tests were pretty hard, prepare well for it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Willis is one of my all-time favorite professors. He is organized with his lectures, is proficient in the subject of Heat and Mass and takes his time to make sure the class is understanding the material. DO NOT USE CHEGG for this class, or you will be penalized. There was one homework problem assigned a week and 4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Incredibly hard class. Great lectures, but the homework is insanely hard. I would go to tutoring every week for those assignments and multiple tutors have trouble figuring out the answers. Took weeks to grade with little feedback. Even though this class is an intro course, it definitely does not feel like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His class is very difficult, but it prepares you well for what to expect with engineering. There is weekly homework, but most of your grade is based on tests. The tests are open book, and the textbook is your bible. I would definitely take a class with Willis again.

For an intro course, he takes the class pretty seriously, but I definitely learned a lot in his class. The tests are difficult but open book. I definitely feel more prepared for some of the more difficult engineering courses. Also, the textbook he chose has a lot of really good conversions and concepts. Keep it if you can.

He is an awesome professor, a lot of people struggle because it is a tough class, but that's expected when you are an engineering major. It is a lot of physics and the class covers a wide range of topics. Open book tests are a big plus. Overall he was a great prof
His lectures are decent, and the tests are hard but not too bad. Always allowed to use textbook during exams.

The class is difficult and broad range of topics are covered. The course material is like applied physics, and grades are not curved, nor is extra credit given. As for the professor, he is quite knowledgeable of the material, and conveys it well. If you have a question about the material (or a tangent to it) he is more than willing to help you.
You think you're doing well, wait until you see his tests.
Willis's lectures are easy to follow and you think you understand until you get to the homework. The tests are impossible and the material covered in class does not prepare you well for the tests.

Good clear, interesting lectures but impossibly difficult.  Homework every week that does not count for much overall.  Tests are a mashup of everything possible so you better study very hard if you want a B or A.  Median grade is a C and since most people drop out you better hope your grade is good because everything is relative. Top half gets C
avg test grade for class is a 50 but theres no curve. smart guy but not great at explaining it in a way that is easy to understand.
Willis' test are impossible, he grades with an iron fist, and he is not very helpful in office hours.

Willis is a great teacher, explains things well, and cares about his students and their learning.  He is very tough though.  His tests challenge you to apply information from class and HW in new, difficult ways. It is definitely a weed-out course for ME.  Our class average before the final was a 72.5 and I believe he curved it a little bit.
Awesome teacher--very helpful.  The class is hard, but Willis will help you with any questions.  Do practice problems, go to class, and stay on top of your work.

This professor is a brilliant man, but does not recognize that students are not as invested in this specific material to get a PhD, nor do we have that amount of knowledge. It's a 3000 level class, and he should treat it as such. Extremely hard, A LOT of homework, and very strict grader. Average on exams - 50.
Be prepared for lab presentations and be as informative and boring as possible. He's uptight but you'll thank him later.
He was a really hard grader but if you went to his office hours he would help you on the homework. He was a nice guy and really prepares you for upper level engineering courses.

I hated him when I had him (during the time I was failing, honestly he was being fair).  He was willing to work with me and answer any of my questions.  I ended up passing.  The class was hard but he really does prepare people for engineering.

He is a nice guy and his lectures are genuinely interesting. A pretty harsh grader though. Especially for the ME lab! It's ridiculous. To forewarn you, do lots of practice problems from the book on your own. Make sure you understand each topic. He makes it look easy but his examples in class are a little too simple. Tests are harder.

Don't let first impressions get to you.  He is a very hard grader and he makes the course 4 times harder than it needs to be.  The hardness is unnecessary.  However, he does help you when you ask him questions and he does answer his emails.  His test are scary and have unfair grading.
HWs can be hard so just get help if you need and you'll be fine. His exams always have one curveball but are otherwise easy
The class skims over a lot of material but it gives a head start into the specific courses. Willis checks his email often and is very helpful and clear with his communication.

Excellent teacher. His exams and HW's are hard! For HW either do in study groups or go to his office. If you can do the HW, exams should be SUPER easy. Time is short for exams. He is a nice guy. His lectures are super important! Sit in front row if you want to make an A! :) Definitely recommended!
extremely helpful and thoroughly enjoys explaining things and conversation. grades the homework extremely harsh but the class isn't too hard so it's not that big of a deal
I didn't know anything about ME going into his class. He explained everything so that anyone could understand and is a very nice guy! I really liked him/his class!
No Comments
hes a pretty good teacher.  he will explain the stuff and he is willing to help his students.
I should not know a professor's religion based on how he lectures in class, nor their politics, personal opinions, etc. Totally not appropriate for class.
Strongest lecturer at SMU. Could probably be at a top university giving the lectures he gives. Articulate and funny, and not at all partisan. A blessing to SMU's political science department
Definitely has a Christian bias but a very strong lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a joke and is clearly here for a free paycheck. Didn't teach anything but rambled a lot. You learn nothing but the A your prize for getting through.

solid professor, can be a little bit of a tough grader, but genuinely a nice guy. no real complaints with the class.

participate / show him you care and you'll get at least a B
Tests are literally ridiculous. Spends class time on tangents. Doesn't provide useful feedback. Unapproachable and dismissive. Avoid this class for your own sanity.
Professor is a joke. Speaks in jargon, expects us to decode. Doesn't care about student success. Arrogant and unhelpful. Avoid this class if you value your GPA.

Hated his class and him, grading was unfair, lectures are horrible, questions are designed to trick you, and his egomaniac persona is nausea-inducing to put up with all week long. Can't be done with him fast enough.

terrible lecturer, unorganized, and his personality can go from "understanding" or "helpful" to pissed off in no time flat if you ask too many or the wrong kind of questions, he designs the course to ensure you don't get an A through trick questions, frankly, not all that smart of a guy of just constantly unprepared for classes, hard to tell

Worse professor I have ever had. Tests were impossible even if you read, multiple right answers, and he constantly contradicts himself so you never know which right answer to choose at any given time.  He's so full of himself that he doesn't even prepare for class, and it shows.

My grade was due to my own lack of effort, but if you make sure to read the textbook and pay attention during the lecture, it shouldn't be difficult to finish the class with a B+ or A-. He was very understanding of my circumstances and helpful. His lectures are also very engaging he knows what he's talking about. Easily approachable.

I 100% recommend Professor Wilson, what an awesome man and teacher! He really cares about what he is teaching and makes it so fun and enjoyable. He's funny, he's smart, and he doesn't always stick to the exact lecture, he veers off into other talks of politics that make it interesting and engaging. I absolutely LOVE this class and LOVE him.

Wilson is a really nice and charismatic professor who does a great job of simplifying readings down to manageable bits. The test can be challenging; he's a guy who really looks for key words. If you don't have the crucial words you're out of luck. Lectures tend to be interesting. Definitely a good among PLSC professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wilson is able to break down convoluted/complicated topics and make them accessible to students. His lectures are clear and easy to follow -- 100% of test information comes from in class commentary on the texts. He is fair and impartial in class. Genuinely one of the most impressive and engaging teachers I have ever had. Highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! So dynamic and passionate. His class is straightforward and he keeps it pretty interesting and has a great sense of humor. There are readings for most classes and you can skim most of them and if you do read most take well under an hour. His tests are very fair and if you put a little effort into studying you will do well

Literally my favorite professor ever. If you are looking for an interesting and easy intro PLSC class this is the one. Tests are straight from lectures and aren't cumulative, just take good notes in class. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Readings aren't bad and the few pop quizzes he gives aren't tricky. Really great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about theology, good lecturer and fair grader. Beware, though, the tests answers are pulled STRAIGHT from the readings so study readings, NOT lecture. Has random pop quizzes about the previous night's readings but not very in depth quizzes, just things like "Name one religion X uses as an example". Few things make up final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: best. class. ever.

I love Professor Wilson. I put very little out of class effort into his classes and still did well. You do have random pop quizzes but as long as you skim the reading before class you'll be fine. His lectures are amazing and he's always willing to go the extra mile to explain things- you just have to ask. His tests aren't bad as long as you study.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hated his class, largely because his test grading was unfair. His tests are tricky and are designed to trick you and make getting an A in this class VERY hard. Seems somewhat pompous and full of it, and not overly approachable.

Wilson was super interesting and super intelligent; really knew his stuff.  his tests weren't too difficult if you studied and took notes in class.  gives pop quizzes, but readings aren't too long so do your reading before class.  great lecturer.  make sure you pay attention in class and make a solid effort and you can get a decent grade
Awesome professor! Loved his lectures and his tests were very straight forward.
Great lecturer, but test are hard, lots of right answers and even if you get 34 answers in multiple choice questions right you will still get the problem wrong.  Good teacher, bad tester. Hard test.

Favorite professor at SMU so far. Professor Wilson is clear in his lectures and is hilarious. His class is interesting. Do the reading because there are pop quizzes throughout the semester. His tests are easy if you take good notes and study them before the exam. That being said as long as you go to class and take good notes, this class is easy.

Professor Wilson is amazing! I've taken him for multiple classes and each class has been worth it. His teaching style is wonderful because he really takes time to explain things until everyone understands it. Also, he's one of the most understanding and nicest professors I've ever had at SMU. Classes aren't hard as long as you do the reading!
Tests are hard, however, I have found my favorite teacher. He articulately gives you all of the information and tries to make the class fun for you. Take him!

What's there to say about Prof. Wilson? Just a great guy. Class is really easy, quizzes are easy, tests are easy. I barely read and nailed down an A. The final isn't cumulative, so there's hardly even a final. This guy is really funny. If you're taking 1320 and you don't pick him, you are a clown. I would literally take any class this man teaches.

An incredible professor! Very articulate, the class (Religion and Politics) is incredibly interesting. Worth pointing out he is the College Advisor for College Republicans, but it doesn't affect how he teaches.

Wilson is awesome. He is a great orator, and enthusiastic about his work. The quizzes are over basic concepts present in the readings, and the tests are based entirely off the notes you take in class. If you want a great intro course to Poli Sci, this is your guy.

A very very good teacher. His tests are pretty tricky, but if you study your notes from class you will do fine. DO YOUR READING. There are 5 pop quizzes during the semester. Prof Wilson is very kind, and can be very funny. Conservative as well.

I have taken two of Wilson's classes so far, he is great!  Attendance is a must, but if you read the stuff and study a bit, getting an A is possible.  The best part is he makes his classes interesting and funny!

It's rewarding to do well in his class; I feel like I work for my grade, but it's interesting, not tedious, work. He's from Louisiana and uses a lot of how-La-does-it-differently/crazily, but that's cool with me because I'm from there too. We actually had a how-hard-it-is-to-adjust-to-SMU-life-and-Dallas-culture coversation. Take him; it's worth it

I love Prof Wilson! He is a genuinely nice guy who is interested in the subject he teaches and makes it very fun (he always has funny stories). VERY slow on grading which can be frustratingbut he's fair and this class is an A if you read and pay attention.

DO NOT TAKE HIS RELIGION AND POLITICS CLASS. IT WAS SO HARD. THE HARDEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. YOU WORK YOUR BUTT OFF FOR A C. EVERYONE AROUND ME IN THAT CLASS WAS DOING REALLY BAD AND WE WERE ALL A STUDENTS. I DONT KNO ABOUT HIS OTHER CLASSES. BUT IF YOUR NOT AN EXPERT IN THEOLOGY DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. HE DOESNT REALLY TRY TO HELP YOU TOO.

Seriously, take him.  He's hilarious - I laughed the entire semester.  I've really never met anyone who doesn't like Wilson.  He's slow on grading, but that's his only real fault. I took him for Political Dynamics, but I hear that all of his classes are good.

I have taken every single class this professor offers.  His exams aren't bad at all, and his sense of humor makes the class fun and enjoyable.  His area of study is public opinion, which is really interesting.  Take him - everybody loves him!
I went to office hours for help, rewrote my entire paper, and still didn't break an 85. Most unhelpful and disingenuous teacher. DO NOT take this class

Her class is very straight forward and always ends early. Minimal hw just complete drafts on time and show up to conferences. Grading is pretty much based on 3 essays. She is a bit of a tougher grader but always gives GREAT feedback, is caring and wants students to succeed. Started out getting B's but improved a lot towards end of the semester.

I think the essays were genuinely fun to write, especially when I heard what other classes were doing. She clearly outlines what she wants to see in an essay and will always point you in the right direction in office hours!
Easy A that's why we take her but no other skills or use to society.

Prof Wood is so sweet. She cares if you participate, so do the readings and engage. She gives really really helpful feedback on paper to prepare you for success. Take her, not a super tough grader and really nice in general

Professor Wood is so sweet and super understanding. I struggled with writing some of the papers in her class at first, but she would always help me and give me good feedback. She also always let us out of class early. I would recommend her class!
Saved me in both WRTR 1312 and 1313 best teacher ever!
So helpful during conferences and gives good feedback on essays. Not a ton of homework either, she's a great choice for 1312.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Incompetent instructor. Shows up late, unprepared. Plays favorites, ignores struggling students. Teaching style is archaic, no engagement. Waste of tuition.

Mrs. Wood is super nice and understanding, but she still grades relatively rough. We have a few assignments but its basically all essays, She's super helpful if you ask for help and overall a great teacher, i don't like anything ELA related but i really enjoyed her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Wood. She's super sweet and understanding about assignments. I love the way she structures class and I feel like she made my writing a lot better. She's super helpful during conferences! I would definitely take her again!!

One of the best profs I have had at SMU. She cares SO MUCH about making you a good writer for your future courses. Prof. Wood is so sweet and improved my writing quality so much. Go to her office hours if you have trouble. I feel like she is more lenient on grading essays if you go to her office hours, not just the individual meetings

Class is very straightforward and there are very few homework assignments outside of a few discussion preps. All you have to do is complete the essays and rough drafts on time, and, trust me, conference with her FOR EVERY ESSAY. She will help you out so much if you come prepared. Also very lenient with missing class due to sickness. Take her!!

Mrs. Wood is a great English teacher. She keeps her classes short and gives minimal homework for a wrtr class. She grades her papers mainly on if you are applying the concepts you worked on in class that unit, so be "teachable." Make sure you participate once each class, and bring a full draft to writer's conferences and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Wood was my favorite professor this semester! She is very caring and wants to see her student succeed! Make sure that you go to her conference because they will help your grade A LOT! She is also available outside of class/ scheduled office hours on Zoom when needed! She responds to emails quick, even if you email late!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Wood was such a sweet professor. Make sure you have the required books for the class because she uses them. Four papers and my only complaint is my high school taught me to write very differently than what she wants us to do. So that's a learning curve; you might not always get the grade you think you will.

I had an awful experience in her class. She is a very nice person and nice teacher but much more difficult than other wrtr professors. In comparison with other wrtr professors, her grading standard is a lot higher. She also will go back on back on something she tells you in a meeting by marking it on your draft even though she said to do it.
The absolute best WRTR prof. 100% take her if you can!!! No one in my class, myself included, has ever complained about her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Wood has been such a great teacher to have for WRTR. I wish I could take her again next semester! You have to show up to every class, but she always lets you out early. There are four papers throughout the semester and you have ample time to complete them. Definitely sign up for her if you can!!!!!!

Prof wood is not only a great professor but also such a kind person. Make sure you do at least one conference with her before each paper and she will tell you exactly what she wants and doesn't want. 10/10 recommend - I wish she was teaching 1313.

Professor Wood is an angel and I really enjoyed her class and learned a lot. She is helpful during conferences and explains clearly what she expects in your work. 4 papers total and no final. She lets us out early most days and no class during conference weeks. Participate in class and meet with her if you are confused or stuck. You'll be fine!
Definitely take her!!!!
very good wrtr teacher, she os very approachable and easy to find outside of class, very understanding and I always enjoyed her class
Best WRTR professor ever! She is so caring and helpful and really wants you to succeed. Super easy going. Ends class early. Would definitely recommend taking.

Professor Wood is the best professor at SMU. She is a fantastic teacher and great at giving feedback. She gives papers back quickly with clear and helpful tips. She rewards improvement and is very accessible. Wish I could take her for all of my English related courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I LOVED professor wood. She is one of my favorite teachers of ALL time. I wish I could take her again. She cares so much about her students and I always looked forward to her class. She is absolutely wonderful I cant express it enough. She is a generous grader and made writing numerous papers a great and easy process. 10000/10 TAKE HER!!!

Professor Wood is a solid choice for WRTR1312. Four papers throughout and she graded very fairly. Adhere to her feedback after your first paper and the rest of your grades will be fine. Shes very sweet and you can tell she cares about her students. Just do your work and put some effort into your essays and the class will be a breeze.

LOVE HER SO MUCH! She is probably one of the most effective teachers I've had at helping you write better. She does an excellent job of conveying material and made an 8 am class actually enjoyable. Most of all, she cares so much about her students and genuinely wants the best for all of us. She will get to know you in and out of the classroom, icon

Professor Wood is amazing, the best WRTR professor to take. Punctual, direct, and nice about feedback and working with students to get stuff done. Easy reading and clear deadlines. Attendance is mandatory, but if you COMMUNICATE, she will work with you. Definitely taking her again, definitely a homegirl I can RELY ON here on campus!

She is the sweetest professor that I have taken at SMU. She sets up the course to make sure you will succeed on your papers. She usually will give you a short reading to complete with easy discussion questions for most class days, and she will actually want your insight on what you think. Her class has made me not hate writing anymore.
I love her so much. She helped me become a much better writer, and it was the only class I looked forward to.

Very qualified professor who clearly knows her stuff. Class graded off of four essays, which account for a large majority of your final grade. Be careful as the class averages for these essays varied greatly throughout the semester. Tuesday Thursday classes always ended early, which was a nice plus. A solid choice for WRTR, but not a guaranteed A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She takes care of her students. When I was sick and slept through an 8 am lecture she allowed me to go to a later section. Extremely kind. Taking her again next semester for DISC1313

She is one of my favorite teachers at SMU. Really sweet and really cares about her students. Best teacher for DISC either for 1312 or 1313. Especially for 1313 which is supposed to be a reading class, we only had to read 1 100 page book which was awesome. Long papers but if you try your best she will notice and give you an A! Really worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took her for 1312 and 1313 because shes a great professor and is so sweet. She's not an easy grader, but there is always a good reason why. She really cares about her students and will help you. Take her if you can.

Great choice for DISC 1313. Doesn't give a lot of homework and will often let you out pretty early if everything has been accomplished for that day instead of dragging out classtime. Very reasonable and will help you with any questions or concerns you may have. Not a ridiculous grader as long as you have decent writing skills. Just put in effort.

While she may not be the easiest DISC professor she gives very good feedback and cares about how her students do. She wants her students to succeed and while giving a good reason if you get a grade on an assignment you don't want. If she sees that you are working hard, she'll reflect it on your grading. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Some people found Prof. Wood to be a tough grader but she gives good grades to people who show up to class, participate in basic conversations, and show that you're trying at least a little. She is so sweet and extremely helpful outside of class. Always lets you out of class early and is very lenient with extensions
Great teacher that cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her conferences are extremely helpful

I love her! If you conference with her she will tell you exactly what she does and doesn't like. She WANTS her students to succeed in her class. Never gives homework as well besides the assigned papers. Wish I could take her again next semester!
Very nice and helpful. Good with office hours. Someone hard grader. Basically, put effort in. You get what you receive!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Wood is awesome. Very organized, kind of a tough grader. Very helpful if you go into office hours. Class can be a tad boring, but I think it is the material not her.

Wood is such a sweet lady and her class is actually enjoyable! She gives very little homework and busy work and lets you out early every class. She does not hand out As but if you listen to her feedback you will be fine. She is super understanding and easy to talk to, I definitely recommend taking her class.

One of the sweetest professors at SMU. This is writing class, so papers are expected, but Professor Wood gives amazing feedback in conferences and cares about her students passing. Her course is over "Truth in Fiction" which keeps the material covered entertaining.
The best. SO nice and class is always engaging
Solid choice for 1313.  Such a nice person and cares a lot about her students.  4 papers (3-7 pages), no final.

It's a small class and it was just so awkward. She pretends to be caring but is actually so not. My favorite part of her class was watching the movie Big Fish because I didn't have to listen to her voice. It's not a bad class, I just don't particularly like her. She's very particular on grammar and gets emotional about the books.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: best professor at smu

loved this class. super sweet lady, definitely a good choice for 1312. minimal reading/homework. grade is from 4 short papers and a handful of grammar quizzes. go to the conferences and make an effort and you'll get a good grade
She is a great option for DISC 1312. MAKE SURE YOU CONFERENCE with her before you turn your papers in.  She will tell you what she likes and doesn't. Nice lady and easy to talk to!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: you HAVE to meet with her before each paper, she is extremely helpful on essays and clear expectations. the more you see her, the better your paper will be, and the better the grade. Not an "easy A" but if you try you will succeed. discussions and readings are interesting. if you participate in the class and show her you care she will help you
Really enjoyed the class and I normally don't like English classes. Professor Wood was a great teacher, and I definitely recommend having her if you can.

Professor Wood is the sweetest lady ever. She is super helpful and ends class early most days. If you go to class and go to the writing conferences you will be fine. There is a lot of reading but some people just skim the reading and pay attention to the discussions in classes.

Professor Wood is very nice, and her class is fun and pretty laid-back. She is there for you, both inside and outside of class and gives great feedback. Discussion is a big part of the class, so participation matters. She's not a super tough grader on papers and is helpful with revising/editing. She's awesome.

Angie is awesome, such a sweet and genuine lady that wants to help her students. Extremely easy grader if you're a decent writer and willing to try. Gives an extra credit assignment, reading outside of class is not that necessary and fairly infrequent, essays are generally easy topics.

Very helpful professor and just overall sweet lady, takes a genuine interest in her student's well-being and their success in the class. Always out of class early. No ridiculous reading requirements. Encourages discussion and diverse thoughts and ideas. Conferences are greatly helpful. Ask questions at any point on your paper and she's glad to help
She makes class really enjoyable and helped me improve a lot as a writer. I would definitely take her class again.
Very helpful and very little reading or homework. Tells you exactly what she wants you to write about and considers others opinions well. Very easy and very nice.
I love her! She is so sweet and always lets us out early. The essay we have to write are not bad at all. Her main goal is to make us better writers, which I love.

Easy class as long as you are present and know how to write a good essay. She is very sweet and willing to help. She lets you out early if you have an hour and a half class and I thought the class was relatively easy.
Such a sweet, nice professor. We get out early every class and she really values her student's opinions. The American Family class is really interesting and the topics are easy to write about.
Loved her class. I'd definitely reccomend it.  I thought it was an easy A=/B+.

I got a C on the diagnostic essay, As on all the middle ones but a C on the final essay. I don't think anything changed about my writing though! Grading makes no sense, but she's a nice lady and her class is interesting. Only had one reading quiz and our T/TH section ALWAYS got out early. She's not the worst, I'd reccomend her

If you have her for TuTh, you will ALWAYS get out early. However, she isn't always clear with how she will grade things. Her individual conferences do absolutely no help, either.I did exactly what she told me to do in my paper and still received a poor score.
I had her this spring and I LOVED her! I found her extremely sweet and helpful, and she really made it interesting. Not too tough as a grader - I definitely recommend her class.
Do not take this teacher.  She is a terrible person. I had great attendance and did what I could to make an A and she just ridiculed me and even lied to me.  AVOID!
