One of the best professors I have had. Always available and making time for students. Go to his lectures as he will explain the content on detail and give examples. Wish I could take more of his classes. He really wants to help students.

Amazing professor who is there to help you succeed. He is available outside of class during office hours both in person and through zoom. His flexibility with due dates and missed lectures helped significantly with balancing other course work. He grades fairly and provides good feedback. The best professor I've had at SMU.

I wish I could submit a longer review for Professor Yamamoto, so I could praise him even more! My ADHD made it difficult to do the work at first, but he worked with me and met with me outside of class and because of him, I went from getting a 13 on the first test to a 92 on the second and third! I'll miss him so much. THANK YOU SO MUCH, PROFESSOR!!

The class was organized poorly, study guides were nothing like the test, and he slammed us with work. The tests were extremely hard and often nothing like the material in class. Went to office hours but it did nothing in the long run. Class was awful I would never take it again. Class averages were terrible and he was okay with it.

Worst teacher ever. Shows no mercy grading. Unorganized and late. Tests make up majority of your average. Seems accessible but does not give actual help. I do not recommend taking him. Teaches simple concepts that are nothing compared to the difficulty of the tests. Made me cry daily.
No matter how frequently you see him during office hours, he will never present you with questions that are close to those on tests. Talks a lot about his life.

No matter how many times you go to his office hours, he will never give you problems similar to what he puts on tests. Even though he says he does. Horrible professor. Wouldn't even round my final grade when he knows I tried my absolute best in his stupid class.

The test average on the last test was a 50%. He regraded it 3 times to bring it up to 60%. Refuses to give curves and makes problems overly complicated. Would not recommend. IN class problems are way easier than homework. Makes everything much more difficult than it needs to be. Even taught new material on the last day of classes right before exam.

Most of the prior ratings are not indicative of Ken's actual course. Between himself and his TA, there are office hours each day. He also provides solutions for every homework, daily practice, and test as well as provides an abundance of extra credit. He is an exceptional professor and I highly suggest enrolling in his course! :)
He is a super caring professor and wants everyone to do well. His material is fairly hard but the tests are a lot like the homework. Just make sure to do the homework and go to his office hours.

Professor Yamamoto gets way too much hate for what he provides. Although the class is hard, the grading is tough, and the learning curve is great, Prof. Yamamoto cares about what he is teaching and wants everyone to do well. The class is hard, even for someone who has previously taken Calculus, but if you put in the work you'll be fine.

he gave us 2 homeworks that were after the last day of classes and during exam week! You won't get a thing in class and if you don't do things his way he doesn't score your tests. 3 Tests each worth close to 16% of your grade and the final (worth almost 35%) will make you think you did good until you get your scores.

This class literally gave me anxiety and stress rashes. I practically lived in-office hours, TA sessions, and never missed a class and he failed me. He seems accessible but is not helpful at all. He is the toughest grader at SMU. Each "minimal mistake" you make will cost you 10% of the test. I cried every day due to this class.

Was a really nice person, but not a good professor. I spent hours in his office hours trying to get help, but he tends to get off track and go on and on. DON'T take this class if you have never taken Calculus 1 before!!! He is really disorganized and constantly changed his syllabus and changed his entire grading system halfway through the course.

A good professor for a tough class. Do the classwork and the homework and memorize how you solved the problems. This is because you must be able to know what you are doing during the exams which are designed to be crunched for time.
This class is test heavy and there is so much homework that it becomes hard to keep up. Concepts are overly complicated and difficult. All assignments are way too complex and dont help for the test.

Professor Yamamoto genuinely knows the material and can teach it; however, his lectures are not enough to understand the topics many times. He has a very organized appointment system, making him accessible outside of class, but the workload is still frustrating. The exams are heavily weighted, so you have to study a lot even to pass. Very hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes nice as a person but the worst teacher I have ever had. When I go to tutoring he laughs at questions asked. Makes concepts you think you knew complicated and hard to follow. An insane amount of homework and hes awful at grading on time so you dont know what grade you have in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a very nice teacher and when talking, he could even remember exactly the way I work through specific problems, but there was so much work that even with a rigorous work ethic, I was still drowning in homework from this class. Things are due on breaks, weekends, and grades take weeks to get back. I learned a lot, but only bc it was drilled in.

The professor is extremely nice and genuine but his style of teaching wasn't the best. The professor assigns way too many assignments (and a lot of them were confusing since he makes them on his own). He offers online & in-person classes but I would recommend being there since you can get easily distracted online. Goes past questions quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ken tries to be understanding and caring, but it doesn't work. His tests are extremely difficult if you have a lot of time to STUDY HARD & go to office hours, you can do it, but even tutors at the ALEC were stumped by some of his questions. HW is nothing like the test, and tests determine your grade. Not good, but he's accessible outside of class.

if you really put in the work and study A LOT, you will probably pass. other than that it is very hard to do well. he gives homework and classwork that are helpful and don't weigh too much but the tests is where its all or nothing. the exams are very difficult and are based off of 5 or 6 questions. he is available outside of class. take at own risk

He gets flustered really easy so when kids criticize him at the back of the class you can tell it definitely makes it harder for him to teach. He is good at teaching when he is calm, and he is very lenient and honest with his grading of homework. Overall he is a very nice person and will try his best to explain something when you don't understand.

Avoid at all costs!!! He takes forever to grade stuff to the point he wont have the last test grade in until a day before the next test- so you dont really know how well youre doing/ if youre doing things correctly. He says study the hw to do well on the exams but the exams are nothing like the hw. I got several tutors who also struggled! AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is difficult to understand, and the way she words test questions are really tricky. Lecture power-points are not offered on Blackboard, so a missed class means missed notes. Lectures do not supplement textbook readings, just summarize them, which is boring and frustrating. Lack of attendance affects final grade on a full-letter basis.
She's so cute and nice. I don't mind waking up early for class because she makes it enjoyable.
Awesome!!!
no comment
Awesome professor !!! She's not only knows math, but also knows how to explain problems very well. Test is easy for those who study, homework is not required, but it does help for the test.

Among 5 people that I know in the class, only 2 passed, including me. Within the first two weeks of class, she says "Don't trust my algebra" and does her signature laugh. Terrible professor; follows straight from the book but is harder to understand. Quizzes are very easy. Tests are fine if the student keeps up and doesn't listen to her.
great professor who is very understanding from student level and well delivers her knowledge.
Great professor, tests and quizzes are straight from the homework.

Her lecture is hard to understand and she just reads off the lecture slides, which are boring. I went to her office hour once, and she was very nice and patient, but it was not helpful at all. Although attendance is not required, there's a pop quiz at each lecture. The tests are very hard even with the cheat sheet. She's a nice person though.

For someone with a Ph.D in statistics, she really struggles. The lectures are useless because you can't understand what she's reading directly off the slides. Attendance is taken by a challenging quiz every. The TAs are just as bad if not worse. The tests are impossible, the average every test was a low C or D. Yingbo/TAs don't give any extra help

It's a difficult class. Maybe it's because it's her first year of teaching, but it's hard to understand what she's teaching in the lectures, and hard to transfer that learning to the homework and quizzes. Everyone I know is struggling in the class. Wouldn't recommend.
Don't do it you'll regret it. Horrible teaching and horrible TAs. Everyone fails, drops, or struggles.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This is her first year teaching, which is clearly obvious by her lack of explanation skills and unreasonable grading. You can barely understand anything she says, and her TA's expect you to be on the same level as them, when this is an Intro level class. Take this class if you want to take quizzes every day & sit through a horrible lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. She is a horrendous teacher and I can't understand anything she says. Does a quiz every day beginning of class on stuff you don't understand and you have to finish it in 5 minutes. Absolutely horrible. Would rather die than take from the professor again. Also homework is graded by your TA's who suck.
You can NOT understand a word she says. Stats is pretty easy but she makes it so much harder than it should be!!!!!!!! I realllllllly dont like this class AT ALL. Do not take whatever you do trust me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Went into the class expecting a lot. Terribly disappointed, class lectures are absolutely terrible. She does not engage her students and is overall a bad teacher. Try and take another professor as this should be a class that will help you tremendously in the future, that of which it did not do for me or any of my friends in the course.
Worst professor ever. Talks too much with little point. Can't understand her if you don't read the book. I learned everything from the text book....

Great professor if you actually tried/payed attention in class. Homework assignments weren't written particularly well, but if you go to the TA sessions, it's not that hard. This can be a confusing class, but she does review sheets for exams so if you just study those, you should have no trouble with this class. Def one of my fav classes/profs.

Probably the most confusing and most rude teacher at the Cox school of business. Can't believe they hired her. She doesn't answer emails, very unorganized, doesn't follow up with grades. She has her TA's do everything for her so she absolutely does nothing except write on the board and talks so low that you can't hear her.

She is probably the worst professor I have ever had.  She doesn't really teach, and she definitely doesn't seem like she cares about her students.  I highly recommend NOT taking her class and taking it with a different professor (even if you have to wait a semester)

Class isn't too bad. Open notes quizzes every week, couple tests, a presentation, and some cases you have to read and answer some questions about. The content isn't hard but with the Cox grading scale you have to make sure you do well. Don't worry about this class.
I think this class can easily be slimmed down. The class topics are so fluffed up. No one pays attention. Her new grading scale will mess up your GPA fyi

She was fine, but her lectures were very boring. By the end of the semester everyone was doing other hw in class. Not a crazy hard class, but some of her grading criteria can be kind of unclear on her case studies that she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know why people hate on her. Her class is easy and she understands it's a music class, not important. She doesn't require attendance and tests are online, I missed the first test and then she still let me retake it in May. It's really up to you, go to class get an instant A or don't and get a B. If you fail her class you shouldn't here.

This class is very easy - participation matters, but attendance is not required. Just speak up once every class and you'll be fine. Tests are taken at home online, open note. Presentations are easy as long as you follow the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Could be because I love music but I truly enjoyed this class. Professor Mei was very nice, especially to those who are respectful and take the class seriously. Participation is however, very important if you want to do well in the class, but it's not hard to receive participation points at all.

She is a good teacher but she doesn't talk loud and class participation is very very necessary if you want an A. She is chill and if you talk a lot you'll be totally fine. She has an accent but it's not hard to understand her. If you are a participator, take this class!

Falls behind on schedules and lectures a lot, be prepared to learn half a unit the day before a test. Tests are super easy and online, and can be taken as a class. The one thing to look out for is to meet her presentation requirements clearly or she might lecture you in front of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very easy and so long as you do the work you will get an A. She's hard to understand but it would be hard not to get an A.
She wasn't that bad. I just wouldn't take her class if you're not serious about fine art.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
They've deleted 5 comments with a one star including mine, so I'll keep it simple.

Too many assignments (about 7 different assignments per week), unprofessional (She likes to ignore emails and avoid you, and she talks disrespectful), unclear instructions, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
An expert in her field. Mei, has an extensive knowledge of the curriculum. The preponderance of low ratings are students that I have worked with in the class, whom lack responsibilities in their own academic integrity. Do not judge so quickly. Mei is passionate of what she teaches, and even to her students if you show interest.
Advice: Be present.

She extended all due dates in week 1, to give more time than the original syllabus. Students were plagiarizing, forcing her to delay grading, and make homework multiple choice instead of short answer.

Attending class is necessary, but if you read the short readings and pay attention, it's easy to do well. Pop quiz answers are discussed beforehand.

She is very caring about her students. If you show up to class, you will get a high A, as she even gives extra credit for participation. Participation isn't mandatory, so if you want to do other things while in class, you can! She allows collaboration for in-class quizzes as well. The syllabus change was due to students copying on weekly work.

Don't listen to the other reviews. This class was the easiest class I have ever taken. She care about students and gives crazy amount of extra credit. That take home quizzes are verbatim from the reading. The people leaving and reviews are legit dumb asf and lazy. The concert extra credit could have been watched online 😂. Easy A with minimal work.
Started changing the class structure halfway through the class. And argues that she doesn't care what are grades are because they don't impact her future, but ours.

There is no reason why such an easy class should be made trivial and difficult. She won't help you, even if you request it because she seems to never check her emails. And then she gives you a poor grade afterward. Goes on tangents and rants during class and ignores the fact that there are students there who actually want to do a good job.

Do not take this class. Horrible at giving this class direction, Ive read the syllabus at least 4 times by now and I'm still not sure where this class is heading. It's been almost two months and still has not graded any of our assignments. Wont know if I need to improve my performance till its too late. This is the first bad review Ive ever written

This professor referred me to the syllabus over a grade dispute which she would not be flexible on. Once I read through the syllabus I realized she had calculated everyone in the classes grade based on total points while the syllabus clearly outlines the percentages she was supposed to use for each test/category. Do not take her class.

Professor Mei is knowledgeable and passionate about the material, but lectures can get a bit boring especially if you are not interested in world music. Assignments are fairly easy, especially the exams. Final grade is made up of many components, and there are several opportunities for extra credit.

Literally, one of the worst teachers I have had. If music is not your life and you're not a music major, just be ready. She nitpicks at things that you say and even if you choose the paper option over the presentation, she will still make you present and rips everyone apart. She has pop quizzes more days than not and I would rather watch paint dry
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not recommend Professor Mei for MUHI 1302. She is rude and gives very unclear instructions for assignments/class. Doesn't post powerpoints after class to review and hard to get ahold of for help. Says attendance is optional but gives pop quizzes every few classes and no ability to drop any of them. Unnecessarily difficult class and boring

This woman. She is rude, doesn't answer questions, and does not care about you or your grade. She gives random pop quizzes through the semester with 2 questions each and you cannot use notes. She does cancel class a lot, which is nice. But I simply cannot sit through another 1h20 minute class. Do not take, please stay far far away. BAD IDEA!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jeff Yu is a great teacher. His accent is not thick, so don't worry about that. The class is made up of hw, quizzes and tests. The quizzes are harder than the tests and count less towards your grade. The tests are not bad at all-mainly mc and some free response.

If you can avoid Jeff, do! His tests are set up so that you are not meant to finish. His accent makes it hard to understand what he's saying half the time. He's a nice guy for the most part, but when it comes to helping you with individual questions, he's useless and will talk down to you.

I had T.A. Yulan Bai twice. She is very responsible and committed. The labs where she is TA for are challenging courses and are material heavy, still she manages to finish them and give you as much feedback as possible. She is very reachable outside class. You can tell that she tries to do her best. She will help you! you just need to do your part.

Professor Bai is very efficient in helping students. She is quite familiar with the materials and just gets to the point of what needs to be done to solve a problem. She is responsible, respectful and caring for each student especially those in need. All her labs are superb. I learned so much from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS TA AT ALL COSTS.I had her for two of my EMIS classes and she didn't have any knowledge about them. Very rude to students and unhelpful. Takes attendance every class. She has no idea how to do the labs and depends solely on the answer key. Doesn't respond to emails. Grades brutally. Go to lab to check your answers with her

Literally the most useless TA I have ever had. Every question you ask her is responded with "Google it." I've seen freshmen more capable than her. She also is a terrible grader, she takes off as many points as she can and doesn't give a reason why it is wrong when you ask her, its always "It's just wrong, see?" and then doesn't elaborate.

LITERALLY THE BEST PROFESSOR AT SMU. He is so kind and really cares about his students. Also really funny and will go above and beyond to help you if you show you are interested. Take this man over anyone else, he is awesome!
Such a great guy. So understanding and caring. Obviously loves what he does and is a great teacher.
Works with students very well. Genuine and amazing person and teacher. Not many papers, and he grades very fairly.

This prof was great for my first writing class at smu. He was clear with what he wanted but did have high standards for his students. Daily hw assignments are not too bad and useful for discussions. His grading isn't too bad, but be expected to write well and put in the work for an A. He makes time to meet w you outside of class. (had him w covid)

Professor Thriffiley is amazing! His lectures are entertaining, and he makes writing essays fun by giving us current and relevant topics to write about! He is always there to help, and gives amazing feedback on your essays before they're due, so it is pretty easy to make an A in the class!

She knows the material very well but she does not know how to teach it. She flies through the powerpoints so quickly I had to resort to taking pictures of each slide with my phone. She also doesn't put them on BB. Exams are tricky, and quizzes are misleading. With all due respect to Professor Zarazaga, I do not recommend this class at all.

This was a horrible class. This professor was completely scatter brained and tried to cover way too much material in too little time. She went super fast in class and refused to post the powerpoints, so students had no way to get good, concrete notes to study. This class was incredibly unfair and I would NOT recommend this class at all.

Interesting subject matter, but horrible teaching skills. Her powerpoints are completely disorganized and so are her tests. A TON of information to know for the tests, and she expects the class to know all of it. the hardest class I took this semester when I thought it would be one of my easier ones. avoid if possible.

Debatably the WORST class I've taken at SMU thus far. Professor Zarazaga is disorganized, unclear, and is constantly changing her mind about deadlines, assignments and the dates associated with the buildings she covers. An art history background will definitely help if you have to take this class, but if you can avoid it, I would… Bad overall!

Difficult class, disorganized lectures, powerpoints not posted. Attendance sign in sheets for first half of the course. Not a good class to take if you are looking to fulfill requirements. 1 midterm 1 final 1 design project and 7 quizzes and 7 homework's. Midterm and final make up most of the grade. Expects you to know more than she covers.

Prof. Zarazaga obviously really cares about her class and architecture. She sometimes assumes we understand things that we don't. The class is manageable and covers a lot of credits but it isn't fun. 1 Midterm and a final, so a lot rides on that. A few, detailed questions so you have to know everything well.TIme commitment studying, but not too bad

Worst professor ever. Thinks her class is the most important class you take. Gives more work than major classes. A bunch of confusing quizzes, a midterm, final, and group project make up grade. Very confusing lectures and power points. Overall just terrible

Should be an easy A to help students to fulfill UC req. but when an elective is harder than major courses, something is wrong. She says she is straightforward when she is the exact opposite. One midterm, final, and a group project. 3pt quizzes but each question has 5 parts & if you miss one you miss the entire point. Take pillars somewhere else.

TERRIBLE TEACHER! Lectures dont make any sense, power points are all over the place. Quizzes are confusing. Midterm is also very tricky. I took this class in order to fulfill pillars. NOT A GOOD DECISION

If you need this class to cover pillars look elsewhere. Requires many hours of work in order to do well and get an A. Powerpoints and lectures are extremely disorganized thus outside reading is required in order to stay ahead. Don't take this class if you are looking for an easy pillar or proficiency
She does not realize this is a 1000 level class. Really disorganized and not helpful. Don't recommend.

Professor Zarazaga is very passionate about architecture but she does not know how to properly relay information to the students. Her power points are unorganized, which makes staying on track in the class very difficult. The midterm is challenging as it is detail oriented. Overall, I wouldn't recommend taking her class.
Very confusing lectures, powerpoints are all over the place. Not very clear. Quizzes announced class before. One midterm and one final. Midterm very tricky.
Very confusing lectures, powerpoint slides are all over the place. Quizzes announced class before. Can be tricky. Mid term very challenging, very detail oriented

Prof. Zarazaga does a great job covering the material, as well as making it interesting.  I liked how she was extremely flexible with the flow of the class, yet she isn't a push over when students turn in late assignments, although she is very understanding.  There were many out of class experiences that greatly added to the value of the course.

Amazing teacher! Incredibly knowledgeable, engaging, and made the class fun. He's a grad student, but best programming teacher at SMU I've had so far. His quizzes (test really) are pretty much like the reviews, the lab assignments take some time but he's always available to help.  Has a accent, but his English is perfect. Take his class if you can.
Fantastic teacher, incredibly knowledgeable and actually excited about coding, would recommend highly.

He's a grad student who was hired to teach the intro CS courses. Even though he's originally from China his English is pretty good - not perfect - but still can pull off a good lecture. He's sometimes boring but he can get excited about the tangents he will go off on. Otherwise he's a great guy that, if you interact with him at all, gives you an A
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Accent hard to understand at times. Organized and well thought-out lectures. Really pay attention to powerpoints. Doesnt clearly state what to study for exam Will probably curve if the majority does poorly on an exam. 2 midterms, 1 final, 3 assignments, 4 one chapter quizzes. Offers extra credit like most LMU business courses.

If you develop a relationship with her (ie go to her office hours and talk every once in a while during class) you will do very well. I made an C- and two B+s on her three tests and 100s on every online quiz and got an A- in the class. If you do poorly it's because you didn't try at all.

At times it can be difficult to understand her accent. She gets quite upset when people don't participate and takes attendance randomly. The lectures are definitely not clear and you are pretty much left on your own to learn the material, and it can get pretty challenging. She's by no means my favorite professor at Cox but she's also not the worst.

This class was grueling, though this is certainly in part due to the subject matter. The tests shouldn't have been hard, but they are convoluted. Wiley Plus homework is mandatory and must be paid for, which is ridiculous considering how much we already pay for the class. The book is worthless, so pay attention in lecture.

Prof. Li really cares about her students. Attendance is mandatory, and you should at least look over the homework before class. Her tests are a little more difficult than the practice test, but she really tries to be fair. The quizzes are easy and most are based off homework problems. You can tell she really wants her students to learn and succeed.

Attendance mandatory. And while she is no Greg Sommers (very helpful lectures) her classes aren't too bad. 5 online quizzes worth 25% of your grade and you get week(s) notice and multiple attempts per question. Tests are not too easy but she's a nice teacher

If you take her for Intermediate Acct. 2 (3312), you will regret it. Her tests are way different from the homeworks and book exercises, and she cannot be any worse at presenting the material in class. Going to class every day was dreadful, and you have to because she takes attendance.

Dr Li is a great professor. Her lectures are always very easy to follow and tests are exactly like the homework problems. If you do the homework it is a very easy A. I highly recommend taking her class.

I loved her class. If you go to her office hours and ask for help she is more than willing explain things. As a senior now I can say that although her class isn't easy she prepares you for your upper level acocunting courses. I strongly recommend taking her.

Dr. Li was great. Despite other reviews, I just took her class and received a very good grade. Sometimes she is hard to understand. Homework assignments take 1 hour, 1 due every week. Tests are pretty tough but manageable. The key is to have her know who you are. If she does, she will help you out. Visit her at her office. Take this class

Dr. Li was great. Despite other reviews, I just took her class and received a very good grade. Sometimes she is hard to understand. Homework assignments take 1 hour, 1 due every week. Tests are pretty tough but manageable. The key is to have her know who you are. If she does, she will help you out. Visit her at her office. Take this class

Prof Li's class was very manageable.  She understands that students are busy and constantly asks for feedback on how she is doing.  Her tests can be tricky, but she gives review sheets that really help if you study them.  The homework's were intense and hard at first, but after we complained in her survey she cut it back.  TAKE HER FOR ACCT 2301!!
Good professor, always available if you have questions.  Must got to class and try to participate.

I would NOT recommend her.I cannot understand ONE word she says. She is psycho about taking attendance. She teaches the material in the most inconvenient way and makes the material more confusing. Class is worthless because she just reads off of ppts. Her tests are impossible. Avoid at all costs.  She's one of the worst teachers I've had at SMU.
wouldnt reccommend. she gets mad when people dont participate.. she should go teach high school
No Comments

Professor Li was a pretty good teacher to have for accounting 2301.  As long as you keep up on the reading and study the tests aren't too bad.  Also, she does review sessions before all the tests which is very helpful!
I thought she was a great professor and extremely fair grader!  I really learned a lot in her class and understood what I was learning.

Easily my favorite Spanish teacher at this school. She's an angel. You have to do 8 HW assignments, 3 1 page papers, 2 4-5 page papers, and a presentation over the course of the semester. She gives everyone above a 90 on all of them, and as long as you put in some effort she likes you. The class itself can be dry but she makes it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zuese is great. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. If you participate in class occasionally, prepare for her essays (she has essays instead of exams), and do the homework you'll succeed. The lectures can be dry at times but she's a wonderful professor. I've taken her twice and would take her again!
This teacher respects her students- if they want to move a due date for an assignment or an exam she is very considerate and flexible. Her quiz/exams are in class essays- she is a generous grader.

relatively easy but homework due EVERY class. Regularly 2 assignments due for one class. Lots of reading. can get away without reading tho. Class was also BORING and lectures were a waste of time.homework is completion grade. This class is the definition of busy work but easy A. Prof is nice, kinda seems like she hates everyone. No exams, 2 papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So much busy work and her lectures are all over the place but you don't really have to pay attention. Lots of busy work but for most homework assignments you can get away with using chat GPT. Attendance is mandatory and severely affects your grade. She grades pretty easily though as long as you somewhat answer the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Zuese is one of the BEST professors I have had at SMU. The Spanish Civilization class is really interesting and the course material is very interesting. The professor is nice, caring, and teaches well. Super fun class. Make sure to read the material so that you can have examples to help you with the final paper.

Prof. Zuese is AMAZING! She cares about her students so much and truly just wants all of us to learn. She is super clear on the grading criteria and sets you up for success for every test and project. There is a final paper rather than a test, and she will 100% help you every step of the way to make sure you get a good grade. TAKE HER!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can earn up to 3% of extra credit by doing 3 extra case studies. TAs graded cases kind of hard but he graded the group project pretty kindly. Lectures are straightforward and tests are curved fairly.
Solid professor overall. Class topics were interesting.

He is super nice but not a great teacher. Everything you need to know is directly on the slides, and if its not he says it in class. Case Studies can be lengthy and somewhat hard but arent impossible. Exams arent bad if you study the slides. The group project papers are lengthy but not hard. Everything is graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. you need to participate and do case studies basically every other class but theyre really easy. The tests were fine and attendance is mandatory but I thought it was a fun class.

you do not need the textbook. The tests are based on the powerpoints used in class. The case studies are lengthy reads but only need to do some versus all. Not too taxing of a class and the midterm and final are fine if you study the decks.

Very nice and knowledgeable professor. He keeps the class interesting but also realizes that many people take it to satisfy the UC requirement. Read the cases and be ready to participate in class and you will do well.
Really enjoyed this class! Just show up and read the cases and you'll do well. He is soft-spoken so I recommend sitting closer to the front.

If youre planning to take this class online, dont. It was truly a waste of my tuition dollars, and I wouldnt recommend it to anyone. He recorded himself reading the lectures off the PowerPoint and then the quizzes, while sometimes on quizlet, were always so much more detailed than his lectures. Also, the class met like 10 times in total. Stupid.

This class is not particularly difficult. It is a painfully boring subject matter and Daniel Zyung does a good job of teaching it. The tests are pure regurgitation. You have to go to class as he takes attendance and pays attention to who comes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: This is a review of the pompous chem department. SMU is a mediocre university, yet they think that an AP exam score of "4" is beneath them. It's sad. I took this class because I got a 4 on the AP exam, didn't watch one lecture, and didn't study at all, but I still did well in class 4 ON THE AP EXAM.

Incredible at teaching. Hard professor, but if you put in the work, it's easy and it's worth it. His teaching style prepares you for OChem. It'll be hard to have another professor measure up to his amazing lectures :)

Listen, Zoltowski is a nice guy but that doesn't make him a good professor, he tries at least in office hours but no matter how many textbook problems you do or how many practice exams you take, you will receive an exam that is nothing like what you were studying. They will blindside you totally and are all your grade is built upon.

Incredible professor. His lectures are phenomenal-goes out of his way to ensure you understand the content and succeed in his class, despite its rigor. So much so that he has reviews until 10-11pm the night before the exam. He's like a first ex you never get over, except he's a professor I'll never get over LOL. So sad I won't have him again!

Initially appears manageable, only to unravel into an ordeal of excessive material, unclear grading criteria, and point deductions galore. He either is unable to merely refuses to teach the material so you better be able to do all the work yourself. Strongly discourage subjecting anyone to this unnecessarily burdensome experience.

Dr. Zoltowski is an amazing professor. He is so caring and truly wants everyone to succeed. He has a flipped class and spends in-person lectures answering questions and working on different problems. I highly recommend taking his class. His class is difficult for some people, but if you put in the effort you will do fine.

I really liked Dr. Z my only complaint would be I wish he had actual lecture slides. Even though chem was not my best subject and I usually made mid-80s on tests he gave enough pity points and curves that I ended with an A.

Zoltowski is literally the best professor you can have for chem 1303 or 1304! Hilarious and entertaining in lectures and really great at explaining difficult concepts. Do the homework, even if it's optional. Ask lots of questions, too. 10/10 recommend.

THIS IS A VERY HARD CLASS. Do not take it at all if you don't plan on putting in the work. Dr. Z makes it much more bearable though. The lecture videos are detailed and doing practice problems in class instead of the lecture was infinitely more helpful. The exams are very fair, you will pretty much know exactly what's going to be on them.

The best option for chem 1304! Lecture videos have everything you need to know for exams. If you can do the practice exams and in class problems then you will be fine on the exams. His office hours can be busy but very helpful. This class is definitely difficult and takes a lot of work but dr z does everything to help. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
One of the best professors I've had. Go to office hours.

Literally the best SMU CHEM has to offer. Tests are very similar to practice tests and practice problems. Always available (even over text ) for you to ask questions. As long as you put in the work, this class will go well. Also frequently will change grade scale to account for higher grades. (Ex. 85=A-).

This class is TOUGH. However, Zolt will do everything he can to help you as long as you reach out and make the effort. I lived in this guy's office hours, but it was worth it. Do the lectures and lecture problems before class. Go to office hours. You can even ask him about chem lab. Lots of extra credit opportunities. You HAVE to work hard. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He definitely makes you work for it. he makes you apply the concepts rather than memorize and plug and chug equations. super personable and super super accessible dude

I would not have passed CHEM 1304 if not for Professor Z. He's the best. He really does care about how much you learn inside and outside of class. He makes his office hours really flexible and accessible, and caters to the way you learn. CHEM 1304 was hell, but professor Z made it a bit more bearable.

CHEM 1304 is really hard, but Dr. Zoltowski is seriously the best choice hands down. You can email him questions at almost any time of day and he will respond right away. He truly cares about his students is great at explaining difficult concepts. Exams are hard, but he is generous with partial credit. Prepares students very well for future classes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zoltowski is by far one of the best professors at SMU. He's always willing to help students outside of class, and his teaching style will set you up for success in future chemistry courses. While his tests are difficult, he's super generous with partial credit. That being said, don't expect an easy A. He'll make you work for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's no way around it -- 1304, especially during summer, is an extremely challenging course. Dr. Z is an incredible professor -- he is available literally 24/7 via text, email, etc. to help students. He provides resources (practice exams and problem sets) to help students succeed. That being said, averages for exams were between 42-65. Work hard

Dr. Zoltowski is definitely the smartest person Ive ever met. That being said, his class was the hardest thing Ive ever done. He gives amazing feedback and really notices if you are trying to improve. He is basically available 24/7 to answer questions. He will really help you if you just ask. Hes an amazing professor but be ready to work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The way this course was set up was horrible, only exams determined your grade. The exams were some of the hardest I have ever done, I ended up hiring a tutor for twice a week and would feel solid in what I practiced from the practice problems he gave only to get on the exam and feel lost. The entire class was failing with averages of 43-62 on exams

Here's the thing. Zoltowski is a pretty good professor. He is very helpful during office hours and sort of makes the material more interesting to learn. But, no matter how many textbook problems you do or how many practice exams you take, you will receive an exam that is nothing like what you were studying. His exams are unnecessarily difficult.

He is very charismatic! He explains chemistry so well. Watch his lecture videos and attend in-person lecture! He is super accessible outside of class so do not be afraid to go to his office hours. He has extra credit opportunities and an appealing grading scale. He seems unapproachable at first, but he really enjoys talking to his students.

I generally hate chemistry, but I liked this class. If you pay attention and practice the problems and practice exams he gives, an A will be easy. I took his class online, asynchronously, during janterm and loved it.

Chemistry is a tough subject no matter who you take but Dr. Z made questions unnecessarily difficult. When he was absent for like a week Dr. Adams lectured us instead and I understood so much more from her. Went to her once in office hours to try and understand Dr. Z's example problems and even she was confused at times. Better than Patty at least
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is a tough professor, however he challenges his students to prepare them for the tougher chemistry courses in the future! If you start coming in right away to get help you will see improvement right away. He takes time to get to know you in office hours and genuinely cares about his students. He also will take notice of your hard work!
Class is hard, but Zoltowski is available pretty much 24/7 if you have questions or need help. He's also a really chill guy and he's pretty dope.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BZ is a nice guy, but he is completely unorganized in his lectures and his tests are near impossible regardless of how many times you do the homework. Good in his office hours but still completely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is available literally 24/7 to help you. Do the HW, go to class, & seek out the help you need. He really wants to make this easier on you. He's an amazing professor and will explain concepts a million different ways until you understand them - so grateful I had him!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's chemistry - go to class, do the HW, go to office hours. As for Dr. Z: he is available at literally all hours of the day if you ask. Literally he will teach you for as long as you need as long as you are willing to learn. His only goal is to make this course easier on his students-he wants everyone to do well. True professor through & through.

Dr. Zoltowski is a GODSEND to the General Chemistry courses. He warns us that the material is definitely not easy, but he is incredibly helpful in making sure that you truly understand the information. Take his advice, use office hours, do the homework, work on practice tests, and take a deep breath. Dr. Z is on your side.

INCREDIBLE HUMAN BEING AND EXEMPLARY PROFESSOR. Gen Chem is hard. Period. If the material does not come naturally to you, attending lectures, doing the practice problems and going to office hours are absolutely essential. Don't be afraid to ask questions because Dr. Z is very understanding AND super smart. Tests are very challenging so study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: PROS Everything. Cons the material. Hardest class a student can take a freshman coupled to the best teacher you can take as a freshman. Literally the nicest guy youll ever meet. Grades fair, loves what he teachers, and loves his students. Hes a legend. Bought pizza for us 3 times, will meet with you literally any time of day. Outstanding professor.

Dr. Zoltowski is truly an inspirational professor. He knows the subject thoroughly and makes his lectures engaging. There is an opportunity late in the semester for extra credit, which I recommend doing because this class is definitely a weed-out. Dr. Z keeps the class casual, which allows for the course to be enjoyable despite the heavy workload.

Does everything on his part to provide his students with the opportunity to be successful in his class.  Very accessible outside of class and takes the time to get to know his students.  10/10 would recommend this class.

Dr. Z makes chemistry fun. For someone who didn't particularly enjoy chemistry, he taught the class exactly the way I'd want a class taught. His office hours are informal and he's super approachable so if you need the help, he's there and ready for you. He's an amazing professor and everyone should take class with him before they graduate!

One of the best professors I've had at SMU. He takes the time to really explain concepts with lots of examples and is very helpful during office hours. Definitely do the homework and practice tests to do well, but overall not too bad! He's very funny and entertaining as well.

Professor Zoltowski is an amazing teacher. Not only does he know the material, but he expresses it in a way that makes sense to the students. He also truly cares for his students and goes above and beyond to help his students. He is, by no means, an easy teacher, but if you are willing to work hard, then you will be fine.

Dr. Z is hands down the best professor I've had at SMU! He is warm, funny, highly intelligent, and a great encourager. His class is challenging, but in the best way possible and you will leave having learned a ton. He is ALWAYS available for extra help and is more dedicated to his students and their success than any other professor I've met!
He is one of the best and motivating professors I have encountered at SMU.

This is a tough class so be prepared to devote a lot of time towards doing well. In general, chemistry is tough subject. Do the suggested problems over and over again until you feel confident doing them. Do any extra credit assignments that he offers and go to office hours as soon as you start to feel confused.
Love Dr. Z! very funny during lectures but office hours are a must. he is always willing to explain if youre not 100% sure about the subject.

Dr. Z is your greatest resource for learning gen chem 2. He'll challenge you in ways that regular science courses won't, furthering your ability to solve any chemistry problem he gives you. Do the extra homework over and over again until you feel comfortable working it backwards because that's basically the exam. Highly intelligent and caring guy.
Awesome professor. Hard class, but awesome experience.

I took gen chem 2 with him during may term and it was great.  He's an amazing professor and is very clear and helpful with all the concepts.  He's a little tough so you will need to study well for the tests, but he's significantly better than the other Gen chem professors.  He's very fair with partial credit and I would 100% take him again.

Zoltowski is a warm, funny, and intellectual professor. With that being said, his lectures are dull and are for people who have a strong background in chemistry. Tests are nearly impossible to pass. If you cherish your GPA, avoid this man at all costs. Seriously,

Dr.Z was the best teacher i had at SMU, hands down. He is always available to answer questions and he is more dedicated to his students than any other professor ive ever met. His class is extremely difficult but worth taking to have the awesome experience of having him as a prof. His lectures are also engaging. His passion for chem is contagious
lectures are extremely disorganized and his tests are impossible regardless of how well you think you prepared.  The key to a good grade is to make him like you since that's how he grades
Professor Zoltowski is the best chemistry professor to take at SMU hands down. He isn't easy, but he keeps the class interesting and entertaining

This class is challenging but in the best way possible. Dr. Z is very knowledgable & although he moves quickly in class he is ALWAYS willing to answer questions in office hours (with a friendly attitude). Put in work in Dr. Z's class (do the homework, STUDY, go to office hours) and it will pay off. I'm not hating on Patty but Dr. Z is pretty great!

Dr. Z loves chem, but big ego, office hours can be more like social hour, no quizzes only tests which have low averages, but will curve later on and gave an extra credit opp later in semester, test way harder than hw/study guide, feel like I’m destined to fail. B/t him and Patty I def chose him and am glad I did, but his class isn’t easy.

Dr. Z is probably just as hard as Patty but he does it with a smile. He's a great professor to have though and is legitimately always in his office and willing to stay until whenever to help you out. He cares so much about his students and helping them to do well! As long as he sees you trying he'll help you out!!

Really cool, young guy.  The class is hard but so are all gen chem classes and I heard Dr.Z was the easiest.  Hard tests with low grades but he gives big curves at the end of the year.  Lectures can get a bit boring but he tries to add demonstrations to keep it interesting
